Guided by the motto "gemütlich - ehrlich - herzlich" (cosy - honest - cordial), Lokal is a cross between a restaurant and a bar with a relaxed atmosphere; in fine weather, the gorgeous terrace beckons. The cuisine features a modern and plant-based approach, with a strong emphasis on regional and seasonal ingredients. In addition to the à la carte selection – whose dishes such as asparagus, miso and egg yolk are sure to whet the appetite – there is a carte blanche menu with four or five courses. Decent wine list, friendly and professional service. You are also welcome to just drop in for a glass of wine, a beer or a cocktail.

Name: Bazaar
Description: At this restaurant in the chic Alpine CERVO Mountain Resort – which commands a great panoramic view – you are whisked away to an exotic and predominantly vegetarian world of flavours, ranging from Arabic to Chinese specialities, from Lebanese flatbread (manakish) and pistachio baklava to dim sum and much more. In keeping with its name, this place has a lively and friendly atmosphere, to which original and highly disparate decorative details also contribute.

Name: Njørd café
Description: Njørd Café is a spin-off of the restaurant Njørden. It serves fresh and seasonal Scandinavian and Swiss cuisine in a modern, Nordic atmosphere. Breakfast and brunch is also available at the weekend. To the rear of the building, there is a charming terrace planted with herbs and flowers. Hotel Hemma has a number of pleasant guestrooms.

Name: SALZANO
Description: The restaurant of this family-run chalet hotel presents an interesting concept in a friendly atmosphere. Classic cuisine is on offer at lunchtime and in the evening; in addition there is a lunch deal and a "close-to-nature" gourmet set menu every evening from Tue to Sat. The top-notch ingredients are almost exclusively sourced locally, many of them harvested by the chefs themselves.

Name: Birdy's by Achtien
Description: Perfect for anyone who loves to share! For lunch and dinner, chef Christian Vogel (aka Birdy) provides an exciting dining experience. With the "Sharing is Love" concept, he puts the onus on communication as much as culinary enjoyment in a relaxed, modern atmosphere. The cuisine is predominantly vegetarian, but can be supplemented with fish or meat – both of which are of the highest quality. Choose à la carte dishes such as cauliflower tempura, soy sauce, peanut, salted lemon, or roast Hokkaido pumpkin, peanut, Thai curry, kumquat, with optional fried Gotthard zander. The sharing surprise menu for two is also on point – ten dishes are served in three courses.

Name: Alpenblick - Swiss Bistro
Description: Bistro makes for a pleasant alternative to Gourmetstübli in the Alpenblick hotel. Diners soak up the cosy atmosphere as they tuck into the excellent food served here. On the menu: delicious regional and seasonal dishes as well as classics such as Kalbfleisch-Geschnetzeltes (slices of Simmental veal in a creamy sauce) and cheese fondue. And be sure to try the rösti! On Tuesday evenings the restaurant hosts a meat fondue buffet.

Name: Ivy 23
Description: A lively restaurant and bar in the historical centre of Carouge. Whitewashed brick walls and 1930s-style decoration, such as lamps and old posters evocative of the prohibition era in the US, make for a distinctive atmosphere, underscored by a soundtrack of jazz/swing sounds. They serve modern and seasonal food with a French twist. Pleasant little terrace in the courtyard to the rear.

Name: Ô Bois Sauvage
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Great view,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Situated at an elevation of approximately 1 500m above sea level, this restaurant is just 250m away from Hérémence's high-speed lift station. The breathtaking mountain vistas are undoubtedly one of the restaurant's standout features, best enjoyed on the fantastic terrace. Alternatively, you can savour the view from indoors, where the atmosphere is modern and relaxed. Incidentally, the numerous decorative works of art are available for purchase. This restaurant's commitment to sustainability and its strong attachment to the region are evident in the selection of produce, such as fillet of Swiss grass-fed ox or cheese. The short wine list features labels from the region.

Name: L'Agape
Description: This lovely old-school bistro ticks all the boxes when it comes to good vibes. It has been tastefully refurbished to showcase features such as its original tiling, wooden banquette seating, mirrors on the walls, a large chandelier fashioned out of old copper pans and a small service counter. As for the food, chef Clément Thellier has designed a short, savvy menu that makes your mouth water with its well-crafted and beautifully presented dishes: sweetbreads en barigoule, bacon crisps, split peas with bacon; beef tenderloin, toasted bread, pan-fried foie gras, mini vegetables and potato emulsion; poached and glazed pineapple, toasted pain d'épices and rum ice cream. A lovely dining experience at a reasonable price – not to be sniffed at in Geneva!

Name: Bistrot du Lion d'Or
Description: In the restaurant of this hotel dating from 1750, the team offers - in a friendly and relaxed atmosphere - delicious French cuisine with seasonal products, such as artichoke, smoked whitefish from the nearby lakes and buckwheat, or pan-fried sweetbreads, morels and asparagus. The well-curated wine list is also worthy of your attention. In fine weather, the pleasant terrace to the rear of the building is a peaceful little haven for diners.

Name: Stadthaus
Description: In the restaurant of the grand Hotel Stadthaus, you can either dine in the casual Stadtcafé or the elegant La Pendule; the same flavoursome cuisine is served in both areas. There are classics such as cordon bleu, vegetarian dishes and a bistro set menu – an ambitious gourmet set menu is also served on Thu-Sat evenings. The range of wines available by the glass and bottles is also impressive.

Name: Bären
Description: The 14th generation of the same family is at the helm of this gorgeous traditional Bernese inn – it was first documented in 1261. Whether you eat in the pretty, inviting dining area or the lovely garden, you will be treated to friendly service and delicious food with a traditional regional character. One speciality of the house is the Solothurner Wy-Süppli (wine soup). The chef will be happy to explain the origins of their rather special "Bärechöpfli" dessert. Slightly reduced menu at lunchtime. There are also stylish salons.

Name: Blume
Description: At this pleasant restaurant, heart and skill go into rustling up regional cuisine made with top-notch ingredients. Risotto is one of the chef's specialties, but they also serve offal, such as tripe or liver. The spit-roast skewers flambéed at your table and the Chateaubriand have to be ordered in advance and are served to the whole table. The rustic downstairs space is an appealing backdrop for your meal; the upstairs room is a little more elegant. With her friendly, outgoing manner, the owner adds a personal touch to the service. The beautiful quiet location is rural yet still close to Zurich.

Name: 16 ART-BAR-RESTAURANT
Description: Diners will feel right at home in this charming and inviting restaurant. Set in a former bell foundry, the atmosphere is welcoming and delightfully down to earth. The blend of rustic and modern styles is interesting, and the art on the walls is sure to draw the eye. You can look forward to very friendly and attentive service, as well as pared-down and exceedingly flavourful dishes prepared by owner Nik Buchs. Popular choices here include true classics such as entrecôte or veal cutlet. The extensive wine list also includes organic and biodynamic wines.

Name: Rathauskeller Bistro
Description: The friendly service and relaxed atmosphere here are popular with locals and tourists alike. Diners can choose from the selection of classics such as cordon bleu, Lammhacktätschli (lamb patties) and beef roulades, and there is also a seasonal menu. The tables on the gorgeous terrace in front of the building in the cobbled pedestrian zone are coveted. Tip: Just a stone's throw away, the lakeside is perfect for a stroll.

Name: Château de Pleujouse
Description: Perched on a rocky spur, this 10C fortress overlooks the surrounding countryside. A duo of chefs delights diners with organic and regional ingredients; bread, gratins and rice pudding are baked in the bread oven – a truly artisanal approach, which, by drawing on produce from the terroir, takes us back to the feasts of yesteryear! A very warm welcome.

Name: PINOT
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Great view,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: The location in the side wing of the modern Klinik Gut private hospital may be a little unusual, but the food here is excellent… thanks to Roland Schmid, who has made a name for himself in the region over the years. The decor is trendy and minimalist in style, with an open kitchen; the view of the mountains and the surrounding area is fabulous – tables on the terrace are understandably coveted. Tip: the tasting menu on Thursday evenings.

Name: Bistrot Dumas
Description: This buzzy bistro located in the Champel neighbourhood is often fully booked. The interior is done out simply and tastefully – it is the Art Nouveau stained-glass ceiling panels, as well as the columns, that draw the eye. Their classic take on traditional French cuisine is flavoursome and aromatic, plus everything is made in-house. The service is efficient and attentive.

Name: La Fleur de Sel
Description: Regional cuisine and a bistro style atmosphere in the Fleur de Sel.

Name: Restaurant du Quai
Description: This inviting restaurant on the shore of Lake Geneva serves tasty seasonal cuisine with no frills. Chef Jérôme Manifacier is a real pro, whose motto is "take your time"; all you have to do is trust him. Superb terrace shaded by the plane trees and with a fabulous view of the lake and the Jura mountains.

Name: Casa Casutt - Ustria
Description: Linus and Therese Arpagaus offer diners a charming setting in which to tuck into their excellent cuisine made using fresh produce. The menu takes its cue from the region and includes local specialties such as capuns and pizokel. Fans of veal liver, sweetbreads or tripe are also in for a treat. The garden terrace is wonderful, and Sala is another alternative.

Name: Moosegg
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Up here, at an altitude of around 1 000m, there is much to get excited about: the phenomenal view of the Emmental and the Alps – either from the modern, elegant restaurant with its large window front or the magnificent terrace – is complemented by good food with a regional and seasonal focus. For a cheaper but equally indulgent alternative, head to Beiz. The terrific wine selection boasts around 800 different options. Chic guestrooms are available in the adjoining boutique hotel.

Name: Restaurant Schlüssel - Schlüsselstube
Description: Schlüsselstube is a bistro where they also serve outstanding food – and it represents really great value for money. Classics such as braised veal cheeks are delicious, and the desserts are extremely hard to resist! When it comes to wine, this cosy place also hits all the right notes. The service provided by waitresses in traditional dress could not be more charming!

Name: Zum Alten Stephan
Description: This restaurant in the middle of the old town is not only steeped in history, it is also a treat for epicureans. Top-notch, down-to-earth cooking, staff who go the extra mile and a buzzing atmosphere make for a perfect dining experience. While Tamara Bader heads up the service team with effortless charm, her husband Stefan whips us delectable dishes rooted in classic tradition. Think pan-fried sweetbreads with mashed potato, spring vegetables and a morel sauce. House classics such as the cordon bleu are also in high demand. The impressive wine list is dedicated to Swiss, French and Italian labels. Delightful terrace in front of the building.

Name: Auberge de la Croix d'Or - Bistro
Description: Claudia and Olivier Hiernard have combined bistro and restaurant at their charming inn. The delicious bistro fare on the blackboard is now complemented by a market-inspired "Menu du Marché", meaning flavoursome dishes are now served in both parts of the establishment. Just don't forget to leave room for dessert! On Friday and Saturday evenings, only a small selection is available.

Name: Sonne
Description: At the Häfliger family's lovely 100-year-old restaurant, diners can look forward to fresh, flavoursome food and attentive service provided by experienced staff. Classic Swiss cuisine is served in the form of a seasonal or surprise set menu. Alternatively, you can order à la carte. This place even has its own excellent spring water! Pleasant terrace to the rear of the building. Tip: Delicious cheese is sold in the cheesery next door.

Name: Edo
Description: You can be in the Swiss mountains and still enjoy authentic Japanese cuisine, including dishes such as Japanese fondue, grilled chicken with Teriyaki sauce, and delicious gyozas and sushi (takeaway dishes are also available). Here, legendary specialities from Japan are prepared in front of you with high-quality ingredients and meticulous care. Terrace with views of the surrounding peaks.

Name: Wirtshus zum Wyberg
Description: The restaurant on the first floor is a little more elegant and comfortable than the bar. The large menu ranges from a delicious veal schnitzel in morel sauce to the classic saddle of venison grand veneur, not to mention a popular lobster menu which includes home-made ravioli.

Name: Centrale
Description: Particularly renowned and popular with locals, this restaurant has a delightful family ambience. It offers delicious regional cuisine that can be enjoyed outdoors on the lovely terrace in fine weather.

Name: Braui
Description: Housed in the cultural centre that shares its name, braui serves good traditional cuisine in a pleasant, brasserie atmosphere. The menu is made up of seasonal dishes and includes classics such as beef tartare or veal cordon bleu. Smaller choice available at lunchtime. Tip: The public car park, Braui-Parkhaus, is handy.

Name: Adler
Description: The name of the game here is "Gasthaus at its best" – this applies to the cosy space, the cordial, attentive service, and chef Daniel Jann's cuisine. Whether you opt for Murmeltierpfeffer (marmot stew), Gitzi-Bratwurst (a goat meat and beef sausage) or asparagus dishes, meticulous craftsmanship and flavour are guaranteed. The focus lies squarely on the region. Eating here is fun! Stylish guestrooms are available for overnight stays.

Name: Bistro by Regina Montium
Description: Whether you hike up or take the mountain railway (ideal from Vitznau), it's well worth stopping off here. The location is idyllic – at 1 550m above sea level, the terrace is wonderful – and the "natural cuisine" is another big attraction! This includes smaller plates and regular dishes such as Rigi beef ragout or burger with Alpine cheese, many of which are made with produce from the immediate vicinity or grown in their own garden. Individual ingredients are explained in a friendly and competent manner. Why not try a gentian root tonic with Rigi juniper gin before dinner? Both the Bistro, for lunch, and fine dining restaurant, Regina Montium, for dinner, are located in Kräuterhotel Edelweiss, where you can stay overnight after your meal.

Name: Kaiserstock
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Credit cards not accepted,Great view,Terrace
Description: This charming establishment perched in a small mountain village is your reward after the narrow, steep drive up! The fact that the restaurant has many regular customers is of course mainly down to its tasty traditional cuisine. The dishes are prepared with flair from good, fresh produce from the region. Popular options include stews and ravioli. A four- to seven-course set menu is also available if you pre-book (two days in advance). Seasonal specialities such as venison and chamois or Metzgete (pork platter) are also worth considering. Tip: Soups, sausages, jams and other delicacies can be purchased to take home. There are pleasant rustic-style guestrooms for overnight stays. N.B. Cash only!

Name: Panorama - Bistro
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: This attractive alternative to the Cayenne offers excellent cuisine at a very reasonable price. Although the dishes are simpler in style, they are prepared with equal sophistication using quality regional produce, always with a certain modern twist. Attentive service, plus the same wine list as in the Cayenne. Wonderful views!

Name: Landgasthof Ochsen
Description: The food is terrific in this inn dating back to 1288 – the skilful chef clearly pours a lot of love into his cooking. As well as regional dishes and classics, Asian and Mediterranean influences also make their way onto the menu. A meal in their Gaststube is a somewhat simpler affair. There is a lovely terrace overlooking the pond, plus a charming smoking lounge. Pleasant and handy guestrooms.

Name: Chappeli
Description: In this pleasantly laid-back restaurant overlooking the village, the Hausmann/Köhli husband-and-wife team propose a really fun dining experience! The chef-patron cooks up delectable dishes that are delightfully down-to-earth: drawing inspiration from the region, they are big on flavour, with options including, for example, leek and bacon ravioli with fresh morels, or pork steak with Meaux mustard, mashed potatoes and vegetables. Nicely curated wine list and highly attentive service courtesy of the lady of the house, whose natural charm shines through. Be sure to bag a table on the delightfully verdant garden terrace!

Name: Gasthaus Schupfen
Description: With a history dating back to 1455, this lovely half-timbered house is really something special. In an inviting atmosphere, food is served in three charming rooms and on the idyllic terrace overlooking the Rhine. The menu features classics, including Kalbsgeschnetzeltes Zürcher Art (veal ragout), and seasonal dishes such as Kundelfinger trout with boiled potatoes and spinach. If you are looking for a good location for a wedding or event, the premises can also be rented out.

Name: Chez Philippe
Description: Philippe Chevrier from the Domaine de Châteauvieux is the brains behind this huge restaurant inspired by New York-style steakhouses. Relaxed atmosphere, meats sourced from the renowned Boucherie du Molard, fish caught by small-scale fishermen, dishes cooked over a wood fire, a truly authentic cheesecake and an expansive wine list. A real favourite!

Name: Bacchus Bistro & Genussmanufaktur
Description: You will feel right at home at this restaurant, thanks to the tasteful, upscale decor, friendly service and – last but not least – good-quality, fresh dishes cooked up by Werner Tobler. There are two set menus: "Du Terroir", comprising three to four courses, and four- to six-course "La Table chez Bacchus". Tip: Genussmanufaktur sells an appealing range of cheeses, spices, cakes, wines etc.

Name: Hardern Pintli
Description: This picture-perfect inn is warm and welcoming and certainly looks inviting with its red shutters. Chef-patron Falk Fleischhauer achieves a fine balance between traditional fare and classic cuisine, resulting in delicious dishes that are reasonably priced. Both tripe and sole are to be found on the menu. The service is very friendly and anything but stuffy. In summer, the lovely terrace with its trees is very inviting.

Name: Auberge Communale
Description: This rather inconspicuous Auberge is located in a small village set slightly above Vevey. Run by the Konrad family, it not only has guestrooms for overnight stays, but also serves really good food! Whether eating in the refined modern space or on the pretty terrace, choose between delicious bistro dishes and the "Gastro" set menu. It is always tasty and prices remain very competitive.

Name: Bären
Description: At this rather grand establishment with two dining spaces, Gaststube and GnussStube, the wide-ranging menu includes simpler dishes and more sophisticated fare, plus vegetarian options. You can dine à la carte or opt for a set menu – the fine-dining set menu ("MundArt"), has to be ordered in advance. At lunchtime, a reduced à la carte selection and daily specials are available. Ingredients are sourced as locally as possible. There is a decent wine list with a focus on Swiss labels. The waitstaff are friendly, attentive and well trained.

Name: The Mansard Restaurant
Description: Located on the ground floor of boutique hotel Miiro The Mansard, this restaurant has a modern and elegant brasserie-style interior with an Alpine feel. There is a terrace with a few tables out on the pavement – this is a place to see and be seen. Martin Bieri is in charge of the hotel, restaurant and kitchen. Using top-notch ingredients, many of them Swiss, he and his team cook up flavoursome international cuisine to be ordered à la carte. The menu includes dishes such as Lauenen dried meat with Gstaad mountain cheese, and Balfego tuna carpaccio with a sesame marinade. You can also look forward to a well-curated wine list and friendly service. Tip: For a cool rooftop bar experience with stunning views, head to the bar The Mansard Rooftop on the fourth floor, which serves drinks, cocktails and a small selection of snacks. Thanks to its central location close to the Gstaad Promenade, the hotel is also an ideal starting point for a stroll around the shops.

Name: Là-Haut
Description: Julien and Morgane Ostertag's winning combination of good produce and no-frills, expressive, gourmet dishes creates a moment of indulgence, enhanced by the view over the lake. From the terrace or behind the bay windows of the elegantly decorated dining room, bistronomy is at the heart of the chef's offering: Valentin Chappuis' caramelised pork belly, patatas bravas and crispy sucrine; Mediterranean-style scorpion fish, taggiasche olives, tomato marmalade with basil and panisse. The service is friendly and charming. Don't hesitate to head upstairs!

Name: Schüpbärg-Beizli
Description: This restaurant is quite out of the way, but it's worth the journey here to this remote location, where a cosy, rustic-style interior awaits diners, as well as a lovely terrace, which is very popular in summer! But let's not forget the cooking of owner Christoph Hunziker: he prepares home-style Swiss dishes with a modern twist, stamped with his own ideas. In addition to this, you can expect charming service – sometimes the chefs, too, come to the tables.

Name: Colani Bistrot
Description: Located just off the reception area of the tasteful and well-appointed Hotel Colani, Colani Bistrot is the alternative to the fine dining restaurant. The food served here – Mediterranean cuisine with a local twist. We can certainly recommend the "Ravioli of the Day". Meat eaters should ask about the main dish centred on venison or veal – showcasing a different cut every day. Friendly service, a laid-back atmosphere and modern interior design featuring light wood and a whole host of decorative details.

Name: SUAHOY
Description: It quickly becomes clear that this friendly, buzzy venue is not your average Thai eatery. Everything is made fresh, the ingredients are good quality, and the flavours are well rounded and pack a punch – everything you could ask for from this type of cuisine. Cordial staff. In summer, a small terrace is laid out in front of the door. A word to the wise: booking is essential, even at lunchtime!

Name: Le Café Valrose
Address: Place de la Gare 2, Rougemont, 1659, Switzerland
Description: Part of the same establishment as La Table de Valrose, this bistro has a comfortable rustic-style Alpine atmosphere, both outside, on the terrace shaded by chestnut trees, surrounded by mountains, and inside, by the fireplace, in the wood-panelled space. Relax in the lounge bar with a coffee or cocktail in hand. The menu features tasty seasonal fare in the form of simple dishes, while classics such as Valrose fondue (champagne version available), malakoffs and Valrose burgers (meat or veggie) are permanent fixtures on the menu. The dessert trolley is available all afternoon, for teatime.

Name: Grotto Valmaggese
Description: Situated in an excellent location slightly above the road, this traditional grotto-style restaurant with a large car park is quiet and cool in summer, with a dining room warmed by a fireplace in winter. In this delightful location, enjoy classic, well-prepared and generous cuisine with personal touches made using top-quality, seasonally inspired ingredients. Make sure you try the venison tartare with marrow gratin and pear jelly, as well as the delicious artisanal ice creams. The highly welcoming and attentive service is clearly in evidence in the dining room.

Name: Barranco
Description: Eat, drink, make merry, meet friends… the Kreis 4 district is to Zurich what the Barranco district is to Lima. Nestled among a host of other restaurants and bars, the Peruvian neighbourhood's namesake serves modern Peruvian cuisine that is bursting with flavour, zing and spices. The dishes are designed to be shared and tasted together. The atmosphere is pleasingly unpretentious in this inviting space with a trendy decor featuring Peruvian murals – the relaxed yet efficient service is the icing on the cake. Great cocktail selection. There is a terrace in front of the building, separated from the pavement by plants.

Name: Myò Sushi Bar
Description: Set in the Esplanade de Montbenon park, opposite the courthouse, this Japanese restaurant will win you over with its peaceful setting and quality cuisine. In summer, the terrace boasts a breathtaking view of the lake. Comfortably perched on a high stool, you can savour a variety of authentic Japanese dishes, including delicate sushi, tasty teppanyaki, beef tartare with wasabi, and a refined take on soba noodles. This is a popular place, so booking your spot at the counter is strongly advised.

Name: Gaijin Izakaya
Description: This place with a name that translates as "foreigner bar" is a really cool spot that follows the style of Japanese izakayas (casual bars that also serve food). A team led by chef-patron Daniel Shu, who trained in Chicago and New York, and his business partner bring you delicious contemporary Asian soul food. There is a reduced menu at lunchtime. Expect creative cooking such as their spicy Korean pork belly: thin, slightly crispy slices of pork belly marinated in a spicy sweet and sour sauce and accompanied by a beautifully soft egg cooked sous vide and placed on sesame rice. The atmosphere is relaxed, with modern music playing in the background.

Name: Le Bistro by Décotterd
Description: Like its fine dining counterpart, Le Bistro also promises diners a stunning view! In this worthy alternative with a modern interior, the food is simpler, but absolutely the equal in terms of taste and culinary know-how. Be sure to try the pâté en croûte or tarte au chocolat!

Name: Flamel
Description: Housed in the historic, recently renovated LUGANODANTE hotel, this restaurant serves excellent contemporary cuisine, with a simple menu at lunchtime and more elaborate fare in the evenings (tasting menus and à la carte), including carefully selected Swiss meat, herbs and salads from their own organic kitchen garden. There’s also a mixology bar which, in addition to unique cocktails (made from their own home-grown or locally sourced ingredients), offers an array of beers, fruit juices and home-made chocolates.

Name: au violon
Description: This place exudes brasserie appeal thanks to its charming, stylish atmosphere and unfussy, honest seasonal menu, which also includes classic dishes. Despite its proximity to the centre, the location is pleasantly quiet – outside, an attractive terrace with shady trees beckons. There are well-kept guestrooms for overnight stays. Tip: Take the opportunity to visit Basel Historical Museum opposite.

Name: Le Restaurant
Description: The stylish restaurant of the tasteful and historical La Couronne hotel not only has a unique atmosphere but also promises exquisite French and Swiss-inspired cuisine served by a friendly and attentive front-of-house team. The location in the old town, nestled beside Kathedrale St Ursen, is a draw in itself; the terrace in front of the hotel makes for a delightful spot in which to "see and be seen" – especially during a romantic sunset. The wine list comprises some 150 moderately priced labels and includes a decent selection of half bottles. The fantastic wine bar is ideal for a nightcap. Smaller lunchtime menu. Tip: Complement your culinary adventure with a leisurely stroll between Baseltor and Bieltor.

Name: Albrun
Description: The journey up to this enchanting mountain village is something of an adventure, but the food makes it worth it! In a rustic chalet-style setting, diners tuck into flavoursome regional dishes prepared with seasonal produce – the chef is always happy to showcase Swiss ingredients. The menu features mouthwatering options such as "Mario's Signature Black Forest" (beef sirloin, sour cherries, cocoa, kirsch 40% volume) and the "Alpen Tapas" starter. Friendly and charming front-of-house team.

Name: Nest- und Bietschhorn
Description: This cosy rustic restaurant enjoys a wonderful location at 1 490m above sea level. It is housed in the Lötschental's oldest hotel, which opened in 1868 (the modern Alpine-style guestrooms are gorgeous!) and serves exceptionally good food. The dishes are prepared with regional and seasonal ingredients. Tip: leave some room for one of the fabulous desserts! To accompany your meal, there are Valais wines. Overlooking the valley and mountains, the delightful lounge and terrace area is adorned with flowers and herbs. Shorter menu served 2-5pm.

Name: La Bottega di Mario
Description: Housed in a historical building (1913), La Bottega is a wonderfully inviting and lively ristorante and salumeria under one roof. Guests are spoilt for choice between the tasty dishes, clearly influenced by Ticino tradition, and the superb selection of salami and ham at the counter – here, the friendly mastri salumieri serve up the cold cuts. Tip: Try the house wine, Merlot di Ticino, poured from a six-litre bottle!

Name: Brasserie Le Gogant
Address: Route de France 8, Le Brassus, 1348, Switzerland
Description: Both this restaurant and the designer Hôtel des Horlogers in which it is housed exude a stylish and upscale ambiance. A feast for the eyes awaits: aside from the elegant interior design, guests can relish the panoramic vistas of nature through expansive floor-to-ceiling windows, or opt to observe the captivating culinary artistry in the kitchen, visible through a generously sized glass pane. The seasonal dishes harmoniously blend classical and traditional flavours (with rich stocks and delectable sauces), presented in a contemporary fashion. The aesthetics and impeccable quality of these creations seamlessly complement the overall setting.

Name: Auberge Communale Le Mont
Address: Place du Petit Mont 4, Le Mont-sur-Lausanne, 1052, Switzerland
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Burgundy ham terrine, gherkin and fresh herb condiment; Jorat veal belly, pistachios and green asparagus: the Burgundian chef and Meilleur Ouvrier de France definitely knows his stuff. This is a fine dining version of modern French cuisine that highlights local and fresh ingredients and showcases small-scale producers. He successfully pulls it off, and keeps it affordable. Fine selection of wines by the glass.

Name: Muntanella
Description: The restaurant in the long-established Arosa Kulm Hotel, not far from the ski slopes, has adopted a dual concept: a simpler lunch menu featuring rösti, pasta, burgers etc, and a more ambitious menu in the evening. High-quality regional ingredients such as Grisons lamb or Val Lumnezia Alpine char take centre stage. The glass-walled walk-in wine cabinet is quite something. The terrace is a delightful spot from which to take in the mountain scenery.

Name: Alpenblick
Description: The Anderhalden family have remodelled this inn set in a rather remote location. Diners now take their seats in the restaurant-cum-parlour – the lounge area with its fireplace is ideal for an aperitif – or in the cosy Stübli with its beautiful wooden floor and elegant table settings. The chef-patron cooks up flavourful seasonal dishes; service comes courtesy of the attentive lady of the house, who is always on hand.

Name: Philipp Blaser
Description: A popular place to eat! In this modern interior, where a relaxed atmosphere reigns, diners tuck into tasty and pleasingly unpretentious dishes. The culinary offering here features not only traditional and regional cuisine, but also Asian specialities – see the options in the "Thai Corner" section of the menu. There is also a pleasant terrace, and the small adjoining Hotel National has spruce, trendy guestrooms.

Name: Les Curiades
Description: A truly historic restaurant which has been serving food since 1850. The present chef has experience in some of the finest restaurants, and it shows! His cuisine is elegant and refined, including dishes such as chuck beef braised in beer (paying tribute to the chef’s Belgian origins) and a delicious vegetarian menu which is always available. An unqualified success!

Name: D'Chuchi
Description: This small restaurant in a side street in the old town has a charming, down-to-earth and almost intimate atmosphere. It also serves really good food, which owner Jan Schmidlin creates by drawing almost exclusively on regional produce. Shining examples of his delicious modern seasonal fare include veal – saddle, Bäggli, Schupfnudeln (potato dumplings), lettuce, tarragon. There is a four-course set menu and an à la carte selection of dishes. You can also look forward to extremely pleasant, cordial hospitality.

Name: La Trattoria
Description: In the charming Hotel Walther, one of Pontresina's most emblematic hotels, this lovely Trattoria has an authentic, lively atmosphere and a stylish rustic feel. The appetising menu embraces all regions of Italy, with delicious pasta as the centrepiece and the focus firmly on flavour and freshness. Friendly Italian service and a good selection of wines.

Name: Anker
Description: On the first floor, wood panelling and low ceilings provide a cosy setting in which to choose the appealing mix of traditional and international dishes on the menu. The calves’ liver with sage, onions and rösti, for example, is delicious. A significant amount of the restaurant’s meat comes from its own butchery.

Name: Bauernschänke
Description: This gem of a restaurant is somewhat tucked away in a narrow alley in the city centre. In a historical setting with a cosy, rustic feel, diners tuck into international dishes such as king mackerel with radicchio tardivo, coconut and calamansi, as well as regional specialities such as pork belly gröstel (a traditional Tyrolean potato-based fry-up) with cucumber and butterhead lettuce. Order dishes to share à la carte or take a punt on the five-course surprise menu. The staff will be happy to provide wine recommendations. The well-curated selection is international and includes a decent range of natural wines (unfiltered and sulfite-free). Options are somewhat reduced at lunchtime.

Name: Golden Dragon
Description: Davos's restaurant scene is not only about regional food – the Chinese restaurant at the Grischa hotel serves Cantonese and Szechuan-style cuisine. Tip: Some dishes are designed for sharing. If you fancy the Peking duck for two, be sure to pre-order (at least 48hr in advance). You can also combine many of the ingredients yourself according to your preferences. The upscale design features wood, stone, leather and a palette of elegant dark shades for a lovely ambience.

Name: Stiva Grischuna
Description: In this traditional Bündnerhaus dating back over 300 years, the wood-panelled rooms abound with charm, and the down-to-earth cooking looks to the region for inspiration. Whether traditional dishes such as capuns and maluns or classics such as "Norbert's Stroganoff" and cordon bleu – this is simply tasty fare! The prices are also very reasonable. It's best to book. Locals also dine here.

Name: Didi's Frieden
Description: A fun dining experience is guaranteed at this delightful restaurant with its inviting decor – the wine glass chandeliers are certainly original! In the evening, there is a set menu comprising three, four or five courses. For each course, you have delicious options such as sea bass fillet on spaghetti alla chitarra with summer vegetables and octopus in a saffron sauce. There is a daily set menu at lunchtime, plus a nicely curated wine list. In summer, the gorgeous spacious terrace beckons.

Name: Café de Riex
Address: Route de la Corniche 24, Riex, 1097, Switzerland
Description: Artisanal seasonal cuisine that showcases small-scale producers and local artisans, featuring hearty meat dishes (pork belly, kidneys, sweetbreads), sauces with real flavour, and delicious home-made ice creams flavoured with herbs from the garden (savory, sage, rosemary). Guests are in for a real treat in this café in the Vaud! The wine list is just as tempting, and features wines produced here in Riex.

Name: Gasthof zur Sonne
Description: This 500-year-old heritage-protected inn is run by Patricia and Cäsar Meyer, who represent the second generation of their family here. He has a penchant for fish caught in Lake Zurich, just a stone's throw away – you can't get any fresher or more regional than that! The menu includes some truly rare specialities such as fried livers of fish from Lake Zurich. This attachment to regional produce is, not least, indicative of a commitment to sustainability. The cosy, very well-kept dining rooms are on the first floor, along with the gorgeous balcony terrace, which affords an unobstructed view of the lake. The staff are very attentive and cordial – you're sure to want to come back! Comfortable guestrooms.

Name: Eintracht
Description: In this restaurant dating back to 1870, the dedicated Meier family have cultivated a sense of tradition while also introducing modern influences. This approach makes itself felt in the bistro and the more elegant restaurant area as well as in the cuisine – from classics such as veal cordon bleu to a gourmet set menu composed of three to five courses. Excellent wine selection. Simple daily specials are also available in the bistro.

Name: Zum Pflugstein
Description: Considered the largest erratic boulder in the canton of Zurich, the Pﬂugstein is located close to this distinguished vineyard farmhouse and lends its name to its fabulous restaurant. The interior comprises an attractive wood-panelled space and a room with a fireplace, while outside there is a truly idyllic terrace. The service team overseen by the charming Jeannine Meili also deserves a mention. Tip: Try the tender boiled beef!

Name: Candela
Description: This pleasantly lively place is located right in the city centre. With high ceilings, dark wood panelling, exposed brickwork and large windows, the restaurant is really atmospheric. As well as Swiss classics, the menu includes Mediterranean fare. There is also a decent selection of vegetarian and vegan dishes. Tip: Take the time to peruse the digestif list.

Name: Alla Cantina
Description: Although all the staff at this beautiful historic restaurant on the village square hail from Sicily, they have been working in Switzerland for years. Here, authentic Sicilian cuisine is served in a rustic and welcoming setting that also provides the backdrop for regular music events: the only concessions to Ticino are the polenta-based dishes. Our inspector particularly recommends the sarde in “Beccafico”(stuffed sardine roulade with breadcrumbs, sultanas, pine nuts and orange peel). There’s also a pleasantly cool and tranquil outdoor space for summer dining, plus four attractive and inviting guestrooms on the top floor.

Name: Buech
Description: An absolutely delightful place: an idyllic location overlooking the village and Lake Zurich, a stylish dining area exuding traditional charm, a uniquely beautiful vine-kissed terrace affording stunning views! The few seats in the "wine huts" are much coveted. In the kitchen, the emphasis is on select produce from the region.

Name: Casa Caminada
Description: This restaurant enjoys a lovely quiet location in the castle grounds. Inside the bright, high-ceilinged space, modern design meets warm wood; outside, there is a delightful terrace. A charming team provides competent service. They serve regional cuisine, in which seasonal ingredients sourced from select local producers go into extremely flavoursome dishes – the produce steals the show! Andreas Caminada's take on Grisons classics can also be found on the menu. Be sure to try his quark bizochels, for example. Tip: You can buy bread baked in the on-site bakery and other goods in their shop next door.

Name: Netts Schützengarten
Address: Sankt Jakob Strasse 35, Sankt Gallen, 9000, Switzerland
Description: Housed in the Schützengarten Brewery building, this trendy restaurant is popular, not least among the locals! The decor here is lovely – rather rustic at the front, more elegant in the area to the rear. The terrace and beer garden are delightfully secluded – the brewing happens next door, so you're often greeted by pleasant malty aroma. Along with Swiss classics such as Züricher Geschnetzeltes (sliced veal served in a cream and mushroom sauce) or beef Stroganoff, the menu includes Asian-inspired dishes and vegetarian options. Tip: In the courtyard, the brewery has a small bottle museum – well worth a short detour.

Name: Zer Schlucht
Description: This place boasts a fantastic location right next to the rugged and dramatic Saas-Fee gorge, through which the Feeru Vispa glacial stream flows. Hotel La Gorge offers comfortable, modern accommodation and a delightful dining experience at its restaurant, Zer Schlucht, serving regional and seasonal cuisine in a charming Alpine setting. The mouthwatering options on the menu include classics such as ossobuco, specialties such as Thurgau apple-pomace fed pork with apricot, chanterelles, rosemary and spaetzle, as well as vegan dishes such as gnocchi, mushrooms, chard and pine nuts. Request a table by the floor-to-ceiling windows for stunning views of the gorge and forest. Shorter menu available at lunchtime.

Name: Le Bologne
Description: Next to the Fine Arts School, this vintage bistro cuts a fine figure with its cement tiles, hanging globe lights and bare bulbs, as well as its bar, banquettes and bistro chairs. The dishes feature high-quality, carefully prepared seasonal ingredients: celeriac "risotto" and foie gras, confit lamb shoulder, cumin, asparagus and labne...

Name: Café du Levant
Address: Rue du Vieux Four 53, Aire-la-Ville, 1288, Switzerland
Description: In a quiet little village in an attractive rural setting, you will find this warm and welcoming restaurant with a down-to-earth vibe. The property backs onto fields and the fresh air is a real tonic. They serve flavoursome seasonal cuisine and regional French fare, which you can accompany with your choice from a good selection of wines from the Geneva region. Lovely terrace.

Name: Pensiun Aldier
Description: If you like your food straightforward and pared down to the essentials without compromising on taste, then you'll love the excellent Engadine cuisine here. In the pleasingly unpretentious restaurant of the charming little hotel of the same name, the dishes forgo any frills and instead focus on select, fresh local produce. Good wines at fair prices. Shorter menu at lunchtime.

Name: SALZHAUS
Description: An attractive blend of urban cool and historical ambiance is the backdrop here and the exposed old brickwork certainly adds to the effect! On regular evenings, the kitchen serves up regionally inspired dishes with an international twist, either as a set menu or à la carte. The chicken cordon bleu with ham, Gruyère, Schupfnudeln (finger-shaped potato dumplings) and spring vegetables is an especially delicious example. Thursday evenings are dedicated to Japanese fusion cuisine. More limited options at lunchtime. Attentive, charming and adept service. Thanks to the beautiful old town location right by the Aare River, tables on the waterfront terrace are coveted in summer.

Name: Gommerstuba
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: The friendly hosts here serve contemporary cuisine, which can be ordered à carte or as a set menu – there is also a vegetarian set menu. Many regional wines are featured. A restaurant decor blending wood and stone makes for a pleasant atmosphere. The lovely terrace is also inviting!

Name: Bären
Description: Diners come here for straightforward seasonal cuisine that is not only prepared with fresh produce but, most importantly, is utterly delicious. In the evening, you can opt for the set menu, which comprises three to six courses, or order à la carte. At lunchtime, the options are more limited, with the three- to four-course "Gourmet Express" set menu, and an à la carte selection. The house specialty is Parmesan cheese wheel spaghetti. The lovingly decorated Gourmetstübli is a particularly appealing space. There is also an attractive room for events.

Name: Osteria della Bottega
Description: This lively restaurant is located on a steep little street in Geneva's old town. Against a chic industrial-style backdrop with an open kitchen, diners are treated to modern, seasonally inspired Italian cuisine and fine wines, plus attentive and friendly service. It's best to book, as Osteria is very popular! Across the street there is a lovely terrace.

Name: Collonge Café
Description: This modern restaurant boasts a great location next to the historical town hall and has a charming terrace laid out in the garden. The seasonally inspired menu successfully brings together modern Italian and French cuisine, while keeping an open mind when it comes to international influences. Cordial and competent service. Tip: the competitively priced lunch menu.

Name: Rigiblick Züriberg Beiz
Description: In this restaurant in the upper reaches of the city, a rather elegant yet relaxed atmosphere awaits you. The kitchen team showcases in-season regional produce, which is used to create really delicious dishes. You can order à la carte or opt for the "Genuss Menü" comprising three or four courses. Maître d' and owner Vreni Giger provides service with a personal touch. In summer, head for the leafy terrace. Tip: It is easy to get here by taking tram no 10 or the Funicular Rigiblick.

Name: Zum Kaiser Franz
Description: Here, you won't want to miss out on the Austrian specialities such as Backhenderl (breaded fried chicken), Tafelspitz (prime boiled beef) or Topfenknödel (curd dumplings)! Available in a large or small portion, the Wiener schnitzel is a real highlight. Be sure to ask about the fish of the day, freshly caught from the adjacent Lake Zug. As well as the good food, diners can look forward to professional and attentive service in a cosy and stylish setting – the Austrian charm of the decor is the perfect match for the cuisine. The lakeside location provides a lovely backdrop. The nearby multi-storey car park is handy.

Name: Café de Peney
Description: Located on an arm of the River Rhône, this popular, bustling eatery, decked out in a profusion of nostalgic paraphernalia, calls to mind a vintage picture postcard and also boasts a wisteria-covered terrace. Fine ingredients are consummately and delicately crafted into delicious dishes, examples of which are the flawlessly cooked Black Angus steak or raspberry tartlet with a refreshing raspberry sorbet.

Name: Linde
Description: The secret of Linde's success is a formula of classic Swiss cuisine made from good ingredients coupled with reasonable prices. A lively atmosphere reigns in this attractive, well-run place with its various dining spaces, large bar area and glassed-in kitchen. Steak tartare and Zürcher Geschnetzeltes (veal) are among the permanent fixtures on the menu. For lunch, the offer is somewhat reduced. The wonderful terrace comes into its own in summer, and there are well-kept guestrooms too.

Name: Balm - Bistro
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: The charming and laid-back second restaurant at Hotel Balm also serves ambitious cuisine. This can be enjoyed in the form of a set menu of three or four courses which you can mix and match as you see fit. Options include dishes such as Lake Lucerne whitefish fillet with a champagne sauce, morels, leaf spinach and new potatoes. It is also possible to dine à la carte. At lunchtime on Wednesday to Friday, the moderately priced two-course set menu draws a crowd. The terrace is a delightful spot.

Name: Mont-Rouge
Address: Route de la Télécabine 23, Haute-Nendaz, 1997, Switzerland
Description: The standout features of this mountain-style restaurant are its pleasant, elegant atmosphere and its chef, who has been dedicated to his work here for 20 years. He invites you on a culinary journey, with Swiss, French and international dishes inspired by local produce. Another option is the small adjoining brasserie and its daily specials, including poached sole roulade with home-made sauerkraut and champagne beurre blanc… a real treat! Pleasant guestrooms available.

Name: Dal Mulin
Address: Plazza dal Mulin 4, Saint Moritz, 7500, Switzerland
Description: This restaurant in the heart of St Moritz makes diners feel very much at home with its wonderfully stylish and modern take on rustic decor and its charming and attentive front-of-house team. As for the food, it is pleasingly uncomplicated, yet carefully considered and subtle. The wine selection is outstanding – and they even have their own wine shop.

Name: Josef
Description: This trendy, urban restaurant and bar is located in the middle of a residential area in Kreis 5 (Zürich's fifth district). The atmosphere is lively and bustling, and in light of their interesting concept, it comes as no surprise that the place is well frequented: they serve tasty modern European cuisine with dishes in starter-sized portions (four is a good number to order). Mouthwatering options include the likes of veal shank ragout with mashed potatoes, confit garlic and Trevisano. Alternatively, there is a five-course set menu – available in omnivore and vegetarian versions. Good wine list and cocktail selection.

Name: Gasthof zum goldenen Kreuz
Description: This restaurant is steeped in tradition, and much sought after for its excellent seasonal cuisine. At lunchtime, you can order à la carte or opt for one of four three-course set menus. In the evening, there is a tasting menu in addition to an à la carte selection. Attentive service comes courtesy of a friendly and well-organised front-of-house team. Goethe himself was a guest here – the pretty Goethe-Stübli is named after him – and the well-preserved, painted panelling from the 17C adds rustic charm. The terrace is a delightful spot, secluded from the street by abundant greenery. Modern, functional guestrooms are available for overnight stays. Tip for motorists: public car park behind the building.

Name: Les six
Description: The chef mixes his own sensibilities into cuisine rooted in French bistro fare. The blackboard menu is a medley of authentic dishes and à la carte items made with seasonal ingredients. Generally, an appetiser and a main course is the perfect amount, but some items can be ordered as half portions, so ask your server.

Name: Ma Poule
Description: The chef opened a small restaurant, Ma Poule to celebrate the appeal of Jura, in eastern France. This region, with its beautiful forests, valleys and wetlands and its wonderful ingredients and people, made a profound impression on the chef. Chicken and morels in sauce vin jaune is a Jura dish in which the chef takes great pride. This dish is paired with specially produced yellow wine. The façade and interior, and even proprietress’s clothing, are yellow as well. A restaurant filled with love of Jura.

Name: BRASSERIE POISSON ROUGE
Description: The draw is the generosity of the portions served throughout, from appetiser to dessert. The menu is a tour of France’s regions, with regional favourites including salad Niçoise, fish purée soup and cassoulet de Toulouse. Roast lamb or duck smothered in sauce is a fulfilling meal. Each plateful expresses the chef’s simple message: French cuisine satisfying to both belly and soul. Wine makes the perfect companion.

Name: Fry-ya
Description: Tonkatsu, seafood, vegetables—select the ingredients of your choice and the kitchen will prepare an original ‘mix fry’ just for you. As the name says, this is the ‘fry house’. Daytime fare consists of set meals of a variety of items. In the evening, multi-course prix fixe is the theme, with each morsel fried and served fresh. In a couple of unique twists, different types of breadcrumbs are used, depending on the main ingredient, and some items are fried in lard while others are fried in sesame oil. Chicken tenderloin is fried at a low heat carefully calculated to cook every part of the meat.

Name: le bistrot des bleus
Address: 2F, EAT PLAY WORKS, 5-4-16 Hiro, Shibuya-ku, Tokyo, 150-0012, Japan
Description: The ‘blue’ of this ‘bistro of the blues’ refers to the blue in the French flag, which represents liberty. The young chef and sommelier enthusiastically pour out their passion for French cuisine. Home cooking from throughout France, such as choucroute and bouillabaisse, are available à la carte.  Doors open at 3pm. Its location in a narrow restaurant row and the casual atmosphere within capture the bistro’s spirit of freedom.

Name: Japanese Ramen Gokan
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining,Credit cards not accepted
Description: ‘Japanese ramen’ was added to the name from a desire to spread Japan’s culinary culture to the world. As befits the name, the shop specialises in domestic ingredients. It serves two flavours of ramen: soy sauce and salt. The soup layers multiple sources of flavour on top of each other: free-range chicken, Berkshire pork, clams and mussels. Cooking over charcoal introduces a Japanese element. The food looks great, the aroma whets the appetite, the flavour captivates: this ramen sets all five senses tingling.

Name: Pot-Bouille
Description: The softly lit counter creates a stylish mood conducive to gatherings of friends. French favourites such as rillettes and ratatouille share the menu with international items like tripe, shrimp spring rolls and tom yam goong ramen, stoking the imagination. The restaurant’s name is French for ‘hodgepodge’, an apt metaphor for Pot-Bouille’s medley of gastronomic influences, somehow in perfect harmony. A free-spirited style all its own.

Name: YAKUMO
Description: Customers flock to Yakumo for its famous wonton ramen. Two types of wonton, one with pork infused with the tang of ginger and the other with shrimp cooked to delightful texture, each play their part in the dish’s popularity. To enjoy both, order the special ‘Tokusei’ ramen. The choice of soups is ‘White dashi’ made with white soy sauce, ‘Black dashi’ using rich, dark soy sauce, and ‘Mix’, a mixture of the two. And choose from thin noodles or flat. This flexibility to tailor your order is a special pleasure of Yakumo.

Name: Sushidokoro Shigeru
Description: With his restaurant, the chef depicts a local unassuming sushi shop. The small counter fosters an air of kinship, as does the friendly service. His conviction shows in the meticulous care he pours into each item. Dishes are not only salted, marinated and simmered, they are prepared with knife techniques so practiced as to seem effortless, then formed by hand to finish. An omakase set menu with snacks is on offer, but the focus here is on nigiri sushi, what a sushi shop originally was.

Name: Hatsuogawa
Description: Founded in 1907, this restaurant is run by the proprietress and her son. Though the building is new, the interior exudes the same charm diners have loved for decades, parlaying an unchanging old-school elegance to a new generation. Unagi is prepared in the old style, time-consuming in its attention to detail but well worth the wait. Side dishes such as steamed egg custard and soft-boiled soybeans help pass the time until the eel is ready.

Name: ROZZO SICILIA
Description: A Sicilian eatery run by a chef and waiter who struck up a friendship during the former’s apprenticeship. Enveloped in the sunny mood of southern Italy, guests delight in the cuisine of Chef Nakamura and the service of the host, Abe. With fried chickpeas, seafood couscous and cannoli of local confectionaries, the duo serve up authentic flavours of Sicily in a simple, honest way. The ever-present lemon wedges on the table are a nice Sicilian touch.

Name: Tonkatsu Nanaido
Description: To order, you buy a ticket from a dispensing machine, each button listing a different brand of pork. Knowing the owner-chef is a yakitori craftsman, however, means chicken cutlet is also tempting. Note the attention to detail: the thick-cut pork loin is thin only at the ends because it’s full of fat and fibre there; rice cooked in an earthenware pot is transferred to a wooden tub to control its moisture content. Care is also taken with the plates and bowls, with antique Imari porcelain adding a note of elegance.

Name: Tempura Kakiage Yukimura
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining,Credit cards not accepted
Description: ‘Cheerful, fun, exciting’ sums up the credo of the owner-chef. The convivial atmosphere and friendly service attracts customers of every generation. The menu reflects this positive attitude, with bowls of rice with toppings, teishoku set meals and à la carte items available at both lunch and dinner. The dish of fame is the kakiage-don, a bowl of rice loaded up with shrimp. The chef treasures the advice he learned as an apprentice: ‘Offer top-rate food at third-rate prices’. He’s always smiling, trading jokes with his guests.

Name: Osobano Kouga
Description: Taste sake and snacks while dining on soba. Think of the culture of the soba shop, the beloved essence of Edo popular culture, plunked down near Nishi-Azabu Intersection for the modern generation to enjoy, and you have the atmosphere of Osobano Kouga. Evenings bring prix fixe presentations that encourage you to linger over cups of sake. Tensui, tempura soba with the soba removed, is an old-timey snack. Soba in season and appetisers of vegetable or fish of the day are a delight.

Name: Watabe
Description: Watabe was formerly a trader in river fish and shellfish; the third-generation owners are brothers who turned it into an eel restaurant. New touches are added to traditional dishes, like steaming unagi with tea leaves to produce a tender texture. Opposite from Watabe is Genkakuji Temple, famed for a legend about the god Enma. In tribute, Watabe offers ‘Enmaju’, a multi-tiered food box containing both shirayaki, or eel grilled without seasoning, and kabayaki, or eel dipped and broiled in sweet sauce.

Name: Kinoshita
Description: Jellied pork, soupe de poisson, beef simmered in red wine – filled with respect for classic French cuisine, the chef is keen to serve dishes that warm the soul. The style is universal yet prepared with a unique touch, honed by constant improvement. A collection of Bourgogne wines that have aged along with the restaurant await the discerning tippler.

Name: Tachigui Sushi Tonari
Description: Sushi Tonari means ‘sushi next door’, and indeed Tachigui Sushi Tonari is tucked away next to its flagship restaurant. The intimate space, quick turnover and experience of the youthful staff achieve a comfortable informality. Ordering is refreshingly casual, too: requesting one piece at a time is fine. The prevailing theme is ‘vinegar and sushi’. Rice seasoned with rice vinegar harmonises beautifully with the oil of the fish. Reservations, orders and billing are all managed on a digital system. Standing and eating, Edo’s street-stall dining culture, updated for the modern era.

Name: L'AMITIE
Description: Apprenticing at a bistro in Paris, the chef was captivated by its lively energy. At L'AMITIE, he has put down roots in Takadanobaba with this intimate diner where you can feel like part of the daily life of France. Offerings include meat terrine À la campagne, cassoulet and beef cheek simmered in red wine. À la carte items are prepared for two, so you can enjoy sharing. Savour Gallic culinary culture and the ambience of the French countryside.

Name: REI
Description: The name REI comes from reimeiki, ‘a new beginning’. The décor is monotone, the food pairing is wine, the fare is modern Chinese. The familiar standards of Chinese dining are on the menu, including Sichuan-style bean curd, steamed chicken with spicy sauce and stir-fried shrimp in chilli sauce. The chef deftly matches home-style seasonings with seasonal ingredients. This is neighbourhood Chinese food refined with a distinctive inspiration, such as twice-cooked pork with spring cabbage, and sweet-and-sour pork.

Name: Edosoba Hosokawa
Description: The chef tours the regions in search of the highest-quality buckwheat and kneads his noodles with reverence to the producers he has used for years. You can compare buckwheat from different regions, tasting the unique character the terroir imparts. The spring ‘Wakatake’ with bamboo shoots and wakame is fragrant with the aroma of young pepper leaves; in summer, ‘Hiyakaki’ includes the luxury of large oysters. Tasting the soba of each season is one of the pleasures of eating here. The mood of the restaurant and the charm of the dining vessels are part of the flavour.

Name: Le cabaret
Description: The restaurant’s name evokes a French nightclub with a stage. Service is informal and relaxed: as music plays in the background, the staff greet customers in their everyday clothes. Dishes are served in traditional style, with each table sharing a single plate. With the feel of a Parisian bistro, this was also the place that first started serving natural wine. With an atmosphere that says ‘café’ and cuisine that says ‘bistro’, the fun of the cabaret never changes.

Name: Ma Cuisine
Description: The chef’s dedication to strong relationships with producers around the country stems from his choice of ingredients. His talents are on full display in bistro fare such as ratatouille and bouillabaisse. An abundance of à la carte items makes choosing part of the fun. Pork preparation is tailored to the characteristics of each cut. Charcuterie, petit salé of boneless rib, and spareribs grilled smothered in herb-seasoned breadcrumbs are all highlights.

Name: Le Monde Gourmand
Description: A chef with passion for his culinary art and a proprietress schooled in the ways of graceful service enfold this French restaurant in a warm atmosphere of bustling activity. Dishes listed on the blackboard are orthodox: pâté en croûte, baked fish in pastry, beef cheek stewed in red wine. The restaurant’s name means ‘the world of the aficionado of food’. The world of the good old bistro lures us in.

Name: Les Copains de DOMINIQUE BOUCHET
Description: A bistro by Dominique Bouchet. The theme is ‘bistronomy’: a bistro with added gastronomic enhancements. Favourites such as pâté en croûte and steak frites are everyday standards in France. Lobster macaroni is a Bouchet speciality that captures the hearts of Parisian epicures. Savour the profundity of French cuisine from popular fare to modern haute cuisine.

Name: Mejiro Shunkotei
Address: 2F, Trad Mejiro, 2-39-1 Mejiro, Toshima-ku, Tokyo, 171-0031, Japan
Description: ‘Novel yet nostalgic Western food’ is the theme here. Hamburger steaks with dollops of demi-glace sauce and gratin dressed in silky smooth béchamel sauce are prepared in time-honoured ways, bringing back the flavours of the good old days. Decompression-prepared salad offers rich flavours and uniquely fresh textures. Unchanging methods combine with advanced cooking techniques declare a new approach to Western favourites.

Name: there is ramen
Description: This shop’s message is “Life is well lived that appreciates a nice bowl of ramen”. As a young man, the chef learned these words from his grandfather, and they still reverberate in his heart. Like many from the Mogami region of Yamagata Prefecture, he uses light soy sauce. He seeks a natural flavour for his ramen by using dried sardines and the umami of meat to good effect. Ramen here reminds customers of their hometowns. A photo of his grandfather, smiling kindly, watches over the room.

Name: Cristiano's
Description: Portuguese cuisine seems distant yet familiar to Japanese people. The word ‘Takoten’ is often heard in kitchens and dining halls and refers to the octopus fritters that recreate the local tastes of Portugal and is also the roots of tempura. Local wine brings out the flavour of this local-style cuisine – flavours that win over the local palate with tastes that seem somehow familiar. The owner-chef’s speciality is bacalhau (dried cod).

Name: SUSHI KOURIN
Description: To encourage diners to drop in casually, the chef even accepts orders for single pieces. A blackboard crammed with lists of sushi items and snacks shows his commitment to service. This is the joy of the local sushi shop, where you can choose your items as you sit face-to-face with the chef. While easy to order, each item is still painstakingly prepared. He hangs out his shop curtain at 3 PM, so guests can start drinking while it’s still light out.

Name: SOBAHOUSE KONJIKI HOTOTOGISU
Description: The shop curtain reads, ‘If the cuckoo (hototogisu) won’t sing, I will want to make it sing’. This maxim, which summed up the character of Toyotomi Hideyoshi, who unified Japan in the 16C, also exemplifies the chef’s labour of culinary love. The clam soup evolved out of endless trial-and-error to find just the right umami components. Each bowl of ramen finely tunes the affinity of the noodles with the more than 60 other ingredients.

Name: T'astous
Description: T’astous presents as a ‘neo-bistro’, the sort of chic bistro you might find in Paris. Regional cooking arranged for a modern sensibility. The chef trained in the south of France, so he excels with foie gras and truffles that are this region’s gift to the world. The restaurant name is the word for a black-truffle canapé in the Cahors dialect. He expresses through his cuisine the wonder he felt upon tasting this delicacy in southwestern France.

Name: Washokuya Taichi
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining,Credit cards not accepted
Description: The owner-chef’s experience in Japanese cuisine is immediately evident. Goma tofu (tofu-like dish of sesame paste) is normally served with sesame sauce, but in summer tomato jelly is substituted. In this season, fragrant roast corn with butter soy sauce is recommended. The corn is shaved from the cob to make it easier to eat, reminding one of food stalls at temple festivals. The pork fillet cutlet sandwich amazes with its super-thick-cut pork. Japanese cuisine prepared with consummate skill.

Name: Tohakuan Karibe
Description: With the temperament of an artist, the chef places everything in its proper proportion. Gathering unpolished buckwheat from Nagano and Niigata, he grinds the two together, checking moisture by hand to produce nihachi and juwari noodles. Soba and broth are served in harmony: as seiro, accompanied by soup redolent of katsuobushi, or as kake, steeped in hot katsuobushi broth. Side dishes are soba-shop favourites, such as Pacific herring simmered for days or seafood and buckwheat flour wrapped in nori and deep-fried.

Name: Tonkatsu Narikura
Description: The pork cutlets, refined through a process of tinkering and improvement, are surprisingly light-coloured, thanks to coating in low-carb breadcrumbs and frying at low heat. The pork juices cling to the delicate batter, not going to waste. In addition to loin, tenderloin and belly, there’s even a mille-feuille cutlet. The chef’s approach is trial-and-error: time-consuming and with mistakes along the way, but the result is success. A unique tonkatsu born of theory, experience and instinct.

Name: Seki Hanare
Description: Creative dining focused on affinity with sake. Appetisers are served as a combination platter, the better to keep the libations flowing. Tsukuri feature ingenious arrangements of condiments. Uniquely, meat dishes are an indispensable part. Each dish is generous, making every morsel an unforgettable memory. The collection of sake and shochu, amassed on visits to breweries, is impressive; as the shop specialises in local tipples, the wine and whisky selection is also strictly Japanese.

Name: Homemade Ramen Muginae
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining,Credit cards not accepted
Description: One of the essential processes of wheat cultivation is treading the wheat. When the wheat plants bud, farmers tread them down so they grow up strong. The owner-chef named his shop Muginae, ‘wheat seedling’, as a prayer that it would grow as it overcame adversity, a hopeful shoot on the forest floor. Ramen, fragrant and homemade, has a smooth finish. Soup is seasoned with soy sauce, salt and dried sardines. Word has spread like wildfire, and now customers tread the streets of Minamioi from early morning for a cup of this restaurant’s delicious broth.

Name: Yakitori Abe
Description: The chef assembles the sequence of yakitori chicken cuts according to customer preferences. To their delight, he starts beer drinkers off with chicken breast and wine tipplers with chicken heart. Seasoning is simple: salt, sauce or soy sauce, depending on the item—whichever best brings out the flavour. The top recommendation is the chicken wings, which ticks all three boxes. The skin is fragrant, the meat and fat are sweet, and the umami unique to meat on the bone.

Name: Torishige
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining,Credit cards not accepted
Description: A pork-skewer eatery established in 1949. Yuji Sakamaki, third owner-chef, prizes the flavours he remembers from his youth. Meat-stuffed bell peppers are a popular skewer item from the days of the first chef. Beef dishes are a relative novelty, having been introduced by Sakamaki’s predecessor. For his part, the set menu Sakamaki added allows diners to enjoy dishes from the good old days. Guided by his pet saying, “lifelong training”, he preserves the flavours of Torishige across the generations.

Name: grill GRAND
Description: The charm of a Showa-era (1926–1989) Western eatery. In true Asakusa style, the whole family pitches in. Brothers race to finish shredding the cabbage, with the winner allowed to prepare food. This time it falls on the elder brother to wait on tables. Hamburger steak, rice-stuffed omelette, beef stew and other ‘Japanese-Western’ favourites remind patrons of the good old days. With the teachings of their grandfather and father in their hearts, the family upholds the goodness of Asakusa.

Name: BRAMASOLE
Description: Kenta Takahashi was charmed by olive oil grown under the Mediterranean sun. The restaurant’s name means ‘one yearning for the sun’, referring to Takahashi himself. One taste of what he can do with olive oil will convince you of his expertise. Pasta dishes feature things like vegetables and dried mullet roe; seafood includes items such as aqua pazza. Ever eager to please his guests, Takahashi will even prepare items not on the menu. Taking the freedom of à la carte one step further is one of the joys of Bramasole.

Name: Yakitori SANKA
Description: The spirit in Takamasa Yamanaka’s heart is one of giving back to his home region. To showcase the appeal of his native Kochi, he sources Tosa chicken. The shop’s name is a portmanteau combining characters from his name and that of his hometown, Kahoku. After dusting his skewers with sun-dried salt from eastern Kochi Prefecture, he grills them over Tosa binchotan charcoal, another point of hometown pride. He lists the names of his producers as a way to express his gratitude.

Name: Ramen Break Beats
Description: ‘Break Beats’, the name of a musical genre, is the perfect name for this shop, whose chef wears two hats as an active DJ. The clear base soup uses Amakusa Daio chicken, while black maitake mushrooms add umami for the soy sauce-flavoured ramen, and freshwater mussels does the same for salt-flavoured ramen. Ingredients such as smoked pork fillet and fried enoki mushrooms switch up the flavours. A catchy remix of old ramen favourites.

Name: Sasaki Seimenjo
Description: The chef ’s aim is to create a ramen shop beloved by locals. He sources ingredients from greengrocers and butchers in Nishiogi, treasuring his interactions with local people. The distance from the train station is also a blessing, as neighbourhood schoolchildren and their families can be seen sitting shoulder-to-shoulder, happily slurping noodles. As befits the ‘Seimenjo’, or ‘noodle-maker’, in the name, his use of Japanese wheat is a selling point. In addition to standard thin noodles, he also offers flat noodles. The miso flavour is a much-anticipated treat in autumn and winter.

Name: IRUCA TOKYO
Description: The chef displays his originality in each bowl as he pursues a unique interpretation of ramen. Broths of clam, spiny lobster, free-range chicken and beef combine to create a soup of satisfying depth. Paste of porcini mushrooms and truffles switches up the flavour of soy-sauce ramen. Salt ramen is infused with yuzu flavoured butter to impart a creamy fragrance. ‘Iruca’ comes from the Japanese for ‘dolphin’, a symbol of peace and a message of friendship to spread across the oceans.

Name: Kuhara
Description: The friendly couple who run Kuhara—the chef a disciple of Japanese cuisine, the proprietress a welcoming figure in kappo wear—make us instantly feel at home. The signature fare is duck. In addition to salt-grilled duck, they offer chilled breast stew in summer, and a hot duck stew called jibuni in winter. Dried baby fish with soy and pepper on rice and Kokusho miso soup of root vegetables are must-try items. Unripe pepper is gathered by the couple and their children when they visit her hometown in Tochigi Prefecture. Kokusho miso soup brings back memories for the chef, who sampled it when he applied to a restaurant specialising in shojin ryori.

Name: wokotote
Description: The chef studied the art of kaiseki multi-course meals. In addition to omakase set meals, he serves prix fixe meals to which à la carte items can be added, so diners can enjoy Japanese cuisine as they please. Sashimi is accompanied by a dipping sauce of malted rice and fish sauce; mixed platters of drinking snacks include grilled and fried items prepared with care. The shop name is inspired by grammatical particles used to form sentences in Japanese. Cuisine, people, drinks and interior blend agreeably together, so relax and let time flow by.

Name: Tachiguisushi Sushikawa
Description: Sushi got its start as hawker food that flourished in Edo (old Tokyo). To impart a feeling for that culture, Tachiguisushi Sushikawa is a standup sushi bar (and is what the name means). No drinking snacks; this is nigiri only, which you can order piece by piece according to your taste. Sushi toppings display an old-school craftsmanship. The chef harbours doubts about the recent trend of taking sushi up-market, which is why he recreated the atmosphere of a real-deal, no-nonsense sushi joint. A sushi local where regulars come to chat with the chef.

Name: HARU CHAN Ramen
Address: 1F, Shimbashi Ekimae Ichigokan, 2-20-15 Shimbashi, Minato-ku, Tokyo, 105-0004, Japan
Description: The Chinese soba noodles feature a rich stock made from pork and dried sardines, flavoured with salt and lard. The soup is filled to the very rim of the bowl, a thoughtful gesture by the chef to ensure the noodles stay hot until the last bite. The pork is stewed until exquisitely tender and sliced just before serving, preserving its savoury flavour. Adding a touch of visual charm, the bowl is uniquely adorned with flower-shaped and ball-shaped wheat gluten bread. The generous portion sizes guarantee that you’ll leave feeling satisfied.

Name: Katchar Batchar
Description: From the north, butter chicken; from the west, pork vindaloo; shrimp curry from the south – such a lineup of flavours from every region of India adds breadth to the joy that is Indian cooking. Tandoori chicken and vegetables are cooked using the radiant heat of a tandoor. For spices, the basic triad is cumin, coriander and turmeric. To keep the flavours of meats and vegetables at the fore, the number of spices is kept to a minimum.

Name: Katsuyoshi
Description: You’ll find Katsuyoshi in a back-alley of Ningyocho. The interior of the shop, a refurbished traditional home, uses recycled wood to convey a retro feel. In the kitchen, you’ll see two copper pots. When deep-frying pork cutlets, the owner-chef uses hotter oil for some dishes and cooler oil for others. Fried seafood morsels such as scallop and tiger prawn are popular. If you get a seat at the counter, you can watch the chef’s work, which starts with preparing the meat.

Name: Ginza Katsukami
Description: Tonkatsu served prix fixe using a wide range of pork cuts. The restaurant works with multiple brands of pork to make every bite of freshly deep-fried tenderloin, loin and shoulder count. The cut face is placed at the top so that none of the juices are wasted, bringing out the full true flavour of the pork. A variety of other fried items can be added, such as crab croquettes and deep-fried breaded minced pork. Shaved ice with your choice of syrups is a post-prandial treat to look forward to.

Name: BISTRO GLOUTON
Description: From down a back alley in Ikejiri, light beckons from a counter bistro. Draw closer and a crowded blackboard lists such a range of items, from French regional cuisine to Western-influenced dishes like hamburger steaks and croquettes, that you’ll hardly be able to choose. The menu doesn’t change, to keep quality consistent and high. ‘Glouton’ refers to someone who enjoys their food whole-heartedly. Every item here will tickle your fancy, and once you’ve sampled the food here, you’ll want to return.

Name: roku
Description: The name, meaning ‘six’, comes from this couple’s birthday month, June. The aim is to serve the Sangubashi area with French cuisine rooted firmly in the region. The chef adds a unique touch with ingredients sourced from producers with whom he has strong relations. Edible wild plants, mushrooms and game are products of his native Nagano. Desserts prepared from seasonal fruits are handled by the proprietress. At the counter, which appropriately seats six, the chef’s explanations create a feeling of intimacy.

Name: LA BETTOLA da Ochiai
Description: ‘La Bettola’ is Italian for ‘the dining hall’. With its casual atmosphere and fare that is good value for money, this trattoria draws throngs of guests day after day.
