FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: As a sophisticated alternative to Seestern, Treibgut adds to the gourmet credentials of the Lago hotel. Modern cuisine is served in a trendy and exceedingly stylish interior. There are also dishes for sharing, e.g. steak cuts, whole fish or snack platters. They offer a nice selection of goods from their own bakery, butcher's shop and ice cream factory.

Name: Mühlenhelle - Bistro
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: This charming bistro set up in a pleasantly light and airy space is an attractive alternative to the fine dining restaurant. The food here is also top-notch, with Michael Quendler preparing delicious seasonal cuisine in the open kitchen. Much of the food also draws on tradition and showcases the region. Take, for example, the variation of Lambachtal salmon trout or the pan-fried Eifel pork blood sausage – two knockout dishes that linger in the memory. An appealing selection of wines is also on offer. Cordial service with a personal touch.

Name: Little John's
Description: Housed in a spruce building dating from 1905, Tim Lellau's restaurant is appealingly laid-back with a Scandinavian feel. Here, attentive and well-drilled waitstaff serve high-quality, fresh cuisine. There is a choice of two set menus: "Weide & Wasser" (Pasture & Water) and the vegetarian "Wald & Wiese" (Forest & Meadow) – this can be made vegan by prior arrangement. Alternatively, you can also order à la carte. There is also a reasonably priced three-course set menu at lunchtime. From the entrance area, you can see into the kitchen, which is sure to whet your appetite! N.B. cash payments only.

Name: Sommerau
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Great view,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: The trip to the Hegar family's restaurant just outside Bonndorf is definitely worth it! Nestled in a quiet valley, surrounded by woods and meadows, the setting could not be more idyllic. There's an inviting terrace, but you can also enjoy the view from inside. The cuisine is regional and seasonal, including French and Mediterranean influences. The dishes are meticulously crafted and packed with flavour. Great care is taken to source ingredients that reflect the restaurant's commitment to sustainability. The wine list showcases a number of gems from the region, with a special emphasis on Baden Burgundy – the selection of half bottles is excellent. In the hotel of the same name, there are cosy, modern guestrooms and a beautiful sauna house, plus a natural swimming pond. And so that you can really unplug and unwind, there's no Wi-Fi or mobile phone reception!

Name: Seehaus
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Great view,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: This is a gorgeous spot at any time of the day. In the summer months, the terrace overlooking the lake is perfect for a relaxed lunch or afternoon cake (summer weekends only). In the evening and in winter, you'll be just as happy to sit inside – there's something romantic about this charming restaurant done out in warm rustic wood. They also serve fantastic modern and international cuisine, such as "bouillabaisse à la Seehaus" with lobster, rouille sauce and bread chips.

Name: Lucky Leek
Description: "Fine Natural Dining" is the concept here at this pleasant restaurant. Charming staff serve up fully vegan cuisine in the form of a three- to five-course tasting menu – it's also possible to order à la carte. Made with seasonal vegetables, the creative, plant-based dishes are packed with flavour, and they are just as popular with international visitors as they are with locals. In summer, the best place to dine is on the terrace out front.

Name: Landhaus Lebert
Description: In a small town about 10km from Rothenburg ob der Tauber, this cosy restaurant serves really flavoursome cuisine made from good-quality regional produce – importance is attached to sustainability. In summer, there is a lovely beer garden. Well-kept guestrooms for overnight stays, and a barn for private events. Tip: In the old shepherd's caravan, you can buy products made on site, such as lemon liqueur, spice mixtures, jellies and jams.

Name: Almer Schlossmühle
Description: This carefully converted old mill next to the little Schloss Alme is a highly appealing restaurant that abounds with rustic charm. The delicious food features seasonal dishes from the regional repertoire as well as classic fare from the chef's native Austria. Head for the lovely terrace in fine weather. There are also guestrooms for an overnight stay.

Name: Mussumer Krug
Description: Whether you are seated in the rustic-style old brick building or the laid-back modern annexe, the atmosphere at this restaurant is very pleasant. The menu features modern international dishes such as yellowtail ceviche and traditional specialities, for example braised beef shoulder. A three-course surprise menu is also proposed. The kitchen takes its cue from the changing seasons with a penchant for regional produce. There is a great selection of German wines, and the service is friendly and attentive. Covered terrace.

Name: Restaurant Villa Esche
Description: Built in 1903, the former coach house of Villa Esche (now the Henry van de Velde Museum) houses this bright, tastefully designed restaurant where diners can enjoy attentive service and top-notch seasonal cuisine. Opt for the four-course menu or order à la carte. At lunchtime, the options are slightly more limited but include moderately priced daily specials. Delightful terrace overlooking the grounds.

Name: EssBar fein & pfiffig
Description: The outwardly unimposing restaurant run by Daniel Baur and Olga Jorich is situated only a few steps away from the Hofgarten public park. Pleasant atmosphere, plus flavoursome dishes prepared from good-quality ingredients and offering good value for money. Neither will you be disappointed by the wine list! Attractive protected terrace to the rear.

Name: Rait'ner Wirt
Description: This beautifully renovated and well-established 17C inn now houses attractive, comfortable guestrooms and exceedingly cosy dining areas brimming with rustic pub charm – it's not uncommon to share a large table with other diners. The glorious beer garden is a real draw in summer! The kitchen serves up hearty regional fare with no frills but plenty of flavour, including roast pork, cheese spaetzle and Kaiserschmarrn (shredded pancake). Be sure to take a look at the daily specials.

Name: Staudenwirt
Description: This well-established restaurant with its spruce little hotel has been run by the same family for three generations. Each dining area has quite a different style, from rustic to pleasingly contemporary, plus there is a delightful terrace. The menu features a diverse range of options, from comforting regional fare such as half a rotisserie chicken, or "Grandma Hilde's Rohrnudel" (oven-baked yeast dumplings) for dessert, as well as modern, seasonal and internationally influenced dishes. Vegetarians are well catered for, too. Fantastic value for money!

Name: Rührberger Hof
Description: The historical Rührberger Hof estate, which is home to this long-established family business, has been around since 1902. The fact that it was once used for farming is no longer apparent today. The pleasingly modern interior is an attractive setting in which to savour the excellent cuisine of brothers Christoph und Felix Düster. This is based on classical foundations and takes its cue from the region and the seasons. At lunchtime, the reasonably priced set menu of the day is very popular. There are also well-kept contemporary-style guestrooms.

Name: Fürstenfelder
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: This former monastery makes for a wonderful setting. In what was once the cattle shed, the impressive Bohemian vaulted ceiling has been incorporated into the modern interior design, with a centrally positioned open kitchen. Out in the courtyard of the Cistercian monastery, there is a lovely terrace, slightly separated from the beer garden. The menu is varied, featuring dishes with a modern twist and made with sustainably produced (organic) regional produce. Options include dishes from the Josper grill, as well as vegetarian and vegan alternatives. Lunchtime buffet.

Name: Zöllner's Weinstube
Description: Surrounded by splendid gardens, this 18C half-timbered sandstone building is as charming on the outside as it is on the inside. Sitting beneath a striking vaulted ceiling, diners can enjoy regional as well as Mediterranean-inspired cuisine made from first-rate produce. There is also an excellent selection of Franconian wines. In summer, the terrace is a must!

Name: Aschbacher Hof
Description: This pretty country hotel run by the Lechner family offers not only fabulous views of the region and tasteful, cosy rooms but also exceptionally good, fresh cooking. The regional and seasonal dishes include game as well as classics like Zwiebelrostbraten (fried beef and onions in gravy). Wonderful terrace.

Name: Zur Krone
Description: Set in a spruce country house, this establishment has been run with great dedication and a sense of tradition by nine successive generations of the same family for over 200 years. Taking its cue from the seasons, the ingredient-led cuisine is flavoursome. Asparagus dishes are served in spring, game and goose in winter. For those with a sweet tooth, the meringue with cream, vanilla ice cream and egg liqueur is a must-try! Food is served in the cosy interior or out on the gorgeous terrace.

Name: Café Rapp
Description: Originally a bakery and café, the family business is now also a restaurant, where quality, flavour and price are spot on. The emphasis is on regional and seasonal products – vegetables and meat are sourced from the village, herbs are grown in the kitchen garden. A must in the afternoon: the delicious fresh cakes! Pretty guestrooms.

Name: Sennhütte
Description: Family hospitality is the name of the game here! Since 1918, the Grether family have put their heart and soul into this place and not least into the good food, made mostly with regional produce. Dishes ranging from traditional to slightly more sophisticated are served in a space divided into smaller rooms or out on the lovely verdant terrace. Snacks and cakes are available throughout the day. They have their own distillery, smokehouse and Alpine dairy. Pretty, comfortable guestrooms.

Name: Weedenhof
Address: Mainzer Straße 6, Jugenheim in Rheinhessen, 55270, Germany
Description: The restaurant is wonderfully cosy with its rustic exposed timber frame and dry-stone interior. Michael Knöll conjures up cuisine that combines Mediterranean and regional influences, making use of excellent produce to deliver flavoursome dishes. Choose between à la carte options and seasonal set menus, including a vegetarian version. They also have lovely and well-maintained guestrooms.

Name: Landgasthaus Gidibauer-Hof
Description: You eat well here, and furthermore the regional cuisine comes at very fair prices. The home-reared beef, for example, is sure to whet the appetite. The ambience is friendly, cosy and rustic. The converted cowshed is a great venue for parties. In the hotel of the same name, the guestrooms are furnished with natural wood furniture.

Name: Allgäuer Stuben
Address: Lindauer Straße 75, Isny im Allgäu, 88316, Germany
Description: The good food and welcoming atmosphere are the main draws of this restaurant run by the Rimmele family, whose dedication to their work is palpable – that is certainly the case for chef Susanne Rimmele. She cooks regional as well as Mediterranean dishes. The front-of-house team are charming and obliging. Tip: the delightful terrace. They also offer cookery classes, tackling eg pasta, asparagus, game. Pleasant overnight accommodation is available at Hotel Hohe Linde.

Name: Capricorn [ i ] Aries Brasserie
Description: Located in a neighbourhood with a unique character, this appealing, laid-back restaurant has plenty of regulars. Welcoming and lively, it's everything a brasserie should be. The menu, too, is down-to-earth, including mouthwatering options – house-made venison ham, brasserie classics such as steak-frites and vegetarian dishes. Tip: Take a punt on the moderately priced surprise menu. Friendly and professional service. Pavement terrace.

Name: Restaurant Corona im Hotel zur Post
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Credit cards not accepted,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: It's a real treat to eat here! In this classic restaurant, Sergio and Kerstin Corona work as a well-coordinated team, providing charming service and Mediterranean-inspired cuisine. In addition to the "Méditerranée" and "Corona" set menus, from which you can also choose à la carte, there is also a bargain to be had in the three-course lunch menu.

Name: Die Windmühle
Description: In this former corn mill, the Lemke family now run a restaurant that serves excellent food. There are two comfortable dining spaces – the Mühlenstube and the Kaminzimmer – plus a delightful terrace where you can tuck into delicious seasonal and regional dishes. The friendly and attentive front-of-house team take delight in talking diners through their selection of German wines.

Name: Landgasthof Löwen
Address: Kirchdorfer Straße 8, Kirchdorf an der Iller, 88457, Germany
Description: Alexander Ruhland represents the fourth generation of his family to run this traditional country inn, and his kitchen turns out top-notch dishes. He combines classic and modern influences, with the region and the seasons playing a major role. Modern and comfortable guestrooms are also available.

Name: Poppenborg's Stübchen
Description: This is the more relaxed alternative to Poppenborg's more traditional eatery. Try the Atlantic sea wolf with mustard sauce or the Westphalian-style boiled top-side of veal. Pretty garden terrace.

Name: HYGGE Brasserie & Bar
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: This hip place is named after the concept of hygge. In Danish and Norwegian, this describes a feeling of cosy wellbeing and comfortable conviviality – very fitting for the atmosphere conjured up in this pretty half-timbered house, which used to be a stable for polo horses. Allying rustic timber elements and modern design, the interior is chic and stylish, with the central fireplace as the focal point. The atmosphere is pleasantly lively. Unfussy seasonal dishes make up the HYGGE set menu and surprise menu; alternatively go à la carte – there are great vegetarian options, too. Or why not order a selection of plates for everyone in your party to tuck into? Appealing wine list. The trendy bar lounge is also popular, as is the charming terrace in summer.

Name: Zur Krone
Description: In the centre of the village you will find this charming restaurant with its comfortable dining rooms. Ralf Restel serves simple, flavoursome regional fare with international influences. Try the boiled rump of beef with herb sauce and pan-fried potatoes or the breast of corn-fed chicken with stir-fried vegetables and curry sauce. In summer the best tables are those outside on the quiet leafy terrace.

Name: Nil
Description: Diners are bound to enjoy their time here! This restaurant in the trendy Schanze district has a delightful ambience, the service is informal and friendly, and you can certainly expect to eat well. The delicious food follows the seasons and draws on international influences. Opt for the five-course set menu. Excellent and reasonably priced short wine list.

Name: Gasthaus Egertal
Description: The Rupprecht family have brought together two concepts in their attractive traditional guesthouse: the elegant restaurant and the bistro serve the same menu. It features freshly prepared dishes with regional and classical influences. Most of the fruit and vegetables are home grown. The terrace out front is lovely in summer.

Name: Wirtsstube im Hotel Burkhard
Description: In the second restaurant of the hotel Landgasthof Burkhard, the cuisine is somewhat simpler, which does not detract from the quality. Dishes range from cordon bleu to sea bream with lemon. The dining areas are cosy and prettily done out – you can choose to enjoy your meal in the Wirtsstube or the Esszimmer. The inner courtyard terrace, which is shared with the Kaminstube, is also very appealing.

Name: Kleines Meer
Description: Laid out over two levels, this convivial restaurant has exposed roof timbering that lends a pleasant airy atmosphere. Lake Müritz is just in front of the building, making the terrace with its small lounge area a popular spot with guests. Made from good-quality ingredients, the cuisine here is regional and seasonal; there are also vegetarian options. The hotel of the same name has well-kept guestrooms.

Name: Long March Canteen
Description: Currently one of "the" places to eat, Long March offers a dimly lit interior, informal service and a kitchen open to the diners’ gaze. The menu features Cantonese fare in the form of a variety of dim sum and dumpling dishes. Wide selection of wines, spirits, cocktails and tall drinks.

Name: Landgasthaus Hirsch
Description: The Waldenmaier family (now in their fourth generation) cook excellent, seasonal, regional fare at their traditional country inn. The game is locally hunted, the bread comes from the little bakery next door, and even the schnapps is home distilled. There is also a pretty terrace on the first floor and a lovely rustic beer garden.

Name: Freihaus Brenner
Description: This lakeside inn overlooking Tegernsee is picture perfect; in summer, the terrace is the stuff of dreams. The interior is especially inviting, with cosy dining spaces done out in warm wood. The menu features delicious regional classics such as roast pork with dumplings or locally caught char with parsley potatoes, as well as more upscale fare such as turbot fillet with pumpkin risotto. The service is friendly and efficient, and the staff are all dressed in traditional Bavarian attire. Gorgeous suite on the top floor.

Name: Erbgericht Tautewalde
Description: Inside, the modern dining rooms are done out in a pretty, rural style; outside, there is a lovely courtyard with a view of the kitchen. The seasonal cuisine is regional and international, and they are keen to use local produce. You can choose between the "Landidyll" set menu and "A la carte menu". And those who want to do without meat can look forward to a vegan set menu. Overnight accommodation in the traditional Erbgericht.

Name: Landgenuss
Description: Run by the Hämmerle family, this restaurant enjoys great popularity, so it is advisable to book well in advance! With a friendly country house feel, charming service and great food, this place is a nice alternative to the gourmet restaurant. Made with plenty of local produce, the dishes served here are seasonal with occasional Mediterranean touches. The wide-ranging menu includes their "Original Wiener schnitzel" and sea bass with rosemary and thyme. In summer, make a beeline for the terrace.

Name: Bergfriedel
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: This establishment has been run by the same family with great dedication for years! The welcoming team serves delicious, fresh food that diners can enjoy as they take in the views over the Bühlertal. They follow a philosophy that is close to nature - and their own chickens in the garden fit in nicely. The wide-ranging menu includes traditional cuisine from Baden, vegetarian/vegan dishes and gourmet specialities. Add to that an extensive wine list. The chic restaurant extension is done out in a modern take on regional style. Pleasant overnight accommodation is available – the rooms and suites ("Natur-Zimmer" and "Natur-Suiten") are done out in locally sourced materials and are contemporary in their design.

Name: Gasthof Brink
Description: A place with charm! The traditional style that is cultivated here will evoke childhood memories for many diners. Family-run since 1880, the restaurant serves classic French cuisine that is down to earth and delicious. The pleasant setting has an elegant feel. The house-made pâtés and terrines are just as popular as the saddle of veal with Béarnaise sauce or the sole meunière.

Name: Hirsch
Description: "Modern tavern cuisine" is the name of the game in this family-run establishment, which has been in business for 12 generations in a quiet suburb of Ellwangen. At the helm is the son, Dennis Wiche, who has worked in several MICHELIN-starred restaurants. The menu comprises an abundance of appealing dishes, from regional classics such as Zwiebelrostbraten (roast beef with onions) and spaetzle to the chef's more modern creations, such as vitello forello. Be sure to try the house-made maultaschen! The chefs work only with the finest seasonal and regional produce – in fact, the restaurant had its own farm until a few years ago. In summer, you can dine on the terrace, which is sheltered from the wind. Overnight accommodation is available on site, in the hotel of the same name.

Name: Zur Glocke
Address: Friedrich-von-Teck-Straße 12, Höchstädt an der Donau, 89420, Germany
Description: The Stoiber family have put their heart and soul into running this trendy, modern restaurant. Their commitment is particularly evident in the excellent cuisine, which sticks close to the seasons and draws on quality ingredients. There are two set menus, one of them vegetarian, but you can also dine à la carte from the small menu of the day. The terrace in the front garden is ideal for warm summer days, and there are modern guestrooms ranging from "classic" to "design".

Name: Zum Fischer am See
Address: Harrasser Straße 145, Prien am Chiemsee, 83209, Germany
Description: The name says it all. As soon as you set foot in the small entrance hall you are greeted by a picture of various freshwater fish, and the kitchen specialises in fish dishes. However, the well-curated menu also includes steaks, regional classics such as braised ox cheek, and vegetarian options. The grappa and brandy selection is really impressive and might tempt you to stay for a nightcap. In fine weather, the best spot is the terrace with a view of the lake – small boats can also moor there. Good overnight accommodation available. Motorists will be pleased to know there is a large private car park.

Name: Hirsch & Jägerstüberl - Ostiner Stub'n
Address: Schlierseer Straße 60, Gmund am Tegernsee, 83703, Germany
Description: This typical regional inn proposes two separate culinary concepts: The fine dining restaurant is open Fri to Sun evenings, and the more rustic Hirsch & Jägerstüberl is open Wed to Fri from 6pm and Sat to Sun 12-2.30pm and 6-9.30pm. The emphasis is on produce from the region, and the dishes take their cue from the changing seasons. The fine dining restaurant also serves set menus. Attentive service. In summer, tables on the lovely terrace overlooking the garden are much in demand.

Name: Schwarzkopf
FacilitiesAndServices: Credit cards not accepted,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: Run by Stefan Pumm and his charming wife Anja, this restaurant serves fresh, tasty cuisine including chateaubriand steak with Béarnaise sauce (for two), a popular house speciality. Elegant wood-panelled dining room, inviting terrace, plus good accommodation also available (ask for one of the refurbished rooms).

Name: Schäck's Adler
Description: Christoph and Sandra Schäck have brought to life this picture-perfect hotel. The atmosphere in the wood-panelled dining rooms is really cosy, the service is very friendly, the cuisine is ambitious and tasty – the emphasis is on regional ingredients and seasonal produce. There is also the appealing Strumbel Bar and a number of extremely well-kept rooms.

Name: Gasthaus Scherz
Description: A native of Vorarlberg, Michael Scherz – no stranger to Cologne's gastronomy scene – focuses on Austrian cuisine, with classics such as Tafelspitz (boiled beef), Wiener schnitzel and Kaiserschmarrn (shredded pancake with raisins). Great Austrian wines. The service is speedy; the staff friendly and well-trained. Very nice terrace to the rear of the house. Good to know: the restaurant is easily accessible from the city centre by tram.

Name: Gasthaus Weißenbeck
Description: You will find plenty of satisfied customers here, and no wonder! The mother and daughter Weissenbeck team cook up a storm using regional and seasonal produce – and the prices are fair. The lovely inn also makes for a cosy setting, and in summer the delightful garden terrace is most inviting.

Name: Zum Rebstock
Description: A fun place to eat! This handsome historical half-timbered house has been in the same family since 1750. Sit back in the delightful wood-panelled interior as the cordial front-of-house team brings out really good Baden cuisine, which can also be enjoyed on the terrace in summer. The menu includes dishes such as pikeperch-salmon dumplings, and stuffed guinea fowl breast with a chive cream sauce to whet your appetite. Tip: Sample the tempting little starters and desserts (look for the "Versucherle" sections on the menu)! With some 500 labels, the wine list is excellent. To take home: house-made cherry and plum brandies. The establishment also has well-kept guestrooms.

Name: ROSE
Description: The Tress family is all about organic produce, with a vegetarian and vegan take on regional cuisine taking centre stage. The complex, aromatic and carefully considered dishes win diners over with their depth of flavour – the pea and broad bean tartare, for instance, make a lasting impression. Meat can be ordered as a side dish – here, they follow the principle of nose-to-tail eating. All the wines are Demeter-certified. Should you wish to stay over, there is the guesthouse opposite.

Name: Landgasthof Zur Post
Description: Owned by the same family since 1870, this restaurant is now in its sixth generation. They are passionate about cooking, and use fresh produce sourced almost entirely from regional suppliers to serve up sustainable, locally sourced cuisine at reasonable prices. The delicious dishes cooked up by the chef showcase his experience in fine dining. In addition to the appealing à la carte options, a seasonal three-course set menu is also on offer. The ambience is cosy and rustic; in summer the terrace commands lovely views of Nieder-Moos. Five guestrooms and a holiday apartment are available for overnight stays.

Name: LAMM
Description: A really cosy place, where you will also eat very well: seasonal Swabian-Baden cuisine, with an emphasis on regional produce; some of the meat comes from the restaurant's own highland cattle. There are good wines to accompany your meal, as well as a special whisky offer. In summer, try and bag a spot on the terrace. Pleasant guestrooms also available.

Name: Harmonie
Description: This charming building dating from 1823 has not shed its traditional character – lovely old wood panelling makes it really cosy! Here you will get to enjoy friendly service and regional, seasonal dishes, such as braised leg of venison. At the entrance you can sneak a peek into the kitchens.

Name: Zu den drei Linden - Lindenblüte
Description: Tanja and Thomas Siemes run their family business with great dedication, and the food here is exceptional. He cooks up international cuisine that takes its cue from the seasons and incorporates Mediterranean and regional influences; she provides charming service. You can opt for the set menu or order dishes à la carte, such as the mouthwatering pan-fried turbot fillet with spinach and truffle ravioli. The atmosphere is friendly and the decor has an elegant Mediterranean feel.

Name: Zum Goldenen Anker
Description: Not only does this 18C hotel offer a comfortable stay (opt for one of the newer guestrooms), it is also a popular modern take on a rural restaurant. Diners are waited on by a friendly front-of-house team in an attractive modern setting with a rustic touch. The food is flavoursome, fresh and seasonal. The main courses are also available in smaller portions. In summer, make a beeline for the gorgeous terrace to the rear of the building.

Name: HENNE.Weinbar
Description: Set in the heart of the old town, Hendrik ("Henne") Olfen's appealing bistro-style restaurant has a pleasantly laid-back atmosphere – and it's really popular! Likewise, the excellent food, which represents great value for money, goes down just as well! There is a simple menu at lunchtime and, in the evening, a range of modern, seasonal tapas-style plates that are ideal for sharing. Decent wine list. Delightful little courtyard terrace.

Name: Flux - Biorestaurant Werratal
Description: Unpretentious, natural, simple and honest – that's the motto here. The dishes, which are created using organic seasonal produce sourced from the region wherever possible, are packed with flavour. The menu is vegan/vegetarian, but meat and fish can be ordered as add-ons. Gluten- and lactose-free options are also available. In summer, the garden is idyllic. Cosy guestrooms at Biohotel Werratal.

Name: Seehof
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Boasting a lovely lakeside location on the marina, this restaurant offers a popular terrace as well as its “Badische Weinstube” and panoramic “Alois” dining rooms. Flavourful and classic artisan dishes feature on the menu. Tip: the local classics ("Alemannische Klassiker"). Accommodation is also available – the “boathouse” and rooms with views are particularly recommended.

Name: Zur Flottbeker Schmiede
Description: Experience a slice of Portugal in Hamburg! The setting, a heritage-protected historical forge, exudes traditional German charm with its authentic decor and period open fireplace. It makes for a pleasantly laid-back atmosphere in which to tuck into delicious tapas, freshly made with no fuss. The chef-patron serves up genuine Portuguese cuisine with the occasional South American twist. Try, for example, her "barbecued calamari, marinade, garlic" or quesadillas with braised short rib, cheese and guacamole. The well-curated wine list is dedicated to Portuguese labels.

Name: Feilmeiers Landleben
Description: This cosy and modern restaurant knows how to makes diners feel welcome. For Johann (who goes by Hans) Feilmeier, his "country life" cooking reflects both a love of his native region and a sense of duty. He cooks regionally and seasonally inspired food. Choose from one of the different set menus or order à la carte. Extremely charming and cordial service - matching wine advice included. Tip: the home-made jams!

Name: Weinhaus Stern
Description: A popular address and deservedly so: an inviting, rustic-style interior, a pretty courtyard, friendly service and, last but not least, good seasonal cuisine. Chef Klaus Markert relies on honest craftsmanship and flavours, along with fine wines from the region. Be sure to try the house brandy production. Charming guestrooms are also available, and there are home-made fruit jams for breakfast.

Name: Felsenbirne
Description: This restaurant with a friendly atmosphere and a sleek modern interior is located on a cobbled street in the pretty old town, not far from the Elbe. Chef-patron Felix Mikulla uses seasonal ingredients – his dishes are fresh and delicious, as well as good value. The menu also includes vegetarian and vegan options. In summer, diners can make the most of the terrace in the inner courtyard.

Name: Alte Posthalterei
Description: Regional and seasonal cuisine is served in the delightful interior of this long-established, family-run restaurant. On the menu, classics such as trout meunière, Wiener schnitzel, and beef tenderloin goulash Stroganoff whet the appetite. For those who like to dine al fresco, a cosy beer garden nestles in the shade of the chestnut trees. There are beautiful, spacious guestrooms available for overnight stays.

Name: Gasthaus Wolters - Zur Börse
Address: In der Langen Straße 22, Wurster Nordseeküste, 27639, Germany
Description: Formerly a livestock exchange, this appealing inn is steeped in tradition. Behind the typical brick and half-timbered façade, tables are laid out in a pleasingly rural interior where diners enjoy a quality take on regional home-style cooking made using excellent produce. Friendly service completes the picture. Be sure to reserve your table – the Gasthaus Wolters tends to get booked up.

Name: Gasthaus Stromberg
Description: This old-established restaurant in the pedestrian zone offers minimalist-style and a friendly atmosphere as traditional meets modern. The food is seasonal and regional – try the pumpkin variations with Dorstener goat’s cheese or the beef roulade with speck and curly kale. Werkstatt, just 1. 5km away, is ideal for groups.

Name: Talblick
Description: Brothers Claus and Rainer Weitbrecht are carrying on the tradition of their parents' business – the dedication of the whole family is palpable. As head chef, Claus Weitbrecht delights diners with both Swabian and international cuisine, including vegetarian dishes. The craftsmanship and harmonious flavours are excellent in equal measure. There is also a well-curated wine list. For a more upscale alternative, head to the hotel's Gourmetrestaurant. Comfortable guestrooms available.

Name: Gasthaus Ödenturm
Description: As if straight out of a picture book, this beautiful inn stands on the edge of the forest. Diners can look forward to a friendly, family atmosphere and great food, which can also be enjoyed out on the delightful terrace. The dishes on the menu range from regional to Mediterranean. Whether you order steak, fish or local game, there is something for everyone. Modern yet cosy guestrooms for overnight stays.

Name: Landhaus Gräfenthal
Description: Steeped in tradition, this establishment has a solid reputation in the area. Peter Lauterbach represents the fourth generation to run this family restaurant in an idyllic location. The food is a contemporary take on regional, seasonal cuisine and influenced by Mediterranean culinary tradition. Inside, pale wood, a tiled stove and pleasing decorative touches make for an inviting setting; outside there is a beautiful garden terrace. With warm and attentive service, this place has everything it takes to ensure a comfortable dining experience.

Name: Altdeutsches Restaurant
Description: Florian Kellerbauer's kitchen philosophy centres on quality ingredients, with a strong commitment to regional and seasonal sourcing. Diners can opt for a set menu – either with meat or vegetarian – comprising four, five or six courses. You can also order à la carte. The service is friendly, attentive and professional. The restaurant occupies a prime spot in the historical centre – Kirche St Georg just opposite is well worth a visit. For overnight stays, there is Hotel Deutsches Haus, a patrician house dating from 1440, or in the Ehemalige Sparkasse, both just 50m away.

Name: Weisses Rössl
Description: Standing in the heart of the beautiful old town is this house with a strikingly painted facade. The many regulars appreciate the pleasant, contemporary-rural ambience, charming service and fresh, tasty dishes, such as marinated salmon with wasabi and cucumber or braised venison with bread dumplings and vegetables. Small terrace in summer.

Name: ElbUferei
Description: This friendly restaurant with a gorgeous terrace, bar and open kitchen is just outside the centre, on the Elbe Cycle Route. The atmosphere here, on the ground floor of ARCOTEL HafenCity, is pleasantly laid back, and the modern decor has a maritime feel. The food is predominantly Mediterranean (served à la carte or as a set menu) along with light bites and steaks. Mouthwatering options include dishes such as Arctic char, potato, fennel, mustard and sauerkraut.

Name: Schatzhauser
Description: Another iteration of the Finkbeiner family's Traube Tonbach suite of restaurants. The interior is minimalist and modern, airy and light, with a terrace boasting a great view of the valley. They serve a pleasant mix of international cuisine, seasonal dishes and regional classics, plus steaks cooked on the Lavastein grill. The service courtesy of well-trained staff is very friendly. Incidentally, the place is named after the good forest spirit from a Black Forest fairy tale.

Name: Kaufmann's
Description: In this lovingly renovated former castle brewery, nowadays the name of the game is good, fresh cuisine. In an attractive setting of exposed old brickwork, vaulted ceilings and sleek, modern style, the restaurant serves flavoursome dishes with a regional dimension as well as international influences. For example, Rhön trout is served all year round, along with seasonal dishes such as braised haunch of venison.

Name: Die Bürgermeisterei 1728
Description: A location steeped in history in which to enjoy a meal! The lovingly restored building, which gives directly onto the market square, was once the mayor's residence and dates back to 1728. The elegant fusion of modern style and historical details lends the place atmosphere. The evening menu is ambitious, fresh and full of flavour, with appetising options such as beef bourgignon, dried fig crumble and potato-parsnip mash. The small selection of seasonal dishes is also proposed in the form of set menus, one of which is vegetarian. In summer, make the most of the secluded terrace.

Name: Lotters Wirtschaft - Tausendgüldenstube
Description: Hotel Blauer Engel not only offers lovely guestrooms, it is also home to this restaurant. With 360 years of tradition to its name, it oozes historical charm. Warm wood panelling lends the space a cosy atmosphere, and the old tiled stove is a quaint detail. Added to that is service with a personal touch and very good food – to be sampled à la carte or in set menu form. Lotters Wirtschaft brewery is also pleasant with its rustic-style vaulted ceiling.

Name: Bistro
Description: It's no wonder the charming restaurant in this spruce historical building is so popular: the food here is unpretentious and packed with flavour! The combination of a modern yet cosy interior and genuine, personable service overseen by the owner fosters a truly pleasant and welcoming atmosphere. The small terrace overlooking the church and market square is also lovely. At lunchtime there is a small a la carte option or a three-course meal deal and in the evening the  ‘St Benedict’ gourmet menu.

Name: Barra
Description: Be careful not to overlook the house with the inconspicuous front! A thoroughly and unabashedly trendy concept, from the minimalist urban look and relaxed, pleasantly neighbourly atmosphere to the nicely pared-down modern cuisine served in the form of small sharing dishes. High-quality ingredients with a preference for those sourced in the region. Tip: From the seats at the counter you have a very good view of what's happening at the cooker.

Name: November Brasserie
Description: This Japanese brasserie in a bustling neighbourhood of Prenzlauer Berg entices diners with an interesting range of Japanese specialities in the evenings – including sushi and sashimi, of course. The flambéed toro nigiri, for example, is a treat. Other draws of this place include competent service courtesy of a friendly and down-to-earth front-of-house team, and the pleasingly bright and modern minimalist-style interior, complete with a small sushi counter, where you can see the chefs at work. In summer, the outdoor tables shaded by trees are highly coveted.

Name: Holzgarten
Description: This pleasant, bustling restaurant in Holzgartenstraße (from which it takes its name) serves modern, seasonal cuisine that also incorporates international influences. The appealingly straightforward dishes (eg brasato, parsley root purée, rapini) are often reduced to a few components and carefully prepared for maximum flavour. The menu, which is purposely kept short and changes frequently, is accompanied by a well-curated wine list. Diners are seated in a trendy interior with an open-plan kitchen; there are some high tables too. Lovely terrace. Be aware that bookings are possible for two time slots.

Name: Poststuben
Description: It is hardly surprising that this restaurant is so popular. As well as charming and attentive service, diners are drawn by the regionally influenced cuisine conjured up by chef-patron Sven Molitor. Made using carefully selected ingredients, his dishes reveal talent and good craftsmanship. They are down-to-earth, but also show a certain finesse here and there. On the menu, for example, the delicious spinach and cheese dumplings will whet your appetite. The likeable traditional family-run hotel Die Post offers well-kept, contemporary guestrooms for overnight stays – an ideal base for exploring the beautiful surroundings of the village, which is located in the Meerfelder Maar volcanic crater.

Name: Rotes Ross
Description: If you are a fan of fresh and seasonal regional cuisine, the Bogner family's restaurant will be right up your street. This place is cosy and the service comes courtesy of friendly and well-drilled waitstaff managed by the lady of the house. As for the wine, the focus is also on the region. In summer, the leafy courtyard terrace is in great demand. You can also spend the night in one of the well-kept, comfortable guestrooms.

Name: Zum Falken
Description: Lars Zwick has been running this cosy, rustic-style inn in the charming Tauber Valley for many years. The cuisine is regional and seasonal, and the excellent produce is sourced locally as far as possible. Freshly prepared sausages (made in-house) are served on Thursdays and Fridays. Some of the wines – to pair with delicious dishes such as rack of lamb in a herb crust – come from the restaurant's own vineyard. They also produce their own fruit brandies and keep bees. The old barn serves as a function room and wine tastings are held in the vaulted cellar. The pretty guestrooms exude rural charm.

Name: AS am See
Description: "AS" refers to the lakeside location (am See) as well as to owner and head chef Andreas Staack. In this inviting cross between a wine bar and a bistro, the affable chef-patron proposes a modern five-course menu featuring dishes such as venison fillet, wild broccoli, cranberry jus. This restaurant is nestled in a side street in a quiet, leafy residential area, a stone's throw from Kurpark Bad Saarow. Lovely terrace.

Name: Gasthaus Goldener Stern
Description: Run with great dedication by the same family for three generations, this place operates as a traditional gasthaus at lunchtime and as a casual fine dining restaurant in the evening. The attractive interior is modern and cosy. The menu features flavoursome regional and seasonal cuisine that also draws on contemporary influences, with a focus on sustainability. Friendly and adept front-of-house team. The Eichen Loft can be booked for events, and from October to April, the stylish wine shop can be reserved for celebrations (max. 12 people). The pleasant beer garden has a slightly smaller menu.

Name: Stocks Restaurant
Description: This restaurant is housed in a charming half-timbered building with a thatched roof. The comfortable interior is done out in dark tones that exude an air of chic elegance. Friendly waitstaff serve delicious fish dishes or sushi, and those who prefer meat will also find plenty of tempting options on the menu. There is an additional lunchtime special. Tip: Parking is available to the rear of the building.

Name: Moarwirt
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Great view,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: Bio-Landhotel Moarwirt is an idyllic escape and on top of that they serve fantastic food! This lovely inn, so typical of the region, boasts a gorgeous interior with modern Alpine-style decor. In this setting, diners tuck into freshly prepared regional cuisine made using predominantly local organic produce. The potato dumplings are a must! The restaurant raises its own chickens and sheep and has a small vegetable and herb garden. In summer, the beer garden overlooking the Isar Valley is the place to be. If you want to stay a little longer, cosy guestrooms are available.

Name: Jägerwirt
Description: With its cosy rustic-style interior, charming service and down-to-earth, flavoursome cuisine, this is the archetypal Bavarian inn at its best. The menu features regional dishes and Mediterranean-influenced options. The chefs make a point of sourcing their ingredients locally and work with trusted producers. Alongside the standard menu, there is a varying menu of the day plus a weekly special. Popular grilled veal and pork hock dishes, as well as goose and duck, are also available if ordered in advance. The rural location is also delightful.

Name: derWaldfrieden
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: Run by the Hupfer family, this establishment enjoys a tranquil location on the Herrenschwand high plateau, 1 020m above sea level. Son Volker's culinary expertise shines through in his delectable cuisine, which showcases the finest regional and seasonal ingredients. In addition to set menus (regular or vegan) and à la carte dishes, there is a selection of traditional Black Forest snacks. Pleasant garden terrace. Guestrooms are available in stammHaus and spaHaus.

Name: Gasthof zur Sonne
Description: Set directly across from the Swiss border, Gasthof zur Sonne serves fresh, flavoursome cuisine with regional and Mediterranean influences in a country-style setting. Try the emmer risotto with Trollinger and grilled Calabrese salami or the duet of skrei and wild salmon in lemon sauce. The restaurant also offers three simple but beautifully kept guestrooms.

Name: Knippschild
Description: With its homely farmhouse furniture this restaurant makes a great first impression. The great regional menu makes an already perfect dining experience even better!

Name: Klösterle Hof
Description: Chef Markus Klein and his wife put their heart and soul into running this restaurant. In a charming rustic setting, friendly waitstaff serve delicious regional and seasonal cuisine made using good-quality ingredients. Good to know: Hot meals are available from noon to 8pm. Guestrooms available in three different levels of comfort.

Name: Am Kring - Büschker's Stuben
Description: In the mood for traditional regional dishes like Münsterländer Zwiebelfleisch (beef and onions)? Enjoy your meal in the rustic-style dining room or cosy fireside lounge. In addition, the hotel Am Kring offers modern guestrooms. Attractive location in this village built around the church.

Name: Vetter.
Description: Located in a residential area, this popular restaurant proposes a pleasant interior in which to tuck into regional classics or Mediterranean dishes. Good, fresh ingredients are skilfully prepared in a refreshingly uncomplicated way. In summer, spaces on the pretty terrace are hotly contested.

Name: Gasthaus Hofmann
Description: It is no wonder that this inn run by Bettina Hofmann attracts so many regulars – diners are won over by the cosy, elegantly furnished interior, as well as the exceptional food. Her appetising cuisine is regional, seasonal and dotted with modern influences, and the wines are excellent. In addition, they serve a vegetarian set menu. The service is friendly and well organised. There are also comfortable guestrooms. The eggs served at breakfast are laid by the establishment's own hens!

Name: Gasthof Berghof - Ursprung
Description: Rustic wood matched with clean lines and fresh splashes of colour provide an ‘old meets new’ look at this restaurant. The decor is mirrored in Alexander Schütz’s excellent cooking, which comes both as an upmarket set menu or simply a hearty Bratwurst. The delicious food and reasonable prices make dining here a real pleasure.

Name: Landhaus Tanner
Description: Diners are assured of warm hospitality at this long-standing family business run by Stefanie and Franz Tanner with palpable dedication. As well as providing chic, modern Alpine-style guestrooms, they serve delicious seasonal food made with select ingredients (e.g. Chiemgau beef loin with herb butter and BBQ sauce) in the cosy, tastefully designed restaurant. The kitchens are open for hot meals September to April Mon-Wed 5-9pm and Thu-Sat 12-9pm; May to August Tue-Sat 12-9pm. Incidentally, the restaurant is a member of the Slow Food community.

Name: Tölzer Schießstätte - Hager
Description: This gem of a restaurant brimming with traditional Bavarian charm serves exceptional food in an inviting rustic setting. It is understandably popular, so be sure to book well in advance! Andreas and Michaela Hager form a harmonious team and this is clearly reflected in the delicious dishes they craft. Their short menu showcases superb local ingredients in classic dishes such as liver dumpling soup, Tafelspitz (prime boiled beef) with horseradish or salmon trout fillet with a mustard sauce. Service comes courtesy of a friendly front-of-house team.

Name: Weinhaus Zum Ritter
Description: This converted 500-year-old farmhouse certainly has character. The many regulars come for the cosy atmosphere in the charming dining area (the old Swiss church window draws the eye), the cordial service and, of course, the fresh regional cuisine courtesy of chef-patron Thomas Hausin – his flavoursome dishes are clearly the work of a chef with experience at top-flight establishments! NB: different opening hours in summer.

Name: Landgasthof Rebstock
Description: In the heart of the wine village, the Keller family runs this cosy, rustic, centuries-old house, where the welcoming hosts offer fresh, seasonally inspired cuisine. They like to use ingredients from the region, but international influences can also be detected on the menu. The service is professional and very attentive. They also have guestrooms.

Name: Reck's
Description: Cuisine, art and accommodation are combined in this long-running family business. Three sisters run both the hotel – with some classic, some stylishly modern guestrooms – and the restaurant, which offers really good seasonally influenced cuisine. There are three cosy dining areas inside; outside, there are tables on the terrace in the shade of the plane trees, which affords views of the orchards! There is art displayed everywhere in the house.

Name: Forst's Landhaus
Description: Run with great dedication, this restaurant is located by a small stream – tables on the terrace overlooking the water are in great demand! The seasonal menu uses plenty of regional produce, such as lamb from the Bavarian Jura. The vegetarian dishes are also appealing, imaginative and delicious! The friendly maître d' provides good service with a personal touch. There are simple but well-kept guestrooms for overnight stays.

Name: Landhaus Hohenlohe
Description: This long-standing family business, now with Matthias Mack at the helm, is run according to a winning formula. In a very pleasant informal atmosphere, extremely friendly and experienced waitstaff are always on hand. The delicious food is freshly prepared and feautures regional and international influences. You can compose a three- or four-course set menu from the appealing list of options (also vegetarian) or order à la carte. Appetising dishes include porcini ravioli, baby spinach, Brettenfeld Jerusalem artichokes, truffle fonduta. The restaurant also has its own herb and vegetable garden. Overnight accommodation is available in this well-kept country house nestled in a residential area.

Name: Zur Sonne
Description: Run by the Glück family, this place serves fantastic seasonal dishes and regional classics. From game to Altmühltal lamb and their unique "Sauerbraten 2.0", the menu is packed with delicious options. With a clear commitment to sustainability and a preference for local produce, the kitchen team serves up dishes that are beautifully balanced in flavour. The bright, modern conservatory is a delightful space, as is the splendid terrace in summer. Comfortable and attractive guestrooms.

Name: Gaststube
Description: Housed inside Krone is this pleasant and down-to-earth restaurant that is also run by the Wölfelschneider family. The Gaststube menu will appeal to those who appreciate traditional regional fare. As well as delicious food, guests can enjoy the friendly service, which contributes to the congenial atmosphere. In summer, the terrace is a dream!

Name: Bärenkrug
Description: Whether you are seated in the Friesenstube or the secluded courtyard garden with its old chestnut trees and abundant greenery, at the Sierks family's restaurant you can look forward to quality cuisine with a regional and seasonal focus in the form of daily specials, classics or set menus. Tip: Be sure to try the home-made chocolates. The hotel of the same name, also part of this long-standing family business, has attractive, comfortable guestrooms.

Name: Freihardt
Description: Eating here is a real pleasure! The cuisine is international and seasonal, the highlight being the Bavarian beef steaks. They also serve burgers on Wednesdays and Thursdays. Head here on a Saturday for a three-course surprise lunch or on a Sunday for a traditional home-style roast. A friendly atmosphere reigns in the restaurant and its conservatory, and the terrace on the busy street is a place "to see and be seen". Right next door is the restaurant's own butcher's shop, which for many years has employed so-called humane slaughtering methods.

Name: Gasthaus Waltz
Description: A fashionable and lively restaurant in Munich's Glockenbachviertel, run by an enthusiastic young team. The secret of its success is the chefs' modern take on Alpine cuisine – sometimes creative, sometimes more traditional, but the presentation is always sharp, and the ingredients are the region's finest. Dishes such as the Tafelspitz-Sülze (jellied prime boiled beef) with horseradish, root vegetables and seed oil vinaigrette or the char with lentils, apple, trout caviar and beurre blanc can be ordered à la carte or together as a set menu comprising four or five courses. Wine is taken very seriously here and, consequently, the list is not only well curated in terms of quality, but also surprisingly extensive. Motorists should note that parking options are limited.

Name: Landhotel Krone
Description: Here, tradition rubs shoulders with current trends in cosy little spaces that feature an attractive blend of old brickwork, wood, steel and glass. The regional and seasonal cuisine is scattered with international influences. Medieval vaulted cellar for events. This family-run business also offers attractive, individually designed guestrooms and wellness facilities.

Name: Kulturhof Stanggass - Gasthaus
Description: The Gasthaus, which annexes the Kulturhof Stanggass located on the road between Bischofswiesen and Berchtesgaden, offers a culinary alternative to the restaurant Solo Du. Done out in light wood, the minimalist-style interior has a modern yet cosy feel. The glass façade affords views of the garden, which includes a children's playground. Book a spot at the "Stammtisch", a long handmade wooden table for 25 diners. The menu draws on the region and nature's bounty – the ingredients are locally sourced. The good food is complemented by friendly service.

Name: WEINreich
Description: A modern wine bar in a tranquil little village. The historical setting has been given a makeover including attractive decorative touches; to complement the numerous wine bottles on display, the ceiling is adorned with a depiction of the wine route marked with its famous wine villages. Outside, there is a charming courtyard terrace. Led by Jeanette and Henning Weinheimer, the very friendly and proficient team go about their work with great dedication, serving high-quality regional and seasonal cuisine – as a set menu or à la carte. Meat-eaters should ask about their "Steak Weeks"; Sunday roast is available if pre-ordered. You can also purchase their bread, which they bake on site. For overnight stays there are really pleasant guestrooms.

Name: CARUSO Pastabar
Description: Neapolitan-born Anna and Marcello Caruso, working with Emanuele Barbaro, have come up with a cool concept: a flavoursome, relaxed and lively dining experience, played out in a chic atmosphere. Service comes courtesy of a relaxed, attentive team under the tutelage of the charming proprietress. They serve a three-course set menu, which you can put together yourself and add to as you wish – the main course is flavoursome house-made pasta! N.B. You should allow about two hours for three courses. There are two seatings: 6pm and 8.30pm. Trendy drinks at the bar.

Name: Weinstube zum Engel
Description: With his Weinstube (or "wine tavern"), Christian Beck, son of the owner of the hotel and restaurant Heiligenstein, also located in Neuweier near Baden-Baden, has brought a new layer of culinary enrichment to the village. The cuisine here comprises regional, seasonal and Mediterranean dishes. Vegetarian dishes and small bites are also available. Regional wines are offered. Friendly service in a cosy interior that blends tradition and modernity. The terrace is also lovely.

Name: Rebblick
Description: Housed in Korb's Remstalhalle, this restaurant has retained a certain 1970s feel, while incorporating chic modern design features and an attractive glass façade. Jochen Gromann serves up flavoursome seasonal cuisine drawing on regional and international influences (including Swabian Zwiebelrostbraten). Managed by Nadine (his wife), the front-of-house team are friendly and well drilled and provide astute wine recommendations. Delightful terrace – with a view of the vineyards, depending on where you sit.

Name: Regional Friesoythe
Description: "Regional" is more than a name here, it is a philosophy! Since September 2022, Timo Plenter and Ina Stuke have been running this traditional restaurant in the centre of town and are completely committed to sustainability. The chef cooks honest flavoursome food, sourcing seasonal ingredients from the region and favours local suppliers. You can choose between a three to five-course menu (also vegetarian) and the 7-course "Signature Dish" menu. The interior decor marries modern and rustic elements. Cordial service from the attentive staff. In summer a few tables are set up in front of the building.

Name: Wirtshaus Mättle
Description: Dating from 1848, this inn has been given a tastefully modern makeover. High-quality, market-fresh produce is used to conjure up cuisine that looks to the Mediterranean as well as the local region for inspiration. In addition to à la carte dishes (the whole roasted trout, for instance, is a house speciality), a surprise menu is also on offer - conventional or vegan. Guests also like to come for the reasonably priced 2-course lunch menu. Gorgeous terrace. Located in the basement, bar-cum-restaurant THEODOR is ideal for events.

Name: Salt & Silver Levante
Description: Salt & Silver now boasts a new charming urban restaurant serving Levantine cuisine next door to its Latin American eatery in the St Pauli neighbourhood. Here you dine mezze-style, following the example of the cuisine of the southeastern corner of the Mediterranean: Levant-inspired dishes, both big and small, come together to the table and are made for sharing. To really experience what this place is all about, order the "Yallah-Combo", which is ideal for group dining. Overlooking the harbour, the terrace in front of the building is fabulous in summer.

Name: Geberts Weinstuben
Description: Freshness, flavour, aroma – this is how you might sum up Frank Gebert's cuisine. He also likes to use produce from the region to create his classic dishes. The restaurant, located in a side street not far from the Rhine, is furnished with a touch of elegance; outside, meanwhile, it is pleasant to sit in the courtyard on the vine-clad terrace.

Name: Landgasthof Schwanen
Description: A Landgasthof – country inn – in the best sense! The Fräulin family is committed to its patrons; the whole establishment is very well looked after, from the restaurant to the comfortable guest rooms. The tasty food is fuss-free and influenced by regional culinary tradition. A visit is not least worthwhile during asparagus season - these dishes are particularly well-known. As for the interior, the dining rooms are done out in a traditional-rural style with the occasional modern touch.

Name: Landgasthof zum Müller
Description: At their established country inn, Ingrid and Markus Buchner serve fresh regional and seasonal cuisine with international and Mediterranean influences – responsible for this is chef Marcel von Winckelmann. The service is friendly and cordial, the rustic-style restaurant rooms are inviting, and the leafy terrace with its small open barn ("Salettl") is delightful. They have modern rural-style guestrooms, too.

Name: Hirsch
Description: This picture-perfect Baden country inn boasts tastefully designed, inviting guestrooms and serves excellent food. The owner's son-in-law runs the kitchen, serving up regional cuisine that showcases seasonal produce – dishes such as braised beef cheeks in a Burgundy sauce or saddle of venison with cranberries and spaetzle are especially popular. Putting the emphasis on flavour and proper seasoning, only the finest and freshest ingredients are used. Charming and professional front-of-house team.

Name: das asam
Description: You dine in the Modlersäle, once the refectory, on the first floor of this former monastery building. It has beautiful high ceilings decorated with lovely mouldings and paintings – the historical setting is tastefully combined with an interior design of clean lines. The food is modern and seasonal, and the tasty Zwiebelrostbraten (fried beef and onions in gravy) is a classic. On warm summer days, the terrace in the cloister garden of the monastery courtyard is idyllic! You can stay overnight in well-kept, simply charming guestrooms.

Name: Die Krone
Description: Chef Volker Lahn continues the family tradition in the kitchen at Die Krone. The cosy Baden setting of the dining rooms is matched by good local Baden cooking. The seasonal fare is available in the form of a set menu or à la carte.

Name: Gasthaus Schwanen
Description: Now in its third generation, this charming family-run inn opposite the church serves very good food. A cosy atmosphere awaits you inside, while the idyllic garden terrace beckons outside. Here, they keep chickens, hunt game and make schnapps, and their own produce often features on the menu. Accommodation options: Gasthaus Schwanen, Villa Pfarrhus with its beautiful garden, and the Malermeisterhaus guesthouse.

Name: Goldener Adler
Description: Everyone would love to have a cosy and buzzing restaurant like this in their neighbourhood! The contemporary decor strikes a rustic note; the traditional regional cuisine is based on fresh produce. The menu ranges from classics such as cordon bleu with potato salad to internationally inspired dishes such as pan-fried prawns with shellfish noodles. Vegetarian options are also available. The beautiful large terrace (you can park here in winter) is a stand-out feature in this city-centre location.

Name: Gutsküche
Description: It is a real pleasure to see the terrific produce gracing the plates at Gutsküche, just outside Hamburg – this is sustainable gastronomy par excellence! The organic ingredients from their own estate, Hofgut Wulksfelde, are the absolute focal point of the cooking, and the menu features vegetarian dishes that can be supplemented with fish, poultry and meat "garnishes". GUT's caprese with hand-scooped buffalo mozzarella, rocket and tomato pesto, for example, is a marvellous seasonal dish – the wonderful aroma of fully ripe tomatoes remains in the memory! Tip: Snacks can be purchased at GutsDeli and delicatessen shop, as well as organic produce in the on-site farm shop. In summer: organic ice cream in the lovely GutsGarten.

Name: Lohmayr Stub'n
Description: Chef Sebastian Oberholzner puts his heart and soul into his cooking, meaning his delicious dishes are much in demand. He uses seasonal and regional ingredients, making sure to know his suppliers and the origin of the produce. There is also a good selection of wines. Diners enjoy charming service in the setting of a fine historical building.

Name: Sticky Fingers
Description: Located in the beautiful Old Town, this is a fashionable restaurant and bar. The decor and background music are very much on trend and lend this laid-back establishment something of a club atmosphere. The appealing international menu features flavoursome dishes including fish and chips, panzanella and paella – all served by very friendly waitstaff. As well as wines, there is an extensive selection of cocktails, another big draw of this place.

Name: Auers Schlosswirtschaft
Description: It's no surprise that this restaurant, run with dedication for over 30 years, is so popular! Diners are won over by both the cosy space that is beautifully done out to exude rustic charm and chef Astrid Hilse's fresh cuisine, which takes the form of a menu that changes on a daily basis. Top-notch produce goes into seasonal dishes with a definite wow factor, such as braised lemon chicken with roasted vegetables and garlic potatoes, or local lamb prepared two ways and served with olive confit and green beans. The service is friendly – and the chef, too, gets in on the act. Attractive tree-shaded terrace. N.B. Credit cards are not accepted.

Name: Bauernstuben
Description: This cosy rustic-style restaurant is housed in the venerable Ochsen Post. The menu features the traditional cuisines of Baden and Swabia, as well as internationally influenced dishes. Along with Maultaschen, Zwiebelrostbraten (fried beef and onions in gravy) and steaks, there are also less conventional options such as sour kidney or tripe soup. Diners can also look forward to a delightful terrace, attentive service and a well-curated wine list that includes a number of rare gems. Tip: You can purchase their wonderful bread to take home, and some meat dishes are also available for takeaway. Lovely guestrooms.

Name: MundArt2015
Description: Located in a beautiful spot not far from Salzburg, the attractive Gut Edermann hotel awaits you with tastefully designed guestrooms and a 2 700m2 spa area, as well as appealing dining options including Bauernstube1910 and MundArt2015. Friendly waitstaff serve up the flavoursome seasonal cuisine in a cosy setting. The preference for locally sourced ingredients reflects the restaurant's commitment to sustainability.

Name: Ramster
Description: An inviting family-run restaurant renowned for its fine seasonal cooking. A deep connection to the region is reflected in the use of predominantly local ingredients. The menu features traditional dishes – the Heidschnucke lamb is a house speciality not to be missed. Some dishes can also be ordered in small portions, and there are vegetarian/vegan options available. Lovely terrace overlooking the garden. For overnight guests there are exceedingly cosy guestrooms, some with balconies.

Name: Graf Everstein
Description: The Multhoff family's restaurant draws in diners with the promise of skilfully prepared food and wonderful views over the Weser. The friendly and attentive staff serve up beautifully fresh cuisine that sets great store by both seasonal produce and selected ingredients.

Name: Zur Linde
Description: The Trautwein brothers run this 300 year-old former posting house with its charming mix of historical and modern decor with great dedication. The menu includes Swabian classics such as Gaisburger Marsch beef stew, maultaschen ravioli and veal tripe with braised oxtail, alongside seasonal offerings. The rustic vaulted cellar is available for events.

Name: Landhaus Zum Rössle
Description: Family tradition since 1780! Here the hospitality extended to diners is just as important as the tasty cuisine made from regional produce. Besides classic dishes, a surprise menu is also served. In summer the garden is a delight! There is a fantastic barn venue for parties. You can also stay overnight.

Name: Landhotel zum Hirsch
Description: This traditional inn dating back over 300 years serves regional cuisine made with seasonal and predominantly locally sourced ingredients. The menu ranges from classics such as Hirschwirts Gaisburger Marsch (a traditional Swabian beef stew) and Swabian tripe ragout to Mediterranean-influenced dishes such as fried Atlantic sea bream fillet with a white wine sauce on bell peppers and courgettes with risotto. This elegant family-run establishment has comfortable guestrooms.

Name: Das August
Description: It's no wonder this place is so popular! The Gehrke family have made it a point of honour to uphold their long-standing tradition of offering outstanding cuisine, plus friendly service and an inviting atmosphere. The food is fresh, seasonal and made with select ingredients. The menu includes, for example, vegetable curry, roast corn-fed chicken breast with mushrooms or local game. There is also an impressive selection of schnitzels. Well-stocked wine cabinet. Attractive guestrooms at Schmiedegasthaus Gehrke.

Name: Feine Speiseschenke
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: This friendly restaurant is located in a small village in a quiet side valley surrounded by woods and meadows. It offers seasonal cuisine bearing regional and international influences. They even raise Scottish Highland cattle here. You can choose from various set menus (including a vegetarian one) or go à la carte and opt for one of the classic dishes.

Name: Das Fetzwerk
Description: Das Fetzwerk feels modern and pleasantly uncomplicated - this applies as much to the trendy ambience as the food. Tasty, fresh dishes with a certain pizazz are served here. The service is friendly and attentive. The restaurant is located in the comfortable Das Freiberg hotel. Open from 12 noon. Tip for sunny days: the terrace.

Name: RÖHMS DELI
Description: A pleasantly straightforward concept that goes down well with restaurant-goers. The seasonal and internationally influenced cuisine is served in a friendly, modern atmosphere. The à la carte menu is complemented by daily specials on the board. At lunchtime, there is an additional dish of the day. For those with a sweet tooth, the counter displaying fine home-made pastries is a highlight! Attentive service. The terrace – in a traffic-calmed area here in the middle of the city – is also pleasant. There is a pretty holiday apartment for overnight stays.

Name: Die Krone
Description: Owner and head chef Markus Elison previously worked at Herrengass in Gschwend, where he proved his worth in the kitchen. Here, he cooks up delicious dishes made with high-quality ingredients. His cuisine is regional, with some Mediterranean influences. One of his signature dishes is Zwiebelrostbraten in a Spätburgunder wine sauce with spaetzle. Dine à la carte or opt for the seasonal set menu or "Das Krone Menü". Friendly service. Sleek modern decor. For overnight stays, there are functional yet chic guestrooms available – the prices are lower in the guesthouse.

Name: Am Osterfeuer
Description: Hans-Jörg Dunker and his team have long been synonymous with quality and Westphalian cuisine with an international twist. The restaurant interior is attractive and cheerful, having been given a skilful modern makeover, but care has been taken to leave the traditional character of the building intact. One of the chef's specialities is the wonderful fish and shellfish soup with aioli, bread and parmesan. A gorgeous terrace for summer.

Name: Schorse im Leineschloss
Description: This pleasantly down-to-earth restaurant is the second in the cube-like extension of the Leineschloss, along with Votum. The flavoursome food is made with select ingredients and draws on French influences, for example pan-fried meagre with Champagne cabbage, grapes and herby mashed potatoes. They also serve a simpler quick lunch set menu. Delightful terraces at the Leinewehr and on Platz der Göttinger Sieben.

Name: Froschgrundsee
Description: This appealing country house lies above a small lake, in the town's Schönstädt neighbourhood. Hannes Scammell shows his culinary mettle, cooking up fresh and tasty seasonal dishes. You can also dine outside. At lunchtime, the menu is somewhat reduced. The good cuisine is complemented by the friendly service provided by the hostess. Barbecue fans, take note: they also organise regular evening events dedicated to grilled meats.

Name: Cube by Mika
Description: This trendy and lively spot is in the heart of Schwerin – the cathedral is very close by and the castle is also within easy walking distance. The atmosphere is laid-back and casual in this maisonette-style restaurant occupying two levels, and on the lower floor, diners can choose between high tables or counter seats with views of action in the kitchen. This place specialises in delicious izakaya cuisine – predominantly Asian dishes and finger food for sharing. On certain days, they also propose an ambitious tasting menu. Don't forget to book!

Name: Jäger & Lustig
Description: What a cosy and quaint-feeling place, serving what the owners term "Heimatküche": think hearty, fresh, flavoursome cuisine. Classic German dishes are the stars of the show – game and goose are specialities of the house. They are at pains to use regional ingredients and remain aligned with the seasons. Service courtesy of friendly and competent staff. Make the most of the beer garden in summer.

Name: Melkhus
Description: The former cowshed of this beautifully renovated historical Immenhof estate houses this charming alternative to the Rodesand restaurant. The cuisine is traditional, regional and seasonal, made with top-quality, fresh produce. The classics on the menu include Holstein-style sour meat and roasted suckling pig ham. Vegetarian options are also available. The food is complemented by friendly service and a cosy, rustic atmosphere – the open fireplace is a nice touch. In summer, make a beeline for the terrace, which overlooks the lake. Coffee and cake are served in the afternoon. Pick up some home-made jam, souvenirs etc at the farm shop.

Name: Bistro Margarete
Description: With this lovely bistro, Thorsten Bender offers an alternative to sein, his restaurant right next door. The place has a stylish vibe and lively atmosphere; the terrace in the courtyard is irresistible in summer with its romantic feel. The commitment that the owners bring to their work is palpable – both in the delicious regional cuisine, which includes classic and modern dishes, and the inviting and pleasingly laid-back service under the direction of the lady of the house. Good food is accompanied by wines at prices that won't break the bank. Lots of people come for the bargain lunch set menu.

Name: WurzelWerk
Description: This restaurant lives up to its name: Wurzel, meaning "root", signifies a dedication to the local terroir, Werk, meaning "craft", highlights a commitment to artisanal cooking techniques – chef-patron Benjamin Bendzko puts both into practice in his market-fresh cuisine. Exceptional and almost exclusively regional ingredients are used to create flavoursome and pleasingly down-to-earth dishes. Two buildings, built in 1875 as a farmstead, now house a guesthouse (with a café at weekends) and this restaurant, whose rustic charm and pretty decor make for a cosy atmosphere. In summer, the garden terrace is the place to be.

Name: MaMi's
Description: Having gained many years of experience in the fine dining sector, brother-and-sister team Marcel and Miriam Hertrampf have opened this laid-back little restaurant. The location alone is great: the street lined with tall trees and buzzing with a lively atmosphere has a charm all of its own – the terrace on the wide pavement is especially inviting. In the kitchen, patron Marcel serves up flavoursome modern fusion cuisine, drawing on a wealth of culinary influences from Spanish to Asian, with or without meat. There is also a sharing menu comprising eight or ten small dishes. The service team led by hostess Miriam is charming and professional. She is a professionally trained sommelier and will be happy to guide you through the wine list, which features around 200 different labels.

Name: Berggasthof Schlüssel
Description: This mountain inn dating back over a hundred years is located at an altitude of 700m in the district of Pfaffenberg. Your dedicated hosts propose regional dishes that are in tune with the seasons and peppered with modern touches, to be savoured in cosy dining rooms with plenty of rustic charm. If you fancy a bottle of wine with your meal, why not stay over in the well-kept guestrooms?

Name: Dorfstuben
Description: The two charming farmhouse dining rooms (the "Clock Room" and the "Förster Jakob Room", which date back to the 19C, have been lovingly and authentically decorated down to every last detailare. Extremely cordial waitresses in traditional dirndl attire serve excellent seasonal and regional cuisine, including game from the hotel's own hunting grounds and trout from its fish farm. The braised beef roulade in Pinot Noir sauce is equally tempting. "Dorfstuben Classics" such as, such as the Zwiebelrostbraten (fried beef and onions in gravy) with maultasche and sauerkraut are also popular, not to mention the wonderful apple cakes! Tip: Take a look at the set menu of the day.

Name: Alter Esel
Description: The couple who run this restaurant put everything they have into creating a warm atmosphere and serving seasonal cuisine that draws on regional and Mediterranean influences. The set menu also comes in a vegetarian version. In addition to the cosy, lovingly decorated dining area inside, there are a handful of outdoor tables affording views of the historical buildings of this charming little town. This business is a Slow Food member and is committed to sustainability.

Name: Michels Stern
Description: The Michel family have always run their restaurant with great dedication, and now the fourth generation is at the helm. Two brothers make this an experience to remember: Wolfgang draws on good produce to cook tasty dishes ranging from traditional home-style fare to refined cuisine. Stefan will be delighted to recommend the right Franconian wine to go with your food. Plus well-kept guestrooms.

Name: Funky Fisch
Description: Are you in the mood for fish of the uncomplicated and Asian-inspired variety? Then head to the trendy and lively Funky Fisch by The Duc Ngo. The centrepiece is the large fish counter, where you choose the fish you want to eat, which is then prepared in the open kitchen. A wide range of Asian food, from Chinese to Vietnamese, is served, with influences from all over the world.

Name: Speisemeisterei Burgthalschenke
Description: The Großhammer family has been renowned for its good cooking for years! Diners can choose between the set menu or classic dishes. The cuisine follows the seasons, with ingredients being sourced in the local area. Laid out over three levels, the restaurant also has a lovely terrace. On a practical note: large car park.

Name: Zum Kreuz
Description: This inn has existed since 1683. Matthias Schwer is the 4th generation of the family to carry on the tradition.
