Start with a drink in the shabby chic lounge or well-kept garden when the weather permits. During the day a simple grazing menu is offered, but it’s the evening tasting format that holds the most appeal. The cooking has a creative make-up, with numerous processes involved, resulting in precise and eye-catching dishes; many of them incorporate intensely flavoured elements like dill oil with sea trout or mushroom ketchup with pork.

Name: Horse & Groom
Address: Bourton on the Hill, GL56 9AQ, United Kingdom
Location: Bourton on the Hill, United Kingdom
Description: Offering a lovely overall package that includes bedrooms and a warming atmosphere, this cosy pub makes a perfect base for exploring the Cotswolds. The 19th-century building has been renovated into a fine-looking property, with a bar area where every local and their dog can have a relaxing drink. The cooking is generous in both size and flavour, with desserts a highlight thanks to options like the terrific poached pear and almond tart. Several themed evenings offer particularly great value for money, be it ‘pie night’ or ‘steak and a pint’.

Name: North Street Kitchen
Address: 55 North Street, Fowey, PL23 1DB, United Kingdom
Description: In the busy months you might have to queue at this simple, trendy boat house conversion – but it’s well worth the wait. The menu is constantly changing as it’s informed by the freshest catch from nearby waters, with the array of seafood allowed to shine with a delicious purity thanks to the simplicity of the preparations. Fowey oysters are often a favourite, as is the signature brown crab rarebit. Owner Ethan cooks on his own and there’s an endearingly rustic, no-nonsense feel to the place.

Name: Capsule
Description: On the ground floor of a handsome Haussmann building, this bistro exudes Parisian charm: at the entrance, a few places at the convivial bar and a handful of tables; to the rear, a retro-chic space (snazzy green imitation leather banquettes, white walls, vintage hanging lamps) and an open kitchen reminiscent of – you guessed it – a capsule. The chef's comforting home cooking may be simple, but it is precisely executed using fresh ingredients. The roast chicken jus is quite something! The floating island with salted butter caramel and roasted almonds confirm that the proof is in the pudding.

Name: Adraba
Description: The team at the helm of this trendy restaurant with an upbeat atmosphere is a group of friends headed up by Israeli chef Elior Benaroche, once sous-chef at Balagan and an associate of Assaf Granit since his early days in the heart of Jerusalem's Old City. Tapping into the Levant and the chef's family history, this cuisine is a festival of spices and condiments: hilbeh (fenugreek paste), ezme (Turkish salad of charcoal-roasted vegetables), tahini, zaatar, harif (marinated chillis), tulum (Turkish cheese) – rounded off by a fine cocktail menu. A culinary voyage.

Name: Mirabelle
Address: Clos Vauban, 1 place du Colonel-de-Grouchy, Langres, 52200, France
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Martine and Laurent Petit have chosen to write a new chapter in their story on these premises that used to be an officers' mess – in an elegant townhouse next to the Porte des Moulins. The great chef has teamed up with Valentin Loison (in the kitchen) and Anaïs Bercegeay (front of house) to bring this ambitious project to life. Surrounded by a magnificent vegetable garden, the house has been turned into a hotel that accommodates two restaurants. At Mirabelle, the atmosphere is resolutely warm and convivial, providing the perfect setting for diners to savour the indulgent cuisine made with ingredients from the garden and small-scale local producers: think chicken pâté en croûte with black trumpet mushrooms, trout coated in a bread crust and cooked on one side, or roasted hazelnut millefeuille.

Name: ANTO
Description: Anto... as in Anthony Bisquerra, who, as you may remember, held two MICHELIN stars at La Table de l'Alpaga in Megève. Originally from France's South-West, he worked for a time in Bordeaux and La Rochelle. The chef fell in love with Haute-Savoie, its mountains and lakes. He tells this story at his establishment, in Annecy's old town, in a harmonious decor of whitewashed walls, wood and stone. His cuisine is a skilful balancing act, juxtaposing Savoie with other regions that he knows well. For example, popcorn flirts with Espelette chilli pepper, or fir buds with leek and trout gravlax; for dessert, chocolate and piquillo pepper confit ice cream find their perfect match in the spicy smoked sriracha powder.

Name: Le Sarment
Description: At this restaurant, the name of which means "vine shoot", a pair of chefs work in tandem to cook up honest, unpretentious cuisine. The ingredients and produce – particularly the vegetables – retain all their flavour and remain true to themselves, in dishes such as roast beetroot with beef tataki and a hint of garlic. The desserts, too, are meticulously made, a case in point being the amandine-style pear with green cardamom and yuzu. The menu-carte features mouthwatering dishes!

Name: Jarapea
Description: After spending almost 15 years in Chile, Michel Moutroustéguy and his partner decided to return to the chef’s homeland. In the peaceful Basque countryside, their table is open for lunch on weekdays and on Saturday evenings. The simply presented blackboard menu reveals a concise selection of sensibly priced dishes in a market-fresh vein. The chef seeks to highlight local seasonal produce, rolling out his know-how gleaned all over the world: sauces and gravies that pack a punch, consummate craftsmanship and high-flying seasonings. From starter to dessert, everything is spot on!

Name: L'Angle
Description: This hidden gem is nestled in a village at the confluence of two rivers – the Aveyron and the Viaur. A contemporary take on an artists' bistro, it boasts artwork on the walls and affordable prices. Working solo in his small, glass-walled kitchen, chef Arnaud Ronxin crafts ingenious dishes with the mission of showcasing seasonal produce. Think oven-roasted veal with confit potatoes and chanterelles, or lamb trotters with a red wine sauce. The more ambitious multi-course evening set menu is different every evening.

Name: L'Atelier
Description: Xavier Giraudet, chef at La Robe, has opened a second establishment in a bistro vein. Diners know they are in safe hands here as they tuck into traditional, flavourful and generous cuisine: succulent and aromatic pâté en croûte, melt-in-the-mouth black pudding with mashed potatoes, and a dessert inspired by the Paris-Brest, which is as indulgent as they come. You get up from your table with a smile on your face and your finances intact, thanks to the affordable set menus at lunch and dinner. A bright and modern setting; friendly service from the cheerful waitstaff.

Name: Turbulent
Description: Just off the tourist trail, these premises, once a crêperie, are now the new headquarters of Jarvis Scott. The bad boy chef, previously at the helm of Liquide, flaunted his talents on French TV's Top Chef. There is a rock 'n' roll vibe to this stripped-back, minimalist space: an intimate first room centred on an open kitchen and, upstairs, a communal table seating 10 guests in a more refined atmosphere. Far from the culinary mores of a seaside resort, the chef shakes up diners' expectations with uninhibited pairings that make a statement: frog's legs teamed with merguez, whelks mingling with sauce algérienne. The chef's message is loud and clear: bold flavours delivered without unnecessary frills. The wine list gives pride of place to natural and organic wines. Be sure to book to save disappointment! Love at first bite.

Name: L’Écrin de Marlène
Address: 6 square de la Source-de-l'Hôpital, Vichy, 03200, France
Description: Nestled in the spa district, the Fer à Cheval shopping mall surrounds the bandstand and the Source de l'Hôpital, which location lends it an undeniable charm. This is the setting in which chef Marlène Chaussemy has set up shop, creating an attractive contemporary decor for her restaurant. Opt for the dining area overlooking the park. By focusing on freshness and seasonality, this cuisine revolving around top-notch ingredients delivers on its promises: tender rack of pork, flavoursome parsnips, delicious delicately breaded black pudding, chocolate soufflé with ice cream and banana flambéed with rum. For those who want to take things up a notch, there is a set menu featuring more premium ingredients (eg pan-fried foie gras, scallops, lamb fillet).

Name: Table Penja
Description: After a successful stint at Le Garde-Temps in Pigalle, Cameroon-born chef Pierre Siewe now runs this restaurant with a modern bistro decor, where the warm interior is subtly reminiscent of Africa. As for the food, this former mentee of Yves Camdeborde seasons his local bistronomy with African spices (djansang, pebe, turmeric and the famous Penja pepper) and ingredients (hibiscus, yam, cocoa etc). This approach lends his dishes a unique personality: the perfectly braised chuck of beef is spiced up with a coffee, caper, red onion and hibiscus mustard condiment; the classic Mont Blanc dessert is accompanied by a green peppercorn ice cream that brings a fruity, invigorating freshness to the dessert.

Name: Dandelion
Description: Antoine Villard, previously chef at Double Dragon and sous-chef at Septime, and Morgane Souris, formerly sommelier at Parcelles, have polished up this little gem of a contemporary bistro in eastern Paris, with its waxed-concrete floors and façade giving onto a tree-lined square. The chef showcases the experience he already has under his belt as he turns out precise and creative cuisine that draws on a variety of influences. He brilliantly combines unexpected flavours: bluefin tuna with redcurrant and marigold; raw prawns with kimchi and ginger – made with carefully selected quality ingredients. Attentive, relaxed and smiling service.

Name: Erso
Description: Having met at Le Pantruche, these two form a crack team. In the welcoming blue and wood-panelled restaurant room, Marine Bert is in charge of service; Yann Placet's domain is the open kitchen, and seeing his handiwork from the handful of counter seats whets the appetite. The chef's main aim is to please, and he won't fail to win you over with his modern bistronomy, eg mushroom millefeuille with a coffee emulsion. Tempting lunch deal; booking definitely recommended for dinner.

Name: Ken Yamamoto
Address: 144 rue de la Pompe, Paris, 75116, France
Description: In a quiet residential street, the establishment of Kenichi (Ken) Yamamoto lies behind a midnight-blue façade. The decor of his intimate restaurant combines contemporary design with Art Deco elements. The eye is immediately drawn to the carefully selected tableware, which includes top-quality meat knives and Japanese crockery. Yamamoto's contemporary cuisine subtly incorporates Japanese ingredients: miso saikyo accompanies the foie gras, yuzu goes into the white wine sauce served with the pollack, and Padrón peppers in tempura sit alongside the beef tenderloin. There is a single set menu in the evening; with options at lunchtime.

Name: Phébé
Description: Located next to Place du Maréchal-Juin, this charming little 1900s restaurant has a glass front, green wood panelling and listed ceramic tiles. Chef Pauline Nicolas, who trained at Maison Rostang, conjures up enticingly named dishes that live up to their promise once served. For lunch, a delicious starter of Morteau sausage, mushrooms and a vin jaune sauce, followed by trout with braised baby gem lettuce, and for dessert, it doesn't get more indulgent than the poached pear tartlet. Here, the high-quality ingredients are treated with the respect they deserve.

Name: Restaurant F
Description: This compact little restaurant with a chic, contemporary decor exudes a friendly vibe. The Spanish-born chef (who previously headed up the kitchens at Hôtel Raphaël and worked for Hélène Darroze) devises a concise menu of refined modern cuisine, carefully prepared, with meticulously plated dishes: potato fondant with truffle; sea bass, celery and liquorice; crunchy meringue with figs.

Name: Hestia
Address: 8 rue de la Huchette, Paris, 75005, France
Description: Hestia, goddess of the hearth, presides over this restaurant that absolutely oozes cachet, with its white beams, stone walls and mirrors. Normandy-born chef Loïc Dantec (previously at 114 Faubourg) devises a seasonal menu only, with dishes that hit the mark, such as Cantal pork entrecôte cooked over an open fire with sweet spices. All the meat is grilled to perfection on the barbecue, ready to be carved tableside. The chef cooks without showboating, making flavour the priority. His partner Filipe Fernandes competently and assiduously manages the restaurant floor.

Name: La Table d'Éole
Description: Sylvain Gauthier (formerly of La Maison des Cariatides in Dijon) and Valentine have set up shop in a beautiful traditional stone house in the heart of this Burgundy wine-growing village. Instead of a set menu, there is a short à la carte menu of dishes the names of which alone are mouthwatering. The chef's expertise shines through in every course with consistently winning flavour combinations (scallops, cauliflower mousseline, green apple and hazelnut sauce vierge, hint of ginger). The sweet finale hits a perfectly seasonal note with a dessert starring pear. The dining area comprises two distinct spaces: the first is contemporary, with grey tones and a glass-walled kitchen; the second, warmer and more traditional, is laid out beneath a stone vaulted ceiling.

Name: Bulle d'Osier
Address: Clos Vauban, 1 place du Colonel-de-Grouchy, Langres, 52200, France
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Wheelchair access
Description: A former officers' mess, this mansion standing proud next to the Porte des Moulins is now a charming restaurant, designed and set up by chef Laurent Petit. Both the name and decor of this elegant property surrounded by a large vegetable garden pay homage to the tradition of basket-making in Fayl-Billot – the birthplace of this champion of ingredients from Lake Annecy. The carte blanche menu devised by Valentin Loison (the chef from the Jura previously worked at Le Clos des Sens and Mirazur) is creative and on point, drawing inspiration from foraging (polypody), garden vegetables, local livestock (matured Black Angus beef), Saône fishing (carp ventrèche, matured pike-perch, catfish) and hunting (roe deer). These fine, well-balanced dishes are enhanced by sommelier Anaïs (partner of the chef), who oversees things front of house with professionalism and warmth, dispensing judicious wine recommendations.

Name: Les Gamins
Description: This buzzing contemporary restaurant in the heart of the city welcomes diners in an inviting space – terracotta-coloured walls, wooden tables, velvet-upholstered chairs and lighting fixtures with an original design using bicycle wheels and exposed light bulbs. The dishes, largely inspired by the market, are well made: poached egg with a smoked paprika and corn emulsion, thyme and garlic oil and guanciale; pork pluma with guacamole, kiwi and chimichurri… The wine list is predominantly organic and stars Burgundy and Jura labels.

Name: L'Altitude
Address: Le K2 Altitude, 356 route de l'Altiport, Courchevel 1850, Courchevel, 73120, France
Description: At Le K2 Altitude, this restaurant is comfortably installed in a chic mountain-style decor with an intimate atmosphere. The menu comprises traditional French cuisine, and the eye immediately homes in on the classics, the likes of which are served at the great Parisian restaurants – think calf sweetbread, truffle and crayfish vol-au-vent. Flavour and generosity certainly do not fall short, and the whole experience is thoroughly enjoyable, right through to the desserts by Sébastien Vauxion.

Name: Maison Avoise
Description: Having previously worked in some prestigious MICHELIN kitchens, (in the restaurants of Guy Savoy, Yannick Alléno and Jean-François Piège), chef Alexis Voisenet has decided to make his mark by opening his restaurant in the casemates of the old fort at Issy-les-Moulineaux. This historical site is a unique setting, with its beautiful contemporary furniture laid out beneath a stone vaulted ceiling. The chef's creative approach results in refined dishes such as John Dory, samphire, kale and rounds of green meat confit in butter, with a matelote sauce. The front-of-house team, all professionals with plenty of experience in MICHELIN-starred kitchens, provides impeccable service. The restaurant also boasts a cellar, where diners can enjoy home-made charcuterie and house-cured meats.

Name: Coup de Main
Description: Victor Berthe (previously at Rozó) and Clément Delécluse (France's Young Sommelier of 2021) have set up shop in the heart of the Saint-André neighbourhood in Vieux Lille. With good humour, the two partners welcome diners to their compact little restaurant and wine shop with an open kitchen and vintage furnishings. The short menu sets the tone: starters for sharing, a choice between fish, meat and a vegetarian main, and just two desserts. For dinner, there's also a tasting menu that brilliantly combines seasonal dishes with playful and varied cuisine based on ingredients from small-scale producers, with whom the duo maintain close ties. Natural wine list.

Name: Vous
Description: A gorgeous building typical of the sort you find in Megève, a refined decor with an abundance of wood, an elegant counter seating 14 diners: a warm welcome awaits you at Vous! Under the guidance of Julien Gatillon (previously at Le 1920), young chef Jean Pastre delights diners with modern cuisine prepared before their eyes. The finest local (and international) produce is used: vendace, watercress and caviar; langoustine, potato and Savoy saffron; farmhouse veal fillet, celery confit and lovage emulsion. Elegant, delicate dishes boasting clarity and bold flavours.

Name: Anata
Description: Under the same roof as Vous but upstairs, this light wooden counter serves traditional Japanese fare. All the nigiri, California rolls, sashimi, maki, tempura and gyoza are crafted with top-drawer ingredients, such as wagyu beef or Otoro tuna belly. Bento at lunchtime.

Name: Le Tire-Bouchon Rodier
Description: This restaurant taken over by Marc Favier embodies the spirit of a convivial wine bar, with its counter and tables conducive to sharing. The "picorages" (the term coined by the chef for his dishes) evolve according to the chef's inspiration and the names alone will make your mouth water: veal sweetbread fricassee with button mushrooms and vin jaune; kabocha gnocchi, Vieille Mimolette cheese and curry; brioche perdu, salted butter caramel and cream. Cooked with top-notch ingredients, the comforting and generous dishes are mostly inspired by traditional fare. The already extensive wine list is constantly being expanded.

Name: 19 Saint Roch
Description: Pierre Touitou – one of the emblematic chefs of the new Parisian bistronomy – has already made his mark on the trendiest echelons of the capital's restaurant scene (Vivant etc). Black and white floor tiles pave the way to an open kitchen separated off with a stainless steel-topped counter – eat here for a front row view of the action in the kitchen. The chef and his brigade can be seen conjuring up food in a fresh, creative vein. The seasonings and condiments leave nothing to chance – eg the house-made harissa on the ox tongue and spinach pkaila (Jewish Tunisian stew), or the fresh peas with capers, toasted pine nuts and barberry that accompany the bonito. As you would expect, natural wines take pride of place. Pure dining pleasure.

Name: Brion
Description: With a star-studded CV (including Pierre Gagnaire and Jérôme Banctel) to his name, chef Geoffrey Lengagne has opened this restaurant with a refined decor (waxed concrete floor, light wood furniture, open kitchen). An avid seasonal cook, he uses the freshest ingredients to deliver predominantly vegetable-forward and fish- and seafood-based cuisine. The roasted Jerusalem artichokes, Jerusalem artichoke purée and Tomme cheese sabayon, with XO sauce for spice and chopped mint providing a twist, epitomise his modern touch. The lunch set menu is good value for money; pricier and more elaborate fare in the evening.

Name: Kedem
Description: Previously cohorts at Miles (now closed), Gil Elad and Ronan Cadoret strike again! In this small bistro complete with a counter, they serve up a veritable feast of small plates celebrating the flavours and spices of the Middle East. Their dishes make good use of the locally sourced produce at hand (Landes free-range chicken marinated in sumac with a spicy chicken jus; shish barak stuffed with porcini and seasonal chanterelles). Other highlights include a wide variety of delicious house-baked breads (eg Yemeni kubaneh) and some excellent desserts, including a Lebanese turnover filled with a date and dried fruit mixture, accompanied by a tasty pistachio ice cream. The short wine list has a penchant for natural wines, in particular Mediterranean labels.

Name: Première édition
Description: In this pleasant bistro in the heart of the city, with its industrial-style interior, street art touches and an open kitchen with a waxed-concrete bar, Jonathan provides friendly, professional service. Meanwhile, in the kitchen, chef Aurélie cooks up creative dishes inspired by bistro recipes or comfort food, adding a playful twist by means of spices, herbs, berries or dried fruit. Examples include devilled eggs with red curry, an old-school pita bread with braised shredded beef and a sesame cream, Carnaroli risotto with chanterelle mushrooms, or Aubrac beef tenderloin with a chicken sauce and suji seaweed. This is tasty, lively fare with a sense of fun, and the motto "come, eat, drink" perfectly sums up the simplicity and bon vivant spirit of the place.

Name: Dasuke
Address: 375-2 Siwei Road, Da'an District, Taipei, 106, Taiwan
Description: The dining room features two areas – counter seats for diners ordering à la carte, and itamae for the omakase menu. The chef hailing from Niigata, Japan reinterprets flavours of his home prefecture using first-rate local ingredients, such as taro and root vegetables in a flavourful stew, known as noppe. His signature Dasu burger is only available on the omakase menu; the ingredients of the deep-fried patty change often.

Name: fumée
Address: B3, Regent Hotel, 3, Lane 39, Section 2, Zhongshan North Road, Zhongshan District, Taipei, Taiwan
Description: The sister restaurant of the Osakan yakitori institution Ichimatsu sports a dark colour scheme, reminiscent of an opera house. The young Japanese chef sources local poultry such as Hsinchu free-range chicken, and Wenchang chicken for his kebabs along with local herbs like prickly ash and maqaw. The set menu with 10+ courses showcases an array of textures and flavours. Consider paying extra for rare cuts such as shiro reba and kinkan.

Name: J Parc
Address: 1 Dexing Street, Sanmin District, Kaohsiung, Taiwan
Description: After formal training in the US, the chef-owner launched J Parc in 2023. His 10-course prix-fixe aligns with the seasons, presenting audacious creations that celebrate local vegetables and Japanese seafood, underpinned by French, Italian and American techniques. Mildly sweet bread made with chestnut flour is a nod to the harvest season. Ask for counter seats for up-close views of the chef at work in the semi-open kitchen.

Name: Yung Yen
Address: 528 Chenggong 1st Road, Cianjin District, Kaohsiung, Taiwan
Description: Formerly known as Yun Lai Fang, this place was renamed and relocated to this address in 2024. The light-drenched room over two levels has wooden furnishings that impart a home-like feel. Regulars will find all their favourites on the menu; these are impeccably made to order by the chef, the son of Yun Lai Fang's founding chef. His signature scrambled egg comes with bouncy, umami-laden shrimps enrobed in silky half-set egg.

Name: Su Lai Chuan
Address: 4, Lane 176, Section 3, Heping West Road, Wanhua District, Taipei, Taiwan
Description: Famous for ba-wan and taro cake, this institution celebrated its 70th anniversary with a facelift in 2024. The third-generation owner still makes ba-wan like his grandparents did – freshly ground rice milk is poured into a bowl before a filling of pork shin, shiitake, chestnut and bamboo shoot is added. The steamed dumpling is then poached in oil, and drizzled with a sweet bean paste and miso sauce. Add garlic purée or home-made chilli sauce for an extra kick.

Name: Gallina
Description: A fine-dining restaurant with a focus not just on the quality of the cuisine but also on a genuine connection between art and gastronomy. Here, chef Pavlos Kiriakis combines French and Greek culinary traditions in dishes that showcase fish and seafood in particular. This harmonious experience extends beyond the boundaries of food thanks to the team of mixologists who create sophisticated cocktails, each one of which is named in honour of a mythological character. In addition, the impressive wine list boasts over 800 labels from different countries. In this vibrant ambience, with its elegant marble tables and a completely open-view kitchen, it is possible to sit in front of the latter to watch the chefs in full action. The floor upstairs is available for a more exclusive and intimate dining experience.

Name: Merceri
Description: This welcoming bistro, close to the Herakleidon Museum is run by two chefs with experience gained at luxury hotels on the island of Santorini. Here, they showcase their talents through contemporary dishes with an international flavour, but which are based around typical Greek recipes. The offer is available à la carte or in a tasting menu, with wine pairing options.

Name: VERi TABLE
Description: A pleasant French-style bistro away from this delightful city’s main tourist haunts but which comes as a pleasant surprise thanks to its cuisine and friendly service. In this informal space, which is nonetheless elegantly decorated in dark tones and bathed in subdued lighting, savour dishes inspired by Provençal cuisine with a Mediterranean touch. True gourmet-lover and chef Aladin Parodi infuses his dishes with superb technical skill, with a focus on top-quality ingredients, as witnessed by the duck à l’orange – an absolute must here. The dining room is overseen by his wife, Christine Parodi, who devotes herself to providing exquisite service as well as managing the enticing wine cellar, featuring an extensive choice of French labels.

Name: GB Roof Garden
Address: 1A Vasileos Georgiou A street, Athens, 105 64, Greece
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Great view,Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: If you’re on the lookout for a restaurant that is a little bit special, this could be an excellent option on the 8th floor of the Hotel Grande Bretagne, thanks to its elegant setting and superb picture-postcard views of the Acropolis from both the delightful terrace and dining room. Despite not being overly extensive, the Mediterranean-inspired à la carte focuses specifically on fresh seasonal ingredients, with a special emphasis on Italian cooking, including a small section dedicated to pasta and risotto.

Name: Annie Fine Cooking
Description: This attractive neighbourhood restaurant, located along a tranquil tree-lined street away from the busy tourist heart of the city, boasts an everyday, informal ambience, along with a simple pavement terrace and striking touches of color in the dining room, with its open kitchen. It’s mainly local clientele flock here to enjoy dishes from the concise à la carte that are an updated take on Greek recipes and based around fresh, seasonal and locally sourced ingredients that showcase the country’s cuisine to the full.

Name: Linou Soumpasis k sia
Description: A casual and contemporary “new-age taverna” in the central Psiri district of the city where it occupies a former candle shop (whose products are still sold here to this day). Greek cooking is based around unpretentious yet delicious dishes that always showcase the restaurant’s commitment to organic ingredients.

Name: Ovio
Description: Run by celebrity chef Panos Ioannidis, this restaurant is, without doubt, an excellent choice for those exploring the busy streets of central Athens. In this spacious setting, divided into three dining areas (one on the ground floor, a few tables upstairs, plus a pleasant terrace) the chef offers a menu based around Italian cuisine. This includes homemade pastas, such as the delicious Gnocchi with a velvety sauce, diced pear, grated walnuts and finished with gorgonzola in two textures. These are complemented by meat dishes and pizzas cooked in the wood-fired oven, plus an extensive selection of Italian wines and a balcony where guests can savour an array of impressive cocktails.

Name: Simul
Description: Personality, irreverence, risk, youthfulness, technique and quality are the words that spring to mind when we think of Simul, a restaurant that is always focused on cuisine prepared “in-situ” with the very best seasonal ingredients. In the informal dining room, chef Nikos Thomas (perhaps better known for his appearances on MasterChef) offers his guests a choice between a continually evolving and creative à la carte and an impressive tasting menu.

Name: Aleria
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: Time seems to have stood still in this beautiful restaurant occupying a neo-Classical residence from the mid 1800s, where the delightful patio, contemporary decorative features and 19C spirit come as a pleasant surprise. Here, the focus is on updated Greek cuisine presented in two menus (both with 5- or 6-course options): one entitled Earth & Sea, the other, the vegetarian-based Garden & Nature.

Name: Aneton
Description: Aneton moved from its previous location in Maroussi to this stylish, two-floored restaurant in the heart of the city, bringing with it its vibrant, eye-catching cooking. Lunch is light, with dinner providing the most interesting options, and the seasons lead the way. Service is friendly and engaging.

Name: Dolli's
Description: If the thought of enjoying a pleasant meal with an idyllic view appeals to you, then this could be the place. This restaurant is located on the fifth floor of the luxury The Dolli at Acropolis hotel, a historic mansion that has been completely remodelled and boasts picture-postcard views of the Acropolis. The menu here is a combination of Mediterranean cuisine with Asian options prepared by a chef who conjures up dishes within full view of guests in the dining room. Precise and meticulously presented, his dishes are always based around top-quality seasonal ingredients. The gourmet experience is more extensive in the evening and is complemented by the extensive array of wines, including labels from leading wine estates as well as artisanal vineyards.

Name: SENSE
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Great view,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: Located on the 7th floor of the AthensWas Hotel, SENSE boasts a stunning panoramic terrace with truly spectacular views of the Acropolis at sunset. The cuisine is centred around two tasting menus plus an additional vegetarian option, on which the innovative dishes are a fusion of international cooking and authentic Greek flavours, with plenty of creative detail as an added touch. Many of the aromatic herbs used in the dishes here are grown on the roof terrace.

Name: Vezené
Description: If you’re a fan of wood-fired cuisine, we recommend a visit to Vezené (located next to the Evangelismos metro station), a bistro-style restaurant with plenty of elegant decorative touches and an impressive glass porch. The menu is based around traditional Greek cuisine, in which fire plays a key role and via which the majority of the ingredients are prepared, endowing dishes with their unique flavour. It also includes various types of seafood sourced from local producers, as well as aged meats and impressive pastas. At the weekend, the generously portioned Sunday roast is available, which can be enjoyed with all the family, along with the restaurant’s famous signature dessert and a real must: Ari's Deal Closer!

Name: Le Pavillon
Description: (Temporarily closed for refurbishment) As soon as French-born chef Jean-Charles Métayer set eyes on this delightful whitewashed villa he is said to have fallen in love with it and immediately decided to set up a restaurant here. On his menus (one with 9 courses, the other 12), guests can savour contemporary cuisine that constantly interlinks French and Greek culinary influences, as both countries are key components of the chef’s unique career and life. The delicious and unusual “chocolate and mushroom textures” dessert definitely came as a surprise!

Name: Varoulko Seaside
Description: If you’re looking for a restaurant with an authentic maritime flavour, this eatery overlooking the small yet attractive port of Mikrolimano will come as a pleasant surprise. Here, the relaxing ambience is in perfect harmony with superb views of the fishing boats moored out front. Traditionally, Piraeus is known as the port of Athens, hence the plethora of tavernas and restaurants specialising in fish and seafood located here. Varoulko Seaside follows the same influence, although chef Lefteris Lazarou takes his maritime cuisine to another level. The freshest ingredients are key to his cuisine which is based around the catch of the day (sea bass, red mullet, grouper, tuna, shrimp, prawns etc) and presented on an à la carte and two tasting menus.

Name: see|ds
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Wheelchair access
Description: A restaurant with plenty of personality located in a residential district of the city and which takes its name from the combinations of the word “see” and the initials of young chef Dimos Samouraki to create “Seeds”. The simple, modern cuisine, centred around locally sourced seasonal ingredients and a minimalist aesthetic, is showcased on two tasting menus (Short Talk and Long Story) that show French culinary influence and vary only in their number of courses. In addition, an interesting vegan option is also available. For those who prefer more exclusivity, the floor upstairs has a loft with an elegant dining space for 10 guests, where they can enjoy a more personalised experience seated next to the superb wine cellar.

Name: Okio
Description: Okio comes with a cool atmosphere and a laid-back vibe; order a cocktail and settle in to enjoy the experience. The chefs add touches of originality to traditional Mediterranean recipes to create vibrant, interesting dishes which feature some bold Asian flavours; fish and shellfish feature highly.

Name: Esthiō
Description: This restaurant, the name of which translates as “eat and treat” in Ancient Greek, occupies a charming neo-Classical building dating back to 1931 close to the heart of the city. Here, Albanian-born chef Elvi Dimitris Zyba curates Balkan-inspired cuisine which offers a fusion between different cultures and combines the traditional with the contemporary. His cooking takes its inspiration from recipes that his mother used to prepare when he was a child to which he adds a more sophisticated and refined touch. Examples include the traditional “Giaourtotavas”, made with lamb sweetbreads, yoghurt and rice, and various seafood-based options, such as the Octopus stew, wrapped in handmade filo pastry with a sublime salmon roe cream. Desserts also have a Balkan touch, such as the Grape juice cream served with grape must cookies.

Name: Pinus im Seegut
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Great view,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Following stints at some prestigious restaurants, Philipp Heid has been head chef at the Pinus restaurant at Seegut Zeppelin hotel since May 2024. Here, he has created a laid-back sharing concept featuring modern and light dishes. The menu is predominantly vegetarian, but there are also meat options. Feel free to order as you please – there's no traditional menu progression, and sharing is optional. The dishes are arranged according to their flavour profiles: fruity, spicy, with roasted notes, earthy, plant-forward… In addition to fine wines, they have a wide range of non-alcoholic alternatives. The decor is modern upscale, but the atmosphere is comfortably relaxed. There is also a terrace overlooking the lake and the Alps.

Name: SchwarzGold
Description: The journey here is an experience in itself: At 6.30pm, diners are picked up from the main car park by golf cart and chauffeured to this restaurant located on the expansive grounds of the Kokerei Hansa industrial heritage site. In keeping with the name, which refers to coal – known as "black gold", the decor here in the basement of an old gas storage features an elegant black and gold colour scheme. Led by Pierre Beckerling, the kitchen team serves up a modern and very creative take on Ruhr Valley cuisine that, while clearly labour-intensive, adheres to a distinct flavour identity. Setting the stage for the five-course set menu (vegetarian version available) are the amuse-bouches titled "Straight outta Ruhrpot". The chefs bring out all of the dishes themselves and are happy to answer any questions. The bartender's house-made non-alcoholic beverage flight is an excellent alternative to the wine pairings. For an aperitif or a nightcap, head to the large bar on the ground floor – the gallery overlooks the open kitchen.

Name: Restaurant 1250
Description: Even the drive up to the Boutique Hotel Blaue Burg is an exceptional experience: the view of the region is breathtaking, with a new photo opportunity at every turn. Against this sensational backdrop, the Schlachter family, known for their dedication to the job and their reliably good food, serves seasonally and regionally minded cuisine at Restaurant 1250 – making it a wonderful alternative to the fine dining restaurant, PAVO. The terrace with a view in the direction of the castle and Austria is simply divine. Good to know: they also serve lunch.

Name: Marcel von Winckelmann
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Armed with valuable experience gained in top establishments, Marcel von Winckelmann has struck out on his own with this restaurant with an open and friendly vibe. The centrepiece is the horseshoe-shaped chef's table wrapped around the visible kitchen, where you are right in the middle of the action. You can really sense the young team's enthusiasm for interacting with diners – this creates a personalised and authentic atmosphere. The seasonal cooking uses selected ingredients. There is one five-course and one seven-course set menu, with dishes such as Norway lobster, pumpkin, sea buckthorn or pointed cabbage, stracciatella, calamansi. A cheese course can be added to either menu. A vegetarian option is also available upon advance request. As an alternative to the classic wine pairing, the restaurant has a terrific and completely house-made non-alcoholic beverage pairing. Tip: book ahead! For those who prefer a more discreet experience, the private room can accommodate up to 15 guests. In summer, the sheltered terrace is delightful.

Name: Le petit CINQ
Description: This is a pleasant alternative to the two-star restaurant Esplanade in the very tastefully designed boutique hotel of the same name. The food is modern, with two set menus, one of which is vegetarian. Each comprises three or four courses and changes on a weekly basis. Le petit CINQ takes up residence in the beautiful rooms of the fine dining restaurant when the latter is closed. David Wottke, long-time sous-chef to Esplanade's head chef Silio Del Fabro, is at the helm in the kitchen.

Name: Marly Privé
Description: The restaurant previously known as "Marly" has moved and is now operating under the name of Marly Privé. In its new smaller and more exclusive setting, this eatery serves classic French cuisine made from top-notch ingredients – chef-owner Gregor Ruppenthal's love for France is on full display. A maximum of 12 guests per seating are lucky enough to partake in a five- or seven-course set menu in an intimate, elegantly designed space (on Fridays, four or five courses). Dishes have names such as "Our octopus salad depuis 1999" or "Line-caught sea bass from Quiberon, leeks, nori algae, pink onions", and are accompanied by a well-stocked wine list. The service team is friendly and attentive. Tip: Don't forget to reserve your spot!

Name: Osteria La Fenice
Description: A slice of Italy in Cuxhaven! Behind a rather unassuming façade on a busy shopping street, a truly welcoming osteria ambiance awaits – the decor features decorative wine racks, closely spaced marble tables and even a Vespa! Not to forget the authentic Italian cuisine made with high-quality, fresh ingredients – the sourdough bread and pasta are both made in-house. The wine list showcases Italian labels. Tip: Italian food items can be purchased to take home.

Name: MiZAR
Description: In April 2024, Konstantin Kuntzsch – formerly of the restaurant Speiseberg in Halle an der Saale – opened his own establishment near Frankfurt's Main River and old town. His business partner and co-founder Florian Mack is your host and sommelier, and heads up the friendly front-of-house team. Ambitious chef Konstantin Kuntzsch conjures up a creative seasonal seven-course set menu. The top-quality ingredients and wines are sourced locally. The attractive modern interior features eye-catching artwork. Tip: Book well in advance and allow plenty of time (dinner starts at 7pm and ends at 10.30pm).

Name: Damson
Description: Formerly known as The Winterbourne Arms, this smartly refitted former pub is now home to a quite formal yet intimate restaurant. Guests are spread over several rooms, enlivened by splashes of colour, while the open kitchen lets you glimpse the team at work. The menus range from a well-priced lunch offering and an à la carte to a seasonal tasting menu and a Sunday roast, where the meat changes each week. Whatever you order, ensure you finish with a coffee and warm madeleines straight from the oven.

Name: Duchy Grub
Address: Higher Harlyn Park, Saint Merryn, PL28 8SG, United Kingdom
Description: A friendly young couple run this endearing little bistro in a holiday caravan park on the north Cornish coast. After years of cooking for pop-ups and private dining events around the county, they now have a permanent space and we should all be very grateful for it. The well-priced sharing plates really pack a punch and showcase an expansive range of global influences; you could order a manchego snack, soy-glazed pork rib and kaddo bourani in the same visit. Two to three dishes per person is about right, but a group of four could probably eat the entire menu.

Name: Cardinal
Address: 14 Eyre Place, Edinburgh, EH3 5EP, United Kingdom
Description: Dark, intimate and moody, Cardinal makes for an atmospheric place to dine in the smart suburb of Stockbridge. The set menu – available in a choice of lengths – takes a modern, sometimes creative approach to Scottish produce from both land and sea. Preservation techniques play a key role in several of the dishes, whether it’s fermented plums to accompany the oysters or pickled walnuts to go with the chicken. An international wine list is on hand to accompany the cooking, with a leaning towards natural and low-intervention options.

Name: Walled Garden
Address: Lucknam Park, Colerne, SN14 8AZ, United Kingdom
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: The titular garden is that of the exquisite Lucknam Park, one of the finest country house hotels in all the land. Hidden within the carefully manicured hedges, behind the 18th-century manor house, is this inviting, glass-enclosed brasserie. Sit on the gorgeous terrace or at oversized, marble-topped tables in the bright, pristine dining room and choose from a concise selection of vibrant, proudly executed dishes underpinned by textbook culinary technique. Pastas, risottos and freshly fired pizzas add to the Mediterranean vibe, while the day boat fish is hard to resist.

Name: Donia
Address: 2.14 Top Floor Kingly Court, Carnaby St, Soho, London, W1B 5PW, United Kingdom
Description: Occupying the site where its neighbours Imad’s Syrian Kitchen and Darjeeling Express both started out, Donia is a hugely likeable Filipino restaurant that’ll have you googling flights to Manila before you know it. The young, Filipino-born owner grew up in the UK so expect to see plenty of homegrown produce along with those sweet and sour flavours. Crisp adobo mushroom croquetas are a must, as are the succulent chicken Inasal and the lechon (suckling pig) served with a lovely liver and peppercorn sauce. Bring friends, ignore the slightly testing acoustics and share the love.

Name: Ibai
Address: 90 Bartholomew Close, City of London, London, EC1 7BN, United Kingdom
Description: Large, airy and with an industrial-chic vibe that perfectly matches the buzz of its open kitchen, there’s something quite cool about Ibai. Backed by one of the co-owners of Lurra and Donostia, it takes those restaurants’ love of Basque cooking and leans it further towards the region’s French influences. The signature ‘Croque Ibai’ is a prime example and a delicious pintxo to start your meal with. Quality ingredients are used throughout, treated with care and often cooked over fire. Wine enthusiasts will be impressed by the well-stocked cellar.

Name: Mignonette
Address: 109 Kew Road, Richmond, London, TW9 2PN, United Kingdom
Description: How lucky are the residents of Kew? Not only do they have the world-famous gardens on their doorstep, but they’re also the beneficiaries of this terrific little restaurant. Simple, homely and French to its core, this is the epitome of a neighbourhood bistro. The cooking is uncomplicated, hearty fare; bookend your meal with the homemade bread and the pear tarte Tatin, which is well worth the 20-minute wait. Come in the day for the exceptionally well-priced lunch menu, where the dishes are just as delicious and generous.

Name: The Kirkmichael Arms
Address: 3-5 Straiton Road, Kirkmichael, KA19 7PH, United Kingdom
Description: A small, well-kept Borders village in the shadow of the ‘Ayrshire Alps’ is the setting for this whitewashed pub with a traditional aesthetic and cosy, homely feel. The extensive menu includes some global influences among the pubby favourites, but it’s the signature country pot pies that catch the eye, with a different filling each week and a generous enough portion to satisfy even the most hearty of appetites. Every dish comes with a wine or cocktail recommendation from the well-priced list, and the warm, welcoming team show a real desire to please.

Name: Ardor
Address: 45 Fore Street, St Ives, TR26 1HE, United Kingdom
Description: Named after a Latin word meaning ‘fire’ or ‘passion’, Ardor is a smart modern brasserie in the heart of St Ives. Chef-Owner Dorian spent a lot of his childhood in Spain and it shows on the menu from beginning to end, from chorizo pillow bread to crèma catalana. Cornish seafood plays a key role, given a vibrant Mediterranean touch by the chefs, while some produce is cooked over the charcoal grill. Get a table on the lower floor to watch the kitchen in action and begin with a sherry tasting to enhance your Spanish experience.

Name: Aragawa
Address: 38 Clarges Street, Mayfair, London, W1J 7EN, United Kingdom
Description: It’s all about the beef at this elegant Mayfair restaurant. Luckily, it’s beef of such extreme quality – so succulent, so naturally flavoursome and so expertly cooked over binchotan charcoal – that you’ll forever be wishing every steak was this good. The available cuts are all Tajima Wagyu, one of the most delicious and highly prized meats in the world, with only salt and pepper used to season the meat. The restaurant itself feels like stepping into someone’s (extremely well-decorated) living room.

Name: DOSA
Address: Mandarin Oriental Mayfair, 22 Hanover Square, Mayfair, London, W1S 1JP, United Kingdom
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining,Interesting wine list,Notable sake list,Wheelchair access
Description: Its stunning marble counter is an instant signal of the quality you will find at this Korean restaurant in the basement of the Mandarin Oriental Mayfair hotel. Students of the cuisine will recognise several elements, from kimchi and bibimbap to multiple forms of jang made in-house. It’s all executed with utmost skill and the mostly British produce is of superb quality. The chefs and well-versed service team work in impressive harmony and have a real desire for you to understand the cuisine, but most importantly to enjoy it – and you very much will.

Name: Nest Farmhouse
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Wheelchair access
Description: Part of a 1,000-acre farm and estate, this spacious restaurant is housed inside an extensively rebuilt former farm building that is impressive in both size and structure. The cooking is the sort of uncomplicated, rustic-style fare that makes you want to order every dish on the menu. Traditional options such as lamb faggot or confit duck leg are executed with suitable skill to ensure they’re highly satisfying. There are bedrooms available and a short walk away is a terrace where you can sit back and enjoy the peace.

Name: Raymond's
Address: 8 Stoney Street, Nottingham, NG1 1LH, United Kingdom
Description: In the heart of the city’s historic Lace Market neighbourhood, you’ll find this fun and welcoming restaurant that could scarcely be more on-trend. Sharing plates, counter seating, moody lighting, stylishly understated décor… it’s got the lot – and judging by the buzz it’s a recipe for success. Start with the fish crackling if you can, a totally addictive snack served with punchy homemade tartare sauce – it sets the tone perfectly for a menu full of immensely satisfying dishes that are both generously sized and priced.

Name: Arlington
Address: 20 Arlington Street, St James's, London, SW1A 1RG, United Kingdom
Description: The much-missed Le Caprice, a celebrity-laden London icon in the affluent environs of St James’s, has been reborn as Arlington. It has the same charming décor as its predecessor, all black-and-white photographs and ’20s elegance, with the banquettes at the back the best seats in the house. The menu dispenses with anything too trendy and instead keeps things classic and wholly enjoyable – think dressed Dorset crab, chicken Milanese and one of the best fishcakes in London. The service team play their part by running the place with a terrific efficiency.

Name: Mary's
Address: 8-10 Pollen Street, Mayfair, London, W1S 1NQ, United Kingdom
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus
Description: The one-time site of Pollen Street Social is now home to this relaxed and accessible member of the Jason Atherton stable. Its aim is to cater to all-comers and the chefs pull it off with aplomb. Those in a hurry can sit in The Blind Pig bar area with a Cumbrian beef burger and one of “Mary’s Blood Marys”, while a prix fixe menu offers good value and there’s a vegan offering too. The main à la carte is centred around prime cuts of British meat and fish cooked over the wood-fired grill with impressive technique.

Name: Chartwell
Address: Aldwark Manor, Aldwark, Alne, YO61 1UF, United Kingdom
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Wheelchair access
Description: This attractive restaurant inside Aldwark Manor boasts a range of eye-catching features; your interest may be captured by the boldly coloured fabrics decorating the room, the huge windows affording views over the lawns or, if you’re looking closely, the mirror with camera views into the kitchen. What’s more, one of the well-stocked bookcases even conceals a secret door into a snug bar that’s perfect for a digestif. The cooking itself consists of modernised classics on a choice of tasting menus, Romeo or Julieta – plus vegetarian versions Pol and Roger.

Name: Sesta
Address: 52 Wilton Way, London Fields, London, E8 1BG, United Kingdom
Description: Fans of Pidgin had little time to mourn its closure in 2024 as it quickly reopened as Sesta, thanks to the original restaurant’s former chef. The look of the room is similar, but gone is the tasting menu and in its place is an appealing à la carte, which includes delicious snacks such as pea and ham fritters and a beef ragu toastie. British ingredients like Yorkshire chicken and Chalkstream trout sit alongside European and Asian influences from dolma to tempura. There’s a short but terrific cocktail list and plenty of natural wines – and the delightful staff sashay around the small space in an impressively efficient way.

Name: Lan y Môr
Address: Coppet Hall Beach, Saundersfoot, SA66 9AJ, United Kingdom
Description: Meaning ‘seashore’ in Welsh, Lan y Môr is an apt name for this stunningly located beachside restaurant; grab a table on the enclosed terrace to make the most of the view. The menu offers something for everyone, whether you’re after ‘Sea’, ‘Pasture’ or ‘Land’, but in this location your eye is sure to be drawn to the oysters, ‘frockles’ (fried cockles) and fish of the day. Ensure you save some room for pudding, especially if the terrific chocolate and cherry cake is on the menu.

Name: Llama Inn
Address: 1 Willow St London EC2A 4BH, London, EC2A, United Kingdom
Description: Look for the bright yellow door, then take the lift to the seventh floor and you’ll find this colourful Peruvian restaurant, sister to the Manhattan original. The long, narrow room is bright and sunny, with an open kitchen and bar counter running along its length; there’s also a great terrace. A pisco sour, with some cheese yucas, will let your taste buds know that fresh, perky flavours are coming their way. If you’re new to Peruvian cuisine, then there’s a glossary on the back of the menu and the service team can offer helpful advice.

Name: NIJŪ
Address: 20 Berkeley Street, Mayfair, London, W1J 8EE, United Kingdom
Description: The Japanese concept of ‘katei ryōri’ – home-style family dining – is the driving force behind this slick Mayfair operation. Diners are split across two rooms, one more moody and clubby, the other brighter and featuring a small sushi counter. Endo Kazutoshi has designed the menus, which combine the katei ryōri sharing dishes with a sushi selection and Japanese beef cooked over charcoal. Unifying it all is an attention to prime produce, be it the wagyu, the hamachi for the sushi or roasted turbot with furikake and miso butter. Bookend your visit with a drink in the Nipperkin cocktail bar.

Name: RT Café Grill
Address: Royal Maritime House, 17 St. Thomas Street, Ryde, PO33 2DL, United Kingdom
Description: This detached period house in an enviable position overlooking the Solent is the latest enterprise from renowned Isle of Wight chef Robert Thompson. Here, he has created an accessible bistro de luxe offering something for everyone: pies, burgers, steaks, pasta – you name it, they do it and pull it off with aplomb. The dishes may appear straightforward, but the care and technical skill of the chefs ensure they really deliver on flavour. A large garden makes for a perfect summer terrace and the friendly, unfussy service is pitched just right.

Name: Pollini at Ladbroke Hall
Address: 79 Barlby Road, Notting Hill, London, W10 6AZ, United Kingdom
Description: The former head office of car manufacturer The Rootes Group is perhaps not where you’d expect to find an Italian restaurant, but Ladbroke Hall is no ordinary venue. Located at the top of Ladbroke Grove, it’s a restored Edwardian building that is now a haven for artistic types, holding exhibitions, workshops and music events within its century-old walls. The cooking is textbook Italian, with an ingredient-led simplicity and terrific homemade pastas such as spinach and mozzarella tortellini.

Name: Akub
Address: 27 Uxbridge Street, Notting Hill, London, W8 7TQ, United Kingdom
Description: Named after the flowering thistle that’s also known as 'cardoon', Akub celebrates traditional Palestinian recipes, while simultaneously invigorating them with contemporary twists. The colours and intense flavours are particularly evident in sharing dishes like the ‘crunchy mansaf’, which consists of crispy golden parcels stuffed with rice and tender lamb shoulder. Everything is served in a bright, airy space situated on an equally colourful Notting Hill street. Accompany the food with wine from a list combining French favourites with options from Palestine and Jordan.

Name: Quartz
Address: Rue de la Réforme 22, Ixelles, 1050, Belgium
Description: Local foodies still remember the street corner premises that housed La Canne en Ville for many years. Chef David-Alexandre Bruno has retained the soul of this former butcher’s shop with its wall tiles and floor mosaics. Bruno honed his skills and love of classical cuisine in upmarket establishments, as the personal spin he effortlessly adds to familiar recipes demonstrates. His take on Bellevue lobster is a splendid example: he pairs the tail with a skinned tomato stuffed with meat from the claws, samphire, a herby cream and vanilla-flavoured tomato stock. Sauces are one of the pieces de résistance of this chef, whose bold personality seeks to shine the spotlight on preferably local produce – simplicity and harmonious flavours are the goal.

Name: Divino Gusto
Address: Square des Nations Unies 4A, Nivelles, 1400, Belgium
Description: Despite the Italian name of this elegant restaurant, Marc Grislain’s style is far from restricted to the bel paese. He may be a fan of Mediterranean panache, but that doesn’t prevent him showcasing his mastery of classical techniques together with Asian notes. For example, he might flank a rare rib of steak with veggies such as cream of squash and ginger and a gutsy cooking gravy flavoured with smoky black tea. The sommelier and owner, Gaëtan Poels, can be relied upon to ply you with insightful wine tips to create the perfect pairing. Hats off to this establishment that is enjoying a new lease of life!

Name: Klaver
Description: According to chef Korneel Verhulst, there is no reason you can’t start your meal with fries, even in a fine dining establishment. So should you wish to kick off with piping hot French fries and a caper mayonnaise, then go for it! Such is the down-to-earth outlook of this friendly, welcoming establishment. Before finishing your meal with a pancake and coffee, try out the chef’s main courses, some of which are enhanced with Japanese notes. Finely diced kohlrabi, seasoned with a sushi dressing garnish a tartare of Holstein beef, grated Belper Knolle cheese, caviar and curry. Klaver adds a brand-new youthful dimension to fine dining, embodied by Grace, your charming hostess.

Name: La Maison Thai
Description: Adorned in wood carvings in tropical hardwoods, Buddha statues and paintings from the Far East, the setting is as charming as its name suggests (we especially love the room to the rear). The options on the expansive menu are every bit as authentic as the decor. Savour the classic aromas and depth of flavour of succulent chicken thigh in a fragrant massaman curry, or heavenly sweet and sour chilli sauce that elevates fresh spring rolls: a meal here is a leisurely culinary journey with these timeless dishes. Fans of Thai fondue have also come to the right place, but be sure to pre-order.

Name: Rock-Fort
Description: North Sea fish and natural wines are the bedrock of this bright, elegant bistro. Chef Laurent and Eline, in charge of the front of house, who first came to our notice at Amuzee in Zeebrugge, are going from strength to strength as they settle in here. The menu overflows in the generous produce of the North Sea with a distinctive subtle, sometimes spicy edge. The fascinating culinary score is depicted by almost translucent grilled langoustines, which are paired with a dashi umami edge or raw scallops served with green apples and jalapeno. Rock-Fort is alive and kicking – in every sense!

Name: Restaurant Cloche
Description: The bright, elegant venue of Tobias Clocheret and Wim De Mulder stands in the shadow of the belltower of Hofstade church and the front terrace is heavenly in summertime. Top-drawer produce like langoustines and sweetbread is pampered and delicately crafted into succulent recipes. The chef slices scallops into wafer thin carpaccio, adding a beurre blanc enhanced by fermented asparagus peelings, lovage oil and cauliflower textures. A felicitous feast designed to appeal to today’s tastebuds courtesy of a range of enticing textures.

Name: Bistrot de Pottenbrug
Description: This former café’s wooden bar counter, floral wallpaper, wainscoting and old wood-burning stove set the quintessentially Parisian bistro scene of this characterful town house, providing the perfect foil to a soul-warming culinary score that stars outstanding ingredients. Vincent Greeve enjoys crafting gutsy, big-boned recipes, exemplified by a melt-in-the-mouth house terrine of foie gras with onion preserve or a Rossini steak with a punchy port wine sauce, all of which define the chef’s consummate culinary technique. The Pottenbrug sings a splendid ode to fine produce.

Name: Contre-Façon
Description: Whether you prefer classic cuisine or something more creative, Loïc Pierard has it covered with his à la carte menu. Whatever you choose, his dishes are built on high-quality (often local) ingredients and precise cooking techniques. Al dente spaghetti in a rich and creamy sea urchin sauce, paired with a spicy langoustine tartare, or barbecued monkfish with crunchy vegetables and an indulgent Choron sauce – the depth of flavour in these dishes is second to none. The charming blend of historical and vintage decor is also sure to impress. Contre Façon is the real deal.

Name: Artis
Description: Hao Guo entirely redesigned the interior of Artis with a brand-new colour scheme of soft shades and a cornucopia of contemporary comforts. The food is emblematic of the veteran chef’s experiences in top establishments in Belgium and abroad. While the backbone of his cuisine may be Gallic, he doesn’t hesitate to add international influences. For example, his bouillabaisse reveals the full depth of the salty seafood and is underscored with a rich, yet subtle stock. Chef Guo has an undeniable knack for sauces and his culinary technique is second to none. The extensive menu impresses, as does the spot-on selection of French and Luxembourg wines.

Name: The Twenty Two
Description: Situated on the rooftop of the Metropol Palace Hotel, this restaurant offers fine views of the city and St. Mark’s Church, along with delicious cocktails and gourmet international cuisine. The menu features a good selection of steaks, which we highly recommend, accompanied by a variety of Serbian and international wines. With its soft background music, it’s the perfect place for an aperitif or a post-dinner drink.

Name: Enso
Description: The dishes served at this lively, modern and trendy restaurant are based on solid French culinary traditions, skilfully blended with Serbian flavours (the sea bream with Serbian plum gnocchi is both delicious and original) and exotic influences (the miso and mango cake offers a delicious conclusion to your meal). The focus here is on seasonal ingredients cooked and presented with real attention to detail.

Name: L'Adresse
Description: Housed in the Saint Ten boutique hotel not far from the San Sava church in the Vracar district, this contemporary-style restaurant is situated just beyond the modern and welcoming open-plan lounge space. European-influenced cuisine is to the fore here, with a focus on meat (try the Hoisin duck or the Saint Ten beef fillet, the latter the house speciality), although the menu also features a few fish-based specialities, such as tuna fillet and grilled or steamed salmon. Vegetarians will enjoy the kale rolls. The comfortable Lounge Bar is the perfect setting for a relaxing aperitif or post-dinner drink.

Name: Ebisu
Description: As soon as you exit the elevator on the seventh floor of the Square Nine hotel, you immediately step into this intimate and elegant restaurant (named after the Japanese goddess of Fortune) where you can choose to sit on one of the four bar stools or on the terrace boasting fine views of the city centre. The menu features Japanese cuisine, including sushi, sashimi, maki (the tuna maki with jalapeno pepper is particularly delicious), tempura (soft-shell crab served with wasabi mayonnaise and pickled ginger), teppanyaki, at least one ramen, and much more besides. The desserts, on the other hand, are modern European in style. The adjacent bar also offers a menu of “saketini”-based cocktails.

Name: Klub Književnika by Branko Kisic
Description: The young chef at this long-established restaurant popular with locals and tourists alike has been at the helm since 2019. Here, guests can choose to eat in a winter garden or in the dining room, where there’s often live music during the colder months. The menu features classic favourites, such as the Krempita dessert which has been served here since the restaurant opened in 1946, and traditional Serbian specialties (there’s a 25-minute wait for the savoury Gibanica dish), with the occasional interesting, personalised touch and a focus on careful presentation. Since its opening at the end of the Second World War, the restaurant has served as a gathering spot for writers, journalists, and politicians. It continues to host cultural events, including exhibitions and concerts. Careful attention is also paid to sustainable practices such as reducing food waste.

Name: Na Ćošku
Description: Situated to the east of the city just outside the historic centre, this restaurant boasts an intimate ambience that comes as a surprise when compared to its exterior. The dining room has the feel of a French bistro, with small tables, background music (often French), and a few cubby-holes that are perfect for couples. The cuisine has solid roots in Balkan tradition, featuring traditional soups and stews, such as lamb in white wine served with mashed potato and seasonal vegetables, various fresh pastas and vegetarian options such as vegan curry with chickpeas, sweet potatoes and green beans.

Name: Mezestoran Dvorište
Description: Both the bright decor and colourful tableware at this restaurant demonstrate the light, happy spirit of the Mediterranean, as does the array of tempting dishes on the menu, including chickpea fritters, tzatziki, different kinds of olives, typical “Dokos” from Crete (imaginatively flavoured croutons), as well as chicken and pork gyros. This is a pleasant, informal setting in which to enjoy traditional Greek cuisine, with a cool, relaxed outdoor space in a shady courtyard that adds to its appeal, making it very popular with locals.

Name: Magellan
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Credit cards not accepted,Interesting wine list
Description: This restaurant in Novi Beograd, the modern part of the capital, boasts a dining room dominated by a beautiful aquarium. Here, the new local chef, who has plenty of experience behind him, is ably assisted by a professional and attentive front-of-house team. Both the chef’s tasting menu and the extensive à la carte showcase original dishes with a hint of Italian inspiration, including fresh pasta dishes (fish and meat). We particularly enjoyed the excellent sea bass in a herb crust served with zabaglione and blanched fennel, and a highly memorable dessert (“Autumn”) inspired by the season with a mix of textures and just the right amount of sweetness.

Name: Bela Reka
Description: Inspired by traditional Serbian cuisine, this restaurant proudly showcases local and regional ingredients, many of which (such as their goat’s cheese and hams) are produced on their own farm in the Homolje mountains. In addition to the à la carte, there are two tasting menus based on meat and fish served with seasonal accompaniments sourced from all over Serbia, as well as from the restaurant’s own farm. Both menus offer a wine-pairing option. A professional yet simple outfit that is impressive in the way that it manages to maintain a high quality of cuisine and service despite the large number of covers.

Name: SkyLounge
Description: As its name suggests, this elegant, modern restaurant with a decidedly international feel boasts stunning views of the city (especially impressive at sunset) thanks to its location on the eighth floor of the Hilton hotel. The chefs here create a varied menu that combines elements of Mediterranean cuisine with Asian influences, with a whole page dedicated to different types of sushi. They have also added lobster from the North Sea and king crabs to the menu, which can be chosen directly from the fish tank. In addition to the wine list, you’ll also find a good selection of other drinks on offer. The lounge-style ambience adds to the enjoyable experience, creating a warm atmosphere in which guests can enjoy contemporary cuisine together with unforgettable views of Belgrade.

Name: Homa
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: It might be located in the historic Dorćol quarter, but Homa has a thoroughly modern look and feel. Take a sit on the leafy terrace during the day or in the intimately lit restaurant at night to enjoy creative cooking with subtle Italian influences where you can choose from two tasting menus or an à la carte featuring a selection of vegetarian, fish and meat dishes. The tables are beautifully set with classic cotton tablecloths, while the pleasant outdoor space is perfect for alfresco dining in summer.

Name: Pinòt
Description: This contemporary-style bistro is situated in Novi Beograd, a modern business and shopping district across the Sava river from Belgrade’s city centre. The menu features seasonal cuisine which changes throughout the year depending on market availability, including a small number of daily specials announced at your table and a tasting menu accompanied by an appropriate wine pairing  (one of the owners, Vuk Vuletiḉ, is a young, award-winning sommelier).

Name: Salon 1905
Description: Situated on the first floor of the 19C Geozavod building, this majestic, aristocratic restaurant boasts modern furnishings that provide a pleasing contrast to the marble, stucco, brass and gold-coloured decor which creates a truly spectacular overall effect. This sumptuous setting is the backdrop for cuisine crafted by two young chefs who prepare strictly seasonal menus that successfully reinterpret classic Serbian dishes. Ask for recommendations from the small yet interesting choice of Serbian wines, which are also available by the glass.

Name: GiG
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: Despite its slightly hidden location among the hotels and modern high-rise buildings in Novi Beograd, this recently opened restaurant is well worth searching out for its warm welcome, beautiful and elegant contemporary-style decor and personalised, modern cuisine. The latter focuses on ingredients sourced from small-scale producers and the restaurant’s own biodynamic vegetable garden, all of which are showcased on three tasting menus and an extensive à la carte. Although the restaurant is owned by the Imperator winery, the extensive wine list also includes international wines and some rare labels, as well as bottles of various sizes. The excellent service is efficient and professional.

Name: Legat 1903
Description: Although the best way to experience the international cuisine prepared by this local chef is probably to opt for his tasting menu, there’s also an extensive à la carte selection including a few vegan dishes. The wine list is as international as the cuisine, with labels from the United States and Argentina featured alongside bottles from major European wine-producing countries.

Name: Gušti mora
Description: It’s all about fish from the Adriatic Sea at this well-regarded restaurant just outside the city. It’s a comfy place with a rustic look and a long family tradition which started in the bay of Boka Kotorska and arrived in Belgrade in 2003 to share the same passion for good cooking. Italian-influenced cuisine is to the fore here, including a good selection of first courses.

Name: The Square
Description: Just behind the busy Knez Mihaliva shopping street, this restaurant takes its name from the Square Nine hotel – one of the most beautiful hotels in the city – in which it is housed. Situated on the ground floor, the elegant dining room has soft lighting in the evening, while a pleasant outdoor space is perfect for alfresco dining. The contemporary-style cuisine focuses on modern Serbian specialties offered in its à la carte menu. The superb wine list is complemented by one of the city’s best selections of cocktails, served in The Lobby Bar.

Name: Metropolitan
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Wheelchair access
Description: Although this restaurant within the Regency Hyatt hotel is situated away from the centre, it boasts a convenient location for anyone visiting the area for business and is the perfect choice for a relaxing meal, offering excellent service. The menu features international cuisine alongside various local specialties. The "Metropolitan Specials" include beef cheek cooked over a low heat for 24 hours, although it's also possible to create your own dish featuring something from the grill, a side dish and a sauce. The restaurant places great emphasis on ethically sourced produce, such as free-range eggs, and avoids ingredients like shark's fin and foie gras from force-fed geese. Recycling is also a top priority. Additionally, the wine list has been recently upgraded, enhancing the overall dining experience.

Name: Comunale Caffè e Cucina
Description: When the sun shines head for this super riverside spot in the shadow of Belgrade Fortress. It’s one of several whitewashed former customs warehouses with open terraces – but this one is owned by an architect, so inside it’s sleek and stylish. The classic Italian cuisine served here features traditional recipes such as tagliatelle al ragù, bruschetta, tiramisu and a few pizzas. Impressive choice of liqueurs and spirits, in particular gin, and good selection of cocktails and mocktails.

Name: Feld
Description: It may be in the city—Chicago's Ukrainian Village neighborhood, to be specific—but Feld is focused on the farm, sourcing most products from within a four-hour radius. Their passion is clear, as paintings of the farms they partner with line the walls, though all eyes are trained on the kitchen team as they work in the center of the room. Chicago native Chef Jacob Potashnick steers a tasting menu with dishes like pattypan squash roasted with brown butter and served in a fig leaf-infused cream. Other items include flame-kissed corn arranged over leek soubise and sauced with a caramelized onion broth; heirloom purple crowder beans in a pool of flavorful Benton's country ham stock; and Japanese white sweet potato pavé nestled in a creamy pecan puree.

Name: Baron
Address: Unit 46, Mina District, Doha Port, Building 415, Zone 19, Street 200, Doha, Qatar
Description: Baron is sister to a well-known restaurant of the same name in Beirut and occupies a striking, pastel-pink property in the recently redeveloped Mina District, home of the Old Port. It’s a large place with exposed pipework adding a contemporary feel and an open kitchen that’s very much part of the room. The menu offers a wide choice of what they describe as ‘Mediterranean fusion’, which means the addition of some North African and even Asian influences. Dishes like capellini with crab and shrimp toum are generous in size and ideal for sharing.

Name: TONO
Address: 6 La Croisette, Porto Arabia The Pearl Island, Doha, Qatar
Description: This restaurant’s narrow ground-floor entrance belies the glitzy, capacious dining room you’re greeted with two floors up. For wonderful waterfront views, you can also try to secure a table on the enviable terrace. The Nikkei cuisine, curated by international chef Akira Back, is a worthy match for the glamorous surroundings; the ‘prawn cigar’ will raise a smile, while the classic sea bass ceviche should always be ordered. The smart service team are chatty and alert. Look out too for the weekly offers.

Name: Morimoto
Address: Mondrian Doha, West Bay Lagoon, Doha, Qatar
Description: From the catwalk entrance to the DJ, from the theatrical cocktails to the uber-contemporary hotel in which it sits, it quickly becomes obvious that this is a beautiful restaurant for beautiful people. The sushi counter is striking and there are booths for those wanting privacy, but for most guests a night out here is more about seeing and being seen. The contemporary Japanese menu offers something for everyone, with wagyu a speciality along with items like king prawns and lamb chops cooked on the robata grill.

Name: BiBo
Address: The Pearl, Costa Malaz Bay, Doha, Qatar
Description: Acclaimed Spanish chef Dani García’s BiBo is found on a small island within the grounds of the palatial Marsa Malaz Kempinski Hotel and shares a detached property with its sister op, Lobito de Mar. Dani’s travels as well as flavours from his native Andalusia inform the menu; the tapas and sharing plates have a modern edge but a traditional heart. ‘Langostinos fritos’ and oxtail brioche are just two of the dishes not to be missed, while the chocolate tart is enough for two people. The room has a clubby feel, with a centrepiece fish tail hanging from the ceiling.

Name: La Mar by Gastón Acurio
Address: Street 900, Bldg. No. 25, Zone 61, Al Dafna, Beachfront, InterContinental Doha, West Bay, Doha, Qatar
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Counter dining,Great view,Terrace,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: Come for the beachfront location, stay for the vibrant Peruvian dishes at this whitewashed restaurant within the grounds of the InterContinental Hotel. Gastón Acurio is a fine ambassador for Peruvian food and all bases are covered here, from ceviches to anticuchos. The colourful, rustic dishes deliver plenty of punchy flavours and are perfect for sharing. As you sit and soak up the lively atmosphere, you’ll be struck by what a fun night out it all is. And the wallet-friendly prices make it even more appealing.

Name: Curiosa by Jean-Georges
Address: Four Seasons Hotel, The Corniche, Doha, Qatar
Description: The eponymous Jean-Georges is none other than the world-famous Vongerichten, who has brought a sassy Latino vibe to the elegant Four Seasons Hotel. Ask for a table in the bar for the Gulf views, and then sit back and wait for the band to start playing as you enjoy a sparkling selection of Latin and globally influenced dishes. That could mean a classic ceviche, tacos and tortillas, sizzling shrimp or crispy fried chicken.
