FacilitiesAndServices: Counter dining,Great view,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: Alaf is a bustling restaurant with a fabulous cocktail bar on the roof terrace – perfect for a romantic dinner for two overlooking Istanbul's eastern coastline. Chef Deniz cooks up dishes with various influences: sometimes it is inspired by Yörük cuisine, sometimes Kurdish, the list goes on. With his wood-fired oven, he enthusiastically melds authentic traditional Turkish recipes with new-age cooking methods. Whether it's al dente squid with an exciting Mediterranean twist using sun-dried tomatoes, or medium-rare goose breast elevated by satsuma and harissa, a diverse journey of discovery awaits your taste buds!

Name: Şans
Address: Hacı Adil Caddesi, Palmiye Sokak No:1, Levent/Beşiktaş, Istanbul, 34330, Türkiye
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Valet parking
Description: This elegantly appointed villa has been a favourite destination for business clientele since 1992. They come for the attentive service, private dining options and expert wine recommendations (be sure to try one of the Turkish reds!). But the principal draw is undoubtedly the cuisine: a fusion of authentic Turkish flavours and Mediterranean influences. From steaming cheese dumplings to a creamy mushroom risotto and slow-cooked lamb neck with barbecued vegetables: generosity is always on the menu here. A firm favourite with many foodies.

Name: Gallada
Address: Kemankeş Karamustafa Paşa, Kemankeş Caddesi No:34, Beyoğlu, Istanbul, 34425, Türkiye
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Gallada is the epitome of luxury. Located on the fourth floor of The Peninsula hotel, this exclusive restaurant seats more than 200 guests! Diners are drawn in by the stunning views of the Bosporus, the upscale decor and delicious cocktails served at Topside Bar. But they mainly come for the captivating fusion of Turkish and Asian flavours over the course of a culinary journey along the Silk Road. The melt-in-your-mouth tuna is first marinated in soy sauce, yuzu and ginger then combined with a tahini and yoghurt cream. You should also definitely try the tandoori duck and the restaurant's own version of baklava. At Gallada, an extraordinary experience awaits you.

Name: Çok Çok Pera
Address: Meşrutiyet Caddesi No:54/A, Beyoğlu, Istanbul, 34430, Türkiye
Description: Exotic artwork by a Singaporean designer gives this elegant restaurant a distinctive South Asian feel. Having spent time in Thailand, the chef has gained an intimate understanding of the nuances of its cuisine. Skilfully balancing spicy and sweet notes, he presents a diverse spectrum of flavours. As an example, he tempers a chilli sauce with the sweetness of fruit and a bold fish sauce. Signature dishes such as green curry with scallops and red curry with duck unfurl their depth and umami-rich profiles here. A slice of Thailand in the heart of Istanbul!

Name: Ruby
Address: Yıldız Mahallesi, Ortaköy Salhanesi Sokak No:5, Beşiktaş, Istanbul, 34349, Türkiye
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Great view,Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: With stunning views over the Bosphorus, a roof that can be fully opened when the weather is fine, and a terrace that turns into a DJs' playground at weekends: Ruby is one of the hot spots in Ortaköy. The menu comprises dishes for sharing, traditional Turkish fare and a tempting range of pasta and risotto options. And whether you opt for the penne puttanesca or the grilled sea bass with spinach and orzo in a cream sauce, rest assured that your meal will be indulgent and brimming with rich flavours.

Name: Zuma Bodrum
Address: Cökertme Caddesi No:36, Yalıkavak Marina, Bodrum, 48400, Türkiye
Description: Zuma is not at all out of place among the impressive yachts and luxury boutiques. This restaurant has a sophisticated feel with its phenomenal sea views, clubby vibe and laid-back atmosphere. They are open from May to October, delighting diners with their trendy take on Japanese cuisine. Think different types of nigiri, or salmon marinated in teriyaki then grilled and served with pickled cucumber. Meat lovers might prefer the 700g dry-aged ribeye. The extensive menu is full of irresistible options! Be sure to cap off your adventure at this hip establishment with a refreshing cocktail at the bar.

Name: Sait
Address: Yalıkavak Marina, Çökertme Caddesi No:2 D:06 Blok, Yalıkavak, Bodrum, 48990, Türkiye
Description: While the luxury yachts and chic boutiques may call to mind Saint Tropez, you are in fact sitting on a terrace on Yalikavak's marina. The maritime decor gives away the fact that fish and seafood are the speciality of the house. As you enter, you will see the delicious mezze on the counter, such as marinated sea bass cooked until translucent with a mustard and dill sauce. After that, you can choose your super fresh fish that will be served in a generous and simple fashion. Home cooking is at the heart of this family-run restaurant, and has been its key to success.

Name: Nobu İstanbul
Address: Süzer Plaza, Askerocağı Caddesi No:6, Elmadağ/Şişli, Istanbul, 34367, Türkiye
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining,Great view,Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Located in the Ritz Carlton Hotel, the Istanbul branch of the Nobu restaurant chain embraces the Eastern facets of this cosmopolitan city. Whether you choose a table on the large terrace, in the bar or in the restaurant, the setting is as hip as it is minimalist. The stunning view over the Bosporus and the Asian part of the city is quite a sight to behold. Modern Japanese and South American influences are blended here with great precision. Think sea bass cooked in a light tempura batter and served with a vinaigrette in which chopped pineapple and orange create surprising nuances. The menu is impressive, and the omakase menu aptly captures the essence of the kitchen's offerings. The selection of signature cocktails, Turkish wines, and sakes is simply delightful.

Name: Saku
Address: Bomonti, Cumhuriyet, Silahşör Caddesi, Yeniyol Sokak No:2, Şişli, Istanbul, 34367, Türkiye
Description: Located in the NOW Bomonti building, Saku is something of a hidden gem, offering an exotic and cosy dining experience. The restaurant's open space and long, extended kitchen are impressive. The cuisine is Asian with a big nod to Japan. The chefs like to let their creativity speak for itself, a case in point being their take on nigiri with tournedos Rossini that really melts in the mouth! Be sure to leave room for dessert, too. After all, you wouldn't want to miss out on a punchy combination of poached peach, buttery crumble and vanilla and umeshu ice cream, would you?

Name: AZUR
Address: Yeniköy Mahallesi, Köybaşı Caddesi No:71, Sarıyer, Istanbul, 34464, Türkiye
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Great view,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: As you make your way through this chic restaurant, you will certainly be drawn to the modern works of art and the panoramic view of the Bosporus. But what really catches the eye at AZUR is the seafood on display. The quality is second to none! All that excellent produce is showcased in dishes that fluidly blend Turkish and Mediterranean culinary traditions. Think Atlantic bluefin tuna tartare with creamy stracciatella, super-fresh fish on the plancha, paella or pasta. Meat fans are also well catered for. The servers will be happy to give you a few pointers to help you get the most out of this culinary adventure.

Name: Lucca by the Sea
Description: The idyllic Lucca by the Sea feels like a secret island getaway. The white sand, the crystal-clear water, the soft materials of the lounge-style decor: this is the Turkish Riviera at its best! Seafood dominates the extensive menu, be it barbecued, on pizzas or in pasta options. The chefs showcase their skills with dishes such as barbecued octopus escabeche garnished with fresh chives, or beef tenderloin tagliata. NB: This restaurant is only open in the evening. Lunch is served at Lucca Beach – the cuisine is the same but the menu is shorter.

Name: Yeni Lokanta
Address: Kumbaracı Yokuşu No:66, Beyoğlu, Istanbul, 34433, Türkiye
Description: A side street off the famous main road of Istikal Caddesi, a bright Mediterranean decor and the creativity of a discerning chef – welcome to Yeni Lokanta! Here you can enjoy Turkish flavours that draw on original ideas, resulting in fresher and lighter dishes that lose none of their exuberance. Order à la carte or opt for the set menu (a selection from the menu) and discover how the focus on vegetables, local produce and Turkish wines makes this dining experience all the more engaging.

Name: Kasap Fuat
Description: You enter a butcher's shop with an impressively well-stocked counter and are guided to the restaurant tucked away at the back. Here, an almost magical atmosphere reigns in the colourful dining areas, and that is added to by the old Turkish classics playing on vinyl records. This place is certainly one of a kind! The restaurant produces its own meat, and the barbecue takes centre stage. Take your pick from the counter, where you'll find top-quality beef burgers and lamb fillets, and order some mezze that are bursting with flavour. For local colour, you need look no further.

Name: Loft Elia
Address: Gölköy Mahallesi, 325. Sokak No:7, Bodrum, 48400, Türkiye
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Great view,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: The olive trees around you and the views over the bay accentuate Loft Elia's Zen feel. Although this lounge-style restaurant is fully open to the elements, it nonetheless has an intimate atmosphere. The natural vibe suits the menu down to the ground. A commitment to local produce and sustainable practices are part of their ethos underpinned by respect for the planet. The kitchen team's inspired, fine dining-quality dishes are deliciously spicy. For example, their airy feta sponge cake is freeze-dried with three varieties of tomato to give it delicate sweetness and tang. This cuisine is truly inspiring!

Name: AQUA
Address: Yıldız, Çırağan Caddesi No:28, Beşiktaş, Istanbul, 34349, Türkiye
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: Everything revolves around water at the fish and seafood restaurant of the Four Seasons Hotel, which is also right on the waterfront. Not only can you enjoy a unique view of the bustling strait and Bosphorus Bridge, but this elegant restaurant also provides a romantic backdrop. Delicious seafood is showcased in typical Mediterranean fare, modern Asian creations and dishes cooked on the grill. Aromatic, subtly spiced, accompanied by rich buttery sauces: this is generous cuisine prepared using premium produce.

Name: Birinci Kordon Balık Restoran
Address: Alsancak, Atatürk Caddesi No:196/A, Konak, Izmir, 35220, Türkiye
Description: Fish, fish and more fish – that's what you can expect at this rather simple restaurant. The refrigerated display counter immediately catches the eye as the charcoal grill works overtime in the kitchen. After some freshly prepared mezze, for example, allow the chef to delight you with succulent barbecued calamari rings in a chilli crust, or just as expertly flame-grilled sea bass. Such incredible flavours! No frills here: the focus lies squarely on unadulterated top-quality produce. A gem among the many restaurants on the quayside.

Name: Oro by Alfredo Russo
Address: Gölköy Mahallesi, 312. Sokak No:3, Bodrum, 48400, Türkiye
Description: Authenticity meets creativity at this gem of a restaurant, which is part of the Maxx Royal resort. The fantastic à la carte menu reads like an ode to the classics of Italian cuisine, but the chef gives them his own sophisticated spin. For instance, he gives extra body to potato and fish gnocchi by servinging them with a shellfish coulis, mussel jus and lime zest. This chef zeroes in on the essence of flavours, deftly weaving together freshness and that quintessential Mediterranean exuberance. The wine list certainly does not disappoint. And it would be remiss not to mention the beautiful natural surroundings, which create a sense of intimacy and elegance… Be sure to book ahead!

Name: Apartıman Yeniköy
Address: Yeniköy, Köybaşı Caddesi No:153, Sarıyer, Istanbul, 34464, Türkiye
Description: A mostly youthful and hip crowd frequents this pleasant bistro, which matches the energy of its neighbourhood. Lounge music plays in the background, the impressive drinks list features a notable selection of orange wines. The kitchen is run by a female chef who has composed an extensive and enticing menu that combines Mediterranean verve with Middle Eastern spiciness. For instance, she barbecues lamb to medium-rare and serves it with orzo cooked in a kokoreç broth and greengage. Tip: For a truly filling meal, consider ordering an additional starter.

Name: Akira Back İstanbul
Address: Ataköy 2-5-6. Kısım Mahallesi, Rauf Orbay Caddesi No:2/1 LB, Bakırköy, Istanbul, 34158, Türkiye
Description: The view of the Sea of Marmara is the highlight of this modern and inviting restaurant located in the JW Marriott hotel. Be sure to go for a spot on the terrace! Akira Back has restaurants all over the world and has appointed one of his right-hand men as head chef in Istanbul. The dishes embody a distinctive fusion of predominantly Japanese and other Asian cuisines. Fine sushi, tasty gyoza, beef tataki that melts in the mouth, perfectly robata-grilled prawns… You will definitely want to come back for this contemporary whirlwind of Eastern flavours.

Name: Sia Eli
Address: Gümüşlük Mahallesi, 1120. Sokak No:108, Gümüşlük, Bodrum, 48970, Türkiye
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Terrace,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: Sia Eli takes full advantage of its environment – they grow vegetables, herbs and fruit in their five acres of kitchen garden, and catch fish in the sea a little further away. The natural splendour of the surrounding hills is also central to this open restaurant, which blends beautifully into the green setting – perfect for a romantic dinner for two! While Tolgar Mireli only serves pizza and burgers in the afternoon, in the evening he pulls out all the stops to showcase his take on Turkish cuisine. He primarily bases his dishes on vegetables, with which he creates small plates and mezze. He also serves lamb skewers, charcoal-grilled until perfectly medium-rare, accompanied by a lamb jus and spiced aubergine. Farm-to-table with a unique twist!

Name: SOTA ALAÇATI
Address: Alaçatı Mahallesi, 11039. Sokak No:18, Çeşme, Izmir, 35937, Türkiye
Description: The lobster and oyster tanks give away the fact that this open-air restaurant's main supplier is the sea. SOTA's Mediterranean soul is evident in everything from its mosaic tiles to the fresh seafood on the menu. The squid has the perfect firm texture and is seasoned to have just the right amount of zing. The seafood is super fresh and wonderful in combination with al dente tagliatelle. There is also an irresistible selection of sushi. This restaurant is dedicated to showcasing the sea's rich bounty.

Name: Rumelihisarı İskele
Address: Yahya Kemal Caddesi No:1, Rumeli Hisarı/Sarıyer, Istanbul, 34470, Türkiye
Description: At this classic waterfront pavilion, every table enjoys panoramic views of the mighty Bosporus, with its endless stream of boats – a breathtaking setting in which to savour the finest seafood. Having sampled the aromatic mezze presented at your table, you pick your fish from the abundant selection and indicate if you would like it steamed, barbecued or deep-fried. The kitchen puts the emphasis squarely on flavour, without any unnecessary flourishes. The Iskele special, a seafood pan with octopus, prawns and more, is seasoned only with paprika and chilli.

Name: Sunset Grill & Bar
Address: Kuruçeşme Mahallesi, Yol Sokak No:2, Ulus/Beşiktaş, Istanbul, 34345, Türkiye
FacilitiesAndServices: Great view,Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: Sunset Grill & Bar could be in a Hollywood film. This spacious, upscale restaurant is located in the heights of Ulus Park, providing a magnificent view of the city and the Bosporus – be sure to ask for a table by the window. The well-heeled clientele is drawn by the attentive service, and the extensive menu, which features classic French cuisine, Asian-inspired dishes and trendy sushi options, as well as the impressive wine list. Treat yourself to one of the barbecue specialities – think butter-soft beef fillet with a brown sauce enhanced with yuzu and mustard. An exhilarating dining experience!

Name: Tuğra Restaurant
Address: Çırağan Caddesi No:32, Beşiktaş, Istanbul, 34349, Türkiye
Description: At Tuğra you'll feel like royalty. Here you can bask in the historical splendour of the magnificent Çırağan Palace – the luxuriousness never fails to impress. Look beyond the marble pillars and admire the sparkling Bosphorus. Ottoman culinary tradition goes hand in hand with the customs of haute cuisine. Chef Emre Inanir puts his own spin on classic flavours. For instance, grilled beef liver is paired with crispy börek, deliciously unctuous on the inside, and an onion compote seasoned with sumac. What a combination!

Name: Lokanta Göktürk
Address: Göktürk Merkez, İstanbul Caddesi No:16/E, Eyüpsultan, Istanbul, 34077, Türkiye
Description: Leave the centre of Istanbul, head to Eyüpsultan district and sit down on the terrace or in front of the open kitchen. That's it, your work is done. Now all you have to do is enjoy! Muhsin Ertürk draws inspiration from, and puts a new spin on, recipes from Anatolian tradition, and has a penchant for regional produce. For instance, you can enjoy wonderfully creamy hummus, as well as prawns marinated in ginger then fried in garlic butter and served with creamy risotto, strands of soft cuttlefish and an aromatic clam broth. A creative blend of old and new!

Name: Beyti
Address: Şenlikköy Mahallesi, Orman Sokak No:8, Florya/Bakırköy, Istanbul, 34153, Türkiye
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Beyti Güler is a living legend in Istanbul. Since the 1980s, Istanbulites have been coming to dine in this stylish building, a fine example of nostalgic Turkish charm, with its little fountains at the entrance and sculptures in the garden. And this historical establishment boasts no fewer than 12 dining rooms! The charcoal grill is at the centre of the kitchen, where the experienced chefs cook all kinds of meat to perfection. Take the imam bayildi, for example: meltingly tender braised aubergine topped with tomatoes, bell peppers and onions, cooked just long enough to bring out all their flavours. And be sure to try one of the kebabs, too. Traditional Turkish fare just as it should be.

Name: Mürver
Address: Novotel İstanbul Bosphorus, Kemankeş Caddesi No:57-59, Karaköy/Beyoğlu, Istanbul, 34425, Türkiye
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining,Credit cards not accepted,Great view,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: Take the lift to the top floor of the Novotel Istanbul Bosphorus and discover the world of Mürver. You can start with an aperitif in the hip cocktail bar, then soak up the romantic atmosphere of the restaurant. Finally, take in the breathtaking views of the metropolis from the fabulous terrace. An open fire is the centrepiece of the kitchen, where you can also see meat and fish drying. Smoky and barbecue notes form the basis of captivating creations featuring regional produce and original combinations. The dishes are spicy, bold and fiery. Think grilled squid rings with green beans and a subtly spicy muhammara sauce, or 28-day aged ribeye. This buzzing establishment is the place to be!

Name: Borsa Restaurant
Address: Vaniköy Caddesi No:12, Adile Sultan Sarayı, Üsküdar, Istanbul, 34684, Türkiye
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Great view,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: The Adile Sultan Palace is an events venue that is as spectacular as its name suggests. A stroll through the building will give you a sense of its grandeur and splendour – characteristics that Borsa is fortunate to share. To dine against a breathtaking backdrop of the Bosporus, head to the terrace. This upmarket restaurant showcases traditional Turkish cuisine on an à la carte basis. In his dish featuring medium-rare lamb ribs, spinach and roast potatoes, the chef allows the distinctive flavours of the ingredients to shine through. Less is more at Borsa. Make sure you leave room for dessert – the classic katmer (crispy filo pastry filled with pistachio) is very tempting!

Name: Aila
Address: Büyükdere Caddesi No:76/B, Mecidiyeköy/Şişli, Istanbul, 34394, Türkiye
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Valet parking
Description: Aila radiates luxury and grandeur. Smooth marble, high ceilings, dark wood: the decor is a feast for the eyes. Turkey's rich cuisine is given a contemporary twist, with the focus on spices – they even have a spice library – and getting the most out of top-notch produce. This modern take on tradition should definitely be combined with a glass of raki – what a selection!

Name: İsabey Bağevi
Address: Gölcükler Mahallesi, 901. Sokak İstasyon Mevkii No:38, Menderes, Izmir, 35470, Türkiye
Description: The Isabey wine estate grows mostly Sauvignon Blanc, but you will find more than impressive rows of vines on its land. Indeed, there is a magnificent terrace on which to dine in the shade of a majestic plane tree that is over 350 years old. This restaurant is committed to serving food and wine of the highest quality. The buttery lamb stock with medium-rare lamb chops and the squid stuffed with minced lamb and accompanied by a fine white wine sauce are testament to the depth and flavour of this classic cuisine.

Name: Orkide Balık
Description: At Orkide Balik, you can almost feel the sand between your toes as you enjoy your meal. The chef takes advantage of the restaurant's location to bring fresh fish straight from the sea to your plate. But before you order your main course, be sure to check out the mezze in the refrigerated counter. The dishes are prepared without any fuss, and with that traditional sense of generosity. Think marinated squid or deep-fried sea bass with aubergine and a bechamel sauce seasoned with mustard. Sometimes the best things in life are the simplest.

Name: AŞEKA
Address: Müeyyedzade Mahallesi, Arap Oğlan Sokak No:6, Beyoğlu, Istanbul, 34425, Türkiye
Description: Within the walls of this rather unremarkable historical building tucked away on a side street in the Karaköy district, this restaurant with intimate lighting is done out in a tasteful palette of dark brown hues, and displays regularly changing artwork. To showcase his creativity, Ömer Akosman focuses exclusively on an à la carte approach. His dishes are not unnecessarily complicated, but bursting with flavour – spiciness and robust sauces make the difference here. An intense gravy and garnishes such as marinated tomatoes, kalamata olives and crispy polenta are the perfect accompaniment to the patiently braised beef.

Name: Zuma İstanbul
Address: İstinye Park No:461, Sarıyer, Istanbul, 34460, Türkiye
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Wheelchair access
Description: The Istanbul branch of this chic Japanese restaurant is on a par with those in London and Dubai, among other places. That means top-notch ingredients showcased by a contemporary approach to authentic Japanese cuisine. On the menu: sushi, tempura dishes, fish from the robata grill, vegetarian options... High-quality produce and subtle influences from the East always hit the mark. Rest assured, the cosmopolitan Zuma feels right at home amid the most exclusive fashion boutiques.

Name: Mori
Address: Fevzi Çakmak Caddesi No:24, Fethiye, 48300, Türkiye
Description: With the azure sea against the backdrop of the majestic mountains in the distance and the palatial yachts in the marina just a few metres from your table, the terrace here is the place to be. Located at Yacht Classic Hotel, this restaurant specialised in Italian cuisine eschews unnecessary frills and focuses on flavour. Think al dente linguine with a light velouté sauce and ultra-fresh seafood such as tender squid and pink prawns. The extensive menu will not disappoint!

Name: Barbarossa
Address: Adnan Menderes Caddesi No:89, Asarlik Mevkii PK 225, Bodrum, 48400, Türkiye
Description: The luxurious Caresse resort's Mediterranean restaurant offers a delightfully laid-back dining experience. Watch the chefs at work in the outdoor kitchen while cocktails are shaken in the bar and chill-out music fills the air. The view of the sea and the moored yachts never gets old! Seafood takes centre stage here, cooked up in traditional Greek and Italian ways. Wonderfully crispy deep-fried squid with a fresh tartar sauce, barbecued sea bass with perfectly seasoned vegetables: the best of Mediterranean cuisine served up without any fuss. Reserve a poolside spot ahead of time and enjoy a refreshing swim after dinner.

Name: Seraf Mahmutbey
Address: Mahmutbey Mahallesi, Peyami Safa Caddesi No:38/D, Bağcılar, Istanbul, 34200, Türkiye
Description: Sinem Özler sets great store by goods from local producers. You can taste and see this for yourself, because they are also for sale in the shop of this spacious, modern restaurant, just outside the city centre. For example, she works with Trakya Kivircik lamb in a bid to keep traditional recipes alive. The İçli Köfte with the same lamb is an absolute must. To bring those ancient Anatolian flavours to the table, this chef likes to use a wood-fired oven, and she never loses sight of the changing seasons and her surroundings.

Name: 1924 İstanbul
Address: Istiklal Caddesi, Olivya Geçidi No:7, Beyoğlu, Istanbul, 34435, Türkiye
Description: The original incarnation of this restaurant was opened by Russian refugees in 1924. Today diners can relive those glory days in a beautifully restored and opulent setting that exudes historical grandeur and features eye-catching panelling and mirrors. Live music makes for a buzzing atmosphere. Here they put a modern spin on Russian specialities. Think generous portions of stuffed pirozhki and beef Stroganoff, juicy meat and amazing flavour. And to drink? A glass of vodka from their impressive selection, of course!

Name: Deraliye
Address: Divanyolu Caddesi, Alemdar Mahallesi, Ticarethane Sokak No:10, Sultan Ahmet, Fatih, Istanbul, 34110, Türkiye
Description: Deraliye is a landmark of the historical Sultanahmet neighbourhood, where there is one tourist restaurant next to the other. The colourful, opulent decor immediately catches the eye and, like the cuisine, is a tribute to the Ottoman Empire. The extensive menu features an array of dishes devised for sharing and specialities such as mezze, barbecued offerings and kebabs. Tempting options include duck stew in filo pastry with fragrant spiced rice, or a lamb and tomato dish, slowly simmered in an earthenware pot to let the flavours meld. Here, you can savour sumptuous Ottoman cuisine, occasionally presented with a touch of showmanship. Good to know: Deraliye also organises cookery classes.

Name: OCAK
Address: Hobyar Mahallesi, Mimar Vedat Sokak No:5, Fatih, Istanbul, 34112, Türkiye
Description: OCAK has breathed new life into this former tobacco warehouse in the Old City, turning it into an intimate restaurant with exposed brick walls, soft lighting and marble finishings. The chef proposes only a single set menu that showcases his unique take on Turkish cuisine. He elevates chickpeas to new heights in a variety of dishes, including an amazing crispy deep-fried creation. He consistently strikes a perfect balance between tradition and modernity. Your curiosity will be piqued by every dish.

Name: Levan
Address: Kuşçular, Kuşçular Caddesi No:3, Urla, Izmir, 35430, Türkiye
Description: Dining with a view of the vineyards, or surrounded by the grapevines on the terrace, is an experience that will leave a lasting impression. Levan offers a convivial atmosphere in a charming and intimate setting. On the chalkboard, you will find a dozen dishes, from mezze to share to main courses to savour on your own. The traditional cuisine of the Aegean coast is given a subtle new twist here. Rice-filled vine leaves served with a yoghurt cream and tomato sauce, and rich lamb stew cooked in white wine: get ready for a Mediterranean feast!

Name: The GALLIARD Vadistanbul
Address: Ayazağa Mahallesi, Cendere Caddesi No:109C, Sarıyer, Istanbul, 34396, Türkiye
Description: The upscale Vadistanbul shopping mall is home to The Galliard, a restaurant that exudes contemporary elegance and boasts a spacious waterfront terrace. The extensive menu comprises international favourites including a unique take on sea bass ceviche, creamy risotto-style creations, generous pizzas, stews quietly simmering in the background… and even soufflés for dessert! Don't be put off by the sheer number of options – these chefs work to the highest standards and their skills are second to none. Those who stay later in the evening can look forward to an electrifying DJ set.

Name: Seraf Vadi
Address: Ayazağa, Kemerburgaz Caddesi No:7G, İç Kapı No:7, Sarıyer, Istanbul, 34396, Türkiye
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: Start your meal with the içli köfte, a house speciality combining a creamy yoghurt sauce with a steamed bun stuffed with highly aromatic lamb. And be sure to sample the other mezze, such as the imam bayildi: stuffed aubergine with a subtle smoky flavour, caramelised onion and candied red pepper. The main courses featuring various cuts of lamb are to die for. This contemporary restaurant not far from Vadistanbul Shopping Mall is a celebration of Anatolian culinary heritage.

Name: Vogue Restaurant
Address: Süleyman Seba Caddesi No:92, BJK Plaza, A Blok Kat: 13, Beşiktaş, Istanbul, 34353, Türkiye
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Great view,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Iconic photographs from the archives of the illustrious Vogue magazine lend the bright interior a fashion-forward touch, but it is the views of Dolmabahçe Palace and the Bosphorus that really steal the show. The extensive menu includes everything from Turkish classics and pasta to sushi and sashimi. So, you can look forward to both a knife-cut tuna tartare with fresh spring vegetables and a beautifully risen chestnut souffle with caramel and tahini. And why not round off your evening with a refreshing cocktail and a dance?

Name: Bağarası
Address: Bitez, Pınarlı Caddesi No:59, Bodrum, 48470, Türkiye
Description: Authentic and welcoming are two words that sum up what Bağarası is all about. Simply to enjoy delicious food in a relaxed environment, this is the place to come. You can choose from a variety of mezze displayed in the refrigerated counter, including marinated cauliflower in red wine with caramelised onions. At the same time, you can order popular classics, such as grilled kofta or sea bass, for your main course. But do leave room for dessert, because you absolutely must try the sweet artichoke confit with ice cream – a house speciality!

Name: Orfoz
Address: Kumbahçe Mahallesi, Zeki Müren Caddesi No:13/1, Bodrum, 48400, Türkiye
Description: The beautiful bay this restaurant overlooks is the pride of the Bozçağa brothers – not only for the azure waters, but also the bountiful fish and seafood they have to offer. The chefs' love for the sea is palpable in every dish, from the tuna sashimi with a light Asian touch to the oysters topped with a parmesan foam, and the perfectly grilled squid. The wine list is worth a look, as it is clearly a passion of the owners.

Name: Lokanta 1741
Address: Alemdar Mahallesi, Profesör Kazım İsmail Gürkan Caddesi No:34, Cağaloğlu Hamamı, Fatih, Istanbul, 34110, Türkiye
Description: This beautiful contemporary restaurant with a romantic roof terrace is right next to Cağaloğlu Hamam. It serves Turkish culinary classics, some dating back to 1741, with a modern twist. The chef sometimes introduces surprising textures and flavours but never loses sight of tradition. In the evening, they serve only a more sophisticated fine dining menu. Here, you can savour a zesty sea bass ceviche, as well as lamb brochettes with distinct barbecue notes and a punchy aubergine caviar. Oenophiles should definitely take the opportunity to explore the wine cellar.

Name: Calipso Fish
Address: Küçükyalı Sahil, Cumhuriyet Caddesi No:2, Küçükyalı/Maltepe, Istanbul, 34840, Türkiye
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Valet parking
Description: Istanbul residents come to this sun-drenched restaurant to escape the hustle and bustle of the city. The waiters give expert advice on the wide selection of mezze in the display fridge – the salads are beautifully fragrant! And that's just the beginning, because the traditional preparation methods accentuate the rich flavours of super-fresh fish and seafood. Whatever you choose, the chef will cook it according to your wishes: the bluefish, for example, can be barbecued whole and served with al dente vegetables. This is ingredient-led cuisine that never fails to impress.

Name: The BARN
Address: Gazitepe Mahallesi, Akören Cadddesi, Ören Çiftliği, No:114, Silivri, Istanbul, 34570, Türkiye
Description: Leave central Istanbul behind and head to Grandma's Wonderland in the Silivri district. This establishment set in verdant surroundings has both a hotel and this cosy restaurant, as well as a farm that supplies poultry, vegetables and other ingredients. Local produce is treated with great respect and, specialising in plant-forward cooking, the kitchen team adopts a zero-waste approach. The menu features skewers, veal tongue pastrami with cherry sauce, kasseri cheese tortellini, spinach and a butter sauce with white wine and sage. The farm-to-table concept is taken seriously here. A spot on the terrace, in the company of the resident dogs, and with a glass of wine from the estate in hand, is a must!

Name: Kornél
Address: Bitez, Adliye Caddesi No:34/A, Bodrum, 48470, Türkiye
Description: Terracotta and sandy hues perfectly complement Kornél's cosy ambiance, and the terrace to the rear has that appealing Ibiza feel. The bar serves up incredible cocktails that change with the seasons, while in the kitchen, the charcoal oven works overtime baking delicious pizzettas and more. The extensive menu includes a beautiful zesty sea bass ceviche, hearty pasta dishes and a vegetarian creation featuring beetroot and dukkah. Kornél offers a relaxed dining experience with great food all year round.

Name: Oi Filoi
Address: Koyunbaba, Zeki Üngör Sokak No:2, Bodrum, 48400, Türkiye
Description: Oi Filoi is an open-air restaurant shaded by two overarching trees. The charm of this setting is accentuated by warm lighting and Greek background music. The latter is no accident: the kitchen team here specialise in serving up classic Greek dishes with subtle contemporary twists. Think medium-rare lamb souvlaki with fresh tzatziki, barbecued sweet peppers and a toasted bun drenched in meat jus. If you would prefer moussaka, you will also, naturally, find that on the menu. And be sure to take advantage of the sommelier's knowledge – her carefully selected Turkish gems are a perfect match for this cuisine.

Name: telezzüz
Address: Kuzguncuk, Koç Topluluğu Spor Kulübü, Kuşbakışı Caddesi No:16, Üsküdar, Istanbul, 34674, Türkiye
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: Even before you walk into this colourful establishment, the ornate exterior hints that nature is celebrated at Telezzüz. The location, in a sports complex, is also rather unique. The restaurant clearly prioritises sustainable practices such as local sourcing, a zero-waste approach and plant-forward cooking. The chefs are creative in crafting delicious vegan dishes. Think mushroom ceviche, or deep-fried artichoke with a rich mushroom ketchup, a sweet plum and chilli sauce, olive oil mayonnaise and crunchy vegetables. And what better than a refreshing cocktail to accompany such deliciously natural food?

Name: Kasap Fuat Çeşme
Address: Altınyunus, 3435. Sokak No:66, Çeşme, Izmir, 35930, Türkiye
Description: The moment meat lovers walk into this cosy establishment with its delightful terrace at the back, their spirits are lifted. An array of cuts, expertly prepared by the butcher, awaits in the refrigerated display counter, and in the background, you can see the barbecue where the magic happens. Options include marinated ribeye, perfectly rare and with a crispy fat cap, as well as succulent burgers in house-made buns. What you see is what you get, and it's absolutely delicious!

Name: Eleos Yeşilköy
Address: Ümraniye Mahallesi, Yeşilbahçe Sokak No:9, Bakırköy, Istanbul, 34149, Türkiye
Description: Yeşilköy is a residential area outside the centre of Istanbul with airs of a seaside resort. A couple of streets away from the marina, you will find this exciting restaurant reminiscent of a Greek tavern. Delicious seafood is the speciality of the house. Think various mezze bursting with Mediterranean freshness. The sea bass is grilled to perfection and served simply, allowing the natural flavours of the fish to shine through. This is a great place to enjoy good no-nonsense food made from fresh, simple ingredients.

Name: Malva
Address: Torba, Kaynar Caddesi No:15, Bodrum, 48400, Türkiye
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Great view,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Valet parking
Description: Housed in luxury hotel Susona, this restaurant feels both elegant and hip. But the most stunning feature of all is the breathtaking view of the coastline. The chef and his team will be happy to tell you about their commitment to sustainability, including a zero-waste approach and close collaboration with their suppliers. Their creative cuisine draws on traditional and modern influences, celebrating the authentic flavours of the ingredients. For instance, the courgette flowers stuffed with rice and chopped mussels are seasoned with a classic blend of herbs and a judicious twist of lemon. The charcoal-grilled mussels add delightful smoky nuances. A compelling dining experience guaranteed!

Name: Amavi
Address: Alaçatı Mahallesi, 13003. Sokak No:1, Çeşme, Izmir, 35937, Türkiye
Description: Alaçati is a picturesque town with a lot to offer, but Amavi is the place to be for foodies. Walk through the cocktail bar, where DJs play in the evening, and take a seat in the trendy restaurant, which exudes its own unique elegance. The chef loves working with fish, and there is even a dedicated maturation cabinet in the open kitchen. His cuisine is a vibrant expression of his personality, as seen in his innovative take on ceviche of sea bream with samphire, fried quinoa and a pomegranate jus. Or you might prefer the barbecued dry-aged sea bass with its bold accoutrements. The chef will be more than happy to talk you through his captivating dishes.

Name: Ristorante Pizzeria Venedik
Description: Venedik has been a popular spot in Izmir for over 40 years. Diners are drawn by the cosy Venetian decor and Italian classics prepared in time-honoured tradition. The tempting menu has something for everyone, from al dente hand-made ravioli with a delicate shrimp filling to crispy pizza alla turca, not to mention the deliciously creamy tiramisu. This is a perennial favourite in every sense of the word.

Name: Scappi
Address: Gaziosmanpaşa Bulvarı No:1, Konak, Izmir, 35210, Türkiye
Description: Take the lift to the ninth floor of Swissôtel and immerse yourself in the elegant setting of Scappi. It's definitely worth trying to secure a spot on the terrace, where you get to take in the views of the bay and the sea – the sunsets are simply divine! But perhaps you would prefer to home in on the action in the partially open kitchen complete with pizza oven. With great skill, the chefs rustle up dishes such as a creamy risotto with barbecued squid, al dente house-made pasta with an aromatic tomato sauce, or freshly caught sea bass with a saffron-infused lime sauce. This is a popular place, so don't forget to make a reservation.

Name: Karnas Vineyards
Description: As soon as you drive onto this family-owned wine estate, you sense that something special is about to happen. The large pond with its fountain draws the eyes, and the terrace overlooking the vines has a delightful Mediterranean feel – it's the stuff of dreams! The allure of this place leaves no one indifferent. Don't miss the chance to sample the estate's wines – the perfect introduction to Bodrum's terroir. The chef operates on a farm-to-fork principle and is also committed to sourcing local produce wherever possible. She sets great store by her ingredients, which often come from her own garden. For example, she perfectly pan-fries ultra-fresh sea bass and combines it with braised seaweed, mandarin marmalade, a butter oil emulsion and lime zest – this is a chef who brings a unique and nuanced perspective to traditional dishes.

Name: Kurul Bitez
Address: Bitez Mahallesi, 1936. Sokak No:2, Bodrum, 48470, Türkiye
FacilitiesAndServices: Credit cards not accepted,Garden or park,Terrace,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: In the heart of the bustling centre of Bitez, there is a garden where you can unwind amid olive and lemon trees while enjoying delicious food. Welcome to Kurul Bitez, where kebabs are the speciality of the house. You can see this for yourself at the entrance, where the spit is always turning and the bread oven is piping hot. Chef Kemal Karataş gives Gaziantep cuisine a contemporary twist. His kebab with succulent lamb, mild spices, pistachio and a subtle sweet and sour sauce is a shining example. And be sure to try his aromatic mezze appetisers – they are simply too good to be missed!

Name: St. Regis Brasserie
Address: Mim Kemal Öke Caddesi No:35, Nişantaşı/Şişli, Istanbul, 34367, Türkiye
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: A stylish luxury brasserie like the one here in the St Regis Hotel would not seem out of place in Paris. The impressive à la carte menu offers something for everyone. Asian gyoza, Turkish mezze, Italian pasta and risotto...the choice is yours. Flavours from all corners of the globe are brought together here with great skill and care, in dishes that are unfussy and generous.

Name: Dereköy Lokantası
Address: Dereköy, Dereköy Caddesi No:133, Bodrum, 48960, Türkiye
Description: Zişan Altınçaba's culinary approach is creative while maintaining a respect for tradition. She welcomes you warmly in her garden restaurant, where she also has a home accessories shop, and then she lets her cooking do the talking. Fruit is often incorporated for its characteristically refreshing sweetness, eg ripe nectarine lends the scorpionfish ceviche a delicate touch of acidity. However, she proves her classical know-how with her rich pâté of lamb brains and neck. Her dishes are bold – but within reason – with a penchant for fresh and zingy flavours.

Name: Aheste
Address: Asmalı Mescit Mahallesi, Meşrutiyet Caddesi No:107/F, Beyoğlu, Istanbul, 34430, Türkiye
Description: Once you enter the premises, leaving the bustling Pera district behind, you have a choice between a trendy bistro and a more romantic dining space with a vaulted ceiling. In either case, you'll be charmed by the mystical ambiance and the staff's enthusiasm and dedication – and that's before you've even discovered the restaurant's modern take on mezze! Traditional Turkish specialities, such as barbecued lamb heart with roast potatoes, share the menu with in-vogue options, including vegetarian dishes. The tasting menu offers a wonderful opportunity to savour delicacies such as flaky pastry filled with a creamy tuna tarama.

Name: Giritli
Address: Yenigüvey Sokak No:9, Cankurtaran/Fatih, Istanbul, 34122, Türkiye
Description: In summer, Giritli welcomes you to its atmospheric terrace, where the kitchen is also located. If the weather lets you down, you can always cross the street to the romantic Mediterranean-style sister restaurant. Be sure to explore the enticing mezze set menu (drinks included), which inventively showcases the traditional flavours of Crete. The perfectly seasoned and generously portioned dishes feature impeccably fresh produce. Think marinated sea bass with fresh herbs, or potato salad with a judicious touch of vinegar and vibrant tzatziki. A real feast!

Name: Kısmet Lokantası
Address: Çırkan Mahallesi, Çelebi Kaptan Sokak No:3/A, Konacık, Bodrum, 48400, Türkiye
Description: If you're on the hunt for a lively place in which to have lunch among the locals, look no further. Kismet Lokantasi serves delicious food at great value for money in a laid-back atmosphere. Peruse the counter for traditional delicacies prepared by the chef, then choose your favourites. Think succulent meatballs with grilled aubergine and tomato sauce, and, for dessert, a rich patisserie with walnuts and just the right amount of sweet syrup – foodies will be in seventh heaven! This indulgent dining experience will leave a lasting impression.

Name: ROKA
Address: Kılıçalipaşa Mahallesi, Meclis-i Mebusan Sokak No:14/2E, Beyoğlu, Istanbul, 34433, Türkiye
Description: Are you in the mood for aubergine gently cooked in miso/soy/sesame with katsuoboshi, or would you prefer chicken given a smoky flavour on the robatayaki grill? Or how about nigiri sushi with sea bream and a crispy squid tempura? At ROKA, lovers of contemporary Japanese dishes will find a great selection to suit their tastes, accompanied by cool cocktails and fine wines. And thanks to the location on the Galataport promenade, you also get to enjoy stunning views of the Bosporus at this stylish, lively restaurant.

Name: Mezra Yalıkavak
Address: Dirmil Mahallesi, 6885. Sokak No:3, Bodrum, 48990, Türkiye
Description: Large glass façades lend an open feel to give this stylish industrial-style space. On the way to your table, you walk past the lounge bar and the stage where concerts are occasionally held. Right outside the restaurant, there is a vegetable garden and some livestock; the chef also has his own farm a short distance away. Local produce is central to the modern take on Turkish cuisine served here. Open-fire cooking and preservation techniques such as pickling complement new culinary trends. For example, the chef marinates lamb saddle in a poppy seed crust and then flame-grills it. This is accompanied by a cauliflower cream, an intense lamb jus and garlic-infused oil. The attention to detail is captivating.

Name: Hakkasan İstanbul
Address: Muallim Naci Caddesi No:62, Kuruçeşme/Beşiktaş, Istanbul, 34345, Türkiye
Description: Luxury chain Hakkasan likes to establish itself in vibrant cities, and Istanbul is obviously no exception. This restaurant enjoys a prime location at the Mandarin Oriental Bosphorus, which boasts stunning views over the water and exudes Asian elegance with a personal touch. The crispy duck salad, a classic of the house, is a shining example of how Cantonese cuisine is revamped here: the duck skin is incredibly crispy, the meat combines a fine spiciness with a mild sweetness, and the salad offers an interesting contrast with juicy pomegranate. Delicious! And it's absolutely worth taking a look at the exclusive wine list.

Name: Park Fora
Address: Muallim Naci Caddesi No:54/A, Cemil Topuzlu Parkı İçi, Kuruçeşme/Beşiktaş, Istanbul, 34347, Türkiye
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Great view,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: Grilled, meunière, steamed, tandoori – however you like your fish, Park Fora has it covered. At this traditional seafood restaurant, the produce is always in season and super fresh. As you enter, you will see crates of the day's catch stacked and waiting and numerous aquariums filled with king crabs, lobsters and other creatures. Specify your cooking preferences – for us, it was sole à la meunière – and then savour! It will be cooked to perfection and accompanied by carefully prepared accoutrements. Factor in the waterfront location, with views of the boats coming and going on the Bosphorus, and you will really feel like you are on holiday!

Name: Ulus Mahallesi, Ahmet Adnan Saygun Caddesi, Ulus Parkı İçi No:71/1, Beşiktaş, Istanbul, 34340, Türkiye
GreenStar: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Terrace,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
FacilitiesAndServices: As soon as you enter, you realise how exceptional this upscale restaurant is. The views of the bustling Bosphorus, the enchanting minarets and the Istanbul skyline are unparalleled! To really make the most of your fine dining experience at the elegant 29, book a table on the expansive terrace. The generosity and spiciness of traditional Turkish cuisine are given a subtle modern twist, often incorporating Mediterranean touches. Both the authentic mezze and the smooth mushroom risotto make this place the trip. Featuring an impressive selection of top-flight labels, the extensive wine menu is worthy of attention.

Name: Balıkçı Kahraman
Address: Rumeli Kavağı Mahallesi, İskele Caddesi No:15/1, Sarıyer, Istanbul, 34450, Türkiye
Description: Be sure to try the fish kokoreç, a traditional dish made with grilled fish offal; the perfectly grilled turbot, which is the house speciality, is also a must; and let's not forget the dried mackerel, nor the buttery-soft tuna lakerda prepared with house-made olive oil. A word to the wise: The best way to experience Kahraman Altun's cosy fish restaurant is to bring friends and sample as many of his traditionally prepared delicacies as possible. Afterwards, you should definitely take the time to explore the surrounding fishing village of Rumeli Kavağı (also known for its figs). This peaceful corner of Istanbul is sure to enchant you.

Name: Banyan
Address: Yıldız Muallim Naci Caddesi & Salhane Sokak No:3/2, Beşiktaş, Istanbul, 34347, Türkiye
Description: Dinner at Banyan is a real experience. As you take in the view of Ortaköy Mosque and the action on the Bosporus through the large windows, choose an aperitif from the fabulous selection available at the cocktail bar, where a DJ plays the hottest beats. The food is not to be underestimated: expect modern Asian dishes and spicy flavours with fish as the main focus. The menu includes exquisite sushi options, prawn gyoza and chicken with a spicy green curry sauce. And even if you turn up after 10.30pm, the kitchen will still be open with a shorter menu. Very cool!

Name: Kıyı
Address: Haydar Aliyev Caddesi No:186/A, Tarabya/Sarıyer, Istanbul, 34457, Türkiye
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Credit cards not accepted,Great view,Wheelchair access
Description: If you're looking for an atmospheric seafood restaurant adorned with beautiful paintings and affording breathtaking views of the picturesque marina, then this perennial favourite is the place for you (ask for a table upstairs)! Start with a selection of mezze and then choose from the bountiful array of fish and seafood, which will be prepared according to your desires. Our inspector opted for sole from the display fridge, which was flawlessly pan-fried before being filleted at the table. It's all about the produce here!

Name: Atölye
Address: Süzer Plaza, Asker Ocağı Caddesi, Elmadağ Caddesi No:6, Şişli, Istanbul, 34367, Türkiye
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Great view,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus
Description: The fine dining restaurant of the Ritz-Carlton hotel boasts a laid-back but luxury vibe. The colourful interior and views of the sea and Besiktas football stadium will draw your eye. Authentic Anatolian recipes are prepared with generosity, sometimes with a dash of innovation and often with a fresh Mediterranean touch. Spicy mezze, aromatic hummus, freshly caught sea bass, rich pide: this is the place to come for authentic flavours accompanied by fine wines.

Name: Khorasani
Address: Alemdar Mahallesi, Ticarethane Sokak No:9/B, Fatih, Istanbul, 34110, Türkiye
Description: The Sultanahmet neighbourhood is known for all its tourist restaurants, where menus consist of photographs of dishes. In that respect it's no different at the rustic-style Khorasani, but what sets this grill restaurant apart is the chef's dedication to quality. The meat, barbecued to order, and the kebabs are second to none. We thoroughly enjoyed the kebab with succulent lamb, crisp vegetables and, of course, the wonderful pita bread that comes with it. For flavoursome food with no nonsense, Khorasani is the place.

Name: Avlu Restaurant
Address: Cankurtaran, Tevkifhane Sokak No:1, Fatih, Istanbul, 34122, Türkiye
Description: Every detail of the Four Seasons hotel in Sultanahmet exudes luxury. One of the hotel's hidden treasures is its Mediterranean-style courtyard. In this tranquil oasis, you can relax and escape the hustle and bustle. Your meal starts with some delicious bread from the wood-fired oven and continues with this fresh take on indulgent Turkish fare. The chef strikes the perfect balance between rich manti stuffed with beef, the freshness of buffalo yoghurt and the pep of spiced butter and a pulled beef marmalade. The extensive and varied selection of Anatolian delicacies is impressive!

Name: Çok Çok Thai
Address: Asmalı Mescit Mahallesi, Meşrutiyet Caddesi No:51/A, Beyoğlu, Istanbul, 34430, Türkiye
Description: Take a seat on the lively terrace at the front or opt for the authentic interior, and let your mind drift off to exotic Thailand. Here you can enjoy typical dishes such as sweet and sour spring rolls with crunchy vegetables and a spicy aubergine and pepper curry. Crisp, fresh produce, authentic flavours and respect for tradition make this a great place to eat.

Name: Gula Urla
Address: Kuşçular Mahallesi, Kuşçular Caddesi No:46, Urla, Izmir, 35430, Türkiye
Description: Whether you're soaking up the sun on the verdant terrace or cosying up by the fireplace, Gula Urla is inviting all year round. The fresh fish on display makes it clear that the sea is the restaurant's main supplier; vegetables and cheese are also sourced locally. After a delicious cocktail or glass of local wine, you can savour a shrimp salad with mango and avocado, or perhaps a tandoori-style squid dish, before finishing off with a creamy katmer with red berries. The extensive menu is a seafood lover's dream come true!

Name: Spago
Address: Mim Kemal Öke Caddesi No:35, Nişantaşı/Şişli, Istanbul, 34367, Türkiye
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Great view,Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: The rooftop of the upscale St Regis Hotel is the place to soak up those hip Istanbul vibes. Sip a delicious cocktail on the terrace that affords sublime views of the city (such romantic sunsets!), sit at the long bar or simply enjoy the lounge music and modern luxury that surrounds you. The kitchen is overseen by Wolfgang Puck, who creates a unique blend of Italian, Californian and Asian influences. Expect sophisticated flavours and techniques, home cooking and international panache. Be sure to try the smoked salmon pizza, as well as the duck spring rolls with their spicy hoisin sauce and sweet plum sauce.

Name: Lokanta Feriye
Address: Yıldız Mahallesi Çırağan Caddesi No:44, Beşiktaş, Istanbul, 34347, Türkiye
Description: Dining in the gardens of the fully refurbished Feriye Palace is a new experience each time. Here on the edge of the Bosphorus – some diners even arrive by boat – you have the ever-evolving backdrop of the constant coming and going of the ships. And there is something magical about the view of the illuminated Ortaköy Mosque and Bosphorus Bridge, especially when you have a delicious cocktail in hand. This restaurant strikes a fine balance between chic and relaxed, and the service is attentive. The chefs, who can be seen at work in the open kitchen, let the ingredients speak for themselves. Their dishes are not overly elaborate, but rather classic fare with subtle zesty and spicy nuances. They give aubergine purée a delightful tang by mixing in yoghurt, making it an excellent accompaniment to barbecued lamb.

Name: Fauna
Address: Küçükbakkalköy Mahallesi, Işıklar Caddesi, Ahmet Muhip Dranas Sokak No:9/A, Ataşehir, Istanbul, 34750, Türkiye
Description: Lunch at Fauna is the perfect excuse to visit the Ataşehir district, just outside the city centre. You sit at long tables, often next to other diners, and watch the pasta being freshly made behind the counter. At Fauna, Italian and Turkish cuisine come together in rich, shareable dishes. Think ravioli with a hearty Karayaka lamb and walnut filling. The superb sorbet of organic strawberries, with a creamy texture and nicely tart, is just one example of the focus on local produce. Booking is strongly recommended!

Name: Tuti
Address: Yokuşbaşı Mahallesi, Suluhasan Caddesi No:18, Bodrum, 48400, Türkiye
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Great view,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: The rooftops of Bodrum, the azure sea, even some Greek islands: the view you have from the top floor of The Marmara hotel is truly breathtaking! The restaurant has a Mediterranean feel and that also applies to the food.. Traditional recipes are revamped with great skill and local produce. The crispy manti with minced meat, yoghurt and chilli oil is a shining example. Be sure to treat yourself to the legendary baklava, too!

Name: Hakkasan Bodrum
Address: Gölköy Mahallesi, 314. Sokak No:10, Bodrum, 48483, Türkiye
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Great view,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Valet parking
Description: Located in the Mandarin Oriental hotel against the wonderful backdrop of the glistening Aegean Sea, and with an elegant dining space done out in wood, this floating open-air restaurant is stunning. Hakkasan is a renowned chain bringing a luxurious take on Cantonese cuisine to your table. Think authentic Peking duck or grilled lamb chops, but elevated with fresh garnishes and rich sauces. For a chic night out, Hakkasan is just the place!

Name: Maison Brut
Description: This elegant contemporary restaurant perfectly reflects the spirit of Breton chef Bastien Djait. After a MICHELIN-star-studded run in Paris, he now expresses himself through lovely inspired dishes: green lentils with sweet onion; cod with cod's head and sea vegetables; poultry, corn and camelina. Respect for the raw ingredient is a golden rule, and the chef only works with French produce - except for the coffee. Attentive service.

Name: Aldehyde
Description: In this intimate establishment near the Quais de Seine, Tunisian-born chef Youssef Marzouk cooks up a delicious culinary symphony in his open kitchen-bar. Flanked by two assistants with equally prestigious pedigrees (Cheval Blanc Paris, Carlton, Ritz, Jacques Faussat), at dinnertime he puts together a single surprise set menu featuring a subtle marriage of French tradition and North African flavours. His confident technique shines through in his meticulously plated creations, bolstered by his Tunisian sensibility, which you can detect in his sparing use of spices, herbs and citrus fruits: saddle of lamb done two ways, grilled summer vegetable foam, meat jus with smoked eel etc.

Name: Les Résistants - La Table
Address: 7 rue de la Fidélité, Paris, 75010, France
Description: This new restaurant has been opened by the owners of Les Résistants, enthusiastic advocates of small-scale farming. On the menu: meats from local breeds, seafood from small boat fishing and, to wash it all down, a selection of "living" wines sourced from 150 producers. The natural decor reflects their philosophy: raw materials, wood, stone and glass panes that let light stream in, and a predominantly green colour scheme. The chef delivers modern, instinctive dishes that make the most of seasonal ingredients, such as his starter of agnolotti del plin, lamb ragout and apricot confit.

Name: Fana
Description: It is clear to see that chef Gabriel Gras Fernandez and pastry chef Jorice Sardain are passionate about food. In their compact restaurant on a pedestrian street in Montmartre (where more and more interesting restaurants are popping up), they work in tandem to create their clever take on seasonal cuisine in the from of carefully crafted dishes: oyster mushrooms, coffee sabayon, parsley, brioche; corn-fed chicken, butternut squash, endive, orange; and a stunning chocolate dessert with an array of textures.

Name: Estime
Description: Tucked away in a narrow pedestrian street in the city centre, this restaurant is run by siblings Maxime (in the kitchen) and Estelle Besnier (front of house). In a pleasant, colourful space (white beams, whitewashed walls, mirrors, stone and brick fireplace, original hardwood floors), this chef has a sure touch, preparing dishes with precision, generosity and a sense of indulgence: chicken oyster with cream of mushroom; hake, potatoes, chorizo and samphire; coconut, kiwi and sorrel. The lunchtime set menu is excellent value for money. A truly joyful dining experience.

Name: Fossé Saint Ange
Description: A new duo has taken over this well-known institution in the pretty village built by Cardinal Richelieu in the 17C. The period varnished wood façade opens onto a bistro-style interior with a warm and friendly atmosphere, where good cheer and good food are the order of the day. The chef keeps things simple: a menu that changes every month, featuring traditional dishes that are firmly rooted in the seasons and spiced up with the odd exotic touch, such as an Asian-inspired guinea fowl raviolo. The desserts, too, hold their own.

Name: Lo Fieu
Address: 55 route de Lyon, lieu-dit La Grive, Saint-Alban-de-Roche, 38080, France
Description: In his "country-style restaurant with a wood fire" (Lo Fieu means "fire" in the local dialect), Romain Hubert and his friendly young team work hard to keep the traditional cuisine of the Dauphiné region alive. A series of comforting and flavourful dishes are prepared right in front of you: soup from the cauldron with Trept chickpea , fried fish from Lake Bourget, sausage (pork or fish) served with gratin dauphinois, and then there is the trolley packed with appetising desserts. The converted barn, which has been restored in a rustic style and wows with its impressive dimensions, provides the perfect setting.

Name: Colette
Description: In the heart of the Forez region, this group of large stone and timber buildings nestles between a fir forest and a lake. The property is conducive to kicking back on the terrace in summer or, in winter, to embracing the hygge lifestyle by the imposing fireplace in the cosy restaurant room. The cooking of chef Thomas Laurier (Maison Pic and Dame de Pic, Chabichou) proves to be comforting and indulgent: an excellent pâté en croûte (a speciality served in different variations throughout the year) and, for dessert, fresh poached peach accompanied by lemon balm from the garden and buckwheat – a little culinary gem. The chef's partner takes care of the restaurant floor, where there is rarely a free table to be had.

Name: Château du Theil
Description: Nothing remains of the ruined château, the site of which has been given a new lease of life thanks to the vision of two childhood friends from the town. Now there are guestrooms, lodges and… a restaurant housed in the timber extension. The chef serves authentic cuisine that is beautifully fresh and packed with flavour: trout ceviche, cucumber aguachile with coriander oil; pulled pork, seasonal vegetables and jus; riz au lait (delectable!). They implement a sincerely eco-responsible approach: priority is given to local producers and an aquaponics greenhouse for growing their own vegetables is being developed.

Name: L'Ogustin
Address: 2 place de l'Ormeau, La Vacquerie-et-Saint-Martin-de-Castries, 34520, France
Description: Not far from the Cirque de Navacelles, in a small village on the southern edge of the limestone plateau that is the Causse du Larzac, Pricillia Lebon's restaurant is housed in a converted inn. Beneath the stone vaults, the inviting, cosy decor reflects the endearing personality of a chef who has come to this beautiful, isolated setting to cook. The surprise set menu celebrates the Larzac area, with ingredients sourced mainly via short supply chains (not least from local market gardens), as well as from mushroom and plant picking. Plants reign supreme in the intuitive, light and aromatic dishes. The dessert is a tribute to the chef's Malgasy origins, with a sweet potato cream spiked with vanilla. Vegetarian options are also available. A unique and authentic place.

Name: La Bistronomie
Description: In this contemporary bistro, the chef cooks up dishes that are as straightforward and satisfying as the name of his restaurant suggests – and it's a joy to experience. Bistro-style recipes (think French onion soup, beef tartare, chocolate mousse) sit alongside traditional specialities, on which he puts a savvy new spin. A case in point would be the grand veneur sauce, in which red wine meets cherries, or the chicken ravioli with tarragon. The indulgent and beautifully prepared desserts are also worth trying – for example, figs roasted in honey and toasted hazelnut crumble with rosemary ice cream.

Name: Ploc
Description: "Cities should be built in the countryside, because the air is so much purer there" (Alphonse Allais): this almost seems to be the case in the old village of Charonne, in this neighbourhood bistro tucked away in a bucolic cobbled street. Inside, the atmosphere is laid-back and lively, relaxed and friendly. The menu is inspired by wholesome ingredients, carefully sourced from small-scale producers. When it comes to the dishes, there is no shortage of skill or flavour – just look at the salsa verde that accompanies the leeks, and the bear's garlic pesto on the toasted brioche, topped with a walnut labneh, green asparagus, peas and roasted button mushrooms. Selection of natural wines.

Name: Jium
Description: Behind a rather nondescript façade lies an authentic Korean canteen which boasts a lovely vintage vibe and is popular with a clientele from the land of the Morning Calm. It is the brainchild of photographer and guesthouse owner, Kim Hong-Seung, and his wife Sun-Hee, a former fashion designer. As well as bibimbap classics, the menu is packed with authentic delicacies (soft shell crabs, oyster fritters) and unusual recipes (seafood pancakes, kimchi stew, pork shoulder and tofu, etc). You can season these culinary delights with homemade soy sauce (or not) before finishing with a dessert, also homemade, illustrated by vanilla-flavoured rice pudding with red beans and caramelised pecan nuts.

Name: Le Matré
Description: Just off rue Lepic, this small bistro with a contemporary feel is tucked away in the heart of the Abbesses quarter. The interior keeps things simple: exposed stone walls, floor-to-ceiling window, modern furniture and an open kitchen. At the helm is Lucas Tresse (formerly at Yves Camdeborde's Avant Comptoir), who takes inspiration from the food markets to deliver his straightforward take on contemporary cuisine. The intentionally short menu changes regularly to align with available produce and the chef's imagination: porcini, gnocchi, red wine sauce; breaded pork loin, sautéed mushrooms, celery purée. A reasonably priced option in Paris, which prioritises spontaneity and super-fresh ingredients.

Name: L'Altro Frenchie
Description: Grégory Marchand strikes again with his eclectic take on dining! In this modern Italian-style bistro, diners will also detect the British and American influences of which the chef is so fond. On the menu: a crudo misto with a series of ingenious vegetable condiments, classic dishes like pappardelle with rabbit or a must-try cotoletta alla milanese (veal chop for two). As for the chocolate cake, it is a homage to the recipe devised by Jamie Oliver at London's River Café. The wines are supplied by Frenchie, the wine shop just next door.

Name: Sétopa
Description: Just a stone's throw from the Carrefour de l'Odéon, Sétopa (for "Seoul to Paris") serves refined Korean cuisine under the stewardship of chef and entrepreneur Linda Lee. She has teamed up with two of the biggest names in Korean gastronomy, Chang-ho Shin and Mingoo Kang, to devise a menu that is both traditional and elegant (eg oyster ravioli, tofu root, gochujang; chestnut and mugwort mochi). The service, courtesy of a Korean team, is attentive and professional, making this an excellent place in which to savour the flavours of the Land of the Morning Calm without leaving Paris.

Name: Marie Akaneya
Description: This is Paris's first sumibiyaki-style restaurant. Particularly popular in Kyoto, this cuisine is prepared with top-drawer ingredients, not least the Wagyu that is shipped here from Ito Ranch, a beef farm on the outskirts of the town of Matsusaka – and according to the Japanese themselves, this is the ultimate breed of Kobe beef. Everything is cooked over the famous binchotan charcoal, which is made mainly from Ubame oak wood – every table in the restaurant has its own barbecue taking pride of place. Some of the menus feature Fukuroi's renowned Crown Melon, which can sometimes fetch a price of several thousand euro.

Name: Habile.
Description: Our chefs and their partners are never short of bright ideas for new ways to dine. After the trend for caves à manger and restaurants with delis, this place unites bistro and knitwear. Upstairs, fashion designer Camille Andrieux showcases her sartorial creations, while chef Éric Fontanini cooks up generous, no-frills meals: The pâté en croûte with pork and foie gras, and the line-caught bluefin tuna, simply seared and served on a delicious compote of onions and peppers, are good examples. As an added bonus, the kitchen is open 11am-11pm (excluding the lunch set menu). The colourful decor is delightfully dapper, and you can even eat at the counter and see the chef at work.

Name: Les Incontournables
Description: Here, the "incontournables" in question are the ingredients: the cooking revolves around produce sourced within a 100km radius of Manosque, which is lovingly prepared by a pleasant chef who prioritises flavour over technique to create no-nonsense Provençal-inspired cuisine: 7hr lamb shoulder, morel mushroom and walnut wine risotto, organic peach confit... Plus service with a smile.

Name: Le Socle
Description: Set back from Place Garibaldi, this little bistro has found its place on Nice's restaurant scene. It is run by a team of two chefs who have experience working in top establishments: chef Dominique Roca (L'Atelier Robuchon Étoile, for example) and, front of house, her partner Mikhaël Lyoubi (Flaveur in Nice with the Tourteaux brothers, to cite but one). Carefully chosen, good-quality fresh ingredients, such as the red mullet on this occasion, a choice of accompaniment (eg sautéed potatoes or roasted vegetables), a fine selection of wines that covers all the regions – and with that the deal is sealed. Appealing lunch set menu.

Name: Azimut
Description: This wine bar/cave à manger serves locavore cuisine whose flavours are drawn from locally sourced and, often, organic ingredients (including free-range poultry, snails from Eyrieu, lentils, fish from a fish farm near Châtillon-en-Diois, olives from Nyons). At lunchtime, there is a short and very reasonably priced set menu, and in the evening you can choose from the list of plates for sharing ("platarges"). To be washed down with organic or sulphur-free wines from a terrific selection – and the recommendations are on point!

Name: Le Sénéchal
Description: In a remote little village in the Haut Ségala known for its 13C bastide house and arcaded square, this restaurant with a plush feel is accommodated in a half-timbered house. Michel Truchon has passed the baton to a family, originally from Normandy, who are perpetuating their predecessor's respect for the finest ingredients. For instance: spinach raviolo with Vieux Rodez cheese – Aveyron's answer to Parmesan – topped with a reduced meat jus and a cazette (Burgundy hazelnut) emulsion; or red mullet cooked à la nacre topped with a rock fish jus and a delicate aubergine pulp. They also have a handful of guestrooms, should you wish to stay overnight.

Name: Le Puy Tilleul
Address: La Borie d'Hélipse, 5 chemin du Moulin, Tournemire, 15310, France
Description: Dominated by the feudal castle of Anjony (15C), the village of Tournemire has preserved its stone houses with stone slab roofs that are so typical of the Cantal region. This establishment, a splendid stone and corten steel complex, blends in perfectly. The contemporary dining space offers a breathtaking view of the sunset. The menu is an ode to marine ingredients. Sprinkled with seaweed and briny condiments, the menu is a meticulous showcase of fish and shellfish, and also takes in skilful surf-turf combinations. For all that, the Cantal terroir has not been overlooked: market gardeners, livestock farmers and local fish farmers are also well represented. An ambitious culinary affair.

Name: Auberge de la Source
Description: A little country inn hidden away in a remote location is sometimes all it takes to pique our interest. Our curiosity was quickly rewarded by Gabin Bouguet, formerly chef at Le Donjon in Étretat, who, here in his own restaurant, wanted to keep things simple without compromising on indulgence. Hummus, haddock, crunchy vegetables; pork belly, carrot mousseline, herb crumble; lemon tart: a treat from start to finish. After your meal, take a stroll to the cliffs a few hundred metres away – there you'll enjoy a beautiful view of Fécamp, as painted by Claude Monet.

Name: Chablis Wine Not
Description: In this world-famous wine-growing village, a "wine bistro" is bound to be a hit. Picture the scene: a local entrepreneur, two Japanese chefs who are huge fans of French cuisine, top-notch ingredients (house-made tapas, charcuterie and purebred meats that have been perfectly matured), and an amazing wine list at bargain prices (to sample here or take away). Local patrons and wine-loving tourists mingle here, and a positive atmosphere reigns. To be consumed in moderation!

Name: La Table By Mi-K'L
Description: Mickaël Pihours (previously chef at Michelin-starred Le Gambetta) has opened a contemporary "cantine plaisir" with lots of wood features and furnishings. The restaurant room is built over two levels, with a table d'hôte facing the open kitchen. The food – designed for sharing – leaves no doubt that we are in the hands of a seasoned chef: pared back to the essentials, his dishes come with an array of garnishes enhanced by aromatic herbs. A case in point is the barbecued organic pork loin and its host of tasty accompaniments (a well-seasoned salad; mushrooms in a savoury broth; a small dish of juicy vegetables). In addition, a few fine cuts of meat for sharing, often offal. The menu changes every week.

Name: Boma
Description: Tucked away behind the town hall, this compact restaurant has a somewhat unusual basement-level dining room with exposed stone, metal beams, glass partitions and modern light fittings. The chef cooks up hearty dishes, remarkable for both their generosity and bold flavours: maiale tonnato, Parmesan and capers; magret de canard, mashed potatoes with whole-grain mustard, vegetables and a piquillo pepper coulis. Friendly welcome and service, and the lunchtime set menu is a steal!

Name: Minore
Description: This "two-in-one" locale – a cocktail bar with a terrace and a traditional fine dining restaurant – is the brainchild of a pair of industry professionals: Japanese chef Katsuaki Okiyama (known from him previous restaurant, Abri) and bartender Hugo Combe. In this pared-back decor, the chef shows he is a dab hand. Shining examples are his signature dish (artichokes, morels, beef marrow and pan-fried foie gras, shallots and chive flowers, served in a casserole pot), or his recipe for monkfish, courgette and nasturtium flowers, topped with a powerful saffron sauce. This modern cuisine comes in the form of a single set menu, to which you can add other dishes.

Name: Acte 2 Yannick Delpech
Description: Yannick Delpech, previously chef of L'Amphitryon, returns to the stage for a second act with this atypical and charming restaurant. In a former sawmill, he combines fine dining with the bohemian spirit of a table d'hôtes. Soaking up an atmosphere created by music and a video projection, some 15 diners per seating are served a surprise set menu. Readable and indulgent, this authentic cuisine enhanced with robust-flavoured sauces and jus (the chef's trademark) never fails to make an impression: octopus cooked in red wine daube-style and married with lamb shoulder confit; red mullet with bottarga butter; offal toast; beef cheek slowly simmered with braised leeks and slices of grilled rib steak… the names speak volumes! All the wines on the menu are organic and natural.

Name: L'Atelier du Goût
Description: In the upper reaches of Vire, this contemporary bistro was born of a friendship between two chefs, Jordan Lebascle (previously sous-chef at Ivan Vautier) and Clément Gosselet (former sous-chef at Manoir de la Pommeraie). They deliver a modern cuisine de terroir, taking advantage of the abundance of ingredients that Normandy and local producers have to offer – think translucent cod in semi-salted butter, served with crispy potato chips and tarragon cream.

Name: Yut Fei
Address: 3F, Sino International Plaza, 137 Wusi Road, Gulou, Fuzhou, China Mainland
Description: This smart restaurant comes complete with a manicured garden, a main dining room and lavish private rooms. The Cantonese head chef, well versed in Cantonese barbecue, sizzling claypot dishes, and dim sum, has been practising his art for over 20 years. He prides himself on his double-boiled soups, slow-cooked for four hours to allow flavours to mingle. Stewed Silkie chicken soup in coconut uses coconut juice instead of water for a nutty-sweetness.

Name: Fuyuan
Address: No.40, Huaqiao Xincun, Xierhuan North Road, Gulou, Fuzhou, China Mainland
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Foreign credit cards not accepted,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: This pink villa is a private-room-only restaurant specialising in the cuisine of Fuqing City, Fujian, with clear Putian-style culinary influences. Seafood like razor clam and shrimp is the house signature. The crispy Fuqing oyster fritter brims with cabbage, oysters, razor clams and pork. Pickled bamboo shoot gives razor clam soup a kick and the bivalves coated in sweet potato starch stay plump and juicy.

Name: Rong Ji Hai Xian Lao Hua (Cangshan)
Address: 161 Liaoyuan Road, Cangshan, Fuzhou, China Mainland
