Description: Lao hua, or Fujian-style noodle soup, is usually considered frugal eats. This shop, however, champions a novel lao hua that uses luxury seafood such as live abalone and razor clam. The modern, cosy room is also worlds apart from your average lao hua stall. Just indicate your favourite toppings and noodles to the server. The kitchen team will then cook them to perfection. Also try pork head meat dressed in Sichuan pepper sauce.

Name: Lvdao Seafood
Address: 447-451 Jiu'er Road, Shishi, Quanzhou, China Mainland
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Foreign credit cards not accepted
Description: In 1989, Lvdao opened its doors with only six tables. Nowadays, it has turned into a leading F&B chain in Shishi and this flagship establishment now spans two floors. Though it specialises in Fujian fare, especially seafood, there are some Cantonese options on the menu. Try the umami-laden swimmer crab – the locals prefer it steamed with black sticky rice or taro balls. Round off with custard-filled buns, best enjoyed with sweet peanut soup.

Name: Qing You Yu
Address: 2F, 535 Huaifu Road, Fengze, Quanzhou, China Mainland
Description: The owner inherited the family business in 2021 and relaunched the restaurant here. As always, the incredible range of live seafood on offer is the main draw – just look at the three-tier fish tanks at the entrance. Diners are expected to choose their own seafood from the tanks, but servers are more than happy to help. Chilled swimmer crab boasts melty roe and firm, flavourful meat. Swamp eel braised with tea seed oil and basil is silky and aromatic.

Name: Wei Rong Lao Hua
Address: 26 Fuer Road, Gulou, Fuzhou, China Mainland
Description: One of the most beloved lao hua noodle shops in Fuzhou, Wei Rong is jam-packed with noodle lovers day and night. Pick your noodles and toppings – the seafood, meats and offal are all fresh and top-notch. The pork broth is loaded with meaty flavours; the best way to enjoy the broth is to dip in a deep-fried dough stick for added crispness. Open from morning till late, this is the place to come for a noodle fix almost any time of the day.

Name: Jiang Nan Yuan
Address: 401, Building 27, Zone A, Yuanhe 1916 Artdistrict, 610 Xinmen Street, Licheng, Quanzhou, China Mainland
Description: Only two set menus are offered, with 11 or 12 ovo-lacto vegetarian courses, which can be made vegan upon request. They change according to the solar terms in Chinese calendar and the more expensive menu includes gourmet ingredients like bird’s nest. As opposed to typically light-tasting vegetarian food, the dishes here pack oomph and intense heat. Richly flavoured, shredded wild rice stem with pea kernels is seasoned with chilli oil and mushroom sauce.

Name: Hatter
Address: 433 Guxi Road, Gulou, Fuzhou, China Mainland
Description: The owner is a returnee from Australia who has worked closely with the chef to develop two tasting menus that mirror the seasons. The menus bear a strong European slant and star first-rate produce from around the world with occasional local ingredients such as Fuzhou condiments like red wine lees and sa cha sauce. The compact dining room sports a casual continental vibe, perfect for date nights and friendly get-togethers.

Name: 1927 Dong Yuan Si Chu
Address: 65 Siming East Road, Siming, Xiamen, China Mainland
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Foreign credit cards not accepted
Description: This private dining concept in a historical mansion (c 1927) comes complete with a Suzhou-style garden. Despite its proximity to a busy road, it offers tranquil respite. With just 10 private rooms across three levels, reservations are a must and menus can be tailored. Items available may vary, but you can expect deftly prepared Xiamen fare such as double-boiled pork shank soup with green olives and whelks, or braised abalone with ginger duck.

Name: Xuanhe Cuisine
Address: Shop 3013, 3F, Art Mall, Rongqiao Center, 100 Jiangbin West Avenue, Taijiang, Fuzhou, China Mainland
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Foreign credit cards not accepted
Description: The wood-rich interior feels warm and cosy and the food, in the same vein, is comforting and familiar. The menu stars the hits of Fuzhou cuisine and cleverly uses local ingredients to create authentic flavours. Expect items like fried pork belly marinated in red vinasse, razor clams and sautéed sticky rice cake with mud crab. The quick-fried crisp duo, jellyfish and pork kidney in sweet and sour sauce, is another bestseller.

Name: Xia
Address: 1F, Lohkah Hotel & Spa, 277 Penang Road, Huli, Xiamen, China Mainland
Description: Since 2018, Chef Yang hailing from Jiangsu has been helming the kitchen with a menu that is half Cantonese and half Minnan. Chilled peanut sweet soup is a modified version of the Fujian classic, with a velvety peanut custard over a bed of toothsome algae. The west-facing views over Wuyuan Bay make Xia the perfect spot for a romantic dinner at sunset.

Name: Lucheng
Address: 39F, Conrad Hotel, 186 Yanwu West Road, Siming, Xiamen, China Mainland
Description: Perched atop the city’s sail-shaped landmark, Lucheng commands fantastic views. Traditional Chinese motifs are stylised and melded with elegant fixtures and fittings for comfort. The kitchen team of Fujian natives managed by a young Minnan chef excels in Fujian classics with creative twists, showcasing the province’s wide range of produce. Try deep-fried starchy taro in aged vinegar reduction, and braised river eel with fish maw and pickled cabbage.

Name: Chosop
Address: Shop 01, 2F, Sandi Union Center, Zhenwu Road, Taijiang, Fuzhou, China Mainland
Description: This stylish venue in a shopping mall sports low fabric-clad partitions that provide privacy and enhance the overall vibe. The kitchen is helmed by a Sichuanese chef; the extensive menu covers most bases of authentic Sichuan fare. Try pork belly braised in wine and soy with salted duck egg and rice for a satisfying meal. The Sichuan classic jidouhua – minced chicken and egg white poached in chicken stock to mimic tofu texture – is also impeccably crafted.

Name: Antstory
Address: 7 Buzhengya Lane, Wudianshi, Jinjiang, Quanzhou, China Mainland
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Foreign credit cards not accepted
Description: Since 2018, Antstory has been running this historic three-storey red brick villa. The young local chef reinterprets traditional Fujian recipes with modern techniques. First-timers can pick from ‘10 classics’, like Shima five-spice pork roll and braised yellow croaker with scallion. The chef’s vinegar pork is a new take on the Quanzhou classic – pork marinated in apple cider vinegar, deep fried and served with wafer and macadamia nuts.

Name: Xing Wang Seafood · Rongting Hui (Siming)
Address: Shop 017, 4F, Xinghe COCOPark, 81-89 Zhanhong Road, Siming, Xiamen, China Mainland
Description: The seafood chain started out as a fishmonger’s back in 1994. It began running a roadside food stall in 2016 and rebranded itself in 2023 with this upmarket flagship in a shopping mall. Live fish tanks are showcased next to a museum-like display of 100+ taxidermy crustaceans. Pick your favourite seafood from the tanks and specify how you want it cooked. The menu also offers other Minnan specialities to accompany your meal.

Name: Harmony Garden (Xierhuan North Road)
Address: No.32, Huaqiao Xincun, Xierhuan North Road, Gulou, Fuzhou, China Mainland
Description: With nine private rooms in a two-storey villa, Harmony Garden offers warm, friendly service and Fujian cooking with creative twists. The owner used to run a tea leaf business, which explains the antique tea ware and tea leaves on sale. Signatures include stir-fried sliced conch in red yeast rice wine lees, which marries lingering aromas and a crisp texture. Drunken pork ribs are deep-fried before being tossed in a tangy wine vinegar glaze.

Name: Yin Lu
Address: Building 66, Gulong Inhabitancy Park, Shangzhong East 2nd Road, Huli, Xiamen, China Mainland
Description: This household name opened its doors in 1996 and moved to this historic villa in 2009. The kitchen specialises in Xiamen classics and the menu is concise yet appetising. Don’t miss the ubiquitous double-boiled Muscovy duck soup with crab, whose robust meaty flavour melds with seafood umami. It is best enjoyed with Xiamen rice noodles that suck up the goodness. Other favourites include oyster omelette and deep-fried five-spice rolls.

Name: Pari-
Address: 8-10 Samlarn Road, Phra Sing ,Mueang Chiang Mai, Chiang Mai, 50200, Thailand
Description: The cosy design and small counter foster a vibrant, relaxed dining experience. The small yet high-quality dishes combine Japanese Izakaya style with Thai ingredients, enhanced with wasabi or yuzu. The ham comes from a Yunnan village in Chiang Mai, perilla from Mae Hong Son, sashimi-grade fish from the south, and meat from organic farms. We recommend the corn-fried rice Yunnan ham and the house-made ponzu sauce, elevated by a refreshing Somsa citrus oil.

Name: Kinu by Takagi
Address: 2F, Mandarin Oriental Hotel, 48 Soi Charoen Krung 40, Charoen Krung Road, Bang Rak, Bangkok, 10500, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Counter dining,Notable sake list,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: Hidden behind sliding wooden doors, Kinu's décor combines Japanese and Thai influences, featuring teakwood crosshatch flooring and a mix of Japanese and northern Thai ceramics. Chef Takagi excels in Kyoto-style Kaiseki, highlighting the natural flavours of top Japanese ingredients. The bar offers an excellent sake collection, and a matcha tea ceremony marks the end of your visit. Additionally, welcome drinks are served in a Japanese-style Minka area.

Name: Yangzi Jiang
Address: 10 Nimmanahaeminda Road Soi 5, Suthep, Mueang Chiang Mai, Chiang Mai, 50200, Thailand
Description: After years working in various hotels and living for over a decade in Thailand, chef Chan went back to his Hong Kong roots to open this simply decorated Chinese restaurant inside a contemporary Lanna house in trendy Nimmanahaeminda. His cooking is fresh, clean and well-executed; the menu includes a variety of house-made dim sum alongside dishes like Chinese stir-fried prawns and a stand-out crispy pork belly. Advanced booking is highly recommended.

Name: Fish Club
Address: Andaz Pattaya Jomtien Beach  345 Mu 3, Na Chom Thian, Sattahip, Chon Buri, 20250, Thailand
Description: Fish Club's location on a serene beach sets it apart from the typical Pattaya dining scene. With indoor and outdoor dining, the restaurant combines a pleasant view with a lively atmosphere. The menu reveals Western and Asian influences, and the chefs excel at grilling, controlling temperatures perfectly. The peanutty sriracha sauce pairs impeccably with your steamed or grilled seafood.

Name: Ayutthayarom
Address: 1/1 Mu 7, Ban Pom, Phra Nakhon Si Ayutthaya, Phra Nakhon Si Ayutthaya, 13000, Thailand
Description: Situated in a pleasant, cool, and shady location, the riverside offers seating in small Thai pavilions and boasts views of a golden pagoda. The space is decorated in traditional Thai style, in keeping with the cuisine, which features intense local flavours. Try the sour soup with fresh chilli and squid, and the aromatic, flavoursome fried river fish in chu chi curry. Round off your meal with classic Thai desserts made with fresh coconut milk.

Name: Jamn
Address: 8 Soi Chan 43 Yaek 41, Bang Khlo, Bang Kho Laem, Bangkok, 10120, Thailand
Description: Jamn offers a private dining experience in a family home. The menu is customised to your preferences or features typical Thai dishes. Their family set menu includes an appetiser, dessert, and a main course presented in the Thai samrap style with five dishes for sharing. We recommend starting with the crispy shrimp paste rice with sweet tiny shrimp and sour mango. A minimum charge per table is required.

Name: Friend's Table
Address: 125 Mu 6, Hang Dong, Chiang Mai, 50230, Thailand
Description: Friend's Table follows a chef's table concept in the glass-enclosed dining wing of the owner's home. Diners can chat with the chefs at work in this stylish interior, dimly lit with a red hue. Collaborating on each dish, the duo of chefs strive for perfection: the food is refined, creatively presented, and packed with flavour, possessing an intensity that is true to the Asian palate. Be sure to be punctual; dinner will start at 7 pm.

Name: NAVAN NAVAN
Address: 55 Mu 7, San Pong, Mae Rim, Chiang Mai, 50180, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Counter dining,Credit cards not accepted,Garden or park
Description: Surrounded by rice fields, this stand-alone cement building affords a clear view of the open kitchen. The chef draws on various cuisines and uses a charcoal grill to cook local ingredients. His unpretentious style promotes healthy eating, and each dish highlights the natural flavours of the ingredients. Arrive before sunset to see the beautiful garden.

Name: Palmier by Guillaume Galliot
Address: Four Seasons Private Residences,  300/1 Charoen Krung Road, Yan Nawa, Sathon, Bangkok, 10120, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Brunch,Car park,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: In 2024, French chef Guillaume Galliot brought this classic yet relaxed brasserie dining experience to Bangkok. Take a seat outdoors to enjoy views of the Chao Phraya River and a menu composed of classic French dishes, signature creations and innovative offerings. The culinary delights include foie gras terrine and Boston lobster confit. A passionate sommelier is on hand with recommendations from an extensive French-focused wine list to match the food.

Name: Indian by Nature
Address: 306 Chateau Dale Complex 64-68 Thappraya Road, Pattaya, Nong Prue, Bang Lamung, Chon Buri, 20150, Thailand
Description: This fine dining spot delivers authentic Indian cuisine in an inviting ambiance featuring contemporary Indian paintings and decorative touches. With creative twists on North Indian staples, highlights include chicken tikka and dal makhni. Main dishes are thoughtfully served in small pots over a flame to keep them warm. For solo diners, the traditional thali sets comprise tasty samples of signature à la carte dishes.

Name: Shrimp Noodles Ao Kae
Address: 76 Phoonphol Road, Talat Nuea, Mueang Phuket, Phuket, 83000, Thailand
Description: It has been crafting meticulous shrimp noodle bowls for over a decade. Tom yum and original shrimp flavour noodles, available as wet and dry options, come with the perfect number of condiments. Pork wontons are the standout! For intense flavour, try the dry tom yum noodles.

Name: Khrua Ohm
Address: 2/99 Mu 2, Wichit Songkhram Road, Kathu, Phuket, 83120, Thailand
Description: After a decade as a musician with a side gig of cooking for bandmates, these days Somphop finds himself enjoying daily walks through the market for fresh catches of the day and hand-cutting them for various southern Thai dishes served at his small, casual restaurant. Braised fish in salted soybean sauce; prawns with salted eggs and acacia; and wok-fried pork featuring the tender, succulent ‘armpit cut’ between the picnic shoulder and belly are not to be missed.

Name: Chop Chop Cook Shop
Address: 328 Yaowarat Road, Chakkrawat, Samphanthawong, Bangkok, 10100, Thailand
Description: Housed in a five-storey Art Deco building, this eatery pays homage to its goldsmith heritage through its design. Chef David Thompson has been garnering acclaim for his Chinese cuisine with Thai touches since opening in 2023. High-quality ingredients that elevate tradition go into his refined yet honest food. Start with the crispy prawn wafer, and don't miss the roasted duck soup… but save room for the ginger milk curd – as simple as it is delightful.

Name: Sushi Saito
Address: Four Seasons Private Residences, 300 Charoen Krung Road,  Yan Nawa, Sathon, Bangkok, 10120, Thailand
Description: Located in the Four Seasons Private Residences by the Chao Phraya River, Sushi Saito is the sister branch of the renowned Tokyo restaurant by Chef Takashi Saito. Specialising in Edomae-style sushi, it showcases chef Maruyama’s skills and Edo-period techniques. The restaurant embraces classic Japanese décor, featuring an atrium with a drinks bar and a dining area with a Hinoki cypress counter-table around an open kitchen.

Name: Pak Mor Robot
Address: 82 Benchama Road, Nai Mueang, Mueang Ubon Ratchathani, Ubon Ratchathani, 34000, Thailand
Description: The chef owner of Pak Mor Robot has satisfied the tummies of locals for over 30 years. She prepares a variety of Vietnamese dumplings in a steamer at the front of this neat little outlet. The signature, her own invention, is the incredibly tasty Vietnamese dumpling with fried eggs.

Name: Bangkok Bold (Pathum Wan)
Address: LGF, Central Embassy, 1031 Phloen Chit Road, Lumphini, Pathum Wan, Bangkok, 10330, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus
Description: Word-of-mouth inspired Chef Nhoi to take the leap from cooking studio in the old town to opening a restaurant in the city centre. Her aim is to preserve the heritage of Thai taste that’s ‘basic and bold’ with creative twists. Check out the unique stir-fried pork and shrimp, hummingbird flowers, fish sauce and scrambled eggs. And the spicy salted beef in coconut cream is tender with balanced flavours, enlivened by fresh shallots and bird's eye chillies.

Name: Fried Banana Rama 5 (Bang Kruai - Sai Noi Road)
Address: 116 Bang Kruai - Sai Noi Road, Bang Si Thong, Bang Kruai, Nonthaburi, 11130, Thailand
Description: This spot is best known for its deep-fried bananas. Coated in crispy batter made from coconut and white sesame, they exude a rich coconut aroma. The sweet potato balls are another standout. Be prepared for queues during peak hours.

Name: TAAN
Address: 25F, Siam@Siam Design Hotel, 865 Rama 1 Road, Wang Mai, Pathum Wan, Bangkok, 10330, Thailand
Description: Like the Siam@Siam Design Hotel Bangkok in which it sits, this rooftop restaurant takes a contemporary approach yet retains an authentic Thai character. The chef produces a seasonally changing tasting menu that uses entirely Thai produce, all of premium quality. Dishes are well-presented, showcase great skill from the kitchen team and often have a story behind them. Try one of the restaurant’s signature cocktails, which are also crafted with local ingredients.

Name: Wah Lok
Address: 2F, Carlton Hotel Bangkok Sukhumvit, 491 Sukhumvit Road, Khlong Tan Nuea, Vadhana, Bangkok, 10110, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: A Singaporean institution for over 3 decades, Wah Lok boasts a strong following, several awards, and this sibling outside Singapore. The plush carpeted dining room sports high ceilings and a stylish mix of modern and classic details. The food is artistically plated and made with premium imports such as Boston lobster, which is consummately braised and enhanced with ginger and spring onion. Book in advance, especially for the expertly crafted dim sum lunch.

Name: Klang Na Pla Khao
Address: 5 Mu 9, Nong Tamlueng, Phan Thong, Chon Buri, 20160, Thailand
Description: This country-style restaurant serves up a splendid array of Isan dishes and Eastern Thai specialties from land and sea. The highlight is a spicy stir-fry with an original curry paste recipe from Chanthaburi province, capturing the authentic essence of Thai cuisine. There's no compromise on bold, genuine Thai flavours. The tranquil outdoor setting affords views of lush green rice fields, and the relaxed atmosphere makes it perfect for friend and family gatherings.

Name: Kang
Address: Jing Jai Market, 46 Atsadathon Road, Pa Tan, Mueang Chiang Mai, Chiang Mai, 50300, Thailand
Description: Opened in 2023, Kang is a fresh addition to Jing Jai Market. It offers a cosy retreat with a laid-back approach to dining, plus a menu that's ideal for sharing the highlights of Indonesian, Malaysian and Thai cuisine with friends. We suggest opting for their signature Nasi Lemak, or one of the bold, aromatic curries. All dishes are made to order, so diners may need to have a little patience while waiting for their delicious meals.

Name: Khrua Ban Po Ta
Address: 23 Soi Pattaya Tai 8, Pattaya, Nong Prue, Bang Lamung, Chon Buri, 20150, Thailand
Description: The breezy, spacious dining room surrounded by vines and plants makes for a relaxing and laidback coastal ambience. The seafood-based menu features shrimp, squid and crab options cooked several ways. The stir-fried squid with black ink sauce is a showstopper, but diners also enjoy shelling the stir-fried whole crab with curry powder. The sweet local seasoning enhances the food's natural umami.

Name: ÎNT
Address: Rooftop F, Best Western Sukhumvit 20, 17 Soi Sukhumvit 20, Sukhumvit Road, Khlong Toei, Bangkok, 10110, Thailand
Description: Ascend to this rooftop restaurant to soak up an ambiance of elegant earthy tones blended with a subtle blue hue, all set against the warmth of an open kitchen. The tasting menu reflects Chef Patin 'Knock' Promsawadi and his team's unique, artistic approach to simplicity. Using French culinary techniques, he strikes a masterful balance between Thai and French ingredients to produce contemporary dishes that capture the essence of Thai cuisine. Advance booking necessary!

Name: Khaan
Address: 14/3 Soi Som Khit, Phloen Chit Road, Lumphini, Pathum Wan, Bangkok, 10330, Thailand
Description: The new restaurant of Chef Sujira 'Aom' Pongmorn, Khaan – meaning both "tiger" and "proclaim" in Thai, roars with impressive Thai flavours, while shining a spotlight on ingredients and the provinces from which they're sourced. The chef's use of modern techniques means her culinary creations, served in an elegant space decked out in deep red hues, retain all their characteristic depth. Opt for the tasting menu, paired with wine or tea, to elevate the experience.

Name: Sushi Saryu
Address: GF, Kronos Sathorn Building, 46 North Sathorn Road, Si Lom, Bang Rak, Bangkok, 10500, Thailand
Description: Saryu, a name that symbolises the precious passing of time, is set behind a discreet wooden door that leads into a lounge-cum-cave. The minimalist dining area sports a traditional omakase counter made out of Hinoki wood. Chef Seiji Sudo meticulously crafts a 15-course omakase menu based on seafood sourced directly from Tokyo’s Toyosu Fish Market. With a mere 6 seats available daily (or 8 for private groups), reservations are essential.

Name: Wagyu Steakhouse
Address: Twinpalms Phuket Resort, 106/46 Mu 3, Choeng Thale, Thalang, Phuket, 83110, Thailand
Description: Spanning two floors of the Twinpalms hotel, this restaurant’s elegant yet earthy interior and dimmed lighting make it the perfect setting for steak and wine lovers. Everything is on display: from the chefs in the open kitchen and the nice beef showcase with a small oyster bar, to the choice cuts of top-quality imported meats. Guests can choose their steak from the fridge before it is expertly grilled by the chefs. A choice of five high-end brands of knives is also on offer.

Name: Pa Porn Traditional Pork Noodles
Address: 121/2 Mu 8, Soi Pa Maphrao 10, U Thong Road, Hua Ro, Phra Nakhon Si Ayutthaya, Phra Nakhon Si Ayutthaya, 13000, Thailand
Description: Auntie Porn has mastered pork noodle soup for over 50 years, initially on her boat at age 17, now on land. Her Tom Yum soup boasts expertly prepared noodles, rich broth, and toppings like minced pork, fish sausage, or BBQ pork, complemented by red shrimp and peanuts. She also offers tasty fish balls.

Name: Nusara
Address: 336 Maha Rat Road, Phra Borom Maha Ratchawang, Phra Nakhon, Bangkok, 10200, Thailand
Description: Chef Thitid 'Ton' Tassanakajohn, renowned for his work at Le Du, leads this inviting restaurant, presenting classic Thai cuisine with a modern twist. The cooking style leans more towards tradition, paying homage to Ton's grandmother and family recipes. Quality ingredients from across Thailand shine in impressive dishes, paired ideally with diverse wines. The top-floor lounge offers a perfect spot for pre-dinner champagne with a view of Wat Pho.

Name: Gaggan
Address: 68 Soi Sukhumvit 31, Sukhumvit Road, Khlong Tan Nuea, Vadhana, Bangkok, 10110, Thailand
Description: Sit front-row at Gaggan’s immersive 14-seater chef’s counter, an experience featuring changing light effects and a thumping soundtrack. Chef Gaggan’s bold personality shines through in the 22-course tasting menu, sharing apocryphal stories and a vibrant narrative. His progressive Indian cooking, using modern techniques and global ingredients, crafts intriguing dishes, each telling a unique story.

Name: Hoi Tod Singha Buri
Address: The night market in front of Telephone Organization of Thailand, Tha Wasukri, Phra Nakhon Si Ayutthaya, 13000, Thailand
Description: Culinary theatre meets a one-man dance party at this Bang Ian Night Market stall named after the chef’s home province of Sing Buri. It serves omelette with crispy mussels – watch him whip them up and top them off with bean sprouts without missing a beat; then enjoy the fruits of his labour.

Name: Sang Thatien
Address: 75 Maha Rat Road, Phra Borom Maha Ratchawang, Phra Nakhon, Bangkok, 10200, Thailand
Description: Formerly an ice factory, this small eatery retains some of the interior structure and incorporates vintage décor in a dining room decorated with basic wooden furniture and collectibles. The chef embraces seasonal Thai ingredients, especially fruit, to produce unique, signature dishes in a home-cooking style, such as strawberry salad with shrimp paste and caramelised pork and spicy plum mango salad. The crab meat with fresh herbs and spicy sauce is unmissable.

Name: Pa Noi Beef Noodles
Address: 57/8 Sisuttha Road, Mak Khaeng, Mueang Udon Thani, Udon Thani, 41000, Thailand
Description: The aroma of beef noodle soup greets diners at this popular eatery. The distinctive tamarind chilli paste pairs perfectly with deep-fried chicken skin or mixed into the noodles. The boat noodles with rich flavours are also a must-try.

Name: Bang Dean
Address: 16/10 Mu 1, Phet Kasem Road, Bang Nai Si, Takua Pa, Phang-Nga, 82110, Thailand
Description: Nearby the Takua Pa Government Office, this street food place serves Thai-Muslim dishes, including excellent chicken biryani, plus crispy rotis paired with savoury curries or sweet condensed milk and banana. Open for breakfast through late lunch, it closes when the food runs out.

Name: Lumdee Te Khuadang
Address: V Community, 345/9 Mu 3, Wongwaen Rop 2 Road, San Phra Net, San Sai, Chiang Mai, 50210, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Bearing a loose resemblance to San Francisco’s Golden Gate Bridge, the bridge in this restaurant’s name (which translates as 'delicious at the red bridge') forms an iconic landmark while also providing guests with a pleasant spot for dining after dark. The range of healthy Northern Thai dishes provides intense flavours; their biotechnology-derived fermented pork has the highest levels of hygiene and quality, and is used in many of the dishes.

Name: Peang-Prai
Address: 101/18 Soi Namtok Bang Toei, Ban Pa Khlok Road, Pa Khlok, Thalang, Phuket, 83110, Thailand
Description: In the depths of the forest at the entrance to Bang Pae waterfall, two wooden pavilions stand connected by a terrace walkway. Here, a family-run restaurant faces a lagoon and a verdant wall of forest, while diners are accompanied by the welcoming calls of birds and gibbons. The tranquil ambiance is joined by traditional Thai and Southern Thai cooking, with local Phuket dishes standing out. Seasonal local clams are delicious and can be cooked many ways, including stir-fried with chilli paste.

Name: Khao Kriab Pak Mor Talat Na San Jao
Address: Na San Jao Market, Tonpo Road, Talat, Muaeng Surat Thani, Surat Thani, 84000, Thailand
Description: The veteran stall-owner has been making her delicious dumplings for decades in this famous food cart in Na San Jao market. The thin steamed rice dumplings combine a sweet, gooey texture with a savoury filling, made with minced pork, crushed peanuts and herbs in creamy coconut milk.

Name: Day & Night
Address: 83/25 Liang Mueang Road, Surat Thani, 84000, Thailand
Description: This enchanting, almost English-looking country pub draws tourists like bees to honey. Boasting a bright, breezy vibe, it serves international favourites, from steak to pizzas and light snacks, with a tempting array of cocktails and craft beers. The fresh watermelon topped with dry salmon and served with a spicy salad dressing is sweet and juicy, while another popular local delicacy, bingsu, salted egg yolk, offers a creamy scent and texture. Smooth live music in the evenings.

Name: Lenzi Tuscan Kitchen
Address: 69/2 Soi Ruam Ruedi 2, Wireless Road, Lumphini, Pathum Wan, Bangkok, 10330, Thailand
Description: It’s a family affair at this authentic Tuscan restaurant, from the top-notch meats and cheeses sourced from chef Francesco Lenzi’s family farm in Pisa to his mother’s limoncello. The chef uses traditional cooking techniques from back home and often pops out of the open kitchen to greet diners like family. Start with antipasti or an iI primi like Risotto Taleggio e Tartufo and then try the flavoursome Filetto Alla Rossini. Reservations are recommended.

Name: Sra Bua by Kiin Kiin
Address: GF, Siam Kempinski Hotel, 991/9 Rama 1 Road, Pathum Wan, Bangkok, 10330, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: Inspired by its sister restaurant, Copenhagen's Kiin Kiin, Sra Bua is one of Bangkok’s original purveyors of modern, innovative Thai cuisine. À la carte and tasting menus are available, with their dishes – from street food starter to dessert – proving creative and original, yet respectful of traditional Thai flavours. Premium international ingredients are used throughout, while both alcoholic and non-alcoholic pairings are available to complete the experience.

Name: Reunros (Yan Nawa)
Address: Bangkok Square, 762/2 Rama 3 Road, Bang Phongphang, Yan Nawa, Bangkok, 10120, Thailand
Description: When Ruenros opened 40+ years ago, its owner came from a medical background, hence the focus on herbal and medicinal braised dishes. The 3rd generation heir now runs it and he chooses all the market fresh ingredients himself every day. Specialties include spring rolls using a family recipe, stir-fried goat with celery, fried rice with salted fish and slow-cooked soup, which is packed with flavour. For dessert, try the taro purée with sticky rice.

Name: Canvas
Address: 113/9-10 Soi Sukhumvit 55, Khlong Tan Nuea, Vadhana, Bangkok, 10110, Thailand
Description: Food meets art at Chef Riley Sanders' plush establishment. Every dish of the culinary journey is depicted as a painting on the menu, like an art gallery brochure. The talented Texan sources seasonal ingredients from all over Thailand and transforms them with a modern interpretation. Counter seats offer views of the chefs, while tables upstairs offer more privacy. Wine pairings are available to complete the experience.

Name: Yamazato
Address: 24F, The Okura Prestige Bangkok, 57 Wireless Road, Lumphini, Pathum Wan, Bangkok, 10330, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Counter dining,Great view,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: The Okura Prestige’s Japanese restaurant boasts 3 dining areas: a sushi bar, teppanyaki grills and a stylish dining room. The fish is sourced weekly from Toyosu market in Japan, and they offer a rotating selection of sashimi options, depending on availability. Dressed in traditional kimono, the staff make every effort to ensure that diners have a great experience, while the panoramic high-rise cityscape offers a romantic setting that couples adore.

Name: Ta Khai
Address: Rosewood Hotel, 88/28, 88/30-33 Muen-Ngoen Road, Pa Tong, Kathu, Phuket, 83150, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Counter dining,Great view,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: Ta Khai means ‘fishing net’, and here diners can choose live seafood from the restaurant’s tank before a chef scoops it up and cooks it. Dishes, including the deep-fried white snapper with fish sauce, are flavoursome, with spicing slightly toned down if you wish, while two set menus offer a variety of items to try. Ask for a table on the lovely terrace for a panoramic view of the bay and cityscape beyond – or for something different, book a BBQ sala.

Name: Aunt Aoy Kitchen
Address: 377 2 Chiang Rai Road, Suthep, Mueang Chiang Mai, Chiang Mai, 50200, Thailand
Description: The décor is simple, with a display of photos and messages on post-it notes from customers gone by. Aunt Aoy spent much of her career cooking in hotel kitchens. Her expertise is realised in the fluffy yet crispy Chef Omelette with stir-fried minced pork, salted egg and pork crackling.

Name: Celadon
Address: GF, The Sukhothai Hotel, 13/3 Sathon Tai Road, Thung Maha Mek, Sathon, Bangkok, 10120, Thailand
Description: There’s more than a hint of romance to dining in these two delightful Salas in the manicured grounds of the Sukhothai Hotel, surrounded by lotus ponds. A wide-ranging menu includes seafood selections and dishes from the charcoal grill; the five- and eight-course set menu delivers smaller tasting dishes. The signature steamed rice dumplings make a delightful starter, while whole seabass baked with Thai herbs impresses. Service is attentive and charming and there are nightly performances of traditional Thai dance.

Name: Royd
Address: 95/1 Dibuk Road, Talat Nuea, Mueang Phuket, Phuket, 83000, Thailand
Description: There are many courses and many delights to be found on the tasting menu at this cosy little restaurant. Seating is divided between tables and the counter, with room for just 12 guests in total; there is an excellent flow to the parade of innovative Southern Thai dishes like crispy bee hoon topped with morning glory, which are all attractively presented and delivered by a likeable team. Accompany the fabulous cooking with a well-crafted cocktail pairing that uses techniques such as fermentation to make interesting drinks that complement the food well.

Name: Baan Landai
Address: 252/13-14 Phra Pok Klao Road, Si Phum, Mueang Chiang Mai, Chiang Mai, 50200, Thailand
Description: Don’t let the slightly unkempt exterior keep you from visiting Chef Landai’s restaurant. The interior exudes charm with its eclectic décor and a window into the kitchen, where chefs whip up pan-Thai dishes like flavourful pork ribs with red wine sauce. The portions are suitable for sharing with friends, and don’t forget to save room for their traditional Thai desserts.

Name: Punjab Grill
Address: GF, Radisson Suites Bangkok Sukhumvit, 23/2-3 Soi Sukhumvit 13, Khlong Toei Nuea, Vadhana, Bangkok, 10110, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: Like its sister restaurants in India and across the world, Bangkok’s Punjab Grill serves authentic yet contemporary Northern Indian cuisine. The menu features creative twists on dishes like chaat, which includes chutney-dressed avocado and puffed rice with yoghurt espuma. Equally flavourful are classics like biryani and tikka. Vegetarian dishes are offered à la carte and as part of tasting courses. A glass wall in the elegant dining room provides a view of the tandoor action.

Name: The House by Ginger
Address: 199 Mun Mueang Road, Si Phum, Mueang Chiang Mai, Chiang Mai, 50200, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: Open for decades on the edge of the old city, this stylish and quirky spot serves a mixture of Northern Thai classics and those with a more modern twist. Premium ingredients like New Zealand beef are a feature, as are organic vegetables and daily picked herbs from their nearby Ginger Farm. The seasonally changing menu includes the Chiang Mai platter – an ideal way to sample an array of dishes. Pair your food with one of their many lovely cocktails and to extend your evening, continue on to the House Lounge next door.

Name: Vacca
Address: 99 Mu 20, Airport Road, Sila, Mueang Khon Kaen, Khon Kaen, 40000, Thailand
Description: Italian chef-owner Fabio Colautti's restaurant near Khon Kaen Airport offers authentic Italian flavours with homemade pasta, wood-fired pizzas, and grilled meats. Opened in 2015, it boasts a classic Italian ambience with a cosy white interior, a large wine cellar, and an open kitchen. Highlights include the Vacca pizza and the grilled Wagyu rib-eye.

Name: Rimsaun
Address: 200 Phu Khao Thong Soi 5, Pratu Chai, Phra Nakhon Si Ayutthaya, Phra Nakhon Si Ayutthaya, 13000, Thailand
Description: The owner hails from Nakhon Sri Thammarat and has been serving quality southern Thai cuisine in the ancient capital for over 25 years. Despite its simple décor, the restaurant with its high vaulted ceilings, shady garden and lack of walls is well worth visiting. The southern Thai sour curry with fish is a family recipe and a must-try, while the fried prawns are glazed in a delectably sticky tamarind sauce. Keep an eye out for the daily specials on the white board.

Name: Embassy Room
Address: 9F, Park Hyatt Hotel, 88 Wireless Road, Lumphini, Pathum Wan, Bangkok, 10330, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Wheelchair access
Description: Embassy Room offers authentic Catalan cuisine with à la carte options and tasting menus. The chefs are happy to personalise dishes to cater to dietary needs. The Bomba rice dishes are perfect for rice lovers, while the private room is ideal for intimate gatherings. The outdoor seating boasts views of the sky garden. For Spanish wine aficionados, the wine list features over 100 labels from seven regions.

Name: Rock-Un
Address: 85 Si Mueang Road, Takua Pa, Phang-Nga, 82110, Thailand
Description: The signature pork leg, which is stewed for 6 hours, has a spicy, charcoal flavour – the tasty recipe comes from the chef-owner’s Chinese great grandfather. Photos of visiting royals confirm its prestige; one of the most popular places among the Sino-Portuguese buildings of the old town.

Name: We-La-Dee
Address: 291 Mu 9, Nong Chom, San Sai, Chiang Mai, 50210, Thailand
Description: We-La-Dee brings central Thai cuisine north in an airy industrial-style dining room marked by playful accents. The restaurant’s large collection of action figures and a floor-to-ceiling installation of artificial flowers inspire photographs. Its extensive menu, which includes some original recipes from the chef, inspire both relaxed meals with family and friends and afternoons spent sipping coffee or tea and enjoying dessert.

Name: Krua Phech Doi Ngam
Address: 267/1 Mu 2, Mahidol Road, Pa Daet, Mueang Chiang Mai, Chiang Mai, 50100, Thailand
Description: This popular open-air eatery serves well-sized northern Thai favourites at fair prices. Kang Liang, the peppery curry paste in spicy mixed vegetables goes well with the prawns’ natural sweetness; while the local fish marinated in herbs and spices is grilled in a bamboo tube until soft, with a smoky aroma. Do check the blackboard for specials of the day, which often focus on seasonal dishes.

Name: Thian Leng Bak Kut Teh
Address: 35 Mu 4, Phet Kasem Road, Khok Kloi, Takua Thung, Phang-Nga, 82140, Thailand
Description: Using heavenly recipes from Kedah, Malaysian Bak Kut Teh is a divine pork rib soup with Chinese herbs, served in a clay pot. The succulent slow-cooked meat simply slips off the bone. The chef is so confident about its tastiness, there’s a money-back guarantee for those who disagree!

Name: Nern Khao View Talay
Address: 18/6 Mu 10, Soi Namtok Wat Khao, Khok Kloi, Takua Thung, Phang-Nga, 82140, Thailand
Description: Nern Khao View Talay offers stunning views of mountains and sea from up high on a hill. Serving Thai and southern cuisine, the stir-fried pork with shrimp paste is a highlight. The aromatic paste mixes nicely with herbal notes and deep-fried shallot, while the thick sour curry soup with shrimp has a deep orange colour, tasty acacia omelette and plump shrimps. What about tackling that steep slope? There’s a shuttle service from the car park at the foot of the hill.

Name: Dhabkwan
Address: Dhabkwan Resort, 178, 180, 182, 184 Nonthaburi Road, Suan Yai, Mueang Nonthaburi, Nonthaburi, 11000, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Cash only,Garden or park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus
Description: Located in a teak house in the middle of Dhabkwan Resort, this traditional Thai restaurant opens onto a tranquil lotus pond and inviting gardens. The atmosphere perfectly matches the authentic Thai menu, which includes hard-to-find dishes like Miang Kam with lotus petals and santol curry with roasted pork. Making it even more authentic, meals are served on Benjarong porcelain. Dhabkwan also offers Thai cookery classes and is available for events.

Name: Banrimbung
Address: 372/21 Mu 2, Nong Din Daeng, Mueang Nakhon Pathom, Nakhon Pathom, 73000, Thailand
Description: Serving family-style Thai cuisine on a large pond in Nakhon Pathom since 2001, the spacious restaurant offers waterside seating in five distinct seating areas with live music during dinner. Everything on the menu is fresh, with the fish and seafood kept alive until cooked. Two highlights are stir-fried prawns with shrimp oil and fried seabass with fish sauce and spicy green mango salad. The restaurant is family-friendly, with a kids’ zone in the garden for young diners to enjoy.

Name: Jay Jia Yentafo
Address: 564 Rama 4 Road, Maha Phruettharam, Bang Rak, Bangkok, 10500, Thailand
Description: For 30+ years, office workers have been making a beeline to Jay Jia Yentafo for their eponymous pink-noodle soup and legendary homemade shrimp balls. The soup packs a knockout combination of shrimp, fish, fish sticks and fried wontons and explodes in sour and spicy notes.

Name: Jao Nai Fish Ball (Bang Khae Road)
Address: 103/14 Bang Khae Road, Bang Khae, Bangkok, 10160, Thailand
Description: Nestled in a vintage townhouse, this popular street food joint serves up savory fish ball noodle soup. Expect fresh, made-to-order meals that might require a wait due to the frequent bustle. However, the wait pays off with homemade seafood like fish balls, fish dumplings, and fish cakes, all enhancing the soup's umami taste.

Name: Samut
Address: 14/119 Mu 1, Rawai, Mueang Phuket, Phuket, 83100, Thailand
Description: Samut (or ocean) is set in a traditional Thai-Chinese building decorated in an Oriental style, with dark teak wood. Previously the lobby of the adjacent hotel, it’s now a gastronomic destination. The set menu, with more than 10 dishes, tours the island’s coastline, offering seafood caught by local fishermen. The chef respects the traditions of the island, selecting flavours and fruits inspired by local creativity, including a reinterpretation of Phuket dim sum.

Name: J'AIME by Jean-Michel Lorain
Address: 2F, U Sathorn Hotel, 105/1 Soi Ngam Du Phli, Thung Maha Mek, Sathon, Bangkok, 10120, Thailand
Description: As you enter this restaurant, your world becomes a little topsy-turvy, with a grand piano suspended from the ceiling and upside-down chandeliers. Protégés of the eponymous Jean-Michel Lorain craft thoughtfully designed set menus that use Thai ingredients while staying true to French roots. The dishes are a masterful fusion of local flavours and French techniques, with each plate narrating the chef’s culinary artistry.

Name: Royal Osha
Address: 99 Wireless Road, Lumphini, Pathum Wan, Bangkok, 10330, Thailand
Description: A majestic twist on its sister restaurant in San Francisco, Royal Osha aims to engage the senses with enticing flavours, aromas, textures, sights and sounds. The setting is a sleek, modern dining room decorated with Thai art. Start with a cocktail inspired by Ramakien characters, before enjoying dishes like the excellent tom yum kung mae nam (spicy, sour soup with river prawns infused with Thai herbs) and the (seasonal) chilled rice served with accompaniments.

Name: Sushi Masato
Address: 3/22 Soi Sukhumvit 31, Khlong Tan Nuea, Vadhana, Bangkok, 10110, Thailand
Description: The Japanese seas provide a rich bounty of seasonal delights: spring offers an abundance of fresh shellfish, while winter brings the indulgence of rich, fatty fish. At Sushi Masato, guests enjoy this premium seasonal produce flown in daily from Tokyo's renowned Toyosu Market. The experience is elevated by Chef Masato's exceptional techniques, perfected over his years in Japan and New York. You may request to be served by Chef Masato when making a reservation.

Name: 100 Mahaseth
Address: 100 Mahaseth Road, Si Phraya, Bang Rak, Bangkok, 10500, Thailand
Description: This nose-to-tail inspired offal restaurant serves elevated Isan fare made from quality locally sourced ingredients. The chef takes great care to balance the flavours and present attractive plates. The Isan complementary set includes somtam, crispy pork skin with Thai chimichurri and chaeo sauce. The hot and sour soup with baby pork ribs and chamuang leaves has lovely acidity with a hint of shrimp paste. Check the blackboard for Thai aged steak specials.

Name: Mana
Address: 420 Mu 21, Sri Chan Road, Nai Mueang, Mueang Khon Kaen, Khon Kaen, 40000, Thailand
Description: After working for years at Thai-Chinese restaurants in Bangkok, chef-owner Mana returned home to open his own outlet. He’s now been serving flavoursome Thai-Chinese-style seafood dishes that are easy on the pocketbook for over a decade. Inside his restaurant’s one-storey white building are two dining areas, one with AC and another open-air one. The oyster omelette and crispy salad with fish maw, shrimp and cashews are recommended.

Name: Baan Suan Mae Rim
Address: 261 Mu 2, Chiang Mai-Fang Road, San Pong, Mae Rim, Chiang Mai, 50180, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Although this restaurant is outside the city centre, it’s worth the drive for its Thai cuisine, and especially its northern dishes, served in a beautiful, natural setting. Open for more than a decade, the place consists of several northern Thai-style pavilions, which all face a pond – and you can also dine in the open air. Either way, there are tranquil views of the trees, pond, and rice fields. Deep-fried snakehead fish with hot and spicy sauce is recommended.

Name: Supanniga Eating Room (Phra Nakhon)
Address: 392/25-26 Maha Rat Road, Phra Borom Maha Ratchawang, Phra Nakhon, Bangkok, 10200, Thailand
Description: The homestyle Thai food at this casual restaurant comes with postcard-worthy views of the Chao Phraya River and iconic Wat Arun. Whether you’re sharing lunch with friends after touring the nearby Grand Palace or enjoying a romantic meal at sunset, try a flavoursome signature dish. The recipes come from the owner’s grandmother; standouts include fried Chinese cabbage and braised pork belly with herbs and cowa leaves.

Name: Sornthong
Address: 2829-31 Rama 4 Road, Khlong Toei, Bangkok, 10110, Thailand
Description: For quality seafood that won’t burn a hole in your pocket, look no further than Sornthong. Easily identified by the crowds dining beneath a large yellow sign in Thai and Chinese, this family-run shop has done a booming trade in prime fresh fish for more than 20 years. Ingredients are taken from tanks outside the restaurant, then cooked under the watchful eye of Mr. Chai – fried oysters with creamy eggs and a sweet-sour-spicy chilli sauce are a must-try. Away from the sea, keep an eye out for the well-marinated grilled pork satay.

Name: Hong Khao Tom Pla
Address: 5 Kra Road, Talat Yai, Mueang Phuket, Phuket, 83000, Thailand
Description: There is always a queue in front of this small shop. The mainstay on the menu is seafood. Dishes are carefully prepared by the owner, and the fresh prawns are a must. Check the whiteboard for the daily catch.

Name: Aeeen
Address: 4/13 Mu 5, Suthep Road, Suthep, Mueang Chiang Mai, Chiang Mai, 50200, Thailand
Description: Aeeen goes the sound of Ken’s unique laughter, according to wife Yuki. Under the concept of Neo Shojin Ryori, the Japanese couple craft their plant-based menu using seasonal ingredients. The dining areas span two floors of a cute wooden house that feels like rural Japan. Lines of jars contain the fermented ingredients they use in the food. We recommend the perfectly judged soymilk udon noodles and refreshing mango with ginger and honey drink.

Name: Yung Khao
Address: 111 Mu 4, Thanaratch Road, Nong Nam Daeng, Pak Chong, Nakhon Ratchasima, 30130, Thailand
Description: Originally from Bangkok, they relocated to Pak Chong 10 years ago. The building is made from wood and bamboo, like many rural rice granaries (yung khao). On offer is southern-Thai dishes, using ingredients from the south as well as their own curry paste, to cook grandmother’s recipes. The deep-fried sand fish is a great starter and the yellow curry seabass emits a gloriously pungent turmeric aroma. Diners on the outdoor terrace enjoy a view of the mountains.

Name: Methavalai Sorndaeng
Address: 78/2 Ratchadamnoen Klang Road, Bowon Niwet, Phra Nakhon, Bangkok, 10200, Thailand
Description: One of the city’s original Thai fine dining restaurants, they’ve maintained a loyal customer base for 60+ years, using the same timeless recipes and cooking techniques. The refined dishes are complex, delivering blasts of flavour. Highlights are crispy rice noodles in sweet and sour sauce, spicy lemongrass salad, and crab meat and acacia red curry. The curry pastes are made from scratch and fishcakes from featherback fish. Small parties should book the private room.

Name: Gen (Vadhana)
Address: Vibes Ekkamai,  267/31 Soi Sukhumvit 63, Khlong Tan Nuea, Vadhana, Bangkok, 10110, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Counter dining,Notable sake list
Description: This trendy spot for yakitori and drinks has a slight vintage feel not dissimilar to a Japanese whisky bar. Smartly dressed staff offer traditional Japanese service, while the menu includes ingredients flown in from Japan – including the prized Hitachiwagyu beef. A variety of dishes are available, not just yakitori, including sashimi, rice and noodles. If you’re lucky, you’ll get to try one of their multiple Japanese eel dishes.

Name: Khao Horm
Address: 34/36 Mu 4, Bo Phut, Ko Samui, 84320, Thailand
Description: Just 5 minutes from the airport, Khao Horm is a great spot to get your last-minute fill of delicious Southern Thai and local recipes before flying home. The family recipes have been passed down from generation to generation for over a century. We recommend the stir-fried minced pork whose yellow curry paste features a gutsy mix of spices. The main dining room is set in a large open-air pavilion. They also offer AC indoor dining and plenty of parking too.

Name: See Na Nuan Café
Address: 164/160 Mu 14, Nai Mueang, Mueang Khon Kaen, Khon Kaen, 40000, Thailand
Description: This 500-seat crowd pleaser close to Khon Kaen University serves flavoursome central Thai fare and Isan dishes in an industrial-style house with a huge outdoor dining area. Inside is all brick and black steel; outside, the steel continues in a birdcage-like dining area next to more seating centred around a lawn. Seafood tanks attest to the food’s freshness; the grilled snakehead fish served with spicy dip is recommended. Chill live music features nightly.

Name: Jum Khao
Address: 104/4 Thetsaban 26 Road, Pak Chong, Nakhon Ratchasima, 30130, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Cash only,Garden or park,Great view
Description: Modestly designed, Jum Khao embraces local influences and serves Isan fare with a little flair. There are a few à la carte and seasonal dishes but a wide variety of som tum options, popular comfort food like crispy grilled chicken wings, golden-brown garlic chips and Korat-style stir-fried rice noodles. The tricolour sticky rice combines butterfly pea purple, turmeric yellow and the natural white and is served with three dips and raw vegetables in a cute bamboo basket.

Name: Maze
Address: 114/3 Set Siri Road, Sam Sen Nai, Phaya Thai, Bangkok, 10400, Thailand
Description: Opened in 2020 by chef May Thongthong, this fine dining restaurant serves two set menus: Northern Thai Creations and Seasonal Creative. The first explores Chef May’s Lanna heritage, while the second plays with European techniques and flavours. The contemporary décor and lighting set the stage for the well-presented dishes. The main dining room includes an open-bar kitchen and counter seating. Above it, a private room seats 10.

Name: Savelberg
Address: 136/1 Soi Yen Akat 2, Chong Nonsi, Yan Nawa, Bangkok, 10120, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Wheelchair access
Description: Food and mood pair well at Dutch chef-owner Henk Savelberg’s eponymous restaurant, now in a contemporary house in Chong Nonsi. The sparkling dining room features an open kitchen, a refined wine cellar and garden views, with private group dining available. The menu boasts adventurous, modern, colourful French dishes with a classical base, made from fine international ingredients. Rounding out the experience is the professional service. Booking is essential.

Name: Anuwat
Address: 201 Mu 4, Phet Kasem Road, Thai Mueang, Phang-Nga, 82120, Thailand
Description: There may be a big sign out front, but it’s the aromatic pork that’s been luring in the locals for more than 40 years. The grilled pork, BBQ pork and crispy pork belly are well marinated and grilled till succulent. Try any or all — plus steamed chicken — on a single plate served with rice.

Name: Lertrod
Address: 17/7 Nai Yang Road, Sakhu, Thalang, Phuket, 83110, Thailand
Description: Across from the airport, this bright air-conditioned restaurant flies under the radar but lands simple, satisfying central and southern Thai fare. The skilled chef sources quality ingredients from local farmers and fishermen. The deep-fried seabass with fish sauce never disappoints. For the spicy southern-Thai sour curry, choose from pickled bamboo, coconut shoots or pineapple. The photo-filled menu, written in Thai, English and Chinese, makes it easy for everyone.

Name: Kruvit Raft (Ban Laem Hin)
Address: 98/7  Ko Maphrao, Mu 6, Ko Kaeo, Mueang Phuket, Phuket, 83000, Thailand
Description: To reach this floating restaurant near Ko Maphrao, take a 5-min boat ride across sparkling waters reflecting the sunshine. Onboard, panoramic views, a gentle breeze and uber-fresh seafood await. The distance from sea to plate couldn’t be shorter. Start with a freshly picked coconut before tucking into delicious southern and central Thai seafood. The grouper soup with Chinese soybean paste and stir-fried black tiger prawns with salt and chilli are highlights.

Name: Rongros
Address: 392/16 Maha Rat Road, Phra Borom Maha Ratchawang, Phra Nakhon, Bangkok, 10200, Thailand
Description: Meaning ‘House of Flavours,’ Rongros preserves the taste of traditional Thai cuisine on the banks of the Chao Phraya River with a stunning view of Wat Arun. Highlights include the green curry with rib eye beef served with roti and the tangy glass noodle salad. The vintage décor, including the chandeliers, painted Chinese panels, and wooden furniture only add to the experience. Book a table on the terrace for dinner to take in the view at sunset. Keep in mind that this restaurant is a favorite spot for tourists, so it's a good idea to make a reservation in advance to secure your place.

Name: Lam Phu 2
Address: 23/1 Mu 3, Pak Nam Road, Bang Kung, Mueang Surat Thani, Surat Thani, 84000, Thailand
Description: Watch the fishing boats on Tapi River while enjoying a bright and airy setting and local seafood cooked southern style. The oyster omelette is gorgeous with a crispy egg base, spot-on seasoning and fresh local oysters; it goes well with steamed rice. The tender stir-fried squid with salted eggs is packed with flavour and flanked by an impressively creamy sauce. With over 100 seats, there is ample room for large groups to enjoy the scenic view.

Name: Villa Frantzén
Address: 7 Soi Yen Akat 3, Chong Nonsi, Yan Nawa, Bangkok, 10120, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: A Nordic god on the fine-dining scene, Chef Frantzén now has an outpost in Bangkok. The swanky villa’s interior is inspired by modern Nordic aesthetics; with an open kitchen, granite floors and huge windows framing lush greens and exotic plants. His modern Nordic style borrows from Asian influences. With eccentric visual detail, every dish delivers a subtle complexity that accentuates the natural flavours of the ingredients. Advanced bookings are essential.

Name: Heng Khao Moo Daeng
Address: 428/1 Namueang Road, Talat, Mueang Surat Thani, Surat Thani, 84000, Thailand
Description: This simple eatery is always bustling at lunchtime with queues for both dine-in and takeout. The owner's inviting and chatty demeanour sets the scene. His signature barbeque pork comes with crispy pork and sweet sausage inside and a large portion only costs 40 baht.

Name: Sripol Seafood House
Address: 61/11, 12 Rama 9 Road Soi 7, Huai Khwang, Bangkok, 10310, Thailand
Description: For an authentic Thai seafood experience, look no further than this restaurant named after the owner's fishing boat, which also catches most of the produce. Expect premium seafood cooking in the heart of Bangkok and hearty portions suitable for 4 or more people. The signature fried rice with salty fish is particularly noteworthy. We recommend any of the generously served dishes and also calling 2 days in advance to book a table and check on menu options.

Name: The Redbox
Address: 6 Soi Jannsaap, Huai Kaeo Road, Chang Phueak, Mueang Chiang Mai, Chiang Mai, 50300, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: With business acumen and cooking techniques gleaned from their travels, Chef Dan and partner Pimmada offer modern Thai with Malaysian and Brunei influences. They import select ingredients like salted eggs from Chaiya, and Gula Melaka (Malaysian palm sugar) to create treats like Siam Ruby, a signature dessert. We recommend the signature creation cocktail with a complexity of flavours before your unforgettable meal. Seating is limited so bookings are essential.

Name: La Gaetana
Address: 352 Phuket Road, Talat Yai, Mueang Phuket, Phuket, 83000, Thailand
Description: It may be tiny, with 6 tables, but La Gaetana, decorated like an Italian house in warm colours, provides a warm welcome and is big on charm. They import most ingredients from Italy and make the sourdough, pasta, gelato and limoncello in-house. Chef Gianni cooks the fettucine with tomato sauce and crab meat using his family recipe from Campania. The menu is largely influenced by such southern classics. As Gianni takes a summer holiday each year, call ahead first.

Name: Eat Me
Address: 1/6 Soi Phiphat 2, Si Lom, Bang Rak, Bangkok, 10500, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Counter dining,Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: Though hidden in a side soi, Eat Me is hardly a secret. Since 1998, it has been known for carefully cooked dishes that join global influences with local flavours. The best meals here start with Thai food-inspired cocktails at the ground floor bar. They continue at the minimalist second-storey dining room or leafy balcony with the star of the menu—mixed clams served with nam, or fermented Thai sausage, and coriander lime broth—and one of the unmissable desserts.

Name: The Smokaccia Laboratory
Address: 116/4 Mu 3, Srisoonthorn Road, Choeng Thale, Thalang, Phuket, 83110, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus
Description: Chef Luca Mascolo has invented a complex crispy sourdough which he has named ‘Smokaccia’, which is served with a variety of inventive fillings. Highlights include slow-cooked Australian Wagyu striploin, Surat Thani oysters and cheese from Nonthaburi. The high-ceilinged dining room features both tables and counter seats overlooking the open kitchen. Things step up a gear at dinner with a creative, 18-course tasting menu showcasing modern techniques. Vegan options are also available.

Name: Saigon Recipe
Address: Piman 49, B3 Building, 46/5 Soi Sukhumvit 49, Khlong Tan Nuea, Vadhana, Bangkok, 10110, Thailand
Description: With its canary-yellow walls, vintage posters and Indochinese décor, this place feels like a home in Saigon, if it was staffed by capable Vietnamese chefs. They carefully select ingredients, including rice wrappers and noodles from Vietnam, to create flavourful rice and noodle dishes, salads and rolls the owner might serve family and friends. Weekday lunches offer set menus that please even the time-pressed. Coffee fans should try the authentic Vietnamese brew.

Name: Saffron
Address: Banyan Tree Samui, 99/9 Mu 4, Maret, Ko Samui, 84310, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Wheelchair access
Description: Elegantly appointed with floor-to-ceiling windows, contemporary lighting and dark wooden furnishings, Saffron also offers alfresco dining with a fantastic view. You can choose from à la carte and tasting menus. The roast duck red curry is paired with a thick sweet and spicy sauce, a fresh lychee and pineapple compote and roasted skin that excite the tastebuds. The fried softshell crab salad with lychee and passionfruit is also a must.

Name: Blackitch
Address: 27/1 Nimmanahaeminda Soi 7 Road, Suthep, Mueang Chiang Mai, Chiang Mai, 50200, Thailand
Description: Hidden in the city centre in plain sight, this second floor 16-seater is decorated with stone, wood and local blue fabrics in a minimalist style. The creative chef, Phanuphol Bulsuwan, honed his skills under his restaurateur grandmother. He constantly adapts his 10-course meal using Thailand’s seasonal ingredients, uniting Thai, Japanese and Chinese influences. He also ferments kitchen scraps to season his dishes and brews beers and sake for food pairing.

Name: Krua Supanniga by Khunyai Somsie
Address: Supanniga Home, 130/9 Phothisan Road, Phra Lap, Mueang Khon Kaen, Khon Kaen, 40000, Thailand
Description: Named after the Supanniga flower, this cute shop offers delightful dishes blending flavours from the eastern seaboard and Isan cuisine. Grandma's recipes inspire the food here. Don't miss the must-order chamuang pork—a juicy stewed pork infused with Chamuang leaf's slightly sour flavour. The restaurant provides indoor and outdoor seating, including shaded tables in the tree house.

Name: Pratunam Baan Ko Noodles
Address: 22 Mu 5, Ban Ko, Bang Sai, Phra Nakhon Si Ayutthaya, 13190, Thailand
Description: Set beside a peaceful canal, the crowds flock here for their speciality: beef noodles. The noodles come with offal, beef balls, spare ribs and tender beef slices. The soup is also superb, with a meaty aroma. It’s so popular, the chef prepares 25-30 kg of fresh offal every day.

Name: Lahnyai
Address: 31 Soi Suan Phlu 2, Thung Maha Mek, Sathon, Bangkok, 10120, Thailand
Description: Initially conceived as a tribute to the owner's grandmother, Lahnyai showcases modern interpretations of royal Thai cuisine sourced from the cremation cookbooks of princesses from 1987 to 1992. The refined dining room delivers an intimate ambiance with velvet walls and Jacquard-covered furniture. Infusing a contemporary twist into historical recipes, dishes satisfy with tried-and-tested flavours, like a great massaman curry that strikes a fine balance between spice and sweetness.

Name: Jay Jew Talew Bin
Address: 117/17 Mu 2, Soi Bangsai 6, Bang Sai, Mueang Chonburi, Chon Buri, 20000, Thailand
Description: This local favourite offers the freshest seafood with bold Thai flavours, cooked home-style. The restaurant is simple, without air conditioning. The menu primarily focuses on seafood options, and the chef excels at deep-fried and stir-fried dishes. The rice dishes and daily catch are listed on the blackboard at the front of the shop. Bookings are only taken for groups of 10 or more. Expect to wait for a table on weekends.

Name: Chom Tawan
Address: 79 Mu 3, Assadang Road, Tha Thewawong, Ko Sichang, Chon Buri, 20120, Thailand
Description: Despite its rustic-looking exterior, Chom Tawan has a certain charm, and prices are reasonable, especially considering the freshness and quality of the seafood. The delicious stir-fried squid with minced pork filling and garlic is tempting, but also ask about the special of the day.

Name: Preaw Pak
Address: 6/6 Mu 4, Ammarit, Phak Hai, Phra Nakhon Si Ayutthaya, 13120, Thailand
Description: Preaw Pak specialises in freshwater fish, with a menu focused on fresh catches and local seasonal produce. From the riverside location you can see fishermen at work. The chef's skill is evident in his perfectly cooked dishes, which showcase traditional local flavours. Highlights include deep-fried river prawns with stir-fried garlic and chilli, and fresh snakehead fish in clear tom yum soup made with dry and fresh chilli. The level of spice can be adjusted to taste.

Name: Tambu
Address: Avista Hideaway Phuket Patong - MGallery, 39/9 Muen-Ngern Road, Pa Tong Beach, Pa Tong, Kathu, Phuket, 83150, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Brunch,Car park,Great view,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus
Description: Inspiration from the opulent Mughal palaces makes its presence felt in this alluring restaurant, where the chef presents modern Indian cooking that embraces the times. He respects the diversity and tradition of Indian cuisine, crafting dishes that showcase his skills and experience. The aromatic plates are packed with spices and enhanced by a smoky flavour, bringing complexity and creative combinations to the palate.

Name: Wansuk
Address: 129/10 Mu 1, Soi Boonpleum, Pattaya, Nong Preu, Bang Lamung, Chon Buri, 20150, Thailand
Description: In a vintage decor featuring wooden accents, music from the 1980s and 1990s sets the mood. At this locally renowned Thai restaurant, the chef-owner's uniquely creative menu boasts intensely flavoured, unapologetically spicy dishes – though milder versions are available upon request. Seafood is the star, with fresh, expertly cooked offerings served at perfect temperatures. Instead of regular rice, we suggest ordering the signature fried rice with salt.

Name: Radna Suanmak
Address: 282 Phoklang Road, Nai Mueang, Mueang Nakhon Ratchasima, Nakhon Ratchasima, 30000, Thailand
Description: In over 30 years serving the community, this humble noodle spot has won local awards and built up a dedicated following. Expect a wait for their lovingly prepared dishes, which include deep-fried fish with thick noodles, and flavoursome crispy noodle stir-fry with holy basil.

Name: Khao Soi Lung Prakit Kad Kom
Address: 53 Suriyawong 5 Road, Hai Ya, Mueang Chiang Mai, Chiang Mai, 50100, Thailand
Description: This place has been serving Northern Thai-style curry noodle soup for over 40 years. Their signature dish is Khao Soi with beef, which features a savoury curry broth and soft, eggy noodles. Don’t forget to squeeze the lemon over your noodles and pair them with side dishes to enhance the flavours.

Name: Mae Khlong Hua Pla Mo Fai
Address: 198 Phran Nok-Phutthamonthon Sai 4 Road, Bang Phrom, Taling Chan, Bangkok, 10170, Thailand
Description: Simple in its design with a white pavilion and modest dining tables, the restaurant has a small garden with some outdoor seating. The owners are hands-on, preparing every dish with care. The stir-fried crab has a naturally sweet meat and wok-fried aroma, and is served with glass noodles, spicy chilli and crunchy mimosa. The large butterfly-cut river fish is nicely char-grilled. The grilled river prawns, meanwhile, are clearly the people’s favourite.

Name: Yu Ting Yuan
Address: LF, Four Seasons Hotel Bangkok at Chao Phraya River, 300/1 Charoen Krung Road, Yan Nawa, Sathon, Bangkok, 10120, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Interesting wine list,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: There is a luxurious feel to this lavish Cantonese restaurant that is a gorgeously designed space inside the equally stylish Four Seasons hotel. Expansive windows look out onto a reflective pool which comes to life at night with the illumination of contemporary artworks. The Cantonese chef brings a modern and creative approach to the cooking, as well as a Thai twist in places. The extensive menus include tasting and à la carte options, plus a dim sum selection at lunch.

Name: Ojo
Address: 76F, The Standard Bangkok Mahanakhon, 114 Narathiwas Road, Si Lom, Bang Rak, Bangkok, 10500, Thailand
Description: Offering breathtaking views over the Bangkok cityscape, Ojo has the honour of being Thailand’s highest restaurant. Glamorous pink and gold décor adds to the appeal of a truly special location in which to dine, while the authentic Mexican cooking means this restaurant is far more than just its setting. The menu of attractive dishes includes tender cochinillo and a selection of raw seafood. Ask for a table by the window or on the terrace to make the most of the view.

Name: Nikaku
Address: GF, W Bangkok, 106 North Sathorn Road, Si Lom, Bang Rak, Bangkok, 10500, Thailand
Description: This Japanese restaurant originating from Kitakyushu, specialises in authentic Edo-mae sushi. Offering an omakase menu, it serves only 12 diners at a counter, showcasing the chef's skills. Ingredients are sourced daily from Japan, ensuring superb quality fish and shellfish, such as Hokkaido's delicate uni. The chef provides detailed seafood explanations, and diners can opt for special tea pairings.

Name: Keller
Address: 1749 Chan Kao Road, Chong Nonsi, Yan Nawa, Bangkok, 10120, Thailand
Description: The restaurant offers an intimate and engaging dining experience. The interior features a beautiful light beige colour palette, complemented by ample natural light. Boasting bold flavours with a strong Asian influence, the food is a testament to the chef's culinary prowess. Each bite is a harmonious blend of tradition and innovation, and the chef's boundless creativity is expressed in a tasting menu that changes every month.

Name: Phensiri
Address: 80/30 Mu 3, Suan Uthit Road, Bo Phut, Ko Samui, 84320, Thailand
Description: Phensiri is a must-visit for Thai and Southern Thai cuisine. Using high-quality local ingredients, the chef-owner ensures each dish is well-balanced and flavourful. A no-fuss approach delivers authentic flavours, with the spice level adjustable to your liking. The welcoming atmosphere is enhanced by Thai-style décor, and the attentive staff, fluent in English, make things easy for tourists. Popular with both locals and visitors, it is especially busy at lunchtime and dinner.

Name: Larb Duang Dee Mee Sook
Address: 74 Soi Ban Huai Sai, Mu 4, Suthep, Mueang Chiang Mai, Chiang Mai, 50200, Thailand
Description: With its simple, rustic look, this quaint eatery specialises in northern larb dishes, paired with a local chaeo dipping sauce with the aroma of toasted sticky rice. The spicy, sour and fragrant beef soup is a must.

Name: Somtum Je Phai
Address: 321/26 Mu 12, Jomtien Beach Road, Pattaya, Nong Prue, Bang Lamung, Chon Buri, 20260, Thailand
Description: This authentic Isan eatery under a PVC tent grills chicken, meat, and pork over charcoal with traditional flair. The owner's passion is palpable as she communicates animatedly with her team. The meat is well-executed and retains its juiciness.

Name: Rabiang Talay
Address: 887 Soi Thetsaban Bang Pu 104, Thai Ban, Mueang Samut Prakan, Samut Prakan, 10280, Thailand
Description: Opened in 1992, this restaurant serves flavourful seafood in a Lanna-style pavilion with relaxing views of mangroves and the sea, especially at sunset. There are three dining areas: one with AC, one open-air under high ceilings and hanging Northern Thai lamps, and one on the terrace. The food is prepared in an open kitchen and made with fresh ingredients, including some from onsite seafood tanks; the signature stir-fried crab with salted egg is recommended.

Name: Som Tum Jae Kai (Asavamit Road)
Address: 230/28 Asavamit Road, Mak Khaeng, Mueang Udon Thani, Udon Thani, 41000, Thailand
Description: This family-operated lunch spot has been a popular haunt for half a century. The dishes get their distinctive flavour from their home-made fermented fish sauce. This tasty addition elevates favourites such as mixed som tum with pork crackling and fermented sausage.

Name: Kinlum Kindee
Address: 172 Mu 3, Mueang Len, San Sai, Chiang Mai, 50210, Thailand
Description: Truth in advertising may be rare, but Kin Lum Kin Dee, which means “to eat delicious food and eat well” in Lanna, allows Northern Thai food lovers to do just that. Formerly downtown, the restaurant is now in a quiet pavilion in San Sai surrounded by gardens, trees, and fields. Dishes are marked by authentic flavours and fresh ingredients, with some from the garden. Grilled field crab innards with egg yolks and northern Thai herb soup with pork are must-tries.

Name: Clara
Address: 69 Soi Prasat Suk, Chong Nonsi, Yan Nawa, Bangkok, 10120, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: Popular among both Thai and foreign foodies and housed in a Bauhaus-style villa surrounded by sculpture-filled gardens, Clara is an elegant Italian fine-dining restaurant from a seasoned Italian chef and his wife. The villa’s two-floor interior has a warm minimalist vibe. The set menu balances flavours and complex textures which are matched by the fine service. Pair with wine for a complete experience.

Name: Favola
Address: 2F, Chiang Mai Marriott Hotel, 108 Chang Khlan Road, Chang Moi, Mueang Chiang Mai, Chiang Mai, 50100, Thailand
Description: At Favola, Chiang Mai Marriott Hotel presents authentic Italian cuisine, featuring homemade pasta and ravioli crafted by the Italian head chef, all served in a dining room that blends contemporary style with a classic Italian restaurant ambience. Among the dishes, the pizzas stand out. Feel free to order half or smaller sizes, perfect for when you’re in the mood to try multiple dishes. The excellent wine selection further enhances the experience.

Name: Aheesah Roddee
Address: 103-105 Tani Road, Talat Yot, Phra Nakhon, Bangkok, 10200, Thailand
Description: Helmed by the son of Indonesian migrants, it has been serving aromatic Indonesian-inspired fare since 1975. The menu features tasty dishes such as chicken or beef biryani and satay. We recommend pairing the beautifully spiced chicken biryani with the hot and sour beef soup.

Name: Gu Cherng
Address: 2F, Krungsri River Hotel, 27/2 Mu 11, Rochana Road, Kamang, Phra Nakhon Si Ayutthaya, Phra Nakhon Si Ayutthaya, 13000, Thailand
Description: Gu cherng refers to the country’s former capital and the dining room, renovated in 2021, mixes elegant modern Chinese style with flashes of the traditional. Popular dishes include a variety of tasty dim-sum. The steamed prawn dumplings with seaweed and steamed rice noodles stuffed with deep-fried prawns use quality ingredients with delicately balanced flavours. The signature Peking duck pancakes use choice cuts of meat, thinly sliced, crispy and with no fat.

Name: Jay Noi Kratoke
Address: 115 Pibool La-lad Road, Nong Phai Lom, Mueang Nakhon Ratchasima, Nakhon Ratchasima, 30000, Thailand
Description: This three-storey house with simple décor is family run and in its second generation. Jay Noi's house special of hao-dong is a popular local treat using sliced pork and spicy Isan sauce, chilli and roasted rice. The four pad mee Korat is also recommended. Its sticky rice noodles are fresh and go really well with the sweet and sour sauce, fresh bean sprouts and chives. You can order the homemade curry puff for take away, with a variety of optional sides.

Name: Food For You
Address: 25 Mu 3, San Phi Suea, Mueang Chiang Mai, Chiang Mai, 50300, Thailand
Description: Food For You has been creating flavoursome Thai food using fresh seasonal ingredients from local farms for over 20 years. Meals here are served chef’s table style, from a menu that changes according to the season and customer requests. The crab meat salad with mixed fruit is highly recommended and comes with a dressing that’s the perfect balance of sweet, sour, and salty. As seating is limited, reservations are essential.

Name: Baan Ton Sai
Address: 189/49 Mu 8, Pratu Chai, Phra Nakhon Si Ayutthaya, Phra Nakhon Si Ayutthaya, 13000, Thailand
Description: The restaurant's vibrant colours stand out from afar. In the backyard, a banyan tree provides pleasant shade. The menu features straightforward and unpretentious seafood, pork and chicken dishes. Expect large servings of seafood that make the mouth water at wallet-friendly prices. We recommend trying their rat na noodles. Closing times may vary, so it's best to arrive early.

Name: Grand Chaopraya
Address: 42/1 Ban Run, Phra Nakhon Si Ayutthaya, Phra Nakhon Si Ayutthaya, 13000, Thailand
Description: Opened in 2009, this riverside restaurant serves Thai cuisine made with local ingredients, including fish sourced from the river. The dining room features high ceilings, spiral staircases and floor-to-ceiling windows, while the terrace offers scenic views and nightly live music. The menu is packed with recipes from the owner’s mother. Her grilled river prawns and grilled fish and shrimp in pineapple curry are a must. Book ahead for an outdoor table at dinner.

Name: Kor Chun Huad
Address: 864 Soi Somdet Phrachao Taksin 34, Bukkhalo, Thon Buri, Bangkok, 10600, Thailand
Description: For more than five decades, Koa Chun Huad has been attracting throngs of locals. Named after the chef-owner who has worked in many a kitchen in Chinatown, it serves classic Thai-Chinese dishes at appealingly low prices. The highlights are the boiled pork slices, perfectly complemented by a soybean sauce, and the intense stewed pork with sweet-salty five spice gravy.

Name: Neon Boat Noodles
Address: 395/7 Pattaya, Nong Prue, Bang Lamung, Chon Buri, 20150, Thailand
Description: Traditional boat noodles are served here with various toppings in a bold and savoury soup. We also recommend the spicy boiled pork and pork condiments, which have an intensely flavoured sauce and the aroma of fried garlic.

Name: Grok
Address: 14 Soi Somkid, Lumphini, Pathum Wan, Bangkok, 10330, Thailand
Description: The interior, decorated in elegant dark tones with wood-clad walls, creates a nostalgic ambiance. The menu offers a modern take on Ratchaburi cuisine, where the intense flavours and aromas of each dish pair well with Thai herbs. The duck confit with red curry and the stir-fried minced chicken thigh with Thai herbs and five peppercorns are recommended.

Name: Ōre
Address: 11/31 Sathu Pradit Road, Chong Nonsi, Yan Nawa, Bangkok, 10120, Thailand
