Description: With a minimalist design of wood, fabric and natural tones, Ōre promises an intimate culinary journey centred on Thai ingredients with select imports. The chef extols the flavour-enhancing properties of the mineral water that he gets shipped in from a spring near Sai Yok Waterfall to use in his cooking. His creative dishes highlight natural flavours and aromas that deepen throughout the meal, making for an unforgettable dining experience.

Name: Krua Sa Ros Jad
Address: 112/1 Soi Vibhavadi 44, Vibhavadi Rangsit Road, Lat Yao, Chatuchak, Bangkok, 10900, Thailand
Description: "Krua Sa Ros Jad" combines the owner's mother's name and a Thai phrase meaning "intense flavour" – an apt description of the boldly seasoned food made with fresh ingredients. Try the deep-fried fish in Choo Chee sauce, the robust, well-spiced flavour of which pairs well with the hot Tom Yum chicken soup with young tamarind leaves. The restaurant boasts a unique collection of Buddha statues and antique European ceramics, as the owner is an avid collector.

Name: Cadence by Dan Bark
Address: 225 Soi Pridi Banomyong 25, Khlong Tan, Khlong Toei, Bangkok, 10110, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Valet parking
Description: Drawing on his Korean-American heritage and experience in some of Chicago's top restaurants, chef Dan Bark uses a clever array of components to craft progressive American cuisine. The elegant space sets the stage for an artful marriage of Western and Asian flavours. The restaurant's commitment to excellence goes beyond the food, with an impressive wine selection, astutely curated cocktail pairings and charming service from a smartly turned-out team.

Name: Terroir
Address: Acmen Complex, 13-15 Ekkamai Road, Khlong Tan Nuea, Vadhana, Bangkok, 10110, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Counter dining,Interesting wine list
Description: Chef Hao believes that the land, climate, and farmers are pivotal in produce quality. This belief echoes in his eatery sourcing 90% of ingredients from Northern Thailand, named meaning 'soil' in French. The restaurant delivers exceptional Franco-Japanese fusion, creatively blending two cuisines. Impressive flavour pairings, notably rich, smoky broths, shine consistently. An outstanding wine selection completes the splendid dining experience.

Name: O
Address: 252/21 Soi Wilai Sena, Prasoet Som Road, Sena, Phra Nakhon Si Ayutthaya, 13110, Thailand
Description: Set in Sena district's old market, this charming wooden house backs onto the River Noi. The relaxed atmosphere and delicious food make it a local favourite, with popular dishes like stir-fried river prawns with salt and pepper, and deep-fried fish with fish sauce.

Name: Aquila
Address: 226/4 Soi Surapol 1, Tha Sala, Mueang Chiang Mai, Chiang Mai, 50000, Thailand
Description: A 10-minute drive is all it takes to escape the city for heartening Italian food, surrounded by plenty of greenery. Despite its industrial design, it’s a casual setting with an expansive view of the garden. The pizza dough, gnocchi and fettucine are all homemade. The squid fettuccine has an enlivening ponzu dressing; and the baked snow fish in a buttery fish broth   beats all expectations with large, slow-cooked pieces that are meltingly soft in a sweet, homemade broth.

Name: Giglio Trattoria Fiorentina
Address: 149 Soi Sathon 12, Si Lom, Bang Rak, Bangkok, 10500, Thailand
Description: A love of tradition, simplicity and authentic flavours are the guiding principles behind this Tuscan-focused restaurant from the former chefs of Bottega di Luca and Appia. The result is their version of a quintessential trattoria, serving savoury dishes like the recommended home-made pici pasta with fresh black truffle slices and fresh cream and the dry-aged sharing steak. While there’s no on-site parking, valet parking is available; and booking is essential.

Name: Baan Watcharachai
Address: 9 Soi Ban Pom 27, Ban Pom, Phra Nakhon Si Ayutthaya, Phra Nakhon Si Ayutthaya, 13000, Thailand
Description: This family-owned restaurant offers central Thai cuisine by the side of the Chao Phraya River. Its name joins those of the family’s father, mother and son and means “house of light and victory”. Recipes have come from the owner’s grandmother, with dishes including sweet, salty and spicy fried snakehead fish with prik-king curry paste – a perfect example of the well-balanced cooking on offer. Guests can dine in the vintage house or outside on the deck or docked boat, both with views of Phra Chedi Sri Suriyothai.

Name: Phi Sao
Description: Delicious meals have been enjoyed at P’Saw for more than 40 years. Under a whitewashed pavilion-like structure, diners can enjoy the sea breeze, a view of the beach and southern-style dishes. The recipes, passed from the restaurant’s founder to her younger sister, offer something more personal and familial than their neighbouring restaurants. The baegu leaf salad with crispy shrimp and tom yum clear soup with young coconut deliver a delightful and flavourful experience.

Name: Ms.Maria & Mr.Singh
Address: 2F, 68 Soi Sukhumvit 31, Sukhumvit Road, Khlong Tan Nuea, Vadhana, Bangkok, 10110, Thailand
Description: Inspired by a Mexican-Indian love story, two cultures combine in both gastronomy and design at this sensorily striking restaurant. Vibrant oranges and blues make for a colourful setting. The food also makes a statement, playing with spices and textures to twist conventional styles. The well-judged fusion cooking includes dishes like pork vindaloo tacos and papdi chaat served on a mini taco shell. The service team provide fabulous hospitality with their high energy and friendly manner.

Name: Juumpo
Address: GF, Hotel Gahn Khao Lak, 1/96 Mu 5, Phet Kasem Road, Khuk Khak, Takua Pa, Phang-Nga, 82220, Thailand
Description: The cuisine of the local Baba (Chinese-Thai) people lives on here. Named in honour of the owner’s grandfather, a 'Juumpo' or chef on a Chinese boat more than 80 years ago and the source of many unique recipes, the open-air restaurant is fitted out with décor that reflects Chino-Portuguese design and culture. Baba-style coconut milk soup with shrimps and Thai herbs, chilli dip with shrimp, and fried fish with sweet and sour sauce are all recommended.

Name: Tonnam Riverview
Address: 26/7 Ban Len, Bang Pa-in, Phra Nakhon Si Ayutthaya, 13160, Thailand
Description: Known for the grilled river prawns it has served since 1991, this family-friendly restaurant on the Chao Phraya River has two dining areas: on a raft and boat, respectively. Either way, diners enjoy gentle breezes and scenic views with their meals. The culinary offerings, which have grown since the restaurant first opened, are skilfully cooked using fresh local ingredients. The speciality, grilled river prawns served with a flavourful spicy sauce, is a must-try.

Name: Loong Loy Pa Lan
Address: 1010 Phet Kasem Road, Huai Chorakhe, Mueang Nakhon Pathom, Nakhon Pathom, 73000, Thailand
Description: A passion for wild ingredients like wild boar, frogs, seafood, and even greens, along with a zeal for local flavours—intense, tangy, and spicy—shapes everything on the menu here. The stir-fried wild boar with chilies and the tom yam soup with snakehead fish are both recommended, as is the seafood cooked according to local recipes. The atmosphere is relaxed and homely, with air-conditioned dining rooms and outdoor seating available.

Name: Phra Nakhon
Address: Lower Lobby, Capella Bangkok, 300/2 Charoenkrung Road, Yan Nawa, Sathon, Bangkok, 10120, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Phra Nakhon offers Thai à la carte and tasting menus with seasonal changes in a charming, modern venue with stunning views of the river. Chef Kannika has extensive experience in luxury hotels in the region; her cooking here focuses on southern Thai dishes and she carefully selects the seafood for freshness and quality. The wok-fried roasted pork belly with crispy chilli and garlic seasoning, and crab and betel-leaf curry with vermicelli noodles stand out.

Name: L'Arôme by the Sea
Address: 247/5 Phrabaramee Road, Pa Tong, Kathu, Phuket, 83150, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Great view,Interesting wine list
Description: Start with a refreshing cocktail and enjoy the sea breeze on the rooftop before descending to the main dining room for stunning ocean views and the 'Vue sur la Mer' tasting menu. The seafood is of high quality, but the roasted pigeon with eggplant is also a standout. Meanwhile, the creamy foie gras and langoustine showcase the chef's culinary skills.

Name: Lab Mu Worachai
Address: 26/3 Posri Road, Mak Khaeng, Mueang Udon Thani, Udon Thani, 41000, Thailand
Description: Pork reigns supreme at this traditional Isan eatery, which may be renowned for its namesake Lab Mu – minced pork, skin and liver – but the flavourful Somtum Lao is another standout. Lunchtime can get hectic, but service is swift. The sharing sets of four to six dishes are perfect for groups.

Name: Acqua
Address: 324/15 Phra Barami Road, Pa Tong, Kathu, Phuket, 83150, Thailand
Description: Chef Alessandro Frau reinvents Italian fare with Sardinian artistry using premium imports. There’s a huge selection of à la carte, pastas and woodfired pizzas. Try the Tortelli Il Mare stuffed with Burrata cheese, glazed in black squid ink with Sardinian sea urchin and marine plankton. Or let the chef guide you through his tasting menu with signatures like lobster salad or raw Sicilian red prawns. Wine lovers will enjoy the fine vintage collection.

Name: Gorjan
Address: 161 Kra Road, Talat Yai, Mueang Phuket, Phuket, 83000, Thailand
Description: If you're near Gorjan Bridge, consider this simple family-run eatery. Every dish is rife with rich flavours, and many are created from their own recipes. The owner is poised to cook your food to order, which ensures a personalised dining experience.

Name: New York Steakhouse
Address: 2F, JW Marriott Hotel, 4 Soi Sukhumvit 2, Khlong Toei, Bangkok, 10110, Thailand
Description: Located inside the JW Marriott Hotel, this restaurant really lives up to its name. Dark wood furniture, oversized leather chairs and monochrome photos of US cities evoke images of a classic Manhattan steakhouse. A selection of cuts are available – including those from the US, Australia and Japan – and the knowledgeable service team are on hand to help guide your decision. Start with the Caesar salad, tossed tableside with a dressing made from scratch, then finish with the creative and equally theatrical ‘Bomb Alaska’ dessert.

Name: Ginza Sushi Ichi
Address: 3F, Gaysorn Village, 999 Phloen Chit Road, Lumphini, Pathum Wan, Bangkok, 10330, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Counter dining,Terrace,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: Spanning Tokyo, Jakarta, Singapore and Bangkok, Ginza Sushi Ichi imports the daily catch from Tokyo’s markets. This Bangkok branch uses the same rice-vinegar formula as the flagship restaurant, importing sushi rice from Yamagata. The quintessentially Japanese decor with neutral pine walls hosts a genial atmosphere. Ten seats circle the marble counter for an omakase experience focusing on nigiri. Private rooms are available and, of course, there’s a good range of sake.

Name: Somchai Go Tae (Bang Len)
Address: 18/13 Mu 1, Bang Phasi, Bang Len, Nakhon Pathom, 73130, Thailand
Description: Go Tae, the owner of this Thai-Chinese restaurant, got his start almost 80 years ago selling stewed duck noodle soup on a boat, before heading to dry land to open this place. Inside the three-storey building (topped with a giant rooftop duck statue), the simple dining room has a roasting and stewing station. The menu features old-school Thai-Chinese fare, including the recommended stewed duck and live river prawn cooked to your preference.

Name: O Cha Rot
Address: 72/1 Yaowarat Road, Talat Nuea, Mueang Phuket, Phuket, 83000, Thailand
Description: In Old Phuket Town, a red sign sits above the white façade; its Thai name in gold lettering declares: Delicious. The plump beef balls are packed with flavour; beef slices tender; bone broth fragrant; and the soft noodles are perfectly cooked. Arrive early for lunch before it runs out.

Name: Heh
Address: 158 Yaowarat Road, Talat Yai, Mueang Phuket, Phuket, 83000, Thailand
Description: ‘Heh’ is an expression of curiosity, according to the chef-owner who leads a youthful and creative kitchen. The aim is to bring Melbourne to the Andaman, combining quality ingredients from the Andaman Sea with Australian imports. The chef injects excitement into the unique menu without ever overcomplicating it. The charred broccoli with anchovy-miso sauce and crispy fish scales, and succulent charcoal-grilled Australian Wagyu short ribs are recommended.

Name: Song 24 Nor
Address: Nikorn Samran Road, Nai Mueang, Mueang Khon Kaen, Khon Kaen, 40000, Thailand
Description: The menu at this boiled rice spot boasts over 200 items, but the sour soup with deep-fried snakehead fish is a must. Like other dishes, it’s fresh, well-cooked and wallet friendly. Seating is available at two dining areas across the street from each other; closing time is midnight.

Name: Paste
Address: 3F, Gaysorn Village, 999 Phloen Chit Road, Lumphini, Pathum Wan, Bangkok, 10330, Thailand
Description: The food here is as intricate as the spiral silk cocoon sculpture that fills the airy dining room. Drawing inspiration from royal Thai cuisine, the kitchen also employs century-old techniques and plenty of local ingredients. The roasted duck curry with lychee, fennel seed and freshly squeezed coconut milk and the char-grilled pork, fennel seed, and smoked tomato relish are recommended and can be found on the tasting menus and à la carte. Excellent service further enhances the experience.

Name: Bang Por Seafood Takho
Description: Bang Por boasts an experienced kitchen team composed of local chefs who have worked here for many years. This simple beach-front restaurant is depicted by holiday vibes and Southern Thai seafood fare. The spicy stir-fried squid with herbs is cooked in a spicy curry paste and the grilled fish is sprinkled with mixed Thai herbs. The house shrimp paste is packed with aromatic plants and coconut chili and grilled before serving, hence the pungent aroma.

Name: Long Dtai
Address: Cape Fahn Hotel, 24/269 Mu 5, Bo Phut, Ko Samui, 84320, Thailand
Description: After crossing shallow waters, you reach this private island resort off Samui’s east coast. From the restaurant’s terrace, diners enjoy panoramic views of the bay as they sample chef David Thompson’s fab creations. His Southern Thai menu is deceptively simple and his consummate culinary talent is revealed in the details. Start with grilled squid, marinated in turmeric and coconut milk to accentuate its freshness. Marine sustainability is the name of the game here.

Name: Nan Bei
Address: 19F, Rosewood Hotel, 1041/38 Phloen Chit Road, Lumphini, Pathum Wan, Bangkok, 10330, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Bring your own bottle,Car park,Counter dining,Great view,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: Nan Bei means ‘south’ and ‘north’ so it’s no surprise to discover that this restaurant specialises in China’s southern and northern regions, from where the recipes come and ingredients are flown in. It sits on the 19th floor of the Rosewood Hotel, offering fabulous views of Bangkok while you dine. Braised abalone and braised pork belly shouldn’t be missed, though the prized item is Peking duck. Sit at the counter to see the chefs at work or to watch the birds being roasted over lychee wood. Lunchtime dim sum is also worth exploring.

Name: Baan Phraya
Address: Mandarin Oriental Hotel, 48 Soi Charoen Krung 40,  Charoen Krung Road, Bang Rak, Bangkok, 10500, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Valet parking
Description: The original owner of this 120-year-old heritage house served the government as Phraya, one of the highest ranks of Thai nobility. Previously Mandarin Oriental's cooking school, they switched operations in 2022. Chef Patchara serves traditional Thai dishes inspired by those school recipes. Surrounded by shady greens, the whitewashed house has a terrace with stunning sunset views over the river. The dining room inside fits a capacity of 20 guests a night.

Name: Krua Samchai
Address: 282/1 Phalochai Road, Nai Mueang, Mueang Ubon Ratchathani, Ubon Ratchathani, 34000, Thailand
Description: Two roosters stand guard at the entrance. Krua Samchai is famous for serving iconic Isan food befitting of the region. Fresh fish from the Mekong and Mun rivers is cooked using the chef's secret mix of herbs and spices that produces a powerful aroma. The grilled chicken has a crispy golden skin from the charcoal flame but retains its juicy meat. The Isan-style spicy fish maw and bamboo shoot soup uses tiliacora juice to perfection.

Name: Arunwan
Address: LGF, Park X Building, 295 Soi Ekkamai 15, Khlong Tan Nuea, Vadhana, Bangkok, 10110, Thailand
Description: Opened over 60 years ago and now run by the founder’s children, this spot specialises in a pork offal and pickled cabbage soup that they have honed over the years using a family recipe. It’s a fresh-tasting dish and the cabbage combines well with the sweetness of the pork consommé. The crispy pork wontons with sweet black sauce are well worth ordering while you wait for your soup.

Name: Go Ang Seafood
Address: 226 Mu 2, Phuket Road, Talat Yai, Mueang Phuket, Phuket, 83000, Thailand
Description: From humble origins as a small shop with a zinc roof, it’s now one of the most popular seafood restaurants with a comfortable interior and Chinese décor. Chef-owner Go Ang cooks the entire southern Thai menu. The blue swimming crab, horseshoe crab and mantis shrimp are sourced daily from 5 markets. The steamed crab with tangy seafood dip and fried mantis shrimp with garlic are delightful, while the Southern Thai spicy sour soup with seabass is also a must-try.

Name: Yi-Oui Noodles
Address: Behind Thai Mueang Shrine Chinese theater, Phang-Nga 3025 Rural Road, Thai Mueang, Phang-Nga, 82120, Thailand
Description: Aunty Oui has been delighting locals with the intense flavour of her noodle soups since 1971. Each table is laden with a basket of soft-boiled eggs; diners are welcome to finish as many as they can manage. The pork rib soup is a highlight and a Thai dessert rounds off the meal nicely.

Name: Sawang Noodles
Address: 264 Si Phraya Road, Maha Phruettharam, Bang Rak, Bangkok, 10500, Thailand
Description: This is the place to enjoy crab noodles in Bangkok. The sweet, giant crab claw meat pairs well with sticky egg noodles and shrimp dumplings. Be sure to try their signature noodles with extra soup and barbecued pork on the side.

Name: Chum (Saraphi)
Address: 1/1 Mu 7, Tha Wang Tan, Saraphi, Chiang Mai, 50140, Thailand
Description: Chum serves Northern Thai cuisine cooked from the recipes of the family's grandmother. The colourful restaurant is simply decorated with red and yellow walls and brightly coloured parasols of Northern Thai design hanging from the ceilings. The stir-fried pork and liver is well cooked, and packed with Thai herbs, wild pepper and coriander. The mixed Northern Thai starter uses a tasty young chili relish with the scent of green chili that isn’t too spicy.

Name: Jongjit Kitchen
Address: 9/1 Mu 4, Wichit Songkhram Road, Kathu, Phuket, 83120, Thailand
Description: Southern recipes, affordable prices and down-to-earth hospitality – this is why locals pack out this family-run business at lunch and dinner. Their family recipes pack great intensity. The Phuketian stir-fried pork rump with salt is lovely, with tender meat and lip-smacking pork skin.

Name: Suay
Address: Baan Wana Park, 177/99 Mu 4, Si Sunthon Road, Choeng Thale, Thalang, Phuket, 83110, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Counter dining,Garden or park,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: The acronym of ‘sassy, unique, authentic and yummy’ may sound kitsch, but the airy and bright interior with its Portuguese-tiled floor is anything but. Outdoor seating with garden and live music is equally pleasant. Owner-chef Tammasak skilfully updates Thai food with modern techniques and artsy presentation. Dishes, including the signature grilled lemongrass lamb chops with papaya salsa, are seasoned with bold but well-judged spicing. Also try the crab cakes with Sriracha chili aioli and mango chutney.

Name: Enoteca
Address: 39 Soi Sukhumvit 27, Khlong Toei Nuea, Vadhana, Bangkok, 10110, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Valet parking
Description: The name means ‘wine library’, so it will come as no surprise to find a list of nearly 400 bottles here, including a fine selection of Barolo. While it sits in the city’s bustling business district, this Italian restaurant is a haven of tranquillity. Floor-to-ceiling windows offer charming garden views, and the cosy, friendly atmosphere makes you feel as though you’re dining in an Italian home. All regions of Italy are represented, with ingredients flown in from Europe and used in dishes with a modern twist. Risottos are a highlight, and for the Secondi Piatti, don’t miss the Barbecue Pigeon. They also offer set menus for more variety.

Name: Shirokane Tori-Tama
Address: Park Lane, 18 Soi Sukhumvit 63, Khlong Tan Nuea, Vadhana, Bangkok, 10110, Thailand
Description: Experienced chefs from Tokyo have brought authentic yakitori cuisine to Bangkok, here at the group’s fourth branch in Asia. Beak-to-tail cooking is celebrated, where various chicken parts are prepared in several ways to create countless dishes that are full of flavour. Diners seated around the open kitchen in the middle of the dining room get to watch the chefs at work, listen to meat sizzling over hot coals, and take in the intoxicating aromas. Aside from the yakitori, the chicken liver pâté with warm baguette is a must.

Name: Guang Tang Noodles
Address: 18/15 Pimpasut Road, Nai Mueang, Mueang Khon Kaen, Khon Kaen, 40000, Thailand
Description: The history of this egg noodle soup spot stretches back more than 70 years to the owner’s grandfather. Today, it still satisfies — especially the noodle soup with wontons and barbecue pork (the noodles and wontons are homemade) and the deep-fried noodles with gravy and pork or beef.

Name: Kai Yang Sueb Siri
Address: 49 Sueb Siri Road, Nai Mueang, Mueang Nakhon Ratchasima, Nakhon Ratchasima, 30000, Thailand
Description: This 50-year-old family-run business has a large cooking station at the front that radiates a welcoming smell of grilled chicken. Most customers come in big groups to share popular Isan dishes. Three varieties of tender chicken are served; the crowd favourite is their signature barbequed chicken marinated in Thai herbs. The fermented fish sauce, made daily, emits an encapsulating aroma and the papaya salad hits the perfect balance between spicy and sour.

Name: Jaras
Address: InterContinental Phuket Resort, 333, 333/3 Mu 3, Kamala Beach, Kamala, Kathu, Phuket, 83150, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Wheelchair access
Description: Despite the luxury setting, Jaras retains honest roots. The intimate design draws influence from the Li Thai, Sukhothai era. The restaurant is named after the owner's grandma whose cooking inspired some of the recipes. Today’s chef embraces sustainability, serving a modern showcase of Thai flavours sourced locally, including microgreens grown on-site. For the full experience, request the Taste of Jaras tasting menu with wine pairing. Book at least 24 hours in advance.

Name: Kai Yang Wanna
Address: 271 Mu 11, Mittraphap Road, Kham Muang, Khao Suan Kwang, Khon Kaen, 40280, Thailand
Description: Grilled chicken is the name of the game at this Isan shophouse restaurant. Launched in 1973 by the current owner’s father, it uses a local breed, spices them using a family recipe and skilfully grills them over charcoal. They only make 200 a day, which always sell out, so reserve a bird or arrive early. Also on the menu are simple Isan dishes, including delicious pork larb. Seating is available inside with or without AC and outside on the veranda.

Name: Guay Jub Mr. Jo
Address: 86 Soi Chan 44, Wat Phraya Krai, Bang Kho Laem, Bangkok, 10120, Thailand
Description: From early morning until late afternoon, locals flock to the small room at the front and large dining area at the rear. Enjoy guay jub as an entrée or in a sweet, peppery rice noodle broth; rich layers of soft pork are encased in a crispy skin. Can be ordered with or without pork offal.

Name: Beach Grill and Bar
Address: Devasom Khao Lak Beach Resort & Villas, 79 Mu 3, Khuekkhak, Takua Pa, Phang-Nga, 82220, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Great view,Terrace,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: Offering a relaxing setting with indoor and outdoor seating perfect for enjoying cocktails and a delightful mix of Mediterranean dishes, against the backdrop of the evening sunset. Specialising in fresh seafood grilled over a wood-burning stove, the restaurant's standout dish is a seafood pizza with shrimp, squid, mussels, and mozzarella. Complete your dining experience with a delicious dessert like crispy fried bananas served with coconut milk ice cream.

Name: Khrua Nong
Address: 132/8 Phet Kasem Road, Bang Nai Si, Takua Pa, Phang-Nga, 82110, Thailand
Description: The husband-and-wife team go to market every day to select fresh, local ingredients and seafood and offer a wide selection of Thai dishes. Check the blackboard for the specials which change every day, but the crispy softshell crab with a peppery chilli sauce is unmissable.

Name: Khao (Vadhana)
Address: 15 Soi Ekkamai 10, Khlong Tan Nuea, Vadhana, Bangkok, 10110, Thailand
Description: Khao presents delightful Thai cuisine in a beautiful dining space that is inspired by traditional rice barns. The menu is all about attention to detail, using premium ingredients and blending diverse flavours that cater to every palate. Whether for casual dining or business meetings, it's an ideal spot to experience a thoughtfully curated meal that stays true to the essence of Thai cuisine. Book the Chef's Table menu for an exquisite culinary journey.

Name: O Tao Bang Niao
Address: 362 Phuket Road, Talat Yai, Mueang Phuket, Phuket, 83000, Thailand
Description: Since 1982, this family-run spot has been serving flavoursome O Tao, a stir-fried dish found only in Phuket. Made with seafood and battered taro, O Tao is cooked over a charcoal flame and boasts a combination of soft, gooey and crispy textures. They are well-balanced here, and the smoky aroma from the charcoal also helps to elevate the dish. Other options available include a fried crispy seafood omelette that is well worth ordering.

Name: Go La
Address: 11 Kra Road, Talat Yai, Mueang Phuket, Phuket, 83000, Thailand
Description: In its third generation of family ownership, this is one of Phuket’s best Hokkien-style fried noodle joints. Its charm is conjured up by a concoction of special flavours, the sounds of the wok and charcoal smells. Order the yellow hokkien noodles with an extra egg for a creamier texture.

Name: Khanom Jeen Mae Ploy
Address: 7/1 Mu 6, Siriratchathani Road, Muen Wai, Mueang Nakhon Ratchasima, Nakhon Ratchasima, 30000, Thailand
Description: The secret to Mae Ploy’s bouncy yet gooey noodles is the fermented rice flour from Ban Pra Dok. There’s a creamy, peppery spicy fish curry with coconut cream, a red chicken curry with offal, and a sweet, nutty peanut curry. The spicy fish curry has a lovely, aromatic fermented taste.

Name: Sookjailand
Address: 98 Mu 7, Maliwan Road, Nong Bua, Ban Fang, Khon Kaen, 40270, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Cash only,Garden or park,Great view
Description: Time drifts past at this tranquil Isan restaurant, where diners eat in private bamboo pavilions dotting a large rice field. There are no tables—meals are served on woven mats on the floor, local style. And the food, which comes in both shareable set menus and à la carte dishes, is just as authentic as the setting. Made from quality, fresh ingredients, simple dishes like the grilled snakehead fish set and the local crab soup with veggies, are highly recommended.

Name: Baan
Address: 139/5 Wireless Road, Lumphini, Pathum Wan, Bangkok, 10330, Thailand
Description: At this sister restaurant to Le Du, comforting family recipes take centre stage. The intimate venue boasts a contemporary look with marble tables and chic lighting. They prioritise high-quality ingredients, including beef from Pak Chong's Islamic farms and responsibly sourced seafood from southern Thailand. Pair dishes with their selection of biodynamic, organic wines and house cocktails.

Name: Kaithong Original
Address: 164/13-15 Soi Chaeng Watthana-Pak Kret 33, Chaeng Watthana Road, Bang Phut, Pak Kret, Nonthaburi, 11120, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Wheelchair access
Description: This family-run establishment is renowned for its traditional recipes, serving fresh meat and seafood flavours in simple yet refined and lightly seasoned dishes. Catering to different tastes, the stir-fried liver with garlic is made with either pork or chicken liver. The inviting, comfortable space can also accommodate larger groups.

Name: Khao
Address: Four Seasons Resort, 502 Mu 1, Mae Rim-Samoeng Old Road, Rim Tai, Mae Rim, Chiang Mai, 50180, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Terrace,Valet parking
Description: Khao serves Northern Thai cuisine, along with some dishes from other regions. The chef, a prestigious culinary school graduate with 10 years of luxury hotel experience, brings an international perspective and a modern identity to traditional Thai dishes. The dining room is contemporary and inviting – crystal chandeliers coexist with carved teak panelling – and the terrace offers serene views of rice fields and hills.

Name: Tang Sui Heng (Banthat Thong Road)
Address: 649 Banthat Thong Road, Wang Mai, Pathum Wan, Bangkok, 10330, Thailand
Description: This iconic family-run shop has been packed with locals for more than 50 years. These days, the family’s second generation runs it, but the founder’s talent for cooking dishes like the signature claypot stewed duck with intestines, blood jelly, and feet clearly runs in the family.

Name: North
Address: 8 Soi Sukhumvit 33, Khlong Tan Nuea, Vadhana, Bangkok, 10110, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Wheelchair access
Description: This classic Thai house, painted in green with a lush front garden, offers an oasis in the city. Under Chef Chumpol's guidance, a skilled team led by a northern Thai head chef presents a menu preserving the traditional taste of northern Thailand. The lunch offers à la carte choices, while dinner features a seasonal set menu using ingredients from various regions. Highlights include the herb-packed Northern sharing set, Khan-Tok, and the flavourful Khao Soi.

Name: Guay Jub Ubon
Address: 7 Phrommathep Road, Nai Mueang, Mueang Ubon Ratchathani, Ubon Ratchathani, 34000, Thailand
Description: For over 70 years, this little gem has maintained strict quality control, carefully selecting offal from more than 10kg of offcuts each day. Their specialty is guay jub rice noodles with pork offal in a dark five-spice soup. They also serve delectable egg noodle and wonton soups.

Name: Samchai Coffee (Thepyothi Road)
Address: 168/4 Thepyothi Road, Nai Mueang, Mueang Ubon Ratchathani, Ubon Ratchathani, 34000, Thailand
Description: The menu boasts a tasty dried shredded pork and a range of sausages. A highlight is the Indochina pan-fried egg served with a side sandwich. The eggs are cooked sunny side up with margarine, then topped with sweet and salty Chinese sausage and peppery Vietnamese sausage slices.

Name: Antito
Address: 14F, Eastin Grand Sathorn 33/1 Sathon Tai Road, Yan Nawa, Sathon, Bangkok, 10120, Thailand
Description: Located on the 14th floor of Eastin Grand Sathorn, Chef Amerigo Sesti’s restaurant-bar offers a creative take on Northern Italian classics from his childhood, complemented by stunning city views. The stylish dining room features pop art and cosy seating. Try the handmade Italian pasta or tiramisu, showcasing the chef’s flair for authentic flavours. A DJ sets the mood from Thursday to Sunday nights.

Name: Kagero
Address: Modernform Forty 9 55/1, Sukhumvit 49 Road, Khlong Tan Nuea, Vadhana, Bangkok, 10110, Thailand
Description: At Kagero, a fusion of Japanese and Italian cuisine is created by combining Japanese and European techniques to transform premium ingredients into a sensory delight. Diners can watch the chef at work from the counter or choose a private room for a more exclusive experience. We recommend the Kani Croquet, renowned for its bold flavours, succulent crab meat, and tantalising aroma. Conclude your meal with a delicious kakigōri, featuring a milky ice cream centre.

Name: Buabok
Address: Amanpuri Resort 118, 1 Si Sunthon Road, Pansea Beach, Choeng Thale, Thalang, Phuket, 83110, Thailand
Description: Buabok is set in a tranquil resort that features reflective pools and swaying palms, creating the perfect backdrop for dining. Enjoy aromatic Thai cuisine beneath the pitched roof of an elegant wooden villa. From Thai salads to smooth curries, the menu is crafted from fresh local produce. Arrive before sunset to embrace the gentle pace of nature and stunning views of the Andaman Sea. Don't miss their rich, flavourful Panaeng Nuea, an Angus beef red curry.

Name: Noodles Soi 12 (Ban Suan)
Address: 44/8-9 Mu 6, Soi Ban Suan-Setthakit 30, Ban Suan, Mueang Chon Buri, Chon Buri, 20000, Thailand
Description: With its wooden furniture and rustic charm, this is a delightful spot for an early breakfast or lunch. The real star here is the soup with aromatic dried squid and pork ribs imparting rich flavour. Each tasty spoonful is testament to the traditional recipe.

Name: Krua Pla Tu Tid Oun
Address: 8/1 Nadedee Road Soi 5, Saen Suk, Mueang Chon Buri, Chon Buri, 20130, Thailand
Description: This place near Bang Saen beach has been popular with tourists for decades. The signature is, of course, pla tu (Thai mackerel), but the menu extends from seafood options such as sillago, sea bass and local scallops – all cooked in classic Thai style – to crispy deep-fried mackerel cheek with a chilli-garlic aroma that's addictive. If you prefer a milder taste, the staff are happy to adjust the spice level to suit your palate.

Name: Baannok Bangkok
Address: 34/3 VIVRE Building, Lang Suan Road, Lumphini, Pathum Wan, Bangkok, 10330, Thailand
Description: Baannok serves authentic Korat-style Thai food, in which the sweetness that is typical to the region is toned down for broader tastes. To awaken the palate, try the sweet and sour Korat sausage salad. The signature Pad Mhee Korat with a giant river prawn is expertly wok-fried with duck egg and accompanied by a smooth sweet sauce. For something comforting, take the Kaeng Liang Kam Thale So, a spicy vegetable soup, fragrant with herbs and spices commonly used in Isan cooking. Advance reservation is a must.

Name: Uan Ja Noodle
Address: 45 U Thong Road, Ho Rattanachai, Phra Nakhon Si Ayutthaya, 13000, Thailand
Description: A popular lunch spot for over half a century, they sell a prolific 100kg of meatballs a day. The buoyant balls playfully float in the noodle soup and the condiments are homemade, including a spicy, sour chili vinegar sauce. Fresh-cooked or slow-cooked beef options are also available.

Name: Yong Poo Ob
Address: 1844/1 Mittraphap Road, Nai Mueang, Mueang Nakhon Ratchasima, Nakhon Ratchasima, 30000, Thailand
Description: It’s hard to miss this restaurant with its large orange crab statue out front. And you wouldn’t want to miss eating here either. Inside is a mix of industrial and rustic décor, with a stage for live music. A small English-style garden with a water fountain surrounded by trees provides tranquil outdoor dining. The fresh catch of shrimp, prawns and crabs are as fresh as can be, swimming in their tanks up until an order comes in. The signature baked glass noodles with hot pot crab is superb in a herby gravy; the grilled tiger prawns and Thai spicy seafood sauce is also delightful.

Name: Yommarat O-Cha
Address: 9-11 Yommarat Road, Nai Mueang, Mueang Nakhon Ratchasima, Nakhon Ratchasima, 30000, Thailand
Description: The standout dish at this local favourite is the yentafo soup with fish balls, soy sauce and tofu. The flavour is pleasantly sweet and sour but this isn’t the spicy yentafo tomyum common in Bangkok. The soup is cooked fresh using a vibrant mix of condiments. Dry and wet options are available and all the great toppings are homemade.

Name: Whale Chicken Noodles
Address: 156 Sri Chant Road, Nai Mueang, Mueang Khon Kaen, Khon Kaen, 40000, Thailand
Description: The secret to the popularity of this eatery is its tender chicken and flavoursome broth – made with chicken bones and vegetables, it has a rich, meaty and naturally sweet flavour. Enjoy the breeze as you dine on the sidewalk, just like a local.

Name: Withee Laab
Address: 94-120 Charoen Muang Road, Wat Ket, Mueang Chiang Mai, Chiang Mai, 50000, Thailand
Description: This charming wooden building down a narrow alley has been serving delicious laab for years. The spicy minced buffalo meat and zesty cooked minced pork are sure to impress. With surprisingly affordable prices, this is a gem worth seeking out.

Name: Baan Rearn Mai
Address: Ban Khok Kloi - Na Tai, Khok Kloi, Takua Thung, Phang-Nga, 82140, Thailand
Description: Operating for 25 years, this small eatery offers an à la carte menu focused on seafood. The freshly prepared meals are light, allowing the natural umami of the seafood to shine. In addition to their signature yellow curry crab, the steamed sea bass with soy sauce is a must-try.

Name: Klai Lib
Address: 126 Bangsaenlang Road, Saen Suk, Mueang Chon Buri, Chon Buri, 20130, Thailand
Description: Attracting younger diners, this eatery has a reputation for fresh, affordable Thai seafood of uncompromising quality. The generous portions with sweet seasonings are good for sharing; the deep-fried mackerel with fish sauce is a must for its crispy skin and tender meat.

Name: Fuego
Address: 2F, The Taste Thonglor, Thong Lo Soi 11, Khlong Tan Nuea, Vadhana, Bangkok, 10110, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Counter dining,Interesting wine list,Notable sake list
Description: Helmed by a Spanish chef with a passion for Japanese cuisine, Fuego boldly blends these two culinary traditions. From your seat in this intimate setting, watch premium-quality Spanish and Japanese ingredients being meticulously crafted in the open kitchen. Don't miss the signature paella. Another standout is the tapas, complemented by Japanese whisky and sake. The velvety, multidimensional miso cheesecake is the perfect ending.

Name: Baan Suriyasai
Address: 174 Surawong Road, Si Phraya, Bang Rak, Bangkok, 10500, Thailand
Description: Located in a restored 100-year-old mansion in the heart of the city, Baan Suriyasai evokes early 20C Thai elegance with time-tested dishes and old-world hospitality. The menu is drawn from royal recipes from the Rama V era and bygone family favourites, including the five-spice stew with boiled eggs, and the stir-fried crispy pork belly, fish flakes and dried shrimp with seasoned paste. Head to the classic Thai cocktail bar upstairs for an after-dinner drink.

Name: Santi
Address: 101-17 Chawala Nok Road, Nai Mueang, Mueang Ubon Ratchathani, Ubon Ratchathani, 34000, Thailand
Description: Diners can sit inside or roadside in this simple, open-air restaurant. Thai-Chinese is the fare and dishes are prepared at the front. The sound of the wok and sight of the flames make an impressive spectacle. The stir-fried minced pork with olives is a must for its smoky, intense flavours. The deep-fried seabass with sweet fish sauce takes a little longer to prepare but the result is a fantastically crispy skin that goes well with the homemade spicy sauce.

Name: Meesapam Khun Yai Chian
Address: 56/8, 65/24 Mu 1, Thep Krasatti Road, Ko Kaeo, Mueang Phuket, Phuket, 83000, Thailand
Description: Grandma Chian opened this Hokkien restaurant in 1952. Her great-great grandchildren have stayed loyal to her recipes and proudly exhibit her cooking utensils. Serving Phuket favourites, the Mee Sapam, stir-fried Hokkien noodles with seafood, is great. The stir-fried oysters with crispy egg roll are beautifully crafted with beansprouts, kale and a tasty chilli sauce.

Name: Kiti Panit
Address: 19 Tha Phae Road, Chang Khlan, Mueang Chiang Mai, Chiang Mai, 50100, Thailand
Description: Turning their great-great-grandparents’ 1880s mansion into a restaurant, Kiti Panit’s owners decided to create an updated take on traditional Lanna cuisine. The results include intense and complex Hang Le, or northern Thai curry, and savoury grilled chicken salad with coriander. Also recommended are the signature Khao Mao Gorn Rad Gati, or unripe rice with coconut milk, and the creative seasonal desserts.

Name: Baan Mai Rim Nahm
Address: 43/1 Mu 2, U Thong Road, Pratu Chai, Phra Nakhon Si Ayutthaya, 13000, Thailand
Description: This local favourite has been serving flavoursome Central Thai cuisine in a laid-back setting by the Chao Phraya River for over 20 years. The skilled chef cooks everything, including the recommended Tom Yum with redtail catfish and the huge grilled river prawns, with quality ingredients from local farmers and fisherfolk. Meals can be enjoyed in the air-conditioned dining room, on the terrace, or even on the water if you book the restaurant’s riverboat tour.

Name: Nai Liak Beef Noodles
Address: 6/7 Pa Maphrao Road, Ho Rattanachai, Phra Nakhon Si Ayutthaya, 13000, Thailand
Description: Mr. Liak, this eatery’s owner, started his business way back in 1961 – before moving to his current roadside location in 1977. He serves delicious beef noodle soup at wallet-friendly prices. Beef offal, braised beef, beef meatballs and stewed tendons are among the options available in the savoury broth – vermicelli, herbs and spices are also packed into this signature dish. Expect a wait during peak hours.

Name: Baan Pomphet
Address: 13/5 U Thong Road, Ho Rattanachai, Phra Nakhon Si Ayutthaya, 13000, Thailand
Description: This Thai restaurant next to Pom Phet (Diamond Fortress) is in the distinctive-looking boutique hotel of the same name. Inside, the stylish dining room is fitted with large windows that frame a view of the restaurant’s deck and the Chao Phraya. Sourcing ingredients from the river and local farms, the chef creates flavourful dishes like standouts grilled river prawns and boiled freshwater snails in red curry soup. Book ahead for a riverside table at dinner.

Name: Sang Ka Sri
Address: 262/8 Yaowarat Road, Talat Yai, Mueang Phuket, Phuket, 83000, Thailand
Description: This outlet with a red-brown zinc roof offers a menu of both individual and sharing dishes, with nicely balanced flavours. Despite its humble guise, Sang Ka Sri attracts a crowd, so be prepared to wait for a table before enjoying the fresh squid with herbs and tangy dressing.

Name: Krua Taan
Address: 65/16 Mu 7, Soi Mu Ban Chang, Pai Ling, Phra Nakhon Si Ayutthaya, 13000, Thailand
Description: In this spacious, open-air pavilion, Aunty Taan serves traditional-style cooking that has won the hearts of local diners and tourists alike. Do try the prawn and herb spicy salad, which features just-right grilled prawn meat and various refreshing herbs bound together with a flavourful dressing. The fiery stir-fried minced pork cartilage is also delicious and aromatic. This is the perfect stop after visiting the nearby floating market and elephant village.

Name: Suriyan Chandra
Address: 38 Mu 7, Phra Khao, Bang Ban, Phra Nakhon Si Ayutthaya, 13250, Thailand
Description: The old mill that houses this riverside restaurant is over 130 years old and provides a unique vintage atmosphere to diners seeking a memorable experience. Delicate titbits such as Toong Thong and the flower-like Chor Muang make delightful starters, before moving on to main courses including the fabulous fried snakehead fish with herbs and deep-fried shrimp with tamarind sauce. They also offer a river tour package along the Noi, which culminates in dining at the restaurant. Booking is essential.

Name: La Cucina
Address: Andaz Pattaya Jomtien Beach  345 Mu 3, Na Chom Thian, Sattahip, Chon Buri, 20250, Thailand
Description: Off the beaten tourist path, La Cucina offers an escape to a lush, tropical garden setting, where blue and white tiled floors, French windows and bossa nova tunes foster a relaxed atmosphere. This restaurant helmed by local chefs and an affable service team has an enticing Italian menu. Handmade pizzas are the stand-out.

Name: Khao Tom Ped Jek Tong
Address: 421/1 Vachira Prakarn Road, Makham Yong, Mueang Chon Buri, Chon Buri, 20000, Thailand
Description: For a taste of long-established local fare, this eight-decade-old gem that holds itself to exacting standards of cleanliness is a must. Tender braised duck meat with savoury gravy is the signature, best enjoyed with rice; fans of spicy food will relish the house-made dipping condiments.

Name: Bisou
Address: 68 Soi Langsuan 9, Lumphini, Pathum Wan, Bangkok, 10330, Thailand
Description: Chef Antoine Darquin and sommelier Théo Lavergne bring a fresh, fashionable Parisian flair to Bangkok's dining scene. Bisou delivers sexy simplicity through modern French cuisine, prioritising premium ingredients. The stylish yet relaxed space features enchanting lights, a spiral staircase and wall art. The dishes and rare wines contribute to a unique local experience influenced by the latest trends from Paris.

Name: Mae Pong Sri
Address: 42/99 Mu 9, Sukhumvit Road, Pattaya, Nong Prue, Bang Lamung, Chon Buri, 20150, Thailand
Description: The go-to spot in Pattaya for pork offal soup with boiled sweet leaf bush, this eatery draws inspiration from Thai cuisine nationwide to offer a plethora of quick street food dishes. From the many noodle and rice options, the stir-fried glass noodles with seafood stand out.

Name: Phae Krung Kao
Address: 4/1 U Thong Road, Ho Rattanachai, Phra Nakhon Si Ayutthaya, 13000, Thailand
Description: This well-known restaurant, whose name means ‘raft at the old city of Ayutthaya’, started selling food on the river in 1966. It has since moved into a traditional Thai house, where diners can enjoy flavoursome Central Thai cuisine; local ingredients are used in dishes like their signature green curry with fish balls. The huge river prawns are charcoal-grilled by the restaurant’s entrance, creating a wonderful smoky aroma for everyone who visits. Sit on the terrace for a river view.

Name: hom
Address: InterContinental Phuket Resort, 333, 333/3 Mu 3, Kamala Beach, Kamala, Kathu, Phuket, 83150, Thailand
Description: After a stroll through a serene garden walkway, you will find this restaurant inside the InterContinental Resort. The Portuguese chef showcases a fermentation-heavy concept on the menu, highlighting new sides to local produce. Leeks, betel leaves and pandan are just some of the ingredients that are given the fermentation treatment, in delicately executed dishes. The natural wine list is in keeping with the restaurant’s ethos, and the intimate atmosphere makes it ideal for a romantic dinner.

Name: Garlic
Address: 44 Soi Chotiwat, Bang Sue, Bangkok, 10800, Thailand
Description: Head to this unassuming yet charming restaurant for Thai home-style cooking in Bang Sue district. For over 40 years, diners have been relishing the cosy ambience and a Thai menu that favours seafood over meat. The crispy pork pairs up with a distinctive apple sauce; the tom yum coconut soup is enriched by the flesh of young coconut for a flavour that is a delightful deviation from the norm. Call ahead to nab a table at this neighbourhood gem.

Name: Juksunchae
Address: 5F, Woodberry Common, 15/3 Soi Ruamrudee, Lumphini, Pathum Wan, Bangkok, 10330, Thailand
Description: Driven by the chef’s desire to put an original twist on Korean recipes, this restaurant delivers well-known cuisine through a creative lens. The flavours and combinations may be long established, but they’re presented with original touches – such as a painting-like uni bibimbap that will make you see the dish in a completely new light. A few flavour innovations can also be found, such as strawberry doenjang. The contemporary reinvention of classic cooking is reflected in the combination of chic décor and traditional Korean furniture.

Name: Den Kushi Flori
Address: LGF, Erawan Bangkok Building, 494 Phloen Chit Road, Lumphini, Pathum Wan, Bangkok, 10330, Thailand
Description: A collaboration between two Japanese chefs, and their first overseas outpost, this minimalist restaurant consists of a U-shaped wooden counter wrapped around an open kitchen. The chefs have experience in both Japan and France, meaning their 5 or 7 course tasting menus blend French technique with the essence of Japanese cuisine – a few Thai touches, like a spicy watermelon sauce, provide a nod to the locale. Rice cooked with corn is a highlight, well-judged in texture and topped with teriyaki beef.

Name: Small Dinner Club
Address: 1109 Charoen Krung Road, Si Phraya, Bang Rak, Bangkok, 10500, Thailand
Description: Set in a 2-storey house in the historic town, Small Dinner Club exudes mystery and charm. The dimly lit interior sports a striking black colour scheme. In his own words, Chef Sareen “pulls apart, questions and reimagines Thai cuisine”. Unafraid of challenging conventions, he includes savoury ingredients in sweet recipes and sweet ingredients, like seasonal fruit, in savoury dishes, resulting in intelligently crafted and artistically presented Thai food.

Name: Chuan Kitchen
Address: 50/666 Mu 6, Soi Mu Ban Mueang Thong Thani, Ban Mai, Pak Kret, Nonthaburi, 11120, Thailand
Description: With Singaporean chicken rice, Indonesian laksa and Malaysian Bak Kut Teh the highlights, Chuan Kitchen is the only restaurant in Nonthaburi offering this mix of national cuisine. Its stylish design is welcoming, with a high wooden ceiling, and floor-to-ceiling windows, accentuated by black stainless-steel frames and lighting. The fried typhoon soft shell crab stands out with its light crispy texture with a chilli, deep-fried crispy garlic and onion black bean sauce.

Name: Riva del Fiume
Address: LF, Four Seasons Hotel Bangkok at Chao Phraya River, 300/1 Charoen Krung Road, Yan Nawa, Sathon, Bangkok, 10120, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Counter dining,Great view,Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: The view from the terrace is of the Chao Phraya, but inside, this modern Italian restaurant in the Four Seasons Hotel feels more like Lake Como with its Euro vibes, open kitchen and wood oven. At the helm is an Italian chef who worked at several famed restaurants in Europe. Here he deftly cooks favourites like his pizza and home-made pasta with quality ingredients imported from Italy. Adding to the experience is the high level of service of the team.

Name: Tiffin by La Sala
Address: Anantara Mai Khao Phuket Villas, 888 Mu 3, Mai Khao, Thalang, Phuket, 83110, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus
Description: Al fresco dining by a tranquil lagoon is the big draw at this restaurant located in Anantara Mai Khao Villas. The chef, from Maharashtra, takes diners on a journey through authentic Indian cuisine via an extensive à la carte featuring curries, a tiffin chaat platter and dishes from the tandoor oven. The cooking is flavoursome and well-spiced, with their signature lamb vindaloo a stand-out and the freshly baked naan well worth trying. Indoor dining with a view of the open kitchen is also available.

Name: Ruen Jarung
Address: 67/3 Mu 2, Ban Wa, Bang Pa-in, Phra Nakhon Si Ayutthaya, 13160, Thailand
Description: Eating here requires foresight, but your efforts will be rewarded. Booking only opens twice a year for three seatings a day Friday-Sunday. To book, check social media and follow the rules, which change each time — oh, and you’ll also need to choose your order in advance. But once you arrive at the vintage Thai house, you’ll be regaled with generous portions of expertly cooked authentic Thai fare, like the impressive Nam Prik Song Mae.

Name: Praya Dining
Address: Praya Palazzo 757/1 Soi Somdet Phra Pin Klao 2, Bang Yi Khan, Bang Phlat, Bangkok, 10700, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus
Description: Accessible only by boat, the Praya Palazzo hotel’s Praya Dining is located in a century-old Palladian-style mansion on the banks of the Chao Phraya River. Inside, it exudes historic charm to complement its culinary offerings. The menu unites iconic dishes from the Sukhothai and Ayutthaya Kingdoms with the Rattanakosin Kingdom and modern Bangkok; Gaeng Rawang, a stir-fried beef curry flavoured with turmeric and lemongrass, stands out for its great aromatic spicing.

Name: Kampun Gai Yang
Address: 94/7 Mu 6, Rochana Road, Phai Ling, Phra Nakhon Si Ayutthaya, 13000, Thailand
Description: Opened in 2017, this restaurant serves authentic Isan food in a commercial building on Rochana Road. Air-conditioned and filling two floors, the casual dining room is decorated with wood panels and other touches that suggest traditional Thai houses. The skilled chef cooks halal-friendly food following recipes from his grandmother, who is from Nakhon Phanom. His signature dish, Kampun grilled chicken, is recommended. The quality of service adds to the experience.

Name: Angeum
Address: 55/17 Mu 7, Khlong Suan Phlu, Phra Nakhon Si Ayutthaya, 13000, Thailand
Description: The story of Vietnamese food in Ayutthaya started over 150 years ago with the Vietnamese community in Bang Sai District. It continues at this modern two-floor restaurant smartly decorated with wooden walls, colourful paintings and a stylish bar. The menu may be short but it’s packed with authentic Vietnamese dishes. The skilled chef prepares everything using fresh quality ingredients. The signature dish, Nem Nuong is a delight to assemble and eat.

Name: Khaotom Chedi
Address: 254/14 Rochana Road, Phai Ling, Phra Nakhon Si Ayutthaya, 13000, Thailand
Description: This popular late-night spot is known for its fresh ingredients and flavourful dishes. The chef-owner warmly welcomes guests and takes orders with a smile. The menu changes daily, depending on the ingredients available. Enjoy dining outdoors with a view of Sam Pluem Temple's chedi.

Name: Nitan
Address: 177/38 Mu 6, Si Sunthon Road, Choeng Thale, Thalang, Phuket, 83110, Thailand
Description: Nitan, or ’determination’ in Thai, may refer to the chef’s aim of creating a real gastronomic experience. This is most evident in the tasting menu and wine pairing, where quality seasonal and local ingredients inform the cooking. Contemporary techniques are used to prepare classic Southern Thai dishes, with well-balanced flavours and a dash of creativity. The restaurant has a warm vibe and is minimally decorated, with wooden furniture and a window into the kitchen.

Name: FishHouse
Address: Kimpton Kitalay Samui, 10/79 Mu 5, Bo Phut, Ko Samui, 84320, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view
Description: Set inside the Kimpton Kitalay resort, FishHouse crafts à la carte European recipes using the freshest local ingredients. Take a seat on the deck overlooking the beach and enjoy the sea breeze and the lively atmosphere by the pool where sunbathers sip cocktails. Start with ceviche, bursting with fresh tropical passionfruit flavours and perfectly marinated diced seabass. The Black Paella with squid and squid ink is ideal to share.

Name: Vilas
Address: F207, 2F, Mahanakhon CUBE, Naradhiwas Rajanagarindra Road, Si Lom, Bang Rak, Bangkok, 10500, Thailand
Description: Their seasonal menu here is themed around different regions of Thailand, while expertly combining imported European produce with local ingredients. The modern and original interpretations of classic Thai dishes are executed using contemporary techniques and deliver well-judged spicing and layers of texture. There is a casual feel to the dining room, with simple décor and whitewashed walls; there’s a lively open kitchen too, so ensure you sit at the counter to watch the chefs in action.

Name: Jampa
Address: The Community House, Tri Vananda, 46/6 Mu 3, Thep Krasatti, Thalang, Phuket, 83110, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Wheelchair access
Description: Chef Dingen’s inventive contemporary European menu embraces a philosophy of sustainability and zero waste. À la carte is available all day, but we recommend the exquisitely prepared Jampa Experience for lunch, which features complex natural flavours that change with the seasons. For a unique lakeside experience on Saturdays, Hideaway’s 4-course lunch, cooked over a wood fire, both tantalises the tastebuds and educates the diner about sustainable farming.

Name: Chom Chan
Address: 242/2 Yaowarat Road, Talat Yai, Mueang Phuket, Phuket, 83000, Thailand
Description: Chom Chan has flourished with its own charming character and refreshing ambiance. Situated in a small white house with a leafy façade, the interior is a blend of modern Sino-Portuguese with antique decoration. Some dishes are shared with the other restaurants but do try the fried crab’s spawn with chilli, pepper and garlic; steamed minced pork with salty egg; and deep-fried pork belly with salt.

Name: Tumkratoei Sagate
Address: 88-89 Mu 20, Maliwan Road, Ban Pet, Mueang Khon Kaen, Khon Kaen, 40000, Thailand
Description: The owner is from Roi Et Province (formerly Sagate Province). The place offers flavourful food, warm service and wallet-friendly prices in a relaxed setting. The signature spicy seafood salad with fermented fish sauce is recommended, and beyond the Som Tum dishes, standouts include fried sour fish and spicy chicken soup with glass noodles. Indoors and outdoor seating are available. Nightly live music adds to the experience.

Name: Sanyod (Bang Rak)
Address: 89 Soi Charat Wiang, Si Lom, Bang Rak, Bangkok, 10500, Thailand
Description: With a history spanning more than half a century, what started as a food stall located in a small alley has since grown into a popular and bustling neighbourhood restaurant. They specialise in Cantonese cuisine, and their roast duck and signature sauces are highly recommended, especially paired with Cantonese-style noodles. The menu also features a deliciously tender clay pot-braised beef.

Name: Loba Bang Niao
Address: 18/61 Mae Luan Road, Talat Nuea, Mueang Phuket, Phuket, 83000, Thailand
Description: Loba was a traditional snack for Fujian Chinese in Phuket and this shop has remained consistent since day one. The semi-crispy pork offal and aromatic spices of the mixed loba blend well with a sweet chilli and crushed peanut sauce. The 4 deep-fried dishes are also mouth-watering treats.

Name: Talung Thai
Address: GF, Paresa Resort, 49 Mu 6, Layi-Nakhale Road, Kamala, Kathu, Phuket, 83150, Thailand
Description: The views from Paresa Resort, high on a clifftop, are breathtaking at sunset. It’s an idyllic spot to sip cocktails, before moving to the terrace for sumptuous southern and central Thai cuisine. Start with mixed Thai canapés or the soft shell crab miang, followed by the fragrant stir-fried Phuket lobster. Don't forget to save room for the Thai-styled dessert.

Name: The Thai Library
Address: Trisara Resort, 60/1 Mu 6, Srisoonthorn Road, Choeng Thale, Thalang, Phuket, 83110, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Great view,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: Inspired by local recipes and ingredients, The Thai Library has created a refined, southern menu. Take the Massaman Plamuek for example, which uses local Andaman octopus in a sweet and creamy sauce, while the stir-fried jumbo black tiger prawns, with crispy garlic and chilli, sing subtle herbal notes. To top it off, it’s the perfect romantic experience with an intimate setting indoors and breezy sunset views on the outdoor terrace overlooking a secluded beach.

Name: Huen Lamphun (Taling Chan)
Address: 64/233 Mu 5, Suan Phak Road, Chimphli, Taling Chan, Bangkok, 10170, Thailand
Description: Northern Thai food has a special place in the hearts of locals, but finding good food like this outside the region can be tough. So Huen Lamphun is a gem of a find, to such an extent that large groups from the neighbourhood return in droves. Every dish uses organic vegetables grown onsite. The grilled, fermented northern Thai pork in banana leaf explodes with chilli and garlic. Another favourite is Makwan-marinated grilled chicken with a peppery flavour and herbal aroma.

Name: Indus
Address: 71 Soi Sukhumvit 26, Khlong Tan, Khlong Toei, Bangkok, 10110, Thailand
Description: Indus presents a diverse and approachable selection of Indian dishes, showcasing flavours from Punjab, Kashmir, Goa, and Rajasthan, skilfully adapted to the Thai palate. As a certified Halal restaurant, it upholds the highest standards for both its meat and vegetarian offerings. The signature Raan is available in various sizes. This special lamb leg is slow-cooked for seven hours and then gently grilled to achieve tender, juicy perfection.

Name: Saawaan
Address: 39/19 Soi Suan Phlu, Sathon Road, Thung Maha Mek, Sathon, Bangkok, 10120, Thailand
Description: "Saawaan", meaning "heaven" in Thai, delivers a transcendent dining experience courtesy of a set menu that artistically plays with Thai flavours and cooking techniques including fermenting, steaming, boiling and grilling over charcoal. Each dish is plated and served in its own unique way, delighting diners. The menu highlights both imported and local ingredients, emphasising the restaurant's commitment to quality and community.

Name: Maadae
Address: 86-88 Thapae Road, Chang Moi, Mueang Chiang Mai, Chiang Mai, 50300, Thailand
Description: Meaning ‘come’ in the Southern language, ‘Maadae’ invites you to enjoy delightful seafood in a welcoming atmosphere. Supporting local Chumphon fishermen and sourcing seasonal organic produce, their menu rotates with fresh ingredients. The evening selection offers diverse options, including superb freshly grilled seafood paired with a spicy sauce.

Name: Talung
Address: 8 Chotana Road Soi 12, Chang Phueak, Mueang Chiang Mai, Chiang Mai, 50300, Thailand
Description: Having recently relocated to this ground floor eatery under a residential apartment, Talung is simply decorated with air conditioning, a lively bar and serves Southern Thai. It’s a small family business, the staff are friendly and attentive, and help each other from kitchen to table. The stir-fried squid with squid ink has a rich, well-seasoned sauce and herbal scent. The stir-fried prawns come with a homemade southern Thai shrimp paste and young bitter beans.

Name: Guay Tiew Pet Tun Saraphi
Address: 80 Mu 3, Liap Thang Rotfai Road, Saraphi, Chiang Mai, 50140, Thailand
Description: Take a break and make tracks to this wallet-friendly shop that’s mastered braised duck. The duck noodles use the family’s secret blend of spices, while the roasted duck has succulent meat and crispy skin, moistened by the duck's own jus. Northern-Thai and other dishes are available.

Name: Koh Thai Kitchen
Address: Four Seasons Resort Koh Samui, 219 Mu 5, Ang Thong, Ko Samui, 84140, Thailand
Description: Koh Thai Kitchen is located on a hilltop within the Four Seasons Hotel. The restaurant's alfresco dining areas sport a rustic style. Diners can enjoy southern and central Thai dishes made with premium ingredients such as local seafood, Australian lamb and Wagyu beef. All of which while breathing in the fresh air as you admire the drop-dead vista of sprawling jungle and blue sea dotted with nearby islands, as you snap the dramatic Instagram-perfect sunsets.

Name: Kaow Laor
Address: 11/4 Mu 6, Soi Wat Thammaram,  Ban Pom, Phra Nakhon Si Ayutthaya, Phra Nakhon Si Ayutthaya, 13000, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view
Description: With a whitewashed interior and views of the garden and river, Kaow Laor feels like a modern country home. The Thai menu is replete with grandma's recipes, offering giant river prawns, featherback fish balls and other local river fish. Each dish is expertly cooked and seasoned, and it’s like eating authentic Thai food at home. The imported mackerel with fish sauce is prepared with a light crispy skin, an aromatic fish sauce, deep-fried edible flowers and a spicy dressing.

Name: Mook Manee
Address: 1120 Wiset Road, Rawai, Mueang Phuket, Phuket, 83100, Thailand
Description: Located near Rawai Beach, Mook Manee stands out for its array of live seafood for diners to choose from, including squid, tiger prawns, a variety of crabs, and 3kg Phuket rainbow lobster. The restaurant holds up to 300, but the best seats offer views of the vibrant seafood market trading outside. Menu highlights include the fragrant stir-fried clams with chilli paste. A wooden terrace on the beach is also available.

Name: Jhol
Address: 7/2 Soi Sukhumvit 18, Sukhumvit Road, Khlong Toei, Bangkok, 10110, Thailand
Description: Indian-born, New York-based restaurateur Hari Nayak creates South Indian coastal cuisine rooted in his youth and transformed by his years of experience in world-class fine dining establishments; particularly representative is the delicious avocado mousse-filled Panipuri with passionfruit sauce. Meanwhile, the dining room balances vintage refinement with contemporary elegance and the beautiful Indian- and Thai-influenced cocktails are just as inspired.

Name: Khun Thip's Satay
Address: 184 Phet Kasem Road, Thai Chang, Mueang Phang-nga, Phang-Nga, 82000, Thailand
Description: Serving satay, and only satay, since 1975 – it’s now Phang-Nga’s iconic food. The 2-day marinated sauce smothers charcoal-grilled chicken, pork, pork intestine or shrimp. Our favourite is the tender pork satay with coconut aroma, rich peanut flavour and fresh cucumber relish.

Name: Blue Elephant
Address: 96 Krabi Road, Talat Nuea, Mueang Phuket, Phuket, 83000, Thailand
Description: Following the lead of Bangkok’s flagship, their colonial-style mansion with wood-panelled interior, wicker furnishings and louver shutters, set in lush gardens, pulls in the crowds. They serve a roll call of Thai classics, but the main attraction, the Peranakan Menu, for couples to share, is unique to Phuket. The signature Peranakan Tumee King Mackerel comes in large pieces of fish in a rich coconut curry with crispy okra. They also have a great cocktail selection.

Name: Chomjan
Address: 119/1 Mu 8, Niwatwithi Road, Kham Nam Chaep, Warin Chamrap, Ubon Ratchathani, 34190, Thailand
Description: On the banks of the Mun River, next to a 100-year-old bridge, sits Chomjan, popular with locals and non-locals enjoying penetrating sunsets, a fresh river breeze and live music across different themed dining areas. It caters for everyone, serving classic Thai, Isan and international dishes and fresh local fish. The deep-fried snakehead fish with stir-fried eggplant is recommended; the juicy giant catfish with fresh herbal soup is also delightful.

Name: Philippe
Address: 20/15-17 Soi Sukhumvit 39, Khlong Tan Nuea, Vadhana, Bangkok, 10110, Thailand
Description: Chef Philippe Peretti’s proudly by-the-book French cooking has been a feature of the city since 1997, so why try and change it? The décor, like the food, doesn’t sway into the innovative – dark wood panels, traditional furniture and white tablecloths give the dining room a traditionally elegant feel. The well-seasoned Burgundy snails are a treat, as is Philippe’s special chocolate soufflé. If you’re searching for the classical French experience, look no further.

Name: Charoen Saeng Silom
Address: 492/6 Soi Charoen Krung 49, Silom Road, Suriyawong, Bang Rak, Bangkok, 10500, Thailand
Description: Stewed in a rich, aromatic gravy with Chinese herbs, the soft, caramelised pork tantalises the tastebuds, and is a Bangkok favourite. The recipe, created by the owner’s grandfather in 1959, was adapted by her father. It’s served with a homemade spicy sauce and pickles and is great value.

Name: The Local
Address: 32 Soi Sukhumvit 23, Sukhumvit Road, Khlong Toei Nuea, Vadhana, Bangkok, 10110, Thailand
Description: This colonial-style building provides an elegant contrast with the skyscrapers of Bangkok. Its private dining rooms ooze old world charm, while the main restaurant has thick wicker chairs and artful murals. The secret family recipes pay homage to the diversity offered by Thailand’s regions. We recommend the deep-fried seabass: deboned and served in large slices with an intense sweet and sour sauce. The assortment of desserts with homemade ice-cream makes for a refreshing finish.

Name: Chef Man (Sathon)
Address: 3F, Eastin Grand Sathorn, 33/1 Sathon Tai Road, Yan Nawa, Sathon, Bangkok, 10120, Thailand
Description: Hongkonger Chef Man Wai Yi has a stellar reputation for ‘home-style’ Cantonese cuisine, delicious dim sum and legendary Peking duck. The mule duck, from a private local supplier, is roasted for 4 hours. His special recipe and sweet mango combine for a mouthwatering affair. The glutinous crispy shrimp with soya sauce is also good. The restaurant has a classical Chinese décor and each station in the large open kitchen is staffed by chefs from Hong Kong.

Name: Chakrabongse Dining
Address: 396/1 Maha Rat Road, Phra Borom Maha Ratchawang, Phra Nakhon, Bangkok, 10200, Thailand
Description: A spectacular setting, where views of the Chao Phraya River and Wat Arun provide the perfect backdrop to your culinary journey inside one of Bangkok’s most precious historic houses. Well-known for its delicate and authentic royal Thai cuisine, the menu offers a different set selection every day. Impressive dishes include river prawns in spicy and sour coconut broth with banana blossom and Chakrabongse roasted duck red curry with mixed fruits.

Name: Banya
Address: 317 Tiwanon Road, Talat Khwan, Mueang Nonthaburi, Nonthaburi, 11000, Thailand
Description: Banya, or ‘Grandma’s house’ in Thai, embodies this maternal spirit. The menu, conceived by acclaimed culinary teacher Rachadapa Amatayakul, comprises typical Thai fare, some rarer recipes and their famous homely signature – Khao Chae. Also popular is the homemade spotted knifefish with green curry; the tender fish is an umami pleasure in an intense mix of herbs broiled in rich Thai curry. No wonder this place is always crowded with locals and foreigners.

Name: Cuisine de Garden
Address: 99 Mu 11, Nong Khwai, Hang Dong, Chiang Mai, 50230, Thailand
Description: Self-taught Chef Nan uses a wide range of modern culinary techniques to transform local produce into seasonal lunch and dinner tasting menus. Both change according to what’s obtainable and are ambitious, playful, and delivered in a rapid cadence; a highlight is ‘Nest’, available year-round. Along with the cutting-edge cooking and theatrical presentation come sleek, modern Scandic décor and warm, friendly service. Enhance your experience with the wine pairing.

Name: The Ranch
Address: The Ritz-Carlton Koh Samui, 9/123 Mu 5, Bo Phut, Ko Samui, 84320, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Wheelchair access
Description: The Ranch at The Ritz-Carlton Koh Samui is the place for meat lovers and the only real steakhouse on the island. The premium Australian beef is dry-aged in-house and served on hot plates with a wide range of sauces and side dishes, without forgetting a knockout line-up of grilled dishes and seafood options. High ceilings, wooden furnishings and a splendid display of old and new world wines set the scene in the smart dining room.

Name: Kao Lao Siang Ji
Address: 8 Sathityutitham Road, Nai Mueang, Mueang Khon Kaen, Khon Kaen, 40000, Thailand
Description: Started 50 years ago in a hawker stall by the owner’s grandfather, this shop continues to serve delicious pork blood and offal soup following the founder’s recipe. Pork balls make a tasty addition; organs can be added or subtracted. Also recommended are the deep-fried shrimp wontons.

Name: Kaen
Address: 140/64 Adunyaram Soi 7, Nai Mueang, Mueang Khon Kaen, Khon Kaen, 40000, Thailand
Description: ‘Kaen’ in Thai is a homonym with many meanings. Owner Chef Paisarn, who worked as executive chef at a 5-star resort, infuses those meanings into this restaurant in his hometown (Khon Kaen). The cuisine is contemporary Thai at its core (kaen), yet also playful, (kaen kaew), as in the recommended Massaman curry with lamb shank. Even the dining room reflects it — a large table with exposed heartwood (kaen mai) made at his family’s wood shop is a centrepiece.

Name: Rabiang Patchanee
Address: 53/1 Bannon Road, Ban Lueam, Mueang Udon Thani, Udon Thani, 41000, Thailand
Description: Popular with local families, this restaurant focuses primarily on meat and freshwater fish, serving Chinese, Vietnamese, and Thai fare. They trade on authentic Thai flavours and daily specials featuring the freshest ingredients. The highlight dishes, which have been passed down for 30 years, are crispy duck topped with crab meat and gravy, and Vietnamese stuffed omelette. Make sure to book outdoor seats with a view of the pond.

Name: Baan Chik Pork Noodles
Address: 89/3-4 Naresoun Road, Mak Khaeng, Mueang Udon Thani, Udon Thani, 41000, Thailand
Description: This eatery has thrived in a traditional shophouse for over 30 years. Choose between the original flavour and tasty tom yum with its fresh lime and roasted peanut aroma, served with or without soup.

Name: Khanom Jeen Baan Bang Kan
Address: Mu 4, Mueang Phang-nga-Takua Pa Road, Thung Kha Ngok, Mueang Phang-nga, Phang-Nga, 82000, Thailand
Description: For over 20 years, locals have enjoyed this shop’s Khanom Jeen, or rice noodles, which are served with a choice of three curries and more than 20 types of fresh or pickled veggies. Noodles are unlimited, but save room for the refreshing cendol in coconut milk. Closed Thursday and Friday.

Name: Khanom Chin Pa Son
Address: 3 Borirak Bamrung Road, Thai Chang, Mueang Phang-nga, Phang-Nga, 82000, Thailand
Description: Across from a Chinese shrine, this self-service buffet has been drawing devotees for over 30 years with its tasty khanom chin and four curry options to mix and match. Pick from a wide range of condiments, fresh vegetables, boiled egg and crispy anchovies. Lunchtime is always busy, so arrive early.

Name: Jok's Kitchen (Pom Prap Sattru Phai)
Address: 23 Soi Charoen Krung 21, Phlapphla Chai Road, Pom Prap, Pom Prap Sattru Phai, Bangkok, 10100, Thailand
Description: In the debate between quality and quantity, this Thai-Chinese spot hidden in a wet market sides with quality. Starting with a single table, it has since expanded to five. The skilled chef, whose family has sold crabs for over 80 years, sources quality ingredients to create an Omakase set menu which he cooks chef’s table-style. The shrimp wonton, deep-fried snow fish with soy sauce and stir-fried kale with salted halibut are recommended. Booking is mandatory.

Name: Scarlett
Address: 37F, Pullman Hotel G, 188 Silom Road, Suriyawong, Bang Rak, Bangkok, 10500, Thailand
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Counter dining,Great view,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: Located on the top floor of the trendy Pullman Hotel, Scarlett offers a fashionable and lively spot to enjoy a creative cocktail and dine while the lights of Bangkok twinkle below. Alongside a list of classic French dishes, prime Australian steaks are broiled on the chargrill – the focal point of the lively open kitchen. Allow the knowledgeable staff to help you choose from the comprehensive list of reasonably priced wines. Desserts are a highlight so save room for something sweet.

Name: Jadjan
Address: 4/27 Sakdidet Road, Talat Nuea, Mueang Phuket, Phuket, 83000, Thailand
Description: Chef Suthee, a former 5-star hotel chef, uses expertise to produce simple southern Thai fare that’s packed with flavour. The crab meat curry with betel leaves and southern Thai sour curry with fresh local fish and pineapple get our nod of approval.

Name: Tempura Kanda
Address: 1F, Eight Thonglor Building  88/36, Sukhumvit 55 Road, Khlong Tan Nuea, Vadhana, Bangkok, 10110, Thailand
Description: This was one of the first omakase restaurants in the city, which means you’re placing your order in the hands of an experienced chef – in this case one with a mastery of tempura. Seasonal Japanese ingredients are imported, then carefully cooked. The batter is light and crispy, while the filling retains the produce’s natural flavours. The interior décor sticks to a simple approach, with a marble-topped counter adding some charm. Booking is essential.

Name: Somboon Seafood (Bang Rak)
Address: 169, 169/7-12 Surawong Road, Suriyawong, Bang Rak, Bangkok, 10500, Thailand
Description: Known for its fried crab curry, Somboon first put its name on the global culinary map in 1969. Fresh ingredients, impeccable cooking and reasonable prices keep it there. They now have 8 branches around town, but this is the best and the largest, seating up to 200 people. In addition to their famous crab curry, we recommend the deep-fried seabass with sweet fish sauce and Thai seafood spicy soup. Flawlessly fresh seafood and generous portions.

Name: Thana Ocha
Address: 29 Ratchawong Road, Chang Moi, Mueang Chiang Mai, Chiang Mai, 50300, Thailand
Description: Every day at lunch long lines form in front of this decades-old shop selling Hakka-style noodles. House-made Hakka stuffed tofu, fish sausage and crispy wontons find their way into every dish including tom yum noodles and the classic Yentafo. The latter is highly recommended, with a well-seasoned soup made from fermented bean curd and fresh chilli.

Name: 5 SEN:SES by Mario Aliberti
Description: A fine addition to Karlsruhe's culinary scene. Chef-patron Mario Aliberti fuses Italian cuisine with international – especially Asian – and regional influences. A wide range of dishes is available: Lunchtime features four different moderately priced set menus (individual courses can also be ordered separately), along with additional à la carte options. In the evening, the array of options includes the "Fine Dining Menu", the "Italian Menu" and the "Menü Sharing", as well as an extensive à la carte selection. You can also order whole fish and different cuts of meat. There really is something for everyone's taste! The well-stocked wine list is worth a look, too. The interior is modern and inviting, with a distinct lounge feel. In summer, head for the quiet terrace laid out right in front of the restaurant.

Name: GLORIE
Description: Almost a restaurant within a restaurant. On a mezzanine with a limited number of tables and a bird's-eye view of the open kitchen – practically directly above 100/200 Kitchen – owner Thomas Alfons Imbusch presents his second culinary concept: "Old school, reimagined".
