Address: via Andreas Hofer 23, Termeno sulla Strada del Vino, 39040, Italy
Location: Termeno sulla Strada del Vino, Italy
Description: An attractive, well-kept restaurant in a historic building with a romantic, rural feel, especially in the beautiful garden. Although the menu is not that extensive, the chef is highly skilled, and it doesn’t feel as though anything is missing here. The dishes reflect the flavours of the region, making use of local ingredients such as venison and asparagus from Termeno accompanied by home-produced speck ham. The menu also features a couple of fish-based recipes and all dishes are modern and imaginative in style. Beautiful guestrooms are also available.

Name: Da Guido
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: The story of this restaurant began in 1967, when Guido and Giovanna Fasan, both of whom still work front of house, met in Germany. They then moved back to Italy, where they opened Da Guido in the early 1990s. White dominates in the elegant, contemporary-style dining room, while the cuisine features delicious seafood dishes with a focus on grilled specialities. In summer, there’s a welcoming bar in the garden, which boasts a romantic atmosphere. Together with other restaurant-owners from Venice, the Fasan family also have a kitchen garden on the Venetian island of Sant’Erasmo, where they focus on sustainable growing methods.

Name: La Valle
Address: via Umberto I 25, località Valle Sauglio, Trofarello, 10028, Italy
Description: A well - run restaurant in a quiet area just outside the village, where the owner - chef serves modern cuisine with the occasional regional influence. Careful attention is given to the use of seasonal produce and natural herbs, and there is a small selection of fish - based dishes.

Name: La Sponda
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Terrace
Description: An elegant restaurant within Le Sirenuse, one of the most prestigious and glamorous hotels on the Amalfi coast, with an attractive outdoor terrace for summer dining with views of Positano’s colourful houses clinging to the cliff face. Whether you choose to eat inside or out, a romantic atmosphere is guaranteed thanks to the hundreds of candles lit every evening. At the helm, Neapolitan chef Gennaro Russo maintains the restaurant’s high standards with his Mediterranean dishes, often influenced by Campania and inspired by classic favourites. The flavours of southern Italy are showcased in delicious dishes such as lemon risotto with capers.

Name: Oberwirt
Description: The various Stube-style dining rooms in the Oberwirt hotel restaurant have a typical Tyrolean ambience, while the cuisine is decidedly traditional with its focus on seasonal and regional ingredients, although a few fish options also always feature on the menu. Wine-enthusiasts will be delighted with the excellent wine selection.

Name: La Coccinella
Description: Three brothers, all of them experts, are the enthusiastic managers of this very fine restaurant. Recent renovation has increased the comfort and popularity of the place. The cuisine is Piedmontese.

Name: Le Lampare al Fortino
Address: via Tiepolo, molo Sant'Antonio, Trani, 76125, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Great view,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Built over a medieval church, this old fort that once guarded the port has become the enviable location of a restaurant. It serves delicious fish and seafood specialities with the distinct flavour of Puglia.

Name: Braunwirt
Description: A modern and welcoming restaurant in the heart of the town, where the modern design is echoed by the contemporary cuisine which combines regional dishes with influences from elsewhere in Italy. Food-lovers will enjoy creating their own tasting menu by choosing dishes from the à la carte. Friendly service and a cosmopolitan clientele.

Name: Boccadoro
Description: Situated on the outskirts of Padova, this classically elegant restaurant is very popular with locals – and for good reason! The menu includes skilfully prepared dishes influenced by the traditions of the Veneto (from bigoli pasta to dried cod and liver Venetian-style) as well as a selection of grilled options.

Name: La Locanda del Notaio
Address: Via Piano delle Noci 42, Pellio Intelvi, 22024, Italy
Description: An elegant restaurant with a warm atmosphere embellished by a central fireplace. Chef Marco Moretto creates modern dishes which are elegant and balanced, with a focus on seasonal produce from the region and elsewhere – in this region of lakes, just a stone’s throw from Switzerland, you’ll be surprised by the fragrant seafood specialities which feature on the menu alongside freshwater fish dishes.

Name: Bon Wei
Description: China on a plate! This attractive restaurant with an intriguing decor combining elegance, modern style and Asian influences serves a wide selection of Chinese specialities. Dishes include appetisers, dumplings, noodles and meat options, as well as a huge array of specialities from eight different regions, from the spicy dishes of Szechuan to the delicate flavours of Zhejiang.

Name: Colonne
Address: via Fincarà 37, Santa Maria del Monte, 21100, Italy
Description: Beautiful views of Lake Varese and its surrounding countryside, especially from the attractive summer terrace. At lunchtime, the upper section of the restaurant houses the bistro, while the elegant dining room provides the backdrop for more creative cuisine in the evening. Chef Silvio Battistoni is very well known in the region.

Name: MikEle
Description: Located in a residential district on the edge of town, this unexpected, elegant fish restaurant offers a refreshing change from the typical boiled meat dishes of Modena. Guests can choose their fish from the display cabinet, with classic Italian seafood recipes taking pride of place on the menu.

Name: Kleine Flamme
Description: In his small open-view kitchen situated in the centre of this restaurant, chef Bacher Burkhard develops his vision of fusion cuisine with energy and precision, combining flavours from Italy and the Alto Adige with Asian spices and techniques to create delicious and imaginative dishes. His tuna tataki is superb, seasoned with salty lemon oil and accompanied by intriguing bitter herbs that (as Professor Montanari has noted in a recent book) are particularly popular with Italians. The chef’s wife Annelies works front of house, where she looks after guests in a friendly and professional manner.

Name: Lapprodo
Address: via Roma 22, Vibo Valentia Marina, 89900, Italy
Description: Definitely one of the most reliable restaurants in this area, Vibo Valentia Marina overlooks Vibo Marina port and is the perfect choice for anyone keen on classic Mediterranean cuisine with a focus on fish (most of which is caught locally), although meat dishes also feature on the menu. The restaurant also offers guestrooms in its Cala del Porto hotel.

Name: Bacco e Arianna
Address: via Circonvallazione 1, Trezzano sul Naviglio, 20090, Italy
Description: Enjoy attentive service from the female owner in this small modern restaurant situated on the outskirts of Milan. The cuisine has an equal focus on meat and fish – our inspector particularly enjoyed the lobster roll with avocado, celeriac and pan brioche, as well as the roasted scallops with lentils, salicornia and creamed potatoes. An interesting and reasonably priced lunch menu is available at midday.

Name: La Chiocciola
Address: via Runco 94/f, Quartiere di Portomaggiore, 44015, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: A restaurant and an inn in a small country village, it’s the right place if you’re looking for hospitality and you appreciate the regional cuisine, made of snails and frogs, but also fish from the nearby sea. Something for every palate.

Name: Osteria Numero Sette
Description: There’s been a recent change in management at this informal, friendly restaurant which serves generously portioned, carefully prepared dishes from the region and elsewhere in Italy, all at highly competitive prices. Although the cuisine might not be particularly modern, this is good solid cuisine served in a welcoming atmosphere.

Name: LeoneFelice Vista Lago
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Terrace
Description: The new chef at this restaurant focuses on highlighting produce grown in the property’s own kitchen garden, as well as meat from the farm in the Grosseto area that is also run by the Andana estate. The classic-style cuisine on the à la carte features occasional personalised touches (for example, aubergines baked in fig leaf with oregano, and perch or sea bass fillet served with coloured beets and soft potato), while in the evening a tasting menu is served in a dedicated part of the restaurant. The expertly explained wine list focuses on the estate’s own labels and the Franciacorta region in general, yet at the same time includes a selection of wines from elsewhere in Italy and further afield.

Name: Da Giovanni
Description: The 18C ceramic stove, bright, colourful decor (both period and vintage), long family tradition and excellent cuisine all contribute to making this restaurant which opened half a century ago a bastion of fine cuisine in Piacenza and the wider Po valley. Meat and fish both feature on the menu, although it is the latter that has become renowned as the restaurant’s speciality over the years. The excellent service is friendly and informal yet highly professional, while the extensive wine list also includes a good selection of wines by the glass.

Name: Darmagi
Description: Small villa in secluded position with warm, homely atmosphere, especially in the nice room with fireplace. The range of cuisine is rich in tradition.

Name: L'A Gourmet L'Accademia
Address: via Largo C. Colombo 6, Reggio Calabria, 89125, Italy
Description: From the classic restaurant on the first floor (no lift) of this early 20C palazzo, you’ll enjoy fine views of the sea and the Strait of Messina. Here, skilled chef Filippo Cogliardo prepares fish-based dishes which include classic recipes (raw seafood and amberjack with rapini) as well as more modern options (cuttlefish tagliatelle with avocado cream, cucumber and salted lemon). A few meat dishes also feature on the menu. Definitely the best restaurant in town!

Name: La Fugascina Ristorante
Description: Situated on a small square with an attractive outdoor space, this restaurant offers a menu which features fish from the lake and other seasonal produce prepared with both modern and traditional techniques, but always with a contemporary flair. The focus is on locally sourced (zero-mile, wherever possible) produce.

Name: Riso Amaro
Description: This elegant, contemporary-style restaurant is situated right in the historic centre. The menu features a host of gourmet dishes as well as more modern fish and meat options, all created by the talented owner-chef.

Name: Al Capitan della Cittadella
Description: Situated just outside the town walls, Al Capitan has been one of the most renowned fish restaurants in Verona for over fifteen years. Classic Italian dishes with a contemporary twist added by the owner-chef take pride of place here, with an emphasis on top-quality ingredients. The wine list includes a good selection of French wines, with a particular focus on champagnes.

Name: Trattoria alla Pergola
Description: An old-fashioned trattoria with a simple, homely atmosphere which attracts guests from all over the province who are drawn here by the classic, unfussy regional cuisine. Although the menu is concise, it includes specialities such as tortelli, tortellini, the region’s famous risottos (this is rice-growing country) and renowned boiled meats. Make sure you leave room for the tempting dessert trolley.

Name: Hosteria Giusti
Description: Situated in an attractive retro-style room to the rear of an elegant delicatessen, this restaurant offers just four tables and a restricted menu of top-quality, traditional Emilian dishes. In the evening, the restaurant is open by reservation only for groups of at least 12 people with a pre-arranged menu.

Name: Trattoria I Masenini
Description: Situated in an attractive part of Verona right opposite the famous Castelvecchio, this restaurant boasts a relaxing ambience with wood ceilings, classic yet informal furnishings, subtle lighting and soft background music. The menu features regional dishes alongside typical Italian fare, as well as the house speciality – meat kebabs cooked on a skewer. There’s also an outdoor space for alfresco dining in summer.

Name: Giorgio e Flora
Address: via Baldonò 1, lago di Velo d'Astico, Velo, 36010, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Terrace
Description: This small chalet - style villa overlooks the valley. It has an attractive, elegant and quiet dining room decorated with a feminine touch and a panoramic outdoor terrace. Modern cuisine from the Veneto takes pride of place on the menu.

Name: Quellenhof Gourmetstube 1897
Address: via Passiria 47, Saint Martin in Passeier, 39010, Italy
Description: Situated in a refined and elegant setting (also home to an intimate private dining area separated from the main room by a few steps), this new gourmet restaurant offers various tasting menus with a distinctly creative flavour.

Name: Marcandole
Description: This restaurant managed with passion has become a cornerstone of Treviso restaurants thanks to a fish cuisine contaminated by contemporary inspirations. Do not miss the raw specialties!

Name: Gino Sorbillo
Description: Situated along the "via della pizza", this historic restaurant boasts a simple yet lively ambience with a local and international feel. Excellent pizzas made from quality - label produce. You’ll need plenty of patience if you’re here at busy times and if you choose to share a table, you’ll really enjoy the convivial atmosphere!

Name: Menegaldo
Address: via Pralongo 216, Monastier di Treviso, 31050, Italy
Description: This restaurant, once referred to as “l’osteria dei cava’i” in reference to the cart drivers and their horses who used to stop here after the First World War, has a history dating back 100 years. Now specialising in fish and shellfish from the Adriatic, Menegaldo has become one of the area’s most popular restaurants.

Name: Al Fogher
Address: strada statale 117 bis, Piazza Armerina, 94015, Italy
Description: This small, rustic-style restaurant just outside the centre of Piazza Armerina serves personalised cuisine in which local ingredients take pride of place. Influences from elsewhere in Italy are also evident, with dishes such as artichoke pansotti (stuffed pasta) with local tuma cheese and black truffles on the menu.

Name: Trattoria di Coronate
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Housed in a splendid 16C farmhouse just a few minutes from the beautiful Morimondo abbey, this restaurant has an elegant and friendly ambience. The wooden ceiling and furniture in the dining room gives it a warm and welcoming feel, while the cuisine, deeply rooted in the region, is reinterpreted with a contemporary twist. The delicious options on the menu include highlights such as quail breast with a thigh-meat “lollipop” and ravioli stuffed with braised beef.

Name: Muraglia - Conchiglia d'Oro
Description: Here, choose between the simply furnished, bright dining room with a proudly vintage feel that dates back to its opening in the 1970s and a tiny yet attractive terrace with sea views (there are just a few tables, so it’s best to book in advance). Fish has always been – and still is – the house speciality, with fresh, top-quality dishes simply prepared according to classic methods such as the barbecue grill visible in the dining room. The fish is so fresh that the handwritten menu changes daily.

Name: Gratschwirt
Description: Housed in a building which dates back to the 16C and is part of the hotel of the same name, this Stube-style restaurant at the foot of the Tre Cime is typical of the Alto Adige, as is the simple, abundant regional cuisine served here. Highlights on the menu include dumplings in broth, herb-crusted lamb, apple strudel and the less traditional but excellent beef tartare which is seasoned at your table.

Name: L'Archivolto - Osteria Nostrale
Description: Situated on Ovada’s main square, this restaurant has the pleasant friendly ambience of an attractive trattoria, while its menu takes guests on a delicious culinary journey through the Piedmont region, including local specialities such as home-made tajarin pasta, braised beef in Ovada wine with mashed potato, and the local bunet dessert (finanziera stew also makes an occasional appearance). The restaurant is also a wine bar/boutique offering a selection of wines, including different Barolo labels (presented area by area) and aperitifs served both at lunchtime and dinner.

Name: Trita Pepe
Address: via Gabriele D'Annunzio 4, Manoppello Scalo, 65024, Italy
Description: Situated on the road that passes through Manoppello Scalo, this restaurant with a car park right in front of the building boasts a spacious, simple dining room and is our recommended choice in the region for anyone keen to try typical Abruzzo cuisine. Meat takes pride of place among the main courses (with an exception for salted cod), while menu highlights include excellent fried gnocchi with local salumi and cheese.

Name: Bistrot de Venise
Address: calle dei Fabbri 4685, sestiere San Marco, Venice, 30124, Italy
Description: Diners will enjoy the lengthy wine list (available by the glass) and "historical" cuisine at this restaurant in a location known for its atmosphere.

Name: Io Osteria Personale
Description: The young owner of this restaurant has an interesting background – a former vet with a passion for food. He has opened one of the most fascinating restaurants in Florence, serving original dishes to diners looking for a change from more traditional fare.

Name: Hidalgo
Description: Although fish dishes also feature on the menu, Hidalgo has long enjoyed a reputation for its excellent meat options thanks to its different cuts of steak and beef sourced from all around the world and cooked mainly (but not exclusively) on the barbecue grill. In a separate room(Aomi, a kind of restaurant within the restaurant), guests can choose from a menu dedicated uniquely (from antipasti to main courses) to Japanese Wagyubeef.

Name: La Martinatica
Description: Housed in an old mill, this restaurant boasts a warm and welcoming dining room crowned by wood beams and elegant furnishings. The menu offers a selection of meat and fish dishes, although the latter are the main speciality of the owner-chef, who can usually be seen taking orders in the dining room. The raw seafood option demonstrates the skill and imagination of the chef, with its array of small bites which are both creative and delicious. The attractive outdoor space is perfect for summer dining.

Name: Rezzano Cucina e Vino
Address: via Asilo Maria Teresa 34, Sestri Levante, 16039, Italy
Description: This restaurant is constantly improving and now boasts a comfortable dining room, which has been slightly enlarged thanks to a few adjustments and a reduction in the number of guests allowing for more space between tables. The cuisine pays careful attention to the seasons and to local traditions, with a particular focus on top-quality fish. The small outdoor space in the piazza makes a pleasant setting for dinner.

Name: Il Melograno
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Wheelchair access
Description: In the village centre and therefore not right by the sea, this successful, well - established restaurant is decorated in elegant contemporary style. The menu focuses on fish dishes reinterpreted with a touch of imagination.

Name: Villa Giulia - Al Terrazzo
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: Housed within an elegant late-19C hotel overlooking the lake, this romantic restaurant offers stunning views from its outdoor terrace. The cuisine is mainly Italian, with the occasional modern and imaginative twist. Add in a charming stone wine cellar stocked with top-quality labels, plus modern guestrooms for anyone wanting to prolong their stay.

Name: Umberto a Mare
Description: Situated in a breathtaking location below the Chiesa del Soccorso, this restaurant boasts views of the sea and sunset that are hard to beat, while its fine, elegant cuisine, based on updated Campanian recipes, is more than a match for the spectacular setting. Featuring delicious dishes such as tagliatelle with squid, lemon and soya milk, a reinterpreted version of parmigiana, “mescafrancesca” (mixed pasta) with prawns and Controne beans, and a mouthwatering dessert trolley, Umberto is one of the island’s unmissable restaurants. The impressive wine cellar (which can be visited) is home to more than 1 000 labels, including a fine selection of champagnes.

Name: Da Gigi
Address: piazza IV Novembre 4, Crandola Valsassina, 23832, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Great view,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus
Description: Enjoy specialities from Valsassina in this friendly restaurant in a panoramic location. There is a rustic ambience in the dining room with cuisine focusing on local ingredients (many of which are organic), and produce from the restaurant’s own garden.

Name: Alla Laguna - Vedova Raddi
Description: Situated in a charming small town criss-crossed by canals, this restaurant serves traditionally inspired fish-based dishes. The restaurant stands on the port facing the fish market, so it’s no surprise that the fish served here is of the freshest quality.

Name: Corte Visconti
Description: A classical, rustic style environment with walls in stone and brick vaulted or wood and stone ceilings. The cuisine is authentically local but with a pleasant touch of creativity.

Name: La Terrazza
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Great view,Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Wheelchair access
Description: Situated on the rooftop of the Eden hotel, this modern restaurant boasts enchanting views of the historic centre of Rome, from the Quirinale to St Peter’s. At the helm in the kitchen, Salvatore Bianco creates two imaginative tasting menus from which dishes can also be chosen à la carte style. A superb fine-dining experience overlooking the rooftops of Rome.

Name: Corte Sconta
Address: calle del Pestrin, sestiere Castello 3886, Venice, 30122, Italy
Description: From its flooring to its tables, this restaurant has the charming, nostalgic feel of a typical trattoria in its simple dining room, while the outdoor space in an inner courtyard under a vine-shaded arbour is a charming place to eat in fine weather – a real gem right in the centre of Venice. The cuisine is as simple in style as the decor, with traditional Venetian fish and seafood dishes taking pride of place on the menu.

Name: Trattoria Glisenti
Description: Situated on the lakefront with beautiful views from its terrace, this restaurant focuses on freshwater fish, while also serving a selection of classic regional specialities. Careful attention is paid to natural ingredients, with vegetarian options also available. An elegant restaurant which belies its description as a “trattoria”.

Name: Sapereta
Address: via Provinciale Ovest 73, località Mola, Porto Azzurro, 57036, Italy
Description: Housed in a historic winery, this simple, rustic - style restaurant is surrounded by a well - kept garden where farmyard animals roam freely. Don’t be fooled by appearances, however – the cuisine here is modern, with meat dishes taking pride of place on the menu.

Name: La Filanda
Description: Housed on the first floor of an old silkworm factory, with a contemporary-style dining room that opens out on to a beautiful terrace in fine weather, this restaurant is one of the few in the province to serve top-quality fish and seafood, including a good selection of raw options. The cooked dishes on offer demonstrate a light modern touch and are prepared whenever possible using vegetables from the restaurant’s own garden.

Name: Due Pini
Address: via Spinale 37/bis, Madonna di Campiglio, 38086, Italy
Description: Although recently restored, this restaurant has retained its strong Alpine character. The cuisine is regional in style and reinterpreted with an imaginative and contemporary twist.

Name: Enoteca Del Duca
Description: Despite the change of ownership at this centrally located restaurant right behind the castle and the main square, there’s a certain continuity to the cuisine which remains focused on classic dishes with a regional flavour (with the option of steak on the menu). The dining room features old stone walls, plus there’s also an attractive outdoor space for summer dining.

Name: La Cantinella
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Great view,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: A little country restaurant with pleasantly distinctive interiors and summer service al fresco on the terrace. Traditional Tuscan cuisine on the menu, with a modern touch.

Name: La Lumira
Description: Situated in a village famous for its “tortellino in brodo” dish, Lumira serves Emilian cuisine with a modern twist. Highlights on the menu include fresh home-made pasta such as traditional tortellini and modern tagliatelle verdi with a beef and pea ragù, as well as the highly recommended veal fillet in a traditional balsamic vinegar sauce, which is full of intense flavours. Contemporary decor and welcoming service add to the relaxing dining experience. Among the Sangiovesi wines from Romagna on the wine list, we recommend Lillybet, a well-structured red with superb floral notes.

Name: Trattoria Ceriati
Address: Località Cangelasio Ceriati 18, Salsomaggiore Terme, 43039, Italy
Description: Situated in attractive countryside where the plains give way to rolling hills (a perfect destination for a Sunday outing), this simple yet well-kept trattoria serves all the usual traditional local specialities. The typical fresh pasta and the desserts are all home-made.

Name: Villa Arcadio
Address: via Palazzina 2, località Villa di Salò, Salò, 25087, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Terrace
Description: The new chef at this restaurant prioritises beautiful presentation in his modern interpretations of Italian dishes, which are even more enjoyable in summer when meals are served outdoors, surrounded by greenery and with fine views of the southern part of Lake Garda and its shoreline.

Name: Cascina Vittoria
Description: Situated in a rural setting surrounded by rice fields outside Milan, this restaurant specialises in home-made pasta and breads, vegetables grown in its own garden, and Piedmontese meat cooked in traditional fashion over a barbecue grill. Takeaway produce is also available for purchase.

Name: Il Favri
Address: via Borgo Meduna 12, San Giorgio della Richinvelda, 33095, Italy
Description: This inn, which has been serving food since the early 19C, boasts a warm atmosphere with a rustic feel. The beautiful garden makes a delightful setting in fine weather, while the cuisine focuses on traditional dishes from Friuli, such as “frico” (potato, onion and cheese fritter) and cured ham.

Name: Il Trillo
Description: Situated in the hills overlooking the town, this restaurant occupies an old house that is also home to the estate’s wine cellars. Charming setting and cuisine full of flavour, with the option of alfresco dining on the panoramic terrace in summer.

Name: I Tigli
Description: An iconic pizzeria which has brought Italy’s favourite street-food snack right up to date! With almost 30 years’ experience behind him, Simone Padoan knows how to make difficult things easy: he uses a mix of wholemeal flours and pays meticulous attention to natural leavening processes to create a dough which has a crispy crust yet soft interior. He also focuses on different types of toppings, including fish, meat and vegetables – whether your preference is for traditional or more imaginative pizzas, every option is of the highest quality. A choice of excellent desserts provides the perfect conclusion to your meal!

Name: Tola Rasa
Description: Having mastered his culinary repertoire working in other restaurants, the chef at the elegant and minimalist Tola Rasa creates successful reinterpretations of classic Italian dishes by adding exotic spices and other ingredients (often from Asia) to his dishes. The gourmet dining room on the ground floor is supplemented by a wine bar in the annexe which serves a selection of snacks. Book a table facing the kitchen to watch the chef at work!

Name: Pacifico
Description: Although its dining rooms are fairly small, this restaurant, which acts as an ambassador for Peruvian cuisine with the occasional Asian influence, has an attractive, trendy ambience and a theatrical feel. Excellent choice of ceviche – raw fish or seafood dishes marinated in lemon and flavoured with spices such as chilli pepper and coriander – which are a typical speciality of Latin American countries along the Pacific coast.

Name: La Cantina di Manuela
Description: The dining room in this young, dynamic restaurant is surrounded by bottles of wine. Elaborate dishes feature on the menu, with antipasti available in the evening. At lunchtime these are replaced by various salads aimed at a business clientele in a hurry. Milanese-style cutlets are the house speciality.

Name: Voltalacarta
Description: A tiny doorway leads to this simple, friendly and intimate restaurant with just a few tables, where booking in advance is highly recommended given the restaurant’s excellent reputation in the city. Its renown stems from the owner-chef’s cuisine, which focuses mainly on top-quality fish prepared in imaginative and personalised recipes using classic techniques. If it’s on the menu, make sure you try the “cappon magro” (a type of seafood salad), which is so good that it even has its own identity card!

Name: Opera|02
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: A farm with rooms, a spa, a bistro and a gourmet restaurant! At the latter, enjoy regional cuisine with a creative twist added by the chef, on two tasting menus that can be modified as required. Don’t miss the chocolate soufflé served with hazelnut ice cream and caramel sauce. The farm’s own produce can also be purchased here.

Name: La Filanda
Description: Situated in the heart of the historic centre, this restaurant occupies an old spinning mill ("filanda")  that has been completely restored without losing any of its original charm. Here, self-taught chef Barbara serves traditional dishes reinterpreted with real flair, such as the involtino di ciaffagnone filled with Maremma beef on a bed of melted pecorino cheese and crispy leek. The chef’s husband oversees the wine list, which includes a selection of Tuscan labels.

Name: Da Noemi
Description: The mother of the current owner opened this busy restaurant in a medieval alleyway in the historic centre, giving it her own name. The historic dishes here reflect the culinary traditions of Ferrara, with specialities such as salama da sugo (pork sausage) and pasticcio di maccheroni (a baked pasta dish) on the menu. A must for anyone looking to sample local dishes already famous during the time of the Este family.

Name: Da Bibe
Description: Immortalised by the Italian writer Montale in his poetry, this trattoria has been run by the same family for almost two centuries. The menu features traditional Tuscan dishes, such as pici pasta with wild boar sauce. Alfresco dining in summer. There are also apartments with kitchens for guests that wish to extend their stay.

Name: Il Liberty
Description: Occupying an Art Nouveau-style palazzo, this small restaurant with two rooms and a loft area has a friendly, welcoming atmosphere. The menu includes a selection of fish and meat dishes.

Name: Punta Lena
Address: via Monsignor Di Mattina 8, località Ficogrande, Stromboli, 98055, Italy
Description: At this restaurant, dine under a pergola with superb views of the sea and Strombolicchio – the perfect setting for any occasion. The menu focuses on fish, including raw and dry-aged fish options. The first courses have a local flavour and are particularly delicious.

Name: Il Merlo
Address: via Bernardini 660, Lido di Camaiore, 55041, Italy
Description: Situated right on the beach, Il Merlo boasts a welcoming dining room decorated in elegant, contemporary style. The owner is at the helm in the kitchen, where he creates dishes with a focus on fish and seafood, such as the raw seafood platter and the salt-baked catch of the day. A few delicious meat options, such as plin pasta and pigeon, are also available.

Name: Battipalo
Description: A young couple opened this attractive restaurant next to the ferry dock some years ago. The large windows offer romantic views of the lake, while the distinctly modern cuisine focuses on meat and fish alike. Excellent care has been taken in selecting the wine list. There is also a pleasant outdoor area for alfresco dining.

Name: Il Capestrano
Address: via Gian Francesco Pizzi 14, Milan, 20141, Italy
Description: This restaurant takes its name from the warrior statue dating back to the 6C BC which was discovered in Capestrano (Aquila province) in 1934. The statue, carved from a single block of local stone, is one of the most mysterious finds in history. No such mystery surrounds the dishes served in this restaurant, which focuses on cuisine from the Abruzzo, including top-quality hams and cheeses produced by small-scale producers, as well as mutton, lamb, beef, barbecued lamb kebabs and other culinary delights.

Name: Meltemi
Description: A maritime focused oasis in a city where the traditional specialities revolve around meat, this restaurant serves fish dishes with various options ranging from raw fish to antipasti. Pleasant ambience with an attractive modern decor.

Name: Trattoria del Vicolo
Description: Overlooking the piazza for almost 50 years, this restaurant has been modernised but has nonetheless managed to retain its friendly ambience, especially in the outdoor space facing the narrow alleyway. The owner-chef serves regional specialities reinterpreted with his own individual twist, such as his famous swordfish rolls served in a type of pie.

Name: Casa D'Angelo
Address: via San Nicola 5, Fara Filiorum Petri, 66010, Italy
Description: Housed in what was once an old family home, this elegant restaurant serves delicious regional cuisine. The menu includes dishes that have been skilfully and imaginatively enhanced by the chef, such as warm pheasant terrine with apple, alongside more traditional fare, from cured ham to charcoal-grilled local lamb and potato gnocchi with a duck sauce. The restaurant’s own extra-virgin olive oil often adds further flavour to the dishes. The 4-course tasting menu deserves a special mention for its excellent value for money.

Name: Ba Restaurant
Description: Two huge red lamps welcome guests to this minimalist-style restaurant decorated in dark, typically Asian colours. The carefully prepared cuisine focuses on modern, reinterpreted Chinese dishes, while the wine list also includes a good selection of wines by the glass.

Name: Taverna Kus
Address: contrada Castello 14, San Zeno di Montagna, 37010, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: An attractive restaurant situated on the western slopes of Monte Baldo overlooking Lake Garda, with a number of rustic yet elegant and welcoming dining rooms, including a bright veranda with partial views of the lake (enjoy the full vista from the outdoor terrace). Various culinary options feature on the menu, including meat, fish and vegetarian dishes, all colourful, full of flavour and beautifully cooked and prepared using mainly local and seasonal ingredients. The well-stocked and carefully chosen wine list deserves a special mention: among the 1 000 or more bottles stored in the old giasàra (underground cellar), you’re sure to find something you’ll enjoy.

Name: La Taverna di Fra' Fiusch
Description: Nestling in a charming hill town, this restaurant will delight visitors looking for traditional cuisine with an updated, contemporary flavour. Specialities include agnolotti (a type of ravioli) and Piedmontese fritto misto (fried seafood and vegetables).

Name: Il Ristorante - Niko Romito
Address: via Privata Fratelli Gabba 7/b, Milan, 20121, Italy
Description: Housed within the Bulgari hotel, a secluded haven of elegance right in the heart of the most exclusive district in Milan, this restaurant alternates the trusted chefs at its helm, all of whom continue to serve light, contemporary Italian cuisine in dishes that focus more on substance than form. Choose between tasting menus and a generous à la carte selection featuring meat and fish dishes alike, including classic local favourites such as risotto and vitello alla Milanese (breaded veal cutlet).

Name: Orto
FacilitiesAndServices: Brunch,Car park,Garden or park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: Orto is the restaurant of the delightful Nina Trulli resort. In its beautiful Mediterranean courtyard, enjoy personalised, well-presented dishes where meat and fish are balanced by the use of fruit and vegetables, many of which come from the restaurant’s own kitchen garden and orchard. Reservation strongly recommended.

Name: Profumi di Cous Cous
Address: via Regina Margherita 80, San Vito lo Capo, 91010, Italy
Description: As the name of this restaurant suggests, couscous takes pride of place on the menu, although other Sicilian specialities can also be sampled here. Delightful atmosphere, especially in summer when meals are served in the internal courtyard among the citrus trees.

Name: Da Nicolo
Description: Located in an advantageous spot along the promenade, where there is a summer dining area, this restaurant is really patronized for the quality of its food. Serving seafood and Carlofortinian specialties.

Name: Lo Scalco Grasso
Description: A small, intimate restaurant with a welcoming ambience and simple yet lively feel, where the owner-chef at the helm in the kitchen also makes an appearance front of house. Mantuan traditions are evident in the generous portion sizes as well as in dishes such as the legendary pumpkin tortelli (served with butter or a tomato and sausage sauce), while other options are more creative in style – the Emilian lamb tartare delicately flavoured with its own cooking juices, and served with sautéed chard, savoury sbrisolona cake and black truffles from the lower Mantova region in season is particularly delicious.

Name: Ca' Apollonio Gourmet
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list
Description: This restaurant is housed in the Salone delle Colombe (the name comes from the fresco of doves on the ceiling) of a villa which dates back to the 16C, although its present appearance dates mainly from the 19C. Here, chef Alessio Longhini serves two tasting menus prepared partly using ingredients from the property’s own kitchen garden, which is surrounded by 18ha of grounds. Elaborate, creative and top-quality dishes served in an elegant setting.

Name: Locanda dei Salinari
Description: In the old village of Salinari, a young enterprising chef runs this simple restaurant. His creative cuisine is prepared with the best regional produce of Romagna.

Name: Essenziale
Address: piazza di Cestello 3 r, Florence, 50124, Italy
Description: As its name suggests, this restaurant (once a garage) on Piazza di Cestello has a young, minimalist ambience. The welcome and service here are friendly, while the cuisine is never ordinary, offering combinations that are pleasantly contrasting without being too bold. The chef, who is originally from Livorno, is particularly adept at creating fish and seafood dishes. You’ll find your cutlery in a drawer in your table, in an interesting nod to household traditions of bygone days.

Name: L'Antico Giardino
Description: Choose from an interesting, traditional à la carte and two tasting menus (one autumn-based, the other traditional, both excellent value for money) at this comfortable restaurant, where guests are welcomed by the friendly owner who is on hand to offer wine pairing recommendations. The menu features meat tartares and flans, agnolotti and ravioli pasta, and superbly cooked, top-quality cuts of meat, with truffles often making an appearance in season. We visited in autumn and particularly enjoyed the pumpkin cappellaccio with butter, sage and almonds – a dish that stood out for its delicious, creamy flavours.

Name: Stella d'Italia
Description: Regional specialities, including snails and pike, in a historical establishment, once an inn now an elegant establishment under the management of Signor Umberto.

Name: La Braseria
Description: This restaurant is a paradise for meat-eaters – its signature dishes are prime cuts of meat (mostly beef) from different breeds, which are displayed in the refrigerated cabinet at the entrance. There’s an extensive à la carte, with various appetiser options and a small choice of “primi”, but all the attention here is on the main course. The meat is either smoked and grilled over beech wood or roasted in the wood-fired oven – there’s something here for every taste! A cheese selection and delicious desserts complete the picture.

Name: De Gustibus - Maurizio
Description: Simple, modern fish dishes full of flavour take centre stage at this family-run restaurant in the charming historic centre of Palmi. The raw fish dishes served here include a delicious carpaccio made with the catch of the day and seasoned with a delicate home-made vinaigrette and cherry tomatoes, while the “Intrusi” menu offers three or four meat options for non-fish eaters. Desserts are announced at your table and always include a delicious cannolo. The wine list features mainly Italian labels, as well as a choice of champagnes. An intimate and warmly recommended restaurant.

Name: Baccanti
Description: Facing Matera’s picturesque cave churches in one of the most charming parts of the old town, this restaurant is housed in a complex of old caves. Despite being inspired by local traditions, the cuisine is modern and creative in style and always of the highest quality.

Name: Botero
Description: Close to the town centre and within walking distance of the Duomo, this restaurant is housed in a beautiful historic palazzo. The cuisine is delicious, with a menu featuring fish dishes (depending on market availability) and a few more traditional recipes such as sweet tortelli and the excellent nettle and angler fish gnudi. The friendly welcome and streamlined service explain the restaurant’s popularity at both lunch and dinner, so booking is recommended!

Name: Lipadusa
Description: In the centre of the village, a classic very simple atmosphere for this family run establishment with typical gastronomic dishes.

Name: Pierino Penati
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Terrace
Description: Surrounded by the greenery of the Brianza hills, this villa on the outskirts of the village boasts a delightful garden and an elegant dining room with a veranda. Although the cuisine here is traditional in style, it showcases the best of the Mediterranean in dishes that often feature modern preparation and combinations. Special attention is paid to the desserts, many of which are highly innovative, including one that pays homage to the Rubik’s cube. The impressive, well-structured wine list includes a selection of renowned labels from Italy and further afield alongside some younger, lesser-known options.

Name: Da Odino
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: This restaurant has stood on this square for many years, having been built as a “casone” and previously used as a dance hall. Despite its large size, the atmosphere is pleasant and convivial, helped by the staff here who are friendly yet professional. Situated just a stone’s throw from the Park Hotel Junior, a modern hotel under the same ownership, the restaurant specialises in fish and seafood, although you’ll also find meat and vegetarian options on the menu.

Name: La Gritta
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: Two of your senses will experience powerful marine sensations in this place. Your sight will be delighted with the enchanting view, especially from the terrace, and your taste will be tantalised by the imaginative, top - quality cuisine.

Name: Al Paradiso
Address: via Sant'Ermacora 1, Paradiso di Pocenia, 33050, Italy
Description: A small gem of a restaurant housed in an old farmhouse adorned with beautiful drapes and decorations. Although there’s a new chef here, the long family tradition of regional cuisine (mainly meat dishes and game) remains unchanged, with a large spit for roasting meat in the fireplace in the main dining room.

Name: Sibilla
Description: This long-established family-run restaurant occupies a stunning location at the foot of the Temple of Vesta, which can be admired from the attractive outdoor terrace. The classic cuisine served here is prepared mainly with local ingredients, although a few fish dishes also feature. Grilled dishes are among the house specialities.

Name: Mildas
Address: via Rosmini 7, località Vadaione, Giustino, 38086, Italy
Description: Housed in what was once the chapel of a medieval monastery, Mildas serves classic specialities from Trento alongside a selection of dishes created by Mirko, the late founder of the restaurant, which is now run by his son. The wine list features illustrations and descriptions.

Name: Degusteria del Gigante
Address: via degli Anelli 19, San Benedetto del Tronto, 63074, Italy
Cuisine: Country cooking, Cuisine from the Marches
Description: Situated in the charming historic centre of the upper part of the town, right behind the Torre dei Gualtieri, this restaurant occupies a 19C building with 15C foundations. Regional cuisine skilfully reinterpreted with a modern twist takes pride of place on the menu, where the focus is on flavour and seasonal ingredients rather than a vast selection of dishes. House specialities include options such as boned caramelised rabbit served with its own jus (inspired by the better-known traditional Marche dish), while daily visits to the market usually result in one or two fish-based recipes.

Name: Next2
Description: This restaurant is renowned for its excellent, modern and inviting cuisine. The menu showcases mostly regional ingredients (including meat) that are transformed into delicious recipes – the spinach ravioli with braised beef and blue bufala cheese, and the raw and cooked tuna with burrata, cherry tomatoes and basil are highly recommended. The impressive wine list and selection of cocktails can also be enjoyed as an aperitif or post-dinner drink at the wine bar.

Name: La Fiaschetteria
Description: Enjoy excellent reinterpretations of Emilian classics in this large 18C farmhouse. It is lit with modern designer - style chandeliers and warmed by a large fireplace. The three splendid guestrooms combine elegance with typical regional decor.

Name: Balin Sestri Levante
Description: An intimate restaurant on the seafront with a tiny dining room and small veranda, and a young, contemporary ambience. The Mediterranean-style cuisine is modern and creative with a focus on Ligurian ingredients to which the chef adds the occasional Asian twist, often in the sauces. Booking ahead is recommended given the limited number of tables here!

Name: Osteria dalla Peppa
Cuisine: Cuisine from the Marches, Traditional Cuisine
Description: Already popular in the late 19C, this inn in the town’s historic centre has retained its vintage atmosphere, period furnishings and decor. The cuisine focuses on local produce, with fresh pasta a house speciality.

Name: La Cascina 1899
Description: Situated on the main road running alongside the sea, this pleasant restaurant with a large car park occupies a late-19C building that has been transformed into an attractive, rustic-style eatery with plenty of outdoor areas and air-conditioned rooms with exposed-stone walls and wooden ceilings that provide welcome respite from the heat of summer. It’s no surprise that fish and seafood take pride of place on the menu, although meat dishes also feature. The shop next door sells regional specialities, some produced by the restaurant itself, including the famous local bergamot citrus fruit.

Name: Corsaro Nero
Address: Località Portu Maga, Marina di Arbus, 09031, Italy
Description: A wide choice of fresh fish and a menu with a firm focus on fish and seafood served in a large dining room offering views of the spectacular sunsets.

Name: Crotto Valtellina
Address: via Fiume 11, località Valle, Malnate, 21046, Italy
Description: With a bar or wine cellar located just inside the entrance, followed by a rustic dining hall, this restaurant serves strictly Valtellinese cuisine. Outdoor service in the summer, in the area below the cliff.

Name: Cavalluccio Marino
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Terrace
Description: Imaginative cuisine in a long - established family restaurant, which is constantly updated by each generation. Situated away from the town centre, yet easily accessible, the restaurant boasts an enviable seafront location. Excellent selection of local and international wines.

Name: Nicolin
Address: via Paisiello 4, località Maggianico, Lecco, 23900, Italy
Description: Run by the same family for over 30 years, this restaurant has recently been fully renovated. It serves traditional cuisine, as well as some imaginative dishes and a good choice of wine. Alfresco dining on the terrace in summer.

Name: Tre Galline
Description: A bastion of traditional Piedmontese cuisine, the main dining room at this restaurant boasts a profusion of wood from its parquet flooring to the wood panelling and exposed roofbeams. The warm, hearty cuisine features local specialities such as vitello tonnato, agnolotti pasta with roast meat sauce and a selection of mixed boiled meats, as well as a cheese trolley.

Name: Fiorfiore
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Terrace
Description: This restaurant occupying an elegant villa in a panoramic location with views of Todi and the surrounding countryside serves modern cuisine with its roots in Umbrian tradition. The extra-virgin olive oil comes from directly from the estate, as does some of the wine; there’s also an interesting selection of champagnes. Our inspector recommends the roast suckling pig accompanied by rosemary-flavoured potatoes, as well as the hazelnut cream, yoghurt sorbet and warm chocolate foam dessert. Quiet, comfortable guestrooms complete the picture.

Name: Osteria 1126
Description: The 1126 in the name of this restaurant refers to the year in which the hilltop hamlet in which it is situated was founded. Today the hamlet is home to apartments with their own kitchen, as well as the main villa. In the restaurant, a young enthusiastic couple serves contemporary - style cuisine made from local ingredients.

Name: Casa del Nonno 13
Address: via Caracciolo 13, loc. Sant'Eustachio, Mercato San Severino, 84085, Italy
Description: Recently re-opened under new management, this charming restaurant winds its way from room to room until you finally arrive at the palazzo’s old cellars, the jewel in its crown. The cuisine here has quickly made a name for itself, focusing on strong links with regional traditions and showcasing local favourites on a menu full of tempting options, including salumi, local vegetables, pasta dishes, grilled meat options and typical local ingredients such as San Marzano tomatoes. The delicious cuisine pays tribute to the fine culinary traditions of Campania.

Name: Estro Vino e Cucina
Address: calle Crosera, sestiere Dorsoduro 3778, Venice, 30123, Italy
Description: Situated slightly off the beaten track, this modern wine bar is also a restaurant serving Mediterranean cuisine accompanied by a selection of 700 organic wines. Snacks are available at aperitif hour.

Name: Christian & Manuel
Description: This restaurant features sophisticated, creative cooking and top quality ingredients, without forgetting the culinary traditions of the area and region. Therefore, don't be surprised by the special attention reserved for rice: the menu offers a selection of twenty risottos, but also a lot of delicious land and sea specialities.

Name: Duo Ristorante
Description: This elegant, intimate restaurant with subdued lighting is the perfect choice for a romantic gourmet dinner. The chef offers several different menus, allowing guests to choose their main course from any of these. Creative cuisine, with a strong focus on ingredients from Puglia.

Name: Gatto Rosso
Description: This small, long - established restaurant has been run by the same family for three generations, as depicted by the black - and - white photos on the walls. Simple and well - maintained dining room, plus a menu which focuses uniquely on fish dishes.

Name: Umberto De Martino
Address: via Madonna d'Argon 4/6, San Paolo d'Argon, 24060, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Part of the Florian Maison hotel in a bucolic setting of rolling hills, this large, elegant restaurant serves as a backdrop for tasting menus from which guests can choose dishes (three or more) à la carte style on weekday lunchtimes. Originally from the Sorrentine peninsula, chef Umberto Sorrentino’s origins clearly influence some of his recipes, which feature vegetables and plenty of fish alongside a few meat options.

Name: Rifugio Fuciade
Address: località Fuciada - Soraga di Fassa, San Pellegrino, 38035, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Garden or park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Terrace
Description: To give you an idea of the Alpine location of this restaurant framed by the Costabella mountain chain, suffice it to say that for centuries it was used for mountain pasture. There’s a breathtaking view of the Dolomites which extend into the distance as far as Pale di San Martino, while the menu here focuses on regional recipes such as canderli dumplings on a bed of cabbage, veal stew with polenta and chanterelle mushrooms, and polenta gnocchetti with herb pesto, smoked ricotta and lemon thyme. The wine cellar is home to more than 600 labels, plus accommodation is available in a choice of tranquil guestrooms.

Name: Il Capriolino
Address: via Nazionale 108, Vodo di Cadore, 32040, Italy
Description: This elegant restaurant has been run by the same family for years and has a history dating back over two centuries. It serves regional yet creative cuisine and has a distinctly Middle European ambience with its hunting trophies, clocks and frescoes.

Name: Cucina Bacilieri
Description: There are just a few tables in this excellent restaurant, which takes its name from its owner - chef. It serves modern and occasionally creative cuisine with strong links to typical regional specialities, such as eel and pasticcio ferrarese (a baked pasta dish).

Name: Al Gatto Nero
Description: Family - run, informal service, care in the choice of raw materials in a typical welcoming trattoria with Venetian and seafood cuisine; delightful outside area in the summer.

Name: La Meridiana
Description: In business for over 50 years, this long-established, centrally located restaurant has changed its look over the years and is now a modern bistro with an attractive outdoor summer space overlooking the magical town centre. Here, the owner-chef serves fish prepared in two different ways, either in typical Italian tradition or in a style inspired by his native Spain – his paella is definitely worth sampling! The front of house is overseen by the owner’s friendly wife, who is also at hand to help with your wine choices.

Name: SaleGrosso
Address: viale II Giugno 15, Milano Marittima, 48015, Italy
Description: One of the town’s authentic favourites, this fish restaurant has a pleasant, light - coloured decor inspired by the sea. The eclectic cuisine includes tapas and raw fish dishes.

Name: Satricvm
Description: Their experience in London, as well as in restaurants around the world, is evident in the pleasant yet somewhat unexpected international atmosphere created by this husband-and-wife team. Using modern techniques and locally sourced produce, the chef succeeds in showcasing the Agro Pontino area in his cuisine which is contemporary while still respecting the traditions of the region.

Name: Cocchi
Description: This restaurant adjoining the Daniel hotel is the town’s pride and joy. Here, two quiet, rustic-style dining rooms provide the backdrop for typical Parma specialities that change with the passing seasons – the “tortelli alle erbette” (tortelli pasta with herbs) with parmesan and melted butter is particularly delicious – all accompanied by an excellent choice of wines. Booking in advance is highly recommended as the restaurant is extremely popular with visitors and locals alike.

Name: Parizzi
Description: Based around carefully chosen ingredients sourced from the best local producers, the cuisine served at this restaurant is light and yet tasty. You’ll find typical Parma dishes on the menu here alongside more creative fare, with a slight emphasis on fish and seafood although meat and game (one of the chef’s passions!) also make an appearance. Together with his wife Cristina who oversees the front of house, chef Marco Parizzi continues his family’s tradition of providing a warm welcome and excellent cuisine. Guestrooms (this is a convenient central location) are also available.

Name: Antica Locanda del Villoresi
Description: What was once a post station is now a renowned restaurant overlooking the Villoresi canal. Although the attractive dining room has retained some of its historical features, the decor here is more contemporary in feel. The Mediterranean-style cuisine focuses mainly on fish and is beautifully presented, with dishes such as fried artichokes with red prawns and bottarga on the menu in season. Raw fish dishes are also occasionally available.

Name: Le Viole
Address: strada nuova di Castelnuovo 60/a, Castelnovo di Baganzola, 43126, Italy
Description: Regionally based cuisine with the occasional hint of creativity and a good choice of à la carte dishes are the highlights at this friendly restaurant on the outskirts of Parma. An authentic, genuine welcome, with an attractive lounge near the entrance and the warm ambience of a private home.

Name: Il Basilisco
Description: Situated in a residential district on the outskirts of town, this simple restaurant with a colourful decor serves excellent cuisine. Although many of the dishes are typical Italian favourites, it is the local specialities, such as the sopa coada di piccione (a type of warm pigeon soup), that particularly won us over. The menu also features a few fish options.

Name: Da Concettina ai Tre Santi
Address: via Arena alla Sanità 7 bis, Naples, 80137, Italy
Description: Situated in the heart of the ancient, lively and often chaotic working class district of Sanità, this excellent pizzeria has been run by the Oliva family for over 60 years. It has succeeded in reinventing itself with each generation while retaining its traditional roots. Modern and imaginative pizzas feature on the menu alongside various fried specialities.

Name: Ma.Ri.Na.
Address: piazza San Gregorio 11, Olgiate Olona, 21057, Italy
Description: The classic and timelessly elegant Ma.Ri.Na restaurant has been a bastion for fish and seafood enthusiasts for decades. The menu features classic Italian specialities alongside more creative options, including a good selection of raw dishes as well as delicious seafood pastas and risottos. The wine list is also impressive and includes an array of wines by the glass.

Name: Franceschetta 58
Description: This lively, welcoming restaurant serves simple and traditional regional cuisine, especially from Emilia Romagna, alongside more creative fare. The “Tradizione in evoluzione” menu features classic favourites such as gramigna pasta with cream and sausage, while the “I love Modena” menu showcases more imaginative recipes, including a sweet cacio e pepe dish as a dessert. The menu also includes tortellini made by the Il Tortellante association founded by Massimo Bottura, a rehabilitation centre where young people and adults on the autistic spectrum learn to make fresh pasta by hand. The wine list has just a few carefully chosen wines, with a whole page dedicated to Lambrusco.

Name: Sa Corte
Description: Local gastronomic traditions are demonstrated at their best in this rustic restaurant, which serves delicious pasta, excellent meat and fragrant Sardinian wines. Our favourite dishes include the goat kid with artichokes and the almond and flower petal desserts.

Name: Regio Patio
Address: via San Francesco d'Assisi 23, Garda, 37016, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Situated just a stone’s throw from the lakefront, this elegant gourmet restaurant in the Regina Adelaide hotel boasts an attractive English-style garden, as well as a beautiful outdoor patio and stylish dining room. The two tasting menus served here (one of which is vegetarian) showcase the traditions of Lake Garda and its surrounding region with a creative twist using vegetables from the property’s own kitchen garden and a focus on seasonal ingredients. There’s also an extensive wine list.

Name: Teresa
Address: piazza Lido di Pegli 5 r, Pegli, 16156, Italy
Description: Over half a century has passed since this restaurant was opened in 1968 by “mamma” Teresa and “papa” Giuseppe – and it’s still going strong! And although the staff here are proud of the restaurant’s long history and sense of tradition, they are not bound by it, as demonstrated by dishes that have successfully moved with the times, incorporating modern touches to the classic recipes, while always retaining a focus on fresh, high-quality ingredients (especially when it comes to choosing fish).

Name: Il Mecenate
Description: Occupying the premises of a historic local laundry along the city “moat”, this authentic trattoria has a friendly, convivial ambience. The menu showcases local dishes to the full, including specialities such as “tordelli lucchesi” (ravioli stuffed with different meats, thyme and nutmeg and always served with a meat ragù), tripe and bread pudding, the original recipe of which dates back to the 18C. A picturesque outdoor terrace facing San Francesco church and an excellent wine selection complete the picture.

Name: Osteria del Guà
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Guà was the name in local dialect of the River Novo, alongside which the property is situated. Dine under the arcades of the barchessa in fine weather, soaking up the tranquil atmosphere of the park, and in the intimate, romantic dining room in winter, which boasts the same elegant style as the rest of the hotel. Enjoy refined reinterpretations of local specialities in the evening, and simpler fare at lunchtime.

Name: Ristorante 1500
Address: via Pavicolo 43, funivia per raggiungere il ristorante in via Villa 3, San Vigilio, 39011, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Garden or park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Wheelchair access
Description: If you’re not a guest at the Vigilius Mountain Resort hotel where this restaurant is situated, leave your car in Lana and take the short cable-car ride to Monte San Vigilio where you’ll find the hotel at an altitude of 1 500m (remember to check the time of the last cable-car back down the mountain!). Decorated with a profusion of wood, the dining room has the same modern feel as the creative mountain cuisine prepared by the new chef who started here in 2023.

Name: Vino Buono
Address: via Castello 20, Grumello del Monte, 24064, Italy
Description: Housed in an old 17C hay barn near the Duomo belltower, this interesting wine bar offers around 400 different labels to accompany an array of simple yet well-prepared traditional dishes (including a few fish options). Highlights include the cured hams, cheeses and the excellent starters.

Name: Finger's Garden
Description: Firmly aimed at a trendier crowd, this restaurant has soft lighting and an Oriental feel. The chef here skilfully creates a range of dishes, including raw fish options and original fusion cuisine with a hint of Brazilian flavour. Gourmet diners will be happy to give full rein to the chef on his surprise menu.

Name: Emilio
Address: via Girardi 1, loc. Casabianca, Fermo, 63900, Italy
Description: With 60 years of history behind it, Emilio can definitely be described as a leading light on the region’s restaurant scene. The restaurant is renowned for its excellent fish, which is usually cooked in classic style (fish stew and mixed steamed fish served on steamed vegetables are prime examples) and often announced at your table, although a concise menu is also available. The elegant dining room is enhanced by a collection of striking works of art.

Name: da Omar
Address: via Dante Alighieri 21, Lido di Jesolo, 30016, Italy
Description: Passion and enthusiasm overcome all obstacles and lead to the best results: this summarises the professional journey of the chef at this restaurant. He prepares fish dishes inspired by classic Italian cuisine, sometimes with a modern twist, but always using the best quality produce.

Name: Belle Parti
Description: Occupying the ground floor of the historic Palazzo Prosdocimi in a delightful arcaded alleyway in Padova’s pedestrianised centre, this charming restaurant has a warm and romantic atmosphere thanks to its decor of paintings, mirrors and wood panelling, plus a beautiful ceiling with exposed wooden beams. The menu follows the changing seasons, offering a selection of delicious, classic dishes, with meat and – especially – fish (mostly from the Veneto) featuring on the menu.

Name: Campiello
Address: via Nazionale 46, San Giovanni al Natisone, 33048, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Wheelchair access
Description: Although the homemade breadsticks and preserves (available for purchase) at this long-established restaurant should not be missed, Campiello’s highlights are its fish and wine – the fish served here is among the best in the region. We highly recommend the fish soup served with shellfish and a Buzara sauce, while the wine cellar is home to a selection of 25 000 bottles, with wines from the nearby Collio and Colli Orientali vineyards taking centre stage. A selection of renowned labels from Italy and abroad also features, offering an incredible choice of the highest quality for wine connoisseurs. There’s also the option of dining at the informal osteria next door.

Name: L'Acchiatura
Description: Delicious cuisine from Puglia, including excellent orecchiette pasta with clams and chickpeas, served in a delightful ambience with a number of different rooms and internal patios. The same traditional atmosphere is evident in the attractive, well - equipped guestrooms, as well as in the picturesque swimming pool housed in a grotto.

Name: Degli Angeli
Address: località Madonna degli Angeli, Magliano Sabina, 02046, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Terrace
Description: The family that runs this excellent restaurant with views of the surrounding countryside has been doing so with passion and experience for over a century. The menu here focuses on the culinary traditions of Lazio, while the wine and extra-virgin olive oil are also sourced locally. The restaurant is part of a hotel and includes a shop (La Bottega delle Delizie) selling home-made produce.

Name: Trattoria al Ponte
Address: via Bertolda 27, località Bornio, Lusia, 45020, Italy
Description: Meat and freshwater fish feature on the menu at this restaurant, where the chef creates traditional dishes with an imaginative twist, such as his legendary risotto (made from seasonal ingredients) and breast of guinea fowl with mustard. An oasis surrounded by greenery, situated right by a bridge, and embellished by a small illuminated pool.

Name: Palazzo Petrucci
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Great view,Interesting wine list,Wheelchair access
Description: The entrance from the street does little to prepare you for the surprise that awaits once you’ve taken the lift down to this restaurant, where the dining room looks out at the beach and guests dine with the sound of the waves as a romantic backdrop. In a modern and minimalist setting, chef Lino Scarallo offers a choice of tasting menus, include a surprise option on which he has carte blanche, and others based on signature dishes that include raw fish options and meat specialities.

Name: Il Pozzo
Description: This restaurant is housed in a historic palazzo. It has a traditional dining room, as well as an area that was once home to a wine bar (vaulted ceilings and more convivial atmosphere). A full range of Italian specialities are served.

Name: La Saletta
Description: Just a stone’s throw from the seafront promenade in the historic centre of Alghero, this small gem run by Gian Luca Chessa offers the best of Sardinia. The cuisine is showcased on different tasting menus, including Rivoluzione (creative yet with a regional focus); Radici (vegetables take centre stage); Riviera (local fish); and Cortile (traditionally inspired dishes). We particularly enjoyed the gnocchi stuffed with sheep’s ricotta cheese, beetroot sauce and Sardinian scorzone truffle – a real treat! All the wines are available by the glass, so don’t hesitate to ask the sommelier for recommendations.

Name: A Spurcacciun-a
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Always a good choice for gourmet cuisine, this lovely restaurant within the Hotel Mare boasts a fine location with a garden for summer dining overlooking the beach and the sea. Whether you’re soaking up the views outside or sitting comfortably in the attractive contemporary-style dining room, it’s Simone Perata’s cuisine that will convince you that you’ve chosen the best place in town. The menu is teeming with delicious dishes made from top-quality ingredients (especially fish, such as the delicious whitebait with grilled artichokes and green curry sauce), all prepared with a modern twist and beautifully presented. The excellent wine list (including a few vintage labels) provides the perfect accompaniment to your dining experience.

Name: Aquadulcis
Address: contrada Tenda, Vallo della Lucania, 84078, Italy
Description: Following careful restoration, this old mill has been transformed into a gourmet restaurant with just a few tables. Here, skilful young chef Vincenzo Cucolo delights guests with his cuisine – a combination of creative dishes and old recipes focusing on traditional Cilento ingredients.

Name: Langosteria
Description: If you are looking for fish specialities, you will find this restaurant a real revelation. Raw dishes, oysters and seafood take pride of place on the menu, alongside freshly caught fish. An excellent wine selection and a glamorous ambience complete the picture.

Name: La Perla
Description: Housed in a historic palazzo on the charming Piazza della Motta in the town centre, this restaurant is one you will immediately want to share with family and friends thanks to its delicious cuisine. The menu focuses mainly on fish and seafood (including impressive raw fish dishes) although a few meat options are also available. Good choice of wines and spirits.

Name: Maxi
Address: via Luigi Serio 8, SS 145 Sorrentina km 14,500, Vico Equense, 80069, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: From the entrance to the Capo la Gala hotel, you head down to the seafront to this restaurant, where a long terrace overlooks the rocks – if you’re looking for a romantic place to eat, this is one of the best options on this coastline (there’s also an indoor dining room for inclement weather). The cuisine is equal to the setting, thanks to the chef from Ischia who skilfully creates imaginative dishes using ingredients from Campania.

Name: Punto G
Address: via Gian Francesco Parravicini 34, Monza, 20900, Italy
Description: Situated not far from the town centre, this restaurant has two different spaces – a ground-floor bistro, plus a gourmet dining room on the first floor, both beautifully maintained and decorated with simple elegance. Here, a young chef from Campania who has experience working both in Italy and abroad creates modern, elegant and contemporary cuisine. In the bistro, the choice of gourmet pizzas is a reminder of the chef’s origins.

Name: L'Ambasciata
Address: piazzetta Ambasciatori del Gusto 1, Quistello, 46026, Italy
Description: This has long been one of those restaurants in Italy where the opulent interior decor has no equal – at Christmas, the mirrors, rugs, silverware, chandeliers and piles of books are joined by the largest and most ornate Christmas tree that you’ll ever see in a restaurant. The cuisine created by owner-chef Matteo Ugolotti is inspired by Mantuan traditions and the restaurant’s previous famous owners, occasionally going all the way back to the Renaissance. Special mention should be made of the extraordinary chocolate salami – a dessert coated with a delicious, frothy, warm zabaglione poured from a copper pan at your table. The menu also features more modern recipes and tasting menus.

Name: Marixx
Description: Located well away from the busy city centre and overlooking the luxury yachts and boats moored in the harbour, this restaurant opened in the summer of 2021, at the same time as the modern Cala del Forte marina in which it is situated (the name of the marina comes from the Forte dell'Annunziata, the ruins of which are visible from the side facing the sea). Fish and seafood take pride of place here (especially raw fish dishes), served with classic, seasonal accompaniments, as well as snacks, while an oyster bar is an added attraction. Although the best tables are in the glass-fronted veranda overlooking the pedestrian promenade, the contemporary-style dining room is also attractive. The owner-chef has plenty of experience behind him, especially working in the region.

Name: Locanda Nelli
Address: via Vittorio Veneto 15, Pietra Ligure, 17027, Italy
Description: A friendly and welcoming little restaurant in the heart of the town’s historic centre. It’s no surprise that the specialities here focus mainly on fish and seafood, with an emphasis on Mediterranean cuisine, homemade pasta and the use of extremely fresh ingredients – the menu changes daily depending on market availability. The charming outdoor space boasts tables set out along the small pedestrianised street.

Name: I Giardini dei Rodo
Address: via Bonomo Alto - Scauri, Pantelleria, 91017, Italy
Description: As its name suggests, this restaurant’s guests can enjoy their meal surrounded by verdant gardens, which are planted with palms, flowers and citrus trees. Regional flavours take centre-stage in the modern dishes in this romantic and original setting.

Name: La Cucina dei Frigoriferi Milanesi
Description: An interesting location in the artistic-cultural setting of the Frigoriferi Milanesi industrial complex for this restaurant with a modern feel both in its decor and its market cuisine.

Name: Osteria Borgo Ronche
Description: Just a few tables and an elegantly contemporary decor provide the setting for cuisine with a focus on the sea, with simpler dishes available at lunchtime and more creative fare served in the evening. There’s just one thing left to do and that’s book a table!

Name: Da Nando
Description: The whole family is involved in running this typical trattoria, which has become one of the standard - bearers of the region. The decor is classic and elegant, while the menu focuses on local specialities such as excellent hams, good fish and, in season, superb truffles. The huge wine cellar is home to 120 000 bottles, so you are bound to find a wine that suits!

Name: Osteria Bellavista
Address: via Piovega 30, località Farra, Paderno del Grappa, 31017, Italy
Description: An excellent modern inn offering a warm, family welcome. Imaginative yet traditional dishes made from market-fresh ingredients, with a balance of fish and meat dishes featuring on the menu.

Name: Osteria Il Principe e Il Pirata
Description: This restaurant is housed in a typical island house with rustic furniture and a large terrace with sea views. Here, the Casano family look after guests, are responsible for the impressive wine list and, of course, prepare the cuisine that focuses on top-quality ingredients and Sicilian recipes. Specialities include couscous with fresh fish and vegetables, cuttlefish “alla fiamma” and courgettes marinated in mint, as well as typical desserts such as the “bacio pantesco”.

Name: Gong
Description: East meets West in a harmonious fusion of flavours at this restaurant, which takes its name from the imposing gongs dotted around the modern, elegant dining room. The attentive and thoughtful staff are always on hand to explain the different dishes, which are influenced by Chinese traditions yet often have an innovative feel. Beautiful presentation and carefully chosen ingredients typify the contemporary international flavour of this type of cuisine, with an extensive and varied selection of dishes on the à la carte and various tasting menus. One of the latter is dedicated to Peking duck, the restaurant’s signature dish.

Name: Ruris
Address: Via Spiaggie Rosse, località Mazzotta, Isola di Capo Rizzuto, 88841, Italy
Description: Despite its rural setting inland, this restaurant is still situated within the Capo Rizzuto e Mar Ionio protected marine reserve, which helps to explain the focus on fish and seafood dishes demonstrated by owner-chef Natale Pallone on the menu. The wine cellar boasts over 200 different wines and more than 60 internationally renowned spirits.

Name: Le Due Lanterne
Description: Situated in the town centre, this typical family-run trattoria is highly popular with locals and offers excellent value for money. Iconic dishes on the menu include rabbit all'Arneis and Piedmontese battuta (a type of beef tartare), while the extensive wine list features a good selection of labels. We recommend booking a table in the first, more comfortable dining room.

Name: Ai Campi di Marcello
Description: Not far from the shipyards, simple but pleasant atmosphere in a family-run restaurant with good seafood options.
