Among the many specialties, we recommend the cold soup with raw and cooked fish. Curious note: the owner's passion for rum translates into an intriguing and unexpected selection of this liqueur.

Name: Armani/Ristorante
Description: Elegant and carefully prepared contemporary cuisine served on the seventh floor of a palazzo which is totally dedicated to the world of Armani. Superb views of Milan combine with a decor of black marble and backlit onyx to create an exclusive and fashionable ambience.

Name: Al Cjasal
Address: via Nazionale 30, località San Giorgio al Tagliamento, San Michele al Tagliamento, 30028, Italy
Description: A new generation is now at the helm in this warm and elegant restaurant decorated with a profusion of wood, adding a more modern touch to the cuisine while maintaining its regional character and excellent local ingredients. The menu has its own unique flavour thanks to the option of numerous cicchetti (tapas-style snacks) options available, either in half- or full portions, enabling guests to create their own menu.

Name: Terrazza Fiorella
Address: via Vincenzo Maggio 5, Massa Lubrense, 80061, Italy
Description: Housed in the Villa Fiorella Art Hotel, this restaurant boasts a stunningly located terrace with spectacular views of the Bay of Naples and its islands. The cuisine pays tribute to Campania and its top-quality ingredients which the chef uses to create imaginative dishes reinterpreted with his own personal twist.

Name: Al Tonno di Corsa
Description: Not only the restaurant, but a large part of the tantalising menu as well is based on the tuna caught in the nets. Open kitchen; two small dining rooms and two pleasant little terraces.

Name: A' Cuncuma
Description: In 2022, young sous-chef Gianfilippo Gatto became the owner-chef of this simple and intimate restaurant situated in Palermo’s historic centre. The key attraction here is the quality of the cuisine, which features colourful dishes and modern interpretations of Sicilian recipes (meat and fish alike). Examples include arancina stuffed with young caciocavallo cheese and cooked in the oven, then topped with orange prawn tartare and served on a prawn bisque. The excellent wine list is completely Sicilian, with separate sections dedicated to the Etna wines produced in different parts of the region, many of which are young, promising and highly recommended!

Name: Soprattutto
Address: via Noalese 124, Santa Maria di Sala, 30036, Italy
Description: This tiny, welcoming restaurant with a bright, simple decor has long since come of age, having been opened and run by the same family for years. The wife supervises the front of house, while the husband (whose past experience includes working as a metalworker as well as a chef) is at the helm in the kitchen, where he creates classic fish dishes which are full of flavour and simply prepared from top-quality ingredients. As the restaurant is very popular with its regular clientele, booking in advance is essential – you won’t be disappointed!

Name: MoS
Address: via Porto Vecchio 28, Desenzano del Garda, 25015, Italy
Description: The young Stefano Zanini, with plenty of experience in Italy and further afield, has injected new life into this old trattoria situated right in front of the marina in the historic heart of Desenzano. The personalised cuisine focuses on seasonal ingredients, including meat and fish from the lake and sea; one of the restaurant’s key tenets is recycling waste as much as possible. In summer, dine at one of the outdoor tables with views of the boats in the marina.

Name: Gina
Address: via Croce di Città 25, Aosta, 11100, Italy
Description: In the old town, a simple and informal location (but on the floor below there are two rooms between the Roman walls of Aosta!) for a cuisine of remarkable quality: the chef often starts from local traditions to develop them into more creative dishes, whose protagonists are often mountain products.

Name: Secondo Tempo
Address: via Vittorio Amedeo 55, Termini Imerese, 90018, Italy
Description: Situated on the first floor of a building (formerly home to an apartment owned by chef Salvatore Campagna’s family), this intimate restaurant dates back to the 1920s, as do the frescoes on the ceiling and the Art Nouveau-style flooring. In contrast, the cuisine is modern Italian with obvious Sicilian influences, including a focus on seasonal vegetables (there’s even a tasting menu that is completely vegan). All the extra-virgin olive oil used for cooking and as a condiment is home produced.

Name: Motelombroso
Description: An old, carefully restored road worker’s house on the Alzaia Naviglio Pavese canal is the setting for this modern, stylish restaurant where Alessandra and Matteo welcome guests in a graceful, elegant and yet informal manner. The menu features contemporary meat and fish dishes accompanied by a good choice of wines. If you’re curious about the restaurant’s name, ask the owners for an explanation: could it be something to do with the private dining room perhaps?

Name: Osteria Billis
Description: The former bar of the railway station (situated in the park next to the station) has been transformed into this glass-fronted restaurant with a terrace for summer dining. Exciting, personalised dishes based around regional traditions and seasonal ingredients feature on the menu here.

Name: DaV  Mare
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Great view,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: The classic, wrought-iron outdoor dining space at this restaurant overlooks one of the most romantic little squares in Italy, while the view takes in the promontory dominated by its castle – a picture-postcard view that is famous around the world. The experienced Cerea family from the famous three-starred Michelin Da Vittoria restaurant in Bergamo are at the helm, serving consistently top-quality cuisine whether you’re here for a quick lunch or a gourmet dinner. It’s best to book ahead as the few tables are much in demand!

Name: MaMe Restaurant
Description: Situated in central Viareggio near the town’s shipyards, MaMe occupies a long, narrow space that is reminiscent of Oriental restaurants with its long bench running alongside one wall and small bistro-style tables. This informal yet beautifully kept dining room is the backdrop for cuisine with interesting technical details such as the home-made mayonnaise served with the highly recommended steamed fish dish, and the delicious sourdough loaf which is freshly baked and served warm.

Name: Locanda Marchesani
Description: In addition to specialities such as oysters and caviar, this restaurant serves sophisticated classic, traditional cuisine reinterpreted with a modern twist. Choose between à la carte options or tasting menus prepared with refined ingredients of the highest quality.

Name: Aria
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: The Villa Riviera resort home to this restaurant is situated slightly inland and uphill from the sea in a tranquil oasis of greenery. The modern, minimalist veranda-style dining room is welcoming and elegant, while the summer terrace has a romantic ambience with superb views of the coast, especially at sunset. The menu features modern, occasionally creative cuisine with Ligurian influences evident in dishes such as the “La mia Liguria” dessert which combines ingredients such as basil and olives with white chocolate, pine nuts and fiordilatte ice cream.

Name: Rada Rooftop
Description: Right at the end of Positano beach, and above the ground-floor night club, this restaurant on the first floor of an old fishermen’s warehouse offers breathtaking views of the village and the sea. Creative cuisine inspired by Mediterranean traditions.

Name: Locanda La Raia
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: The magnificent biodynamic La Raia farm, an enchanting 180-hectare oasis between Novi Ligure and Gavi, is home to a contemporary art foundation, the Rossi Cairo family winery, a Steiner school for employees’ children, guest accommodation, and this restaurant which benefits from a fertile ecosystem that provides much of its zero-mile produce. The cuisine is rooted in local traditions which have been reinterpreted in contemporary style. In the evening (and at lunchtime at weekends), choose between an à la carte, a tasting menu inspired by wines from the property’s estates between Gavi and Langhe, and a delicious “Sei mezze” menu featuring small samples of the restaurant’s most iconic dishes.

Name: Specus
Description: This charming restaurant’s name comes from the Latin and refers to the small grotto carved out of the tufa rock in the courtyard, which is home to just a few tables. The restaurant is run by a young couple, with Flavia front of house and Alessio at the helm in the kitchen. The cuisine is authentic in style, with imaginatively named dishes such as “Quel viaggio che non scordo” (“This journey I’ll never forget”) and “Dal 2014” (“From 2014”). The Riso Acquerello with fermented goat’s cheese, black truffle and herb pesto is truly memorable, while the desserts (especially the apple strudel) are equally delicious.

Name: Cucine Nervi
Description: Housed within the Cantine Nervi in the town centre, this contemporary restaurant with a completely open kitchen offers guests the choice of eating at the large counter facing the kitchen or at one of the more traditional tables. Very chic ambience, with a focus on imaginative and creative cuisine.

Name: Olio
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Housed within The Box, a multi-functional space that is home to vintage cars and contemporary art works surrounded by a garden with splendid olive trees, this restaurant serves excellent fish and seafood (there’s also a bistro serving quicker lunches from Tuesday to Friday). The delicious, substantial dishes are prepared using top-quality ingredients and a focus on traditional recipes with just the right amount of creativity. Pastas, risottos, fried dishes and soups all feature, followed by an excellent selection of desserts.

Name: Da Carla
Address: via Necchi 3/5, fraz. Molino Isella, Gambolò, 27025, Italy
Description: Once a mill, this restaurant still stands next to its old canal which lends the setting a delightful bucolic ambience echoed in the warm, welcoming dining room. Highlights on the menu include risottos, frog’s legs, snails and goose - based dishes, as well as cured meats. Inviting guestrooms complete this delightfully rustic picture.

Name: Hosteria Toblino
Address: via Garda 3, Sarche di Madruzzo, 38070, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: The most welcoming section of the extensive Cantina Toblino complex is home to the large, contemporary and minimalist-style Hosteria. Here, a young chef serves simple reinterpretations of regional dishes with a focus on zero-mile produce with the occasional yet astute use of ingredients from further afield.

Name: Jamantè
Address: via San Vito 97, Polignano a Mare, 70044, Italy
Description: Located not far from the historic centre and the picturesque Lama Monachile beach, Jamantè is an elegant restaurant with well-spaced-out tables perfect for a stylish night out. With a focus on fish and seafood, the dishes have their roots in Puglian traditions yet have been successfully reinterpreted with personalised touches by the chef.

Name: Gimmi Restaurant
Address: via San Pietro in Lama 23, Lecce, 73100, Italy
Description: Despite its location in a Dominican monastery dating from 1442 (also home to a boutique hotel), this restaurant is decidedly modern and minimalist in style, with a light-coloured floor, imposing stone columns, a cross-vaulted ceiling, and a dining room with a view of the glass-fronted wine display. The service here is friendly, attentive and highly efficient, while the top-quality cuisine includes highly recommended specialities such as Capelli d’angelo Benedetto Cavalieri, angel-hair pasta with mantis shrimp, seaweed spaghetti, Galateo saffron, celery and sweet pepper.

Name: Filo
Description: This restaurant boasts a superb lakeside location, offering views of the opposite shore, Comacina island and Villa Balbianello. The experience is enhanced by the modern cuisine, in which dishes from all over Italy are created by the young chef from Campania, from the opening appetisers to the coffee-paired desserts at the end of the meal. The recipes are sophisticated without being overly complicated, offering a choice of tasting menus or à la carte options. The full flavours of Italian cuisine delight the palate, while the beautiful presentation provides a feast for the eyes.

Name: Dry Aged
Address: via Cesare Da Sesto 1, Milan, 20123, Italy
Description: Two partners with significant experience opened this lively venue: the rooms combine modern and classic styles in an industrial-New York style decorated with works by major street artists. At the entrance, the glass counter shows off meats of different breeds to be enjoyed even charcoal grilled, but there are also other specialties: appealing dishes with a modern preparation and homemade pastas.

Name: Hydra
Description: Situated in the picturesque historic centre of Salerno, this is one of the city’s best restaurants. The dining room here is almost minimalist in style, yet thanks to the soft lighting and beautiful background music it has a pleasing atmosphere; in fine weather, tables are set out in a charming inner courtyard. The cuisine is Mediterranean and contemporary, with a selection of light and creative meat, fish and vegetable dishes featuring on the menu.

Name: Bottega Culinaria
Address: contrada Pontoni 72, San Vito Chietino, 66038, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Nestled amid a charming landscape of olive groves, this restaurant is not particularly easy to find, so make sure that you use a satnav or ask for directions when booking. A simple, minimalist-style dining room provides the backdrop for imaginative cuisine which includes plenty of vegetables and is full of contrasting flavours and reinterpreted regional influences.

Name: Antica Trattoria Centro
Description: Situated in the heart of Levanto just a stone’s throw from the sea, this trattoria serving traditional fish and seafood (as well as a few meat options) has been run by the same owners for almost 20 years. Friendly ambience, good service, plus a few tables in a small outdoor space which need to be booked well in advance.

Name: Bebop
Description: Having studied classics, this young self-taught chef decided to follow his true passion, namely cooking. He prepares dishes inspired by Sicilian traditions yet reinterpreted with a personal twist, using the best regional products. The restaurant, situated in the heart of Palermo, is quiet and elegant yet also pleasantly informal in its service.

Name: Corbezzoli
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Wheelchair access
Description: Situated in the Relais Bellaria hotel on the outskirts of the city, this contemporary-style restaurant serves equally modern cuisine which ranges from vegetarian dishes to meat and fish options, all of which are featured on three tasting menus and an à la carte. In the kitchen, the chef from Campania skilfully combines the flavours of his native region with those of his adopted Emilia in dishes which are both copious and colourful.

Name: Augurio
Address: via Dietro le Mura B 16, Trento, 38122, Italy
Description: Opened by three brothers (Augurio is the family name), this restaurant in the city centre successfully combines the traditional and the modern in both its cuisine and its decor. The dining room, with an open-view kitchen on the ground floor, boasts an old, vaulted ceiling, while its wood furniture adds a contemporary look. The menu features local and Italian dishes reinterpreted with flavour and style. Lighter options are available at lunchtime; the grande carte needs to be ordered ahead of time.

Name: Radici
Description: Accursio Craparo from the nearby Michelin-starred Accursio restaurant is the chef at the helm at Radici. In two simple yet elegant dining rooms, he serves more traditional and authentically Sicilian cuisine than at Accursio, offering guests the opportunity to sample dishes created by a great chef at a reasonable price.

Name: L˜ARIA
FacilitiesAndServices: Garden or park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Occupying a modern lakeside building nestling in botanic gardens, this restaurant has an elegant and contemporary feel. Although the dishes served by new chef Massimiliano Blasone have a cosmopolitan flavour with the occasional hint of Asia, the selection of delicious desserts that follow are prepared with a combination of regional and exotic ingredients.

Name: San Domenico
Description: Perched high on the tufa cliffs overlooking the Costa degli Dei, this contemporary-style restaurant boasts superb views from its dining room and especially from its panoramic summer terrace. The cuisine served by the young owner-chef is as modern as the setting – dishes are light and almost exclusively focused on local fish.

Name: Antica Trattoria Giovanelli
Description: Situated in a charming rural setting at the foot of the surrounding hills, this trattoria has been run by the same family (now on the third generation) since 1939. Regional cuisine is to the fore here, with cured hams and roast and boiled meats all featuring on the menu, as well as its highly recommended homemade pastas and the almond tart with zabaione.

Name: iPalici
Address: via Antonello da Messina 3, Viagrande, 95029, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Garden or park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: Situated behind Acireale at the foot of Mount Etna National Park, this restaurant is located within the Relais San Giuliano. Deceptively uninteresting from the outside, this historic building and its inner courtyards boast a charm and grandeur that will take your breath away. A huge 16C wine press provides the backdrop for fine cuisine that is more than equal to its impressive setting. Here, the menu makes full use of vegetables and other Sicilian ingredients in dishes that are influenced by the island’s culinary traditions yet reinterpreted with a skilful contemporary twist by the chef.

Name: Modì
Description: This restaurant has moved from its previous location in central Torregrotta to a more secluded setting slightly above the town centre, where it aims to offer its guests an even better dining experience. The owner-chef has more than achieved this, serving excellent Sicilian dishes reinterpreted with careful precision and a contemporary twist. A good wine list completes the picture.

Name: Opera
Address: via Sant'Antonio da Padova 3, Turin, 10121, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Wheelchair access
Description: The former nineteenth century refectory of the nearby church has become the laboratory of a chef who is as skillful as he is creative: wrapped in the warm atmosphere of the brickwork of the evocative dining room, all the dishes have fruit as a recurring ingredient, which adds a touch of acidity and flavor to dishes of creative cuisine, whether of meat or fish, further enhanced by the work of an excellent sommelier.

Name: Autem*
Description: Situated in a lively district just a stone’s throw from the Porta Romana, this modern restaurant with an open-view kitchen (also visible from outside) now has a new wine cellar which is accessed via a flight of stairs and also doubles as a convivial dining room. Menus are handwritten on rice paper by the chef, emphasising the artisanal approach here, with recipes then explained by staff at your table. Luca Natalini, originally from Tuscany but also with experience from around the world, creates personalised meat and fish dishes such as red mullet and seasonal vegetables with a hollandaise sauce and lobster reduction.

Name: Canova Restaurant
Description: Housed in an elegant hotel just behind St Mark’s Square, this gourmet restaurant is home to chef Gennaro Balice, who prepares visually impressive dishes from carefully chosen ingredients. Guests can choose from an à la carte or two tasting menus, one creative and Venetian in style, the other vegetarian. Simpler fare is available in the bistro next door or at tables on the outdoor terrace in fine weather.

Name: L'Insolita Trattoria Tre Soldi
Description: A long-established trattoria opened by a married couple in the 1950s and now run by their son Lorenzo who serves highly personalised cuisine with a focus on local ingredients. The dishes have amusing and entertaining names such as “Amici per la pelle” (“Friends for life”), “Non è un pomodoro” (“This isn’t a tomato”), and “Solo un chicco di caffè” (“Just one coffee bean”). In addition to a classic menu, an intriguing "Unconventional Experience" is offered, in which guests have to guess the ingredients of the dishes by following some clues.

Name: Rear Restaurant
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Wheelchair access
Description: This restaurant with a modern, elegant dining room in which an entire wall is taken up by the open-view kitchen serves varied cuisine. In addition to more elaborate dishes, there’s also a choice of street food such as fried dishes, sandwiches, Spanish prosciutto and tacos, as well as raw fish and seafood, classic and more creative options, and various fish and meat main courses, many of which are cooked over the barbecue grill. The superb wine list includes a fine array of champagnes.

Name: Quel Fantastico Giovedì
Description: Two small modern dining rooms with contemporary paintings on the walls provide the backdrop for classic specialities from Ferrara, as well as the chef’s renowned fish dishes at this restaurant, where booking is highly recommended, even at lunchtime!

Name: Le Cicale in Città
Description: A classic-style dining room adorned with mirrors and silverware acts as the backdrop for fish and seafood dishes at this restaurant. The raw fish is particularly excellent, as are the mupa (a little-known fish that lives in the deep waters of the Mediterranean), prawns (in season) and home-made primi served with delicious sauces, such as the chicken plin with brown gravy. For special occasions, we recommend the table to the rear of the room near the arte povera-style dresser. Cheerful, friendly service adds to the appeal.

Name: La Maison de Filip
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Situated at the entrance to the pedestrian section of the beautiful city of Trento, this intimate restaurant has a modern, minimalist and vaguely Nordic style, with just a few solid wood tables and stools of different sizes. The menu features a concise selection of carefully thought-out dishes, with starters, first and main courses (meat, fish or vegetarian) that are elegant, well prepared and contemporary in style. Beautiful presentation completes the picture.

Name: Duo
Description: In this restaurant housed in a historic palazzo in the centre of Chiavari, the owners have used the structural beauty of the building to showcase the skills of local artisans, resulting in a very attractive ambience. The modern cuisine is simple in style, allowing all the flavour of the ingredients to shine through.

Name: Hazama
Description: Japanese cuisine served in a small restaurant where both the cuisine and decor are minimalist in style. Here, young chef Satoshi Hazama creates light dishes full of Japanese flavour, all made from top-quality ingredients. The kaiseki menu served in the evening consists of seven or nine different courses.

Name: Il Marchese - Osteria Mercato Liquori
Description: Boasting a sumptuous Art Deco setting that contrasts pleasingly with the traditional cuisine served here, this restaurant is the Milanese sibling of Il Marchese in Rome which pays tribute to the famous Italian film “Il Marchese del Grillo” starring Alberto Sordi (it is also the first bar in Europe to offer more than 600 “amaro” liqueurs). The culinary philosophy here is based on traditional Roman cuisine with a contemporary flavour, including delicious specialities such as pasta with carbonara, matriciana and gricia sauces, veal saltimbocca, pork belly and much more besides!

Name: GioEle
Description: Situated in the town centre, this colourful and discreetly elegant restaurant offers friendly and professional service. The classic cuisine served here is modern in style, offering a choice of meat and fish dishes as well as a convenient business lunch menu. In summer, tables are arranged outdoors on the terrace and in the small courtyard.

Name: Radici Osteria Contemporanea
Description: Having moved to the pedestrianised section of historic Gallarate, Radici Osteria Contemporanea has also adopted a new look, with a lounge-bar ambience that is young and trendy, making it the perfect setting for its aperitifs and superb cocktails. The restaurant’s excellent, modern and personalised cuisine remains unchanged, however.

Name: Aprudia
Description: At this restaurant in the historic centre, where the vaulted brick ceiling provides a striking contrast with the modern furnishings, the chef celebrates the seasons through a whole range of ingredients to create truly delicious cuisine. Interesting tasting menus add to its appeal.

Name: Rueda Gaucha
Description: This restaurant is justifiably renowned for two specialities – firstly, its wide selection of cured hams including the famous Friuli prosciuttos as well as hams from further afield; and secondly, dishes (mainly meat sourced from Italy and further afield, although fish also features) cooked on the barbecue grill.

Name: Antica Macelleria Cecchini - Solociccia
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Bring your own bottle,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: One of the most famous butchers in Italy has now turned his hand to cooking. At two locations, Solociccia or Officina della Bistecca, the menu is unique and served at a specific time with a meat proposal or a vegetarian option. Solociccia is only open for lunch.

Name: Brindo
Description: The service is characterized by a cohesive and friendly team in welcoming guests to their small home. Brindo is an informal reality, where the cuisine is fun, engaging and more than simply territorial: raw foods, tartar and fish of the day are at the top!

Name: Ceresio 7
Description: This designer-style restaurant is housed on the fourth floor of the historic ENEL palazzo, remodelled and converted into the Dsquared2 building. It combines the use of brass, marble and wood to create a successful blend of attractive colours and vintage decor. The view of Milan (even better from the long outdoor terrace with its two swimming pools) completes the picture, while the cuisine reinterprets Italian classics with a contemporary twist.

Name: L'Aia dei Cappellani
Description: In the dining room there are old photos and equipment from country life, from the terrace the entire valley. Among widespread grasslands and olive trees enjoy fresh produce and home - cooked local dishes. In the dining room there are old photos and equipment from country life, from the terrace the entire valley. Among widespread grasslands and olive trees enjoy fresh produce and home - cooked local dishes.

Name: Serendepico
Address: via della Chiesa di Gragnano 36, Capannori, 55012, Italy
Description: An entertaining culinary experience, thanks to the Japanese chef who serves his own “fusion” cuisine influenced by Italian dishes (and occasionally European, such as the Basque cheesecake) with the occasional Japanese twist. On Thursdays, the menu is completely Japanese with a focus on typical specialities such as sushi, sashimi, tempura and gyoza dishes.

Name: Caffè Dante Bistrot
Description: This restaurant boasts an outdoor terrace overlooking one of the most beautiful squares in Verona, plus an equally attractive 19C-style room for indoor dining. The menu features a good balance of local and Italian specialities, with an emphasis on grilled main courses and a careful selection of high-quality meat. The extensive wine list includes labels from around the world.

Name: Locanda Sensi
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: We highly recommend this pleasant country restaurant run by friendly and enthusiastic staff, where the owner appears frequently in the dining room. The ambience is modern and comfortable, the outdoor dining area boasts typical views of the Piacenza hills, and – last but not least – the food is excellent! The options on the fine-dining menu range from regional specialities to fish-based dishes, as well as various delicacies cooked on the barbecue grill, such as pigeon breast (served with pigeon leg, marinated breast, offal and rice timbale). The wine selection is also excellent.

Name: Le Cedrare
Description: This restaurant is housed in the 18C Villa Perez - Pompei - Sagramoso, in a room once used as a conservatory for orange and lemon trees. It serves excellent, inventive and regional cuisine in a charming location.

Name: Osteria da Pietro
Address: via Chiassi 19, Castiglione delle Stiviere, 46043, Italy
Description: Housed in an elegant period building in the historic centre, this restaurant is run by a friendly couple, with the wife at the helm in the kitchen and the husband keeping a skilful eye on the front-of-house staff. Highlights on the menu include pumpkin tortelli and rose tart with Muscat zabaglione.

Name: Il Convito della Venaria
Address: via Andrea Mensa 37/g, Venaria Reale, 10078, Italy
Description: This restaurant is run by an enthusiastic couple, with Lucia front of house in the classic and welcoming dining room and Christian at the helm in the kitchen. The menu is lighter (and less expensive) at lunchtime with a wider choice of regional and Italian fare in the evening, plus a few more creative options, including fish dishes. Comfortable guestrooms are also available, two of which have views of the royal palace.

Name: Wicky's Innovative Japanese Cuisine
Description: Although the contemporary, minimalist-style decor is typical of Japanese restaurants, the cuisine will come as more of a surprise, with its magical blend of classic Japanese dishes made from Mediterranean ingredients, beautifully presented and full of flavour. There are two dining rooms: one overlooking the road, and the other with an open-view kitchen and sushi bar, where the chef serves an evening tasting menu for guests happy to put their faith in his imaginative improvisational skills.

Name: Piazza dei Mestieri
Description: Situated on a redeveloped industrial site and part of a training school, this restaurant offers a more concise menu at lunchtime with lower prices than the evening, but with the same high-quality cuisine. Our inspector recommends the spaghetti with spring onion and bottarga, accompanied by one of the craft beers produced on site. There’s also an attractive terrace for alfresco dining in fine weather.

Name: CiPASSO
Description: This contemporary bistro with a hint of vintage style in its decor now has a new location. The menu is inspired by Roman traditions, with the occasional imaginative twist and other more Mediterranean-inspired dishes, all showing a strong focus on seasonal ingredients. The excellent wine list includes a whole page dedicated to wines by the glass. Friendly yet professional service from the young team completes the picture.

Name: Osteria alle Testiere
Address: calle del Mondo Novo, sestiere  Castello 5801, Venice, 30122, Italy
Description: This restaurant, now one of the most popular bistros in Venice, started out as a typical Venetian “bacaro”. The cuisine focuses on traditional Mediterranean and Venetian dishes, including vegetables, many of which are grown in a kitchen garden on Sant'Erasmo island (Osti in Orto) – an initiative which sees a number of small restaurants coming together to grow and share produce. The menu changes in line with market availability. With just a few tables, booking well in advance is highly recommended.

Name: Bacchus
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Ideal for visitors to Olbia, this modern, fresh and young restaurant serves typical regional specialities alongside more imaginative fish dishes. In fine weather, ask for a table on the lovely terrace overlooking the swimming pool.

Name: Maso Runch-Hof
Description: Surrounded by woods, a trip to this restaurant housed in an 18C farmhouse is like taking a journey back in time. Take a seat in one of the wood-adorned Stube-style rooms and enjoy generous portions of delicious home-cooked Ladin specialities featured on a single tasting menu, including cajinci t’ega (spinach-filled ravioli), excellent pork ribs with polenta, and apple strudel. The small wine list has the same local focus, featuring labels from the Alto Adige region. A recent addition, the restaurant also now has a few spacious, welcoming chalets available for guests.

Name: Impronta
Description: Occupying the site of a restaurant that was highly successful in the 1980s and 90s, Impronta is home to a young local chef who showcases skills acquired in a leading Michelin-starred restaurant in Sicily. As a result of this experience, his enticing dishes have a light Mediterranean feel, embellished with the occasional personal twist.

Name: Antica Osteria Moirago
Description: This old monastery in Moirago, overlooking the Naviglio Pavese canal, was founded in 1250 and converted into an inn as early as 1478. Centuries may have passed, but the tradition of hospitality continues in the building’s enclosed painted portico, as well as in its two warm and atmospheric dining rooms. The chef’s Puglian origins explain the abundant use of vegetables and raw fish dishes, while in winter the cuisine takes on a more northern Italian flavour. Good selection of wines by the glass.

Name: Cuculia
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Wheelchair access
Description: This beautiful restaurant with a smart and elegant decor has the feel of a stylish French bistro with a small library-style dining room displaying books on cookery and other subjects. Chef Oliver Betancourt left his home country of Venezuela to train in well-known restaurants in France, Spain and Italy, experiences which have resulted in multi-faceted cuisine influenced by different traditions and prepared using seasonal Italian produce as well as more exotic ingredients such as kombu, soy sauce and koji. The menu offers a good selection of vegetarian dishes, as well as a few vegan options. The wine list includes extensive information on the different labels featured, including an excellent red from Bolgheri Acciderba.

Name: Locanda Viola
Description: In this elegant restaurant with chairs and tables of different designs and original workmanship, it is skilful chef Filippo Moriggi’s cuisine that really captures your attention. The interesting appetisers take guests on an exotic journey, featuring options such as empanadas, fish bao (steamed buns, also available with a barbecue sauce) and Chinese dumplings. Other dishes are more typically Italian in style, with pastas, risottos and Bergamo-style mutton all on the menu. Desserts include a selection of ice-cream and affogato.

Name: AlpiNN
Address: Plan de Corones, alt. 2275, Brunico, 39031, Italy
Description: Situated at an altitude of 2 000m in the Plan de Corones ski area, this restaurant stands next to Lumen, a museum dedicated to mountain photography. To get here, you take the cable-car from Riscone and then, in winter, walk for around 150m through the snow. This impressive project by Norbert Niederkofler, holder of three Michelin stars, showcases the chef’s “Cook the Mountain” philosophy, where a modern approach and Alpine traditions combine to create perfect dishes full of flavour and historic appeal. The memory lingers long after your return back down the mountain (NB: the last cable-car leaves at 5pm!).

Name: Duo
Address: via Cavour 7, San Felice del Benaco, 25010, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Counter dining,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: Situated in the historic centre of the charming small village of San Felice del Benaco, Duo is the project of young chefs Daniele Ghedini and Federico Pelizzari (the latter also oversees the front of house). Their personalised, modern cuisine is Mediterranean in style and features meat-based dishes, vegetarian options and fish recipes (salt- and freshwater), with a focus on freshly caught fish which even has its own dedicated tasting menu. This colourful restaurant also boasts an outdoor space shaded by a pergola and surrounded by walnut trees.

Name: Senso Alfio Ghezzi Lake Garda
Address: via IV Novembre 86, Limone sul Garda, 25010, Italy
Description: Eala is a new luxury, designer-style hotel jutting into the lake, where top chef Alfio Ghezzi from Trento is at the helm in the restaurant. The gourmet formula on offer here, already successfully tried and tested at the Mart in Rovereto, consists of just one single tasting menu (guests choose the number of courses and some of the dishes), with precise, well-balanced cuisine made from carefully selected seasonal ingredients, including plenty of vegetables.

Name: Al Petes
Description: Situated amid the alleyways of the historic centre, Al Petes has a pleasant contemporary feel and is run by young, welcoming and friendly owners. Marko’s menu demonstrates an obvious preference for seafood, most of which comes from the Adriatic, and which is served with Mediterranean and even occasional Asian influences. The surprise tasting menu is highly recommended. Just around the corner, the restaurant’s small hotel (James Joyce) is the ideal choice for overnight accommodation.

Name: La Foresteria
Address: Contrada Passo di Gurra  SP 79 km 91, Menfi, 92013, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Terrace
Description: A luxurious guesthouse belonging to the famous Sicilian winery Planeta and surrounded by beautiful vineyards is the setting for this restaurant serving top-quality Sicilian cuisine. Home-grown ingredients make an appearance in some dishes, while the extensive wine list obviously features a good selection of Planeta’s own labels.

Name: Ca' del Profeta
Description: Situated in a tranquil location overlooking the vineyards, this winery and elegant restaurant is owned by the “Prophet” Hernanes, a Brazilian footballer who played for many years in the Italian championship. The menu here features regional dishes alongside a few more creative options, while five modern guestrooms (some with a view) and a panoramic swimming pool complete the picture.

Name: i-Fame
Description: Enjoy creative cuisine made from excellent, locally sourced produce in this attractive restaurant. It is decorated in the same white colours and modern style as the hotel.

Name: Kirchsteiger
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Terrace
Description: This restaurant has long been one of the most interesting in the area. It has a pleasing combination of traditional and modern cuisine created by the expert chef. The dining rooms have the same blend of old and new with an elegant use of local materials in the decor. Ask for one of the newer guestrooms.

Name: Da Orlando
Description: Simply arriving in Cusago near Milan, where the imposing castle dominates the attractive centre, puts you in a good mood. At Da Orlando, the menu is equally balanced between top-quality fish dishes such as the “bollita di mare” and meat-based dishes that will delight food-lovers, such as snails with trumpet mushrooms and duck breast with ginger. Two elegant dining rooms are the perfect setting for a romantic evening, while the attractive outdoor space comes into its own in summer. A good restaurant with over 40 years of history.

Name: Da Ercole
Description: Situated on Crotone’s seafront, Da Ercole is a culinary institution for anyone who loves fish, with the benefit of 40 years in the business behind it! The salty tang of the Ionian sea is celebrated on an extensive menu, although if you really want to enjoy yourself to the full, let owner-chef and old-school host Ercole guide you in your choice (including some excellent raw fish dishes).

Name: La Rosa dei Venti
Address: via Piero della Francesca 34, Milan, 20154, Italy
Description: This small restaurant is perfect for anyone keen on fish prepared simply with a personal touch – and with the added bonus of providing good value for money. The restaurant belongs to the AIC network (Italian Association for Coeliacs) and therefore offers a good selection of gluten - free dishes, including bread and pasta.

Name: I Due Cippi dal 1976
Description: The first sight to greet you when you enter this restaurant is a barbecue grill for cooking meat; the meat itself can be seen ageing nearby, with numerous cuts and meats to choose from and the famous Chianina beef taking centre stage. The small yet elegant dining rooms, welcoming ambience and friendly service all add to the appeal, as does the excellent section of wines. Meals are served outdoors in summer.

Name: L'Ancora della Tortuga
Address: salita Cappuccini 4, Monterosso al Mare, 19016, Italy
Description: Decorated in maritime - style, this restaurant is literally perched on the cliff (one of its walls is actually rock). The views from its upper terrace are breathtaking. Fish takes pride of place on the menu, which also features a few meat dishes.

Name: Taverna dello Spuntino
Description: This Roman trattoria has a particularly striking interior. From its old tufa passageways converted into a wine cellar in the basement, to its charming dining rooms with brick - vaulted arches where hams, flasks of wine, fruit and antipasti all form an attractive display.

Name: Piacentino
Description: Restaurant with pension near the old town, where you can enjoy Piacentine dishes served outdoors in nice weather and in the airy indoors dining hall during the colder months. The rooms are in two styles, one with wrought iron beds and Arte Povera furniture, the other being more modern.

Name: Le Logge del Vignola
Description: This small establishment is a good spot in the old town centre. Its tables are a bit cramped but they have smart table settings and well - prepared, regional ingredients are served.

Name: Tubladel
Description: Although this restaurant with wood-adorned dining rooms has the rustic and romantic ambience of an old Alpine hut (the name “tubladel” is the Ladin for hay barn), it is actually situated just a stone’s throw from the centre of Ortisei. The cuisine focuses on local ingredients such as meat and game, with dishes such as venison pappardelle and roast pork shank on the menu, and very few fish options. Good selection of wines by the glass.

Name: La Corniola
Address: via dei Mastri Lombardi 24, Pescocostanzo, 67033, Italy
Description: Known throughout Italy for its pillow lace, the small town of Pescocostanzo in the Parco della Maiella is one of the most beautiful in Italy. It is also home to the Relais Ducale hotel and its La Corniola restaurant, which is renowned for its excellent modern Abruzzo cuisine, including delicious, seasonal dishes made from different vegetables, potatoes and onions grown in the hotel’s own kitchen gardens. Simple yet elegant dining room.

Name: Terre Alte
Address: via Olmadella 11, località Balignano, Longiano, 47020, Italy
Description: One of the best-known addresses in this region for fish enthusiasts, this restaurant serves freshly caught fish prepared in simple, traditional dishes that allow the quality of the flavour to shine through. A good wine list (particularly champagnes) and a panoramic terrace add to the appeal.

Name: Antico Morer
Description: Not far from the Duomo, this historic restaurant takes its name from the mulberry tree (morer in local dialect) that once stood in front of the building. Elegant, simple decor in the dining room, which is adorned with a wooden - beamed ceiling. The menu features fish and seafood, including a good choice of raw dishes.

Name: Ca' Mia
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: This welcoming restaurant in the hills surrounding Lake Alserio makes guests feel completely at home. The two young chefs with plenty of experience behind them create modern dishes with a preference for quick cooking methods and a focus on a wood-fired oven and barbecue, as well as fermented ingredients.

Name: Dulchemente
Description: A contemporary-style restaurant which serves modern dishes alongside simpler, more classic options, with a notable focus on fish. A splendid outdoor terrace for alfresco dining and friendly, professional staff complete the picture.

Name: Piccolo Lord
Address: corso San Maurizio 69 bis/g, Turin, 10124, Italy
Description: Professional service in a welcoming, modern restaurant run by a young couple. He works in the kitchen while she (having also worked as a chef in the past) runs the front of house. Delicious Mediterranean cuisine with a seasonal focus.

Name: Villa Fiordaliso
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Terrace
Description: Villa Fiordaliso is one of the beautiful early 20C villas that line the lake front. Surrounded by verdant grounds and extending out into the lake on a pontoon, the restaurant serves creative, modern cuisine. The chef is equally at ease with fish and meat dishes, while the extensive wine list suggests that you’ll have no problem finding your favourite wine here.

Name: Osteria Antico Brolo
Description: Situated in the upper part of the town near the Vittoriale estate, this rustic 18C building is the setting for regional cuisine prepared using seasonal ingredients. The charming small courtyard offers shade for summer dining, while the interior dining room also includes a single table on a small balcony which needs to be booked well in advance.

Name: Osteria del Borro
Address: località Borro 52, San Giustino Valdarno, 52024, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus
Description: Decorated in soft colours, the elegant gourmet restaurant on the first floor (lift available) serves classic regional dishes reinterpreted with a contemporary flavour and hint of modernity. At the Tuscan Bistro on the ground floor, the menu is simpler in style but just as delicious and firmly rooted in the traditions of the local area.

Name: Capriccio
Description: Young chef Graziano Accolla has returned to his native city where he serves creative cuisine of the highest quality, while at the same time raising Augusta’s gastronomic profile. Thanks to his experience in Michelin-starred restaurants, he offers highly interesting dishes which focus on the use of top-quality ingredients.

Name: Sora Maria e Arcangelo
Description: Those who judge only by appearance will walk on, those who do not will cross the threshold of this small restaurant to savour the delight of local recipes reinterpreted in modern form.

Name: Al Vecchio Convento
Description: Ask for a table in the main dining room, with a classic atmosphere and elegant furnishings, to taste the dishes of a cuisine, which is seasonal and mainly Tuscan.

Name: Le Cupole
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Situated on the sixth floor of the Grand Hotel Bristol, this restaurant is home to an experienced chef whose unique cuisine has a light modern touch and encompasses the whole of Italy, with a particular emphasis on regional specialities. Fish take pride of place on the menu, which also features vegetarian dishes and a few meat options. And last but not least, the restaurant’s roof-garden location gives it breathtaking views of the Portofino promontory.

Name: Filia Ristorante
Description: An intimate and modern restaurant with just five tables and a minimalist design (with the exception of the “hip-hop” bathroom). Filia expresses the full character of its owner Michael Silhavì who has chosen Borgo Trento, a residential district not far from the city centre, in which to fulfil his dream of opening his own restaurant. He serves two tasting menus here (although he also sensibly also offers à la carte options), which are creative in style and occasionally play with traditional recipes such as the “Polpo alla Luciana” octopus dish. Simpler, faster options available at lunchtime. A colourful restaurant in every respect!

Name: Tamo
Description: This new restaurant occupies  a historic palazzo in this small town. Served by the owner (outdoors in summer with views of Città Sant’Angelo in the distance), the cuisine is authentic, unfussy and prepared using top-quality ingredients with a focus on vegetables from a nearby farm.

Name: Gunè San Frediano
Address: via del Drago d'Oro 1r, Florence, 50124, Italy
Description: The chef at this small gastronomic restaurant serves cuisine which acts as a bridge between Basilicata and Tuscany, the two most significant regions in his life, resulting in creative, delicate and beautifully presented dishes.

Name: Milano
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: This historic restaurant, run by the same family for many years, is situated right on the lake (with its own private mooring), which can be best appreciated from the charming veranda. The current owner-chef has retained the cuisine’s classic style, while adding his own contemporary touch to top-quality meat and fish dishes (including freshwater fish).

Name: MARdiVINO
Description: Francesco is in the kitchen and his partner is front of house in this bright, modern and elegant restaurant serving beautifully prepared dishes in which fish takes pride of place. Contemporary cuisine with the occasional Puglian influence in a nod to the chef’s native origins.

Name: Kosmo Taste the Mountain
Description: Just a stone’s throw from the centre and also accessible from the ski slopes, this contemporary, Alpine-style restaurant boasts a spacious dining room and large picture windows. Traditional regional and mountain cuisine with a modern twist and a wine cellar focusing on mountain wines from producers working  sustainably.

Name: Gainn
Description: Since 2007, Gainn has showcased the fascinating and delicious flavours of colourful Korean cuisine, with its rice-based dishes, soups, meat, fish, plenty of vegetables and soya. The best way to experience the food here is to order a selection of different dishes to be shared with your dining companions. Those with a sweet tooth, be warned – there are no desserts on the menu.

Name: Cosmo Restaurant
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Although the cuisine at Cosmo is influenced by the ingredients and culinary traditions of Campania, this restaurant is also an excellent choice for those in search of more elaborate and creative fare. Top-quality, complex dishes prepared by two young chefs.

Name: Vitique
Address: via Citille 43/b, Greve in Chianti, 50022, Italy
Description: Providing a splash of modernity in the Florentine Chianti region, this restaurant is highly contemporary both in its decor and its cuisine, the latter available in the form of tasting menus only (guests can choose the number of courses they want). Meat and fish are cooked with expert precision and prepared with real creative flair.

Name: Guallina
Address: via Molino Faenza 19, località Guallina, Mortara, 27036, Italy
Description: Situated in a small house in an outlying village in the countryside, this is a simple, inviting restaurant where you can enjoy seasonal local cuisine. Excellent wines.

Name: Cavallino
Description: Il Cavallino, a long-established restaurant which pays tribute to Ferrari – a symbol of Maranello and Italy across the globe – now has the added attraction of Massimo Bottura’s creative cuisine. Traditional regional dishes, such as the delicious tortellini del Tortellante, are given interesting, personalised twists, as evidenced by the crème caramel made with 36-month-aged Parmesan cheese, chives and 12-year-old balsamic vinegar. Trendy decor, plus a flower-decked garden.

Name: Osteria del Tasso
Address: via Bolgherese km 3,9, località San Walfredo, Bolgheri, 57020, Italy
Description: Just a stone’s throw from the famous Viale dei Cipressi avenue in one of Italy’s best-known wine-producing areas, this restaurant occupies one of the region’s most famous wineries, namely Guado al Tasso, renowned for its excellent wines. In fine weather, guests can dine in the shade of plane trees looking out over the vineyards. Simple, delicious and well-prepared cuisine, mostly traditional in style, plus specialities such as cured hams and grilled dishes.

Name: La Madernassa
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: Situated in one of the most magical locations of the Roero region, this restaurant boasts a terrace with breathtaking views of the Langhe. Here, Giuseppe D'Errico serves dishes on a series of set menus with surprise options that vary according to the chef’s inspiration. The cuisine isn’t necessarily rooted in the region but features top-quality ingredients that are presented in the style of famous contemporary artists such as Jackson Pollock and Alberto Burri – dishes are also given unusual and imaginative names such as “Grande Rosso” and “Inedita Croccantezza”.

Name: Vivace
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Wheelchair access
Description: Situated right in the heart of Brescia, this new 4.0 restaurant with geothermic heating and technologically controlled energy serves contemporary-style cuisine in a modern bistro with a “wine theatre” in the middle of the dining room. There’s also an attractive space with a brick vaulted ceiling in the basement.

Name: Mogano
Address: via del Praticello Alto 7, Formello, 00060, Italy
Description: Aiming to promote craft beers as a worthy pairing for gourmet cuisine, the Faenza family opened Mogano – a modern, elegant restaurant with a wood-inspired decor, soft lighting and just five tables, right next to their Ritual Lab brewery. One of the sons (Matteo, the chef here) greets guests before dinner with an aperitif served in the kitchen. With plenty of international culinary experience behind him, he combines Italian flavours with influences from all around the world. Despite the focus on beer, a wine list is also available.

Name: Zàghara Restaurant
Description: Housed in the elegant Relais Villa Flora, this restaurant occupies a natural terrace with breathtaking views of the Nissene hills. The dishes are predominantly regional in style yet reinterpreted with a modern twist. There’s also a good wine selection with a focus on Sicilian and Italian labels.

Name: Materia Prima
Address: Località Piana Santa Liberata, Castel di Sangro, 67031, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: This restaurant boasts a pleasant terrace overlooking a small man-made lake used for water sports, as well as a simple, modern dining room with picture windows offering the same view. The minimalist style of the decor is echoed in the cuisine, which is creative with occasionally more technical twists. The desserts offer a fitting end to your meal – the interesting selection includes one striking dish featuring the unusual combination of chocolate and saffron.

Name: Vecio Macello
Description: Although Vecio Macello has retained a few unusual features on the ceiling from its former life as a meat-processing plant (such as the old pipes used to provide steam for the plant’s pasteurisation and meat preparation processes), this restaurant now has a strong focus on fish. The menu offers a selection of raw dishes and classic seafood recipes alongside a few regionally influenced meat options.

Name: Scatto
Description: From Turin’s beautiful Piazza San Carlo, you head through an inner courtyard to this restaurant’s modern dining room with its open-view kitchen. Whether you opt for the à la carte or tasting menu, you’ll find a balance of traditional Piedmontese and more creative dishes, all of remarkable quality, in keeping with the superb wine list.

Name: Antica Osteria il Ronchettino
Description: The name seems to originate from the broken horseshoe (ronchetto) of Napoleon, who in 1800 appears to have stayed the night here, where there was indeed a post house where horses were shoed. Later converted into a bakery, butcher’s shop, but also a trattoria with an annexed bowling alley, today it is a restaurant of rustic elegance; the regional cuisine expresses itself in specialties such as fried brains and the ever-present Milanese-style cutlet that here becomes even “imperial”, definitely to be shared.

Name: Ichikawa
Description: Ichikawa is one of the culinary masters who played a part in introducing Japanese cuisine to Italy. After decades in the country working in various restaurants, this chef has finally opened his own eatery, where he serves top-quality Japanese cuisine ranging from familiar favourites such as sushi and sashimi to other less-known family dishes and street food from the land of the Rising Sun. A good place to discover the joys of Japanese cuisine!

Name: Le Macine
Address: via Lino Carlo del Favero 11, Vittorio Veneto, 31029, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Housed in a recently renovated 18C mill on the banks of the Meschio river, this restaurant is run by brothers Giuseppe (front of house) and Adriano (in the kitchen), who serve top-quality cuisine with its roots in local traditions and the occasional imaginative twist with warmth and professionalism. It is even more appealing in summer, when meals are served on the beautiful outdoor terrace.

Name: Le Cementine
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: This rustic, vintage-style country restaurant run by the Alajmo brothers stands on the banks of the Sile river, just a few minutes from the Venetian lagoon, and overlooks a vegetable garden, vineyard and beautiful green meadows. The cuisine demonstrates a strong focus on seasonal, regional ingredients, featuring meat and fish alike, with vegetables taking centre stage in many of the dishes.

Name: Casa Vicina
Description: Renowned over the years for its traditional Piedmontese cuisine, Casa Vicina is situated near the Lingotto factory (easily accessible by metro if you don’t have a car) on the top floor of the “Green Pea”, a building that showcases sustainable and environmentally friendly products. Meat dishes (including specialities such as Fassone steak in a tuna sauce, rabbit and ossobuco-filled agnolotti pasta) dominate the main courses although fish options are also available. Make sure you leave room for desserts such as ice cream, zabaglione and Ivrea tart.

Name: La Società Milano
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Situated near Porta Venezia and its lush gardens, Giulia and Andrea’s restaurant boasts a warm and original ambience. Three dining rooms adorned with tapestries and an entrance with a fine white marble fireplace act as the setting for Mediterranean cuisine with the occasional exotic twist. Don’t miss the amberjack caponata in which the ceviche flavours contrast with the sweetness of the fried breaded aubergine.

Name: Campocori
Address: via di Santa Maria de' Calderari 49, Rome, 00186, Italy
Description: This gourmet fine-dining restaurant, the brainchild of the South African designer Tristan Du Plessis, has arrived in the Italian capital where it’s overseen by chef Alessandro Pietropaoli. Here, choose from the à la carte or opt for one of the tasting menus (5 or 7 courses). Elegant, contemporary and cosmopolitan cuisine.

Name: Radicì
Description: Situated beneath the walls of Castello Oldofredi in the centre of this delightful lakeside village, not far from the lake itself, this restaurant with a young team at the helm has a light contemporary feel, both in its decor and cuisine. The modern design contrasts with the restaurant’s setting in a historic building, while the dishes are inspired by the recipes and ingredients of the region. Influences from elsewhere in Italy as well as further afield are also in evidence on the menu.

Name: Delicato
Description: Situated in a picturesque medieval hilltop village in the province of Rieti on the border with Umbria, this restaurant serves cuisine that is influenced by different regions and traditions. Choose between the minimalist-style dining rooms with exposed stone walls and, in fine weather, a charming outdoor space at the foot of Contigliano’s church. Here, chef Carlotta Delicato brings out the best of local ingredients in dishes that are kept deliberately simple and unfussy yet are full of flavour. We highly recommend the “spaghettone mare e lago” with a light brunoise of courgettes. As the restaurant is situated in Lazio, guests can enjoy good local wines made by small-scale producers, such as the Cabernet Sauvignon Masseria Baroni, which is of medium intensity with broad and pronounced aromas. .

Name: Nugolo
Description: A restaurant with a friendly ambience and a chic, colourful decor and design that includes an open-view kitchen. In the latter, the young, talented chef uses seasonal ingredients to create contemporary-style dishes with an imaginative twist. The enthusiastic front-of-house team provides friendly and attentive service.

Name: Osteria Ricanatti
Description: Enjoy delicious updated regional cuisine made from carefully chosen ingredients at this restaurant, where all the vegetables are sourced from the property’s own kitchen garden just a few kilometres from the village. Dishes are showcased on various tasting menus and an à la carte, and feature options such as pecorino cheese and potato tartare with a chimichurri sauce (a typical green sauce from Argentina), and paccheri pasta cooked al dente with a sauce made from two types of tomato, raw red tuna and fried capers. Enthusiasm and modesty are the key characteristics of the chef at this restaurant, which also offers a warm welcome and excellent service.

Name: TerraMadre
Description: This small, modern and minimalist restaurant is tucked away among the alleyways of the historic centre. The predominance of black combined with a dark colour scheme gives the dining room an elegant feel, while the cuisine, prepared using regional ingredients, is contemporary and creative in style.

Name: Altatto Bistrot
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Wheelchair access
Description: Situated on the edge of old Milan, this former bakery has been converted into a tiny restaurant serving vegetarian cuisine in a contemporary-style setting. The two tasting menus include delicious, colourful and beautifully presented dishes which can also be ordered à la carte. Booking is essential.

Name: Altriménti
Description: An informal and contemporary restaurant which is elegant and yet retains a bistro feel. The cuisine is modern with meat and fish dishes featured on the menu, as well as a good number of vegetarian options. Good wine list.

Name: La Torre
Description: Housed in the picturesque medieval castle of Spilimbergo, this restaurant boasts a splendid façade adorned with 14C frescoes, plus two rustic yet elegant dining rooms. If you’re looking for somewhere for a romantic dinner and modern cuisine, then this is the place for you!

Name: Comi 107
Description: Situated near the lake at the entrance to a narrow street dotted with various shops, this small contemporary-style restaurant boasts an equally tiny outdoor space for summer dining and is run with skill and professionalism by a young couple. The friendly, welcoming wife oversees the front of house, while her husband creates dishes full of character in the kitchen.

Name: Fè Ristorante
Description: Situated near the centre, this restaurant occupies a small group of eight carefully restored trulli which provide an elegant and charming setting, with just 20 seats arranged throughout its small buildings. Traditional, regional cuisine reinterpreted with a skilful modern twist.

Name: Cucina Rambaldi
Description: Regional dishes with the occasional subtle contemporary twist are to the fore here. The chef’s culinary techniques bring out all the flavour of the carefully selected and preserved ingredients, with a focus on cooking temperatures and the cut of the meat, resulting in excellent cuisine. The menu also features a few specialities from Ferrara, the chef’s native city.

Name: Madama Piola
Description: The aptly named Madama Piola (in Piedmontese dialect, “piola” is a village inn) has a simple yet attractive and friendly ambience that serves as a backdrop for typical Piedmontese dishes. Highlights include the memorable stuffed onion, as well as tonnato, braised cheeks and hot zabaglione. Regional wines take pride of place on the wine list, which includes a good selection by the glass.

Name: Osteria Bakaré
Address: Via Venezia 30, Peschiera del Garda, 37019, Italy
Description: This small but beautifully kept restaurant set back from the lakeside serves contemporary-style cuisine that includes a good balance of meat and fish recipes, all made from top-quality, seasonal ingredients. Dishes are creative and full of individual character, with the occasional nod to Asia. Attractive enclosed veranda.

Name: Carlo e Camillo
Description: This quiet and elegant bistro, the Grand Hotel Sitea’s second restaurant, offers a charming setting in which to enjoy skilfully prepared Piedmontese-influenced cuisine. The venue is also perfect for an aperitif, with excellent wines and cocktails.

Name: Remo Villa Cariolato
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Long recommended by the Michelin Guide, the historic Remo moved a few years ago from its old premises to this beautiful villa typical of the Veneto region, once the home of an Italian hero, one of Garibaldi’s famous “Thousand”. Large and small dining rooms, perfect for special events, act as the backdrop for good regional and Italian cuisine, with a menu divided between meat and fish options. The latter comes almost exclusively from Chioggia market.

Name: PS Ristorante
Address: via di Petriolo 7, Cerreto Guidi, 50050, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Counter dining,Garden or park,Great view,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Situated in the beautiful countryside outside Cerreto Guidi, PS Ristorante is housed in the magnificent Medici Villa Petriolo which is also home to 36 luxurious guestrooms. The restaurant’s appeal is enhanced not only by the charm of the villa and its delightful garden (overlooked by the restaurant terrace), but also by the property’s delicious home-produced ingredients, such as extra-virgin olive oil, wine, Cinta Senese pork, meat and chicken, produce from the kitchen garden, traditional cereals and other zero-mile ingredients, all reinterpreted in a creative, modern style by the chef (as in the egg and artichoke dish). The estate’s wine is also highly recommended – we particularly enjoyed the organic red Golpaia, a medium-structured blend of Merlot and Sangiovese with characteristic soft aromas.

Name: Diana's Place
Description: Facing the square in front of Termini station, this wine bar-cum-restaurant is striking for its fresh and creative approach to cuisine. Nearly all the top-quality ingredients are local and can be purchased from the food counter. The excellent staff are happy to help with your choice of wine, which is also available by the glass.

Name: Enotavola Pino
Description: The entrance to this restaurant through a wine-bar can be misleading, as you are eventually led to simpler – yet still attractive – dining rooms. In this wine-themed setting, enjoy delicious fish and seafood dishes with the occasional creative twist, accompanied by a particularly extensive selection of wines by the glass. A highly recommended address for fish lovers, situated right in the historic centre of Padova.

Name: Il Presidente
Description: This restaurant situated in an alleyway in the historic centre just a few metres from Lucera’s cathedral was once home to the stables of an old palazzo. Nowadays, the dining room, which is crowned by a stone-vaulted ceiling and decorated in shades of black and gold, is divided into small sections. In the middle room, two glass cabinets display the wine selection, which includes over 400 different labels. The Mediterranean cuisine served here is modern and colourful, with vegetables often accompanying the fish and seafood (red tuna, swordfish, prawns, scampi and a delicious seafood focaccia). The ingredients are more important than the technique, resulting in dishes that are full of flavour!

Name: Osteria della Tana
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Terrace
Description: Occupying the same red house as chef Alessandro Dal Degan’s gourmet restaurant, the Osteria is where this chef turns his attention to more traditional dishes (meat and fish alike), which are often typical of the Veneto. There’s one highly recommended exception, however, namely the carbonara dell’Osteria, prepared with top-quality ingredients from the region. Also popular are the baccalà alla vicentina (dried cod) and the tripe, both of which feature on a menu with a wide selection, including renowned dishes from the chef’s Michelin-starred restaurant. Full-bodied flavours that will delight the palate.

Name: Trattoria da Me
Description: This lively and very busy trattoria run by the energetic Elisa owes its success to a winning combination of traditional dishes (the fresh hand-made pasta, also sold in the shop next door, is a particular highlight) and specialities reinterpreted with a touch of imagination by the female chef, such as the ossobuco cut lengthways. You may like to try both by choosing a typical Bolognese dish as a starter followed by one of the chef’s more original options for your main course.

Name: Seta Sushi Restaurant
Description: It was friendship and passion for Japanese cuisine that prompted two young business partners to open this quiet, welcoming restaurant in the heart of Bologna. Situated in a courtyard with medieval origins, Seta Sushi Restaurant has a modern bistro-style dining room, as well as plenty of outdoor space for summer dining. The menu features an impressive selection of traditional Japanese dishes with the occasional personalised touch, all made from top-quality ingredients. Don’t worry if you’re new to Japanese cuisine – Maurilio is front of house to offer guests friendly, expert advice on both food and beverage. The latter includes a choice of sake for those wishing to immerse themselves fully in the Japanese dining experience.

Name: La Chandelle
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Decorated in the same classic, elegant style as the famous Hermitage hotel in which it is located, this spacious restaurant offers an impressive menu of modern yet unfussy dishes alongside a selection of more traditional options. Grilled meats are cooked over the imposing charcoal grill in the evenings, while the fine views of the surrounding mountains and an excellent wine list add to the enjoyment of your dining experience.

Name: Balìce
Description: The chef patron Giacomo Caravello in the short span of a few years has created his “space” in the area, definitely becoming one of the best places in Milazzo: the contemporary interiors are truly refined and airy, while the cuisine–which grows year after year–is assured thanks to modern techniques and Sicilian and Mediterranean references. The wine selection is accompanied by an intriguing range of cocktails.

Name: L'Ostì
Address: strada Sassongher 2, Corvara in Badia, 39033, Italy
Description: A minimalist-style restaurant featuring a wood decor, an extensive display of bottles, and some windows boasting partial yet splendid views of the Dolomites. The chef here prepares creative cuisine using local ingredients alongside produce sourced from other regions. The wine list includes a wide selection of natural wines.

Name: La Locanda dei Beccaria
Description: Housed in the village’s historic wine cellar, this well - kept, rustic - style restaurant with typical wooden ceilings serves traditional, regional cuisine.

Name: Palazzo Petrucci Pizzeria
Address: piazza San Domenico Maggiore 5-7, Naples, 80134, Italy
Description: Situated right in the city centre, this pizzeria with the same name and owners as the gourmet restaurant has a contemporary, minimalist feel, plus an attractive outdoor space on the piazza. Among the excellent pizzas made from top-quality ingredients, you’ll find a few created by the young, skilful pizza chef, as well as one by chef Scarallo. Don’t miss the desserts!

Name: Cortile Arabo
Description: In one of Sicily’s most iconic fortified villages which once prospered as a tuna fishery and is now a popular tourist attraction, Cortile Arabo serves carefully prepared and occasionally elaborate dishes of the highest quality, with a focus on fish (the menu also features a few meat dishes). The terrace on the rocks overlooking the sea, where the sound of the waves provides a soothing backdrop, is one of the highlights here.

Name: Acciuga
Description: This restaurant with a simple dining room and open-view kitchen serves some of the most interesting fish cuisine in the Della Vittoria district. Chef Federico Delmonte skilfully searches out “poor” varieties of fish which are nonetheless full of flavour on an open menu that is adjusted according to the catch of the day. The chef’s native Fano makes an appearance in a few recipes from the Marche, including the famous brodetto (a typical fish soup).

Name: Giannino dal 1899
Description: A renowned name in Milan, this restaurant is the setting for a Mediterranean cuisine  with an international twist. Although recently renovated, the dining room has an attractive old-fashioned feel with old photographs of celebrities who have eaten here since it opened more than 120 years ago.

Name: Bottega Lucia
Description: Bottega Lucia serves a cuisine which is mainly Italian in style, with the addition of a few specialities from the Iberian Peninsula and other countries. Home-made pasta, meat and fish can be enjoyed in an attractive New York-style bistro, while the American bar serves drinks and a selection of delicious, tempting snacks in the evening.

Name: Concezione Restaurant
Description: This minimalist-style restaurant is home to one of the most interesting young chefs in Catania. In this historic building with beautiful ceilings, enjoy top-quality Sicilian cuisine created by Manuel Tropea, who focuses in particular on specialities from Catania which he interprets in a highly personalised way with a real focus on tradition. Dishes such as “L’Asina e la lattuga” and “Good morning in Catania” are good examples. The chef’s surprise menu takes guests on a culinary journey full of contrasts which is inspired by his own memories and experiences.

Name: Meraviglioso Osteria Moderna
Address: largo Gelso 16, Polignano a Mare, 70044, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus
Description: This attractive, welcoming modern restaurant stands in Polignano’s main street, scene of the town’s evening “passeggiata”, not far from the statue of the great Domenico Modugno, a native of this beautiful town. Although the lunch menu is simple in style, it is still inspired by fresh fish and seafood, while in the evening the young yet experienced chef creates more imaginative and inventive fare. There’s a convenient private car park nearby: if you want to take advantage of this, make sure you advise the restaurant of your arrival time.

Name: Gennaro Amitrano
Description: The large picture windows at this restaurant offer fine views of the Tyrrhenian sea, while the menu features imaginative recipes with a focus on fish and seafood. The most popular dishes include “Mamma Maria’s parmigiana”, the fish and shellfish soup, and the lemon dessert.

Name: Locanda Perbellini al Mare
Description: Enjoy imaginative Sicilian dishes created by multi-starred Michelin chef Perbellini in this beach restaurant that was once a family-run trattoria. The delightful natural setting acts as the perfect backdrop for Giancarlo’s original and exciting cuisine.

Name: Il Giardinetto
Address: piazza Garibaldi 10, Mandello del Lario, 23826, Italy
Description: Looking out over the calm blue water, this classic restaurant serves traditional cuisine with the occasional imaginative twist. Fish from the lake feature on the menu, as do meat and seafood options with something for everyone. There’s also a small outdoor terrace where guests can enjoy a pre- or post-dinner drink.

Name: Locale
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus
Description: Situated within a palazzo full of history, from the medieval basement to the Renaissance-style architecture of the restaurant itself, Locale is also home to an old courtyard with a lounge bar and large cocktail counter, as well as some beautiful rooms to the rear of the building. Enjoy creative, innovative cuisine with personalised touches influenced by the chef’s professional experience around the world (Australia, Japan, France). Our inspector particularly enjoyed the Risoni pasta with cuttlefish liver and cherry tomatoes.

Name: Fàula
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Fàula is the restaurant at the Casa Langa hotel, a large property which opens out like an amphitheatre to offer panoramic views of the valley. Here, the young chef skilfully creates cuisine which blends the culinary traditions of the Piedmont with more modern dishes. A good selection of wines from the region, plus a biodynamic kitchen garden add to the appeal.

Name: Asina Luna
Address: via della Resistenza 23, Peschiera Borromeo, 20068, Italy
Description: A restaurant with an attractive atmosphere, thanks to its profusion of wood, soft lighting and contemporary colour scheme. Meat aged for different periods takes pride of place on the menu.
