Sourced from different countries, it includes sweet Piedmontese Vicciola beef fed on hazelnuts and tender and delicately marbled Australian Scottona beef. Good selection of strongly flavoured and aged meat options.

Name: Il Barolino
Description: The friendliness and Emilian genuineness of the Barolo brothers and of the whole team cheers a break here where you can enjoy the authentic regional cuisine. Parmesan cream tortellini are a must: large portions and top quality of these little pasta bundles still strictly made by hand! The room is simple and suitable above all for informal meetings among friends and colleagues.

Name: Il Rivale al Lago
Address: via Marconi 93, Padenghe sul Garda, 25080, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Situated just a stone’s throw from the lake, this multi-faceted restaurant serves classic Italian dishes, often with a creative twist, alongside top-quality international ingredients such as Cantabrian anchovies and Japanese Wagyu beef. Grilled meats and vegetable dishes also make an appearance on the menu.

Name: Lillotatini
Description: Situated in the heart of a small medieval castle-hamlet, this traditional-style restaurant with an attractive terrace on the historic square provides the setting for local specialities such as freshwater fish and truffles in season. There’s also a wine boutique on the same piazza (reached as soon as you come into the historic centre), which sells typical local produce and a good selection of wine. The latter also features on the restaurant’s wine list, with the family on hand to offer recommendations.

Name: Boccon DiVino
Address: via Traversa dei Monti 201, località Colombaio Tozzi, Montalcino, 53024, Italy
Description: In a farmhouse on the edges of town, this restaurant has a rustic dining area with modern tables and chairs and a beautiful summer terrace with a view. Authentic local dishes.

Name: Il Giardino "Da Felicin"
Description: A bastion of classic Piedmontese cuisine, this restaurant housed in a beautiful period palazzo boasts a panoramic terrace and a romantic garden for alfresco dining. The dining rooms echo the palazzo’s sumptuous and traditional feel, as does the timeless, regional cuisine which is carefully prepared and full of delicious flavours. The building is also home to an “albergo diffuso” hotel, with some guestrooms in the building itself and others dotted around the village, including in Palazzo Boeri which also has a small spa (reservation required). The owners are happy to share their knowledge of the Langhe, either on their own guided tours or visits led by another local expert.

Name: Antica Locanda dell'Orco
Description: Fans of Piedmontese cuisine will find one of its best exponents in this restaurant located at the end of a beautiful porticoed street in the historic centre. Savour some of Italy’s most exciting regional cooking, such as snails, bagna caoda, agnolotti pasta, a few (mainly freshwater) fish dishes, braised and boiled meats, “finanziera” stew and some extraordinary desserts – all prepared in magnificent style.

Name: Le Vele
Address: via Litoranea Sud 71, Bagni 70, Misano Adriatico, 47843, Italy
Description: This modern, minimalist - style restaurant is practically on the beach and almost within touching distance of the sea. It specialises in fish dishes with a contemporary flavour.

Name: Risorgimento
Description: This restaurant situated in the centre of Sirmione just a stone’s throw from the lake is striking for its elegant outdoor terrace. This refined setting provides the backdrop for creative meat and fish dishes full of individual character. A fine display of wines adorns the shelves in the lounge-cum-wine bar on the first floor.

Name: Giardinetto
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: Situated on the lakeshore in the elegant Hotel Giardinetto (now approaching its centenary), this restaurant boasts stunning views of the lake and San Giulio island. The focus here is on Mediterranean cuisine with the occasional imaginative twist, while the hotel’s Roof Top Bar is the perfect place for an aperitif or after-dinner drink.

Name: Kro
Address: via Tollarini 70/c, località Pontagna di Temù, Ponte di Legno, 25050, Italy
Description: The courteous service, stylish mountain decor of wood and stone, and regional cuisine with a modern twist are just some of the attractions of this restaurant, whose name loosely translates as “inn”. A real treat for the eyes and the tastebuds!

Name: Trattoria di Campagna
Cuisine: Cuisine from the Aosta Valley, Modern Cuisine
Description: This famous trattoria, now run by the third generation of the same family, serves traditional, seasonal cuisine from the Aosta valley, enhanced by the occasional imaginative and personalised touch. The new well-stocked wine cellar includes a table for a dozen guests, while sommelier Beatrice is on hand to assist guests with their choice of bottle. Excellent array of delicacies from the dessert trolley.

Name: Makorè
Description: Makorè’s new gourmet venture offers guests a delightful dining experience where the focus is on vegetables, as well as fish from the adjacent fishmongers. The chef demonstrates his culinary skills and techniques on three surprise tasting menus (of different lengths) and an à la carte, featuring dishes such as the familiar yet far from ordinary grilled squid (with a fragrant tuna and stracciatella stuffing) and a selection of boiled fish including cod tongue, ventresca tuna, tuna and cuttlefish sausage, gurnard, giardiniera vegetables and potatoes. We asked the excellent sommelier for recommendations and enjoyed a deep-gold Abate wine made from red Fortana grapes in line with local tradition. An elegant restaurant that has really made its mark in Ferrara.

Name: Lo Stornello
Description: Offering quality and professionalism in a tourist setting, this small restaurant is popular with locals as well as visitors. The menu focuses on imaginatively presented Mediterranean cuisine.

Name: Il Chiosco di Bacco
Description: This restaurant boasts a rural location in the Montefeltro region, to which half the menu is dedicated (fresh home-made pastas, salumi, porchetta-style rabbit etc). The other half focuses on meat dishes, with an interesting selection of steaks and ribs from Italian and Scottish breeds (including more expensive beef that has been left to age for a month). You’ll find the perfect wine pairing on the excellent wine list.

Name: Antica Moka
Description: Situated on the Via Emilia, this elegant, owner-run restaurant has for decades been renowned for its top-quality regional cuisine with an updated twist, as well as its reinterpreted fish specialities. Our inspector very much enjoyed the cuisine here, with a particular mention for the home-made pastas and excellent wine selection.

Name: Almatò
Description: Situated in the elegant, residential streets of the Prati district, this modern, minimalist-style restaurant is the setting for top-quality creative cuisine. For the most part, the menu eschews traditional Lazio dishes making this a good choice for anyone looking for something a little different.

Name: Razzo
Description: A quiet restaurant with a relaxed, young and modern feel serving contemporary cuisine prepared from seasonal, regional products. Charming romantic outdoor area with soft lighting.

Name: 3.0 Ciro Cascella
Description: Fans of Neapolitan pizza will be in their element at this restaurant, where the pizzas are light, with a larger and softer crust, thanks to the long fermentation and leavening process – some people come here simply to eat the crust, it’s so good. There’s also a wide choice of excellent toppings, including top-quality ingredients from Campania. Gluten-free options and dough made from different flours are also available.

Name: Baracca - Storica Hostaria
Description: A classic, attractively elegant restaurant which boasts an extensive choice of dishes on its menu. The varied options here range from meat to fish dishes, often prepared in regional recipes such as tagliatelle with duck ragù and toasted hazelnuts, chicken liver risotto, Vicenza-style baccalà and meat casserole.

Name: Nascostoposto
Description: Easily found despite its name (nascosto posto means “hidden place”), this restaurant lies in the alleyways of Terni’s old town. In its modern, minimalist-style dining room, an enthusiastic couple (she runs the front of house, while he’s in the kitchen) delight their guests with delicious and imaginative cuisine with regional, Italian and unexpectedly exotic influences.

Name: Duanima
Description: This is one of Cagliari’s most interesting restaurants – a real must if you find yourself visiting Sardinia’s capital city. In its long, narrow dining room with modern furnishings, enjoy simple, unfussy cuisine that is full of intense flavours. Most of the dishes are influenced by the chef’s experience working abroad, while also demonstrating his re-connection with his native island, with a focus on Sardinia’s top-quality ingredients.

Name: Adelaide
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Although it’s not obvious from the exterior, once you’ve crossed the threshold of the Vilòn hotel you step into a succession of highly decorated rooms that are full of charm. The cuisine is of the highest quality, showcasing dishes from chef Gabriele Muro’s native Campania alongside the famous pasta specialities of his adopted city (amatriciana, carbonara, cacio e pepe etc), and finishing with the superb “l’oro di Procida” dessert.

Name: Al Persef
Description: A small yet very comfortable dining room with large windows and just a few tables provides the setting for modern, creative cuisine prepared by a young and ambitious chef. Locally sourced ingredients are prioritised here, plus there’s an excellent wine list.

Name: CENERE - Museum & Bistrot
Description: Fans of Campanian cuisine will be in their element at this restaurant situated opposite the archaeological site. Here, the chef serves traditional regional favourites alongside more creative recipes, often prepared using local specialities such as purple artichoke from Schito, chickpeas from Teano, Provola cheese from Agerola, red sausage from Castelpoto and Black Casertona pork. Of the two dining rooms, the one in the cellar is particularly charming.

Name: Livello 1
Address: via Duccio di Buoninsegna 25, Rome, 00142, Italy
Description: Situated in the suburbs off the main tourist trail, this fish restaurant also has a fishmonger’s next door. The fish and seafood cuisine served here is highly interesting, featuring modern recipes made from top-quality ingredients. There’s also a small lounge in which to enjoy a cocktail, plus a selection of good wines. The open-view kitchen allows guests to observe the skilful chef at work.

Name: W Villadorata Country Restaurant
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Great view,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: Part of the Country House Villadorata resort in the hills outside Noto, this restaurant boasts a delightful setting with the sea as a backdrop, surrounded by gardens which provide many of the vegetables used in the cuisine. Viviana Varese, a Michelin-starred chef from Milan, is in partnership here with Matteo Carnaghi, who is at the helm in the kitchen, with excellent results. The cooking is rooted in Sicilian ingredients, with one weekday evening in summer dedicated entirely to barbecue-grilled dishes.

Name: Josto
Description: One of Cagliari’s most interesting restaurants, Josta boasts two small dining rooms with an original decor that combines modern design with a few traditional features – the room by the entrance has the open-view kitchen to the rear. The menu focuses on Sardinian specialities reinterpreted with a contemporary twist, such as the delicious ham (from a typical Sardinian breed of pig), fregula pasta, mullet, and traditional Saba dessert.

Name: Bramea
Address: viale Villa d'Errico 10, Palazzo San Gervasio, 85026, Italy
Description: This gourmet restaurant with just a few tables is run by two young friends, now business partners at Bramea, with one at the helm in the kitchen, the other front of house. Extensive tasting menus are the focus here, featuring creative and original dishes often made from local ingredients. The end result is fascinating and of the highest quality.

Name: Toe Drûe
Address: via Corsi 44 r, Sestri Ponente, 16154, Italy
Description: Soak up the ambience of historic Genova in this restaurant which serves specialities such as panissa rice, seafood salad and Ligurian fish dishes in its informal and comfortable dining room. The building dates back to the early 19C: fans of naval history may be interested to know that the REX transatlantic liner was built right opposite. There’s also a small lounge space where you can savour a glass of wine and a selection of cheeses.

Name: Dimora Ulmo
Description: The three tasting menus (Contaminazioni, Dimora Ulmo and A mano libera) served at this restaurant housed in an old restored palazzo with a splendid summer terrace overlooking the Sassi feature a balance of modern cuisine and traditional local dishes. The dining room is equally attractive, while the interesting wine list includes labels from the region alongside a selection of wines from elsewhere in Italy and further afield.

Name: Fattoria delle Torri
Description: A small slice of paradise in the historic centre of Modica, where the daughters of owner-chef Peppe Barone continue the family culinary tradition while adding their youthful influence to the innovative and yet traditional cuisine served here. In fine weather, dine among lemon trees on the attractive outdoor terrace.

Name: Momento al 25
Description: Housed in a late-19C palazzo, this restaurant serves a good selection of meat and fish dishes with both traditional and creative cuisine on the menu. Delicious flavours typical of the Emilia region.

Name: Buca di Bacco
Description: The seafood specialities, the care in the choice of rare produce and the originality of the Proprietor characterise this establishment, situated as it is in the basement of a building.

Name: Da Miky
Address: via Fegina 104, Monterosso al Mare, 19016, Italy
Description: Situated right on the seafront, Miky is one of the best restaurants for fish (including the famous Monterosso anchovies) in the region, serving cuisine which is more and more exciting and individual every year. There’s also a small shop selling local produce.

Name: Osteria Il Maialetto
Address: via Della Repubblica 348, Monsummano Terme, 51015, Italy
Description: This lively restaurant with a young, vibrant atmosphere stands next to the butcher’s shop run by the same family. The menu features delicious Tuscan cuisine, including dishes such as pappa al pomodoro and Florentine steak, which you choose from the display counter. Good wines and friendly service add to the appeal.

Name: Posillipo
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Boasting a superb location above Gabicce Monte, this excellent restaurant run by the third generation of the same family offers breathtaking views of the Romagna coast. Posillipo’s superb fish dishes have made the restaurant a must in the region, with options ranging from raw fish to traditional pasta specialities and delicious main courses (fish fillets, catch of the day, fried options etc). There’s also a tempting dessert trolley and an excellent wine list.

Name: La Pineta
Address: via Gualco 82, località Struppa, Genoa, 16165, Italy
Description: Now a gastronomic institution in the city, in a secluded setting immersed in nature, La Pineta occupies the ground floor of a nondescript building in which the simple, “dated” yet comfortable decor provides the backdrop. Although there is a menu (but no wine list), the dishes are usually announced in person at your table by the owners. Simple, traditional and abundant cuisine which is mainly cooked on the open grill in the centre of the room, including meat (its signature speciality) and fish.

Name: Stefano Paganini alla Corte degli Alfieri
Description: Occupying a superb 17C castle, this restaurant has two dining rooms: one is decorated with works by local artists which change throughout the year, while the other, more romantic in feel, is adorned with roses and boasts splendid frescoed ceilings. There’s no choice here, just a tasting menu (although guests can select just a few courses if they wish), but the cuisine is of excellent quality and offers good value for money.

Name: Vini da Gigio
Address: calle Stua Cannaregio, sestiere Cannaregio 3628, Venice, 30121, Italy
Description: In the district of Cannaregio, a rustic environment and informal service in an inn where you can see into the kitchen, and which offers both fish and meat dishes; a good choice of wines.

Name: Porcino
Description: After gaining experience in top-quality restaurants, chef Marco Verginer has embarked on a new adventure running his own brand-new restaurant in the equally new Badia Hill hotel. In an elegant and spacious setting, enjoy modern, occasionally creative cuisine which skilfully blends Alpine flavours and ingredients with delicious Mediterranean influences.

Name: Essenza Bistrot
Description: A welcoming and original bistro-restaurant in the historic centre, where the stone walls are typical of the region’s architecture and an attractive outdoor area offers a few tables just in front of the entrance. The experienced owner-chef is at the helm in the kitchen, preparing beautifully presented, contemporary-style dishes which are full of flavour. The menu also features a selection of raw fish and seafood options.

Name: La Gallina
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Terrace
Description: This attractive restaurant offers three tasting menus featuring traditional and more creative dishes, in which influences from Piedmont, Liguria and Campania (the chef’s native region) combine, with truffles taking centre stage in autumn and home-grown vegetables in spring. Culinary highlights include Piedmontese-style Fassona beef tartare (the beef is sourced from the La Granda consortium) and cream ice-cream whipped in a 1982 Carpigiani machine served with a selection of sweet delicacies. The decision to offer wine uniquely from Champagne and Piedmont is somewhat unusual but works well – we recommend the house Barbera del Monferrato, preferably one that has been laid down for a few years.

Name: Acqua
Description: Situated slightly above the marina, this elegant restaurant has a young chef at the helm who has cemented his reputation via contemporary, occasionally creative dishes which showcase the best local ingredients, including fish and seafood. The fact that the latter come directly from the family’s own fishmongers adds to the appeal.

Name: Gagini Restaurant
Description: Situated in the lively heart of Palermo between the Vucciria and the small Cala port, this restaurant boasts a modern design and bold colours which are all the more striking for the charming old building which it occupies – the 16C studio of sculptor Antonello Gagini (hence the restaurant name!). The cuisine focuses on showcasing the quality of local ingredients, including wild rabbit from Pantelleria and donkey meat from the Nebrodi region, in dishes that are contemporary in style and full of flavour.

Name: Menabò Vino e Cucina
Address: via delle Palme 44 d/e, Rome, 00171, Italy
Description: Two brothers have brought fresh life to this exciting bistro in the heart of the Prenestino-Centocelle district, where the delicious cuisine is prepared by Paolo and the wine selection overseen by Daniele. The menu features a good balance of meat, fish and vegetarian dishes with a focus on seasonal ingredients and the best market produce. Very popular, so booking is recommended!

Name: Il Poggio
Description: This simple yet welcoming family-run restaurant is situated on the wine route that wends its way through the hills behind Sondrio, less than 5km away. The dining room boasts a cheerful open fireplace (also used as a grill), while an attractive outdoor terrace offers fine views of the valley. In the kitchen, the family’s second generation combine traditional recipes and ingredients with the occasional modern twist.

Name: Tenne Lodges
Address: strada Racines di Dentro 51, Colle, 39040, Italy
Description: Situated near the ski slopes in the Gourmethotel Tenne Lodges, this restaurant is decorated with a profusion of wood. The large dining room is the backdrop for delicious modern cuisine which is regional in focus yet also influenced by the chef’s professional experience around the world. Excellent wine list offering plenty of choice, plus a stone wine cellar which makes a charming setting for a pre-dinner drink.

Name: Osteria Il Cappello
Description: The outdoor terrace at this restaurant overlooks a pleasant pedestrian piazza in the historic centre, while the welcoming dining rooms are decorated in a style typical of the Trentino. The cuisine – reliable, seasonal and full of flavour – is traditionally Italian, yet with a contemporary touch. The menu also features a few regional options as well as the occasional fish dish. The quail stuffed with acacia honey, pumpkin purée and stewed radicchio is superb.

Name: Bentōteca
Description: Top-quality Japanese cuisine with heavy Mediterranean influences takes pride of place at this restaurant, where talented chef Toku Yoji Tokuyoshi creates dishes such as horsemeat tataki with a pizzaiola sauce, and barbecued fish neck with friggitello pepper. If you opt for a seat on the large bench facing the kitchen, you’ll be able to watch the chefs at work and admire the precision required to prepare different types of sushi. Modern, understated decor.

Name: Signore te ne ringrazi
Description: At this restaurant in the charming historic centre of Macerata, chef Michele Biagiola serves dishes inspired by rural culinary traditions, with herbs gathered in the fields nearby featuring in some of his recipes. Elaborate, gourmet cuisine is served at lunchtime, while the evening menu focuses on simpler, less expensive fare.

Name: Burjè 1968
Address: str. Burje 11, Corvara in Badia, 39033, Italy
Description: Ambitious Italian cuisine including some dishes inspired by French traditions, all creatively prepared with the occasional use of more exotic ingredients. If you’re having problems choosing from the à la carte, why not opt for the 5- or 7- course tasting menu?

Name: La Ciambella
Address: via dell'Arco della Ciambella 20, Rome, 00186, Italy
Description: Originally from Testaccio, the district of Rome that is historically associated with butcher’s shops, chef Francesca Ciucci serves some of the best meat dishes in the Italian capital, including offal such as sweetbreads, a delicious Roman-style tripe dish and her own reinterpretation of “coda in carrozza” (an oxtail recipe). Meat dishes, often with a creative twist, take centre stage here, offering a delightful gastronomic experience that is not to be missed!

Name: Incàlmo
Description: “Clean”, almost naive dishes full of clear and defined flavours take centre-stage at Incàlmo, where the cuisine is distinctly unfussy with no unnecessary frills. As a result, ingredients are clearly recognisable (as is the way they are prepared), allowing guests to focus on their contrasting textures and flavours. In the chef’s view, “if one element does stand out, it’s probably the bitter flavours that we enjoy playing with,” says the chef, “while at the same time balancing this with other elements. We also prioritise the use of vegetables.”

Name: Bino
Description: Situated in the historic centre near the ceramic museum (some of its pieces are also on display in the restaurant), Bino Ricchebuono boasts an attractive outdoor space in a charming small square. Michelin-starred chef Ricchebuono from Noli is the brains behind this restaurant, which serves fish and meat dishes prepared with a touch of creativity.

Name: Cortile Pepe
Description: Situated among the narrow streets of the historic centre just a stone’s throw from both the cathedral and the sea, this restaurant boasts a dining room with an old, vaulted ceiling and an attractive outdoor space. Here, the chef (who has plenty of experience working in Michelin-starred restaurants) serves regional cuisine reinterpreted with elegant and modern touches that result in precise, colourful and beautifully presented dishes. Attentive, friendly and welcoming service.

Name: Casu Osteria Contemporanea
Description: Situated on Giarre’s main street, this small, simple restaurant has just a few tables and an informal atmosphere. The menu offers a small selection of reasonably priced dishes with a focus on Sicilian cuisine made from top-quality ingredients that guarantee delicious flavours.

Name: Bianca sul Lago
Description: Housed in a smart hotel, this modern and minimalist-style restaurant boasts large picture windows which allow guests to enjoy some of the most beautiful sunsets in the region, either from the dining room or perhaps while sipping an aperitif in the lounge bar. The new chef serves contemporary Mediterranean cuisine with the occasional international influence, in which his creative flair is enhanced by expertly applied modern techniques. Good wine selection.

Name: Mirabelle
Address: via di Porta Pinciana 14, Rome, 00187, Italy
Description: Without a shadow of a doubt, the view of Rome from this restaurant situated on the penultimate floor of the Splendide Royalhotel has few equals: from Villa Medici to Trinità dei Monti, and St Peter’s to the Gianicolo, the only way to enjoy a better view is to head up a floor to the hotel’s new Adèle lounge bar for an aperitif or after-dinner drink. Excellent service (especially in the evening) and modern yet traditionally influenced cuisine make this one of Rome’s best fine-dining restaurants.

Name: Il Portolano
Address: via Molara 11, Porto San Paolo, 07020, Italy
Description: This simple restaurant right on the seafront facing the island of Tavolara is run by a highly experienced couple working alongside an excellent chef who creates modern cuisine from the best fish in the region, as well as offering a few local meat dishes. Reservations are highly recommended in summer when the large outdoor panoramic terrace is always teeming with customers.

Name: Il Bikini
Address: SS 145 Sorrentina km 13,900, Vico Equense, 80069, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Terrace
Description: This Mediterranean - style restaurant surrounded by a small outdoor terrace stands slightly above the beach club of the same name. Its elevated position gives it stunning views, which guests can enjoy as they savour the top - quality meat and fish dishes on the menu.

Name: Abraxas Osteria
Address: via Scalandrone 15, località Lucrino, Pozzuoli, 80078, Italy
Description: Situated inland at a slightly higher altitude than the coast, this restaurant on two floors focuses all its attention on its regional cuisine and its wine list. Very good value for money, although you will spend a bit more (and it’s worth it! ) if you choose one of the grilled meat options.

Name: Henri Restaurant
Description: The name of this restaurant refers to its owner Henri Prosperi, who returned to his beloved Viareggio in 2021. This accomplished maître d' from another era will introduce you, with both charm and professionalism, to his daughter Serena’s dishes, which are finely balanced between classic and modern flavours, with the occasional French influence. The chef’s menu features meat and fish dishes, with a firm focus on luxury ingredients. The same is true of the wine list, which includes renowned labels such as Petrus and Sassicaia, as well as some of the best French and Italian sparkling wines. Welcome back, Henri!

Name: Deste
Description: Set back slightly from the port, this restaurant boasts stunning views from its terrace which is highly recommended in fine weather. The culinary focus here is on modern dishes with an interesting choice of meat and fish options. Tea and kombucha offer an alternative to wine, while the home-produced gin is definitely worth sampling.

Name: De' Minimi
Description: Situated within the beautiful Villa Paola hotel just outside Tropea, this gourmet restaurant is named after the Frati Minimi (Order of Minims) who once occupied this old monastery. The cuisine here is modern and occasionally creative, especially the à la carte dishes (meat and fish), all of which are prepared from the best Calabrian ingredients including many vegetables and citrus fruit grown on the property. The small wine list also has a regional focus and is complemented by a choice of cocktails served at the bar.

Name: De Gustibus
Address: via Martiri della Libertà 9, Chieri, 10023, Italy
Description: Enjoy modern, Mediterranean-influenced cuisine in an elegant restaurant with an attractive vintage-style ambience, where the excellent menu is announced at your table and varies according to daily availability. Very friendly and attentive service.

Name: Il Rivale in Città
Description: Situated in a beautiful 18C palazzo right in the centre of Brescia, this elegant restaurant consists of several small dining rooms of different colours, fabrics and furnishings yet all with the same historic atmosphere – the room with just one table is truly intimate! The cuisine features substantial recipes with a contemporary Italian flavour including top-quality options such as potato puff pastry, scampi, caviar and hazelnut cream, while one of the highlights of the new formula is the wooden dessert trolley on which a selection of tempting home-made delicacies is presented. The wine list (easily consulted on a tablet) is also impressive, with a particular focus on labels from nearby Franciacorta.

Name: Kohaku
Description: As if by magic, once you step over the threshold at this restaurant you feel as though you are in Japan, thanks to the soft music, elegant ambience and stylish decor. Japanese Kaiseki dishes take pride of place here, all made from seasonal ingredients with a real respect for integrity. We particularly enjoyed the duck with miso cooked at low heat for eight hours. An interesting sake selection and a lighter menu at lunchtime add to the appeal.

Name: Salsedine367
Address: via Marradi 11, Lido di Savio, 48125, Italy
Description: Meals are served outdoors at this beach restaurant, which is also a private beach club. Here, the cuisine focuses on imaginative and personalised dishes that stand out for their excellent ingredients, among other things! The “blind” tasting menu is based around the chef’s inspiration, while the varied à la carte offers dishes with generous portions.

Name: Flurin
Description: Flurin occupies an old medieval tower in Glorenza, a small hamlet in the Val Venosta which is surrounded by walls that also date back to the Middle Ages. Furnished in a modern style that contrasts with its old vaulted ceiling, the restaurant serves contemporary cuisine that the enthusiastic owner-chef prepares from carefully selected seasonal ingredients from the region. His creative and imaginative recipes include dishes such as Alpine char ceviche with grapefruit, cucumber and sesame seeds. A bar and guest suites complete the picture.

Name: Al Malò - Cucina e Miscelazione
Description: Under the porticoes of the evocative Piazza Cavour you can see the double entrance: the door for the evening cocktail bar on the ground level, while–hidden on the left–there is a lift to the first level where there is the restaurant: the contemporary dining room is animated by bright wallpaper that seems almost to reveal in advance the imaginative cuisine of the chef-patron. Colorful, contemporary, with neat creative presentations he skilfully alternates meat (their signature is tongue mille-feuille, on the menu since the opening in 2019) and fish, but there is no lack of vegetarian dishes. Half portions are available. The fun grows with the mixology option of the cocktail list–in the evening–as well as the good wine list that, ça va sans dire, has great consideration for Franciacorta.

Name: Il Cavallo Scosso
Description: A young and modern restaurant situated in a residential area about 2km from the centre, where the owner-chef offers three tasting menus: Territorio e Tradizione, Il Cavallo Scosso and the more creative Fuori Gara.

Name: Scuderie Sabaude
Address: via Amedeo di Savoia 5, Pollenzo, 12042, Italy
Description: This restaurant just a stone’s throw from the Università del Gusto di Pollenzo is accessed via an old courtyard with a beautifully tended garden. Housed in the rustic setting of the former royal stables, the restaurant serves a delicious Piedmontese cuisine, light and impeccably presented. The “Tistot”, a delicious panna cotta, is a must!

Name: Nello
Address: Via IV  Novembre 66, San Casciano in Val di Pesa, 50026, Italy
Location: San Casciano in Val di Pesa, Italy
Description: Michele, in the kitchen, and pastry chef Chiara, who also works front of house, have renovated this historic local address and transformed it into a restaurant offering a modern interpretation of Tuscan cuisine. On the varied and intriguing menu, you’ll find dishes such as the intense and highly technical ravioli filled with Parmesan cream (made with milk from Reggiana “red cows”) with chanterelle mushrooms and onions. The concise wine list focuses on nearby Chiantis but also includes bottles from elsewhere.

Name: Terrazza Gallia
Description: Situated on the seventh floor with panoramic views of the city, this restaurant is an excellent choice for a light lunch, a cocktail or an informal dinner. Two young brothers from Naples are at the helm here, creating traditional Italian and Lombardian dishes with a creative and contemporary touch.

Name: Teresita by Giardino di Mari
Description: Housed in the private beach club of the same name, this elegant restaurant serves fish and seafood dishes made from carefully selected and top-quality ingredients. A whole page of the menu is dedicated to oysters and raw fish options. An attractive outdoor dining space completes the picture.

Name: Marc Lanteri
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Wheelchair access
Description: Situated right next to the Fratelli Massucco winery, with which it shares its comfortable outdoor spaces as well as stunning views of the surrounding hills and vineyards, this restaurant is run by Marc Lanteri and Amy Bellotti, partners in life and work, who have chosen this setting for their new Piedmontese adventure. Their cuisine is full of individual character, with three tasting menus (including a vegetarian option featuring produce grown in their own garden) and dishes also available à la carte style. Local ingredients and recipes naturally take centre stage, always enhanced by small touches of colour and imagination. The wine list showcases the property’s own wines, as well as offering a choice of labels from elsewhere in Italy and further afield.

Name: Locanda San Martino
Address: via Don Ermolao Barattin 23, Chies d'Alpago, 32010, Italy
Description: Founded in 1952, this inn has been run by the same family – and especially its female members – ever since. It now boasts the presence of a chef whose many years of experience are evident in his dishes. Much of the meat (especially lamb) is raised in the restaurant’s own farm nearby, while the dishes on the menu are seasonal and classic in style yet with a hint of modern flavour. When the weather allows, make the most of the large terrace boasting fine views of the sunset over the surrounding Alpago region.

Name: Il Principe
Address: via Colle San Bartolomeo 4, Pompei, 80045, Italy
Description: This restaurant focuses on a skilful and creative reinterpretation of Campanian specialities, serving the type of cuisine that you’d be happy to eat every day. Although the dishes are inspired by the chef’s childhood memories and his grandmother’s cooking, he adds his own contemporary touch and careful presentation. Both meat and fish feature, showcasing all the colour and imagination of the best regional cuisine.

Name: Café Cracco
Address: Galleria Vittorio Emanuele II, Milan, 20121, Italy
Description: The bar-pasticceria in Milan par excellence, this café run by the famous Michelin-starred chef (his gourmet restaurant is on the first floor of the same building) also makes a pleasant choice for food, with a menu which moves easily from Milanese specialities to international dishes, including pizza. The display of sweet options at the dessert counter is a feast for the eyes and the palate. This extraordinary corner of Milan’s famous Galleria also offers outdoor tables.

Name: Luciano Cucina Italiana
Address: piazza del Teatro di Pompeo 18, Rome, 00186, Italy
Description: It is widely accepted that the best carbonara in Rome is served in this restaurant. We have to agree – and this is no mean feat, given that this is one of the capital’s iconic dishes. However, Luciano Monosilio’s culinary experience also extends to other equally delicious dishes, some inspired by the traditions of Lazio, others more creative in style, but all full of intense flavours.

Name: L'Imbuto
Description: One of the most talked about and controversial chefs in Italy, thanks to his creative dishes and original combinations, Tomei has made his home in the former stables of the 17C Pfanner palazzo-museum. Here, guests choose the number of courses they want, let the chef know if they have any allergies and then sit back and enjoy whatever surprising dishes he creates for them.

Name: Josef Stube
Address: Località Certosa 29, Madonna di Senales, 39020, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Wheelchair access
Description: Run with passion by the two owners who continue the long family tradition in this hotel-restaurant is one of the most picturesque sights in the Val Senales. Its beautifully kept dining room is romantic and typical of the region, providing a backdrop for just a few dishes which are prepared by the chef with a focus on local ingredients. A hint of Mediterranean influence adds to the appeal.

Name: La Barca
Description: Run by the Virgilio family since 1967, this popular restaurant pays tribute to historic Bari with its delicious fish dishes and specialities from Puglia. Don’t miss the grilled fish and the reinterpreted cannolo dessert made with sheep’s milk ricotta, pear sauce and pistachio waffles.

Name: Casa Perrotta Restaurant
Description: This small, welcoming restaurant with a hint of minimalism and just a few tables serves personalised meat and fish dishes which aim to offer something a little different, with a choice of three tasting menus and an à la carte. Having previously gained experience outside the area, the young family team from Campania runs the restaurant with enthusiasm and a real love for the region’s cuisine.

Name: Impronta
Address: via Angarano 7, Bassano del Grappa, 36061, Italy
Description: All'inizio del Ponte Vecchio, icona cittadina nell'incantevole centro storico, il ristorante si sviluppa su diverse sale, a cui si aggiunge un romantico servizio all'aperto di fronte al fiume (quest'ultimo con pochi tavoli, quindi meglio prenotare). Cucina molto creativa ed elaborata, chi ama le sorprese e gli accostamenti originali troverà in questo ristorante un ottimo indirizzo.

Name: Faletta 1881
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Wheelchair access
Description: Nestled amid the wine estates and rolling hills of Monferrato, this historic farmhouse has been carefully restored its enthusiastic owners. The restaurant here serves contemporary dishes inspired by regional and Italian recipes, as well as offering welcoming guestrooms (one or two with their own kitchen), a saltwater swimming pool and the relaxing ambience that comes with this rural setting.

Name: Osteria Grande
Description: This restaurant overlooking the magnificent Piazza Grande and the Loggia Vasariana that takes up one whole side of the square was opened in the summer of 2022 by the enthusiastic Fatjon and Lorenzo (if you ask, they’ll happily share their knowledge of Arezzo’s history with you). The former is at the helm in the kitchen where he expresses his passion for cuisine in seasonal, contemporary-style dishes such as pigeon breast, leg and fillet (each cut is prepared in the appropriate way) served with sweet onion and cocoa nibs, while the latter oversees the wine selection and recommends suitable pairings to guests. For the chef’s pigeon speciality, he may, for example, suggest an original Maturato Tiberini 2018 (a white wine made from grapes that are left to ripen on the vine). Cocktail staff are also hand for guests keen to choose an aperitif or an after-dinner drink from the extensive cocktail list.

Name: Armando al Pantheon
Description: This small restaurant just a few metres from the Pantheon has been run by the Gargioli family since 1961, with the third generation now at the helm. Popular with locals and visitors alike for its traditional cuisine, which includes Roman and Lazian dishes, meat and fish options, and specialities such as offal, veal intestines, spring lamb, fresh anchovies, and sour-cherry tart.

Name: Vite
Address: via Montepirolo 7, località San Patrignano, Coriano, 47853, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Situated within the San Patrignano community, which grows its own crops, raises its own livestock and makes its own cheeses, Vite is now the setting for new, talented chef Giuseppe Biuso’s cuisine, which is made from top-quality ingredients using modern, creative techniques. His Mediterranean dishes are also inspired by his native Sicily, and include several vegetarian specialities. In summer, don’t miss the outdoor dining space which offers fine views of the surrounding countryside.

Name: Quadri Bistrot
Description: A modern bistro with a cocktail-bar, trendy decor, soft lighting and lounge-style background music, as well as a small outdoor space on the pavement which needs to be booked well in advance. The imaginative cuisine comes courtesy of a talented chef who creates dishes full of character from top-quality seasonal ingredients. Our inspectors particularly enjoyed the Bresse chicken stuffed with a cherry sauce.

Name: Trattoria dall'Antonia
Description: Housed in a delightful 19C house facing the Naviglio del Brenta, this restaurant has been fully renovated to offer a welcoming space in which fish and seafood reign supreme. Prepared wherever possible from local fish, the dishes served here are simple, traditional and either from the Veneto or elsewhere in Italy.

Name: Ling's Ravioleria Migrante
Description: A young couple (she was born in China; he’s half-French, half-Italian) have settled in this quiet residential district where they now run a tiny yet successful restaurant with around 20 seats in the dining room and a few small tables outdoors in summer – booking is essential! The menu includes various types of Chinese ravioli as well as dishes described by the couple as “migrant”, in other words “which draw inspiration from different cuisines from around the world, not only Asia but also the Mediterranean, France and Italy, with Emilia Romagna at its heart”. Examples include Peking-styleMora Romagnola coppa ham and pink Adriatic prawns marinated in mirin and soy sauce. The menu changes daily in line with market availability and the inspiration of the chef. Drinks include tea, beer and a small selection of wine.

Name: aldìVino
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: Shelves stacked with wine bottles line the walls at this smart bistro-style restaurant, which also boasts a quiet outdoor space for summer dining. The cuisine is contemporary and creative, and is showcased on three tasting menus from which dishes can also be ordered à la carte. We particularly enjoyed and can highly recommend the chef’s two signature dishes (“piatti firma dello chef”), squid “dripping” and spaghetti with smoked butter, oysters and raspberries. Courses here are divided into meat, fish and vegetable sections (Terra, Acqua and Vegetale).

Name: Selvatico
Address: via Silvio Pellico 19, Rivanazzano Terme, 27055, Italy
Description: Opened in 1912 and now run by the fourth generation of the same family, this is one of the best restaurants in the Oltrepò Pavese area. If you’re looking to sample the gastronomic delights of this region, you’ll find a whole host of delicious specialities on offer, from charcuterie and stews to boiled meats and excellent fresh pasta. Attractively furnished guestrooms with the same nostalgic feel as the restaurant are also available.

Name: Il Marchese - Osteria Mercato Liquori
Description: This genuinely Roman restaurant which takes its name from the Marchese del Grillo, a film which symbolises the spirit of Rome, is elegant and noble in style yet with a hint of irony. Although the focus is on traditional cuisine, the stylish decor, beautiful furnishings and dishes full of delicious flavours will instantly appeal to visitors from other cultures as well as locals. There are no fixed times for eating and drinking here: you can enjoy the fried meatballs, amatriciana pasta, stuffed chicken or a quick spaghetti with a tomato sauce at any time of day.

Name: Locanda La Posta
Description: This traditional restaurant boasts small dining rooms adorned with wooden ceilings, which were redecorated a few years ago with evocative photos and documents depicting its history. The restaurant’s interesting cuisine is also traditional in style, featuring home-made pastas, a typical boiled meat trolley (“carrello dei bolliti”), and an excellent rabbit stew served with a generous portion of peppers. The selection of delicious home-produced fare includes vegetables, preserves and pastries.

Name: Prato Gaio
Address: Località Versa, bivio per Volpara, Montecalvo Versiggia, 27047, Italy
Description: The restaurant trade is in the family genes: already an inn in the 19C, the Prato Gaio takes inspiration from the cuisine of the Oltrepò region. A selection of traditional specialities alongside dishes reinterpreted with flair and imagination are served. An essential stop for anyone looking for local flavour.

Name: I Rodella
Address: strada esterna vicinale della Rocca 2, Deruta, 06053, Italy
Description: This complex, which also includes two junior suites and seven guestrooms, dates back to the early 17C and was commissioned by the Church as a stopping off point for travellers on their way to Rome. For many years now, the restaurant has been run by a Venetian family with twin brothers (both highly experienced) working in the kitchen and a third brother, a sommelier, at the helm in the dining room. The cuisine is inspired by local and Venetian traditions, with a modern approach to the combinations of flavours (including home-grown herbs) and to the presentation of its delicious, generous dishes. We recommend that you do as we did and follow Samuele’s advice when making your choice from the dishes prepared by Stefano and Andrea with great skill and passion.

Name: Materia | Spazio Cucina
Description: The entrance to this restaurant is typical of an old residential-style building, giving the impression that you are stepping into the chef’s own home. Here, the beautiful dining room boasts shared tables and an entire wall covered with shelves of jars containing dried fruit, pumpkin seeds and red lentils. The classic-style cuisine focuses on grilled dishes and modern cooking methods to create typical Sicilian meat and fish dishes that pay careful attention to the seasons. The first courses are excellent, including the spaghetti with butter and anchovies, which is served with Favignana tuna bottarga and muddica atturrata(spiced breadcrumbs) made from Perciasacchi flour.

Name: Stefenelli Desk
Description: This restaurant is situated in an alleyway in the historic centre of Aoste. Full of character and accessed via a staircase from the entrance hall, the dining room is housed in what were probably the palazzo’s 18C stables. Under a brick-vaulted ceiling and arches, enjoy cuisine from the Aosta valley with a creative twist.

Name: Vescovo Moro
Description: Situated 50 metres from the basilica of San Zeno (the patron saint of Verona), this restaurant housed in a renovated workshop boasts plenty of outdoor space for summer dining. Here, enjoy eclectic cuisine with an equal balance of Mediterranean and traditional flavours, including an excellent array of raw fish dishes and a small selection of Italian caviar.

Name: Il Narciso
Description: Housed in the Polda baths near the marina, this recently opened small restaurant on the beach serves cuisine with a contemporary yet classic flavour. The restaurant boasts excellent bread, home-made pasta, traditionally cooked dishes such as chicken casserole and creative desserts. Highly recommended, especially the terrace with its fine sea views.

Name: Osteria 1861
Address: via Valentino Izzo 1, Santa Maria di Castellabate, 84048, Italy
Description: Accessed via a narrow alleyway behind the beach, this restaurant housed in an old warehouse once used for smoking cured meats and drying Cilento figs boasts stone-vaulted ceilings, a romantic ambience and a small terrace embellished by beautiful plants. Chef Antoni Tafuri’s cuisine features on various tasting menus (including vegetarian and vegan) and an à la carte and demonstrates careful combinations that aim to showcase his regional ingredients to the full.

Name: La Musa Restaurant & Rooftop Terrace
Description: Just six intimate tables in a modern restaurant with fine views of the lake through its large windows – the view is even more delightful from the summer terrace. The chef blends the flavors of his Sardinia with alpine ingredients, creating tasting itineraries that enhance the territory and the season.

Name: Santamonica
Description: Head down to the beach along a narrow street parallel to Corso Italia in the Albaro district of the city to reach this restaurant, where the views from both the dining room and summer terrace embrace the sea to the full. And it is, of course, from the latter that most of its ingredients are sourced (it’s not a coincidence that half a page on the menu is dedicated to raw fish dishes), with Santamonica’s chefs creating modern dishes with a strong emphasis on beautiful presentation. As an example, the traditional, fresh and crispy marinated anchovies are plated with geometric precision and attractively embellished with pine nuts and confit cherry tomatoes.

Name: Enoteca di Buttrio
Description: Housed in a beautiful historic building, this business, originally a wine bar (hence the name “enoteca”), gradually developed into a restaurant over the years. The menu focuses uniquely on fish, almost all of which comes from the Adriatic, showcased in traditional dishes enhanced with a creative twist.

Name: Locanda Belvedere
Address: via San Giuseppe 736, frazione San Rocco, Saludecio, 47835, Italy
Description: Using local ingredients, this restaurant offers regional cuisine with some creative touches. Pretty and inviting rooms, tastefully decorated and with period furniture. All overlooking the valley.

Name: Antica Trattoria al Gallo 1909
Description: It is an unavoidable reference point in the gastronomic panorama of Ravenna and, as a matter of fact, it is almost always full! An "Historical Establishment of Italy", and rightly so considering that it has been run by the same family for over 100 years, this restaurant is a trattoria only in its name, given the blaze of art nouveau decorations inside. As regards the cuisine, you can expect regional dishes: truffles, succulent meats and local fish. In the dining room everyone is involved, while the young owner will illustrate the wine selection with the typically delightful congeniality of Romagna.

Name: Osteria Il Granaio
Address: via dei Monaci, Rapolano Terme, 53040, Italy
Description: Although it calls itself an osteria, Il Granaio is really a restaurant. It has elegant brick - arched dining rooms occupying a 17C palazzo in the historic centre of Rapolano. On the menu you will find Tuscan specialities such as pici pasta cooked with various sauces, peppery Tuscan beef stew and a selection of fish dishes.

Name: Osteria L'Abbiccì
Address: via Medici da Seregno 29, Seregno, 20831, Italy
Description: Situated in the centre of Seregno, this modern inn boasts a bright, spacious dining room with an ambience which is both friendly and yet respectful of guests’ privacy. The cuisine is overseen by Davide, who trained with Mauro Elli, the owner-chef of Il Cantuccio in Albavilla. Here, he creates dishes full of character, with a focus on top-quality ingredients and skilful presentation techniques. For a memorable dining experience, the chef’s surprise menu makes an excellent choice. Impressive wine selection and professional service overseen by Gabriele add to the appeal. The business lunch offers excellent value for money.

Name: Spoon
Description: Located in the heart of the historic centre, just a stone’s throw from the beautiful 13C cathedral, this small, simple restaurant with an outdoor space is home to owner-chef Marco Cozzi, whose cuisine is the main attraction here. Having trained with Niko Romito, this chef creates dishes from seasonal, regional ingredients, reinterpreting traditional recipes to give them a contemporary flavour (for example, he transforms pancotto into a cream of bread and Navelli saffron, which he then crowns with Robiola cheese, cime di rapa and triangles of cured pork loin). His two tasting menus focus entirely on meat and feature an impressive selection of vegetables.

Name: Voce Aimo e Nadia
Description: Situated in the heart of Milan, this restaurant owned by the historic Aimo e Nadia in Via Montecuccoli is accessed via its bar-cum-pastry shop which includes a bistro serving a selection of simpler dishes. From here, you enter the main dining room with an open-view kitchen serving excellent Italian dishes reinterpreted in contemporary style. Voce in Giardino, the restaurant’s outdoor summer dining space adorned with interesting sculptures, is a green oasis in the heart of the city.

Name: Sottovoce
Description: One of the first rooftop restaurants in Como, Sottovoce boasts an elegant, contemporary feel, while its cuisine makes full use of Italy’s wealth of ingredients, with a particular focus on local produce such as fish from the lake which is served in an array of creative and imaginative dishes (vegetarian options are also available on the à la carte, plus there’s a dedicated vegetarian menu). Facilities here include a quiet, intimate dining room, a private balcony for groups (a maximum of eight people) and a spectacular outdoor Infinity Bar in which to enjoy a late-afternoon aperitif while admiring the beautiful views of the lake.

Name: Felter alle Rose
Address: via Gasparo Da Salò 33, Salò, 25087, Italy
Description: This historic trattoria has been brought back to life by a local family with years of experience in the hospitality industry and a real commitment to quality. Convenient private parking, an indoor dining room, a closed veranda and a few tables set out in the wine cellar for tastings and aperitifs are just some of the attractions here. The short menu features simple yet carefully made dishes prepared from seasonal ingredients.

Name: Locanda della Luna
Address: via delle Oche 7, San Giorgio del Sannio, 82018, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Terrace
Description: In a remote location in the Sannio, this authentic inn offers fine views from its well-kept dining room-cum-veranda and outdoor terrace. The owner-chef creates dishes with a regional flavour using produce from his own garden, without straying too far from local traditions.

Name: Hostaria di Bricai
Description: Situated in the gardens next to the Sacro Monte funicular, this beautiful and bucolic residence overlooks the village. In this relaxing setting, Giorgio serves traditional local cuisine: the rabbit leg in porchetta with mountain-style purée is one of the highlights.

Name: Osteria dello Strecciolo
Description: Situated in the centre of the village, this popular and professionally run restaurant has an informal atmosphere. The cuisine is inspired by Mediterranean recipes and more regional traditions, with great care taken in the choice of ingredients and beautifully presented dishes. A business lunch menu is also available.

Name: Il Frantoio
Address: via del Castello 40, Colle di Val d'Elsa, 53034, Italy
Description: The 19C millstone, press and cisterns can still be seen in the dining room at this restaurant, bearing witness to its past as an olive oil mill. Situated in spectacular Colle di Val d’Elsa, Il Frantoio boasts old stone and brick walls and vaulted ceilings, as well as tables set out in the piazza for summer dining. Although the setting suggests simple and rustic cuisine, the chef surprises guests with top-quality dishes which are technical and often highly creative, such as liver with sour cherries and pistachios, and smoked spaghetti with an anchovy sauce, capers and black garlic cream.

Name: Il Grifone
Address: via Ca' Masino 611/a - loc. Varignana, Castel San Pietro Terme, 40024, Italy
Description: This fine-dining restaurant housed in the 18C Palazzo Bentivoglio Bargellini is part of the luxurious Palazzo di Varignana resort (with which it shares the Il Grifone symbol), the latter also home to a farm producing olive oil, wine and fruit. In the evening, choose between two tasting menus and an à la carte offering a selection of meat and fish dishes on which the modern recipes feature a careful balance of colours and flavours.

Name: Indigeno
Address: Via di Villa Bianca 15, Montepulciano, 53045, Italy
Description: Boasting an unusually beautiful setting within the Salcheto Organic Winery amid the rolling hills around Montepulciano, this 13C farmhouse has been converted into a wine estate that also includes a restaurant. Simple, home-style cooking with a focus on local traditions takes pride of place here, with dishes made from ingredients either produced on the estate itself or sourced from small-scale local producers. Guests sit at large shared tables made from Amiata oak, or outdoors in summer, where they can enjoy home-made bread and numerous other specialities, including bread gnocchetti with creamed broad beans and bitter herbs, and roast goose leg.

Name: Riccio Restaurant
Address: via Molo di Baia 47, Bacoli, 80070, Italy
Description: Overlooking the port, this restaurant serves top-quality fish and seafood with interesting and personalised touches added by its young chef. We recommend starting with the excellent selection of cooked fish (although there’s also a choice of raw fish should you prefer it), following which you can choose from classic seafood dishes such as spaghetti with clams and fried fish, and a selection of original, top-quality dishes such as dry-aged, smoked and preserved fish and seafood.

Name: MU Dimsum
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Wheelchair access
Description: Already visible from the pavement outside this restaurant, the large kitchen where its staff can be observed busy at work is testament to its success. Inside, the dining room is modern and elegant, with careful lighting effects creating a muted ambience in the evening. The extensive menu features classic Chinese dishes – in addition to different types of delicious dim sum, Peking duck also takes pride of place among the main courses.

Name: La Limonaia
Description: This restaurant occupies a large veranda decorated with an original array of tastefully arranged objects and furnishings. The cuisine is both contemporary and exciting, featuring a few interesting fish dishes alongside regional specialities (including from outside Piedmont) such as mandilli (pasta) in a grouper stew with peas and aromatic herbs, brodetto (fish stew) “alla vastese”, and mutton cooked over charcoal embers.

Name: Hosteria del Platano
Description: Situated on the main road overlooking the lake, this pleasant family-run restaurant serves excellent traditional cuisine with a focus on local fish. Atmospheric dining room with stone walls and vaulted ceilings, plus an attractive outdoor space, and friendly, attentive owners.

Name: Il Molo
Address: via Aganor Pompili 9, Passignano sul Trasimeno, 06065, Italy
Description: Situated in the historic centre of Passignano, where the village seems to jut out into the Lake Trasimeno (some tables in the main dining room boast views of the lake – make sure you book in advance), Il Molo has become a popular choice for guests keen to try top-quality fish from the lake as well as excellent poultry dishes. We highly recommend the delicious stuffed quail served with mushrooms and liver and accompanied by an excellent glass of local biodynamic red wine. There’s also a good choice of sparkling wines and champagnes.

Name: Casa Federici
Description: The area around Montoro, famous for its cipolla ramata (copper onion), is now also home to a gourmet restaurant thanks to young chef Francesco Cerrato, whose cuisine is inspired by locally sourced ingredients from this inland region as well as fish and seafood from the coast. The menu also features creative, carefully prepared dishes served by the attentive young staff. Minimalist-style ambience.

Name: Locanda Martinelli
Description: It’s well worth leaving the coast and climbing into the foothills to get to this small restaurant serving excellent cuisine. Housed in a rustic-style house with individual furnishings, in what could be the sitting room of a private house, the restaurant serves meat and fish specialities prepared with imagination from local produce and ingredients from further afield. As well as being a wine expert, the female owner gathers herbs, flowers and berries to flavour her recipes.

Name: Chat Qui Rit
Address: calle Tron, sestiere San Marco 1131, Venice, 30124, Italy
Description: The generous, colourful and carefully prepared dishes served at this Italian bistro just a stone’s throw from St Mark’s Square could be described as “lagoon fusion” cuisine, thanks to one of the two chefs who demonstrates his love of Japanese flavours in some of his creative recipes.

Name: El Brite di Larieto
Address: Località Larieto, strada per Passo Tre Croci, Cortina d'Ampezzo, 32043, Italy
Description: If SanBrite boasts a collection of Michelin stars (a classic star for its cuisine and a green star for its sustainable approach), it’s also thanks to this agriturismo’s location in a small larch wood, where it is surrounded by the spectacular Dolomites. Opened 20 years ago and renovated over the years, this smart agriturismo is also home to a stable annexe, where its restaurant celebrates the flavours of Alpine culinary traditions in its meat and charcuterie, cheeses, creamy butter and ice cream, as well as herbs, berries and other local ingredients.

Name: Borgia Milano
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Bring your own bottle,Interesting wine list
Description: This Milanese restaurant with a young talented chef at the helm boasts a breakfast area, as well as a lunchtime bistro and evening wine bar. The atmosphere in the dining room is lively and modern, allowing plenty of privacy, while the service is highly attentive to guests’ needs. This is especially true on the flagship “Psyche” menu, on which the chef creates special dishes in accordance with the guest’s personal preferences. The cuisine is creative, contemporary and technically adept as demonstrated in the carefully prepared pigeon served with hibiscus, blackberry and juniper cream. The interesting wine list includes bottles from across the globe, including some rare labels.

Name: [bu:r]
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Wheelchair access
Description: Eugenio Boer offers a 100% Italian menu which focuses on local ingredients, with the aim of showcasing some of Italy’s favourite traditional dishes while at the same time supporting small-scale producers. However, this philosophy is in no way limited to respecting traditions – on the contrary, it offers the chef the freedom to express his own creativity via a selection of dishes which combine past and present. As a result, guests can choose between a concise à la carte and three different tasting menus: “I Classici” (meat-based dishes); “Lo Stagionale” (fish and seasonal ingredients); and “Per mano...”, a menu which changes depending on the chef’s creative inspiration. In short, a flexible approach which offers guests a culinary experience that will certainly make an impression!

Name: La Cucina de' Mibabbo
Description: The name (“My grandfather’s cooking”) says it all: this restaurant serves cuisine from the owner’s native Tuscany, with a focus on Tuscan ingredients prepared with an updated and modern twist. Good selection of Tuscan specialities such as grilled meats and dishes cooked in a wood-fired oven in the evening, while the lunchtime menu is more restricted and Italian in feel.

Name: Al Baccanale
Description: Situated in the heart of the historic centre just a stone’s throw from Piombino’s former Medici fortress, this quiet restaurant boasts a backdrop of exposed stonework and vaulted ceilings and just a few tables, so booking ahead is recommended. Here, the enthusiastic and talented owner-chef serves traditional cuisine reinterpreted with a modern and highly individual twist.

Name: Da Attilio
Description: Situated in one of the liveliest working-class neighbourhoods of Naples, this restaurant serves traditional Neapolitan pizzas, including a few unusual innovations such as pizzas in the shape of an 8-pointed star. In business since 1938 and now run by the third generation of the same family, Da Attilio has just a few tables arranged in two small dining rooms and doesn’t take reservations. Although you may have to wait at the busiest times of day, you’ll find the wait well worthwhile!

Name: Da Luciano
Address: via Nazionale 11, Passignano sul Trasimeno, 06065, Italy
Description: Enjoy beautiful views of Lake Trasimeno from the outdoor terrace of this restaurant, where the menu focuses mainly on fish, alongside original ingredients such as beans and Umbrian truffles which are used in typical specialities such as tegamaccio (fish stew).

Name: Stefano Mocellin al Padovanino
Description: Situated in the historic centre of Padova, this restaurant is home to owner-chef Stefano Mocellin, whose colourful, creative and personalised cuisine is influenced by his past culinary experience in cities such as Milan and Venice. From Milan, for example, he has taken the legendary “cassoeula”, to which he gives a lighter touch thanks to his use of more than one type of meat (pork and duck), while his “saor” and the sardines that he uses to stuff his plin pasta are inspired by Venice. Underlying all of this is his passion for cooking over the barbecue grill, the main focus of almost all the dishes on the menu.

Name: Il Frantoio
Description: This restaurant has undergone a skilful refurbishment with a focus on colour, light and furnishings which combine harmoniously with the valley below, as well as with the dishes in which extra-virgin olive oil takes a starring role (not just as a condiment but as an ingredient in its own right). The view through the floor-to-ceiling windows, which extends along the valley as far as San Pietro abbey in Assisi, is as enticing as the cuisine.

Name: Palazzo Branciforte
Description: A relaxing oasis in the city centre which offers friendly service from staff who obviously want to ensure that your experience here is memorable. The dishes served are carefully prepared and full of flavour, boasting the occasional modern touch yet also inspired by local traditions. Try the "Capricciosa vista mare": toasted black bread with capers and oregano served with red prawn, dried tomato, artichokes, basil and buffalo mozzarella mousse.

Name: Carter Oblio
Address: via Giuseppe Gioachino Belli 21, Rome, 00193, Italy
Description: Following years of experience in renowned restaurants, owner-chef Ciro Alberto has achieved his dream of opening his own place. With its clean lines and natural colour scheme, his restaurant has a slightly Nordic feel, while the reasonably priced cuisine demonstrates the imagination and creativity of a chef who is keen to stand out. Expertly prepared and attractively presented contemporary dishes are to the fore here.

Name: via Paese 18, Soprabolzano, 39054, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: The name of this restaurant refers to the year in which the hotel in which it is located (the Park Hotel Holzner) was opened, while the design is a nod to the Liberty style of the period. Despite this, both the ambience and the cuisine bear the modern and imaginative hallmark of Stephan Zippl. Paying careful attention to sustainability, this chef selects the best regional produce for his dishes – even the Wagyu beef is raised in the chef’s native Renon region. This strong connection with the Alto Adige is also evident on the excellent wine list, which features almost 400 labels from the region and provides perfect pairings for the chef’s tasting menu. Other options include non-alcoholic drinks such as apple juice and alcohol-free cocktails.

Name: La Risacca Blu
Address: via Tunisia, angolo via Tadino, Milan, 20124, Italy
Description: The first thing you see when you enter this restaurant near the central railway station is its large display of fresh fish, all delivered daily. The menu features a selection of classic and authentic fish and seafood options, with pride of place given to its raw fish dishes.

Name: Sostansa
Description: The philosophy of this restaurant of the town centre, situated just outside the traffic-restricted zone, talks about “stories from the kitchen” and “urban” dishes: in other words, it chooses the best market ingredients with an emphasis on (but not exclusive use of) seasonal produce, from which generous, delicious and attractive dishes are created. At lunchtime, there’s a choice of à la carte dishes or a business lunch announced at your table; in the evening, two surprise tasting menus are also available.

Name: Da Lucio
Description: This restaurant boasts an impressive setting on the end of a jetty surrounded by the sea in Rimini docks. The entrance stands next to the open-view kitchen (a spectacle in itself!), which then leads into the long dining room. Nearly all the fish here (which comes from the Adriatic) is aged to allow water to evaporate so that the flavours are concentrated; it is then grilled or baked in a wood-fired oven, as well as served raw, with surprising and remarkable results.

Name: Bis Osteria Italiana Contemporanea
Address: Via 20 Settembre 50, Colle di Val d'Elsa, 53034, Italy
Description: In the glorious premises of the old Arnolfo restaurant in the old town, this restaurant is run by the same management as previously, although with a new young chef at the helm in the kitchen. The delicious yet concise menu features “Italian specialities” (the name given to all the main courses) with a focus on meat and fish, accompanied by excellent bread options (you can even order “scarpetta” dipping bread for mopping up the remains of a Cinta Senese pork sauce). The house speciality is a delicious pigeon dish. In fine weather, guests can dine on the beautiful, tranquil terrace.

Name: Oro Nero
Description: Local ingredients such as Sauris trout, Malga cheese, eggs and herbs feature on the menu at this charming restaurant with spectacular views of the surrounding peaks. In a modern dining room where the colours black and gold dominate, Andrea serves delicious creative recipes such as his signature dish of pigeon cooked two different ways with a sweet and sour bitter cherry, peanut and shallot sauce.

Name: Dallo Zio
Description: A beautifully kept restaurant just a stone’s throw from the Arch of Augustus. Warm and welcoming, the restaurant’s vintage style echoes the 19C origins of the building as well as the 1970s, the decade when it first opened. Divided into two floors with small tables set close together, the menu features meat dishes and, more especially, “fresh fish from Rimini’s fishing boats” prepared in delicious, classic recipes that often have their roots in local traditions.

Name: Between
Description: This top-quality restaurant occupies just one simple, minimalist-style dining room, where the young female chef serves a happy combination of Piedmontese ingredients and more creative dishes acquired during her time working abroad.

Name: Il Colmetto
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: A true gourmet agriturismo, Il Colmetto changes its menu almost week by week in line with the changing seasons. Full of flavour, the ingredients here (many of which are produced on the property, while others are sourced locally) are cooked with precision, avoiding overly fussy and complicated techniques. Instead, the focus is on good, honest cuisine with its roots in peasant traditions, in which the aim is to create comforting dishes that will appeal to the palate. The barbecued specialities, such as the sweetbreads and the excellent Jerusalem artichokes, are particularly delicious, while the superb goats’ milk butter, served soft and fluffy as a cloud with bread and focaccia, is truly delicious – its only drawback is that it can be addictive!

Name: AB Osteria Contemporanea
Description: A small village just a few kilometres from Udine provides the backdrop for modern, regionally influenced cuisine with plenty of character. The renovated dining rooms have two distinct styles: the one near the entrance is friendly and relaxed; the other has a much more formal ambience. The large outdoor space is perfect for summer dining.

Name: Sushisen
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Notable sake list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: Two smart dining rooms offer two different dining experiences at this restaurant: one with chairs at the bar and a conveyer belt of traditional Japanese dishes; the other serving contemporary Japanese cuisine, including the intriguing Omakase tasting menu. Nearly all the wines and sakes on the wine list are also available by the glass.

Name: Giano
Description: Conveniently situated in a quiet setting just behind Via Vittorio Veneto, Giano is housed within the modern Hotel W with which it shares a comfortable cocktail bar and attractive garden. The atmosphere here is modern and informal, with simple fare served at lunchtime and more gourmet dining options in the evening. The resident chef is supported by skilful and experienced Ciccio Sultano who provides valuable input on menus and ingredients. Iconic dishes such as the spaghetto taratatà (with a tuna and bottarga sauce), the em>caponada, and the carpacci are highly recommended, as are desserts such as the reinterpreted millefoglie . Sicilian cuisine takes pride of place here and the service is excellent.

Name: Il Pescatore
Address: via Acqua Dolce 7, Cala Gonone, 08022, Italy
Description: This Mediterranean-style restaurant has the evocative feel of a seaside village with its beautiful photos of the coast on the walls. It’s best to book ahead if you want one of the tables on the small terrace overlooking the sea. To avoid confusion, note that the Il Pescatore that we recommend is situated at 7, via Acqua Dolce.

Name: Bottega Aleotti
Description: Situated in a secluded street in the town centre, this restaurant run by a couple boasts an elegant dining room with an attractive dark parquet floor. The cuisine is a good example of how to add a light modern touch to local specialities as well as typical Italian dishes, while the menu also includes a few fish-based options. Don’t miss the home-made pasta!

Name: Marelet
Description: The name of this restaurant discreetly hidden away in an alleyway on the edge of the town centre is a dialect word meaning “old bachelor”. Small tables set close together give the ambience of a French brasserie and provide the setting for modern, Mediterranean-inspired cuisine. There’s a simpler menu at lunchtime, including salads, tapas and sandwiches, while more choice is available in the evening. Lively atmosphere.

Name: Langosteria Paraggi
Address: via Paraggi a Mare 1, Paraggi, 16038, Italy
Description: The elegant Milanese style of the famous Langosteria restaurant has been given a maritime and holiday feel in its seasonal sibling which is housed within the Bagni Fiore overlooking the small yet stunning Paraggi bay. Langosteria Paraggi boasts a vintage decor which is at the same time glamorous and up-to-date, views of the beach and the sea, and a menu focusing on delicious fresh fish and seafood such as oysters and shellfish.

Name: Mammaròssa
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: At this restaurant, owner-chef Franco Franciosi focuses on the Abruzzo in dishes which are both traditional and modern. The cuisine showcases the best ingredients from the region, including home-grown vegetables from the restaurant’s own kitchen garden and excellent bread made with solina wheat (typical of the Apennines), amid a decor that focuses on sustainability. Daniela looks after guests front of house, offering recommendations from the short yet carefully chosen wine list.

Name: Hostaria del Vicolo
Description: Situated in a central yet secluded location, this intimate and elegant restaurant serves typical Sicilian cuisine with a focus on fish, vegetables from the kitchen garden and delicious cheeses. A good wine selection completes the picture.

Name: 20 Posti
Description: A small bistro-style restaurant with an evening lounge bar, situated in a narrow alleyway in the town centre. The young team here serve imaginative Mediterranean meat and fish dishes prepared from an array of carefully chosen ingredients.

Name: La Ciotola
Description: Situated along the SS13 which leads to nearby Pordenone, this restaurant has a fresh, busy feel. At lunchtime, the service is quicker, the menu smaller and the prices lower, while in the evening guests can choose from a full menu. Whether you’re here for lunch or dinner, you’ll enjoy meat and fish dishes made by the Cover brothers from top-quality ingredients and prepared simply yet with an imaginative touch.

Name: La Pista
Address: Centro Commerciale Lingotto - via Nizza 262, Turin, 10126, Italy
Description: This restaurant is situated on the top floor of Turin’s iconic Lingotto building, the former Fiat factory, where the famous test track for cars has been transformed into a botanic garden – an interesting place to visit before your meal.
