Once at your table, choose from Alessandro Scardina’s three tasting menus: “Radici, gli essenziali” (traditional Piedmontese cuisine); “Botanic World” (vegetarian dishes); and “Trust” (a surprise menu where you leave all the choices to the chef). Whatever you choose, you’ll enjoy remarkable dishes that are balanced and full of substance and intense flavours. To avoid getting lost in the Lingotto shopping centre, make sure you follow the instructions you receive and take the lift to the restaurant.

Name: Hostaria Ducale
Address: Salita di San Matteo 29 r, Genoa, 16123, Italy
Description: Situated just behind the beautiful Piazza De Ferrari, this restaurant with a quiet ambience and elegant decor provides the backdrop for young chef Daniele Rebosio’s superb, ever-evolving cuisine, which is modern, creative and imaginative and yet inspired by regional traditions. Equally at ease with meat and fish, Rebosio occasionally combines the two in one dish, as evidenced by his veal tongue served with langoustine (carpaccio marinated in passion fruit and salted biscuit stuffed with tartare) or with ravioli with rabbit and mussels dedicated to Fabrizio De André’s song Crêuza de mä .

Name: Osteria Contemporanea
Description: Housed in an old butcher’s shop right in the village centre, this intimate and elegantly simple “osteria” is run by a young couple. In the kitchen, Agnese Loss, who was born in 2001, has already acquired significant experience since leaving catering school. She creates personal and carefully prepared cuisine with real passion, with one menu that is dedicated exclusively to offal (all we’ll say about this is that we particularly enjoyed the tongue and sweetbreads – we’ll leave it to you to find out how these dishes were prepared!). The other two tasting menus (to be ordered by the whole table) reflect her own tastes, as well as those of her partner Davide, who runs the front of house with elegance and competence, including overseeing the wine list. A la carte options are also available.

Name: Casa Bertini
Description: This unexpected gourmet restaurant is housed in a sports centre just outside the historic centre of Recanati, birthplace of famous Italian poet Giacomo Leopardi. At the helm in the kitchen, young, talented chef Andrea Bertini has returned to his native region where he reinterprets the traditions of the Marche (especially meat) to create light, simple and unfussy dishes. The same simple style is echoed in the decor, which is elegant and very understated.

Name: Marechiaro
Description: This smart, elegant restaurant, which has a particularly romantic ambience in the evening, has been serving top-quality fish in Bolzano for over 20 years. Prepared in traditional Italian style, the dishes here focus on the flavour and quality of the fish and seafood on offer, most of which comes from the Mediterranean. The two friendly brothers who run the restaurant are originally from Naples, which explains the specialities from Campania and the excellent pizza which also features on the menu. A simpler selection of dishes is available at lunchtime.

Name: Campamac
Description: A real gourmet inn which serves traditional Piedmontese dishes made from excellent ingredients alongside top-quality meats cooked on the barbecue grill. An elegant ambience with a deliberately retro feel, which is beautifully maintained and has plenty of charm.

Name: Trattoria Pomposa - Al Re gras
Description: It’s not just the affordable prices that will keep you coming back here, as the real highlight is its flavourful Emilian cuisine, which has been given a fresh, more modern twist. Among the first courses, we can recommend the tortellini in chicken broth or with a 24-month Parmesan cream; and for the main course, a delicious tripe with bread croutons. The Lambrusco is a must on the wine list here (we can recommend a good Grasparossa di Castelvetro). In the summer, meals are served outdoors on the small Piazza della Pomposa.

Name: Lineadombra
Address: Ponte dell'Umiltà, sestiere Dorsoduro 19, Venice, 30123, Italy
Description: Boasting a splendid location with an outdoor dining space on a kind of raft-cum-platform, this restaurant boasts one of the most delightful views in Venice, with the Giudecca on the opposite side of the canal. Contemporary cuisine with a focus on fish and the occasional creative twist.

Name: Sustanza
Address: Galleria Principe di Napoli 13, Naples, 80135, Italy
Description: The entrance to this restaurant in the Galleria Principe di Napoli is through the 19CScottoJonno café chantant, from where you take a lift to the restaurant’s Liberty-style dining rooms with their elegant, historic feel. In contrast, the cuisine is modern in flavour, featuring complex and elaborate dishes that have their roots in the traditions and ingredients of the entire Mediterranean (including North Africa), as well as fermented products and the occasional grilled option. The end result is a surprising experience for anyone looking for a change from the usual traditional fare.

Name: Radici
Address: Località Borgo La Chiaracia, Castel Giorgio, 05013, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Served in an elegant dining room or on the delightful outdoor terrace in fine weather, the highly creative cuisine at this restaurant has its roots in regional traditions and excellent local producers, while its stunning location within the luxurious Hotel Borgo La Chiaracia among the region’s verdant winding valleys makes it difficult to leave. With a choice of à la carte and tasting menus, our inspectors were particularly impressed by the Origini 20menu, on which all the ingredients are sourced within a 20km radius of the restaurant.

Name: Osteria Origano
Address: via Giuseppina Scarciglia 18, Minervino di Lecce, 73020, Italy
Description: A small wine boutique at the entrance to this osteria in the village centre, displays the restaurant’s own wines, which are the perfect complement to your meal, as well as being available to purchase and take home with you. To the rear, an attractive closed veranda and an outdoor space are the perfect settings for hearty, traditional cuisine which ranges from spit-roasted meats to local salumi and home-made pastas. A few fish options are also available.

Name: Innocenti Wine Experiences
Description: As you enter this restaurant, you’re struck by the sight of hundreds of bottles of wine lining the walls. First and foremost a wine bar, Innocenti Wine Experiences is transformed into a restaurant for lunch and dinner, serving creative cuisine which focuses mainly on meat dishes with the occasional elaborate and original twist. There’s obviously no problem choosing your wine – just look around you!

Name: Da Lorenzo
Address: via Fra' Gerardo Sasso 8, Scala, 84010, Italy
Description: Slightly off the beaten track in the lesser-known village of Scala opposite Ravello, this authentic family trattoria offers an informal change from the many Michelin-starred luxury restaurants dotted along the Amalfi Coast. Da Lorenzo has been serving simple yet excellent fish and seafood cuisine for decades, with a wonderful and highly recommended array of fresh fish on display. A popular panoramic terrace adds to its appeal.

Name: Mirepuà Food Lab
Description: Situated in a picturesque medieval village in the Monferrato hills, this restaurant serves classic Piedmontese cuisine with plenty of meat options, alongside a few specialties from the chef’s native Liguria, including fish and seafood dishes.

Name: La Corte Gourmet
Description: An interesting choice of wine with plenty of options by the glass, attentive service in a classic yet contemporary-style dining room, and good, honest cuisine prepared by owner-chef Paolo. The seasonal menu features classic favourites such as Fassona beef tartare and breaded veal cutlets cooked in butter alongside imaginative pasta dishes and truffles (in season). Guests have the option of dining in the attractive “champagneria”, surrounded by exposed brickwork and bottles that have been carefully selected by Antonella, the life and soul of the restaurant.

Name: Lucia
Description: Having just celebrated their 50th anniversary (they opened in 1971), this restaurant and hotel of the same name remain a solid culinary reference on the Abruzzi coast. The menu here is dedicated solely to fish and, as a result and is often the case, the wine list focuses almost exclusively on white wines. The fish (almost all of which comes from the Adriatic) is carefully sourced, while in the kitchen the chefs prepare classic dishes (such as enormous local langoustines cooked – and served – in a pan with oil, wine, garlic and rosemary) and a few more modern recipes (crispy mullet served with the award-winning spicy Ventricina salami).

Name: Antica Osteria del Mare
Description: Situated on the Naviglio away from Milan’s bustling nightlife, this rustic-style restaurant is decorated with a profusion of wood. As the name suggests, fish and seafood take pride of place on the menu, with a good choice of antipasti to whet the appetite, as well as inviting trays of raw fish dishes (shared by the whole table), followed by delicious traditional pasta and grilled options.

Name: med
Address: piazza del Quartiere Latino 13, Treviso, 31100, Italy
Description: In the pedestrian area of the town, with views of the Sile river from the ground floor, this attractive restaurant serves regional cuisine with a focus on local ingredients, prepared in a classic style attentive to modern tastes. There’s an excellent wine list, plus live music and a pleasant outdoor space for fine weather dining.

Name: Forme Restaurant
Description: Having worked in Michelin-starred restaurants such as Miramonti l'Altro, Arianna Gatti has now achieved her dream of opening her own restaurant. In this restored old building featuring designer-style details and a charming outdoor space, she serves an extensive selection of intensely flavoured dishes from her native Abruzzo and the region of Lombardy where she trained as a professional chef. A delightful all-round dining experience.

Name: Osteria de' Mercati
Description: Slightly set back from the bustling streets of the historic centre yet still in the heart of the town, this delightful small restaurant is a recent addition to Sassari. It boasts a modern, elegant decor, friendly staff and a menu featuring carefully prepared fresh, seasonal dishes. Our inspector particularly recommends the seafood risotto. A choice of regional wines completes the picture.

Name: Gallery Bistrot Contemporaneo
Description: Modern, tasty and carefully curated cuisine, which is prepared using the best seasonal ingredients. There is also a creative touch to some of the dishes, such as the vitello tonnato in which the meat (Fassona veal from the Piedmont) takes on the appearance of raspberries, or the delicate duck breast served with veal jus. The restaurant offers just 20 seats in a long dining room where the walls and ceiling form a sort of light wood-panelled arch that creates a real sense of movement.

Name: Veranda
Description: Alberto Faccani, the two-Michelin starred chef at the Magnolia restaurant in the hills inland from Cesenatico, oversees the cuisine at this restaurant. Fish takes centre stage here, in unfussy dishes that faithfully reflect the maritime traditions of the Adriatic. Primi courses include raw dishes, gratins, seafood salads, pasta and risotto, while secondi feature a selection of grilled, baked and fried fish (depending on the day’s catch).

Name: La Nicchia
FacilitiesAndServices: Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: This tastefully decorated restaurant is housed in a late - 18C building, which is marked on an old map from the Napoleonic era. Here the best local ingredients are selected to create regional dishes with the occasional contemporary twist.

Name: Bistrot La Perla
Address: strada Col Alt 105, Corvara in Badia, 39033, Italy
Description: Take a culinary journey from the north of Italy to the south from the comfort of your table at the Bistrot La Perla, where guests are enthusiastically introduced to the many delightful flavours and ingredients this beautiful country has to offer. Excellent fish specialities also available.

Name: Pascalucci
Address: via Appia 1, San Nicola Manfredi, 82010, Italy
Description: A traditional restaurant serving regional cuisine, as well as skilfully prepared fish dishes made from fresh produce. Specialities include Beneventano beef fillet and octopus in aspic jelly.

Name: Unterwirt
Description: Occupying a private house, this restaurant boasts a couple of old Stube-style dining rooms, one of which is highly romantic and dates back to the 13C – although it looks as though the vintage wood may have come from elsewhere, it has in fact all been here for centuries. The owner-chef creates carefully thought-out dishes which combine precision and classic comfort with the occasional modern touch, harmoniously combining the flavours of the Alto Adige with Mediterranean influences, with a particular focus on fish. A welcoming outdoor terrace for summer dining completes the picture.

Name: Tenuta del Gallo
Description: Whether you dine indoors in the charming, romantic dining room or outdoors with views of the surrounding countryside, you’ll enjoy traditional local cuisine and classic Italian favourites at this restaurant. Our inspectors particularly enjoyed the excellent beef carpaccio with truffles and the local guinea fowl with chickpeas. Comfortable guestrooms are also available.

Name: Crotasc
Address: via Don Primo Lucchinetti 63, Mese, 23020, Italy
Description: Here one can choose between a smaller, typically mountain style dining room with stone paving and open fireplace and a larger room in contemporary rustic style. In summer one can dine on the terrace.

Name: Il Baretto
Description: Il Baretto on the outskirts of Padova is a must for anyone who loves classic, traditional fish and seafood, thanks to its menu which includes a number of typical Venetian dishes. The top-quality fish is skilfully prepared to bring out its full flavour and distinctive characteristics, providing a real treat for the tastebuds in this inland temple to the sea.

Name: La Luge
Address: Perreres, loc. Varvoyes, Breuil Cervinia, 11021, Italy
Cuisine: Cuisine from the Aosta Valley, Italian
Description: This attractive, rustic - style restaurant is situated just a few kilometres from the centre of Cervinia. It stands in a tranquil, panoramic basin where the only neighbours are the marmots in the hills around. Popular with passing tourists, as well as locals who feel the journey out here is well worth the effort. The restaurant offers a good range of choices for all palates. This includes soups, different cuts of meat, typical specialities from the Aosta valley and even a few fish dishes. This address is also worth a mention for the attractive guestrooms available.

Name: Osteria Cascina dei Fiori
Description: This restaurant’s warm, elegant and rustic atmosphere with wooden furniture and exposed beams provides the setting for its seasonally inspired, regional cuisine. The experienced owners are welcoming and attentive, while the menu features specialities such as frogs’ leg and courgette flower risotto.

Name: Paolo Teverini
Address: via del Popolo 2, Bagno di Romagna, 47021, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Wheelchair access
Description: Situated in the charming village of Bagno di Romagna and surrounded by beautiful rolling hills, Teverini is a culinary name full of history in this area. The cuisine here demonstrates different traditions – the local region is an obvious influence (especially its mushrooms), but fish and seafood also feature along with plenty of vegetables.

Name: Antica Osteria dei Camelì
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Occupying an attractive farmhouse dating back to the 16C, this restaurant boasts an interesting combination of antique elegance and modern style. The cuisine is equally impressive, offering a selection of traditional and innovative dishes that pay close attention to nutritional balance and the healthiness of the combinations of ingredients.

Name: Roscioli
Description: This restaurant is part of one of the best food outlets in Rome, which offers delicacies such as typical Roman pastas, cooked and raw fish, meat, an impressive selection of cured hams and cheeses, as well as top-quality ingredients such as anchovies and mozzarella. Excellent home-baked bread and a varied wine list complete the picture. Make sure you book ahead, as it’s hard to get a table here without a reservation.

Name: Osteria degli Angeli
Description: An attractive restaurant which offers a friendly and informal welcome and service, alongside an elegant, personalised yet classic decor. The cuisine is mainly Mediterranean in flavour, emphasised by the use of local and seasonal ingredients. The self-taught chef here is passionate about his cuisine.

Name: Casa Fantini/Lake Time
Description: Situated on the lakefront in the attractive town of Pella, this modern and welcoming restaurant occupies an old building which has been restored and furnished with a stylish and harmonious decor. Offering simpler options at lunchtime, the restaurant serves traditional cuisine reinterpreted and presented with a contemporary flavour. A lounge, garden, swimming pool and 11 guestrooms add to the exclusive appeal.

Name: La Taverna di Bacco
Description: A small restaurant just a stone’s throw from the sea which is memorable for its chic decor and intimate ambience. The cuisine combines traditional influences with an innovative approach resulting in ambitious, creative and modern dishes. The wine list is particularly worthy of note.

Name: Novo Osteria
Address: piazza De Cristoforis 30, Borgonovo Val Tidone, 29011, Italy
Description: Originally a monastery, this building dating back to the 11C was later transformed into an inn. Having closed at the beginning of this century, the building has now been fully renovated and restored to its original function, while retaining much of its original architecture. In addition to the restaurant, which serves traditional local cuisine with a modern focus and plenty of flavour (we particularly enjoyed the savoury zabaglione gnocchi with porcini mushrooms, Jerusalem artichokes and currants), there are also seven guestrooms available in the adjoining Locanda Borgo Impero.

Name: Aqua
Description: The most attractive space in this restaurant is its contemporary, almost Milanese-style veranda-dining room which boasts relaxing views of Lake Garda, with sailboats bobbing on the water ruffled by the famous Ora wind, and the peaks of Trentino in the distance. The Italian cuisine served here is prepared simply, allowing the quality of the ingredients (many of which are sourced locally) to shine through. Fish from the lake takes pride of place, although saltwater fish also features. There’s also a good selection of wine.

Name: Konnubio
Address: via dei Conti 8 r, Florence, 50123, Italy
Description: An informal yet attractive setting in which to enjoy modern cuisine, including a choice of tasting menus with a focus on meat, fish or vegetables. We particularly enjoyed the beef fillet in a seed crust, which was pink and succulent and served with radicchio and buttery mashed potatoes. The interesting wine selection includes labels from Italy and further afield, which are subdivided by grape variety. If you want to eat at the romantic little table on the step, make sure you book well in advance!

Name: Osteria della Foce
Description: This simple restaurant stands out for its delicious, authentic cuisine which is influenced by Ligurian and Italian traditions alike. The culinary techniques used are classic, both in its meat dishes (the roast veal is excellent) and fish options (raw fish dishes often feature on the menu). First courses include a home-made bronze-cut pasta (“trafilata al bronzo”) which is served with sauces inspired by whatever is in season or available in the market.

Name: ConTatto
Description: Situated in a small town just a few kilometres from the capital, this restaurant run by two young food enthusiasts serves regional dishes with a modern touch, such as cuttlefish with asparagus and a Bernese sauce. Guests can visit the interesting tufa-rock cellar, where the chef experiments with old preserving techniques and special flavourings. In addition, the cellar is used as a venue for exhibitions by different art galleries every season.

Name: Il Grano di Pepe
Description: While you’re trying to decide between the tasting menu and the à la carte at this restaurant, you can tuck into its excellent bread, including the “sfincione” – a type of tomato-flavoured focaccia from Palermo which makes the journey here worthwhile on its own! If fish is your preference, we recommend the “Palermo and Marseille” fish stew, an intense dish full of bold and delicious flavours. Minimalist decor and a friendly welcome from chef Rino Duca complete the picture.

Name: Angiò-Macelleria di Mare
Description: The phrase “macellaria di mare” translates as “fish and seafood butcher’s”, a reference to the cured and seasoned fish that features on the menu here. The restaurant offers an original formula in which guests chat to the chef and choose their dish at the counter where ingredients are displayed, before taking a seat in the simple yet attractive dining room with its open-view kitchen. Our advice is to give young chef Alberto Angiolucci free reign – the result is a new take on fish and seafood cuisine.

Name: Emozioni
Description: Situated in the heart of the historic centre, this quiet restaurant with attractive stone walls and wooden ceilings boasts a pleasantly elegant and relaxed atmosphere. The chef pays particular attention to local ingredients which he reinterprets with modern and highly personal touches.

Name: Trattoria del Cimino dal 1895
Description: Situated on the hill leading to Palazzo Farnese, this restaurant occupies the oldest building in the village, which dates back to 1370. Since 1940, the Calistri family have been delighting their guests with delicious specialities from Lazio, including excellent cured hams, fresh pasta (the amatriciana is particularly renowned), grilled meats and an impressive selection of cheeses and desserts. Excellent wines and spirits complete the picture.

Name: Le Colonne
Description: You’d recognise this cuisine as southern Italian even if you were blindfolded, thanks to its strong and intense flavours. Imaginatively prepared and presented dishes, many of which showcase the region’s mozzarella cheese, plus a delicious selection of desserts and pastries. All in all, an excellent choice!

Name: Acqua Pazza
Description: Although this restaurant is not in the centre, if you’re looking for excellent fish (mostly from the Mediterranean) personally selected by the owner - chef, then it’s well worth the few minutes it takes to find a parking space here. Beautifully cooked food, which is simply prepared using top - quality produce.

Name: Sale Grosso
Description: A simple, bistro - style restaurant serving well - prepared, mainly Mediterranean - style cuisine. Although fish and seafood dominate the menu, there are also a few vegetarian dishes and vegan specialities available.

Name: Trattoria Battibecco
Description: Situated in a narrow street in the city centre, this stylish, elegant restaurant is renowned for its traditional dishes and seafood specialities. Simpler fare at more moderate prices available at lunchtime.

Name: SottoSopra
Description: A pleasant and colourful restaurant in the village centre, divided into several dining rooms. The owner-chef prepares a range of eclectic dishes with passion and enthusiasm, offering a menu which includes meat dishes alongside fish options (salt- and freshwater), as well as a few regional specialities.

Name: Madama Vigna
Description: This restuarant has a good wine list with a focus on local labels, as well as an excellent selection of regional specialities on the menu. Dishes include agnolotti (a type of stuffed pasta) with fondue, Piedmontese beef, Villanova chicken and the inevitable bunet dessert.

Name: La Capanna di Eraclio
Address: Località per Le Venezie 21, Codigoro, 44021, Italy
Description: Whenever we visit Capanna di Eraclio, we have the strange yet wonderful feeling of coming home. Opened in 1922 and now in the hands of the fourth generation of the family, this restaurant has changed little – to our relief – since the time when a kitchen was first added to the inn that already stood here. The atmosphere is that of a simple, traditional family trattoria, yet with unexpected touches of elegance. The cuisine, meanwhile, focuses on the best ingredients that the Po delta has to offer, from scallops and small sole to superb eel and blue crab served steamed in its shell to bring out its full flavours, with a fresh mayonnaise on the side. It's interesting to note that this unique restaurant is situated seven metres below sea level!

Name: San Marco
Description: This long-established restaurant in the Asti region has been open for over 70 years and is still renowned for its regional cuisine served in a classic-style dining room. Dishes include cardoons with Raschera cheese fondue, the famous agnolottini del plin (a type of ravioli), and the Piedmontese bunet which is part of a trio of desserts that includes hazelnut tart and zabaglione with Canelli muscat wine.

Name: Bacco
Description: The focus at this restaurant is on a variety of local ingredients and specialities that even a novice food-lover would recognise as typical of this region. The owner-chef at this intimate and elegant gem of a restaurant is Ruggiero Doronzo, whose mantra is “simplicity and seasonality”.

Name: Carne & Spirito
Description: The environment here is elegantly rustic thanks to fine furnishings and colourful décor – an attractive background to the variety of creative and imaginative specialties on offer. Rooms are neat and simple. Charming rooms, furnished in different styles with elegant simplicity.

Name: Osteria Al GiGianca
Description: Although the out - of - town location is a slight drawback, this restaurant passionately run has a welcoming atmosphere. Seasonal, regional cuisine, plus a good choice of wine and beers.

Name: Vicolo Colombina
Description: Situated right in the heart of the historic centre among the narrow alleyways near the market and Piazza Maggiore, this restaurant serves traditional cuisine (no fish) with a subtle contemporary twist. Two modern dining rooms with modern decor, plus a wine list with a focus on regional labels.

Name: Taverna Kerkira
Address: corso Vittorio Emanuele 217, Bagnara Calabra, 89011, Italy
Description: Kerkira (Corfu in Greek) owes its existence to the chef’s Greek mother, who passed on the culinary traditions of her native island to her son. These traditions are alive and well in this taverna, which also features Calabrese and Mediterranean dishes on the menu. Simple dining room with a friendly ambience, not far from the centre and seafront in the village where singer Mia Martini was born.

Name: Benedikto
Address: via Eremo delle Carceri 1/a, Assisi, 06081, Italy
Description: Situated in the elegant setting of the Nun hotel on the edge of Assisi’s historic centre, Benedikto serves typical Umbrian ingredients which are transformed into creative and imaginative dishes by talented chef Enea Barbanera. In fine weather, dinner is served on the romantic outdoor terrace with views of Assisi’s castle.

Name: Zunica 1880
Address: piazza Filippi Pepe 14, Civitella del Tronto, 64010, Italy
Description: The pleasant outdoor space and some of the hotel rooms at Zunica overlook Civitella del Tronto’s central square on which this restaurant stands. For more than 100 years, Zunica 1880 has been a proud standard-bearer for typical Abruzzi cuisine, as well as dishes influenced by the nearby Marche region. Seasonal vegetables take pride of place on the menu, served with carefully selected meat (make sure you try the lamb and pigeon!), all prepared with a fine balance of traditional and contemporary styles.

Name: La Maison du Gourmet
Description: Housed in a fully renovated old farm in the countryside outside Parma, this gourmet restaurant serves top-quality meat and fish dishes with a focus on creativity rather than local traditions. The starters are particularly delicious!

Name: Aubergine
Description: Situated in a town famous for its thermal baths, this classically elegant restaurant serves meat and fish cuisine including specialities from the Veneto such as Berico ham, bigoli pasta with sardines, and veal liver with onions.

Name: Serpillo
Address: via di Mezzo 1, località Torre del Colle, Bevagna, 06031, Italy
Description: Situated in a charming medieval village which is also home to a couple of small hotels, this attractive, rustic restaurant in an old olive mill acts as the backdrop for regional and Italian cuisine. Dishes with a touch of modern flavour are presented on a menu which, although not extensive, offers good value for money.

Name: Il Ristorantino - Da Dino
Address: via XXV Aprile 11, Anzola dell'Emilia, 40011, Italy
Description: Tucked away in an unexpected location in a residential district, this restaurant is nonetheless popular with its loyal and regular clientele. And the reason is obvious – the high quality of the cuisine served here. Bologna’s traditional specialities and other Italian dishes are joined on the menu by a few fish options on Thursdays and Fridays.

Name: Cacciatori
Description: You pass through beautiful hilly scenery to get to Cartosio, where you’ll find this typical country house specialising in local cuisine. Although it’s been in business for several decades, during which nine different generations have been at the helm, the formula has (fortunately!) hardly changed, with a focus on Piedmontese dishes made from top-quality local and seasonal ingredients, with the main courses still cooked on the wood-fired stove. The wine list includes some excellent vertical labels, especially from the main wineries in the Langhe. Simple yet attractive guestrooms are also available.

Name: L'Angolo d'Abruzzo
Description: For almost 40 years, the Angolo d’Abruzzo restaurant has been home to the Centofanti family, who act as excellent ambassadors for the region by offering the best local, seasonal ingredients (for this reason, there’s no fish on the menu) in a host of traditional, regional recipes. Specialities such as cured meats, local ham, bruschetta and fresh home-made pasta (including “chitarra” spaghetti) take centre stage, while main courses include grilled dishes (porcini mushrooms in season, cuts of beef and veal at any time of year) and stews (mutton etc). When it comes to dessert, make sure you try the crème caramel with Navelli saffron. A misleading sign saying “sagrestia” (sacristy) actually indicates the well-stocked wine cellar.

Name: VeRo - Venetian Roots
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Wheelchair access
Description: Situated within the elegant Hotel Ca' di Dio in the Arsenale district where the Venice Biennale is held, VeRo is an elegant, exclusive and trendy restaurant. Despite the ambience, however, it’s the cuisine that is the real attraction here, thanks to excellent local and Italian ingredients which are transformed into creative dishes with references to the Venetian lagoon. Influences from other Italian regions also feature, including the occasional nod to skilful chef Luigi Lionetti’s native Campania.

Name: Alajmo Cortina
Description: Situated in the restored premises of the historic El Toulà restaurant, Alajmo Cortina is home to a bar on the ground floor, with the restaurant occupying the two upper floors (no lift). Although traditional in feel with a profusion of wood, the restaurant is run by a young and enthusiastic team. The cuisine focuses mainly on the region, although the menu also features fish and other imaginative options on tasting menus and an à la carte.

Name: Mirko's
Address: discesa Annunziata 1, Castellammare del Golfo, 91014, Italy
Description: This small restaurant, located near the steps to Cala Piccola, is run by an entire family and is beginning to earn an excellent local reputation. The son is at the helm in the kitchen. Having gained experience elsewhere for many years, he decided to start his own venture, which shows every sign of having paid off. Enjoy excellent fish and seafood specialities cooked in Mediterranean and Sicilian style in a quiet, beautifully kept dining room.

Name: La Bottega del 30
Address: via Santa Caterina 2, località Villa a Sesta, Castelnuovo Berardenga, 53019, Italy
Description: There’s a story behind the name of this restaurant: on the 30th day of every month a travelling salesman used to stop in this small, delightful village. In the meantime, a young French chef, Hélène, arrived here and fell in love with Chianti and its cuisine. She named her restaurant after the travelling salesman and the name has been kept in his memory. In a typical setting of stone walls and old rural objects from bygone days, Hélène is now front-of-house taking care of guests, while Nadia Mongiat has replaced her in the kitchen, where she continues with the restaurant’s tradition of creating simple Tuscan cuisine. The focus here is on preparing ingredients in traditional ways, such as pork liver (the thinnest part of the liver is used) cooked at a low temperature and then stored in lard with fennel for a few days before being re-heated sous-vide in a bain-marie. As a result, the liver (served lukewarm on a bed of Tuscan green beans) is soft and delicious.

Name: Galileo
Address: via IV Novembre conc. 25, Civitanova Marche, 62012, Italy
Description: Boasting a dining room overlooking the beach, Galileo is a typical Adriatic restaurant serving fish and seafood dishes that are popular with many Italians. Options include seafood salad, a selection of antipasti, fish and seafood pastas, assorted small fried fish, and grilled recipes. In other words, delicious, traditional and unfussy cuisine in which fish takes centre stage.

Name: La Bul
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Here, in one of Bari’s most interesting restaurants, chef Antonio Scalera serves top-quality cuisine accompanied by intelligently chosen wines with fascinating stories behind them. The dishes often feature traditional recipes and ingredients from Puglia yet are creative and of the highest quality.

Name: Trattoria Toscana al Vecchio Forno
Address: via Poliziano 18, San Quirico d'Orcia, 53027, Italy
Description: If you are looking for a place to eat that is centrally located and has good prices, you have found it. Captivating trattoria atmosphere. Pretty summer garden.

Name: Caffè delle Rose Bistrot
Description: Occupying an early 20C building in the heart of Pallanza’s picturesque historic centre, this authentic bistro now has a young and contemporary feel. Run by Massimiliano Celeste, a talented chef who is very well known in the region, the restaurant specialises in Mediterranean cuisine prepared with a touch of imagination. There’s a small chef’s table in front of the kitchen, plus an old ice-house (now a small wine cellar housing some excellent wines) which is well worth visiting.

Name: I Carracci
Description: The ceiling at this restaurant is adorned with superb frescoes thought to be by the school of the Carracci brothers, whose painters were definitely responsible for decorating other rooms in this palazzo. This is one good reason for choosing this restaurant, and the cuisine is another – the new chef here creates dishes which are appealingly creative without being overly fussy or excessive.

Name: Alle Codole
Address: via XX Agosto 27, Canale d'Agordo, 32020, Italy
Description: ‘Codole’ is the nickname of the family that runs this restaurant and whose ancestors once worked in the copper mines in the area. Today, the family has exchanged mining for cooking, offering guests specialities such as ricotta and black truffle ravioli with a lamb ragù, and loin of venison in a porcini mushroom crust.

Name: Al Carroponte
Description: This restaurant is renowned in Bergamo for its good choice of varied cuisine, as well as its lively, buzzing atmosphere. The excellent, tasty cuisine is typically Italian and contemporary in style, and includes luxury ingredients such as lobster and caviar, while the “classic” à la carte is enhanced by a selection of cured hams, cheeses and finger food. But the Carroponte’s beating heart is owner Oscar Mazzoleni’s passion for the world of wine, with an incredible selection of over 2 000 labels that puts many more famous Michelin-starred restaurants in the shade.

Name: Barbieri
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Enjoy your meal in the classic - style dining room or on the outdoor terrace in fine weather. The menu here is seasonal, with a focus on delicious Calabrian cuisine, while the wine list also features exclusively local options.

Name: Matteo Ristorante
Description: The soft-toned decor is modern and intimate, while the cuisine also has a contemporary feel. Dishes include meat and fish options, plus numerous types of risottos, many of which feature distinctly modern ingredients. Coffee service and aperitifs in the near Laboratory, at n 10.

Name: Villa Tiboldi
Address: via Case Sparse 127, località Tiboldi, Canale, 12043, Italy
Description: A delightful combination of good food and a romantic ambience in this old restored farmhouse surrounded by hills. Top - quality cuisine and a wine cellar that is well worth a visit.

Name: Trattoria la Colonna
Address: Via Emilia Est 6, località San Nicolò, Rottofreno, 29010, Italy
Description: This classic-style restaurant with a recently renovated dining room is situated on the street that runs through the village of San Nicolò. Although the menu features some meat dishes (on Sundays in winter, this includes specialities such as boiled meats, anolini pasta in broth, and typical desserts such as ciambella cake with zabaglione), it is particularly renowned for its wide selection of fish options. At lunchtime during the week, there’s a choice of simpler recipes, but if you ask, staff will be happy to offer you the longer evening menu.

Name: Lord Nelson
Description: Situated right on the seafront, this restaurant plunges its guests back in time with its polished wood, mirrors and classic decor giving it the feel of an English galleon. Mediterranean cuisine made from top-quality ingredients takes centre stage here, while the extensive wine list features some vintage labels. The American bar offering a good selection of cocktails is perfect for the winter months.

Name: Macelleria Motta
Address: strada Padana Superiore 90, Bellinzago Lombardo, 20060, Italy
Description: Motta has established a reputation for quality, especially for its meat which is carefully sourced from farms in the Piedmont region. Some of the excellent options on the menu are aged in a large fridge near the entrance, along with different types of delicious salumi which are produced and cured by the restaurant. Various types of meat feature here – these are cured or cooked using classic methods with the occasional modern touch. Piedmontese beef is one of the highlights, with different cuts grilled on the barbecue or served boiled. Make sure you try the 300g hamburger with Aosta valley Toma cheese, BBQ sauce and caramelised onions served in a sesame-seed bun. Enjoy alfresco dining in a typical Lombardy courtyard in summer.

Name: Frosio
Description: Housed in a 18C villa which was once a family inn, this restaurant is run by the dynamic and professional Frosio family who have over 30 years’ experience in the restaurant business. There’s nothing improvised about Frosio, where Camillo guarantees impeccable service front of house and Paolo is at the helm in the kitchen, creating carefully prepared dishes with a classic-modern feel and an equal emphasis on meat and fish, often made from traditionally “gourmet” ingredients such as scampi, lobster, foie gras, pigeon and caviar. The wine list continues to offer an excellent selection, with one section dedicated to Italy and another to the rest of the world. Decorated with austere elegance, the wine cellar in the 13C tower is home to more than 1,000 different labels. Attractive outdoor space for summer dining.

Name: Ristorante Mas-cì
Description: Situated in the charming historic centre, this hotel and restaurant are now run by the third generation of the same family. Welcoming dining rooms with a fireplace provide the setting for cuisine which makes the most of local produce while also including dishes from elsewhere in Italy. Don’t miss the black truffle specialities!

Name: Pantagruele
Description: Situated in the town centre just a stone’s throw from the port, this small, typical trattoria is renowned for its delicious fish and seafood, including an excellent antipasto buffet and fresh fish cooked mainly on the grill. The large outdoor area is perfect for summer dining. Informal service.

Name: Locanda Gulfi
Description: Situated in a secluded area of olive groves and vineyards, Locanda Gulfi also produces its own oil and wine, as confirmed by the view of the wine cellar from the dining room. The cuisine features an attractive selection of classic Sicilian dishes, while guestrooms are available for anyone keen to extend their stay.

Name: La Madia
Description: This authentic rural trattoria overlooking the valley and Franciacorta specialises in regional produce and typical Italian cuisine. Each dish on the menu lists the origin of the ingredients used, plus the name and address of the producer. Specialities include tagliolini pasta sautéed in a walnut sauce with tuna. Top quality cuisine offering excellent value for money.

Name: Carlo Magno
Description: This restaurant housed in a country house dating from the 19C offers elegant period dining rooms and a menu featuring Mediterranean-style meat and fish dishes.

Name: Oblige
Description: This new address with a cocktail bar and bistro (Noblesse) in the centre of historic Vignola is also home to a gourmet restaurant (Oblige), where chef Angelo serves easily identifiable yet technically skilful dishes. We recommend the game dishes cooked over the barbecue grill, such as the delicious local guinea fowl served with mustard mashed potato and sautéed radicchio. The wine list features labels from Italy and further afield with something suitable for every dish, including a few bottles that will appeal to wine connoisseurs.

Name: Pierre - Trattoria Sartoriale
Description: Situated on the edge of the historic centre, this simple restaurant with just a few tables serves beautifully presented dishes. The menu features a limited number of options, all made with the best of whatever the market has available, and creatively prepared with little fuss and a focus on bringing out the ingredients’ full flavour.

Name: Podere Belvedere Tuscany
Address: via San Piero a Strada 23, Pontassieve, 50065, Italy
Description: Occupying a tower house dating from 1700, this restaurant is surrounded by typical Tuscan scenery of olive groves and vineyards, as well as vegetable gardens and farms which produce many of the ingredients featuring in the dishes here. The friendly self-taught chef celebrates the best of Tuscan country cuisine, with a focus on meat, including grilled dishes and top-quality vegetables, as well as the occasional more creative dish – the result is cuisine of a very high standard. The restaurant also has a few guestrooms – a convenient option given the property’s attractive secluded location.

Name: Antica Farmacia
Description: As its name suggests, this restaurant was used as a pharmacy until the late 1970s. In 2010, it was taken over by owner-chef Juri who now runs his own restaurant here, serving Tuscan-inspired cuisine made using local ingredients and recipes which he reinterprets with a light touch. Full of flavour, dishes include highlights such as baked marrow and Tuscan Chianti beef stew.

Name: Locanda San Michele
Address: SS 491 3, Contrada Camerale di Tossiccia, Montorio al Vomano, 64046, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Practically on the slopes of Gran Sasso with views of the verdant landscapes of the Abruzzo, this restaurant is home to a local chef who has returned to his roots having spent time away gaining experience in Michelin-starred restaurants. Here, he serves regional cuisine with a modern, contemporary twist and a focus on meat and fish alike (examples include tuna tartare with strawberries finished in the dining room with lemon “snow”) in generous portions that are typical of the Abruzzo.

Name: [àbitat]
Address: via Henry Dunant 1, San Fermo della Battaglia, 22020, Italy
Description: A young, enthusiastic and professional couple has taken over the reins at this modern and welcoming restaurant, serving cuisine that is inspired by a sustainable and seasonal approach. Ingredients include herbs harvested from their own garden, as well as typical produce from the mountains and the sea, all sourced from trusted suppliers who demonstrate full respect for nature and animals. Food waste is kept to a minimum to ensure a circular-based cuisine.

Name: La Porta Antica
Address: via Quarto dei Mille 16, Brescia, 25128, Italy
Description: Having gained experience elsewhere in Italy, especially in Liguria where he gained confidence preparing the best-quality fish and seafood, Augusto Valzelli has returned home to demonstrate his own modern approach to fish cuisine. Fish-lovers will delight in his “gran crudo di mare” (raw fish selection) which allows the quality of the fish – the restaurant’s main attraction – to shine through. If you want to order this particular dish, it’s best to mention it when booking.

Name: Parco Gambrinus
Address: via Capitello 18, San Polo di Piave, 31020, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: A rustic and romantic setting provides the backdrop for the traditional and creative cuisine served here. It is made from typical local produce with an emphasis on ethical and sustainably produced ingredients (vegan and gluten - free options are also available). Exotic animals inhabit the park, where a stream is home to the house specialities of crayfish, eels and sturgeon. The restaurant also offers a few comfortable guestrooms nearby.

Name: Taverna da Ciacco
Address: via Dante Alighieri 30/a, San Quirico d'Orcia, 53027, Italy
Description: A welcoming restaurant with a rustic feel. The owner - chef delights guests with his traditional yet imaginative delicacies, such as pici pasta with Pachino cherry tomatoes, garlic and chilli peppers and the renowned Chianina steak. Fish occasionally features on the menu.

Name: Osteria del Mare già il "Votapentole"
Address: via IV Novembre 15, Castiglione della Pescaia, 58043, Italy
Description: This charming restaurant right in the town centre boasts colourful decor and a lively, relaxed atmosphere. Fish and seafood from the nearby Mediterranean are served in imaginative dishes full of character, including highly recommended raw dishes and the popular “caciucco” (Tuscan fish stew).

Name: Ai Do Campanili
Description: Both the building in which it is housed and the dining room of this restaurant are on the small side, but the quality of the food more than compensates for the lack of space. Run by young and enthusiastic staff, the restaurant specialises in fish and seafood with raw options and modern dishes featuring on the menu. Excellent selection of wine, also available to take away.

Name: Osteria dai Coghi
Address: via Alcide De Gasperi 9/13, Albarè di Costermano, 37010, Italy
Description: This well-kept, welcoming restaurant with a colourful decor and wine bottles adorning the walls serves imaginative dishes with modern combinations – our inspector particularly enjoyed the guinea fowl supreme with smoked black tea, carrots and beluga lentils. The well-chosen wine list features labels from Italy and further afield.

Name: Locanda dell'Arcimboldo
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: At the town gates, a friendly inn with a family atmosphere in a fine building, with a pleasant veranda. Fish dishes prevail on the menu, featuring an interesting selection of oysters. At midday there is also an easier set menu.

Name: Babette
Description: Situated just beyond the centre of Albenga in a beautiful location right on the beach (with only a small private beach club separating it from the sea), this restaurant has been in business for over 20 years (10 years on this site, and 10 in the town centre before that). It is renowned for its excellent, modern cuisine that focuses on top-quality, fresh and seasonal fish. A lighter (yet equally excellent) menu is also available at lunchtime.

Name: Lu Pisantinu
Address: viale Giovanni Maria Orecchioni snc, loc. Liscia di Vacca, Arzachena, 07021, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Great view,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: A terrace framed by granite columns overlooks the coast and Porto Cervo at this restaurant, which is decorated in light shades and pastel tones echoing the colours of the sea. Imaginative fish cuisine.

Name: Agriturismo Il Cavallino
Address: SP 55 Saturnia-Semproniano, località Fibbianello, Semproniano, 58055, Italy
Description: Situated in a very quiet and secluded location, this restaurant is run by an enthusiastic young couple: he has inherited the family business and, having gained experience in other restaurants in the region, is now at the helm in the kitchen, while his partner oversees the front of house. The options on the à la carte and wine list, the latter featuring a small yet impressive choice of wines, have a strong regional focus.

Name: Zur Kaiserkron
Description: Now under new management, this historic restaurant in the centre of Bolzano occupies the ground floor of the attractive Palazzo Pock overlooking the square. Here, elegant, contemporary-style dining rooms with charming vaulted ceilings provide the setting for Mediterranean-influenced cuisine with a distinctly contemporary flavour.

Name: La Kucina
Address: via Giulio De Petra 67, Foggia, 71121, Italy
Description: This modern, welcoming restaurant on the outskirts of town serves contemporary cuisine on a varied menu which also includes simpler options to suit all budgets, especially at lunchtime. In the dining room, a cabinet for ageing meat houses some excellent Iberian hams.

Name: Feria
Description: Feria has two different spaces – a bistro-bar serving cocktails and street food, and a gourmet restaurant where chef Feltrin and his team showcase the full range of their culinary skills. The dishes here are colourful, full of flavour and carefully thought out, demonstrating Indonesian influences that recall the chef’s personal and professional experiences in this Asian country. Options include two tasting menus (a good starting point that allow you to appreciate the chef’s creativity to the full) and an à la carte. The excellent wine list is overseen by sommelier Régis Ramos who skilfully assists guests with their choices.

Name: Coeur de Bois
Cuisine: Cuisine from the Aosta Valley, Classic Cuisine
Description: The name of this elegant restaurant was inspired by its wooden ceiling. Surrounded by spruce decor dating from the 18C, antique furniture and paintings, enjoy interesting traditional cuisine in this excellent gourmet restaurant, which is all the more attractive thanks to its location in the Gran Paradiso national park.

Name: Michelasso
Description: Situated in the city centre, this refined restaurant with an elegantly classic decor is perfect for a romantic, intimate dinner. The menu features meat and fish, with traditional dishes reinterpreted thanks to the chef’s expertise and proven experience. In summer, choose a table on the pleasant outdoor space overlooking the lively Via Santa Brigida.

Name: Locanda di Nonna Ida
Address: Località Pontarola 12, Marano di Valpolicella, 37020, Italy
Description: A welcoming inn nestled amid the last vineyards of Valpolicella and the first pasturelands of the lower Lessinia region, where a young chef serves cuisine with a focus on local ingredients and classic Italian recipes with a modern twist. In summer, the terrace offers a fresh, cool setting with extensive views. The barbecued meat is superb.

Name: Cappuccini Cucina San Francesco
Description: Housed in the resort of the same name, this elegant restaurant is full of historic charm, enhanced by its white damask linen and beautiful candlesticks. The wine list pays obvious tribute to the famous Franciacorta region and also includes an excellent choice of champagnes, while the modern cuisine shows touches of traditional influence alongside more creative twists. Seasonal ingredients are to the fore here.

Name: Locanda dei Cantù
Description: At the bottom of a steep valley, a rustic restaurant that offers fine cuisine, much appreciated in the area, with a great preference for local products. Old traditional recipes are revisited with a personal touch.

Name: Oltre.
Description: This restaurant in the lively Mercato delle Erbe district has an entrance adorned with hundreds of stickers, giving it the appearance of a record shop rather than a contemporary-style eatery with a bar counter and a highly original surfboard table near the entrance. The modern cuisine has its roots in the region yet also includes skilfully prepared dishes from around the world. There’s also a choice of cocktails to start or round off your meal. Booking is highly recommended.

Name: Villa Pignano
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Terrace
Description: A veritable Garden of Eden just 15km from Volterra, this 300ha estate is home to a restaurant with a strong zero-mile philosophy. This is backed up by its careful use of ingredients grown or produced on the estate itself, such as vegetables, olives and grains, as well as chicken, pork and honey – a sustainable approach that results in delicious, contemporary cuisine. The dishes here are fresh and full of flavour yet elaborate and modern in style (note the simpler menu at lunchtime). The interesting wine list explores Tuscany through its choice of top-quality organic labels as well as including wines produced from the estate’s own vines.

Name: Mater Bistrot
Description: An informal bistro where the imaginative cuisine prepared by the owner-chef showcases the best Italian recipes while remaining open to influences from other parts of the world, resulting in strong, unique and captivating flavours. Guests also have the option of smaller dishes to share, but if you really want to get to know the essence of this restaurant, it’s best to go for the guided menu.

Name: Locanda Stella d'Oro
Description: The original flavour and magic of a trattoria can still be found in this establishment. The cuisine is traditional with a personal touch.

Name: Osteria dell'Arco
Description: Enjoy a warm family welcome at this centrally located restaurant with an internal courtyard, where the menu features a good choice of traditional and authentic dishes full of flavour. The restaurant is run by the same friendly managers as the renowned and popular Boccondivino in Bra, where the Slow Food concept was born. Booking ahead is always a good option.

Name: Andree
Address: via San Martino della Battaglia 16, La Spezia, 19121, Italy
Description: This restaurant in the centre of Spezia boasts a striking open-view kitchen in its small brick-vaulted dining room. Modern cuisine with a focus on superb fish dishes, accompanied by professional service and a wine list full of character.

Name: Tre Scalini
Description: The menu at this restaurant features meat and seasonal ingredients served in personalised recipes and contemporary-style dishes. There are also three tasting menus: the main one consists of eight courses prepared by the talented chef. The restaurant brings to mind a modern bistro with its warm ambience and attentive service.

Name: Le Nove Scodelle
Description: Now available everywhere in Italy, ethnic cuisine is gradually becoming more specialised, as is the case in this restaurant serving specialities from the province of Szechuan in south-west China. Exciting and original cuisine full of spicy flavours.

Name: La Locanda di Fabio e Vale
Description: Young, informal and friendly owners Fabio and Vale welcome guests to their restaurant in Offanengo, just a few kilometres from Crema. A good choice for anyone keen to sample moderately creative cuisine, including a good selection of fish-based dishes.

Name: Casa Coloni
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: Situated opposite the archaeological site, this restaurant occupies an old farmhouse which is part of a splendid 19C residence converted into an elegant hotel following a long and meticulous restoration. In fine weather, tables are set out under a cane pergola in a charming setting in the romantic garden. Here, the chef from Paestum serves his own reinterpretations of regional dishes with superb results. Impeccable service.

Name: Ad Astra
Address: via Cavour 11/13, Santa Maria della Versa, 27047, Italy
Description: This small yet smart restaurant in the Oltrepò Pavese region is a dream come true for owner-chef Alessandro Folli, whose cuisine shows the influence of his experience working in different restaurants around Europe. Ad Astra delights guests with dishes which demonstrate a perfect balance between modern and classic culinary styles. Bravo!

Name: Zest
Description: Situated within the luxury Grand Hotel La Favorita in the centre of Sorrento, this restaurant has the typically opulent style of a grand hotel. In the kitchen, the chef works with top-quality ingredients to create dishes influenced by Campania with his own personalised touches. Seasonal vegetable soup, “scuncilli” and marinated onions; red mullet served with fries, lettuce, radish and saffron mayonnaise; and Caprese 2.0 are some of the more interesting options on the menu.

Name: Azotea
Description: Situated in a central location with a small outdoor space, this restaurant boasts a striking interior with old walls, a verdant decor and climbing plants that add a South American feel. The cuisine shines the spotlight on the chef’s native Peru, with appetisers such as potted umbrine tacos and delicious yet atypical antipasti such as raw squid with saltwort and peas. Soy sauce, umeboshi, and yuyo seaweed sauce provide added exotic flavour. We highly recommend one of the excellent cocktails, such as the slightly sour Americano with yuzu.

Name: Terrazza Tiberio
Description: Housed on the first floor of the Tiberio hotel, this elegant restaurant boasts a terrace overlooking the rooftops of Capri. The regional and island specialities on the menu leave a lasting memory, such as the “montanara” (fried pizza), “casatiello” (a savoury bread from Naples) and the caprese-style ravioli, although more creative options also feature, especially among the desserts. All in all, an elegant dining experience.

Name: Cracco Portofino
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Great view,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: Famous chef Carlo Cracco has opened a restaurant in what was once Il Pitosforo, right opposite the small harbour in Portofino, so that his lucky guests enjoy fine views of the water, the small square and the enchanting bay. Here, skilful and competent executive chef Mattia Pecis serves lightly modern cuisine with occasional references to Ligurian recipes (such as cappon magro salad) and ingredients (many of the vegetables are sourced from Iva’s kitchen garden on the hills nearby), with a new cooling cabinet in which fish are “aged”. The delightful terrace, open in summer from 6.30pm onwards, is the perfect setting for alfresco aperitifs and dinners.

Name: KELINA Fine Dine
Address: Strada Lech de Boà s.n., Corvara in Badia, 39033, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Great view,Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus
Description: From Corvara, take the ultra-modern Boè cable-car to this restaurant (accessible also on skis or by foot) which is one of the dining options at the Piz Boè Alpine Lounge (for access, turn right as you exit the cable car). Open at lunchtime only, KELINA serves unexpectedly gourmet cuisine in a minimalist-style dining room which allows the stunning views of Sassongher, Santa Croce and La Varella to take centre-stage through the restaurant’s large floor-to-ceiling windows. There’s a restricted choice of dishes, all of which are creative and based on Alpine ingredients, with a new, highly experienced chef at the helm since early 2024. An excellent wine list completes the picture.

Name: Chalet Gerard
Address: via Plan de Gralba 37, Selva di Val Gardena, 39048, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: In a breathtakingly beautiful natural setting between the Sassolungo peak and the majestic Sella mountains, this restaurant serves simple mountain fare alongside a few more modern dishes, all of which are prepared from typical ingredients from the Alto Adige. Although you can’t book at lunchtime, bookings are required in the evening. Beautiful guestrooms are also available.

Name: Casa della Rocca
Description: Situated in picturesque Dolcedo, this restaurant occupies an early 20C mill complete with millstone and press. The cuisine focuses on an interesting selection of traditional Ligurian dishes with a satisfying balance of meat and fish (occasionally on the same plate), plus creative touches and hints of the Piedmont, all of which combine to make a trip to this inland restaurant well worth while!

Name: Pellico 3
Description: Situated in the luxury Park Hyatt hotel just a few metres from the Galleria Vittorio Emanuele, this restaurant is home to a young chef who serves elegant and occasionally complex cuisine. His dishes include sauces and traditions learned from his time working in France, as well as plenty of vegetables and Mediterranean influences.

Name: Masseria Moroseta
Description: Chef Giorgia Eugenia Goggi offers a unique and authentic gastronomic experience that focuses on fresh ingredients (mostly vegetables), many of which are sourced from small organic gardens. The 90€ menu celebrates Mediterranean cuisine to the full, with colourful dishes that are full of flavour and in which the freshness of the ingredients is allowed to shine through. The beautifully kept, rustic dining room provides an ideal setting for an unforgettable dinner, while the selection of natural Italian wines offers the perfect accompaniment to the chef’s dishes, further enhancing your dining experience. There are six comfortable guestrooms available should you wish to extend your stay and immerse yourself in these peaceful rural surroundings. Booking in advance is highly recommended given the restaurant’s popularity and unique appeal.

Name: Trattoria Margherita
Description: Don’t be fooled by the relatively simple ambience of this trattoria which is situated in the centre of a town with an interesting history linked to the reclamation of the marshes and the dairy industry. Dedicated to the owner’s two grandmothers, the restaurant serves some of Sardinia’s best-known meat and fish specialities.

Name: Belvedere
Description: Over the years, this family restaurant has become one of the most popular along this coastline. An informal dining room provides the backdrop for the decidedly Mediterranean cuisine served here, where the focus is the fish display cabinet that changes daily and from which guests can make their choice. The friendly and professional approach of the two brothers that run the restaurant has contributed to its success, while the brand-new terrace-lounge, with its stunning view, is the perfect spot for an aperitif or after-dinner drink.

Name: Millo Ristorante
Address: via Garibaldi 4, Santa Teresa Gallura, 07028, Italy
Description: An attractive restaurant serving reasonably priced fish and seafood (try the delicious squid with an orange and chicory sauce). There’s also a charming summer terrace from which to watch the town’s bustling nightlife.

Name: Amanõ
Description: The tilde accent over the “o” in the name of this restaurant is a subtle allusion to the sea that lies between Campania (the chef’s native region) and Sardinia (his adopted home). With just a few tables and an open-view kitchen, the dining room here is adorned with hand-made decorations, hence the name of the restaurant (“a mano” means “by hand”). The chef makes full use of Sardinian ingredients in his elaborate and creative cuisine, so this is a good choice for anyone seeking a change from traditional fare.

Name: Bistrot Royal
FacilitiesAndServices: Great view,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: In the refined rooms of Grand Hotel Royal e Golf, the dining room with its glass wall looks like a stage overlooking the chain of Monte Bianco and Dente del Gigante. The gastronomic proposal is one of the most appealing in the area: creative rather than local, the dishes are refined and technically elaborate.

Name: Ai Porteghi Bistrot
Description: Situated under the picturesque arcades on Via Cesare Battisti, this restaurant is home to a young chef whose cuisine is inspired by traditional and well-known recipes which he reinterprets with his own personal touch to create highly interesting dishes. Simpler and more reasonably priced options are also available at lunchtime.

Name: Stilla
Address: Località Casette 1, Colognola ai Colli, 37030, Italy
Description: Run by an enthusiastic and committed young couple who left the big city to restore the family home and transform it into an elegant, welcoming restaurant, Stilla stands in a tranquil location surrounded by vineyards. Here, Silvia creates original, generous and colourful cuisine which is showcased on an à la carte with just a few dishes which change regularly. We particularly enjoyed the freshly seared bonito served with wild spinach, sour cherries and a cherry barbecue sauce. Meals are served on the outdoor terrace in summer. Accommodation is also available in five beautiful yet functional guestrooms. Well worth a visit.

Name: Cocun Cellar Restaurant
Address: strada Prè de Vì 31, San Cassiano, 39036, Italy
Description: At this restaurant within the elegant Ciasa Salares hotel, guests dine in a wine cellar with a pleasantly informal and friendly atmosphere. In addition to the excellent cuisine, the fine cheese selection comes highly recommended, as does a visit to the room dedicated entirely to chocolate.

Name: Oltremare
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Great view,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: Situated on the fifth floor of the Due Torri hotel, the restaurant has recently been refurbished, giving it an even more charming and atmospheric feel than before. The cuisine is creative in style, almost always using ingredients and recipes from Campania as its inspiration – a good example is the many different ways tomato is used, including tomato water distilled in an alembic still. Chef Alfonso Crisci’s recipes are complex and always full of different ingredients and colours, with a selection of delicious and generous desserts to finish your meal.

Name: Remulass
Description: “Cooking with roots” is the mantra at Remulass, a phrase that has inspired the restaurant’s name (“wild radish” in the local Milanese dialect). This small, lively restaurant gets very busy in the evenings when booking is highly recommended. The attractively modern and colourful dishes here always feature plenty of root vegetables and aromatic herbs. We recommend the fermented vegetables with baked ricotta and a gin dressing.

Name: Pentole e Provette
Description: This restaurant run by Luca Trabalzini and his partner Rossella is a real gem in the small town of Fasano. Their story, which began in Australia, adds a fascinating touch to this gastronomic project. The atmosphere here is warm and lively, making this the perfect setting in which to enjoy the chef’s innovative cuisine, which he showcases on three distinct menus dedicated to meat, fish and vegetarian dishes respectively. Luca’s cuisine is modern and elegant, with particular attention paid to flavours and textures so that each and every dish offers a fully rounded sensorial experience.

Name: Urubamba
Description: Situated amid luxury boutiques and historic palazzi in one of Naples’ most exclusive districts, this restaurant boasts a chic and romantic dining room with soft lighting on the first floor, as well as an exclusive outdoor terrace for fine weather. The cuisine is totally in keeping with the trendy setting, featuring a successful combination of two different gastronomic cultures (namely Peruvian and Japanese) that blend together perfectly.

Name: L'Agave
Description: Perched on the cliff overlooking the small port of Framura, the terraces at this restaurant boast one of the most stunning views in the area. The dishes served up by the young chef are a declaration of his love for Liguria (as is the wine list), featuring a remarkable selection of top-quality regional ingredients such as artichokes and asparagus from Albenga, beans from Pigna, pine nuts, prebugiun (a mixture of wild plants), Taggiasca olives and of course local fish and seafood.

Name: San Tommaso 10
Description: In 1895 Luigi Lavazza opened here a grocery store where he immediately began blending coffee. 129 years later the place hosts a modern restaurant with a superb kitchen run by a chef who, despite hailing from the Marche region, treats guests to one of the most authentic interpretations of Piedmontese cuisine in the city, often with a creative touch. Among the options on offer here, the trolley of antipasti is a must.

Name: Il Tempo Nuovo
Description: Now occupied by a charming boutique hotel, the Castello di Ugento is also home to this restaurant where the Puglian chef reinterprets the traditions of Salento in contemporary dishes that feature an array of meat, fish and vegetables. The staff will be more than happy to recommend the best accompaniment to your meal, whether this is a good wine from the plentiful wine list or a delicious cocktail.

Name: Zanze XVI
Address: fondamenta dei Tolentini, sestiere Santa Croce 231, Venice, 30135, Italy
Description: Although the setting and convivial atmosphere in this restaurant recall that of a typical Venetian bàcaro , the cuisine is completely different in feel. The ingredients are sourced from the best markets and local producers, resulting in unique dishes that reflect the culinary traditions of the lagoon and its surrounding area. The few tables arranged outdoors with views of the tranquil canal add to the appeal, while the professional yet friendly service helps to put guests completely at ease.

Name: Principe di Belludia
Description: The Principe di Belludia is the gourmet restaurant at the Il San Corrado di Noto hotel, a luxurious resort in a secluded rural location with two enormous swimming pools. The new executive chef Martin Lazarov showcases his love for Sicily, with a particular attention to vegetables dishes.

Name: SOMS
Description: Situated in a pedestrianised area of the old town, the historic “società operaia di mutuo soccorso” (SOMS – a workers’ mutual aid association) has been transformed into a bright, welcoming restaurant where the chef creates dishes influenced by the traditions of the Abruzzi yet decidedly original in style (barbecued dishes are one of the specialities). Classic decor, plus a pleasant outdoor space for alfresco dining in summer.

Name: Cut
Description: Situated right in the heart of the Bergamo plain in the small town of Caravaggio, famous for the painter of the same name and for a much-visited pilgrim shrine, this welcoming restaurant boasts a modern decor and vintage furnishings. At lunchtime, it serves a good, competitively priced business menu, while in the evening the more elaborate à la carte features contemporary-style meat and fish dishes (mostly the latter).

Name: Maragoncello
Address: via San Giovanni 1, località Vighizzolo, Montichiari, 25018, Italy
Description: Situated in a small village in the Bassa Bresciana region, this restaurant comes as something of a surprise due to its focus on fish, with the selection of raw seafood options and the good-value-for-money tasting menu particular highlights. Personalised cuisine which is full of flavour, served in modern, convivial dining rooms.

Name: Anastasia
Description: This cocktail bar on the seafront is also a restaurant specialising in fresh fish served in a selection of classic dishes (such as tartare) and more elaborate recipes. The dining room is modern and spacious, plus there’s an outdoor terrace for alfresco dining in fine weather. Guestrooms and luxury apartments are also available (swimming pool on the roof).

Name: Qualia
Description: Situated in a side street in the centre of this charming small town, this restaurant boasts a dining room with exposed brickwork and glimpses of the kitchen, plus a small outdoor space with a few tables for alfresco dining. The dishes here are full of flavour and focus on regional ingredients and fresh fish.

Name: Al Moro
Address: via Pietri 1277, Marina Di Campo, 57034, Italy
Description: Situated away from the main tourist area, in a rustic building that is striking for its attractive outdoor space shaded by a wooden gazebo, this restaurant boasts an informal and relaxing atmosphere. The Mediterranean cuisine is full of character and prepared with top-quality ingredients, including a small selection of oysters.

Name: Li Somari
Description: Transferred to piazza Rivarola 21, Tivoli.Adriano Baldassarre’s small, intimate restaurant is situated in historic Tivoli, which is renowned for its fascinating history and Hadrian’s Villa. Popular with food-lovers, the restaurant serves delicacies such as oxtail ravioli and tripe, with a whole page of the menu dedicated to offal dishes, as well as panzanella and char by Alessandro Narducci, the latter paying tribute to a chef friend of Baldassare’s. A few tables set out on the promenade provide outdoor dining options, while the restaurant’s sustainable approach to dining is explained at the top of the menu.

Name: Cala Luna
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Great view,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: The elegant fine-dining restaurant at Le Calette boutique hotel, Cala Luna boasts an attractive dining room (Rizz'i Mari) where meals are served in low season, as well as an open-air garden on Via Presidiana for summer dining where, just like the dining room, the views take in the Caldura rocks and the La Rocca outcrop, albeit from a slightly different perspective. Chef Dario Pandolfo uses creative techniques acquired during his time working at renowned restaurants, which he applies to Sicilian ingredients and traditions. The result is exciting and colourful cuisine which is creative and full of Mediterranean flavours.

Name: Antiche Carampane
Address: rio Terà delle Carampane, sestiere San Polo 1911, Venice, 30125, Italy
Description: From the typical flooring to the decoration on the walls, the warm and appealing decor in this restaurant highlights its historic feel, providing a setting to which guests happily return time after time. The local fish and seafood specialities served here include sarde in saor (sardines), salted cod, fried soft-shell crab and cuttlefish in black ink – skilfully prepared dishes which remain faithful to traditional recipes.

Name: Phi Restaurant - Giancarlo Morelli
Address: località Forte Cappellini, Baia Sardinia, 07021, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Great view,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: Glamour and fashion are the hallmarks of this restaurant in Phi Beach, one of the most attractive nightclub-cum-lounge bars on the Costa Smeralda. Take a seat on the terrace right by the water and soak up the romantic sunsets and sea views as you enjoy Italian and Mediterranean dishes created by a famous chef from Lombardy who adds just the right touch of contemporary flavour. Also open for lunch, with some of the evening menu dishes available alongside an array of simpler options.

Name: Lanzani Bottega & Bistrot
Address: via Albertano da Brescia 41, Brescia, 25127, Italy
Description: This modern restaurant (open from 7am to 11pm), once the family butcher’s, also acts as a delicatessen and wine boutique. Full restaurant service in the evening with simpler dishes and a more restricted choice at lunchtime. Situated some distance from the centre.

Name: Clandestino Susci Bar
Description: Built on stilts, the Clandestino is a unique restaurant with a simple yet trendy ambience, which overlooks a beautiful unspoilt beach with views of the sea from all the windows and a distinctly romantic feel at night. Here, Moreno Cedroni focuses on gourmet cuisine at lunchtime as well as in the evening. In addition to two tasting menus (Eros & Susci and Susci Memories), for lunch there’s a small à la carte.

Name: La Conchiglia
Description: This small restaurant with a vaulted ceiling provides the setting for dishes that have by now become classics thanks to their focus on top-quality ingredients. The cuisine is light and simple rather than bold and elaborate, with a focus on bringing out the full flavour of the fish (a few meat dishes are also available). If you’re keen to learn more about Ligurian gastronomic specialities, take time between courses to chat with the friendly owner, who has an impressive knowledge of the region.

Name: Le Petit Bellevue
Cuisine: Italian Contemporary, Cuisine from the Aosta Valley
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Situated in one of the region’s most famous and romantic hotels, this small gem of a restaurant offers just a few seats at period-style tables in a small dining room, in addition to two tables with scenic views of the valley and Gran Paradiso. Here, the Tuscan chef focuses on specialities from the Aosta Valley, including popular dishes such as Lillaz char with roe and a butter sauce, and “zuppa del bosco” (stewed seasonal mushrooms served with Aosta blue cheese and a pinch of fresh marjoram), followed by an extraordinary cheese trolley that focuses on regional specialities. Last but not least, talented sommelier Rino Billia (a previous winner of the “passion for wine” award) demonstrates skilful understanding of guests’ requirements as he chooses the most suitable wine for them out of the more than 1 600 labels on the wine list.

Name: L'Argaj
Description: In the Piedmontese dialect, “Argaj” translates as “satisfaction” and never has a restaurant name seemed more appropriate!
