In a simple, colourful and welcoming dining room with windows looking out at the hills, all the attention is on cuisine which is skilfully balanced between classic local dishes and more creative options. Choose between the à la carte and tasting menus, all accompanied by an excellent array of wines.

Name: Oste Scuro - Finsterwirt
Description: Run by the capable Mayr family, this long-established restaurant has occupied a narrow alleyway in the centre of Bressanone (Brixen) since the late 19C. The dining rooms are decorated in historic style, plus there’s a charming terrace for alfresco dining in summer. Dishes are presented on different tasting menus with the option of choosing traditional or Mediterranean dishes à la carte style – we highly recommend the soup made with Sylvaner wine from the Isarco valley, as well as the Tirtl (fried pie) stuffed with ricotta, spinach and cinnamon. Guestrooms are available in the nearby and recently renovated Adler Historic Guesthouse, which is run by the same owners.

Name: Gardenia
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Even if you’re not a local, you’ll feel at home in this old property which offers a glimpse of the Piedmont of old. In this 19C building, with a typical balcony running along the inner courtyard, the atmosphere continues into the dining room and, of course, via the dishes on the menu. Here, regional cuisine is celebrated to the full, so you’ll find lots of meat (although some fish options are also available), accompanied by a carefully selected choice of vegetables, some grown in the restaurant’s own garden.

Name: Il Portico
Description: Chef Lopriore returns to his native region with this new restaurant which offers an original format – the lunchtime menu focuses on single course options, while in the evening the tasting menus comprise an interesting combination of imaginative fish, meat and vegetable dishes which can be combined as you wish. Cuisine with an emphasis on seasonal market ingredients where locally sourced produce takes pride of place.

Name: 85 Bistrot
Address: piazza Martiri di Via Fani 85, Sesto San Giovanni, 20099, Italy
Description: This simple, modern, family-run trattoria with a welcoming ambience is the kind of restaurant that everyone would love to have as their local. The owner-chef, who has plenty of experience working in Milanese restaurants, is a real culinary expert who creates traditional dishes from Milan but also from further afield. Here, the popular breaded cutlet is served thick so that the delicate flavour of the veal can be enjoyed to the full.

Name: Strattoria
Description: Situated in the foothills around Lake Maggiore, this colourful and welcoming restaurant has a pleasantly relaxed ambience. The skilful chef creates cuisine inspired by the region (as well as further afield) that showcases top-quality ingredients, including dishes such as veal tongue with barbecued prawns and carrots. An interesting wine list and friendly service complete the picture.

Name: Belé
Description: The name says it all – in Milanese dialect, “belé” means beautiful and the word is an apt description of this restaurant. Belé is charmingly lit by an old-fashioned chandelier on which the pieces of crystal create a play of light resembling an intricate and shifting lace-like pattern. The dining rooms are decorated in attractive contemporary colours, with comfortable armchairs and acoustics perfect for conversation, while the cuisine is Italian with a modern twist.

Name: Pietramare Natural Food
Address: SS 106, loc. Praialonga,, Isola di Capo Rizzuto, 88841, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Counter dining,Garden or park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: In an elegant setting of dry-stone walls and Mediterranean vegetation, this stylish restaurant boasts personalised decor right down to the smallest detail. The new chef prepares modern dishes inspired by the region and more generally by southern Italy, with a menu that focuses on fish rather than meat, as well as a vegetarian menu. There’s also a charming cigar room with small lounge areas and a fireplace.

Name: Salamensa
Address: via Monsignor Oscar Romero 29, Montichiari, 25018, Italy
Description: A multi-function open space, with a bar for breakfasts and a classic restaurant serving pizzas made from naturally fermented dough. Although the ambience is modern, friendly and minimalist, the attention paid to the choice of ingredients and preparation of dishes is of the highest quality.

Name: Café Quinson
Cuisine: Cuisine from the Aosta Valley, Regional Cuisine
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus
Description: The Café Quinson has reopened! In this rustic yet elegant “mountain restaurant”, the whole family makes guests feel welcome, serving a selection of regional dishes with an imaginative and contemporary touch. Excellent choice of wines, almost all of which are available by the glass.

Name: La Botte
Description: A modern and welcoming contemporary bistro situated in the heart of Stresa’s historic centre. Run by an entire family, the restaurant serves modern and imaginative fish and meat dishes where the focus is always on seasonal ingredients. The interesting wine list also includes a selection of wines by the glass.

Name: Gennaro Di Pace
Address: vicolo della Chiesa 8, loc. Perno, Monforte d'Alba, 12065, Italy
Description: The owner-chef’s Calabrian origins are evident on a menu that combines Mediterranean cuisine (including fish and seafood) with Piedmontese specialities and showcases beautifully presented dishes prepared using contemporary techniques. This small modern restaurant situated near Perno castle is also open at lunchtime (by prior reservation only).

Name: Essentia
Address: piazza San Nicolò 2, Castrocaro Terme, 47011, Italy
Description: Situated at the foot of the fortress in the historic centre of Castrocaro, this restaurant has an interesting young chef at the helm, Andrea Giacchini. The cuisine often (but not always) has a local influence and demonstrates remarkable technical expertise that is neither overly ostentatious nor an end in itself, but rather a way of skilfully showcasing the top-quality ingredients used.

Name: San Martino 26
Address: via San Martino 26, San Gimignano, 53037, Italy
Description: Occupying the wine cellars of an old palazzo in the historic centre, this restaurant has a fashionable feel with just a few tables and a selection of contemporary - style dishes inspired by classic recipes (from Tuscany and elsewhere) on the menu.

Name: Da Cecco
Address: piazza Belvedere Puccini 10/12, Torre del Lago Puccini, 55049, Italy
Description: A cosylittle restaurant at the beginning of the lakefront. Mainly seafood dishes, though in the winter there is also game. Rustic atmosphere.

Name: Trippini
Address: via Italia 14, Civitella del Lago, 05023, Italy
Description: Just a few tables and spectacular views of Lake Corbara characterise this restaurant, which has been run by the same family since 1964. The delicious cuisine is regional in flavour, showcasing home-cooked recipes and typical Sunday favourites yet with a contemporary twist that incorporates plenty of intense flavours.

Name: Osteria Taviani
Address: piazza Vittorio Emanuele II 28, Bientina, 56031, Italy
Description: This pleasant, warmly decorated restaurant is run with passion and enthusiasm by Elena and Alessandro, the former supervising the front of house, the latter at the helm in the kitchen. The cuisine here is modern and full of flavour, with a focus on meat dishes (although a few fish options also feature) with their roots firmly anchored in Tuscan traditions (such as the fried steak). During the hunting season, the contemporary-style game dishes are particularly delicious. The wine list includes a few French labels.

Name: Il Labirinto
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Situated on the outskirts of Brescia, this long-established restaurant has an elegant retro atmosphere. The cuisine is varied with a balance of fish and meat dishes, as well as some excellent home-made salumi.

Name: Lou Ressignon
Cuisine: Cuisine from the Aosta Valley, Classic Cuisine
Description: A pleasant family trattoria which has been in business since 1966, this restaurant serves simple and authentic cuisine which showcases the products of the Aosta Valley, as well as excellent meat, most of which comes from outside Italy. In addition to the first-floor dining room, there’s also a historic taverna, while four welcoming guestrooms are available for anyone wishing to extend their stay.

Name: Daniela
Address: piazza Matteotti 7, San Casciano dei Bagni, 53040, Italy
Description: Just a little under 100m from the Sette Querce hotel and situated opposite a lovely viewpoint, this restaurant is housed in the castle’s old stables. The vaulted ceilings and old stone create a charming ambience, while the excellent local cuisine will definitely appeal to the palate.

Name: L'Osteria del Castellazzo
Address: via Borgo Castellazzo 40, Salsomaggiore Terme, 43039, Italy
Description: The determined and enthusiastic young owner of this restaurant graduated with a literature degree before giving in to her passion for food. She swapped her pen for a ladle and now creates delicious local specialities such as braised veal cheeks, alongside dishes from Pïacenza and Mantua, such as pisarei (a type of gnocchi) and sbrisolona cake.

Name: Pescarino-Sapori di Terra e di Mare
Description: This warm, welcoming restaurant with a wooden ceiling and walls serves simple dishes as well as more creative, elaborate fare. The focus here is on showcasing the top-quality ingredients used (especially fish and seafood) in dishes which are influenced by Liguria, as well as elsewhere in Italy. Given the secluded location, the guestrooms on offer here are a good option.

Name: Badessa
Description: This restaurant has a surprising location in a 19C cheese factory which once produced parmesan cheese. Although the purpose of the building has changed, the love of the region remains the same: the chef goes out of his way to source local ingredients and serve traditional Emilian dishes, often with a modern twist. One of the best restaurants in rural Reggio Emilia.

Name: La Porta Restaurant
Address: piazza Vieira de Mello 4, Bologna, 40128, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Housed in a futuristic building, La Porta Restaurant is a multi - purpose establishment which offers a bar for aperitifs and a highly modern cigar room, as well as a well - stocked wine cellar offering the best wines from Italy and elsewhere. The cuisine is creative with a particular focus on fish recipes, while lighter options are available in the Café from 7. 30am to 7pm.

Name: La Veranda del Color
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: This aptly named restaurant in the Color Hotel just a short distance from Lake Garda boasts a modern, colourful decor and cuisine worthy of its name. Dishes are inspired by Mediterranean traditions and are showcased on a number of different tasting menus.

Name: Loewengrube
Description: This building has been home to a restaurant since the 16C, making it one of the oldest in Bolzano. Today, it houses an elegant restaurant that serves a combination of traditional Alpine cuisine and classic Italian dishes with a contemporary twist, such as carbonara tortelloni filled with parmesan cream and crispy bacon. The attractive wine cellar boasts a selection of approximately 1 000 wines from the region and elsewhere in Italy, as well as a choice of labels from further afield.

Name: Retrobottega
Description: Minimalist decor and clean lines characterise this restaurant decorated in dark tones, where the two owner-chefs have both worked in various Michelin-starred restaurants (and others) over the years. Modern cuisine which showcases seasonal ingredients in regional yet refined dishes.

Name: Già Sotto l'Arco
Description: A historic gourmet restaurant, with an equally historic setting on the first floor of a Baroque palazzo fronting an elegant piazza. A fine staircase leads up to the simple yet stylish dining room, which is skilfully run by a father and his offspring. In the kitchen, his wife Teresa prepares creative, regional cuisine, which is showcased on a surprise menu of four, six or eight courses and which features locally sourced meat and fish. If you’d like to book the delightful table on the small terrace for just two fortunate guests, make sure you do so well in advance!

Name: Saffron
Description: If you like fish and you find yourself in Arezzo, then this is the place for you. Saffron serves a range of traditional and imaginative raw fish dishes inspired by different traditions, from the Mediterranean to Japan, alongside a few cooked fish options and the occasional Japanese speciality such as tempura and Japanese spaghetti and ravioli.

Name: La Terrazza
Description: The aptly named Terrazza is a delightful open - air restaurant overlooking Asolo’s historic centre. In an elegant, fashionable ambience enjoy innovative delicacies that nonetheless make full use of the best local traditions and produce. Ideal for a romantic dinner.

Name: La Locanda del Cardinale
Description: A medieval house with stone arches, built over the remains of mosaics from a Roman villa – the location alone makes this restaurant truly memorable. Add to this modern, beautifully prepared cuisine with a focus on regional ingredients, and all that’s left to do is book your table!

Name: Il Focarile
Address: via Pontina al km 46,5, Aprilia, 04011, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Terrace
Description: The sumptuous entrance gives an elegant tone to a large bright dining room with well spaced out tables; a touch of Tuscany with a cuisine rich in tradition and also imagination. Now offers new, elegant rooms.

Name: La Fermata
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Situated in the countryside around Alessandria, this 18C farmhouse has a modern, minimalist decor which serves as a backdrop for traditional Piedmontese cuisine with a clever modern twist. The chef offers just the right amount of creativity, with a focus on meat dishes and satisfying, memorable flavours that appeal to the emotions as well as the palate. Adding to the appeal, the elegant and exclusive ambience is the result of careful refurbishment, which has transformed the dining room into a triumph of art and design.

Name: John Restaurant-Casamadre
Address: via Santa Maria la Nova 35, Afragola, 80021, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Wheelchair access
Description: Follow the signs to Casamadre (the specialist food shop next door) to get to this gourmet restaurant, where the chef surprises guests with modern cuisine that is full of character. The dishes served here are inspired by classic recipes which are reinterpreted with creativity and a respect for local traditions, resulting in highly distinctive flavours. Each course reflects the region’s history, with a common thread running through the menu to create an authentic culinary experience. To accompany your meal, the wines are presented on a practical tablet which makes it easy to explore the different labels available. Among the different options, the excellent Costa D'Amalfi “Selva delle Monache” 2022 is particularly striking thanks to its fresh, earthy aromas.

Name: Cascina Lautier
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Situated outside the town on top of a small hill, this elegant restaurant serves modern country cuisine, with some personal interpretations.

Name: Januarius
Description: Named after San Gennaro (St Januarius) whose relics are said to lie in the cathedral nearby, this restaurant celebrates traditional, authentic specialities from Campania, such as octopus alla Luciana, zito pasta in a traditional ragu and salted cod with Napolitan-style endives. The entrance opens into a boutique selling top-quality ingredients (mainly charcuterie and cheeses), with two original dining rooms on either side.

Name: Taverna del Castello
Description: Occupying a 15C castle in a medieval village, this restaurant offers fine views of the majestic hills all around. The chef here uses top - quality regional ingredients with a focus on seasonal produce to create tasting menus full of imagination and artistic flair. Excellent meat and fish dishes inspired by Italian traditions.

Name: Marina Grande
Description: Establishment on the beach: wooden floors and white chairs in the linear room, where you can sample the traditional country cuisine; pleasant terrace for service in summer.

Name: Antica Osteria da Penacio
Description: A family - run restaurant in a villa on the edge of a wood: inside two refined dining rooms and a small, but well stocked, wine bar; traditional cuisine.

Name: Antinè
Description: Manuel Bouchard’s cuisine impressed our inspectors thanks to striking features such as his minimalist approach and the use of just a few well-chosen ingredients. Traditional recipes, such as plin pasta and Fassona beef, feature on the menu alongside more alternative, imaginative dishes (including fresh- and saltwater fish). This elegant restaurant is located on the first floor of a building in the old town, just a stone’s throw from the medieval tower. A warm welcome and an excellent wine list complete the picture.

Name: Il Carpaccio
Description: This traditional family restaurant has been recently renovated to include an attractive veranda - style dining room overlooking the valley. Typical dishes from Calabria, fish specialities by prior arrangement, and a good wine list all add to the appeal.

Name: Feel Como
Description: Wild regional produce, game and freshwater fish take pride of place on the menu at this elegant restaurant which celebrates nature in all its glory, despite its town-centre location. The dishes prepared by chef Federico Beretta have a contemporary feel, while the tasting menu is dedicated to wild ingredients foraged from the woods.

Name: Walter Redaelli
Description: In this old 18C farmhouse with exposed brickwork, roof beams and an impressive fireplace, enjoy delicious Tuscan cuisine prepared from local ingredients, with a particular focus on meat. Specialities on the menu include pappa al pomodoro, home-made pici pasta, and sliced veal. Comfortable chairs add to the cosy and enjoyable dining experience.

Name: Il Pavone
Description: Situated in the heart of Alghero and with a beautiful veranda overlooking the sea, this restaurant serves delicious fish and seafood made from top-quality ingredients. Highlights include the “Alessandrina” fried fish and the octopus salad. If available, make sure you try the goats’ cheese made by the owner himself, although be warned – the flavour is quite strong!

Name: Osteria le Logge
Description: Having retained its old shop counter and glass - fronted display cabinets, this former grocer’s shop is perfect for anyone in search of old - world charm. However, the cuisine is the real draw with its focus on quality of the highest level. Wine buffs can ask to visit the wine cellar nearby, housed in a tunnel of Etruscan origin. Simpler dining room on the first floor.

Name: RistoFante
Description: The motto of this restaurant is “In step with the times yet inspired by tradition”. The cuisine here is made from fresh, seasonal ingredients (with a particular focus on fish) prepared using modern techniques. Elegant dining room, plus a shaded outdoor space for the summer months.

Name: Sarti del Gusto
Address: via Vico II Vincenzo Sulis 1/a, Cagliari, 09124, Italy
Description: A small, beautifully maintained restaurant offering a concise selection of carefully prepared and attractively presented dishes. The cuisine here is often creative yet inspired by Sardinian traditions, with an equal focus on meat and fish.

Name: Stube Ladina
Description: The hotel owner is also the chef, serving carefully prepared and well - presented dishes made from regional produce in a quiet Stube - style dining room. An interesting wine list provides the icing on the cake.

Name: Osteria de l'Umbreleèr
Description: Situated in Cicognolo in the Lower Po valley, where early morning mists create an evocative atmosphere in autumn, this traditional restaurant with a rustic feel serves specialities from Lombardy with a focus on delicious starters and top-quality meat. Our inspector particularly recommends the white onion gratin soup and the Burgundy-style snails. A simpler menu is available at lunchtime and there’s a small garden for alfresco dining on summer evenings.

Name: Da Peppe
Description: Situated in the historic centre of a small village in the Parco del Pollino, this long-established restaurant serves traditional and copious local dishes that are always expertly prepared. Guestrooms are also available in the family B&B of the same name.

Name: Ventuno.1
Description: Closed for renovations until April 2024.Two natives of Campania who have settled in the Langhe run this centrally located restaurant, where the black and white decor has a modern feel. The menu focuses on fish and seafood, in addition to meat dishes and truffles in season.

Name: Osteria Ardenga
Description: An authentic trattoria which is a joy to visit, where time seems to have stood still for decades. Situated on the border between two provinces, the restaurant focuses on specialities from Parma, many of which are made from home - grown produce. Homemade pickles and chutneys are also sold here.

Name: Roof Garden
Description: Make sure you ask for one of the tables next to the glass wall in this restaurant, which boasts romantic views of Bergamo’s Città Alta. The innovative, inventive cuisine is tempting and full of flavour.

Name: Villa Baroni
Description: This romantic restaurant on the lakeshore has a welcoming, elegant ambience and a delightful terrace for summer dining. The cuisine pays particular attention to top-quality, seasonal ingredients prepared in traditional recipes with a focus on fish. Cosy, Provençal-style guestrooms complete the picture.

Name: Il Giardino delle Esperidi
Description: The ideal starting point for an exploration of the area. In summer one dines on the terrace located in the heart of the historic centre while drinks and cigars may be enjoyed in the lounge bar.

Name: Molteni
Description: Hospitality abounds in this establishment where the cuisine is inspired by local traditions, especially fish, in a favourably located restaurant in the historical centre on the banks of the Bianco canal.

Name: Doc
Address: via Vittorio Veneto 1, Borgio Verezzi, 17022, Italy
Description: Quiet, well - kept restaurant located in an aristocratic, early twentieth - century villa surrounded by a pretty garden.

Name: Osteria dell'Oca Bianca
Description: In the heart of a small town, right opposite the church, this typical village osteria run by a friendly family serves traditional cuisine from the Piedmont, including goose dishes. Highlights here include the rustic, welcoming ambience, an excellent wine list, a wine cellar that can be visited, and a charming glass-fronted veranda that is used throughout the year. There are also three beautiful guestrooms reserved exclusively for guests dining at the restaurant.

Name: Essencia Restaurant
Address: piazza Santa Maria la Nova 9, Naples, 80134, Italy
Description: Having spent many years living in Spain, the young chef at this quiet, elegant restaurant offers an appealing combination of Spanish and Italian dishes, resulting in his own interesting interpretations of Mediterranean cuisine. Situated in the heart of the historic centre, the restaurant has an open-view kitchen and chef’s table for four guests near the entrance, while the main dining room is on the first floor.

Name: Locanda del Molino
Description: This rustic yet charming restaurant occupies an old family mill. It has attractive guestrooms that reflect the elegant simplicity of the Tuscan countryside. In the kitchen, the female chef creates traditional specialities such as fried rabbit and nettle with ricotta cheese gnudi (ravioli filling without the pasta) in a fresh tomato sauce.

Name: Maré
Description: An unexpected gourmet restaurant in a typical private beach club on the Romagna coast, with a dining room that opens on to the beach with its long line of beach umbrellas. The dishes here are carefully prepared and occasionally creative, and all of good quality. We particularly recommend the monfettini (fresh egg pasta) mantecati with cuttlefish, clams, mantis shrimp and ink, which looks like a risotto and is absolutely delicious. The restaurant also boasts a good wine list with an excellent choice of champagnes.

Name: Indiniò
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Wheelchair access
Description: This restaurant (the name Indiniò means “nowhere” in old Carnian dialect) is run by an enthusiastic female owner-chef who left her former job to realise her dream: namely, to create personalised cuisine of the highest quality with ingredients from her local region and elsewhere, while her partner takes charge of the dining room. Indiniò is both welcoming and elegant, with just a few tables, an intimate ambience and a small space for more private dining.

Name: La Canonica
Description: A small, minimalist restaurant in the town centre, where both the ambience and the cuisine are contemporary in style with a hint of Sardinian influence (the chef is originally from the island). Some of the dishes features fermented ingredients prepared on site.

Name: Quattro Sensi
Description: After working in top-level restaurants both in Italy and abroad, the young chef at this restaurant in the Borgobrufa hotel offers a host of interesting dishes featuring excellent Umbrian ingredients, often sourced from local growers and farmers. Meat dishes dominate the menu, alongside a good selection of vegetables.

Name: Calvi Ristorante
Description: This welcoming, contemporary-style restaurant with a large open-view kitchen serves two different types of cuisine – one regional and Mediterranean in style, the other more creative allowing the chef’s culinary skills to take centre stage. The black rice tacos with roasted eel, green beans, soya bean sprouts and spicy hummus mayo are truly delicious – definitely to be eaten with the hands!

Name: Hostaria dai Musi
Description: Offering a limited à la carte that includes fish dishes (including raw options) which vary according to market availability, this restaurant serves what it describes as “typically modern cuisine”. The breaded and fried anchovies with a typical saor sauce and lemon gel are particularly good, plus the menu features a selection of typical regional specialities. The pleasant setting is enhanced by the backdrop of the large central square in a pedestrianised area on the edge of the old town. The drinks menu includes an excellent selection of wines, plus a good choice of local beers.

Name: Opificio
Description: A modern restaurant in the province of Padova which, over the past ten years, has grown and evolved from a gastro pub to the top-quality eatery that it is today. The cuisine is fairly eclectic, featuring meat and fish dishes alike, with the option of a lighter menu at lunchtime. The best dishes are showcased on the à la carte and are often made using luxury ingredients such as foie gras, scampi and Wagyu beef. The impressive wine list demonstrates a passion for international sparkling wines, while the excellent selection of wines by the glass is further enhanced by a choice of cocktails (also available at midday).

Name: Osteria del Posto
Address: via Calderini 15, loc. Chiugiana, Corciano, 06073, Italy
Description: It's well worth the climb up to this restaurant, where you can be sure of a friendly welcome and professional service. With advice on hand from courteous female staff, choose from a selection of imaginative, locally influenced dishes that are full of flavour. We particularly recommend the pigeon (piccione di tutto un po’), accompanied by a glass of the potent Gamay del Trasimeno Opra red wine with an alcohol content of 14.5°!

Name: Enoclub
Description: Under the arcades of a piazza named after Michele Ferrero, this restaurant has a simple, modern ambience with walls covered with wine bottles, as well as friendly, efficient female staff. The beautifully prepared Piedmontese cuisine is showcased on an à la carte and a tasting menu, accompanied by an impressive selection of quality wine.

Name: Locanda del Marinaio
Description: Delicious cuisine full of the flavours of the Mediterranean (prepared by the German owner - chef! ) in a delightful little restaurant in the bustling centre of Cefalù. Simple surroundings but excellent food!

Name: La Veranda
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Terrace
Description: As its name suggests, the dining room at this restaurant is a splendid and elegant veranda, which transfers out onto the terrace overlooking the lake in fine weather. A perfect setting for the modern, international and Italian influenced cuisine served here.

Name: Trattoria del Bivio
Description: Situated in the Alta Langa region, this old restored farmhouse is now home to an elegant restaurant with a contemporary rural feel. The cuisine has strong regional roots, although the menu also offers a few fishes dishes. Excellent food, as well as attractive guestrooms and a warm, family welcome.

Name: La Casa degli Spiriti
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Wheelchair access
Description: The Chignola family has been welcoming guests in this beautiful, restored farmhouse – a luxurious residence with one of the best views of Lake Garda – for almost 30 years. The ground-floor restaurant occupies a veranda surrounded by greenery facing the lake, where young chef Filippo (following in his father’s footsteps), together with his brother, sommelier Lorenzo, offers his guests an enjoyable dining experience with its roots in the cuisine of the region. The first-floor terrace is home to the Osteria Spiritino, which is more informal in both its cuisine and atmosphere. The remarkable wine cellar is housed in a room adorned with 18C frescoes and boasts more than 1 300 labels, with a particular focus on champagnes.

Name: I Salotti
Address: Località Querce al Pino, SS 146, Chiusi, 53043, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: In summer, the outdoor spaces at this restaurant, such as the garden gazebo, are the perfect setting for a candlelit dinner in total harmony with nature, while in winter, the elegant dining room with just a few tables (book well in advance) really comes into its own. Creative cuisine prepared using produce from the restaurant’s own farm, plus a long-established wine cellar that has been extended over the years so that it now boasts over two thousand different labels from the region and elsewhere in Italy, many of them of the highest quality.

Name: Il Doretto
Description: Restaurant within a refined farmstead. The ancient structure has maintained the rustic style in spite of several hints of elegance in the furnishings. On the menu: interesting offer of meat and seafood (with a slightly more limited wine cellar at lunch). Pleasant exterior for summer service.

Name: Kürbishof
Description: This romantic inn with guestrooms occupies an old farm with a hay barn. In two typical Stube-style rooms, one of which offers views of the Cembra valley, enjoy cuisine prepared by a mother-and-son team. They work side by side, preparing dishes from mainly regional ingredients (the menu often includes the names of producers) each in their own individual way, which is highlighted on the menu: to the left, you’ll find the traditional dishes made by the mother, Sara, while on the right you can choose from a selection of modern, creative options prepared by young chef Mathias. Our inspectors were delighted with their combination of choices from both lists!

Name: Faraglioni Restaurant
Address: lungomare dei Ciclopi 115, loc. Aci Trezza, Aci Castello, 95021, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Situated next to the hotel of the same name (a reference to the Faraglioni islands just off the coast here) but with its own entrance, this restaurant overlooks the beautiful Riviera dei Ciclopi. Sicilian ingredients take pride of place here in traditional and creative dishes with a focus on fish and seafood (vegetarian options are also available).

Name: All'Osteria Bottega
Description: Enjoy top-quality Emilian cuisine at this restaurant, which focuses on the region’s most traditional, best-known and authentic recipes. Featuring a superb selection of hams and salamis, fresh pastas, meat and desserts, the menu offers a real feast for the tastebuds that will linger long in the memory.

Name: Tano Passami l'Olio
Description: Tano Simonato, chef-patron of this stylish modern restaurant located in a fine residential district, offers his creative cuisine that reinterprets Italian flavors in a modern key: food for him is not just nourishment, but also fun. He will then come to your table to advise you and tell you about his dishes, suggesting the best wine pairing, also thanks to a well-stocked cellar. The inspector recommends: Tiramisù of cuttlefish and potatoes, as well as Almond Cannoli stuffed with mousse of ricotta with almonds, candied lemon and chocolate drops, with citrus fruit cream and almond jam.

Name: Ensama Pesce
Address: via Aristide Dondarini 4, Sala Bolognese, 40010, Italy
Description: A menu which focuses only on fish (from the daily market) which is prepared with a hint of Puglia, the chef’s native region. As soon as guests are seated at their table, they are brought a selection of homemade breads, including taralli bread rings and focaccia. Owner-chef Sabino is the heart and soul of this restaurant, where guests can be sure of a memorable culinary experience!

Name: Restaurant 700
Address: largo Michele Ayroldi Carissimo 14, Ostuni, 72017, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Garden or park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: Situated at the entrance to Ostuni’s historic centre, this restaurant is part of the luxury Paragon 700 hotel. The charming dining room combines historic features with a more modern decor, while the exclusive garden is perfect for dining alfresco in fine weather. The menu offers a concise selection of classic Italian dishes at lunchtime, while in the evening the chef conjures up more high-level and elaborate dishes showcasing strong technique.

Name: Osteria alla Chiesa
Description: A young couple has brought life back to this old country inn, retaining its rustic ambience while introducing a menu which focuses on creativity and innovation. Claudio creates a host of meat, fish and vegetable dishes with imagination and originality, while one of the highlights remains the menu dedicated to donkey meat.

Name: uovodiseppia Milano
Description: This completely renovated restaurant is situated in a pedestrianised area near Piazza Gae Aulenti, a new elegant restaurant district in Milan. Here, a wood-fired stove, attractive bar counter and small bistro-style tables provide the setting for carefully prepared Sicilian cuisine. Octopus, grouper and Mazara red prawns are just some of the top-quality Sicilian ingredients on the menu here, which includes reinterpreted recipes such as the “fuori Norma”, where the pasta is wrapped around the stuffed aubergine to create a dish full of Mediterranean flavours and aromas. The outdoor dining space in the pedestrianised street is perfect for early summer evenings, with its almost bohemian feel.

Name: FØRMA contemporary restaurant
Description: Situated in a secluded residential district that is part of L’Aquila’s historic centre, this intimate restaurant with an elegantly minimalist ambience is home to skilful owner-chef Simone Ciuffetelli. Having gained experience working abroad, Ciuffetelli showcases local ingredients in his creative, contemporary dishes, with the occasional use of fermented products and a frequent focus on just three ingredients. A good example is his dessert featuring cream and crunchy toasted hazelnuts generously coated with a white-chocolate mousse that is “disguised” as an Italian-style meringue thanks to a sprinkling of liquorice powder.

Name: Campo Cedro
Description: Situated just a stone’s throw from the centre yet away from the tourist crowds, this restaurant is well worth the effort needed to find it! Here, Japanese chef Sugihara, who has more than 20 years’ experience working in Italy, creates modern and skilfully prepared Italian meat and fish dishes which are fresh and elaborate. You’ll nearly always find seafood risotto on the menu, which is made with fish, mussels and finely chopped shrimps all cooked together with rice and then sprinkled with crumbled seaweed and dotted with tomato paste. Excellent value for money!

Name: Enoteca Meucci
Description: Comprising a wine boutique and a wine bar in its rustic-style room on the ground floor, Enoteca Meucci is also home to a restaurant in the more elegant, classic-style rooms on the first floor. The expertly prepared cuisine is colourful and contemporary in style, with a focus on regional ingredients. Beautiful outdoor area for summer dining.

Name: Granoturco Bistrot
Description: Although the external façade of this restaurant recalls its former life as a pub, the building is now home to a restaurant run by a young chef whose experience working abroad has done nothing to dim his love of the Piedmont. Here, he serves some of the best regional cuisine in the area, with a few more creative options also featuring on the menu.

Name: Anto e Robi
Description: Situated in the heart of a small town surrounded by rice fields, this restaurant has a charming and personalised feel. The cuisine is often (but not always) based around fish, which is showcased in dishes inspired by regional traditions. While Robi oversees the front of house with skill and expertise, offering recommendations on wine (over 300 labels, including many by the glass) and rum (his particular passion), Anto prepares a host of delicious recipes in the kitchen.

Name: Casa Rapisarda
Description: This small welcoming restaurant on the famous Scalinata della Costarella in Numana, with a tiny terrace for summer dining and just a few tables, serves delicious cuisine with an imaginative twist. Originally from Sicily, the highly talented owner-chef has spent much of his life in the Marche and has plenty of experience in leading restaurants. Given the limited capacity here, booking is essential, especially in summer.

Name: Radimare
Address: via Beato Piergiorgio Frassati 5/a, Monopoli, 70043, Italy
Description: There’s no tasting menu at this restaurant but instead a tempting à la carte featuring modern Mediterranean cuisine based on top-quality seasonal ingredients, with fish and seafood taking centre stage. Citrus fruit and a few spices, especially ginger, are used carefully and sparingly, as are aromatic herbs which add a touch of fresh flavour to the dishes. The contemporary decor, enhanced by plants and a profusion of wood, plus friendly service add to the appeal.

Name: La Loggia Bistrò
Description: Slightly off the beaten track yet still in the town centre, this restaurant boasts a courtyard setting for summer dining plus an intimate interior room with just a few small square tables, subtle lighting and an attractive decor featuring old wine bottles. A far cry from the classic tourist fare often available elsewhere, the cuisine served here is imaginatively presented with a focus on the use of seasonal ingredients.

Name: Sücar Brüsc
Description: This interesting new restaurant in the historic heart of Mantova takes its name from a phrase in local dialect with translates as “sour” sugar. The cuisine here is regional yet modern, served in an informal dining room where traditional Mantuan sayings are written on the ceilings. For some months now, the restaurant has also offered an interesting caviar menu.

Name: I 5 Sensi
Description: The whole family (mother and four children) is involved in the running of this restaurant, both front of house and in the kitchen. If you’re looking for top-quality cuisine which focuses on local ingredients yet is also creative and innovative, then this is the place for you! Classic-style dining room with the occasional modern decorative touch, plus a well-stocked wine cellar offering a selection of 700 labels.

Name: Da Marino al St Remy
Address: via San Salvatore da Horta 7, Cagliari, 09124, Italy
Description: Situated on the edge of the pedestrianised area near the Bastione di Saint Remy, this restaurant is named after its charismatic owner Marino, who helps guests with their choice of menu and is happy to tell them all about the history of the restaurant (the street in front of the restaurant, for example, has not always been there). At the helm in the kitchen, his wife Silvana prepares Mediterranean dishes with a Sardinian flavour – the fish and seafood options are particularly delicious.

Name: Repubblica di Perno
Address: vicolo Cavour 5, loc. Perno, Monforte d'Alba, 12065, Italy
Description: Situated in the heart of the gastronomic Langa region, this small, renovated restaurant in the centre of town (reservations required) is imbued with the passion of the couple at the helm (he’s in the kitchen, while she’s front of house). In keeping with Piedmontese tradition, you catch a glimpse of the open-view kitchen as you make your way to the first floor, which is laid out with just five tables. Enjoy traditional cuisine in a rustic, bistro-style setting where the daily menu showcases dishes with a strictly regional focus. Three guestrooms are also available.

Name: Lofficina
Description: This building with a minimalist, contemporary design is situated on the edge of the historic centre at the Sant'Erasmo belvedere from where, in summer, panoramic views extend over Monte Conero and the sea (booking ahead is recommended). In the kitchen, owner-chef Davide Breccia conjures up creative dishes featuring original combinations and mainly inspired by the sea. Our inspector’s favourite dish was the marinated amberjack with passion fruit, black pepper and vanilla. The freshness of the fish is enhanced by the chef’s balanced and individual approach.

Name: Il Cugnolo
Address: contrada Cugnolo 19, Torre di Palme, 63900, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: This gourmet restaurant housed in a restored period residence that once belonged to the counts of Adami is surrounded by the green maquis and hills of the Marche, with the sea visible in the distance just a few miles away. Here, the young Neapolitan chef creates cuisine that is surprising for its attractive, clean lines, providing a real explosion of flavours and a tribute to the region and the Mediterranean in general. The restaurant also owns a nearby agricultural estate which provides many of the wines and olive oils served during tastings.

Name: La RiMa
Description: This restaurant in the heart of the city provides an elegant setting in which to enjoy excellent contemporary Mediterranean cuisine, all with a personalised twist added by the talented chef. Female staff provide the service and the friendly welcome.

Name: Frades La Terrazza
Address: SP94 - Località Abbiadori, Porto Cervo, 07021, Italy
Description: Situated in a panoramic location on Cala di Volpe bay, this trendy restaurant serves excellent cuisine with a focus on Sardinian specialities and other Mediterranean dishes. There’s a beautiful terrace for an aperitif, plus tapas options to share and a good selection of sparkling wines. Young and enthusiastic staff.

Name: Pescheria
Description: The name of this restaurant between the historic centre and the seafront refers to the main item on its menu, which is dedicated almost exclusively to fish (fresh and not farmed). Fish and shellfish are displayed in a glass cabinet and aquarium respectively, both of which are situated to the rear of the long, narrow dining room near the open-view kitchen. Classic fish dishes full of flavour (served raw, baked, cooked in salt, in water or grilled) are to the fore here.

Name: Riva
Description: Riva is the Hotel Vista’s fine-dining restaurant, situated just behind Numana’s beach with fine panoramic views. The restaurant serves top-quality ingredients from the Adriatic and surrounding countryside in creative dishes full of flavour which are showcased on tasting menus and an à la carte.

Name: Dogma
Description: This restaurant may be small (booking is recommended) but it has a big personality. The focus here is on fish and seafood, with nearly all the dishes cooked (at least partially) over the barbecue grill, including desserts! The talented, original young chef creates dishes full of intense and convincing flavours.

Name: Osteria il Moro
Description: Boasting an attractive outdoor space on Trapani’s main street, Osteria il Moro focuses on dishes that are deeply rooted in Sicilian tradition yet enhanced by original and creative touches, resulting in cuisine that is full of flavour and personality thanks to owner-chef Nicola Bandi. The menu features plenty of fish dishes as well as meat, including beef fillet in a red sauce with spices and wild herbs, and Trapani-style mullet. The impressive wine list includes a good selection of regional labels.

Name: La Casina
Description: This large farmhouse with attractively renovated rooms overlooks the verdant landscapes of the Sarca valley from its wisteria-shaded summer pergola. Young chef Giada Miori prepares regional ingredients with skill and precision, serving specialities such as traditional potato fritters and “carne salada” (salted meat) preserved by the restaurant itself, as well as char, meat from the Trentino region and mushrooms. The Miori family also grow their own red berries, which often make an appearance in their desserts, along with their own sweet chestnuts.

Name: InAlto Alfio Ghezzi Dolomites
Address: via San Pellegrino 32, stazione a monte della funivia Col Margherita, Moena, 38035, Italy
Description: Situated on Col Margherita at an altitude of 2 550m and accessible in winter via a cable car (from the San Pellegrino pass in Moena), this new ski bar bears the name of Alfio Ghezzi, the Michelin-starred chef at the Mart museum in Rovereto. Options include burgers and a children’s menu as well as a more elaborate and creative selection of some of the chef’s best-loved dishes. In summer the bar can also be reached on foot or by bike (for the truly athletic!) with recharging stations available for e-bikes.

Name: Hostaria da Franz
Address: salizada Sant'Antonin, sestiere Castello 3499, Venice, 30122, Italy
Description: Founded in a different venue by an Austrian soldier in the late 19C, this historic Venetian restaurant is now run by owner Maurizio, who oversees the front of house in a courteous yet friendly manner. He introduces guests to its variety of dishes, which aim to please rather than surprise. Fish specialities are to the fore here.

Name: Locanda Solagna
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Terrace
Description: Although this restaurant has been in business since the 1950s, it feels much more modern thanks to its updated appearance. Renowned for its excellent regional cuisine served in the evening, the restaurant pays careful attention to seasonal ingredients. At lunchtime, the ”osteria”-style menu is much simpler. Excellent wine selection.

Name: Locanda Altobelli
Description: A pleasant little restaurant that differs from the many fish options in town with its traditional regional meat-based cuisine. There’s a real alchemy here between the young owner who is passionate about wine and the talented chef who boasts an impressive CV. Carefully chosen ingredients sourced directly from small local producers are the basis for its exciting, delicious dishes, while the wine list features some interesting organic wines. Small outdoor space for alfresco dining.

Name: Savô
Description: The reopening in 2022 of the Hotel Windsor with its romantic vintage decor, is a real bonus for Laigueglia, especially the hotel’s new gourmet restaurant Savô (which translates as “flavour” in Ligurian dialect). Here, a contemporary dining room and an outdoor space with views of the beach and the sea provide the setting for modern cuisine prepared from regional, seasonal ingredients with a focus on fish (there is also a meat option for each course). The impressive selection of wine and choice of cocktails from the elegant Windsor Bar adds to its appeal.

Name: Il Grottino
Address: piazza Beato Ugolino 5, Gualdo Cattaneo, 06035, Italy
Description: Situated in the old medieval village of Gualdo Cattaneo, amid the gentle valleys not far from Foligno, Il Grottino is the perfect choice for anyone keen to sample the authentic flavours of Umbrian cuisine. Here, truffles and zero-km produce take pride of place on the menu, with a particular focus on meat which is carefully cooked on the open-view barbecue grill. Alongside locally sourced produce, you’ll also find a choice of carefully selected Prussian beef. Comfortable and welcoming guestrooms complete the picture.

Name: Osteria da Fiore
Address: calle del Scaleter, sestiere San Polo  2202/a, Venice, 30125, Italy
Description: An osteria in name only, this restaurant has an elegant ambience, with two romantic tables overlooking the canal. If you enjoy Venetian cuisine you will be in your element here, as Signora Mara skilfully combines traditional local dishes with her own personal touch.

Name: Castel Toblino
Address: località Castel Toblino 1, Castel Toblino, 38076, Italy
Description: Situated in a bucolic location in the Trentino where the excellent Vino Santo is produced (we recommend rounding off your meal with a glass of the equally superb grappa), this restaurant and adjacent bar occupy a fascinating medieval castle (tours of which can be arranged) jutting out into the lake of the same name. The generous, modern meat and fish dishes are featured on various tasting menus, along with an extensive à la carte. In summer, make sure you book a table on the charming terrace overlooking the lake.

Name: U' Vulesce
Description: First opened over 60 years ago, this restaurant has been built up into a successful business over the years by the Di Donna family, who serve top - quality produce from this fertile region, including meat and fish dishes, cured hams and cheeses, all accompanied by a selection of good wines.

Name: Cravero - Osteria Contemporanea
Description: Warm colours such as teal and ochre give this restaurant a cosy and welcoming ambience. The cuisine here is authentic and traditional in style, with dishes based on top-quality local ingredients accompanied by a choice of regional wines. There’s also an outdoor area for summer dining.

Name: Miseria e Nobiltà
Description: The name of this restaurant occupying a late-18C palazzo with attractive flooring and Murano glass chandeliers alludes to the peasant traditions that influence its cuisine (miseria) and the creative, elegant dishes served here (nobiltà). The menu features excellent home-made pastas, vegetables and meat dishes, including boned rabbit with leeks and Annurca apples and white and black truffles from the Molise in season.

Name: Ginevra
Address: Rupi di via XXIX Settembre 12, Ancona, 60122, Italy
Description: Situated on the fourth floor of the Seeport hotel, this restaurant boasts a summer roof garden offering stunning sea views. The chef, a native of Ancona who trained with Gualtiero Marchesi, serves traditional local dishes prepared using ingredients from the region, as well as remaining open to the rest of the world (just like his town and its port). Lighter fare is available at the Seeport Bistrò.

Name: Al Camin
Description: On the road to Misurina lake, this friendly restaurant with a modern Alpine style offers dishes of the regional tradition with imaginative touches and modern technique. So a great deal of practicality, then, as in the beef tenderloin wrapped in speck dry-cured pork with cep mushrooms and Ampezzo-style potatoes. The chef and sommelier Fabio Pompanin manages a wine list with approximately 200 labels. In the warmer season, take advantage of the open-air service.

Name: San Quintino Resort
Description: Once you have crossed the plain and climbed up into the San Quintino hills, you come to this restored farmhouse surrounded by an attractive garden. The restaurant is divided into a brick - walled dining room and a winter garden, while the charming guestrooms make this a romantic place to stay. Creative dishes with a focus on local ingredients and a few fish specialities feature on the menu.

Name: Malenco
Address: via Funivia 22, Chiesa in Valmalenco, 23023, Italy
Description: Modern furnishings in the dining room, with panoramic windows looking out over the valley, typical local menu: traditional dishes at reasonable prices.

Name: Evan's
Description: This restaurant is run with great enthusiasm by the Evangelista family (hence the abbreviation Evan’s). It specialises in delicious fish and seafood prepared mainly in a classic style, although local dishes also feature on the menu.

Name: Luigi Pomata
Description: This famous classic restaurant in Cagliari serves top-quality cuisine in its modern dining rooms and on an outdoor terrace. The menu features interesting reinterpretations of Sardinian dishes among other options, including their own tuna (the house speciality), which is also available in tins to take away.

Name: Caffè Meletti
Address: via del Trivio 56 (piazza del Popolo), Ascoli Piceno, 63100, Italy
Description: Housed on the first floor of the historic café where the aniseed liqueur of the same name was created, this restaurant serves simple yet creative, regional and maritime - inspired cuisine. Don’t miss the terrace with views of Piazza del Popolo. Faster options available at lunchtime.

Name: IO Luigi Taglienti
Description: In this charming restaurant in Piacenza, where tables are arranged in the courtyard of the deconsecrated church that is also home to the Galleria Volumnia, Luigi Taglienti delights guests with his elegant and refined cuisine. The chef’s personal and decidedly contemporary reinterpretations of classic Italian and international favourites will linger long in the memory, while the interesting menu "Riscoperta" features  local dishes at an attractive price.

Name: Claudio Ristorante
Description: An unexpected surprise in the heart of the lowlands. In this charming farmhouse situated in open countryside, Claudio prepares top-quality, almost exclusively fish and seafood cuisine with a southern Italian influence (especially from his native Puglia). There’s also a simpler, cheaper menu on weekday lunchtimes.

Name: Le Vie del Borgo
Description: Le Vie del Borgo is situated in a restored rustic building situated in the historic centre of the picturesque village of Toceno in the Val Vigezzo. Here, a young couple with a real passion for cuisine serve recipes from the region and elsewhere, as well as dishes that demonstrate remarkable modern techniques, all made from top-quality seasonal ingredients and accompanied by an interesting selection of wines. The restaurant consists of several intimate dining rooms decorated in Alpine style, with an elegant feel and carefully chosen furnishings. The attractive outdoor space with just a few tables is popular in summer, so advance booking is recommended!

Name: Mater
Description: Nature plays a starring role here, both in terms of the restaurant’s location at the foot of the Camaldoli monastery and in the seasonal cuisine made from locally sourced ingredients. Choose 3 courses from à la carte or opt for the tasting menu Deeper.

Name: L'Atelier 26
Description: Situated in a secluded location, this small gem of a restaurant boasts a skilfully restored stone dining room with a welcoming feel. The menu here has a clear French influence evident in both the style of its dishes and ingredients used. Our inspectors particularly recommend the young chef’s iconic snails and duck breast dishes.

Name: Terrazza Bartolini
Address: via A. Boito 30, Milano Marittima, 48015, Italy
Description: Following its reopening in 2020, this seafront restaurant overlooking the beach and small harbour now offers its guests a choice between its indoor dining room or the panoramic terrace in fine weather (if you prefer the latter, it’s best to book ahead due to its popularity). The cuisine here focuses entirely on simple, unfussy fish dishes, with raw options and cooked dishes which make much use of the local Cervia salt. Daily, market-fresh specials are announced at your table.

Name: Tenuta Casa Virginia
Address: via Cascina Violo 1, Villa d'Almè, 24018, Italy
Description: Surrounded by the property’s own vineyards, this restaurant nestlings at the bottom of a gentle hill features an elegant dining room and a beautiful terrace for outdoor dining in fine weather. The cuisine is contemporary (yet not excessively so), with a few freshwater fish also featuring on the menu, while the wine list showcases a good selection of wines. The property’s own wines are available for purchase in the shop.

Name: Osteria da Cippi
Description: We particularly enjoyed this restaurant for its out-of-this-world feel. Housed in a charming chalet with an open fireplace, Osteria da Cippi serves cuisine made from typical local ingredients. At the helm in the kitchen, Nazzarena Del Fabbro is inspired by the seasons, using wild herbs from Valdestali in spring, vegetables from the restaurant’s small kitchen garden in summer, and seasonal fruit from the surrounding forests in autumn. Make sure you try the cjarsons. Guests are required to book in advance.

Name: Il Riccio
Description: Situated just a few metres from the Blue Grotto and perched right above the water, Il Riccio is the quintessential Mediterranean fine-dining restaurant thanks to its tasteful and elegant decor. Undoubtedly one of Capri’s iconic addresses, it focuses uniquely on fish and seafood dishes. Whether you have a sweet tooth or not, a visit to the tempting dessert buffet to admire its array of delicacies is a must!

Name: Rosso di Sera
Address: via Pietro Nenni 2, Castelletto sopra Ticino, 28053, Italy
Description: Situated closed to the motorway exit, this restaurant’s rustic exterior belies its young, colourful and contemporary interior. The dishes are as modern as the decor, yet they have their roots in strong local traditions. The owner has a real passion for French and sparkling wines, including around 160 different champagnes and a wide selection of Burgundies, plus a good choice of wines by the glass, craft beers and cocktails.

Name: Osteria del Tempo Perso
Description: Situated in a hidden corner of the historic centre, this small bistro-style restaurant has a friendly and welcoming atmosphere, with photos alternating with books, wine bottles and glasses on the walls (the wine list includes a few labels from elsewhere in Europe). Small tables set close together, warm, subtle lighting and an almost Parisian ambience make this a perfect choice for a romantic dinner or a meal with friends. There’s also a small outdoor space for fine weather but seats are limited, so it’s best to book ahead!

Name: Laurin
Description: In the magnificent setting of the exclusive Parkhotel Laurin, this restaurant is one of the best in Bolzano, boasting a Liberty-style dining room and tree-shaded tables in the garden for summer dining. The traditional cuisine also includes a few modern touches with ingredients and techniques from all over Italy and beyond, such as the grilled trout and leek terrine wrapped in nori algae in the shape of a flower. The menu features meat and fish dishes, with a small section dedicated to traditional local specialities.

Name: Posta
Description: A corner of Tuscany in Bologna, where famous soups such as ribollita and pappa col pomodoro are followed by pappardelle pasta with wild boar, tripe, beef pepper stew and, of course, Fiorentina steak, although there’s also room on the menu for local specialities such as tagliatelle and tortellini. Many of the wines served also come from Tuscany.

Name: Lio Pellegrini
Description: Despite its location in the town centre, the attractive outdoor terrace of this restaurant offers a peaceful atmosphere with its decor of light drapes. The red - coloured dining room makes a pleasant backdrop for the modern, Mediterranean cuisine served here. Elegant ambience.

Name: Regallo
Description: Situated slightly on the outskirts, this contemporary-style restaurant occupies the unusual setting of an old factory. Here, picture windows in the dining room overlook the stream below, with the sound of the water adding an almost musical note to the ambience. In the open-view kitchen, skilful chef Claudio Ravinetto prepares dishes with an exclusive focus on fish, including delicious house specialities such as scallops with anchovy cream, tomatoes and basil, and the “Sicilia” dessert which pays tribute to the island with its ricotta cream topped with chocolate shavings, orange jelly and dried capers.

Name: Rifugio Col Alt
Address: strada Col Alt, Corvara in Badia, 39033, Italy
Description: During the day this restaurant can be reached in just a few minutes by cable car, providing you with breathtaking views of the Dolomites, while in the evening (when the service is more attentive – things are faster paced at lunchtime) you have to arrange transport via snowcat. The name “refuge” refers only to the location as the cuisine is definitely that of a restaurant: although the menu features hearty mountain fare, it also includes modern options and a few fish-based recipes, including oysters. Last but not least, there’s a good selection of wines.

Name: Ca' 7
Address: via Cunizza da Romano 4, Bassano del Grappa, 36061, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Housed in a charming 18C villa, this elegant restaurant overlooks its attractive garden in a magical setting which is typical of the Veneto. The cuisine also has a regional focus, with classic recipes featuring on the menu alongside more creative dishes (fish appears more often than meat).

Name: Zafferano
Address: viale Icilio Vanni 1, Città della Pieve, 06062, Italy
Description: Famous for its saffron, Città della Pieve is also well worth a visit to admire the Baciadonne alley (“one of the narrowest streets in Italy”) in its beautiful historic centre. This welcoming restaurant in a quiet and elegant hotel boasts an attractive veranda for summer dining that provides the perfect backdrop for delicious cuisine that is influenced by Umbria and Tuscany alike.

Name: Castello Malvezzi
Address: via Colle San Giuseppe 1, Brescia, 25133, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Terrace
Description: This elegant 16C hunting lodge offers a modern menu of fish dishes and regional specialities. Particular attention is paid to the excellent Calvisano caviar, with a dedicated menu. There’s an attractive outdoor dining area facing the gardens with views of the city of Brescia.

Name: Particolare di Siena
Description: A fine-dining restaurant which changed tack in 2020, reducing its number of tables to just ten and embracing a sustainable approach to its cuisine. It now prioritises local suppliers and certified organic and environmentally friendly ingredients, while the restaurant’s own kitchen garden, featuring produce grown in line with biodynamic techniques, provides some of the best seasonal ingredients used in the dishes here.

Name: Baita Fraina
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Terrace
Description: Warm little bar rooms, reminiscent of the German wine bars or "Stube", a summer terrace and well - prepared regional dishes: for those who want to escape the mundane life of Cortina for the silence of an isolated "baita" [mountain hut]. Delightful rooms, colourfully furnished in warm tones so you can better enjoy the silence and scents of the mountains.

Name: I 5 Campanili
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Contemporary cooking with an emphasis on Mediterranean fare in tune with the seasons is to the fore in this elegant restaurant occupying a 20C building with an attractive veranda to the rear. Fish takes pride of place on the menu, with a particular focus on raw dishes and shellfish, but the splendid desserts are also worthy of note, such as cherries in sour cherry juice with fior di latte ice cream.

Name: Vitis
Description: A modern wine bar in the centre of Bressanone (Brixen), situated in the same building as the delightful family restaurant, the Oste Scuro. Here, small armchairs, benches and stools are dotted among low square tables and higher tables, all surrounded by walls completely lined with wine bottles. The contemporary cuisine features tempting, generous dishes such as cod with cauliflower, cavolo nero and beurre blanc. Accommodation is available just two minutes’ away in the historic Adler Historic Guesthouse run by the same owners.

Name: Osteria da Nando
Cuisine: Cuisine from the Aosta Valley, Traditional Cuisine
Description: Opened in 1957, this osteria in the heart of the historic centre is one of the town’s leading restaurants for anyone wanting to sample the cuisine of the Aosta valley. Delicious regional specialities such as cured meats, polenta and fondue are prepared with the best ingredients and served in a simple dining room with plenty of character. Wide choice of excellent wines by the glass.

Name: Elephant
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Situated in the famous Elephant hotel (with which it shares a name), this restaurant has a unique, historic ambience thanks to its decor of antique wood panelling. The cuisine here is regional with a modern twist, featuring dishes such as char with cream of celery and green apple on a bed of fragrant elderflowers. The interesting wine list boasts a selection of almost a thousand different labels.

Name: A' Paranza
Description: For more than 30 years, this restaurant run by the Proto brothers has been a popular choice for visitors to the beautiful Atrani valley. Simple cuisine served in a simple and informal setting (dishes are nearly always announced at your table rather than listed on a menu), with a focus on Mediterranean and Campanian dishes.

Name: Baretto di San Vigilio
Address: via al Castello 1, San Vigilio, Bergamo, 24129, Italy
Description: Situated in the small square in front of the cable-car entrance, this typical bar-cum-restaurant with a retro, vaguely English feel serves generous traditional cuisine reinterpreted with a modern twist, including home-made bread and desserts. In summer, meals are served on the terrace with enchanting views of the town, while the two winter dining rooms have a rustic yet elegant feel.

Name: L'Acciuga
Description: Anchovies, king prawns, cuttlefish and freshly caught fish are just some of the options available in this restaurant specialising in fish and seafood, where guests will be delighted by the fresh flavours of the ingredients. The small wine list, which also includes a few non-Italian labels, offers good value for money. The maritime-style decor evokes the interior of an old ship, while the warm welcome is typical of the region. All in all, an excellent choice!

Name: Agorà
Description: Michele Rizzo is the owner-chef of this interesting restaurant situated in a modern part of Rende. His menu focuses mainly on fish (although a few meat dishes are also available) which he prepares in light, modern dishes with an emphasis on local ingredients. There’s also an interesting wine list.

Name: Le Chiavi d'Oro
Description: Situated in Arezzo’s historic centre, this restaurant boasts an original, minimalist ambience with an elegant wood decor. The main focus here is on the cuisine, which is among the best not only in the city but also in the region. Skilful interpretations of traditional dishes, with a focus on Tuscany, where the gastronomic pleasure increases with each course.

Name: Dispensa Franciacorta
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Wheelchair access
Description: An informal restaurant with bottles of wine from the enoteca on the walls adding a charming touch. The menu features delicious traditional dishes made from top-quality Franciacorta ingredients, including vegetables grown in a large organic garden supported by the restaurant. Many of the ingredients used by the chef (pasta, cheese, ham and salami etc) are served as snacks at the lively bar throughout the day.

Name: Fiamma Cremisi
Address: via De Gasperi 37, località Viadana, Calvisano, 25012, Italy
Description: This country restaurant serves regional cuisine with an innovative twist. Dine either in the main dining room warmed by an open fireplace or outdoors under a gazebo in summer. Lunchtime options are restricted to a business menu or a shorter and more reasonably priced menu.

Name: Marsupino 1901
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: The Marsupino family has been running this trattoria enthusiastically and warmly since 1901. The chef's suggestion pays homage to the territory in accordance with tradition and the wine cellar, managed by the friendly expert Luca, is immense, with an excellent choice by the glass. Five rooms and two suites in the adjacent late nineteenth-century palazzo.

Name: Ladinia
Address: strada Pedercorvara 10, Corvara in Badia, 39033, Italy
Description: Both the Berghotel Ladinia and its restaurant of the same name boast a warm, vintage Alpine-style ambience, with wood decor that tells the story of this business which opened as a simple inn back in 1930. Little has changed since then and guests return here time after time thanks to the warm welcome and attention to detail offered by the Costa family. The traditional cuisine has the occasional modern twist, while the few Ladin-style guestrooms are decorated with a profusion of wood.

Name: La Locanda di Pietracupa
Address: via Madonna di Pietracupa 31, San Donato in Poggio, 50028, Italy
Description: Housed in a beautiful early-20C residence with a panoramic terrace overlooking the hamlet of San Donato in Poggio, this restaurant comprises a dining room and a winter garden to the rear of the building. Tuscan classics take pride of place on the menu, which features a selection of familiar and popular dishes. Four guestrooms are available for anyone looking to extend their stay.

Name: Locanda Alpina
Description: Situated in the enchanting Val di Non with its castles and apple orchards, this restaurant housed in a 19C building has been run by the same family since 1933. It serves excellent cuisine that makes good use of regional produce alongside occasional ingredients from further afield, such as the delicious pistachio ice cream.

Name: Feva
Description: Situated in the historic centre of Castelfranco Veneto, this restaurant has an intimate, elegant and contemporary-cum-minimalist feel despite its period courtyard setting and original wooden beams in the first-floor dining room. Nicola Dinato’s cuisine is showcased on two tasting menus, namely Anima and Corpo. The former offers a selection of new dishes created by the chef, who is constantly updating his cuisine, while the latter features his historic signature specialities (don’t miss the artichoke, crab, fig and leek dish). A lighter, less expensive menu is also available at lunchtime. The impressive wine list includes many French labels – unsurprisingly, perhaps, as the sommelier (and chef’s wife) is from France!

Name: Trattoria Rigoletto
Description: A simple environment, manages to create an interesting cuisine. The menu is quite extensive, the dishes are authentic and the atmosphere is welcoming.

Name: Antico Ristorante Pagnanelli
Description: In business since 1882, yet constantly evolving, this restaurant boasts a superb location overlooking the lake. The menu features meat and fish dishes, enhanced by wild herbs. The extensive wine selection is presented on two wine lists. Don’t miss the famous wine cellars built into the rock, plus the small wine museum.

Name: La Sosta
Address: via San Martino della Battaglia 20, Brescia, 25121, Italy
Description: Housed in a 17C palazzo, this charming restaurant is very popular with locals. Alfresco dining in summer (just a few tables, so it is best to book), as well as efficient and attentive service.

Name: Enoteca di Canelli - Casa Crippa
Description: Occupying a late-19C palazzo, in what was a historic wine cellar right up to the late 1960s, this well-run family restaurant serves regional cuisine with a contemporary twist. The basement dining room is accessible by stairs only.

Name: Residenza del Lago
Description: Boasting a tranquil, homely atmosphere typical of the region and with a name that pays homage to Lake Candia, this restaurant occupies a mid-18C farmhouse that is now located within the town. Its traditional cuisine includes popular dishes such as potato cake with seared shrimp and artichokes, “tajarin vecchio Piemonte” (pasta with a meat sauce), and beef cheeks cooked in Erbaluce di Caluso wine.

Name: Molin Vecio
Description: In the idyllic setting of a 16C mill with a garden and small lake, this restaurant boasts an equally magical dining room with a warm, friendly and traditional feel. Top-quality dishes from the Veneto include a delicious sopressa(the region’s cured ham), Vicenza-style baccalà (cod) with Marano polenta and a soft guancetta served with a superb pendolòn (potato polenta).

Name: El Gato
Description: Chioggia is famous as one of the more active fishing ports in the region and this restaurant takes full of advantage of the local catch. Situated on the central promenade of this picturesque town, the restaurant serves fish of truly exceptional quality served in traditional recipes from the Adriatic.

Name: Dolia Gaeta
Description: This brand-new restaurant boasts an elegant, chic decor and a relaxed and informal ambience. The very young team here is overseen by a talented chef who prepares modern and creative dishes with a focus on fish from the local gulf, as well as elsewhere. The wine list is also particularly interesting, featuring a remarkable choice of champagnes and a special emphasis on labels from Lazio.

Name: Romolo Mare
Description: Situated in a private beach club facing the sea, this restaurant combines a relaxed atmosphere with an elegant feel thanks to its professional owners who have worked as restaurateurs for many years. Here, they serve excellent fish and seafood cuisine with a focus on raw dishes, plus a choice of daily fish specials. A selection of interesting local wines completes the picture.

Name: Da Miro alla Lanterna
Description: It would be difficult for the menu at this restaurant to convey the beauty and quality of the fresh fish on display near the kitchen, where guests can make their own selection. Here, all sorts of shellfish and different fish of all shapes and sizes are transformed into delicious dishes full of flavour. Classic decor, professional service, an excellent wine selection and good value for money all add to the appeal. An address which has been delighting guests ever since 1954!

Name: Pernambucco
Description: This restaurant boasts a garden setting with a pleasant outdoor dining space, plus a long, narrow interior decorated in decidedly classic style. Fish and seafood take pride of place on the menu, with a focus on local fish, including excellent tartare (usually either seabream or tuna, depending on the catch of the day) and shellfish (cooked in salt, baked or grilled). The vegetables are sourced from the restaurant’s own kitchen garden.

Name: Lamberti
Description: This restaurant is situated just a stone’s throw from the sea in a building dating from the 1930s. It serves traditional, regional dishes made from carefully selected ingredients. Don’t miss the fish and the pesto sauce.

Name: Collina
Address: via Ca' Paler 5, Almenno San Bartolomeo, 24030, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: A family style trattoria has now been converted into these modern premises that, while jealously upholding their homely origin, offer dishes of contemporary inspiration. One small dining hall has an open fireplace and the other gives a panoramic view.

Name: Le Cicale
Description: The owners of this pleasant restaurant, once owned by their grandparents, have given it a light, modern feel. A married couple welcome guests front of house, while the wife’s brother creates delicious Italian and regional dishes in the kitchen. Delightful outdoor area to the rear surrounded by greenery.

Name: Mistral
Description: Situated at the tip of Bellagio’s promontory where the two branches of the lake meet, this villa occupies a superb panoramic location, with its restaurant housed in a covered veranda boasting delightful views of the opposite shore, its little villages and exclusive residences. The atmosphere here is reminiscent of a grand hotel, with background piano music in the evening and guests from all around the world. The moderately creative cuisine offers a choice of Italian dishes alongside more international options.

Name: Stube Gourmet
Description: Situated in a pedestrianised area in the centre of Asiago, this small restaurant on the first floor of the Hotel Europa has just five tables and is certain to attract food-lovers thanks to its exquisite cuisine. Now with a new chef at the helm, Stube Gourmet continues to delight guests who are lucky enough to dine here. Classic traditional cuisine based on carefully selected local ingredients with a keen eye for what’s in season provides the foundation for this chef’s dishes. There’s also an excellent wine list that continues to expand, plus a wine shop on the street outside.

Name: Magiargè Osteria Contemporanea
Description: The dining rooms in this lively, typical restaurant in the upper, historic part of Bordighera appear to be almost dug out of the rock. Here, a local chef with plenty of experience behind him creates predominantly Ligurian cuisine (and not just fish and seafood), accompanied by an excellent and extensive wine list, including labels from outside Italy and a good selection of champagnes. Attentive service completes the picture here.
