Name: Alla Fassa
Address: via Nascimbeni 11, Castelletto di Brenzone, 37010, Italy
Description: Although the beautiful views of the lake (with only a cycle path between the restaurant and the water) and mountains on the opposite shore can be admired from the dining room, in fine weather it’s a race for the outdoor tables just a few metres from the water. The cuisine is as impressive as the setting, with a fine balance of classic and modern dishes featuring fish from the lake (such as the “il lago in un piatto” – the lake in a dish – starter) and the sea. A few guestrooms with views of the lake are also available.

Name: I Pifferi
Description: This restaurant occupying an old post house that dates back to the time of Marie Louise, Duchess of Parma, lies amid the verdant landscapes of the Parco Regionale dei Boschi di Carrega, just a kilometre outside the village of Sala Baganza. This stunning setting is the backdrop for typical dishes from Parma, such as Nonna Lina’s herb tortelli served with melted butter and parmesan cheese. In summer, dine alfresco in the cool, shady garden.

Name: Nido del Picchio
Description: This restaurant with a low-key, hushed atmosphere has the feel of a tastefully furnished private home, with an open fire lit in winter and a cool, welcoming outdoor dining space for the warmer months. The restaurant has built up a well-deserved reputation for its fish dishes, although the menu here is equally divided between fish and meat. Options such as anolini in brodo (filled pasta in broth) pay tribute to the region’s traditions, while most of the dishes served here are highly creative. Originally English, the owner’s wife runs the front of house with skill and a warm, friendly manner. The wine cellar is home to more than 700 of the best Italian and international wines, with a curious emphasis on labels from cooler climes.

Name: Pinocchio
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Terrace
Description: This glorious, elegant restaurant is surrounded by a delightful garden where guests can dine à la carte or order copious appetisers in the summer months. The recipes focus on the gastronomic traditions of the Piedmont reinterpreted with a modern flavour, as well as more contemporary dishes with original combinations. Meat and fish dishes (including fish from the lake) always feature, alongside some of the restaurant’s classic house specialities.

Name: Ortica
Address: via Giovanni Migone 4, Pieve Ligure, 16031, Italy
Description: You drive along 4.5km of winding, narrow (occasionally extremely narrow) roads to get to Ortica, the restaurant at the Tenuta Golfo Paradiso about 35min from Genoa. As is often the case, once at your destination the extensive views of the Tyrrhenian Sea from the restaurant more than compensate for the effort of getting here. Neither will you be disappointed by the cuisine, which is prepared using top-quality ingredients such as vegetables from the restaurant’s own kitchen garden, local fish and carefully selected meat. Dishes are fresh and modern, and occasionally cooked over the barbecue grill.

Name: Blum
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Great view,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: Although there is an extensive à la carte at this restaurant, it is on the tasting menus that the chef showcases his creative cuisine to the full. His Suggestioni menu features dishes such as scampi carpaccio with green apple and caviar, while the vegetarian Naturalmente option includes a robustly structured black garlic and almond noodle dish full of decisive flavours, which is well worth trying. The romantic, modern platform where tables are set out is practically on the beach, which means that the restaurant is closed in bad weather.

Name: Antica Locanda
Address: piazza della Seta, località San Leucio, Caserta, 81100, Italy
Description: This establishment is practically a trattoria; one can dine in either of two characteristic rooms separated by a brick archway. The cuisine is typical of the Naples area and rice dishes are the specialty.

Name: Miil
Description: Housed in a converted 15C mill on the Kränzelhof wine estate, this smart, elegant restaurant provides the backdrop for excellent, contemporary-style cuisine prepared wherever possible using locally sourced (and always top-quality) ingredients.

Name: Frades Porto Cervo
Description: This new Milan venture is the brainchild of three brothers who already run a restaurant and delicatessen in Porto Cervo. Elegant and extremely contemporary in style, the restaurant serves modern Sardinian cuisine, while a corner reminiscent of their delicatessen allows guests to taste the island’s hams and cheeses by the slice.

Name: Villa Salina
Description: Named after Edoardo Salina, the chef to the House of Savoy, this villa from the mid-1800s features several rooms embellished with frescoed ceilings. The bold owner-chef here has completely restored the building, bringing it back to life and using it as a backdrop for his evolving culinary skills which started out in the family pasticceria. Nowadays, this “multi-tasking” modern restaurant offers a regionally inspired à la carte alongside fish dishes and a business menu option at lunchtime, while in the evening the menu includes a selection of high-quality pizzas. In summer, the dining room opens out onto a beautiful veranda and guests can also wander through the well-kept garden, which is now owned by the local municipality.

Name: Scola
Description: Instead of the simple, rustic-style dishes you might expect at this restaurant, the cuisine is actually elaborate and of the highest quality – an excellent reason for venturing out here!

Name: Da Poli alla Stazione
Address: viale della Repubblica 10, Castelnovo di Sotto, 42024, Italy
Description: Once you have passed a promising display of products, sit down in one of the two light and airy elegant dining rooms or on the pleasant summer terrace; cuisine from land and sea.

Name: Baita Piè Tofana
Description: On the slopes of the Tofana and directly overlooking the ski slopes, a characteristic and romantic mountain lodge with a contemporary touch, whose design manages to combine tradition and modernity, is also a source of inspiration for the cuisine. Dishes with a contemporary taste–Rossini al mare (beef, foie gras, cuttlefish and Teriyaki sauce) is excellent–made with considerable use of charcoal grilling, in both summer and winter, and ample use of local raw materials. With friends, experience the convivial Larin table, with a central built-in fireplace around which the seats are arranged. The wine list is worthy of note with a large choice of Champagnes and Italian bubbly.

Name: Antica Cucina 1983
Description: An excellent establishment in the town centre, with a dining room that is an old oil - mill. Traditional Puglia dishes tastefully personalised; the service is fast and attentive.

Name: 12 Ristorante
Description: An original ambience with real character, as well as top quality fish and seafood. There is also a charming outdoor area overlooking the canal where old boats from the Museo della Marineria are moored.

Name: Duomo
Description: This small restaurant with a bright and welcoming dining room stands out for its contemporary-style cuisine (based around seasonal ingredients) and many home-cooked dishes. The two brothers at the helm create interesting, often regionally inspired recipes with clever personalised twists. On the autumn menu, we particularly recommend the venison with cauliflower, almonds and Barbera wine sauce. Those with a sweet tooth will enjoy the panna cotta with a persimmon coulis (delicious but not too sweet!), while wine-enthusiasts will find plenty to interest them on the extensive wine list. The restaurant also boasts a superb location, nestled in the narrow streets of the centre just a stone’s throw from the Duomo.

Name: Locanda Baggio
Address: via Bassane 1, località Casonetto, Asolo, 31011, Italy
Description: Standing in a quiet location behind Asolo, this restaurant with an attractive summer garden serves authentic cuisine with an emphasis on top quality ingredients. Wine lovers will appreciate the good selection of international wines on offer here.

Name: Da Tonino
Description: Allow a good half-hour to get to this small restaurant with a simple ambience and an airy terrace which is perfect in the heat of summer. The cuisine has its roots in local traditions – its first courses are particularly good. There’s also an excellent wine selection.

Name: Osteria Casale Ferrovia
Address: via Stazione 1, sulla SP 34, Carovigno, 72012, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Housed in what was once the 20C dwelling of an old olive mill, this restaurant boasts elegant decor, including a few antique family pieces and Art Deco - style tables. The female owner - chef prepares light and modern dishes with a regional flavour, while the wine list also showcases the best of Puglia. As the name suggests, the railway lies to the rear of the property, although there’s very little noise and no disturbance at all.

Name: Villa Pizzini
Description: From Lake Maggiore you climb up Mottarone mountain to an altitude of around 1 400m to reach this 19C hunting lodge, where a young couple of self-taught chefs provide a warm and friendly welcome. The cuisine here speaks for itself – delicious meat dishes, plus a few specialities from the lake which are also served outdoors to a backdrop of stunning views. This couple are passionate about using seasonal ingredients and learning about every different stage in their supply chain. Local game dishes are highly recommended.

Name: MOI Omakase
Description: Situated in the centre of Prato, with views of the Castello dell’Imperatore, this restaurant takes guests on a culinary voyage to Japan without leaving Italy! All guests eat the same single menu, starting at 9pm, as part of which the chef prepares his selection of sushi and sashimi directly in front of them in the dining room. Omakase means “I trust you” – an act of trust that you certainly won’t regret. Our inspector recommends the miso and monkfish soup with kelp and green onions.

Name: Mima
Description: You’ll be won over by the seasonal Mediterranean cuisine created by the young yet experienced chef at this restaurant. Accommodation is also available in modern guestrooms, plus there’s an enchanting roof garden in which to sip an aperitif while the sun goes down.

Name: Al Baliaggio
Address: via Vittorio Emanuele II 136, Venosa, 85029, Italy
Description: Housed in a 15C building in the centre of town, this restaurant boasts beautiful vaulted ceilings and a smart, elegant ambience. The young owner-chef serves cuisine with a traditional focus which is reinterpreted in modern style and made from excellent regional ingredients, as well as a few fish options. Efficient, punctual service.

Name: Osteria Mood
Address: via Cesare Battisti 58, San Bartolomeo al Mare, 18016, Italy
Description: Situated just a few minutes from the seafront promenade in a quiet, residential district, this restaurant with a relaxing ambience serves delicious Ligurian cuisine with a focus on organic vegetables, fish and seafood (local whenever possible), and home-made bread, desserts and fresh pasta. In summer, meals are served by the swimming pool in the garden, while in winter, the welcoming covered veranda boasts extensive sea views.

Name: Suscettibile Salerno
Description: Separated from a street in the centre of Salerno by an inner courtyard, this restaurant is a peaceful oasis with comfortable chairs arranged on a modern and stylish veranda (which opens almost completely in summer) and in an equally elegant dining room. Young chef Mario Quarta (born in Battipaglia) combines influences from his native region with techniques learned in renowned restaurants elsewhere in Italy and abroad, including Michelin-starred addresses. The French influence evident in his cooking techniques makes his Campania-focused cuisine even more exciting and contemporary. Our inspector particularly enjoyed the “Rombo R-otto” – four mouthwatering textures of meaty turbot served in a beautifully presented dish. Elegant, professional service overseen by manager Marco Sesso completes the picture.

Name: Gnocchetto
Description: This long-established family-run restaurant (opened in 1926) with an updated contemporary decor continues to serve cuisine that is classic and generous in style yet adapted to modern tastes. Individual dishes take pride of place on the menu at lunchtime, although you can also order from the À la carte if you wish. There’s also an outdoor space for summer dining.

Name: La Piemontese
Address: via San Martino 48, Mariano Comense, 22066, Italy
Description: The focus at La Piemontese, a simple yet modern restaurant with a convenient car park, is mainly on meat dishes, although game and fresh truffles also feature in season, plus there’s a generous business menu at lunchtime. An enjoyable dining experience that offers good value for money.

Name: Meta Ristorante
Address: via Generale Pescetto 5, Celle Ligure, 17015, Italy
Description: Situated in the picturesque historic centre of Celle, this old boathouse with a typical brick ceiling is now home to an excellent gourmet restaurant, where a young chef creates some of the most interesting dishes in the region.

Name: Capogiro
Address: Località Li Mucchi Bianchi, Baia Sardinia, 07021, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Terrace
Description: Situated on a panoramic terrace with views of the sunsets over Baja Sardinia, a stone’s throw from the Costa Smeralda, this restaurant serves creative cuisine with a focus on local and Italian ingredients in unexpected combinations. Our inspector particularly enjoyed the cacio e pepe cannelloni with raw prawns, salicornia and cuttlefish ink.

Name: Shiroya
Description: One of the most popular restaurants in the historic centre of Rome, Shiroya has just a few tables, so booking ahead is recommended. Served with courtesy and professionalism, dishes include well-known Japanese specialities such as home-made gyoza (dumplings) with various fillings, tempura and other fried options, the inevitable raw fish in all the classic combinations, ramen, different rice dishes and much more besides.

Name: Hebbo Wine & Deli
Address: Località Lago di Dobbiaco, Toblach, 39034, Italy
Description: Situated on a campsite on the shores of Lake Dobbiaco, this new restaurant demonstrates its owner’s passion for wine and contemporary cuisine. The young Austrian chef here has plenty of experience behind him – in the evening, his dishes are showcased on surprise tasting menus of seven or nine courses, while at lunchtime, there’s also a 5-course option. His recipes feature plenty of vegetables and exciting combinations, such as burnt leek, Romanesco sauce and potato or trout, or alternatively, dried beetroot, reduced cream, thyme and Schüttelbrot. Ingredients are sourced from trusted producers, as well as family members who run a biodynamic farm nearby. The superb wine list demonstrates the friendly, competent owner’s passion for wine.

Name: Sotto l'Arco
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Villa Aretusi is a pleasant 17C villa surrounded by its own garden on the outskirts of Bologna. At the hotel’s gourmet restaurant, Sotto l’Arco, on the first floor (lift available), the skilful chef creates modern, interesting Italian dishes, while at the Trattoria on the ground floor the focus is more on traditional Emilian cuisine.

Name: Sa Cardiga e Su Schironi
Address: strada statale 195 rotonda per Capoterra, Capoterra, 09012, Italy
Description: Since 1967, this small restaurant has been delighting locals and visitors alike with its vast array of fish and seafood dishes, including grilled and skewered specialities. The fresh fish display cabinet at the restaurant entrance is one of the highlights here, as is the extensive selection of antipasti which includes tuna and mullet bottarga, “agliata alla bosana” (blue shark with tomatoes in a light sweet and sour sauce) and “burrida alla cagliaritana” (with dogfish). Other dishes include fresh and pasta with various seafood sauces, fried fish, soup, lobster, barbecued fish and even eel.

Name: Erbaluigia
Description: This attractive restaurant with a simple, minimalist decor stands almost opposite the thousand-year-old church of San Frediano. The inviting menu here focuses on regional dishes with a successful combination of traditional and modern styles, including a section dedicated to barbecue options. Meat takes pride of place, although offal, cheese and a few vegetarian options also feature.

Name: Locanda 53 Supper Club
Description: Partners in life and business, Evelyn and Carlo are a young couple who have settled in Arco’s old town where they have restored this old inn, embellishing it with three modern and comfortable guestrooms. The restaurant offers two tasting menus featuring meat or fish – guests are asked to make their choice when booking. Once that’s done, all you have to do is sit back and enjoy the intimate atmosphere of the couple’s small “supper club” and leave everything to the talented Evelyn in the kitchen and skilful Carlo front of house. The recipes here are modern yet unfussy, with a focus on carefully selected ingredients that are prepared with respect and real attention to detail. Fine cuisine and an exquisite welcome combine to offer a truly memorable dining experience.

Name: Osteria Europa
Description: Despite its simple appearance, this restaurant housed in the hotel of the same name serves interesting, traditional cuisine which is well prepared and full of flavour.

Name: Peperosa
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Wheelchair access
Description: Despite its idyllic location facing the picturesque Piazza dell'Anfiteatro, this restaurant has avoided becoming a tourist trap, evolving instead into one of the most interesting restaurants in Lucca. The menu is finely balanced between meat and fish dishes with more than just a hint of added creativity, plus there’s now a new chef at the helm.

Name: Eggentaler
Description: Renowned for being one of the best places in the region for steak cooked over a barbecue grill, this excellent restaurant has a varied menu which also includes a few fish dishes. There’s also a very good wine list, plus the restaurant also offers comfortable guest accommodation.

Name: Crub
Address: corso Umberto I 125, Cava de' Tirreni, 84013, Italy
Description: A modern restaurant with an elegant, contemporary decor situated on the main pedestrian street in the town centre. The menu features an excellent selection of raw dishes, as well as a good choice of oysters and caviar, plus an equally delicious house speciality: fried pizza marinara with San Marzano tomato cream, garlic mayonnaise, black olive ash and Cetara anchovies. Sparkling wines are to the fore on the wine list.

Name: /gu.stà.re/ oltrecucina
Description: An attractive contemporary-style restaurant right in the town centre, with a striking colour scheme and minimalist decor. The cuisine is inspired by traditional Piedmontese recipes which are reinterpreted with an imaginative touch by young, talented chef Valentina Maioni who selects top-quality ingredients and cooks with real passion.

Name: Rendenèr Alpine Food
Description: Situated within the Lory hotel, this restaurant has a contemporary decor and wooden tables that give it an informal ambience. Here, the young talented chef creates Alpine cuisine from carefully chosen seasonal ingredients, with menus changing throughout the year. In spring, for example, ingredients include Alpine sow-thistle, Mugo pine shoots, woodruff and lichen, while in summer herbs and flowers from the restaurant’s own organic kitchen garden add extra flavour to dishes. An interesting wine list with a focus on regional labels completes the picture.

Name: Umami
Address: Via Ugo Secondo Partigiano 1, Badalucco, 18010, Italy
Description: A young chef with experience in renowned restaurants has taken over the old kindergarten in this village and transformed it into a delightful restaurant. Here, he serves contemporary cuisine, often influenced by local traditions and showcased on tasting menus from which individual dishes can be ordered à la carte style. In summer, there’s an attractive outdoor space practically on the banks of the Argentina river, which gives its name to the valley in which this village is situated.

Name: Visione Restaurant and Living
Address: Strada Nicolini Basso 34, loc. Tre Stelle, Barbaresco, 12050, Italy
Description: At this restaurant, new chef Emanuele Bellomo serves three tasting menus – one focuses on traditional dishes, another has a more modern and imaginative flavour, while the third is a surprise menu which allows the chef to demonstrate his skill to the full (all dishes are also available à la carte style). Situated in the Casa Nicolini hotel in a quiet, panoramic location, the restaurant boasts fine views of the hills through its dining room windows and from its terrace, where a bar and bistro with a more concise and reasonably priced menu are set up in the summer months.

Name: Ristorante de LEN
Address: Via Cesare Battisti 66, Cortina d'Ampezzo, 32043, Italy
Description: Just a stone’s throw from the central and very busy Corso Italia, this restaurant has an elegant Alpine feel. Here, subtle lighting, soft background music and larch wood cladding on the walls create an ambience with an attractive blend of the modern and traditional. The cuisine takes inspiration from the local region, with specialities interpreted with a contemporary twist, including a focus on vegetable- and cheese-based dishes such as the excellent “fonduta di Saporito d'alpeggio” (fondue).

Name: AceroRosso
Address: Via Ruvignan 1, Vodo di Cadore, 32040, Italy
Description: This secluded mountain chalet immersed in verdant woodland boasts a welcoming dining room with a decidedly Alpine feel thanks to the profusion of wood and a warming open fire. The cuisine is also regional in style, featuring local recipes and ingredients albeit with a contemporary touch. Popular dishes include the rack of lamb cooked at low temperature and served with creamed sweetcorn, leek fondant and its own jus.

Name: Café Les Paillotes
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: This old acquaintance of the Michelin Guide now has a new chef at the helm! Although the decor and furnishings remain the same with a slightly old-fashioned feel, the cuisine is modern yet with no unnecessary frills and has a fresh and generous flavour. Highlights on the menu include the new raw fish options, which have an entire tasting menu to themselves. The well-stocked wine cellar is home to around 500 labels which offer good value for money.

Name: Meylas
Address: Al Raha Beach, Al Muneera, Abu Dhabi
Description: It may be a little hard to find but this all-day eatery hidden away among the apartment blocks of Al Muneera Island is well worth seeking out. It began life as a food truck but now the two sisters behind it have a thriving business where their passion for their country and its food culture are clear for all to see. The chefs in the on-view kitchen prepare a menu of authentic and satisfying Emirati dishes.

Name: Punjab Grill
Address: The Ritz-Carlton Hotel, Grand Canal, Venetian Village, 3rd Street, Al Rawdah, Abu Dhabi
Description: There are Punjab Grills dotted around the world and this outpost, located in the Venetian Village, part of the sprawling acreage of the Ritz-Carlton hotel, is one of the more established branches, having opened in 2015. Ask for one of the booths and sit back and enjoy the Northern Indian specialities and the attentive service. They also have an attractive waterfront location and a terrace from which to enjoy it.

Name: Em Sherif Sea Café
Address: Rosewood Abu Dhabi Hotel, Zayed the First Street, Al Maryah Island, Abu Dhabi
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Great view,Terrace,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: Meaning “mother of Sherif” in Arabic, this restaurant pays homage to the original Beirut branch first opened in 2011. Situated inside the Rosewood hotel, this light, contemporary space offers far reaching views of the water surrounding Al Maryah Island and interiors boasting Portuguese Azulejo hand-painted wall tiles. The authentic menu is seafood focused – make sure you check out the seafood counter as you arrive – and has a wide variety of vibrant, well-balanced Lebanese dishes made for sharing.

Name: La Petite Maison (LPM)
Address: L1, The Galleria, Al Maryah Island, Abu Dhabi
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Brunch,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: The history of La Petite Maison began in London in 2007, with further outposts opening around the world in the years since. Here in The Galleria, customers can judge it for themselves, with Mediterranean cuisine prepared with Niçoise touches and served by a well-trained team in elegant surroundings. Dishes like thinly sliced octopus or salt-baked sea bass will put you in a sunny mood; and be sure to leave room for the pistachio cake.

Name: Cafe Milano
Address: Four Seasons Hotel, The Galleria Level 1, Al Maryah Island, Abu Dhabi
Description: Powerbrokers, movers and shakers in Washington DC will be familiar with the original Café Milano. This elegant sibling is in the Four Seasons – and if you want to be seen enjoying la dolce vita, then start with an aperitivo in the bar. The Italian chef and his team confidently prepare authentic Italian dishes; the homemade pastas are a highlight. There’s also a great terrace.

Name: NIRI
Address: Building 9, Mamsha Al Saadiyat, Abu Dhabi
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Counter dining,Great view,Notable sake list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Grab a seat at the counter of this contemporary Japanese restaurant to watch the chefs prepare your dishes over the robata grill. The ingredients are top-notch, and the kitchen is clearly motivated. The pared-back interior is very on-trend and comes complete with a sakura tree. People-watchers and anyone who enjoys a good sea view will prefer a seat on the terrace as this spot on Mamsha Al Saadiyat is hard to beat.

Name: Paradiso
Address: Yas Bay Waterfront Pier 71, Yas Island, Abu Dhabi
Description: A partnership between celebrated French chef Pierre Gagnaire and Nicole Rubi of La Petite Maison in Cannes resulted in this bright and colourful restaurant. It’s the perfect backdrop to their favoured cuisine – that of the Mediterranean, so expect everything from snails and roast poussin to fritto misto, pizza and assorted pasta dishes. The terrace overlooking the water is nicely decked out and a very pleasant spot.

Name: Oak Room
Address: The Edition Hotel, Al Bateen Marina, Abu Dhabi
Description: Dressed like a smart London club, all wood and leather – but with the music turned up loud – Oak Room is all about meat. Steaks, largely from the USA and Australia, come in various cuts and are accompanied by a large selection of sides; don’t miss the triple cooked chips. Sunday roasts are popular and there’s a wide variety of other dishes on offer too, from fish and chips to burgers.

Name: Cipriani
Address: Building 1, Yas Marina, Yas Island, Abu Dhabi
Description: Elegance and style are hallmarks of all Cipriani restaurants and Abu Dhabi’s branch of this well-known international group occupies an appropriate glamourous position overlooking Yas Island Marina, with a beautiful terrace to make the most of the great views.  There are Japanese dishes available, but Italian is really the way to go here – and they offer all the classics, from carpaccio to cannoli.

Name: Li Jiang
Address: The Ritz-Carlton Hotel, Grand Canal, Al Maqta, Abu Dhabi
Description: Southeast Asian dishes lead the way at this restaurant within The Ritz-Carlton hotel. All dishes are prepared with equal care – the Szechuan chilli lamb loin will certainly get your taste buds excited – but it’s the wok dishes that are their speciality. Order dishes like wok-fried scallops and butter prawns, then watch the chefs working dexterously and skilfully behind the glass screens. The friendly team run the place well and service is smooth and professional.

Name: Li Beirut
Address: Conrad Abu Dhabi Etihad Towers Hotel, West Corniche, Abu Dhabi
Description: Its contemporary styling, views of the harbour, well-choregraphed service and good food make this Lebanese restaurant a favourite of many. The core of the menu is classic Lebanese, but the kitchen works hard here to impress, especially when it comes to presentation and the subtle addition of modern touches to some dishes. Whilst the main menu is a little more concise than many places, it is supplemented by a very useful selection of fixed price menus.

Name: Broadway
Address: Emirates Palace Mandarin Oriental Hotel, West Corniche Road, Al Ras Al Akhdar, Abu Dhabi
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Brunch,Car park,Counter dining,Terrace,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: This modern, American brasserie located in the Emirates Palace Mandarin Oriental hotel is perfect for a lively evening in a Broadway-inspired setting. Combined with a DJ, live music on Saturday night, sharp service by a well-drilled team and a concise menu delivering a roll call of classics, you’ve got the ingredients for a glamourous night out with friends. The experienced chef delivers comforting dishes such as omelette Arnold Bennett, lobster bisque and their signature beef Wellington to share. Don’t miss steaks cooked to perfection and the glorious tart Tatin. They also offer a brunch on Saturday and a traditional roast on Sunday.

Name: Maté
Address: Park Hyatt Abu Dhabi Hotel and Villas, Al Saadiyat Island, Abu Dhabi
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Counter dining,Garden or park
Description: Descend the stairs to the sound of pumping music and you’ll find yourself transported to Buenos Aires at his atmospheric restaurant in the Park Hyatt Hotel. The centrepiece is the open kitchen and the flaming wood-fired grills here. The menu does have some Lebanese influence but it’s really all about Argentinian dishes with great charred flavours and top ingredients, be they prawns or beef. If you really want to feel part of the action, sit at the counter.

Name: Byblos Sur Mer
Address: Intercontinental Hotel, King Abdullah bin Abdul Aziz Al Saud Street, Abu Dhabi
Description: Start your visit on the wonderful terrace and spend time admiring, or indeed coveting, the boats bobbing in the marina that it overlooks. Sharing is everything at this two-level restaurant, where the service is affable and organised. The Lebanese menu offers bags of choice – the grilled section is a good place to head to, where lamb-lovers should look no further than machawi mchakaleh. Friday and Saturday evenings see live music and entertainment.

Name: Villa Toscana
Address: St. Regis Hotel, Nation Towers, Corniche, Abu Dhabi
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Credit cards not accepted,Terrace,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: As you’d expect from the name, you can find many a classic Tuscan dish here at Villa Toscana, which sits within the St. Regis hotel on the Corniche waterfront. Familiar favourites like spaghetti alle vongole mix with plenty of pizzas and a wide range of other dishes to form a menu with something for everyone. On weekdays, they serve a good value business lunch comprising an extensive buffet of antipasti and desserts, plus a freshly cooked main course.

Name: Moksh
Address: Conrad Etihad Towers Hotel, West Corniche, Abu Dhabi
Description: Step into this bright and colourful Indian restaurant and the world will instantly seem a happier place. The menu offers a wide-ranging selection, from popular street snacks to classic favourites originating from various regions across the country. But what makes the food a little different is that the kitchen is unafraid of adding its own contemporary touches, while all the while respecting traditional flavours. We suggest starting off with the colourful chaat served in fine and crisp puris and ensure you finish with the well-presented kulfi.

Name: Namak
Address: Dusit Thani Hotel, Sultan Bin Zayed The First Street (Al Muroor Road), Abu Dhabi
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Valet parking
Description: A culinary voyage around India drawing on myriad influences is the draw here at this colourful restaurant within the Dusit Thani hotel. The passion of the kitchen team really comes through in the carefully prepared dishes. The lamb specialities are particularly good, whether that’s Kashmiri Rogan Josh or Kakori Reshmi Seekh. There’s plenty for vegetarians too, including sharing platters.

Name: José by Pizarro
Address: Conrad Etihad Towers Hotel, West Corniche, Corniche Road, Abu Dhabi
Description: A small space on the ground floor of the Conrad Etihad Towers Hotel is the chosen venue for José Pizarro's first venture outside London but, instead of adopting a similarly rustic look for his tapas bar, the designers have used plenty of marble to create a more elegant environment. The small sharing plates include great anchovies, satisfying meatballs in a spicy tomato sauce and the unmissable chocolate pot.

Name: Coya
Address: The Galleria, Four Seasons Al Maryah Island Hotel, Abu Dhabi
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Great view,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: Whether you like your Peruvian flavours complemented with Japanese, Chinese or Spanish influences, you’ll find you have plenty of options. Ceviche is always a great choice to begin, while the ‘Chilean sea bass rice iron pot’ is a popular signature dish. Several elegant dining rooms provide a colourful stage for the vibrant food, while the floor to ceiling windows make the most of the waterfront location. The set lunch menu is always good value.

Name: Tean
Address: Jumeirah at Saadiyat Island Resort, Al Saadiyat Island, Abu Dhabi
Description: The first thing you’ll be tempted by will be a quick dip as you wander past the pool of the Jumeirah at Saadiyat Island Resort. The smiling service team will make you feel instantly at home, while the open kitchen prepares an assortment of Lebanese, Greek, Turkish and Middle Eastern dishes, all designed for sharing. There are excellent freshly baked breads aplenty; just be sure to order something from the charcoal grill and finish with Umm Ali.

Name: Mijana
Address: The Ritz-Carlton Hotel, Grand Canal, Al Maqta, Abu Dhabi
Description: Classical Lebanese cooking is served here against an elegant and stylish backdrop provided by the luxurious Ritz-Carlton hotel. The menu offers a comprehensive array of traditional dishes from the region, a large selection of hot and cold mezzeh, and plenty of satisfying options from the grill – the mashawee mshakaleh includes four different meats. Finish the night with a shisha pipe on the terrace.

Name: Kopitiam by Chandy's
Address: Al Falah Street, Old Passport Rd, Zone 1, Abu Dhabi
Description: Owner Chandy and his team runs this sweet little Malaysian restaurant with passion, politeness and professionalism - and clearly want everyone to enjoy themselves. That proves easy, thanks to the inexpensive, fresh and flavoursome dishes on the short menu that’s supplemented with a blackboard of specials; roti jala is always well worth ordering. The place is immaculately kept, with views into the equally spotless kitchen.

Name: Ray's Grill
Address: Podium Level 1, Conrad Etihad Towers Hotel, West Corniche, Abu Dhabi
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: Thanks to the floor-to-ceiling windows and its perch on the 63rd floor, great views are a given at this smart steakhouse in the Conrad Etihad Towers Hotel. Prime cuts from American grain-fed cattle are offered alongside Australian Wagyu and the steaks are cooked on a chargrill; succulence and great flavours are guaranteed. Tartares are made at the table for a bit of theatre and there’s an assortment of other top produce too, from Atlantic lobster to whole sea bass.

Name: Zuma
Address: Abu Dhabi Global Market,  The Galleria Al Maryah Island, Abu Dhabi
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Notable sake list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: Gliding down the softly lit staircase allows everyone to feel like they’re about to arrive at the best party in town – this really is Fun Central, with the music to prove it. As with all other Zuma branches around the globe, the menu covers a multitude of Japanese bases, with seafood from the robata grill being the standout, although the signature corn-fed baby chicken rightly has many admirers too.

Name: Yadoo's House
Address: Al Nasr Tower 2, Al Murror Street, Abu Dhabi
Description: Sitting beneath an apartment block in the suburb of Rabdan is this likeable spot. The purpose-built white space was always going to be a challenge when it came to giving it personality, but assorted artefacts and articles like spice sacks and a sewing machine go some way towards creating the look of ‘Grandma’s house’. The Emirati cooking is done with care and respect for tradition and the portions are as big as the prices are low. We suggest starting with the katlees, followed by the majbous and save room to finish off with the luqaimat.

Name: Finz
Address: Beach Rotana Hotel, 10th Street, Al Zahiyah, Abu Dhabi
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Eating seafood by the sea – there aren’t many things in life that can beat it. At Finz the fish and shellfish come in a variety of styles to suit all tastes, so if you want to feel you’re holidaying on the Med you can order fruits de mer or moules marinières, while those who prefer a more Asian theme can try the tempura roll or teriyaki salmon. The charming service is another delight here.

Name: Al Farah
Address: Khalidiyah St, Al Khalidiyah, W8, Abu Dhabi
Description: The first thing you’ll notice at this bright, contemporary restaurant is a queue of people picking up their orders of manaqeesh and the fresh breads coming out of the oven. The extensive menu offers a range of flavoursome Middle Eastern dishes and it’s a popular destination for breakfast. The restaurant is right in the heart of Al Khalidiyah and is part of a group of family-owned establishments.

Name: Dai Pai Dong
Address: Rosewood Abu Dhabi Hotel, Zayed the First Street, Al Maryah Island, Abu Dhabi
Description: Cantonese is king and sharing the thing at Rosewood’s good-looking Chinese restaurant. Whether you enjoy roasted duck, braised brisket, crispy chicken or double-boiled soups, there’s plenty for you to enjoy here, and if you prefer something a little more fiery there are Sichuan dishes too. ‘All you can eat’ dim sum features on weekday lunches; weekend brunches are hugely popular; while Wednesdays host ‘All You Can Grill’ nights.

Name: Mazi
Address: St. Regis Saadiyat Island Resort, Abu Dhabi
Description: If you have a hankering to holiday in the Greek Islands, then bring some friends here to get yourself in the mood. Mazi began life in London in 2012 and continues here at the impressive St. Regis Saadiyat Island Resort, where olive and palm trees decorate the charming terrace. Flavours are traditionally Greek but modernised with smart twists, and the fresh tasting dishes are designed for sharing.

Name: Oii
Address: Al Qana Marina South, Al Maqta’ Street, Abu Dhabi
Description: Meaning ‘hi’ in Portuguese, Oii is located in Al Qana Marina, next to The National Aquarium. On the inside, this relaxed and casual spot is light and airy, thanks to its floor to ceiling windows, while the outside’s spacious, shaded terrace is ideal al fresco dining. Expect a wide-ranging breakfast menu, followed by a Mediterranean-inspired selection of smaller and larger colourful plates, snacks and salads. One way to start your meal is with a grilled octopus with vibrant mojo rojo, followed by the spiced peri peri baby chicken and finish with fruity passion fruit semi freddo.

Name: Martabaan by Hemant Oberoi
Address: Emirates Palace Mandarin Oriental Hotel, West Corniche Road, Al Ras Al Akhdar, Abu Dhabi
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: In contrast to the huge Emirates Palace hotel in which its located, this Indian restaurant occupies a surprisingly small and intimate space. Its eponymous chef has considerable experience around the world and the menu encompasses all his favourite dishes. The tasting menu is the best form of discovery. The enthusiasm of the service team is thoroughly infectious, and their recommendations are always worth heeding.

Name: Butcher & Still
Address: Four Seasons Al Maryah Island Hotel, 2 Global Market Street, Al Maryah Island, Abu Dhabi
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: Those who like a classic steakhouse will find this one at the luxurious Four Seasons ticks all the boxes. Leather banquettes? Check. Prime American beef? Check. Great cocktails? Check. Start with the generously proportioned crab cake before diving into a steak – there are plenty on offer, from ribeye to porterhouse. To finish, there’s New York cheesecake of course, but the more adventurous should take on the challenge of the Tribune Tower chocolate cake.

Name: Fouquet's
Address: Louvre Abu Dhabi, Saadiyat Cultural District 1, Al Saadiyat Island, Abu Dhabi
Description: As befits the remarkable Louvre Abu Dhabi, its restaurant is not only one with a famous name serving classic French cuisine, but is also one decidedly grander than its ‘brasserie’ moniker would suggest. The huge, laminated menu offers something for everyone, from glazed duck breast to chicken supreme; finishing with crêpes Suzette will set you up nicely for more gallery viewings.

Name: Grand Beirut
Address: Unit 12100-1201 (FB), Level 2, The Galleria Al Maryah Island, Adgm Square, Al Maryah Island, Abu Dhabi
Description: Under the same management as Beirut Sur Mer, this restaurant offers just the thing for refuelling after a gruelling day of shopping around Abu Dhabi. The Lebanese dishes are designed for sharing and generously sized, while proving to be full of flavour and founded upon quality ingredients. Be sure to leave room for their delicious kunafa.

Name: Catch at St. Regis
Address: Nation Riviera Beach Club, Corniche Road, Abu Dhabi
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Credit cards not accepted,Great view,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: A lovely spot on the beach provides the ideal setting for this seafood restaurant. Service is warm and quietly confident; the room is bright and spacious; and the menu wide and varied. There’s quite a Japanese influence, with plenty of nigiri and sashimi; there are also plates for sharing, and good use is made of the charcoal grill. The ‘Blow Torch Dynamite Roll’ makes for an explosive start!

Name: Bord Eau by Nicolas Isnard
Address: Level 3, Lobby Level, Shangri-La Qaryat Al Beri Hotel, Abu Dhabi
Description: This outpost of French chef Nicolas Isnard from Auberge de Charme, in the Côte-d'Or in France, champions inventive French classics and dishes inspired by his travels around the world. It's a spacious and high-ceilinged room, decorated with contemporary chandeliers and large tables. Choose between an à la carte or one of two tasting menus: 'French classics' or 'Travels around the world', which takes influence from the chef’s adventures around the globe. The ambitious and generously sized dishes are boldly flavoured, suitably adventurous, combine classics with a modern flare and use first class ingredients.

Name: terra
Description: At the quieter end of Al Qana yet still with a view of the boats in the marina, sits terra – relatively new to Abu Dhabi but with a well-established branch in Dubai. Being a Mediterranean restaurant, it’s appropriately relaxed in style and the great music makes it a particularly good choice for dinner. Most of the countries that line the Med get a mention and all the classics are here, including raw dishes and pizza, starters like burrata and croquettes, and plenty of pasta dishes and meats from the Josper oven.

Name: HAUT
Description: The 28th floor of SKY Towers is entirely occupied by Belgium’s highest restaurant. The natural serenity of the venue together with the stunning view of the North Sea and the Belgian coast are worth the trip alone. All the more so, when you learn that chef Dimitri Proost’s cooking is fully equal to this high-flying setting. The cuisine is depicted by subtly distinctive Japanese notes, illustrated by a juicy seabass served in a dashi made from fish bones, which he pairs with clams and a velvety smoked butter sauce. Natural and blissfully legible thanks to the subtle talent of a chef you can trust with flavours.

Name: The Black Knife
Description: The pared-back, industrial interior of The Black Knife is far more stylish than its exterior may suggest. Maitre d’ and sommelier Thomas greets diners elegantly and warmly, while chef Yanaika Skrzyszkowia brings her “food art” to life. She avows a weakness for Asian notes and her way with punchy, gutsy sauces can be tasted immediately. For example, she might marinate hamachi to enhance its subtle acidity before scattering shavings of red beetroot for visual appeal and then adding a coulis of beetroot and a sorbet of red shiso. This rebellious chef has matured and her creativity both convinces and astounds.

Name: Le Beau Rivage by Curtis
Description: Curtis Maquet has breathed new life into the Beau Rivage. This landmark of Namur is idyllically located on the banks of the Meuse and its elegant interior commands a fine view of this picture postcard scene. The youthful chef learned the trade at La Table de Maxime, hence his delicate, expressive repertory, steeped in familiar and elegant, yet punchy flavours. His salmon trout cooked in its skin is a masterclass of culinary virtuosity, whose intense flavour is enhanced by a cream of white cabbage, savoury bouchot mussels and apricot jelly, and then further heightened by a beurre blanc and a vegetable oil. The sommelier’s insightful wine tips and the attentive service of the maitre d’ add the final touch.

Name: L'Orangerie de Moulbaix
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: The bright and airy orangery at Moulbaix Castle presents itself as a tasteful blend of the old and the new. The terrace overlooking the vines, the castle and the windmill in the distance are simply idyllic! Maxence Bouralha and Charles-Maxime Legrand, the chef duo behind Quai no. 4, join forces with Philippe Lartigue to create meticulously prepared hearty French brasserie classics. Think sautéed mushrooms with finely chopped shallot topped with an indulgent potato emulsion, an œuf parfait (slow-cooked egg) that really lives up to its name, as well a touch of orange to provide a bright and zesty finish. Other tempting options are prawn croquettes, vol-au-vent or andouillette. The extensive menu is sure to please.

Name: Auberge du Château de Leignon par Isabelle Arpin
Description: Today, the neo-Gothic Château de Leignon is home to a variety of businesses, including a brewery and, of course, this charming restaurant run by Isabelle Arpin, whose market-fresh cuisine showcases ingredients from local producers. Look forward to playful dishes that draw inspiration from all over the world – for example, she pairs brill with barley infused with coffee, artichoke, a creamy fish sauce and a sabayon with aged rum. Be sure to sample the creations of the local brewery, whose beers frequently find their way into the desserts.

Name: Wan Thai Food
Description: A meal at Wan Thai Food is an education in just how irresistible authentic Thai cuisine can be. The decor featuring plenty of wood and bamboo, lanterns, Buddha statues and other Asian-inspired touches has a distinct street food feel. The extensive menu features all the classic dishes of the genre, freshly prepared by chef Wanna. Tempting options include handmade chicken gyoza served with an exquisite umami-rich soy sauce, as well as a rich fruity and spicy curry with perfectly seared scallops. The delicious sauces are definitely worth a mention! Why not add a refreshing cocktail to your order for an extra exotic kick?

Name: Vividu
Description: The sun always shines in Gavermeer thanks to Vividu, a restaurant established in a villa that is reminiscent of Tuscany, albeit with a rock n’ roll soundtrack. The spontaneity of Nicky who is never far from your table makes the experience even warmer. Chef Laurent Messine demonstrates his passion for outstanding produce and Italy, adding his own inimitable stamp. For example, he may coat a loin of Iberico pork in a crust before cooking it in milk and then using ragusano cheese to create a gutsy sauce, all of which flanked by super-fresh side dishes. The legendary bistecca di Chianina is the house specialty, but requires pre-ordering.

Name: Tabernakel
Description: Brothers Steven and Bart refuse to be hampered by a single style. As a result, you may sample an appetiser of fresh, mildly spicy baba ghanoush or a playful new twist on the traditional tomato-mozzarella bruschetta, followed by a rack of lamb in a rosemary jus. Versatile and talented, they create appetising set menus and a splendid à la carte lineup. Kim enthusiastically supervises the front-of-house, bending over backwards to ensure that you savour every morsel of your meal to the full. An elegant, neoteric industrial vibe with just the right dose of authenticity.

Name: Babam
Address: Avenue du Bois de la Cambre 25, Watermael-Boitsfort, 1170, Belgium
Description: Babam is the sort of neighbourhood restaurant next-door to which we would all like to live. Bistronomic cuisine is second nature to the youthful team of chefs, who all trained in top establishments. They might prepare shrimp fritters with textbook precision, flanked by a yuzu jelly and a light bisque. Alternatively, they might jazz up a wing of poached skate with an exciting contrasting touch of fresh acidity. Their crème brûlée dessert is to die for. Whether you pop in for lunch (concise menu) or the full works in the evening, we warrant you will wish you could take out a monthly subscription to Babam!

Name: Norman's Neighbourhood Kitchen
Address: 22A North Road, Kirkburton, HD8 0RH, United Kingdom
Description: The name (almost) says it all here: it is indeed an endearing neighbourhood bistro, but Norman is not in fact the owner – instead, it’s the name of both the owner’s dog and his grandfather. Rustic décor adds to the welcoming feel, as do the polite, helpful service team. The great value sharing plates incorporate influences from both the Mediterranean and Japan, while the ‘eggy bread’ with bacon jam shows off the chefs’ playful side. The wine list is concise but, refreshingly, it’s all available by the glass.

Name: The Torridon, Achnasheen, IV22 2EY, United Kingdom
GreenStar: Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Wheelchair access
FacilitiesAndServices: Situated on the banks of Upper Loch Torridon with majestic mountains in the background and manicured gardens outside, this vibrantly decorated restaurant inside The Torridon hotel is in a truly stunning location. The kitchen’s local and sustainable ethos results in superb Highlands produce from hand-dived West Coast scallop to Ross-shire lamb, in dishes that demonstrate a mature ‘less is more’ approach where the accompaniments enhance rather than mask the central ingredients. An extensive global whisky collection adds to the appeal.

Name: Tassili
Address: Esplanade, Saint Helier, JE2 3QA, United Kingdom
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Wheelchair access
Description: Overlooking St Aubin's Bay, this intimate restaurant inside the Grand Jersey Hotel offers a haven of luxury, not only in its opulent surroundings but also in the ingredients used. While you relax in the elegant room with linen-clad tables, you can expect to enjoy Jersey produce from blue lobster to Angus beef, not to mention excellent wild turbot. While their components are classically luxurious, there’s some playfully creative touches to the dishes. Bespoke wine flights are available to complement the cooking.

Name: Kioku by Endo
Address: Raffles London at The OWO, 6th Floor, 2 Whitehall Place, Whitehall, London, SW1A 2BD, United Kingdom
Description: Enjoy a cocktail or two in the elegant ground-floor bar before heading up to this restaurant at the top of the Raffles hotel inside the spectacular Old War Office. Superb city skyline views await you, while a seat on the terrace is a must in warmer weather. With a name meaning ‘memories’, the menu fuses Endo Kazutoshi’s Japanese heritage with his Mediterranean training, resulting in dishes ranging from lobster fregola to stand-out nigiri. For a special occasion, book the chef’s table or even the private room in a turret.

Name: Cloth
Address: 44 Cloth Fair, City of London, London, EC1A 7JQ, United Kingdom
Description: A hidden gem within the City of London, this sweetly run restaurant is just a stone’s throw from Smithfield Market, tucked down a narrow lane inside a period house which was once home to the poet Sir John Betjeman. It’s now under the watchful eye of Chef Tom Hurst and wine merchants Joe and Ben, who operate the tightly packed space as part bar, part restaurant, but all full of atmosphere. The cooking is pared-back and ingredient-led, with fine produce like Dorset crab and Somerset lamb given the space to shine. The wine list, as you’d expect, is extensive and full of interesting choices.

Name: Goat On The Roof
Address: 1 Bridge Street, Newbury, RG14 5BE, United Kingdom
Description: Bright, colourful décor welcomes you into this former banqueting hall, where the shelves are filled to bursting with pickled and foraged ingredients. It’s an elegant spot, with marble-topped tables lending the place an upmarket bistro feel. The menu is appealingly varied, with ‘smaller’ and ‘bigger’ plates joined by breads, dips and skewers – none of which will break the bank. The Trealy Farm ham and Winchester cheese croquettes, along with some knockout crispy potatoes, are great examples of the kitchen’s talents. The impressive wine list includes a broad range by the glass.

Name: The Tartan Fox
Address: Carvynick Farm, A3058, Summercourt, TR8 5AF, United Kingdom
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: The location in the middle of Cornwall may be a long way from Scotland but, as the name suggests, Adam Handling finds a way to incorporate his Celtic heritage into this stone-built country pub. Another venture in his ever-expanding empire, it’s a sympathetically refitted 17th-century inn located on a popular holiday caravan park. You can expect to find the likes of a haggis Scotch egg and even a deep-fried Mars bar among the extensive menu of generous pubby favourites filled with bold, well-balanced flavours.

Name: Baba'de
Address: The Mews, Baltimore, P81 TC64, Ireland
Description: With a name meaning ‘Baby Dede’, this second Baltimore venture from Chef Ahmet Dede is an ode to his family and comes with all the homespun charm you’d expect. Located mere feet away from his acclaimed flagship restaurant, this is a more relaxed affair but the great value sharing plates retain the older sibling’s ethos of Turkish flavours married with Irish produce. Each dish – from a unique take on oyster chowder to Ahmet’s signature ‘içli köfte’ – is bright, fresh and wholly satisfying.

Name: AGORA
Address: 4 Bedale Street, Borough Market, London, SE1 9AL, United Kingdom
Description: Located on the edge of Borough Market, underneath its sister restaurant OMA, is this simple yet brilliantly effective ‘souvla bar’. Skewers are at the core of the menu – like the excellent slow-roast pork souvlaki – but it would be foolish to overlook the wonderful range of dips and beautifully puffed flatbreads served straight from the oven. It’s stripped-back cooking done with great skill, resulting in dishes so satisfying you’ll want to order them twice. They're deservedly busy, so make sure you snap up one of the limited bookings or get here for midday when they open.

Name: allta
Address: 1 Three Locks Square, Grand Canal Dock, Dublin City, DO2 A5W7, Ireland
Description: After years of moving around Dublin at festivals and pop-ups, the talented team behind allta finally have a permanent home in this spacious dockside building in a swish area of the city. The space is split into two parts: an industrial-chic cocktail bar complete with DJ and a separate dining room with an open kitchen where guests can sit at the counter. The cooking has a strong Irish base, with quality seafood from Union Hall prawns to day-boat sole making an appearance. If you like your dessert with a side of nostalgia, go for the soft serve ice cream.

Name: The Hero
Address: 55 Shirland Road, Maida Vale, London, W9 2JD, United Kingdom
Description: Maida Vale residents hit the jackpot when the owners of Notting Hill’s The Pelican and The Bull in Charlbury chose this neighbourhood for the location for their third venture. The Hero is like a blueprint for how to sympathetically restore and update a pub, and has been understandably packed since Day One. The ground floor offers a great value list of classic pub dishes, from fish pie to sausage and mash. Upstairs is ‘The Grill’, where things are taken up a level with dishes like sweetbreads and lobster gravy.

Name: mrDeanes
Address: 28-40 Howard Street, Belfast, BT1 6PF, United Kingdom
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Wheelchair access
Description: Its full name, ‘mrDeanes Bistro, Bar and Social’, paints a perfect picture of this spacious addition to Michael Deane’s ever-evolving Belfast empire. Grab a cocktail at the bar before taking your seat in a restaurant that’s bursting with vitality. The eminently appealing menu offers well-executed takes on dishes from all over the world, be it Gaeng Phed red curry or ‘entrecôte au poivre’. There's a palpable generosity to the place too, with the food and wine both offering great value for money.

Name: Lita
Address: 7-9 Paddington Street, Marylebone, London, W1U 5QH, United Kingdom
Description: Cooking with fire is all the rage these days and Lita, which opened in 2024, is another expert practitioner, although it also offers so much more. While there’s a strong Mediterranean and southern European element to the menu, prime British ingredients – such as Scottish langoustines and Norfolk quail – along with big, bold flavours and well-made sauces really make the dishes sing. Many of the plates are designed for sharing, like succulent Cornish lamb with smoked aubergine and sheep’s milk. This is roll-up-your-sleeves sort of food – the type that leaves you licking your lips and planning your return.

Name: Gorse
Address: 186-188 Kings Road, Cardiff, CF11 9DF, United Kingdom
Description: You get a good feeling about this intimate, personally run restaurant from the moment you arrive and are greeted by the chefs in the open kitchen. Go for the longer of the tasting menus and you won’t regret your decision, as local chef Tom and his team show a great understanding of flavour and balance across dishes founded upon the bountiful Welsh larder – from seaweed and seafood to Gower salt marsh lamb. The service is genial and unobtrusive, perfectly befitting of such an impressive operation.

Name: Elements
Address: 19 New Kirk Road, Bearsden, Glasgow City, G61 3SJ, United Kingdom
FacilitiesAndServices: Counter dining,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Wheelchair access
Description: A smart neighbourhood restaurant in a very smart neighbourhood, Elements occupies a swish, lavishly renovated premises blending royal blue fabrics with dark wood and gold furnishings. The kitchen applies classical techniques to top-quality Scottish ingredients, while incorporating some subtle international influences – West Coast langoustines combined with chawanmushi and vadouvan is a prime example. Each dish delivers an interesting range of flavours and textures, without ever being too showy in its makeup. The on-display wine is a nod to the well-stocked list featuring something for every palate and purse.

Name: AVERY
Address: 54 Saint Stephen Street, Edinburgh, EH3 5AL, United Kingdom
Description: When American chef Rodney Wages visited Edinburgh on holiday, he fell in love with the city so much that he decided to move himself, his family and his restaurant here. And that's how Avery, which once graced the streets of San Francisco, came to be located in a classic Georgian townhouse in Stockbridge. Rodney has wholly embraced his Scottish surroundings, taking the country's bountiful produce and treating it with a Californian lightness, while providing bold, distinct flavours – like Orkney scallop dressed with pineapple jus. The drinks flight combines wine, sake, sherry and, of course, a wee single malt whisky.

Name: La Maison d'Avignon
Description: Once the sommelier at Petit Amour on Spritzenplatz, Mathias Mercier has now realised his dream and opened his own restaurant just a short distance away. In a relaxed setting, diners are offered a small à la carte selection; if they wish, they can create a small set menu comprising three to six courses from the individual dishes. Alternatively, they can opt for the nine-course tasting menu – the value for money is excellent. The cuisine clearly draws on the chef-patron's southern French roots, featuring delicacies such as fougasse with a superb anchoïade (anchovy sauce) and pralines infused with lavender or pastis. A standout dish is the sea bass with peach, verbena and navy beans. The wine list includes some rare gems at reasonable prices. Friendly and attentive service.

Name: Dallmayr Bar & Grill
Description: Located next to the delicatessen on the ground floor, this Dallmayr restaurant is steeped in tradition and offers a lively and relaxed, yet stylish dining experience. At closely spaced tables, diners enjoy prompt and adept service provided by a courteous and well-staffed front-of-house team in white uniforms. From oysters and caviar to seafood and Bavarian ribeye with balsamic pearl-glazed onions, the international menu certainly whets the appetite. Be sure to sample the beef tomato with feta, honey and sesame. The bar is another highlight, perfect for unwinding with a pre-dinner drink.

Name: Waldschlössle
Description: After driving past seemingly endless rows of vines, you will eventually reach this small vineyard, where a traditional mountain inn has been reimagined as a trendy and modern dining destination. Floor-to-ceiling windows showcase breathtaking panoramic views of the region. There is also a terrace. "Fine Swabian cuisine" is the name of the game at this restaurant, which is run by a young couple – Annika Braun presides front-of-house and her husband, Manuel, is the chef. He mainly uses locally sourced ingredients, following the seasonal availability of produce, and also likes to incorporate elements of other cuisines. The menu includes dishes such as vitello forello (medium-rare boiled veal, smoked trout cream, Fellbach verjus) and Brunnenhof Mäusdorf rooster with crispy skin accompanied by a sour vegetable chutney, artichoke purée and polenta sticks.

Name: Ziegler
Description: It is well worth making the trip to Jacqueline and Alexander Hahn's restaurant in the Hohensachsen neighbourhood, where you will be rewarded with a pleasant atmosphere and really good food. Not only is the quality spot-on, but there is also an impressive array of dishes, ranging from classic options like Zwiebelrostbraten or Wiener schnitzel to international offerings such as Kashmir curry soup or beef fillet tataki. Food is served in an upscale, tastefully modern setting featuring clean lines and soothing tones.

Name: NIGHTINGALE
Description: Having spent years in the bustling metropolis of Bangkok, Dominik and May Carqueville are bringing a slice of the Far East to Dachau. Born and raised in Thailand, the chef has an innate talent for working with authentic Thai flavours. She skilfully incorporates contemporary influences and locally-sourced ingredients into the traditional cuisine of her homeland. Using only the freshest ingredients, she crafts dishes such as Ma Hor (caramelised minced pork with peanuts, pineapple, coriander and chilli) or pan-seared sea bass fillet in a choo chee curry sauce with kaffir lime leaves. Dishes can also be ordered to share. The trendy and chic setting is a combination of restaurant and bar – the latter serves cocktails, beer, wine and house-made soft drinks, as well as finger food. The name "Nightingale" is a nod to Bangkok's vibrant nightlife.

Name: Landgasthof zum Kaffelstein
Description: Having already proven his talent at Kuno 1408 in Würzburg, Daniel Schröder has now struck out alone here with a dual concept: In addition to fine dining at La Boucherie, you can look forward to delicious seasonal cuisine in this lovely alternative. The menu is pared down to a limited number of dishes that focus on the essentials, leaving nothing to chance in terms of expression and flavour. In summer, the terrace in the courtyard is a pleasant place to sit. The hotel also has spruce, modern guestrooms.

Name: Die Speiserei im Maier
Description: The restaurant at Hotel Maier, a family-run establishment since its founding as a café and guesthouse in 1936, showcases fresh seasonal produce that is for the most part organic and sourced as locally as possible. Order à la carte or opt for one of three set menus (one of them is vegetarian), each comprising three to four courses. The setting is inviting: the original traditional character of the interior has been preserved with the addition of subtle elegant and modern touches. There is also a spacious courtyard terrace for those who prefer to dine al fresco. Friendly and professional service.

Name: au lac 51
Description: The location on the promenade is fabulous – in summer, tables on the terrace overlooking the lake are in great demand! But you can also take in the vista from indoors – the window seats here are popular, too. The owners of this cosy modern restaurant, Dieter Maiwert and Frank Heppner, are a well-established team with a strong reputation on the culinary scene. Featuring a diverse range of options, from classic favourites to Mediterranean and Asian-inspired dishes, the menu has something for everyone. Friendly and adept service.

Name: Tiny Lou's
Address: 789 Ponce De Leon Ave. NE, Atlanta, 30306, USA
Description: Named for the popular 1950s dancer in the Clermont Motor Hotel’s “Gypsy Room,” Tiny Lou's is tucked inside the hip Hotel Clermont. Look for the pink neon sign, then descend the stairs to the trendy space set with a moody tone and French vibes. French classics mingle with American comfort food on a menu that showcases Georgian ingredients and a bit of Southern style. The cooking is approachable and earnest, as in wild striped bass with skin that's been crisped to perfection. Served with asparagus, it's the kind of plate where every component is well-executed. The desserts are also a must, with varied takes of the crépe cake and blondie always on the menu, and others always changing. If that means you need to order a few, then so be it.

Name: The Deer and the Dove
Description: Chef/owner Terry Koval and his talented team create memorable dishes at this restaurant with a lovely, rustic feel. First up? House-made salted yeast rolls, served hot alongside garden herb butter, then the harvest plate with a beautiful display of vegetables, that's perfect for sharing. House-made pappardelle tossed with morels, whipped lemon ricotta and parmesan is an elevated dish of comfort, while the smoked duck hits the spot. Crisply skinned duck served alongside duck leg pâté en croûte with Hudson Valley foie gras and a glossy duck bone jus is just right. Cocktails are especially fun, as in the "There's Always Money in the Banana Stand," with Horyzon koji rice spirit, house banana liqueur, house orgeat and tiki bitters.

Name: Delbar
Address: 870 Inman Village Pkwy. NE, Atlanta, 30307, USA
Description: This Middle Eastern spot from Fares Kargar is all about bringing people together over flavorful and authentic food. There is a generous spirit here, where the name translates to "heart, captured." The menu, a nod to the dishes Kargar grew up with, is designed for sharing, with spreads and small bites to start, an entire section dedicated to tahdig, that festive Persian crispy rice dish, and meats. Add the dill labneh to the house bread opener, then go for the lamb neck that is falling-off-the-bone tender, and sabzi polo, a basmati rice dish flavored with scallions and herbs and topped with crispy onions. Conclude the evening with a decadent treat like baklava ice cream or pistachio lava cake with cardamom ice cream.

Name: Woo Nam Jeong
Description: Anchoring the corner of a shopping center along Buford Highway, this busy spot features an expansive Korean menu. With so many options, it may be difficult to pick just one but start with a seafood or kimchi pancake or their seared mandu and you won't go wrong. Then, plenty of specialties tempt but you're here for one in particular: the house specialty "stone bowl" bibimbap. Take a peek at the neighboring tables and nearly everyone is tucking into one of these signature dishes. Bulgogi, or tender beef, is the classic order, and it arrives in the stone bowl sizzling long after it is set atop the table. Rice that has been crisped sits at the base, with beef, vegetables, and a sunny side up egg on top for a delicious one-pot dish that will make you a regular in no time.

Name: Marcel
Address: 1170 Howell Mill Rd. NW, Atlanta, 30318, USA
Description: Here on the west side of town, take a step back in time at this vintage steakhouse named for French boxer, Marcel Cerdan. From the low lighting to the red leather banquette, Ford Fry has created a speakeasy-style space that checks all the boxes. It comes with a high price tag, certainly, but who cares when you're having this much fun? The menu features a few French and European elements in addition to classic dishes. Start with a salad or go big with steak tartare with bone marrow and sourdough. The many steaks include a bone-in côte de boeuf or 60-day dry-aged ribeye. Don't skimp on the sides with French leanings, including pommes aligot and pommes Dauphinoise. Keep things decadent through dessert with a slice of rich chocolate cake.

Name: Han Il Kwan
Description: Located on Buford Highway in Doraville, the setting stands out with its standalone structure and pagoda roof. The large dining area is bright and well maintained, and offers a variety of seating areas including a section with tabletop grills. Tiled flooring, wood furnishings and a beamed roof produce a pleasant arena.The menu covers the delights of Korean cuisine, from appetizers like haemul-pajeon, the crispy pancake studded with vegetables and seafood; to stimulating stews like the kimchi jjigae served bubbling hot with strips of pork belly and cubes of soft tofu. And then there's barbecue, with an array of sliced and marinated certified Angus beef on offer; or one can choose the vegetable platter option. Come hungry or bring a crowd.

Name: Hen Mother Cookhouse
Address: 11705 Jones Bridge Rd., Johns Creek, 30005, USA
Description: Located up in Johns Creek, Hen Mother Cookhouse has a setting that befits its name. This charmer has kitschy farmhouse down pat with blue walls, white-painted bench seating, and wood tables, while Chef/owner Soraya Khoury's menu of breakfast and brunch favorites has exactly what you want. From avocado toast and quiche to Southern classics like sourdough waffles with fried chicken, if you want (and you most certainly do), mornings are met with a bevy of delicious choices, but it doesn't end there. Come lunch and BLTs, burgers, and baked goods are the perfect order. No matter your selection, it's all prepared with skill and care, and you'll have a hard time putting down your fork (though the portions are generous, and sides are shareable).

Name: Nàdair
Description: From the pops of plaid and the jade-green painted wood panels to the rugs inspired by the tartan worn by the chef's grandfather in the Scottish Royal Regiment during World War I, there is no mistaking the inspiration behind Chef Kevin Gillespie's restaurant. It's a tribute to his heritage in more than just looks, though. The Scottish-leaning, contemporary menu (prix fixe or a multicourse tasting) is at once clever and approachable. Smoked sweet Georgia shrimp, clams and mussels in a butter and shellfish foam with crumbled oatcakes is just one of the successful dishes. A round of Stornoway white pudding topped with a single roasted Maine scallop is bold yet balanced. To finish, the “Tipsy Laird” trifle is straightforward yet simply fantastic.

Name: The Chastain
Address: 4320 Powers Ferry Rd. NW, Atlanta, 30342, USA
Description: Set on the verdant edges of Chastain Park and surrounded by trees, this restaurant feels like a modern oasis with charming details (think butterscotch leather booths, exposed brick elements and gas lamps). The setting is stunning, reminding one of a restored carriage house, but Chef Christopher Grossman's seasonally focused American menu with Southern nods is a solid match.  Wondering what to order? You won't go wrong with the beer-battered Dover Sole with sauce gribiche and arugula fennel salad. Mac and cheese is a perfect side, and don't skip dessert, especially the apple-pecan frangipane tart with orange blossom cream.

Name: Food Terminal
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Chef/owner Amy Wong's Food Terminal may have multiple locations, but the Buford Highway original will always stand out from the rest. Located within a cavernous space that sports a contemporary feel (think exposed ducts, charcoal-gray walls and metal chairs), it's designed to resemble a night market. As for the food, it's Malaysian at its core. The massive menu is matched only by the portions, perfect for enjoying family style. It's a celebration of the cultural mash-up that is Malaysia with dishes like garlic noodles, made in house and tossed in a garlic sauce with spinach and mushrooms. It's so good it's nearly impossible to put your chopsticks down. Fried curry chicken nasi lemak features their take on the classic dish.

Name: LanZhou Ramen
Description: Located on Buford Highway in a busy shopping center, LanZhou is both the name of a Chinese city and a type of hand-pulled noodle that just so happens to be this spot's main attraction. Those delicious noodles are available in hearty soups with a variety of proteins, and also come broth-less. From there, broad Sichuan-leaning dishes tempt diners. Fried pot stickers sport a beautiful crispy, lacy base and delight with a savory goodness. Roast duck hand-pulled noodle soup is pure, unadulterated satisfaction, slurp by glorious slurp. Served in a massive bowl bobbing with bouncy noodles, baby bok choy, roast bone-in duck and scallions, it's loaded with flavor and will certainly cure whatever ails you.

Name: Chai Pani
Address: 406 W. Ponce De Leon Ave., Decatur, 30030, USA
Description: Decatur's Chai Pani is a festive place, where strings of lights and colorful artwork keep things high spirited, and the kitchen looks to locally sourced ingredients to create the seasonally minded South Asian dishes. The versatile menu is detailed with enticing descriptions that may just to convince you to try one more dish, and there are plenty of options for family-style dining. Whether dining a deux or with a group, enjoy the likes of butter chicken, that deliciously rich staple of boneless chicken in a tomato-cream butter sauce, or fried okra, with its ever so easy to eat lightly seasoned shards. Gobi pepper fry, a popular hybrid Chinese and Indian dish, is given a unique slant here with battered cauliflower that's both tart and spicy.

Name: Lyla Lila
Description: It bears repeating that Chef/owner Craig Richards' Lyla Lila is a good find. Sharing a contemporary design with a darker, moody color palette, the focus is on southern Europe with pasta as a focal point. They're a must, with house house staples like the crispy duck lasagna with a cocoa béchamel as well as seasonal dishes like the ricotta-miso gnocchetti. They're also available in appetizer portions, though their starters deserve equal billing. Don't fill up too much, as there's roast chicken, veal Milanese or snapper topped with pistachio pesto to be had. End on a sweet note with chocolate orange mousse cake or an ice cream sandwich with cherry gelato, "magic shell" and pizzelle cookies.

Name: Xi'an Gourmet House
Description: You won't get a lot of fuss at this Midtown spot, an offshoot of the original in Duluth. You'll order at the counter and then pick up a paper plate, but what they may lack in niceties, they make up for with dialed-in cooking. Spotlighting the Xi'an region of China, the menu focuses on biang biang noodles and as well as boiled dumplings and dishes featuring plenty of cumin and other spices. Noodles are the way to go, though it’s never a bad idea to supplement with the boldly flavorful cucumber salad, and there must be dumplings, of course. Here, they are available on their own or with soup. Choose from pork and lamb and then tuck in to a baker's dozen of simply boiled treats served with a house-made dipping sauce that brings them alive.

Name: Miller Union
Description: Miller Union is named after the former Miller Union Stockyards that once encompassed a full city block in the old meatpacking district. Nestled within the refurbished warehouse on the former site, the restaurant from Steven Satterfield and Neal McCarthy is a perennial favorite. It's likely because of their seasonal American menu with a Southern twang. Start with the roasted oysters, a plate of six delicate oysters with green garlic cream, strawberry sofrito and breadcrumbs. Then tuck in to a roasted pork loin served with two scallion Johnny cakes, braised chard and roasted carrot and radish that's bested with a rhubarb chutney. It's tempting to fill up, but save room for dessert, especially the blondie, topped with apricot and orange compote and rum raisin ice cream.

Name: Gunshow
Address: 924 Garrett St., Ste. C, Atlanta, 30316, USA
Description: It's almost a decade in, but this spot from Top Chef contestant Chef Kevin Gillespie is firing on all cylinders. It's fun and lively, making it ideal for groups, while the multicourse menu served family-style gives the place a dinner party vibe.
