The cooking here is experimental and creative—you'll always discover something new.A mini tart filled with green garlic and strawberry, then topped with radicchio whipped cream and strawberry pop rocks shows off an ingenious sweet-savory blend and is proof positive that this meal is far from standard. Melting-off-the-bone pork ribs with a tamarind and rose glaze are tangy and tender, while a scoop of salted grapefruit sorbet on a Camembert cheese foam with parsnip olive oil cake is another inventive twist.

Name: Little Sparrow
Address: 1198 Howell Mill Rd. NW, Atlanta, 30318, USA
Description: We'll forgive you if you're looking through rose-colored glasses after a meal here. After all, Little Sparrow was singer Édith Piaf's nickname, and this très French bistro hits all the right notes from its design to its dishes. The menu, though compact, features all the favorites albeit with a little Southern flair. Meals begin with a warm baguette and delicious butter before moving on to a fragrant and hearty onion soup and beef tartare. Entrées run the gamut from pork belly to chicken schnitzel with a mound of seasonal greens. Of course, there must be fries, and these house-made delights are thick cut and triple fried, accompanied by aïoli, Bearnaise sauce, or Raclette cheese service. End with a traditional chocolate soufflé or opt for a unique soft serve sundae.

Name: The General Muir
Address: 1540 Avenue Pl., Ste. B-230, Atlanta, 30329, USA
Description: The General Muir is a looker; light filled and clean with a comfortable retro-chic style. The walls are adorned with black-and-white photos from another era—yet another reminder that this style of food has a deep history. Both a market and a sit-down restaurant, it's the kind of place you'd see every few blocks in New York but not as often in Atlanta. Come as you are for a bowl of matzoh ball soup with its flavorful broth that cures all ails. The Lower East Side platter comprises a bagel, a schmear of cream cheese and thin shavings of that inimitable smoked Nova with its unmistakably buttery texture. Finally, if the cases lined with cakes didn't tempt you already, don't miss the oh-so-classically creamy and rich cheesecake.

Name: Ticonderoga Club
Address: 99 Krog St. NE, Ste. W, Atlanta, 30307, USA
Description: This restaurant from Chef David Bies is located in the Krog Street Market. There's a slight tropical vibe, evidenced by the multicolored lights and vintage, mismatched stools at the bar. It's a contemporary menu split between house classics and seasonal dishes, and most are designed for sharing. Creative but uncomplicated with global touches throughout, the cooking draws a loyal following. Steak tartare is a classic, and a good beginning before moving on to mussels steamed in a flavorful sake broth. Go smaller with a plate of wok vegetables or go big with a bone-in pork chop with a pan gravy and roasted vegetables. If the tiki vibe wasn't a tip-off, there are enough rum-based cocktails here to keep any sailor happy.

Name: The Alden
Description: Warm, attentive service and a sexy, upscale dining room make The Alden a natural choice for a night out. It's the kind of place where plush leather banquettes invite guests to linger a bit longer. Atlanta native Chef Jared Huck is running the show, and his vision internationally inspired cooking is unique. Some dishes might not read regional, but local ingredients and flair ensure pride of place. Case in point? The deliciously gamey knobs of lamb bathed in a white gravy with pink peppercorns. Hot and sour red snapper is Asian inspired but locally sourced, resulting in an elegant but approachable dish. Finish with ruby red grapefruit curd over tandoori shortbread crumbs sided by a scoop of vanilla gelato with beet-hibiscus sauce.

Name: Nam Phuong
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus
Description: Chef/owner Du Nguyen and co-owner Hoa Phan have created a welcoming spot at Nam Phuong, located in a shopping center on Buford Highway, but comfortable booths aside, all eyes are on the large menu. Staples like vermicelli noodles and fried rice are on offer, and you'll never go wrong with a bowl of pho (try pho gâu, which bobs with tender brisket and bouncy noodles). However, it's the Vietnamese street food section that demands attention with treats like bôt chiên, pan-fried rice flour cubes with egg and a sweet soy dipping sauce. No matter your selection, the dishes take some time to come out of the kitchen, since they're not cutting any corners. Come with a group, as family-style menus are designed for up to ten, sample a wide variety and offer great value.

Name: The White Bull
Description: Chef Pasquale Pascarella has created a contemporary space in the heart of Decatur. There are subtle nods to Ernest Hemingway, who famously said the blank page was his "white bull," though this is far from a theme park. This New American, seasonally minded menu has an array of small dishes, house-made pastas and main dishes, all displaying subtle and thoughtful cooking. From churning their own butter to milling their own flour, they take extra steps to ensure freshness. Kick things off with mahi crudo, then tuck in to tortelli in a butter sauce with roasted corn, fresnos, pickled enoki and parmesan. Finally, a fresh peach hand pie with lemon buttermilk gelato seals the deal.

Name: Snackboxe Bistro
Address: 1960 Day Dr. NW, Ste. 1000, Duluth, 30096, USA
Description: Chef/owner Thip Athakhanh may have moved to the United States as a toddler, but her roots in western Laos come shining through at Snackboxe Bistro. The broad menu also overlaps with Thai and Vietnamese cuisine for a likeable selection of dishes that come piled so high you'll have leftovers for days (hint: bring a friend or three). Plates to not miss include wings coated in a funky-sweet jeow bong sauce with just a hint of spice, and nam khao, a classic crispy rice salad, that is a riot of flavors and textures. Made with fermented pork sausage, herbs, onions and peanuts with fish sauce, lime, rice vinegar and sugar, it's positively delicious. End on a sweet note with a slice of coconut cake or fried donuts with condensed milk.

Name: Home Grown
Description: Located in the Reynoldstown neighborhood in East Atlanta, Home Grown is a classic all-day breakfast and lunch spot complete with knotty pine paneling and booth seating. While it has a retro feel to it, don't assume you know everything on this menu. Instead, expect oodles of Southern charm and definitely ask about the daily specials, since you may come across items like house-made tamales, Gulf red snapper tacos, lasagna or even a pu pu platter with frog legs and crab claws. The focused menu stays largely local in both theme and sourcing, delivering country cooking that never disappoints. Case in point? That open-faced buttermilk biscuit layered with perfectly crisp chicken drowned in hearty pork sausage gravy, of course.

Name: Kamayan ATL
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus
Description: You'll see the sign, but the crowd out front will signal that you've arrived at Kamayan ATL. Once a pop-up, this place from owners Mia Orino and Carlo Gan has a serious fan base, so reservations are a must. The tables are tight but it's homey, and the busy cadence, coupled with the tropical island decor, adds to the vibe.  Tagalog for "by hand," kamayan is the traditional Filipino form of dining. Choose from a menu of family-style dishes, with a good dose of classics mixed with regional items. Lumpia are always a hit, while the sinigang, with tender pork ribs bobbing in a tamarind-based broth, is spot on. Sided by rice, it's a feast unto itself. Halo halo is on offer, but most of the items are packaged from local Filipino bakery, Hapag.

Name: Tomo
Address: 3630 Peachtree Rd. NE, Ste. 140, Atlanta, 30326, USA
Description: This spot, at the bottom of the chic and modern Ritz-Carlton Residences, is a contemporary space where floor-to-ceiling windows make a big impression. In addition to tables and a sushi bar, there are four seats reserved exclusively for the omakase, arranged well in advance of your visit. Slightly Americanized, the chef's tasting menu offers eight plated courses before progressing into sushi. One dish, chu-toro nuta, presents three pieces of lightly seared tuna in a miso and rice vinegar sauce, balsamic reduction, crumbled pistachio and seared scallions for a rich and satisfying plate. Sushi, such as the decadent and flavorful kawahagi, is equally impressive.

Name: BoccaLupo
Description: What's not to love about a place that doesn't take itself too seriously yet cares deeply about their food? Chef/owner Bruce Logue is at the helm of this cute and casual spot  where smart cooking and modern takes on Italian-American classics lure a steady stream of regulars. It's comfort food at its best (think Southern fried chicken parm with pasta and creamy collards). Order a la carte or tuck in to a four-course tasting menu, with pasta tagging along on the savory courses. Fresh, local produce stars in many of the dishes like garganelli pasta with seared scallops and sugar snap peas in a tomato water sauce. Quirky cocktails, such as "What are you, the police?" are conversation starters (it's a gin-based milk punch clarified with Greek yogurt).

Name: Storico Fresco Alimentari
Description: Located in a chic Buckhead shopping center, the vibe is rustic and convivial. The generously sized dining room boasts cement flooring, metal-framed wood seating and open shelving, while the ample sidewalk seating provides an al fresco perch to enjoy a sbagliato or espresso martini. Pasta is the thing here with a concise offering of house-made strands, as well as stuffed and baked preparations. The cacio e pepe is a nicely portioned mound of spaghetti alla chitarra tossed with a creamy pecorino cheese sauce hit with coarse-ground toasted Sarawak peppercorn. The lunch menu offers appetizers, salads, pasta and focaccia sandwiches; while dinner drops the sandwiches and adds secondi like fried lemon-rosemary brined chicken with smoked mozzarella and spicy broccoli rabe.

Name: Kimball House
Description: Tufted leather booths, a carved bar and dark wood set a swanky tone at Kimball House, an elegant spot located in a renovated rail depot. It's the place to sip well-crafted cocktails and snack on more than 20 types of oysters (tasting notes make it easy to choose). Beef tartare with sweet-onion jalapeño chips, capers and green olives, crisp garlic and a confit egg yolk is excellent. Grouper crudo is prepared with a tomatillo and pineapple "agrodolce," for a very refreshing dish. Dessert is always a highlight. Butternut crunch cake is layer upon layer of deliciousness, with brown butter-almond sponge cake, butternut squash mousse, hickory foam, and ginger-thyme ice cream. Paris Brest is bested with hickory roasted pineapple, ginger ganache and cashew praline.

Name: Twisted Soul Cookhouse & Pours
Address: 1133 Huff Rd. NW, Ste. D, Atlanta, 30318, USA
Description: Grab a seat at the bar, a free-standing table or slide into one of the banquettes for a taste of local chef Deborah VanTrece's Southern and soul food. Just don't expect your grandmama's cooking. Instead, Southern staples are showcased in unique ways. Try the spread sampler with pimento cheese fondue, black-eyed pea salsa and a creamy collard dip. Other starters include crawfish deviled eggs and fried green tomatoes, served with a drizzle of their comeback sauce and a corn and pepper relish. Fried chicken is always a good choice, especially when served with three-cheese mac and cheese and a collard green roll with sweet potato, apple and golden raisin chutney. Don't skip the peach cobbler, served piping hot in a Mason jar.

Name: Georgia Boy
Address: 1043 Ponce de Leon Ave. NE, Atlanta, 30306, USA
Description: You don't just walk in off the street to Georgia Boy. First, it's secreted away within Southern Belle. Then, if you're one of the diners with reservations, you'll be seated in the "library" for drinks, snacks and a hint of what's to come. Find the chef's favorite book on the shelf and voila!, a secret door opens, revealing an open kitchen. Here, Chef Joey Ward orchestrates a delicate harmony of flavors and textures in dishes such as seared diver scallop bathed in a chocolate-dark truffle and sunchoke sauce or roasted monkfish wrapped in Tennessee country ham over a spring pea raviolo and farm egg. Other courses honor seasonal ingredients, as in a silky Vidalia onion soup. Desserts, like the "lick the beater" with German chocolate cake-flavored pudding, ramp up the fun.

Name: Southern Belle
Address: 1043 Ponce de Leon Ave. NE, Atlanta, 30306, USA
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Wheelchair access
Description: Southern Belle isn't just this restaurant's name—it's a description. It's oh-so-charming here, where a neon blue "Bless Your Heart" sign anchors the bar. It's also a showcase of Southern-inflected food, thanks to Chef Joey Ward and the passionate team who dole our creative dishes like gazpacho with strawberry relish and a goat milk feta foam. Seasons are played up with local vegetables taking center stage, and each course is better than the next. Roasted lamb loin is braised for hours before hitting the grill, resulting in a tender and delicious meal. Wine pairings are terrific, but the non-alcoholic pairings are a nice alternative. Don't miss the Georgia olive oil cake with lime curd and spring pea ice cream, if it's available.

Name: Poor Hendrix
Address: 2371 Hosea L. Williams Dr. SE, Bldg. 2, Atlanta, 30317, USA
Description: While it looks like your average corner restaurant, Poor Hendrix is so much more. It's all about the vibe at this intimate, slightly quirky spot. It’s first come first serve, and the menu changes daily with new specials that you'll want to check out (seared trout over couscous, perhaps?). Expect contemporary, updated bar food with Southern and Asian elements. Don't expect a fuss, since they don't take themselves too seriously. You'll feast on dishes like shrimp skewers dusted with a barbecue rub and served with a white Alabama-style barbecue sauce, and refreshing cold spicy peanut noodles with just the right kick. Even their cocktails hit the spot and fit perfectly at the bar, in the dining room or on their back patio.

Name: Talat Market
Address: 112 Ormond St. SE, Ste. A, Atlanta, 30315, USA
Description: Located in the Summerhill neighborhood, Talat Market is equal parts industrial and vintage, with colorful design elements adding a decorate punch. This trendy no-reservations spot from Chefs/owners Parnass Savang and Rod Lassiter is all about traditional Thai flavors, utilizing the best of Georgia produce, and the bar echoes that ethos. The menu begins with a section devoted to oysters and crudo, then progresses into small plates like crispy rice salad and som tum. Yum phonlamai is a refreshing fruit salad tossed with sesame dressing—perfect for chasing the spicier dishes. Other plates like gaaeng kiew wan, a crab and pork curry, deliver subtle flavors, and curries, many using house-pressed coconut milk, are always a good idea.

Name: B7
Description: Be sure to book ahead at this homely neighbourhood restaurant,which has an experienced chef at its helm. The room has a pleasingly simple rusticity, and the atmosphere and service have a laid-back feel, with the owner both cooking for and serving the guests himself. Pick from around 16 dishes – sharing 4 between two diners is a great way to sample a range of flavours – or simply choose the tasting menu. The flavoursome modern cuisine takes its influences from around the globe, ranging from Cantabrian anchovies to salmon ceviche; desserts are a highlight and the wine list offers great value.

Name: Entresol
Description: Set on the ground floor of a grand city centre property, this small restaurant offers two experiences in one. The front area is filled with memorabilia and has more of a vintage lounge feel, while the raised area behind has a less-cluttered look. The good value tasting menu changes twice a year and offers a selection of modern dishes with a pleasingly unfussy approach, allowing the flavours of the excellent quality produce to shine.

Name: Chef's Corner
Description: A friendly team welcome you into this chic city centre brasserie, where you’ll do well to start with a cocktail while choosing from the classic brasserie-style menu. The emphasis is on steaks from the Netherlands, the UK and the USA, with the steaks to share proving a popular choice. Other options include everything from tartares and oysters to burgers and pastas, which are hit with locals and visitors alike.

Name: MO
Description: Beside the promenade in the historical canal area sits Julianna’s Courtyard, where the 19C printing house and later 20C factories have been lovingly restored to create one of Liepāja's go-to areas. Here you’ll find MO, which offers a satisfying meal out at a fair price. Ask for a table either on or overlooking the terrace, then choose from the wide-ranging menu that includes tartares, carpaccios, sharing plates and main dishes such as beef with truffle mash. Locally produced beers and cocktails make the perfect accompaniment.

Name: TAURO
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining,Interesting wine list,Wheelchair access
Description: This über-smart steak restaurant is secreted away on the ground floor of the Zunda Towers skyscraper and comes with cowhides mounted to look like bulls, hence the name. Forgo starters and enjoy a generous plate of cured meats and salamis from their farm, then move on to a superb steak from Latvia, Spain, California, Japan or Australia. Accompany this with a side – the crispy potatoes with thyme are a must – and one of their freshly made sauces in myriad flavours. The 300+ bin wine list is beautifully curated, with some of the North American classics creating the perfect pairings.

Name: Pavāru māja
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus
Description: A former maternity hospital on the edge of a rural village plays host to this smart, modern restaurant. Here, you are encouraged to relax in their lovely nature observation garden – a place to sit back, listen and watch – before taking time to really savour your meal. Their raised beds and foraging trips provide the kitchen with vegetables and herbs, while the rest of their produce is locally sourced. The 4 course lunch and 8 course dinner are informed by what’s fresh and available each day.

Name: Akustika
Description: Set on the ground floor of the well-known Post and Telegraph building, this faux-industrial neighbourhood bistro was created by three friends and designed as a place they themselves would like to dine. Tasty, modern dishes are informed by the seasons, with local produce taking the lead, be it pikeperch from nearby Lake Burtnieks or locally reared lamb, while the Latvian char is a real hit. Be sure to ask the team for their advice when it comes to both the food and the wine. Occasional music performances add to the appeal, as does the terrace in the warmer weather.

Name: COD
Description: Make for the sultry basement bar for a cocktail or two before heading back up to the atmospheric ground floor restaurant with its dim lighting and on-trend soundtrack. The chefs here might be Latvian, but the cuisine is contemporary Japanese. Start with a selection of sushi and tempura, then choose something from the robata grill. The gyoza ‘of the day’ is a must, the black cod with sweet miso is a hit, and the mochi ice cream is the perfect way to finish. There’s a vibrancy and freshness to the cooking, yet it still respects the fundamentals of Japanese cuisine.

Name: 3 Chefs
Address: Torņa iela 4, Jekaba Arcade 2b, Riga, 1050, Latvia
Description: Located in Jacob’s Barracks – a restored 18C building overlooking the Powder Tower and Swedish Gate – this restaurant lives up to exactly what you might expect. It’s run by three chefs – who help serve the dishes and love chatting with their guests – and the menu sticks with the traditional theme by offering classical flavour combinations, albeit updated with touches of creativity and a little refinement. The tasting menu is the best route to having a great all-round experience, and they hold cookery classes for those who like to get hands-on.

Name: LOWINE
Description: Naturally, wine leads the way at this snug bar located on the very edge of the city. Inside it has a rustic look and a laid-back feel, and on warmer days you can sit outside in the enclosed rear courtyard. The appealing, keenly priced wine list keeps natural wines to the fore and changes weekly, providing plenty of interest for the regulars. Similarly, the menu also lists something for everyone, from the traditional to the modern, with an extensive brunch menu offered earlier in the day and the likes of salmon with ponzu sauce followed by entrecôte with herb cream in the evening.

Name: Kest
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Wheelchair access
Description: The town’s former fire station is now home to a restaurant which provides an experience of two parts. You start in the bright restaurant, where you dine from a 5 course tasting menu made up of modern dishes which keep local produce to the fore – and this is accompanied by an interesting alcoholic drinks flight which also includes cocktails. After dessert, you head through to the dark, moody lounge for the second part of your night: a coffee and time spent over a relaxing post-meal drink. The team really do run the place with genuine warmth.

Name: Ferma
Description: Sit inside at the chef’s table for a view of the chefs hard at work, or outside on the large terrace to take in views of the city’s oldest park. Chef-Owner Māris’ dishes reflect his love of native produce, with local beef and seafood to the fore, especially herring. The à la carte menu is concise and supplemented by a great value option at lunch, and friendly service completes the picture.

Name: Seasons
Description: The luxurious Grand Palace Hotel plays host to this sumptuous restaurant, as well as a supremely comfortable bar which comes packed with antiques and fine art – be sure to either start or end your night here. The seasonal dishes showcase Latvian produce where possible and are themed around the world’s greatest painters. If you spot it on the menu, the wonderful lightly smoked trout with bearnaise sauce is a joy to eat, while the toffee pudding with buttermilk sorbet is a must. The wine list contains some premium bottles, while the plush bedrooms provide a chance for you to sample more than one.

Name: Barents
Description: An early 20C art nouveau property on the edge of town plays host to this spacious restaurant with a large front terrace and a distinct Nordic style. The seasonally changing menu comprises modern dishes that are made up of numerous elements and combine many flavours and textures in great harmony. Seafood is a strength – with some sourced from the Barents Sea – and the produce is displayed on ice in the middle of the room and explained to diners as they arrive. The champagne selection provides a noteworthy accompaniment.

Name: Whitehouse
Address: Vermane Park, Terbatas iela 2, Riga, 1050, Latvia
Description: The former Biblioteka – which was something of an institution – reopened in 2020 as Whitehouse, and its dining terrace remains one of the most sought-after in the city thanks to its views over the colourful flower displays of Vērmanes Garden. It’s a sizeable place, with a long, narrow room, stylish décor and even a living wall. The menu blends modern European influences with subtle Asian touches, and there’s a touch of theatre to the presentation. Desserts are a highlight, as are the signature cocktails, and the place really comes into its own in the evening.

Name: JOHN
Description: Set within the striking A22 hotel, this chic restaurant overlooking the historic Viesturdārzs park is named after John F Kennedy, who stayed here back in 1939; be sure to keep an eye out for some of the original art nouveau features, which have been carefully restored. The room now has a romantic feel, helped along by a ceiling bedecked in roses, and the menu is modern too, with a diverse selection of dishes highlighting seasonal local produce, from Arctic char to locally farmed ostrich. The King crab with lemon aioli and pickled apples is a hit, as is the delicious honey cake.

Name: Barents Cocktail & Seafood Bar
Description: It’s worth booking in advance for this hidden gem – not only is it compact, but it also acts as the cocktail bar for next door Barents. Seasonal drinks are joined by a concise menu; the seafood platter is a feast for the eyes, but don’t overlook the delicious 'small bites' which change with the seasons. The fish burger is a hit and, if you see the rum soaked baba for dessert, be sure to order it. Naturally, you should start and end with some cocktails from their thoughtfully curated selection.

Name: Neiburgs
Description: The crowds thin out as you wind your way down the cobbled streets of the Old Town and find yourself in this peaceful spot. Located on the ground floor of a boutique hotel, this restaurant is the place to dine if you’re looking for a smart environment but with a pleasingly unpretentious atmosphere; there’s also a lovely terrace for warmer days. The menus offer fresh, unfussy dishes with some Mediterranean influences, and the seafood options are particularly appealing. The crab and tiger prawn ravioli with bisque sauce is a real winner, while the herring dishes are always a popular choice.

Name: ZOLTNERS
Description: You'll find the Zoltners Brewery in the heart of the glorious Zemgale countryside, along with this slick, modern restaurant and an attractively restored period house that’s now a small hotel boasting modern bedrooms; make a weekend of it by dining, staying the night and visiting the Tērvete Nature Park. Menus showcase local produce in an appealing mix of flavoursome northern European dishes, and the simple starters go perfectly with their home-brewed beers and local spirits.

Name: Tails
Description: There’s a choice of two bistro-style dining rooms at Tails, but the raw bar counter really is the place to sit to make the most of the experience. The chefs take fish seriously here by adopting a tail to gill approach – and there’s even a drying room on show. They cure their own fish, make their own ceviches, and their sharing shellfish platter is something to linger over. Keep an eye out for the daily specials too, which often feature something a little different. For the ultimate indulgence, accompany your meal with a bottle of champagne.

Name: Stage 22
Description: Set on the top floor of the Grand Hotel Kempinski Riga, this sumptuous restaurant affords superb views out over the park and the city skyline. Start with a drink in the chic cocktail bar or out on the lovely narrow terrace, then settle into plush chairs to enjoy your evening. This is an ideal place for celebrating and you will be looked after with consummate ease by the professional team. The wide-ranging Asian menu includes the likes of spicy tuna roll and Argentinian beef fillet with shallot cream, while the crispy vegetable tempura with dashi sauce is not to be missed.

Name: BABO
Description: Opened in the summer of 2024, BABO is currently something of a lesser-known gem. Set up by a pair of experienced restaurateurs, it’s split between two rooms and a smart terrace. One of the owners hails from Georgia and it’s this that informs the menu. Delicious breads are cooked in the pizza oven and the charcoal grill adds a lovely flavour to the various meats and fish. Order 2 dishes each and share – maybe beef and pork khinkali (dumplings), salmon in bazhe (walnut) sauce or chicken tabaka with salt and lemon. The superb wine list showcases a great mix of classic and modern Georgian wines.

Name: H.E. Vanadziņš
Description: You’ll find plenty of locals here, from the serving team to the regular guests, which creates a welcoming vibe and a convivial feel. The lengthy menus cover all bases, from flavour-packed soups and salads to delicious flatbreads and hearty mains inspired by northern Latvian cuisine. There’s a lovely terrace hidden to the rear that's worth seeking out, and bedrooms are available should you wish to stay the night.

Name: Riviera
Description: This large restaurant has a warm Mediterranean style and a menu to match, offering an appealing selection of dishes from oysters and tartares to fish and steaks, followed by old favourites like tiramisu. Everything is generously sized, with well-defined flavours and textures, and the sizeable wine list (1,000+) offers some great choices from around the globe. There’s a choice of two rooms in which to dine, but the terrace is the place to be when the weather’s right.

Name: Le Dome
Description: Tucked away down the cobbled streets of the Old Town is a 400-year-old building which is home to both a boutique hotel and this intimate restaurant. Black and white photos of Riga adorn the walls of the long, narrow dining room, while in summer the operation relocates to the rooftop terrace which overlooks the Daugava River. Menus are modern and creative, with subtle international influences in evidence. The prime ingredients originate mostly from the Baltic region and Barents Sea, with Mother Nature leading the evolution of the dishes throughout the year.

Name: 36.Line
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Great view,Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Beachside locations don’t come much better than this, as you can walk straight in off the sand. Those after some respite from the sun can stay inside, while those wanting to feel the sea breeze should head for the glass-fronted terrace. The accessible menu covers all options, from lighter sushi and tartares to dumplings and hearty grilled fish and meat dishes. The tiramisu laced with the famous Black Balsam – their national drink – is a must-try, and the extensive selection of wines and cocktails is perfect for watching the sun go down.

Name: Les Ateliers
Description: After having been deserted for some 25 years, this former stainless-steel workshop just behind the railway station has been revived by Jean-Sébastien Ribette and Sahondra Verdan (formerly of Auberge de la Veveyse). An off-kilter, smart industrial vibe sets the scene for a choice of culinary options: brasserie fare to the fore, or more ambitious (and surprise) set menus in the gourmet section. Market availability dictates the menu, hence the freshness of the ingredients. For example, scallops, roasted and tartare, with pumpkin and cloves, roast monkfish in cider butter with textured vegetables, perfectly roasted Bresse pigeon with apple molasses.

Name: Apollo
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Wheelchair access
Description: The name is a nod to the owners' deep-seated interest in NASA's famous programme. The space theme is also evoked through the elegant, dark interior, adorned with reprints of original photos from various missions, accompanied by captivating descriptions. Complementing the setting perfectly is the small open "satellite kitchen", where chef Thomas Huber and sous-chef Sergiu Midori prepare two set menus, one of which is vegetarian. Their predominantly Mediterranean-style dishes are always modern and creative, occasionally incorporating international influences, such as pike-perch, mussel broth, fermented fennel and sherry, or Davos Wagyu, pointed pepper, green beans and Roscoff onions. The restaurant is located in Hotel Grischa, which offers plenty of comfortable accommodation options.

Name: Artis by Tristan Brandt
Description: Under the patronage of Tristan Brandt, head chef Fabian Saalfeld and his team present an array of ambitious dishes. They draw together strands of both classic and regional cuisine in equal measure, also incorporating Asian influences here and there, for example in their aromatic slices of raw scallop with a spicy jalapeño cream and slivers of green apple, served with a clear broth boasting strong umami flavours. Choose between a three- to five-course surprise menu and the à la carte offer. The restaurant is located in Hotel Prätschli, which stands in a quiet location above the village, not far from the ski slope.

Name: Osteria Del Centro
Description: This small, very friendly restaurant offers a successful mix of tradition (the setting is an old house in the centre of Comano), minimalist furnishings and modern cuisine. In the evening, enjoy a surprise tasting menu (five or seven courses) which is almost entirely vegetarian, with the option of choosing your main course. 95% of the ingredients are organic and the owner-chef will be happy to discuss his philosophy on organic food during the course of your meal. The elegant, original dishes include options such as beef wellington with kohlrabi, chimichurri and mushrooms, accompanied by artisanal wines from Switzerland and further afield.

Name: il tiramisù
Description: This restaurant is near the centre but slightly tucked away – it goes without saying that it is a joy to sit on the terrace overlooking the River Murg. The atmosphere is friendly, the service attentive. In the open kitchen, the team meticulously prepares seasonal Italian dishes that are flavoursome and fun! It is definitely worth trying the pasta dishes, smaller portions of which are also available as a starter. Of course, the dessert after which the restaurant is named features on the menu. In the evening, order à la carte or opt for a surprise menu comprising three to four courses. Tip: moderately priced set menu at lunchtime.

Name: Le Jardinier
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Credit cards not accepted,Great view,Terrace,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: This restaurant on the first floor of The Woodward hotel is a magical place, boasting an unobstructed view of the lake from its terrace, and promising attentive service and fresh, harmonious dishes. At the helm is Alain Verzeroli, who, along with chef Olivier Jean, has created a delicious culinary offering that espouses nature, the seasons and the ingredients. And, true to the name (meaning "gardener"), they give plants pride of place. Tasting menu or à la carte choice, plus a wide selection of vegetarian and/or gluten-free dishes. The restaurant also serves an exceptional breakfast and afternoon tea.

Name: SACHI
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining,Credit cards not accepted,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: The luxurious Mandarin Oriental hotel complex houses this restaurant presided over by chef Mitsu – a former disciple of master chef Nobu Matsuhisa, who has earned his spurs in the world of Japanese fine dining. In a resolutely contemporary setting, he serves set menus rife with delicious modern marriages of flavours, plus a fine selection of sushi. You might like to sample these at the counter of Omakase Bar, as you watch the master at work. Alternatively, head for the terrace alongside the Rhône.

Name: L'Écorce
Description: In this convivial, tastefully furnished restaurant in Carouge’s old town the chef conjures up fresh, aromatic cuisine that combines classic and modern dishes such as mi-cuit tuna with a beetroot and watermelon bouillon and raw and cooked vegetables. Charming service, plus a small summer terrace.

Name: Bären
Description: In this old 17C inn, a passion for gastronomy is shared with diners! Owner Christian Mutschler is always on hand, recommending and serving, but also sharing stories about the eventful history of the place. The no-frills food is tasty, and most of the ingredients come from the region. The game dishes are definitely worth trying – made with game hunted by the owner, they could hardly be fresher or more seasonal. At lunchtime, meanwhile, the menu is significantly pared down. The wine list is also dominated by Swiss labels, and there are plenty of good bottles to choose from. Be sure to make the most of the terrace and the great view it offers!

Name: Zermatt Kitchen
Description: A trendy and casual dining concept split between two buildings: Brücke and Ascot. There are a variety of options on offer: breakfast (until 4pm), house-made pastries – their freshly baked croissants are very popular – and the menu of the day featuring international fare (until 6pm). In the evening, Brücke becomes "Zermatt Pho" and serves Vietnamese cuisine. In nearby Ascot, a more multifaceted and modern take on international cuisine is served at dinnertime. Here, there is a spacious terrace with a lounge area. The central location is another draw – the Matter Visper River flows right past Brücke. Incidentally, the coffee comes from the establishment's own roastery in Zermatt.

Name: Café des Banques
Description: In the banking district, this chic and contemporary bistro is the latest venture for Yoann Caloué. Here, the MICHELIN-starred chef serves confident modern cuisine, made with high-quality fresh ingredients to exacting standards. The desserts are also meticulously prepared, cf. his lemon tart, basil sorbet and limoncello sabayon. Those curious to see the chefs at work can sit at the counter facing the kitchen. Business lunch menu (without options). A very appealing restaurant.

Name: Osteria San Gallo
Description: This pleasingly animated little osteria is located at the start of the pedestrian precinct, with the terrace area laid out in front of the entrance. The attractive interior is comfortable, with simple bistro chairs, wooden tables and the activity in the kitchen visible to diners. Authentic Italian dishes are served by an ambitious team – try, for example, the agnolotti piemontesi (handmade dumplings filled with veal).

Name: La Croix d'Or
Description: In the centre of the peaceful village of Ballaigues, not far from the French border, this restaurant is housed in a magnificent historical building. Two French chefs, David Sauvignet and Damien Lanza, run the show with professionalism and a passion for good food. Their ambitious take on seasonal French cuisine is full of finesse and infused with subtle Mediterranean influences. Pretty terrace.

Name: Afghan Anar
Description: Take advantage of the rather rare opportunity to discover Afghan cuisine! Here you can sample some of the country's most popular dishes, such as bolani, kabuli pulao or baklava. The atmosphere is laid back and down to earth, which is in part down to the open kitchen and authentic decor. As an alternative to the conventional tables and chairs, you have the option to dine on traditional mats.

Name: Bergwelt - BG's Grill Restaurant
Description: Modern chic with an Alpine touch: Done out in warm tones, with lovely parquet flooring, striking designer lamps and an open kitchen complete with an impressive barbecue, this restaurant – part of the equally attractive Bergwelt Grindelwald hotel – has a truly unique atmosphere. The cuisine has a Mediterranean feel but also draws inspiration from the region. The menu is full of tempting dishes, such as the butter-soft octopus starter. For meat lovers, the fragrant, golden-brown Wiener schnitzel is sure to whet the appetite, and the same goes for the top-quality signature cuts from the barbecue. There are plenty of options for vegetarians, too. The well-curated wine list predominantly features Swiss and French labels.

Name: Zum Löwen
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Having first worked as sous-chef here, then as head chef, Jonas Ingold now represents the seventh generation of his family at the helm of this picture-perfect establishment, whose charm and atmosphere could not be more inviting. Near the entrance, the bar displays bottles from the wine list (ideal for an aperitif or digestif) and, just next to the bar is the open kitchen. In an attractive interior with a modernised rustic feel, an ambitious tasting menu is served both at lunchtime and in the evening – a vegetarian version is also available. The à la carte selection features simpler options that are nonetheless excellent. Many of the ingredients are sourced from the region. Attentive service is provided by friendly waitstaff. The terraces are delightful in summer.

Name: Mapo
Description: Mapo is run by Emmanuelle and Paul, a talented couple who have opened this refreshing restaurant that breaks with the city’s more traditional dining options. A concise yet mouth-watering menu, meticulously prepared dishes teeming with energy and freshness, and all at a moderate price. A favourite haunt where a delightful experience is guaranteed.

Name: Les Montagnards - Brasserie
Description: Fine dining is not the only option! Hotel Les Montagnards offers a culinary experience that goes beyond its renowned restaurant Le Sommet. The Brasserie can hold its own! The attractive modern interior featuring warm wood and sleek design is as much of a draw as the friendly service and, last but not least, the good cuisine. Here, the focus is on the region and the changing seasons. One of the house specialities, for example, is stuffed morels with a cream sauce. The pike-perch, fished from local lakes, is another popular choice. Tip: Try to get a window seat, then you can take in the view of Gruyères Castle and the surrounding area while you eat!

Name: Izumi
FacilitiesAndServices: Interesting wine list,Notable sake list,Terrace,Valet parking
Description: The atmosphere is truly international: top-notch ingredients go into a fusion cuisine of Japanese and other Asian influences. Perhaps you will be tempted by the Wagyu beef gyoza with a spicy ponzu sauce, or the izumi rolls? The lively atmosphere and chic, modern look of this restaurant on the seventh floor of the Four Seasons Hotel are just as much of a draw as the food. Don't miss the rooftop terrace, one floor up, with its breath-taking view over Geneva, the mountains and the lake. Make a reservation without delay!

Name: Helvetia
Description: With the arrival of Svenja and Adrian Nessensohn (both previously employed at Lampart's in Hägendorf), Helvetia has gained two dedicated and friendly hosts who keep abreast of the latest culinary trends. They are also committed to a sustainable approach and the use of locally sourced ingredients. Some of the meat is even provided by the chef's brother, who runs his own farm. Get comfortable in this pretty restaurant, where a relaxed atmosphere reigns, and savour an appealing set menu with dishes designed to be shared – also available in a vegetarian version by prior arrangement. In summer, make a beeline for the gorgeous terrace. The restaurant is also open at lunchtime on Thursdays – the set menu is shorter but also includes vegetarian options.

Name: Tredecim by Monika Jans und Thomas Huber
Description: Thomas Huber (the 13th generation) and Monika Jans are dedicated to their work in the Krone, an establishment steeped in history. While she is responsible for the cordial and professional service, he takes care of things in the kitchen, preparing seasonal, traditional dishes. They will also prepare a creatively inspired set menu if you order in advance. The cheese trolley selection is fantastic! The wood-panelled interior exudes charm and contributes to the delightful atmosphere. Should you wish to stay overnight, there are attractive individually decorated guestrooms.

Name: Beaufort
Description: This small restaurant is located in the Marina Fallenbach clubhouse, on the outskirts of Brunnen. The place has a lovely friendly atmosphere, refined decor and beautiful views of the marina, lake and mountains, not to mention a wonderful terrace! Their modern and cosmopolitan cuisine is made with good, fresh seasonal produce. In addition to à la carte dishes, there is also a three- to five-course seasonal set menu. Inexpensive lunch menu.

Name: Madre Nostra
Description: Classic Italian cooking is served in the charming restaurant of the modern hotel CERVO Mountain Resort, which is located a little above the village and right next to the slopes. The produce and flavour are the main focus here. At lunchtime, they offer a limited selection from the evening menu, as well as highlights from the establishment's other restaurants. The terrace is impressive!

Name: Loy Fah
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Great view,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus
Description: This chic restaurant on the fourth floor of the tasteful Panorama Resort & Spa boasts a stunning panoramic view over Lake Zurich. Inside, you are served by an extremely friendly and attentive team. The food is a modern take on authentic Thai cuisine, which is also adapted to European palates in terms of spiciness. You can put together your own menu.

Name: L'instinct
Description: Chic and relaxed, this restaurant delights the taste buds with its French-Mediterranean dishes and grilled meats (matured in the display case that was hewn directly out of the stone between the bar and the kitchen). They also like to perpetuate the tradition of serving flambé dishes, lit in the dining area, as well as classic dishes (still recommended!). In keeping with the terrace surrounded by vines, the wine list has a thousand references. Insider tip: come with at least two people and opt for the set menu.

Name: La Muña
Description: In this elegant and contemporary-style setting, the friendly waitstaff serve food that is an interesting fusion of Peruvian and Asian cuisine. Housed in Schweizerhof hotel, this restaurant is only open on winter evenings, offering a choice between raw (crudo) and hot (caliente) dishes – the ceviche comes highly recommended. Don't miss out on the desserts either! Incidentally, la muña is the name of a medicinal plant in the Andes.

Name: Buffet de la Gare
Description: An old-fashioned restaurant of the type that is quite hard to find these days. It has Art Deco-style wood panelling, enamel plaques and coloured windows, as well as a terrace overlooking the surrounding greenery. There is also a traditional feel to the menu, which includes perch from Lake Geneva.

Name: Schloss Binningen
FacilitiesAndServices: Garden or park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: This stylishly furnished restaurant housed in an attractive 13C castle serves contemporary international cuisine with Mediterranean and Asian influences. At lunchtime choose between the "Business Lunch" deal and the four-course "Sorpresa" set menu; in the evening, they serve a four- to six-course "Emozione" tasting menu – or you can dine à la carte, which includes a vegetarian alternative. Under the direction of the dedicated sommelier, the service is friendly and proficient. In summer, the terrace is inviting. The hotel area beautifully combines modern and historical features. Tip: There is covered parking next door; if you prefer to get here by tram, line 10 stops right by the castle grounds. The narrow River Birsig also flows past here.

Name: Ristorante della Stazione
Description: There’s a change of guard at this Ticino dining institution where young couple Eloa Geiser and Yanick Walker have taken over the running of both the kitchen and front of house service. Eloa, the charming female half of the partnership, is also a qualified sommelier and takes very good care of her guests, while Yanick, adds his classic-French culinary stamp without neglecting his Valois roots, although he is not averse to adding some Mediterranean flair to his cuisine. In addition to its usual menu, on Tuesdays guests can order the “Stazione” veal liver, and on Saturdays the special braised beef with Merlot. The gracious building housing the restaurant with its beautiful views remains unchanged, as do the comfortable guestrooms.

Name: Brasserie du Poisson
Description: This contemporary brasserie close to the lake offers unpretentious cuisine. Fish has the starring role (tuna tartare, perch fillets), as well as hearty traditional recipes such as croûte aux morilles (with morel mushrooms) and veal cutlets. A real treat for the taste buds, particularly as everything (including the bread and ice cream) is homemade.

Name: EMOTIONS by Guy Ravet
Description: The classic elegance of the Grand Hôtel du Lac, designed by architect Ernest Burnat, is the perfect setting for Chef Guy Ravet's ambitious cuisine. The finest ingredients are used with mastery and skill, as in the case of the fillet of wild turbot, seared, with cauliflower mousseline, red onion and mustard seed condiment and beurre blanc with chives.

Name: Aroleid Restaurant
Description: Located right by the ski slopes just above Furi gondola station, this restaurant is housed in a modern and stylish chalet that exudes rustic charm. As well as stunning views, diners can look forward to a diverse menu of delicious dishes inspired by the chef's international travels. Incidentally, the coffee comes from the hotel's own roastery and the crockery is also made in-house. For those who don't mind the long walk, it's a 1.5hour hike from Zermatt to the restaurant.

Name: Zwyssighaus
FacilitiesAndServices: Great view,Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: This charming 18C restaurant named after the composer of the Swiss national anthem enjoys a fine location and a view of Lake Lucerne. Wood sets the tone inside, while outside you'll find two wonderful terraces – one on the balcony. A modern take on classic cuisine is served in the form of a three- to six-course menu, accompanied by a decent wine list. For overnight stays there are four simple yet cosy guestrooms.

Name: Repas
FacilitiesAndServices: Great view,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Fancy a delicious meal above the rooftops of Biel? On the sixth floor of the Hotel Elite, in this central location near the railway station, you get a great view of the city and the Jura. The atmosphere is unpretentious, the service is friendly and the cuisine is contemporary, with regional and Mediterranean influences. If you're coming as a group, order a few of the finger food dishes ("Amuse") to share.

Name: Da Adriano
Description: As a true Italian, maître d' Adriano Feraco, after whom this ristorante in a side wing of the Grand Hotel des Bains Kempinski is named, treats diners to an authentic experience. In an attractive setting (here, elaborate moulding, herringbone parquet flooring and pretty details such as wine racks and the unique-looking service station are sure to draw the eye), dedicated and charming waitstaff serve typically Italian cuisine including mouth-watering options such as spaghetti with clams or "duo of lamb".

Name: Römerhof
Description: This beautiful building, the origins of which date back to the 16C, is run with dedication by Dominique and Gerald Bergue-Hunziker. Classic and international dishes are served in an elegant setting – the coffered ceiling is striking. In the evening, there is a choice of two set menus (one of which is vegetarian), each comprising three to six courses, and an à la carte menu. At lunchtime there is a shorter menu including a reasonably priced set menu. You can also relax in the cigar lounge or the pretty salons. Cosy and charming guestrooms are available in the hotel of the same name.

Name: Gasthaus am Brunnen
Description: The picturesque Gasthaus am Brunnen sits in the centre of this Graubünden mountain village. Locals meeting for lunch or a drink favour the rustic dining room, while the smart, minimalist-style restaurant is more elegant. The food is modern and uses exclusively local produce. Try the veal tenderloin cooked on a rock salt slab and served with herb caviar, mustard and garlic risotto and vegetables. The female chef's desserts are delicious.

Name: Ilge
Description: This restaurant is housed in an old half-timbered building in the heart of this idyllic little town. The interior design is chic and tasteful, and in fine weather there is a lovely terrace overlooking the pedestrian zone. Serbian-born Zoran Baratovic presides in the kitchen, turning out dishes that draw on classical and Mediterranean influences. We highly recommend the mouthwatering veal shank ravioli. And to accompany your meal, the attentive maitre d', who is always on hand, will provide you with a well-curated wine list that includes one or two interesting magnums.

Name: Guarda Val
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Great view,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: In the fine dining restaurant of the wonderfully located Maiensäss Hotel Guarda Val, the rustic charm of a 300-year-old cow byre meets modern simplicity. Service comes courtesy of a friendly and experienced team. When it comes to the food, the spotlight is shone on regional specialties. The two set menus (one is vegetarian) and the à la carte dishes are made almost exclusively from Swiss produce. At lunchtime, the offer is somewhat simpler – there is a three-course lunch menu, as well as à la carte dishes.

Name: Villa am See by Sandro Lüthi
Description: Housed in a beautifully located villa, this restaurant has been run with great dedication by young couple Sandro Lüthi (kitchen) and Paulina Soares (service), along with their friendly little team, since spring 2024. They propose two set menus, one of which is vegetarian, plus an à la carte selection. They also serve a "Business Lunch" in the winter season. The cuisine is contemporary, seasonal and ingredient-led – predominantly French and Mediterranean in style, complemented by international twists and a healthy dose of creativity. A pleasantly relaxed atmosphere awaits in the modern and elegant interior. But it's the terrace, separated from the lake by a mere strip of greenery, that is the jewel in the crown! Including an enclosed, glass-walled pavilion offering a cosy retreat on chilly days.

Name: noumi
Description: The restaurant in the basement of the venerable grand hotel Bellevue Palace (Switzerland's official accommodation for foreign dignitaries) used to be Bern's mint – the name is a derivation of "numismatics". The atmosphere is cosmopolitan, chic and relaxed (the resident DJ plays in the evening). In the open kitchen, the chefs prepare "world food" incorporating influences from Asia, Peru and the Mediterranean. The dishes are made with excellent ingredients and are also suitable for sharing. Competent and laid back in their approach, the waitstaff provide recommendations from the selection of fine wines and interesting cocktails.

Name: Weinlaube
Description: Countrified and charming, congenial and friendly! This former farmhouse in a quiet little hamlet not far from the border with the Vorarlberg region offers cosy Stube-style dining rooms and a beautiful outdoor terrace. The menu here features unfussy cuisine with a focus on classic, regional, seasonal and international dishes and the occasional use of the smoker.

Name: Fiskebar
Description: A Nordic enclave at the Ritz Carlton in Geneva, Fiskebar has made a name for itself thanks to its delightful fish- and seafood-based cuisine. The finest ingredients are sourced via short supply chains and skilfully prepared by an expert kitchen team. Diners are treated to fresh and healthy Scandinavian cuisine, enhanced with subtle Mediterranean touches – smoking and fermentation techniques are also put to good use. In a setting that tastefully combines rustic materials with more modern touches, diners take their seats at tables that look onto the open kitchen or afford a view of the lake. On top of that, the wine list abounds with pleasing discoveries, including a range of biodynamic wines.

Name: Le 1913
Description: This elegant restaurant, complete with a terrace commanding a knockout panoramic view of the mountains and valley, is located in the recently refurbished Villars Palace. The ambitious, structured cuisine combines regional and Mediterranean dishes in four- or six-course set menus. The creativity of the "Gambero Rosso", for example, a carpaccio of red prawns contrasted with a perfectly presented dill sorbet, is a case in point. The open kitchen means you can see Christian Bertogna's team at work!

Name: Auberge de la Couronne
Description: Housed in a tastefully renovated traditional edifice, the Auberge de la Couronne morphs from a simple bistro at lunchtime into a fine dining gourmet establishment in the evenings. Generosity and indulgence are the order of the day in dishes such as crisp golden roasted sweetbread served with fresh crayfish and crunchy glazed mini vegetables. The front-of-house team is on hand to help you find the perfect food-wine pairing as you take a seat in the handsome vaulted dining room.

Name: Millennium - La Brasserie
Description: Set in the prestigious Millenium complex, a state-of-the-art business and conference centre, the elegant La Brasserie is under the expert supervision of Fabien Foare. This is the go-to place for a business lunch. A pared-down, less expensive lunchtime menu gives way to more ambitious fare in the evening, with a choice between "Les Inspirations", dishes created to reflect the seasons (cooked and raw Puits d'Amour melon), and "Les Incontournables" such as free-range guinea fowl supreme or fillets of perch from Lake Geneva). Not to mention the trolleys laden with charcuterie and pastries, which will have your mouth watering from the aperitif right through to dessert! The gourmet grocery shop is open in the afternoons.

Name: Esprit par Guy Ravet
Description: The setting by Lake Geneva is truly outstanding and, in the summer, the terrace becomes a standout feature courtesy of its jaw-dropping view! The restaurant is housed in the luxurious Grand Hôtel du Lac, which dates back to 1868. The sleek polished interior, extended by a bright, airy conservatory, is fully equal to the location, as is the food. The menu by executive chef Guy Ravet is seasonal and based on regional produce. The wine list demonstrates a weakness for Lavaux wines. Unobtrusive, slick service.

Name: Schloss Wartegg
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: The elevated location between Lake Constance and the Alpstein is quite something! As in the small castle hotel, the focus in the restaurant, too, is on the organic and ecological. This translates into sustainably produced ingredients and organic produce from local suppliers, plus vegetables and herbs from the hotel's own 2 500m2garden. From the terrace there is a wonderful view of the countryside and Lake Constance.

Name: Le Roc
Description: The restaurant of the Hôtel de Rougemont serves classic French cuisine with a contemporary twist. The house-smoked salmon, green asparagus in breadcrumbs, salsa verde emulsion and citrus fruits makes a lasting impression… enjoyed in a delightful Alpine interior, tastefully decorated (old wood, light-coloured banquettes and seats, modern lighting), or on the terrace, with views of the mountains.

Name: Haberbüni
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Terrace
Description: The atmosphere here is one of a kind! Housed in the airy hayloft of a 19C farmhouse with rustic beams, this place has a special feel to it. The tasteful interior is complemented by a secluded garden terrace with trees and shrubs. The food is fresh and made with high-quality ingredients. In the evening, there is a set menu and an à la carte selection. The latter is also available at lunchtime, supplemented by daily specials and a "Business Lunch" option. Excellent wine list featuring plenty of rarities and magnums.

Name: Principe Leopoldo
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Terrace
Description: Situated in a panoramic and picturesque location outside the town centre, Principe Leopoldo is the gourmet restaurant of a classic-style hotel with an intimate ambience. Take a seat on the veranda with its stunning views of the lake and mountains or make yourself comfortable in the elegant dining room in winter. The cuisine here is based on solid traditional technique and is prepared from seasonal local and Mediterranean ingredients, with an equal balance of meat and fish dishes. The wine list has something for all tastes, including a selection of memorable vintages.

Name: Eden - Belle Époque
Description: At the restaurant of the Hotel Eden Spiez, diners can savour classic cuisine that showcases regional and seasonal produce including homegrown fruit and berries. The hotel also has its own herb garden. Take in stunning views of Spiez Castle, Spiez Bay and the imposing mountains from the stylishly elegant interior or the covered terrace – both spaces are equally delightful. A shorter menu is available at lunchtime.

Name: Panorama
Description: The name says it all! The location at an altitude of over 1 000m makes for a fantastic panoramic view of the surrounding mountains – it would be a crime not to enjoy it from the terrace in summer. The Rindisbachers have been running their establishment since 1985 already, serving food influenced by tradition, made with quality ingredients and paired with good wines. The pasta is manufactured in their own workshop. Panoteca sells delicatessen wares.

Name: Montalbano by Mirko Rainer
Address: via Montalbano 48, San Pietro di Stabio, 6854, Switzerland
Description: Situated on the hill of the same name, this charming, recently renovated restaurant with an attractive veranda and terrace for summer dining has reopened under a new owner who is already well known in the region. The menu features delicious options such as the “cold” spaghetti with raw seafood, pistachios and oregano, as well as dishes cooked over the Big Green Egg grill. The excellent, reasonably priced set menu is announced at your table at lunchtime; in the evening, choose from a selection of exciting dishes from a personalised à la carte.

Name: Marée
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: Park Hotel Sonnenhof's wonderful location and comfortable accommodation options are not its only trump cards. The restaurant, run by chef Hubertus Real, is also in high demand. In a tastefully elegant setting, at attractively laid tables, diners are served classic cuisine made with first-rate ingredients. The friendly and attentive front-of-house team also provide expert advice on their very extensive selection of wines. The magnificent terrace also has a viewpoint – the "Adlernest" (eagle's nest) – from which you can take in the stunning view.

Name: Da Valentino
Description: Although it is the beautiful terrace that first catches the eye at this restaurant, the friendly welcome and attentive service offered by Valentino in the kitchen and Sabine front of house add to the appeal. Mediterranean specialities and traditional classic dishes feature on the menu, while an open fireplace creates a warm ambience in winter.

Name: The Omnia
FacilitiesAndServices: Great view,Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: A lift whisks you up here from the pedestrian area – to some breath-taking views! In the restaurant of the eponymous hotel, the focus lies squarely on vegetarian cuisine. Nevertheless, you have the option to supplement the dishes with fish or meat specialities. Those in the mood for a culinary adventure should opt for the "OMNIA Experience" surprise menu, which comprises four courses, complete with beverage pairings. The interior is modern and upscale, featuring clean lines and large granite-topped tables. Tip: Enjoy an aperitif by the fireplace.

Name: Tao's
Description: Tao's has you covered if you are in the mood for Euro-Asian cuisine. The wide-ranging menu includes sushi and sashimi, steak tartare, poke bowls and dim sum, plus "Signature Grill" dishes such as Thai-style fillet of sea bass, lime, herbs, ginger, soy. The dishes are accompanied by a fantastic and extensive international wine list. A pleasantly relaxed yet stylishly elegant atmosphere prevails. In summer the cosy terrace is a huge draw, and there is also a bar.

Name: Gasthaus Bären
Description: This restaurant serves flavoursome traditional cuisine made from local produce à la carte or in the form of an ambitious set menu comprising three, four or five courses. There are also appetising options for two, such as Chateaubriand. Berner Haus, which first appears in records as a tavern in 1542, makes for an enchanting setting with its charming wood-panelled interior. The lovely old turquoise tiled stove, adorned with Langenthal porcelain, provides comforting warmth in the winter months.

Name: Bianchi
Description: A slice of la dolce vita! Located right by the Limmat River, this ristorante boasts a bright and modern interior where excellent service comes courtesy of a cheerful and adept front-of-house team. Made with top-notch produce, the Mediterranean-style fish and seafood dishes here are in high demand. Gorgeous little terrace.

Name: La Bagatelle
Description: Here you can look forward to classic French cuisine made from top-notch ingredients, including an appealing selection of dishes for two. The cosy ambience created by warm wood, soft lighting and a touch of elegance is inviting. Plus they have a terrace with a stunning view. The service is charming, and there is a terrific wine list – half bottles are available, too. For an overnight stay: Hotel Le Grand Chalet has cosy rustic-style guestrooms.

Name: Stiva Veglia
Description: Situated in an idyllic little village, this lovingly restored Graubünden house dating back to 1761 is replete with Alpine charm. The interior is exceptionally pretty with its wood-panelled rooms that are welcoming and stylish in equal measure. Make a beeline for the terrace in summer. Tino Zimmermann delivers modern regional cuisine. There is a set menu of up to nine courses. A classic of the house is the "Schmauser 45-minute egg". A vegetarian menu is also available upon request. Fantastic produce such as Val Lumnezia Arctic char demonstrates a clear connection to the region. Diners are waited on by a dedicated and friendly front-of-house team, with the chefs themselves making an appearance from time to time in order to talk diners through their dishes. Tip: house-made specialities such as liqueurs, grape jelly, herb salt and lemon salt are also available to buy.

Name: Al Braciere
Address: Via Livurcio 50, Ronco sopra Ascona, 6622, Switzerland
Description: Situated just above Ascona, about 1km from the town centre, this friendly hotel boasts panoramic views of Lake Maggiore, the surrounding mountains and the island of Brissago. Enjoy modern, carefully prepared cuisine in the comfortable dining room or on the idyllic outdoor terrace in summer.

Name: FIVE
Description: Ensconced in the ski resort, with views of the Swiss mountains, elegant restaurant FIVE – part of the Guarda Golf Hotel – creates a contrast with its Levantine cuisine, which features mezze for sharing, among other dishes. Diners can also enjoy the European flavours of the desserts, including chocolate tart and fruit mousse.

Name: Jacques Restaurant
Description: Not far from the opera house is chef Jacques Allisson's "bistronomy" restaurant. His modern, creative and tasteful take on French cuisine is a hit, and the place is very popular. The atmosphere is relaxed, the service friendly and attentive. At lunchtime there is a business lunch; in the evening there are two set menus as well as à la carte dishes.

Name: Ciani
Description: A fashionable restaurant housed in the Palazzo dei Congressi, where famous chef Dario Ranza delights guests with his fresh, Mediterranean cuisine. Don’t miss the delicious risottos, including his recipe with saffron, chanterelles, courgettes and Robiolino cheese. Excellent wine selection.

Name: Esprit Ravet
Description: The Ravet family from the L’Ermitage restaurant in Vufflens-le-Château have brought their own style to Hotel Bernerhof in the centre of Gstaad, in the form of this chic brasserie, which now serves ambitious modern French Ravet-style gourmet cuisine. The service is attentive and friendly. A special feature of the brasserie is a flambé trolley.

Name: Le Cerf
Description: This century-old culinary institution is a renowned name in the region. Reinvented from top to bottom, it now serves good old unpretentious dishes in a traditional vein: for example, strips of veal from the Pays d'Enhaut, golden rösti and green salad… and let's not forget the malakoffs – fried cheese balls made with PDO cheese from the old fort in the valley – and the fondues! Cosy, rustic-style ambience, plus a superb terrace with mountain views.

Name: S.Zimmer
Description: This cosy and intimate little restaurant is run by chef Stefan Zimmermann and hostess Tünde Tamàs. A most cordial family atmosphere awaits you, as well as flavoursome cuisine, with many of the ingredients being sourced from the region. They serve a set menu of up to seven courses. The wine list in particular shows influences from Hungary – the owner's homeland – and you should certainly consider her recommendations! Although located inside the building of Hotel Viktoria Eden, the restaurant is run independently.

Name: Perroquet Vert
Description: This intimate, lively restaurant on the Place de la Fontaine exudes the Belle Epoque charm of the Parisian brasseries of old. A feel that chimes perfectly with the traditional, French dishes chalked up on the blackboard. Favourites include scallop risotto, entrecôte and tarte tatin.

Name: Les Ateliers Brasserie
Address: Rue des Deux Gares 6a, Vevey, 1800, Switzerland
Description: If you're a fan of traditional dishes with a modern twist, then this brasserie under the same roof as Les Ateliers, run by the talented pairing of Jean-Sébastien Ribette and Sahondra Verdan, is just the place for you! Market salad with orange and turmeric vinaigrette; duck confit with shredded green beans in vinaigrette; Madagascar vanilla crème brûlée… Savour cuisine that revolves around freshness and simplicity in a chic industrial-style setting. Dish of the day served at lunchtime.

Name: L'Arabesque
Description: The Arabesque’s attractive decor of gold mosaics, white leather and black lacquerware conjures up pictures of the mysterious Orient, in particular Lebanon. It provides the perfect foil for a pedigree Mediterranean lineup, including hot and cold mezzes and Kibbeh Labanieh, the chef’s signature dish of meatballs, and Samak mechoui, grilled seabass with a sesame sauce. Excellent range of vegetarian dishes.

Name: Pfändler's Gasthof zum Bären
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Steeped in over 200 years of history, this building makes for a really delightful setting: Bärenstube and Orangerie are full of charm and attention to detail. The garden is also attractive – a truly idyllic spot! The seasonal food has regional and Mediterranean influences. You will feel right at home in the pretty guestrooms.

Name: Seven
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Great view,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: The views extend from the lake to the mountains in this informal restaurant, where windows into the kitchen allow guests to watch the chefs busy at work. The menu features creatively reinterpreted, classic-style dishes, with the option of choosing between meat and fish, while the delicious bread comes from the Bottega del Gusto in Porto Ronco. At lunchtime, there’s a bistro-style menu with lighter but equally delicious options such as salads, antipasti and primi, hamburgers, club sandwiches, baked seabass and grilled Tomahawk steak. There’s also a lounge bar plus a wine bar of the same name, the latter offering an interesting array of labels (also available by the glass), as well as cocktails which are a perfect pairing for the dishes on offer. Given the restaurant’s superb location, the tables on the terrace are much sought after in summer, so it’s best to book ahead! Three luxury apartments are also available if you’d like to extend your stay here.

Name: Essort
Description: This inviting restaurant is housed in what was once the US embassy. Its interior design features a harmonious combination of clean lines, warm wood finishings and muted tones. The terrace to the rear of the building beckons in summer. In the evening, a seasonally inspired tasting menu comprising three to six courses is served, with the option to add wine pairings. At lunchtime, a shorter set menu as well as the "Business Lunch" are available.

Name: Käserei
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Wheelchair access
Description: This restaurant with a modern yet rustic feel and a cosy atmosphere is located in the former cowshed of a typical Engadin house. The restaurant still has a focus on cows and dairy products today, serving dishes such as cheese fondues, raclette, capuns and even Chinese fondue. Cheese-making demonstrations are held regularly in the evenings.

Name: Spettacolo
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: In the Lenkerhof spa resort's elegant restaurant, hotel guests can look forward to a great half-board set menu, while à la carte diners are treated to a high-quality and modern take on classic cuisine that also draws on international influences. You can put together a menu of variable length from a selection of 15 dishes. The attractive wine list includes small bottles, as well as magnums. Friendly and proficient service.

Name: Wildenmann
Description: Set in a lovely Zug house built in 1708, Wildenmann serves classic fare with menu favourites including local Zugersee Arctic char and perch. It also offers charming service, welcoming dining rooms and a lovely terrace.

Name: Pinte
Description: Set in a 19C building, Pinte offers something for everyone in its cosy dining room and comfortable restaurant. Menu offerings include ravioli with pear, Jersey Blue and walnuts and pot roast with Ticino polenta and purple carrots. Delightful terrace.

Name: LOFT FIVE
Description: This stylish restaurant stands directly on Europaallee, not far from the railway station (Hauptbahnhof). But it's not only the chic interior and relaxed atmosphere that are inviting – the food is also a definite draw! Flavoursome modern-inspired international cuisine is on the menu. The service is friendly and competent, and there is a good selection of wines and cocktails.

Name: La Place
Description: Cristina and Vincenzo De Rosa run this restaurant with passion and enthusiasm. Throughout the year they delight guests with their modern and colourful cuisine, with dishes such as lobster ravioli in a Thai red curry sauce featuring on the menu.

Name: Landhaus
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Great view,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: This 16C farmhouse is now a really charming restaurant boasting a splendid view of Lake Constance. Featuring warm wood finishings and sleek design, the decor embodies a winning combination of the old and the new. Regional cuisine is served in the cosy parlour. Reduced menu at lunchtime. In summer, make a beeline for the gorgeous terrace. There is a hall for events in the modern converted barn.

Name: Chez Vrony
Description: All the wood and pleasant decor make for a cosy, rustic atmosphere indoors, but with the spectacular view you have at 2 100m above sea level, the terrace is unsurprisingly popular too! Traditional regional cuisine is served by the charming waitstaff. Incidentally, they produce their own dried meat and sausages here.

Name: Arté al Lago
Description: Modern, impeccably presented cuisine with a Mediterranean influence and an equal emphasis on meat and fish in a restaurant whose name lives up to its promise. Interesting wine selection, including a choice of international labels.

Name: Auberge de la Veveyse - Brasserie
Description: A worthy heir to this renowned restaurant, David Tarnowski serves ambitious, refined cuisine that showcases beautifully plated classics and his own personal creations. The creamy risotto with chanterelles and Vaudois sausage deserves a special mention. The pared-back setting is filled with light. Fair prices at lunchtime; bistro vibes in the second space.

Name: Rössli
Description: The first-floor dining area of this 16C half-timbered house is a really pleasant setting in which to dine: the space has a cosy, rustic atmosphere, plus a small conservatory overlooking the lake. Seasonal influences can be detected in the traditional cuisine, while the menu also features classics such as Wiener schnitzel with warm potato salad.

Name: Löwen
Description: In this cosy little restaurant in the vaulted cellar, you can look forward to the "Gourmet Menu", which is served at lunch and dinner, with the option of up to seven courses. At lunchtime, Beiz serves a set menu, as well as a choice of à la carte dishes. There is also a decent wine selection, and the front-of-house team is friendly and competent.

Name: Stapferstube da Rizzo
Description: Here at Stapferstube, a well-known Zurich eatery, Italian dishes such as tris di pasta della casa, gamberoni aglio olio peperoncino, and brasato di manzo al Barolo are a hit with diners. In this vibrant and welcoming restaurant, regulars and first-time guests alike are treated to Mediterranean hospitality and a cosy atmosphere. Their quick lunch at a reasonable price is also popular.

Name: La Grappe d'Or
Description: A restaurant where superb flavours and a friendly atmosphere go hand in hand. Chef Theotim Bioret is strongly inspired by northern Italy, from Venice to Ventimiglia: Piedmont-style agnolotti del plin, sage and a parmesan jus; calf's liver saltimbocca, spinach and polenta. In addition to the à la carte menu, the chef serves a more affordable weekly dish. Meticulous plating, precise cooking and delicious sauces combine to create a faultless dining experience.

Name: Le Maguet
Description: The Le Maguet brothers, Jonathan (serving) and Benjamin (cooking), are carrying the culinary torch of their father Olivier with their sustainable and 100% local concept! They use organic and/or wild ingredients that are of excellent quality, and draw on both traditional know-how and the most modern techniques, resulting in simple and tasty cuisine. For example, pata negra pork shoulder and salsify, slowly and perfectly cooked. Thirty years on, the dessert trolley is still the domain of their mother, Pierrette: don't leave the table without trying her tartlets!

Name: Cavigilli
Description: Combining modern features with the original wood and stone, plus cordial service and a pleasingly down-to-earth atmosphere, this charming 15C Grisons building provides a wonderful setting in which to enjoy seasonal ingredient-led cuisine. The focus is on the essentials, so the flavoursome dishes are served in pared-down combinations. Tip: Make the most of the quiet terrace in summer! There is a small and simple lunch deal.

Name: Sapori
Description: Worth a visit for its stylish historic interior alone, Sapori promises a wonderful parquet floor and an impressively high painted ceiling complete with stucco work. The Italian menu includes tasty stone-baked pizzas.

Name: Gildo's Ristorante
