Description: If you’re in the mood for some authentic, upmarket Italian food, you should try the line-caught sea bass, cime di rapa, garlic, pine nuts and peperoncino at this restaurant. Expect excellent service, plus a stylish Alpine ambience.

Name: 4 Saisons
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Wheelchair access
Description: Attractive picture windows, elegant pale wood, and a menu that takes the four seasons as its starting point, as reflected in the market-fresh ingredients. Locally grown vegetables, fish from the nearby lakes and Swiss meats are accompanied by an appealing wine list that focuses on local producers. Delight in dishes such as morel stuffed with Agria potatoes and Vully asparagus tips. Friendly service and attractive guestrooms at Hotel Cailler.

Name: Du Cheval Blanc
Description: The former chef at L'Écu, in Bulle, has turned Du Cheval Blanc into a veritable haven for foodies. In this convivial light-filled restaurant, he delights diners with his well-crafted, unfussy and straightforward take on traditional cuisine, prepared with care and served by a professional team. The real deal.

Name: Restaurant Hôtel de Ville
Description: This restaurant with a vibrant and upbeat atmosphere is run by a chef who is brimming with energy. He regales diners with delicious and indulgent cuisine that draws on local produce. Daily lunchtime menu inspired by local market fare; fine dining tasting menu in the evening. The opulent interior (a former apartment) is decorated with numerous works of art: paintings, photos, sculptures etc.

Name: La Terrasse Brasserie
FacilitiesAndServices: Great view,Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Wheelchair access
Description: Befitting the elegance that characterises the Victoria Jungfrau Grand Hotel & Spa, which is steeped in tradition, a classically refined atmosphere awaits you here. The location against the impressive backdrop of the mountains is a real draw in itself. In summer, make a beeline for the terrace on the promenade! The menu includes a broad assortment of Arab, Asian, Mediterranean and Swiss dishes – flavoursome food made from high-quality ingredients.

Name: Paradiso
Description: In good weather, you can take in breathtaking views up here at 2 181m above sea level. This down-to-earth Mountain Club restaurant appeals to diners of all ages. You can look forward to good food and a great wine selection, as well as a relaxed atmosphere, partly thanks to the music and DJs. Note: there is an entry fee for non-members. Accessible by chairlift and a short walk (10min).

Name: Verena
Description: This charming historical customs house dating back to 1786 has undergone a transformation under Dave Wälti, who previously worked in the kitchens at Eisblume in Worb and Casino Bern. The cuisine is contemporary, with vegetarian components playing a major role – but not to the complete exclusion of fish and meat. Warm wood tones and clean lines make for a lovely atmosphere, and the service comes courtesy of a friendly, laid-back and professional team.

Name: Restaurant Pony
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: A family-run restaurant, now in the third generation. In the elegant Pavillion dining room, friendly staff serve classic cuisine with Mediterranean influences, while the cosy Beizli is an inn-style room offering more everyday cooking. Pleasant terrace.

Name: First
Description: Somewhat tucked away, this delightful restaurant in the Zurich Oberland has plenty of regulars. One of its draws is the wonderful view; in good weather you can see Mount Säntis. The interior is very pleasing – some aspects are cosy and traditional, others rather more modern. In summer, make a beeline for the gorgeous terrace in front of the building. The menu changes with the seasons. Friendly and dedicated front-of-house team.

Name: Le Jardin des Alpes
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Credit cards not accepted,Garden or park,Great view,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: There’s a new chef and a new concept at this gastronomic restaurant within the walls of the Chalet RoyAlp luxury hotel & spa. In this elegant yet welcoming setting, savour dishes such as snails with herbs and a potato mousse, and fettuccine with parmesan and Alba white truffle sauce, complemented by highly professional service and an impressive wine selection. The terrace is a must in fine weather!

Name: Motto del Gallo
Description: A historic gem of a restaurant, part of a tiny hamlet of 15C houses, featuring a cool, shaded outdoor space for summer dining. Elegance and refinement are to the fore inside, enhanced by antique furniture and works of art, while the menu takes its inspiration from the local region and the Mediterranean. The Chateaubriand is an absolute must!

Name: Marktküche
Description: One tip at the outset: be sure to reserve in good time – this restaurant always gets booked up, so it's hard to get a table! The clue is in the name: the cuisine takes its cue from what the market has to offer, dispensing with meat and fish. Diners can look forward to a vegetarian surprise menu made up of four to eight courses. There is also a lunch menu available on the penultimate Friday of every month.

Name: Elisa - Bistro & Terrasse
Description: Le Tapis Rouge has been reincarnated as Elisa - Bistro & Terrasse, but the commitment to local sourcing and sustainable practices remains unchanged. This restaurant is located in the venerable Grandhotel Giessbach (built in 1875), right at the foot of the waterfalls of the same name, and boasts a wonderful view of Lake Brienz. The food is delicious, contemporary in style and primarily made using produce grown in the hotel's own 2ha vegetable garden. The other ingredients are locally sourced and from small-scale producers: fish comes from Lake Brienz, veal from a neighbouring farmer. On the menu, vegetables take centre stage, with dishes such as Giessbach agnolotti with Meiringen cream cheese and broccoli. Tip: In the evening, opt for the "Tour du Domaine" surprise menu for sharing (for two or more people).

Name: Chrüz
Description: This centrally located inn has tables in the stylish conservatory or a simpler dining room where you can tuck into traditional fare that often draws on international influences. The wide-ranging menu includes spaetzle with Sbrinz (hard cheese) and truffle, cordon bleu with Alpine cheese, "Vorässä 2.0" (beef stew with a twist) and salmon green curry. The service is friendly and attentive. Lunchtime options are more limited and moderately priced.

Name: Seebistro Belvédère
Description: The location right by the lake is superb! The modern bistro is just in front of the fine dining restaurant – the same kitchen team works at both. There is a seasonal set menu with Mediterranean influences and made with regional produce, plus a choice of classics.

Name: Oberer Mönchhof
Description: The dining rooms in this lovely, centuries-old half-timbered building are tastefully and comfortably furnished. Outside a fabulous terrace is laid out under chestnut trees overlooking the lake. The cuisine is seasonal, traditional and international with an additional tasting menu on offer at lunchtime and in the evenings.

Name: Gasthaus Höhwald
Description: In this gorgeous restaurant boasting a stunning view, the atmosphere could hardly be more welcoming. Since December 2023, a dedicated couple have been at the helm, bringing their superlative fine dining experience to the table: Mara Graef cheerily oversees the team front of house, while Thomas Graef prepares tasty seasonal dishes. His is regional cuisine for the most part, but some dishes are clearly influenced by the owners' Austrian homeland: for instance, their classic Tafelspitz (prime boiled beef), available as a Monday special. Hot meals are served throughout the day. Wonderful terrace. Tip for motorists: You can reserve a parking space in the garage.

Name: Mulania Brasserie
Description: With its combination of sleek, contemporary style and rustic ceiling beams, this old Graubünden building provides an attractive setting. Host couple Yvonne Marx and Sascha Meyer have reimagined their place as a brasserie, serving tried-and-tested regional specialities such as capuns (chard rolls) or quark pizokels (buckwheat spaetzle), plus brasserie classics like moules frites or beef bourguignon. Last but not least, there are some delicious seafood options – the chef's first love. Delightful terrace. Open from 3pm.

Name: La Soupière
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Wheelchair access
Description: This sophisticated restaurant on the first floor boasts a stylish interior and professional service. As for the menu, it offers modern variations on classic French cuisine.

Name: La Croix d'Ouchy
Description: This restaurant boasts a loyal following of regulars in Lausanne, attracted here by cuisine that features superb traditional flavours alongside a few pasta dishes with an Italian touch, in a classic setting with plenty of character. Prior booking essential.

Name: La Brasserie du Royal
Description: The Royal Savoy hotel was one of the favoured haunts of the Spanish court. The brasserie’s culinary focus is highly enticing menu that features dishes such as pâté royal en croûte, goose foie gras, and a mousseline of crayfish from Lake Geneva, as well as seasonal recipes such as hare à la Royale. A truly chic experience!

Name: Vieux-Bois
Address: Avenue de la Paix 12, Geneva, 1202, Switzerland
Description: Just behind the United Nations, this 18C building houses Geneva's hotel management school (EHG) and its restaurant, where tradition reigns supreme. Under the expert supervision of their teachers, students prepare the meals and wait tables. The terrace is also very pleasant.

Name: Hirschen
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Classic, seasonal and regional food is the name of the game here. Guests can enjoy fine dining and vegetarian options in the Zeitgeist restaurant, as well as house classics, including the signature dish: chateaubriand. Tip: The chocolate cake with coffee is sensational! Alternatively, you can order burgers, pasta etc in the cosy Hirschenstube. Popular terrace for summer meals, plus comfortable guestrooms.

Name: Kindli
Description: A place steeped in history and full of charm – from the hotel's pretty, individually designed guestrooms to the restaurant, in which old wood panelling exudes cosiness. In a pleasant and lively atmosphere, they serve good classic cuisine in the form of dishes such as sea bass with a lemon and caper butter, or Geschnetzeltes Kalbsfilet Zürcher Art (veal strips in a mushroom and cream sauce). At lunchtime, check out the additional daily specials for a quick meal. Tip: Don't forget to make a reservation, as they always get booked up!

Name: White Elephant
Description: This restaurant in the Marriott Hotel is a must for fans of authentic Thai cuisine. Made with market fresh produce, the food is authentic and authentically spicy! Whatever you do, don’t miss the curries.

Name: Da Enzo
Address: Via Ai Grotti, Ponte Brolla, 6652, Switzerland
Description: This Ticino-style stone house boasts a sun-blessed, verdant setting and a beautiful garden-terrace. Take a seat at one of its typical granite tables, either crowned by stone vaulting or shaded by trees, where you can savour exquisite Mediterranean on several tasting menus (including vegetarian) and an à la carte that includes daily specials. Other features include a well-stocked wine cellar and two romantic rustic-style guestrooms. Open for over three decades, Dan Enzo is now run by the second generation of the family.

Name: La Coupole - Matsuhisa
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Notable sake list,Wheelchair access
Description: "Irasshaimase" – this is the exclamation with which diners are greeted here. Housed in the building that was once home to Europe's first indoor tennis courts, Nobuyuki Matsuhisa's restaurant buzzes with infectious vibrancy. The wide-ranging menu features a fusion of Japanese and Peruvian cuisines – everything is prepared in the open kitchen (there is also a sushi bar). The black cod miso is definitely worth trying.

Name: Le Bocca - Restaurant
Description: This restaurant serving mouth-watering cuisine has been taken over by Alexandre Luquet and Ana Ronc! Whether seated in the bright, elegant dining space or out on the pretty, leafy terrace, you can enjoy ambitious, contemporary French cuisine, such as the "langoustine and fresh peas" starter or the sole meunière made with fish from small-boat fishing, black garlic and braised endives, which is as tender and juicy as can be! They have a good wine cellar (including Swiss wines) that is open to visitors.

Name: Restaurant Chastè
Description: In their delightful little hotel, the Pazeller family offers not only attractive, comfortable guestrooms but also sophisticated cuisine. The restaurant combines two concepts: "Ustaria Chastè" with an upscale evening menu and a simpler lunchtime menu, and "Bocca Fina Chastè" with an evening fine dining set menu. The interior is tasteful and cosy, the service friendly and attentive.

Name: Restaurant de l'Hôtel DuPeyrou
Description: This exquisite 18C palace ticks all the boxes: elegant yet unconventional, classical yet quirky and even better, it is located right in the heart of town! You will taste the cuisine of Edmond Bavois who works with premium produce, adding an Asian spin to a classical repertory.

Name: Ornellaia
Description: Modern-inspired Italian dishes, such as carne cruda, filetto di vitello Rossini and ravioli carbonara, are prepared in kitchens that are visible from the dining area. The appealing wine list includes a selection from the famous Tuscan wine-growing estate, Ornellaia – from which the restaurant takes its name. You are waited on by a friendly team assembled around host Antonio Bordone, who puts his heart and soul into serving you. This gem of a restaurant is located in a beautifully refurbished building that was once a bank – the door even opens automatically. Sleek design meets historical-looking sandstone walls and decorative art, lending the distinctive high-ceilinged space a modern and elegant Tuscan ambience. At lunchtime there is a small selection of additional dishes.

Name: Zum Goldenen Schäfli
Description: Located in the last surviving guild house in the town (1484), this restaurant is full of charm and atmosphere with an all-wooden interior that is especially pleasing. One quirk of the Zunftstube (guild room) is its sloping floor – you might find yourself walking uphill! The cuisine is classic and seasonal, with a Mediterranean touch. Attentive service.

Name: La Sorgente
Address: portich da Sura 18, Vico Morcote, 6921, Switzerland
Description: This welcoming restaurant overlooking the lake in the charming village of Vico Morcote serves simple cuisine with a focus on local ingredients, many of which (biodynamic wines, vegetables, olive oil etc) come from the restaurant’s own farm. It’s fantastic to be able to enjoy such fresh produce at reasonable prices – make sure you try the open ravioli with a rabbit ragu, Gotthard cheese fondue and pepper. Guests are advised to leave their car at the garage at the entrance to the village and then walk the short distance to the restaurant. In summer, meals are served under a pergola on the charming terrace.

Name: Schotte-Sepp-Stube / Flickflauder
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Whether you choose to dine in the cosy Schotte-Sepp-Stube, the bright Veranda or the contemporary, minimalist-style Flickflauder, you’re guaranteed good-quality, seasonally inspired cuisine and friendly service at this restaurant, which hosts an “Appenzell evening” with a buffet every Wednesday. The à la carte is available to non-resident guests from 8pm onwards.

Name: Casa Alva
Description: This restaurant has an upscale, modern interior that beautifully incorporates original architectural features from the former parsonage in which it is housed. The cosy setting is complemented by the warmth and dedication of your hosts, creating a truly inviting atmosphere. A single set menu, "Berg & Küste" ("Mountain & Coast"), is served. Attractive guestrooms available for overnight stays.

Name: Rössli
Description: Rössli is a pleasant restaurant decorated along clean, modern lines in warm colours. Enjoy the smart place settings and friendly service led by the lady of the house and Ueli Kellenberger’s flavoursome, contemporary cuisine. The mouthwatering offerings include open ravioli with spinach, egg, parmesan and beurre noisette.

Name: Le Bistrot des Ours
Address: Route du Pas de l'Ours 41, Crans-Montana, 3963, Switzerland
Description: It's easy to feel at home in this bistro with its rustic, mountain-inspired atmosphere, complete with terrace commanding a magnificent view of the valley and the surrounding mountains. Here they serve ambitious French-Mediterranean cuisine that caters to all food lovers, courtesy of chef Franck Reynaud, who also cooks at the Michelin-starred restaurant, L'Ours. You'll want to come back for more of this delicious fare that will have your taste buds tingling!

Name: Locanda Locarnese
Description: Hidden in an alleyway, this pleasant, modern restaurant serves Mediterranean cuisine made from top-quality ingredients. Don’t miss the “Terreni alla Maggia” risotto and the chocolate dessert with a passion fruit sauce. A large fireplace adds to the cosy ambience, making diners feel as though they are guests in a private house. Friendly service.

Name: Bel Etage
Description: Lovely old parquet flooring, beautiful double doors and high ceilings with crystal chandeliers, as well as decorative art on the walls... Here on the first floor of Der Teufelhof hotel, the stylish salons of the Bel Etage blend harmoniously into the historical setting. In the kitchen, Michael Baader and his team focus on preparing classic cuisine. Diners can either order à la carte or choose between the two set menus – one with three courses, the other with six. The front-of-house team is friendly and professional, providing savvy wine recommendations – the fabulous list is very well curated and comprises 450 labels. In good weather, make a beeline for the pretty terrace and grab a table under the sun awning in the hotel's garden.

Name: Au Chat Noir
Description: In this lively, welcoming restaurant close to the theatre, guests will be tempted by delicious dishes (such as oxtail parmentier – something of a speciality here), a menu of market-inspired specials (on this particular day, a delicious cep fondant as a starter), classic and rather fine flavours. In short, Au Chat Noir is the type of bistro you'd be happy to come across more often. Be sure to book!

Name: Trübli
Description: There are plenty of reasons to stop off at this historical inn (1785) located in the heart of the old town – the cosy and relaxed atmosphere, the friendly and experienced service team, the wonderful food. In the evening, the concept is a surprise set menu comprising three courses (a vegetarian version is also available), to which you can add an extra dish and/or a dessert. The extremely dedicated chef brings a personal touch to the service, and his passion for wine is palpable, not least in his excellent recommendations drawn from the nicely curated wine list with a focus on German estates. There is a pretty terrace in front of the house. Tip for motorists: the public car park 200m away.

Name: Auberge du Prévoux
Description: This inn on the edge of a forest in the heart of the Neuchâtel mountains is well known to food-lovers, who head here to enjoy French cuisine with a focus on the very best products selected by a chef who enjoys working with lake fish and different types of game, in particular. Good value for money in the brasserie at lunchtime, with more ambitious cuisine on offer in the evening.

Name: Drei Könige
Description: This restaurant has a charming bistro feel and serves delicious food expertly prepared with fresh, carefully selected ingredients. At lunchtime, there is a set menu with options, and the atmosphere is upbeat and lively. In the evening, the pace is a little slower, and the food even more sophisticated.

Name: Gandria
Description: Chef-patron Adriano Peroncini is originally from Puglia, but his years of travelling took him through Italy and far beyond. Since 2016 he has had his own restaurant, here in Zurich's Seefeld district. In this nice, cosy space, where an inviting atmosphere reigns, he introduces diners to his fresh southern Italian-inspired cuisine – good choices from the menu include the octopus or Piedmontese Fassona beef and, of course, the delicious pasta dishes! In addition, there is an exclusively Italian wine list that covers most of the wine-growing regions, as well as "servizio alla maniera italiana" – authentic service that will make you feel at home!

Name: Bad Schauenburg
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Great view,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: Whether you're seated in the Basler Stübli, the Gaststube or the Veranda, the fine dining restaurant of Hotel Bad Schauenburg serves classic French cuisine that takes its cue from the seasons in all its lovely rooms. Some of the produce comes from the hotel's own garden. The highlight in summer is of course the delightful terrace!

Name: De la Gare - La Table des Suter
Address: Avenue de la Gare 13, Lucens, 1522, Switzerland
Description: This family-run institution housed in a large ochre-coloured building in front of Lucens train station is a real hit. This is undoubtedly down to its winning combination of professionalism and a very warm welcome. The set menus include ambitious classic French dishes made from top-quality ingredients, eg "grand cru" beef cooked two ways, with a Pinot Noir sauce, Swiss chard and stuffed parmentine potatoes. The adjacent bistro also represents excellent value for money. And if you would like to extend your stay, there are neat and practical guestrooms available.

Name: Le Monument
Description: In this welcoming and well-maintained auberge near the church in the centre of the village, the kitchen team has mastered the classics (the different tartare dishes on the menu are particularly memorable!) as highlighted in cuisine that showcases subtle Italian influences. Recommended.

Name: Rechberg 1837
Description: The Rechberg 1837 is a pleasant restaurant with a unique philosophy – it only uses regional produce that was available around 1837 (the year the house was built), i. e. before industrialisation. Innovative dishes such as slices of country pork on pea puree with fried barley and pickled onion are served in the evening, with a more traditional selection available at lunchtime. Cosy atmosphere and charming service.

Name: Brasserie Süd
Description: This place has the potential to become a mecca for foodies! Located directly in the main railway station building, this restaurant is ideal for a meal when you are waiting for a connecting train, but it also attracts business people and locals. Within an attractive historical setting (notably the high ceiling and large arched windows), diners can immerse themselves in a vibrant brasserie atmosphere, or head to the outdoor terrace overlooking Bahnhofstrasse. The cuisine is seasonal and international, and there are daily specials. Complementing the menu is an intriguing wine list highlighting French and Swiss labels and featuring a well-curated selection of wines by the glass. Adept and well-organised service. Tip: Bouillabaisse is served every Friday; brunch at weekends. For top-notch cocktails, head to Da Capo Bar.

Name: Minamo
Description: With its pared-back Far Eastern decor and an eight-course traditional Japanese omakase menu served to all diners at the same time, this restaurant brings countertop dining and a slice of Japan to the exclusive Mandarin Oriental. From your comfortable seat at the counter, you can watch, for example, various nigiri being prepared before your very eyes – the chef will gladly expound on his work and philosophy. NB: There are a maximum of eight places available, so it is essential that you book!

Name: al lago
Description: Housed in a type of winter garden with a charming terrace (the jewel in the crown!), this restaurant serves dishes that combine modern influences with more classic touches, all prepared using ingredients of the best quality. Make sure you try the risotto made from Carnaroli rice with red pepper, green sauce and Cantabrian anchovies, as well as the Guanaja chocolate mousse and ice cream with mixed berries. An excellent selection of wine and young, friendly service complete the picture.

Name: Riva
Description: Perhaps the only true fish restaurant in Ascona where fish specialities are nothing short of exceptional, but meat lovers will not be disappointed either.Situated inside the Seven Boutique Hotel, Riva offers a maritime atmosphere with colourful touches that recall the blue expanse and a tasty cuisine declined in tasting or à la carte menus, from ‘I Crudi’ with oysters & co. to ‘Sogliola alla mugnaia with lettuce, capers and spring onion’. Definitely a great address!

Name: Gourmet Louis
Description: This idyllic 13C water castle is a tranquil haven nestled just outside Basel. Surrounded by a moat, the property with its old trees can be accessed from two sides via wooden bridges. This establishment boasts two culinary concepts: a brasserie and this fine dining restaurant. Head chef Guy Wallyn, having already worked at the castle for several years, serves up classic French cuisine in the form of a four- to six-course set menu, which can be supplemented with cheeses from the trolley. To complement this, a selection of fine wines is available. Up to 20 guests can be accommodated in the lavishly renovated historical Steinsaal (or "stone hall") in the left wing of the castle – the 18C stuccowork is stunning. The small private dining space in the tower is ideal for groups. Tip: Enjoy an aperitif or coffee in the castle's courtyard.

Name: Brasserie du Château
Description: The brasserie is a wonderful addition to the gourmet restaurant ‘Louis’ on the magnificent historic castle estate. Here you can enjoy French brasserie cuisine made from fresh produce, from ‘Beef tartare classique’ and ‘Moules marnière’ to ‘Veal ragout Blanquette de Veau’ or dishes for two, such as ‘Chateaubriand’, in a classic ambience for lunch and dinner. The well-stocked and extensive wine list is the same as that of the ‘Louis’. In summer, the terrace facing the moat under shady old plane trees is an idyllic spot.

Name: Badalucci
Description: A historic restaurant with its roots in Italian cuisine. Originally from the island of Procida in southern Italy, the chef here focuses mainly on fish-based dishes, although the menu also features delicious meat options and vegetarian recipes for each course – whatever you order, seasonal ingredients are to the fore in this urban-style eatery situated slightly away from the centre. The wine list highlights the owners’ passion for champagne via highly respected labels from interesting small-scale producers.

Name: PURO
Description: The restaurant on the first floor of the Mövenpick Hotel serves interesting and ambitious cuisine. This comes in the form of a very appealing fusion concept of Asian and Latin American-inspired dishes made with plenty of regional produce, but also ingredients from around the globe. The food is down to earth, flavoursome and fresh! This is complemented by an international wine list, extremely friendly service and a stylish interior.

Name: Rosa Pulver
Description: Comprising four, five or seven courses, the "Rosa Pulver" set menu is the perfect choice for fans of modern and creative cuisine based on regional and seasonal ingredients – a vegetarian version is also available. Alternatively, there is an à la carte selection including dishes such as ravioli with a goose egg filling, a potato medley, wild herbs and rapeseed. Individual wine pairings are available for the set menu. In keeping with the traditional setting of the restaurant, rustic elements have been preserved and incorporated into the minimalist-style modern decor. Friendly, easy-going waitstaff.

Name: Equo 1706
Description: Records of this building go back to 1706, at which time it was a tavern. Today, the restaurant of the Rössli hotel, which is not far from Vierwaldstätter See, has a nicely pared-back interior and a pleasant terrace. It serves ambitious modern cuisine with seasonal and international influences – you can order à la carte or opt for the surprise menu. Hotel patrons get to relax in well-kept guestrooms and the spa facilities.

Name: Le Partage
Description: Located in the luxury Aïda Hotel and Spa, this restaurant’s concept is downright intriguing. The set menu is served in courses, each of which is comprised of several small dishes and diners choose either 10 or 15 "tasting portions" to be shared. The ambitious cuisine rolls out a regional score courtesy of a wide range of local ingredients. Established on two floors, the Alpine-inspired interior is both welcoming and stylish thanks to a profusion of reclaimed wood and dressed stone, elegant herringbone parquet flooring and an open fireplace, complemented by high-quality fabrics and splendid solid wood tables, without forgetting the knockout view from the terrace. The front-of-house staff is friendly, attentive and polished. Teatime in the lounge and brunch on Sundays.

Name: Silex
FacilitiesAndServices: Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: This restaurant is located in a lively residential area. Plenty of Swiss produce goes into the modern seasonal dishes, which are created in the partially visible kitchen. The restaurant is just as committed to sustainability as it is to wine – selected by connoisseurs, the distinctive wine list is testament to a true passion for the grape. British-born chef George Tomlin, previously sous-chef at London's The Clove Club, expresses his creative streak in dishes such as grilled slices of elm mushroom with roasted black onions and a creamy buttermilk and roasted yeast espuma. You can opt to go à la carte or take the five-course tasting menu (also vegetarian). The vibe is deliberately kept simple, with a decor boasting clean lines, and there is a nice terrace outside, in front of this corner plot. The service is friendly and laid back. Just the sort of restaurant you would want in your neighbourhood!

Name: Au Vieux Manoir
Description: This spot is truly the stuff of dreams! Built in 1882 by renowned physician Dr Victor Guénebaud, the property boasts historical charm and a magnificent location, complemented by what is probably one of the finest terraces in the Valais canton! Inside, aesthetically pleasing details such as a wonderful old parquet floor, a beautifully crafted wooden ceiling and striking fabric wallpaper make for a stylish setting. The chef-patron's French-based cuisine alone merits a visit – the dishes are expertly prepared with top-notch, super-fresh ingredients. Should you wish to spend the night in this wonderful place, book one of the five comfortable guestrooms done out in a tasteful, classical style.

Name: Rosmarin
Description: Following its relocation within Lenzburg, Rosmarin entices diners with a cool concept: The modern setting allows for up to 12 guests to sit at a counter right by the open kitchen, where chef-patron Philipp Audolensky prepares a creative surprise menu comprising five to seven courses (vegetarian or vegan options are available by prior arrangement). Appetisers and pastries are prepared by Céline Huber. They make a point of using select regional ingredients and combine them with seasonings from around the globe. The chef himself serves the food and recommends the perfect wine pairings, which adds a charming personal touch to your dining experience. Water, soft drinks and coffee are included in the price. There is a beautifully restored old vaulted cellar for groups. Tip for motorists: Sandweg multi-storey car park.

Name: Le Deck Restaurant
Address: Route de la Corniche 4, Chexbres, 1070, Switzerland
Description: The restaurant is part of Le Baron Tavernier, the chic little spa hotel opposite, and boasts a magnificent location with panoramic views. In addition to a fabulous vista over Lake Geneva, this place promises ambitious and tasteful French cuisine, prepared with top-notch produce, as well as friendly and attentive service. In summer, the open-air bar is the perfect spot for a drink.

Name: Le Vingt Deux - Table d'hôtes
Description: It is well worth venturing into this discreet and exclusive fine dining table d'hôte concealed by a secret door behind the bar. A handpicked group of 15 or so guests are welcomed by the owner himself, who is then on hand throughout the meal to ensure that everything runs smoothly. The kitchen sends out elegant and carefully crafted classic dishes based on excellent regional ingredients – some with subtle Mediterranean touches. An intimate and hospitable atmosphere reigns here, with the same relaxed style as in the lively, bustling bar. You'll need to book well in advance.

Name: Alter Torkel - Huus vum Bündner Wii
Description: Even from the outside, Alte Torkel, which is located right on the road through the vineyards, is liable to turn heads! The old stone house at a remove from even its closest neighbours has maintained its regional charm while incorporating modern touches; the wine theme is omnipresent. In keeping with its "Fine Wineing" motto, the menu is characterised by a regularly changing selection of wines by the glass. A contemporary influence makes itself felt in the seasonal, regional cuisine. The hosts are cordial and dedicated. In summer, the terrace with a view of the valley is a real boon!

Name: Carlton
Description: This tasteful, elegant restaurant is located in a historical building that was erected in 1913 to house a department store and later converted into the Carlton Elite hotel. They serve classic, top-notch cuisine; in the evening a more modern five-course menu with beef Wellington, tartar and crêpes Suzette is also available. Great wine list, including an impressive selection of 40 or so types from the Domaine Romanée-Conti.

Name: Le Rossignol
Description: At Le Rossignol (which is French for nightingale but also happens to be the chef's name), Willy Rossignol finds a captive audience for his smooth classical repertoire of indulgent, flavoursome and well-balanced dishes, prepared using fresh ingredients. Mara, his wife, extends guests an attentive welcome in the simple, well-kept space or out on the terrace in fine weather. Dishes to try include the Gragnano paccheri with wild mushrooms with an aged Parmigiano Reggiano gratin, or thinly sliced chamois with Kampot pepper.

Name: MOzern
Description: This part of the Mandarin Oriental's culinary portfolio serves food all day. In addition to lunch and dinner, you can have breakfast and afternoon tea here – all in tasteful surroundings that combine a stylish, old-world feel with a brasserie atmosphere. The menu features international cuisine including classics like Angus beef tartare and raclette cheese burger, as well as Asian bar snacks such as crispy duck rolls. The bar serves an excellent assortment of drinks. Tip: Drop in at the Grand Casino next door.

Name: Le Grill
Description: The knockout view of Lake Geneva and its iconic Jet d’Eau is unquestionably one of the highlights of this fine establishment. However, that afforded by the kitchens, the rotisserie and the cold room where the superb cuts of meat are stored is equally uplifting. Unsurprisingly, specialities include grilled fish and meat but there is also tofu. The set menu known as "Le Grill Experience" is an excellent option for those with a healthy appetite, as is the Grill Burger! Impeccable service.

Name: Le Restaurant / Le Relais
Description: If you are looking for excellence and elegance, you are in the right place at Le Restaurant or Le Relais of the venerable Badrutt's Palace! In an atmosphere of luxury, the attentive front-of-house team provides classic service. The flavourful cuisine is made from exclusive ingredients and the menu also features a number of dishes that are prepared at your table, e.g. flambées, tartar etc. Whatever you opt for, there is a first-class selection of wines from the best vineyards to accompany your meal. Tip: You can also have breakfast here - accompanied by views of the lake and mountains.

Name: Baur's
Description: The chic, rather imposing deluxe brasserie of the famous Baur au Lac hotel does full justice to the top-notch spirit of gastronomy with which the grand hotel is synonymous. It serves international cuisine firmly rooted in the classics and made with excellent ingredients. The wine list is compiled by one of the best sommeliers in the world.

Name: Casino Restaurant
Description: In the beautiful building of the Casino Bern, which opened in 1909 in the centre of the old town, the mixture of a great historical setting and brasserie chic exudes a special flair, which continues in summer on the wonderful large terrace - here you can enjoy the view of the Aare under shady trees. The menu features classic dishes as well as Italian influences. There is a menu (also vegetarian) as well as an a la carte offer in addition to ‘Grosses pièces’ for two people. Next to the restaurant is the ‘Salon d'Or’ with bistro bar - here you can enjoy coffee and cake as well as wines and cocktails throughout the day.

Name: GLACIER
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: What a great location right in front of the Eiger North Face! The fine dining restaurant of the chic boutique hotel (also called GLACIER) makes the most of its surroundings with a floor-to-ceiling window front – and a wonderful terrace for a magical view! The cuisine is ambitious, modern, creative and seasonal. In the evening, a set menu is available in three formats: "Découverte" with three courses, "Promenade" with five courses and "Excursion" with seven courses (the last two courses are surprise dishes). There are vegetarian versions of all three. Great emphasis is placed on selecting high-quality ingredients, with a preference for supplies from local producers. The 320-year-old wine cellar is home to around 500 labels, 160 of which are also available by the glass. An enthusiastic sommelier provides astute recommendations.

Name: Auberge de la Veveyse - Salle grise
Description: In this small space of the Auberge de la Veveyse dedicated to fine dining, owner David Tarnowski offers the best of the market and local produce in the form of several surprise set menus that are not short on finesse: tarragon jelly with lake fish; whitefish from the nearby lakes with tomato; loin of Swiss veal, courgette and a thyme jus…

Name: Franz
Description: Here in the elegant restaurant of the Grand Hotel National, you could almost be in Vienna: marble columns and high ceilings, waltz music (as well as more modern tunes) playing quietly in the background, and classic Austrian dishes, from Tafelspitz and Wiener schnitzel to apple strudel. Choose from a list of good Austrian wines. Great view of the lake, especially from the terrace. Smaller menu in the afternoon. Cakes are also available.

Name: Sablier
Description: Definitely one of the coolest restaurants in town! On the eighth floor of a newly built section of the airport, the incredibly high ceilings, chic interior design, two large glass-fronted wine cabinets and stylish bar are really impressive. The menu features French-inspired cuisine, with an additional lunch deal available daily and brunch served every Sunday. The rooftop terrace has to be the highlight! Tip for motorists: park in Parkhaus 4, south exit.

Name: L'Etoile
Description: Whether you are seated in the chic bistro, in the winter garden or in the attractive shaded garden, this family-run establishment offers a warm welcome and a friendly atmosphere. The seasonal menu, with dishes prepared to order, features local producers. The thick and creamy crème brûlée, delicately flavoured with orange, is unforgettable. The set lunch menu is a must!

Name: Auberge de l'Abbaye de Montheron
Description: Located in a former Cistercian monastery that dates back to 1442, this restaurant proposes food that is very much of the moment. The original and exciting dishes draw heavily on local organic produce and heritage vegetables. Diners are won over by thoroughly modern fare that has been devised with a genuine concern for sustainability, such as suckling lamb served with pak choi and rhubarb. Appealing terrace on the edge of the forest, and a young and trendy atmosphere. A winning formula.

Name: Spices Kitchen & Terrace
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Notable sake list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: The aromas that waft out of the large show kitchen here are sure to get your taste buds tingling with their promise of pan-Asian delights from Japanese to Chinese, Thai and Indian dishes, all authentic and made using the very best ingredients. There’s also a stunning view!

Name: Restaurant Burgstrasse9
Description: Dating back over 300 years, this establishment, once a smithy and locksmith's shop, has a rustic-meets-historical charm that beautifully incorporates more modern features. French-born chef-patron Stephan Koltes uses exclusively regional produce to create modern cuisine that is full of contrasts. The individual courses of his set menu are each available in the form of two small dishes made from the same ingredients – an enticing option. Tip for motorists: Use the Schlossberg multi-storey car park.

Name: OX'n
Description: Where the old Ochsen inn once stood, the new OX'n stands today with its eye-catching modern design – all the glass gives the place an airy feel and a pleasing sense of transparency. The overall atmosphere is trendy yet inviting. In good weather, the terrace beckons. Friendly service. A surprise menu is served Wed-Sat evenings, and there is an additional à la carte selection Wed-Thu. At lunchtime, a simplified version of the evening surprise menu is available. Alternatively, you could opt for the set menu that changes every week, or something from the à la carte selection. Featuring ingredients sourced from local producers, this is flavoursome seasonal cuisine. The Entlebuch trout with asparagus and beurre blanc is a must-try. Tip: If you fancy an after-work beer or a cocktail, pop into the bar for a quick drink, or feel free to stay a while longer.

Name: Ochsen
Description: Located just metres from the monastery, the venerable Ochsen dates back to 1596. In its current iteration with an avant-garde look, it is part of the three-building Hotel Caspar, which has stylishly designed guestrooms. In the open kitchen, regional ingredients go into modern and creative cooking – interesting cuisine that is "close to nature", with fire, aromatic woods, smoked and grilled dishes play a central role.

Name: ROSI
Description: With its vibrant atmosphere and unique charm, this inviting self-proclaimed "neo-Bavarian" restaurant stands out from the crowd. It embodies a fusion of trendy, urban-casual vibes and cuisine inspired by the owner's Allgäu roots. In the four-course "Schmankerl Menu", the 12-course "Wirtshaus Maximus Menu" and the small à la carte selection, Markus Stöckle transforms traditional dishes into original creations packed with flavour. A prime example is the "Radi Wickerl" (braised leaves, sansho, pickled kombu and radish). The wine list, which includes a selection of natural wines, is also impressive. The service is pleasingly down-to-earth and friendly – the charismatic proprietor is also on hand, making sure each guest feels well looked after.

Name: Käserei
Description: Whether you are seated at a bare or beautifully set table, in this listed former cheese dairy, the dedicated hosts serve high-quality international and regional cuisine that is not only a hit with the locals. Tip: From Tuesdays to Fridays, an inexpensive lunch is served. Incidentally, the building is located in the heart of the pretty old town – perfect for a stroll!

Name: Brasserie 1809
Description: The restaurant is done out in a modern Alpine style, with an interior that is upscale, sleek and at the same time inviting. As for the food great store is set by regional produce and sustainable farming. Select ingredients go into creating tasty seasonal dishes. It is pleasant to eat on the lovely terrace, and not only in summer! The Capra hotel has wonderful inviting guestrooms.

Name: mille sens - les goûts du monde
Description: At this pleasantly lively, modern restaurant in the Schweizerhof Passage near the train station, chef Domingo S. Domingo takes you on a culinary journey around the world, also drawing on his Australian and Filipino roots. At lunchtime, options include a small set menu ("Business Lunch") and the "Quicktray" comprising four dishes on one plate. In the evening, guests can choose from the "Domingo Pur Menu Surprise" and "Tavolata" – also available in a large portion to share. The small selection of bowls is available at both mealtimes.

Name: Roter Bären
Description: This pretty restaurant in the red-light district has a rather original concept that is popular with diners: in an open kitchen, the chefs conjure up ambitious appetiser-sized dishes that draw inspiration from modern culinary trends – three are recommended, then maybe a dessert to round things off. Great bar.

Name: Restaurant LA
Description: If you're not careful, you might end up walking right past the narrow façade of this mid-terrace restaurant. Here, an intriguing modern dining experience is proposed – and that goes for both the minimalist interior and the seasonal cuisine. Available either à la carte or as a surprise menu comprising four or six courses, the dishes are well-thought-out, with harmoniously balanced flavours. The staff are more than happy to cater to special dietary needs – please mention these when making your reservation. From some tables it is possible to see into the kitchen. In summer, there is terrace seating on the pavement overlooking the tram line.

Name: Le Guillaume Tell
Address: Route de la Petite Corniche 5, Aran, 1091, Switzerland
Description: A charming pink house in the heart of this wine-producing village overlooking Lake Geneva. In this traditional setting, chef Denis Velen conjures up creative gastronomic cuisine that combines originality with delicious flavours as witnessed in dishes such as crispy spiced sea bass with choucroute.

Name: La Fontana
Address: Via ai Monti della Trinità 44, Locarno, 6600, Switzerland
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Splendidly located inside the Hotel Belvedere, at an altitude of approximately 240m, this elegant south-facing restaurant boasts a splendid terrace and a lounge space. Depending on where you sit, watch the chef at work in the kitchen or enjoy the impressive views through La Fontana’s ground floor picture windows overlooking its verdant surroundings. The culinary focus here is on modern and seasonal Mediterranean cuisine without neglecting the region’s gastronomic roots. In addition to the classic menu, you can also choose the 4- or 5-course tasting option as well as the restaurant’s signature dishes such as the La Fontana tartare, the Chateaubriand, and the Raviolini del Plin. The extensive glass-fronted wine cabinets at the entrance provide an impressive backdrop.

Name: Schmitte
Description: This is the fine dining restaurant of the long-established Hotel Schweizerhof. The small space is inviting, with an elegant and cosy feel, and the service team is friendly and attentive. The dishes are rooted in classic cuisine and draw on modern influences. The tasting menus "Fauna" and "Flora" (vegetarian) can be ordered in a four- to six-course format. The hotel garden has a sun terrace and there is also a bar.

Name: Hide & Seek
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Ayurvedic philosophy inspires part of the menu at this restaurant, where Mediterranean culinary techniques and ingredients result in colourful, playful dishes. In fine weather, don’t miss the magnificent terrace overlooking the garden with its small lake and abundance of flowers.

Name: PRISMA Expérience
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Great view,Interesting wine list,Notable sake list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: Housed in the exclusive Park Hotel Vitznau, which dates back to 1903, this elegant yet casual restaurant whisks you away on a culinary voyage. Japanese fusion cuisine is the name of the game here. There is an omakase menu (for two or more diners), as well as an à la carte selection including sushi, sashimi, Wagyu dishes and ramen. The location overlooking the lake is a draw in itself, and it goes without saying that tables on the terrace are highly coveted.

Name: Chez Be
Description: Following on from their successful restaurant, Amrein's, the amiable couple at the helm has embarked on a new culinary adventure. Romy takes good care of customers, while Beat cooks up fresh Mediterranean dishes. Shorter menu at lunchtime. The charming modern bistro-style interior with its open kitchen and the terrace giving onto the little square (Mühleplatz) are both lovely places to sit and eat.

Name: Lumières
Description: The location is simply divine! The restaurant of Hotel Château Gütsch affords a breathtaking view over the city and the lake surrounded by mountains, especially from the large terrace – the perfect setting for a romantic dinner! Inspired by the hotel's 140-year history, the interior design draws on Belle Époque design elements but also incorporates nods to the natural surroundings. Fresh, modern accents successfully bridge the gap to the present day. The cuisine is influenced by the culinary traditions of France and the Mediterranean. Opt for the "Chef's Choice" set menu or order à la carte. At midday, the shorter "Time for Lunch" set menu is available, along with other dishes.

Name: Sonne Seuzach
Description: Located in the town centre, Sonne is an inviting restaurant. The interior is tastefully sleek, the atmosphere warm and welcoming, and there is a gorgeous terrace out in front of the glass-paned façade. The cuisine is seasonal, and showcases a range of regional produce. Reduced menu at lunchtime. Friendly and professional front-of-house team. There is also a bar. Modern guestrooms available for overnight stays.

Name: Restaurant Olivo
Description: Its Belle Epoque style lends this restaurant on the first floor of the Grand Casino a distinct elegance and charm that hark back to a bygone era. Under a high ceiling with moulding and chandeliers, Mediterranean-inspired cuisine is served in the form of a set menu or à la carte. The "Dinner & Casino" packages are also worth mentioning. Fabulous balcony terrace with lake and mountain views. Tip: Park in the casino garage.

Name: Ahaan Thai
Description: A slice of Thailand in Graubünden! As well as dim sum and the usual range of curries, the menu features specialities such as Goong Hom Pha (shrimp in a blanket) – deep-fried king prawns with a sweet chilli sauce. Diners can also look forward to friendly service in a comfortable setting with elegant Thai-inspired decor. The restaurant is housed in the attractive Arosa Kulm Hotel, which dates back to 1882.

Name: Potato-FINE FOOD RESTAURANT
Description: This pleasant little restaurant in a lively street (Bahnhofstrasse) has a down-to-earth and friendly atmosphere, where the cordial service is in invitation to sit back and enjoy your evening, while. Tasty modern dishes are served in the form of a set menu made from top-notch regional ingredients sourced from within a 50km radius whenever possible.

Name: Belle Vue
Description: To make the most of the simply stunning mountain views, opt for a table near the large glass-planed front – or on the delightful terrace! Complementing the wonderful scenery, the interior of the Bellevue Parkhotel & Spa restaurant boasts a sleek design that provides the backdrop for the fine dining menu: classic dishes such as roast duck breast with potato galettes are served in the evening, and a simpler à la carte selection is available at lunchtime. Choose an accompaniment from the exquisite wine list.

Name: Osteria del Centenario
Description: A restaurant that has been renovated in contemporary style, in complete harmony with its attractive setting overlooking the scenic lakeside promenade. Talented chef Egon Bajardi conjures up interesting Mediterranean cuisine with a focus on creative technique and the occasional exotic touch. Don’t miss his selection of desserts, including Crema Catalana with pumpkin, orange and bay leaf gelato.

Name: Zum See
Description: A pleasant walk in the mountains leads to this charming restaurant with a romantic terrace. Simple, good cuisine is served.

Name: Sonnenhof
Description: Set above the valley, this cosy, rustic restaurant boasts a wonderfully sunny terrace and fabulous views of the mountains.

Name: Kronenhalle
Description: This building, constructed in 1862, is a Zurich institution, and is located on Bellevue Square. Be sure to take a look at the art collection put together over a period of decades. The atmosphere is traditional, as is the cooking.

Name: Accademia del Gusto
Description: This restaurant is a smash hit with its many regulars, which is hardly surprising considering the terrific food and lively and buzzing atmosphere. Over time, various dishes have achieved classic status. While Stefano Piscopo conjures up delectable creations such as home-made pasta (eg veal ravioli with sage butter) or marinated tuna tartare, his charming wife presides front-of-house. The handful of tables on the pavement tend to get snapped up quickly.

Name: Rössli
Description: Since 1995, Susy and Markus Sager-Meyerhans have been the friendly faces behind this long-established restaurant with its roots in the 18C, when it was a tavern. In addition to cordial service, you can expect a hybrid of traditional and modern-meets-classic cuisine; at lunchtime there is a somewhat reduced menu. Outside you will find the Rosenterrasse and Rössligarten. Charming guestrooms are also available.

Name: Landhaus Liebefeld
Description: Diners at this restaurant in a converted bailiwick (1671) choose between the Gaststube and the more elegant – but no less cosy – Rôtisserie. The cuisine is regional and seasonal, eg beef entrecôte with a herb butter foam. In summer, you can tuck into barbecue dishes in the small garden. On Thursday, Friday and Saturday evenings, le caveau serves a vegan set menu. For guests wishing to stay overnight, there are also tasteful guestrooms.

Name: Le Café Suisse
Description: This former village café has morphed into a buzzy, friendly eatery decked in colourful cartoon murals. Youthful Marie Robert, assisted by an almost woman only team, wholeheartedly regales diners with creative, light-hearted dishes that are in tune with the seasons to be washed down with excellent local tipples. Robert has a flair for spontaneously showcasing seasonal ingredients. Examples include a mousseline of seabream enhanced by a whipped beurre blanc or an incredibly powerful and heady duo of blueberry and chocolate. Be bold and opt for her surprise menu – a hit with regulars, it is as playful as it is indulgent.

Name: Lindenhofkeller
FacilitiesAndServices: Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: This place takes home-style cuisine up a notch with its "feinbürgerliche Küche". But soul food is also a very apt description of what is served in this gorgeous traditional restaurant in a desirable old town location, as Sebastian Rösch delivers truly feel-good cuisine. He preserves, for example, the familiar traditional character of a classic beef roulade with potato purée, preparing it without unnecessary frills, but bringing into play a precise craftsmanship and a degree of sophistication, as well as premium-quality produce. The modern decor and relaxed ambience are reminiscent of a chic, trendy gastro pub; the courtyard terrace is also pretty. Extremely friendly waitstaff. Real passion has gone into curating the wine list – a fine selection of well-established names but also lesser-known or smaller winegrowers. Or perhaps you prefer a fresh draught beer? Tip for motorists: Parkhaus Urania is just a short (if steep) walk away.

Name: Le 42
Description: This stylish restaurant, part of the comfortable and tastefully designed Hotel Le White, is located right at the entrance of the village, facing the Dents du Midi mountain range. The decor here is a draw in itself; the seating is spread over two levels, with sleek modern furnishings complemented by warm reclaimed wood and quarry stone, creating a pleasing Alpine feel. The proprietor personally attends to the diners, while his partner manages the kitchen. Her French heritage is reflected in her dishes (be sure to leave room for dessert and try the classic rum baba), but she also incorporates international – especially Asian – influences, such as in her unique take on gyoza.

Name: Auberge d'Onex
Description: Since 1977, this inn has been nestled in verdant surroundings in the former clubhouse of Geneva's first golf course. It serves traditional Italian cuisine, including the chef's specialities of penne with vodka and penne alla Norma (a Sicilian dish that pays tribute to the composer Vincenzo Bellini, who was from the island), but also classics such as vitello tonnato. The dessert trolley features Italian specialities and a choice of fresh fruit.

Name: Landgasthof Wartegg
Description: In this historical inn – run by the Frei family since 1982 – they serve fresh, flavoursome seasonal cuisine with classical foundations, made using excellent produce. The lunch menu is also popular. The ambience ranges from rustic to elegant, with a beautiful outdoor terrace shaded by trees. There are comfortable guestrooms for overnight stays.

Name: Brücke
Description: The superb location on the River Aare is a big draw here, and it goes without saying that the terrace is in high demand! As for the food: a modern spin is put on fresh, traditional cuisine. The emphasis is laid squarely on the quality and seasonality of the produce.

Name: La Table du Palafitte
Description: The “Menu Découverte” carries guests away on a journey inspired by the time-honoured culinary traditions of the Mediterranean coast. Choose between the dining room or the large waterfront terrace.

Name: parkhuus
Description: The restaurant of the luxurious Park Hyatt international business hotel is spacious and high-ceilinged . It has an open kitchen, upscale furnishings and sophisticated modern lighting; the glassed-in wine library, with its outstanding exclusive wine selection, is well worth seeing! The modern dishes are available as a set menu or à la carte.

Name: Sala of Tokyo
Description: Classic Japanese cuisine made from top-notch ingredients is the name of the game here. The sushi and sashimi, tempura, and robata grill specialities, as well as the sukiyaki and shabu shabu stews all come highly recommended. Another draw of this place is its inviting interior, which is sleek and simple, yet cosy at the same time. You can watch the sushi master at work at a small counter.

Name: Hide & Seek
Description: If you like to dine in a lively, modern atmosphere, the restaurant of Hotel Giardino Mountain is for you. The decor features a combination of trendy, chic features and rustic wood. Attentive front-of-house team and Mediterranean and Swiss dishes that are aromatic and flavoursome, made with fresh, often regional produce. Lunch is served in the bar-lounge.

Name: Thai Garden
Description: You could almost fancy you are in Thailand: with dim lighting, Far Eastern background music, Thai decoration, large ceiling fans and a babbling fountain, the setting alone transports you to an exotic world. Complementing this is exceptionally friendly service and authentic Thai cuisine – the spiciness can be adjusted to suit diners' individual preferences. Tip: The appealing lunch deal is available in two variations: the "Thai Box" and the "Vegi Box".

Name: MEGU
Description: This stylish offshoot of the New York flagship restaurant brings a modern and cosmopolitan take on Japanese cuisine, serving up sushi, sashimi and rolls, as well as Wagyu beef and chicken teriyaki. Fittingly, star designer Noé Duchafour-Lawrence drew inspiration from the Far East to create the sophisticated and distinctive interior. There is also a sushi counter, where – as you might expect in an establishment of this calibre – sushi master Tsutomu Kugota works his magic. In summer, the terrace is a delightful spot.

Name: Oliveiras
Description: The friendly Oliveira family runs this establishment, making sure guests feel at home in the harmonious and deliberately informal atmosphere. They are attentively looked after as they tuck into Mediterranean cuisine made from excellent produce. All of this is accompanied by a fantastic selection of wines from the owner's Portuguese homeland.

Name: Des Balances
Description: This place boasts an enviable location in the historic old town, with a magnificent terrace right alongside the River Reuss. Diners can enjoy the chic space of the restaurant, bar and lounge. On the menu: grilled specialities and French-Mediterranean dishes based on regional and seasonal produce; none of the meat comes from factory farms. The restaurant is ensconced within the stunning Hotel Des Balances.

Name: Löwen - Gaststube
Description: Run by Rita and Domenico Miggiano-Köferli, Gasthof Löwen's second eatery is a delightful and more down-to-earth alternative to the fine dining restaurant. The atmosphere is inviting, not least because of the warm hospitality provided by the waitstaff. The freshly prepared, flavoursome dishes include pan-fried Lötschberg perch fillet with lemon thyme and almond butter, and Zurich veal ragout with glazed vegetables and butter rösti. Vegetarian options available. Popular lunch deal.

Name: Auberge aux 3 Tilleuls
Description: If you're passing through Genolier, be sure to stop off at this charming Auberge! Filipe, the young chef here, serves fresh, tasty cuisine infused with contemporary flair: think fillet of turbot grilled skin on, with pesto and crunchy vegetables. An enjoyable mealtime.

Name: Le 1424, La Fabrique Cornu
Description: "La Fabrique" has many strings to its bow: it is a biscuit-maker, an interactive museum and, on the third floor, it houses this chic, contemporary restaurant with a panoramic view of the Vaud Alps. The ambitious and tasty dishes are made with a wide range of regional and national ingredients and given an international spin. Good value for money.

Name: Wirtschaft zur Rosenburg
Description: Wherever you look, there's history – the old fortified tower is magnificent! After 33 years, the business has changed hands, but new owners Lukas and Evelyn Christen are committed to keeping the tradition alive. The menu continues to feature both regional and international dishes. Look out for the label "Guets vo hie" on the menu, which indicates the local specialities such as topside beef carpaccio with horseradish, red onions and fried mushrooms. The courtyard terrace is especially pleasant. Tip: This pretty restaurant also makes an ideal venue for weddings and other celebrations.

Name: La Maison du Village
Address: Rue de la Fontanette 41, Sauges, 2024, Switzerland
Description: With its resolutely relaxed ambience, this auberge is far from the traditional image of a high temple of gastronomy. Here, Marc Strebel, a young chef from the Valais, conjures up dishes very much inspired by a return to nature. Superb view of the lake from the terrace.

Name: Kreuz
Description: Take a seat in one of the gorgeous dining spaces, or on the lovely, pleasantly peaceful garden terrace, to enjoy traditional and regional fare. The menu features, for instance, local lake fish; European perch from the Lötschberg mountains is also popular. The good food is complemented by a really friendly family atmosphere, which comes courtesy of the attentive service team. In the simpler Gaststube, you can order the dish of the day.

Name: L'Auberge
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Opt for a table in either the modern, minimalist dining area or the more elegant dining space; in summer, there is also a delightful garden terrace. Made with top-quality ingredients, the modern French cuisine is infused with a Mediterranean character. Competent sommelier service comes courtesy of the manageress, who will advise you on the appealing wine list. A simpler menu is available at lunchtime. Tip: Book a stay at the tasteful hotel of the same name.

Name: Wirtschaft zum Frieden
Description: This centuries-old inn enjoys a prime location right on Marktplatz, and its charming ambiance, redolent of a bygone era, will have you yearning to return. The dedication of your hosts is also infectious. While maître d' Heidi Bischoff graciously attends to diners in the cosy wood-panelled dining areas, chef-patron Fabrice Bischoff cooks up classic, home-style fare using fresh, high-quality ingredients. Some dishes also incorporate a Mediterranean twist. On the menu you will find beef fillet Stroganoff, as well as Swiss salmon steak with accras. A simpler set menu of the day is also available at lunchtime. The verdant terrace is a delightful spot in the summertime!

Name: Donatz
Description: Cornelia and René A Donatz run their business with great dedication. In an elegant rustic-style decor, they serve good fresh cuisine, including classic veal dishes, Angus beef "bestsellers", vegetarian fare and fish such as Graubünden salmon from Lostallo. They stock some 550 wines (20 available by the glass) – a passion of the owner. Donatz Wine Bar proposes a smaller menu. Hotel Donatz has appealingly modern and comfortable guestrooms.

Name: t3e terre
Address: via Vecchia Stazione 2, Ponte Brolla, 6652, Switzerland
Description: Owned by the Meneganti family, this beautiful house is home to a restaurant with an attractive dining room and stunning terrace that provide the backdrop for delicious Mediterranean cuisine. A charming hotel with welcoming guestrooms (additional rooms are under construction) adds to the appeal.

Name: Centovalli
Address: Via Alla Stazione 5, Ponte Brolla, 6652, Switzerland
Description: This attractive restaurant boasting rustic yet modern dining rooms and a beautiful terrace shaded by a pergola has offered the same format for over 20 years – a single risotto-based dish (the house speciality) served with a delicious meat option, nearly always lamb fillet, and very few fish dishes. Reasonably priced, with everything of an excellent quality.

Name: Windows
Description: This restaurant of Hôtel D'Angleterre commands a panoramic view of Lake Geneva and its emblematic Jet d'Eau, with the mountains and Mont Blanc in the distance. Fresh, seasonal produce takes the limelight in well-crafted French cuisine that mixes classical and traditional influences and which is quite the equal of its splendid setting! Pop into the Leopard Bar for evening cocktails in a buzzy, jazzy vibe, (there is a cigar lounge in the basement). Afternoon tea is very popular.

Name: dr Egge - das restaurant
Description: Located in Muttenz's old town, this compact restaurant delights diners with its stylish and charming decor, warm hospitality and Italian-inspired cuisine. They propose a seasonal set menu made using regional produce wherever possible; the "Piedmontese Autumn Menu", featuring Alba white truffles, is also a popular choice. Astute wine recommendations come courtesy of the maître d'.

Name: Scalottas - Terroir
Description: At this trendy Alpine-style restaurant, the kitchen works exclusively with regional produce, much of it their own. Seasonality and sustainability are a central tenet – the staff will be happy to tell you more about their concept. To order, simply mix and match the dishes on the menu that pique your interest. The wines are also sourced from the region and surrounding areas – astute recommendations come courtesy of the friendly service team.

Name: Osteria Cyrano Cibo e Vino
Description: Enjoy personalised cuisine full of flavour and prepared with excellent ingredients at this restaurant, which offers a simple menu at lunchtime and a wider choice of dishes in the evening. Delicious recipes and a good balance of meat and fish options.

Name: Stiefels Hopfenkranz
Description: This attractive, personally managed restaurant boasts beautiful pictures on the walls, a relaxed atmosphere, and warm, friendly service from the female owner, who also offers good wine recommendations. In the partly open kitchen, guests can watch the chefs at work. Seasonal produce takes pride of place on the menu.

Name: Auberge Les Platanes
Address: Rue du Vieux Collège 2, Chéserex, 1275, Switzerland
Description: An elegant 17C patrician manor house with smart dining rooms furnished in Regency-style. The fine, classic cuisine is in keeping with its surroundings and changes with the seasons, ensuring that only the freshest ingredients are served.

Name: Vecchia Osteria Seseglio
Description: Traditional local dishes, excellent regional produce, plus a few fish and seafood options, all served in warm dining rooms with low wooden ceilings and exposed brick vaults or outdoors in the garden in summer. Friendly service and a good selection of wines accompany the delicious cuisine.

Name: Villa Honegg
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: Set 914m above the ground, Villa Honegg offers a truly grandiose view from its terrace. Inside, enjoy the classic, regional cuisine with a modern twist, which includes the Honegg meatloaf and a six-course set menu.

Name: Sauvage
Description: This place has been dedicated to hospitality for over 500 years. Not only does the long-standing Hotel Wilden Mann have charming, individually styled guestrooms, it is also a bastion of fine dining. Sascha Behrendt has been the head chef at the upscale and elegant fine dining restaurant since April 2022. He incorporates Japanese elements into his classic cuisine, as well as nods to the region and the season. The four- to six-course set menu is available in both an omnivore and a vegetarian version. There are à la carte options too. In addition, the tempting caviar menu showcases different varieties – quail egg, blini, toast and butter are excellent accompaniments. Tip for motorists: the Kesselturm multi-storey car park is just a short walk away. Alternatively, you can park on the other side of the river, stroll through the beautiful old town and then cross the bridge (Reussbrücke).

Name: Chasellas
Description: This charming restaurant in the Suvretta House hotel at the entrance to the skiing and hiking area has found a winning formula, offering rustic specialities for lunch and more sophisticated dishes in the evening, such as herb-crusted rack of lamb, mashed potatoes, chanterelle-asparagus ragout and baby carrots.

Name: Les Touristes
Description: This restaurant has been a culinary landmark for decades, thanks to well-crafted cuisine and inspired recipes. Two young local lads are now at the helm. Their culinary creations, which exhibit a particularly minimalist approach and are refreshingly succinct, star carefully selected ingredients, often sourced locally. There are three set menus to choose from, one of which is vegetarian. In addition to outstanding food, there is a strong emphasis on creating an enjoyable dining experience. The buzzy vibe, stylish interior and attentive and friendly service all play their part, including excellent wine tips (the white Metphusus goes down a treat with the poultry breast stuffed in morels). In summer, the terrace is heavenly.

Name: Corso
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: This modern, urban restaurant on the edge of the old town is dedicated to the Alpine region, serving good, seasonal produce and game dishes in the autumn. The ambience here is minimalist, with an open kitchen which allows guests to watch chef Franz Ackermann creating his culinary works of art. Simpler lunch menu. The bistro “Unikatessen am Corso” next door also sells regional produce.

Name: da Frappa
Description: Childhood friends Fabio Imparato and Alfonso Petti, both from the Italian province of Salerno, have joined forces at this restaurant not far from the lake. The two chefs have adopted a culinary style that draws heavily on their roots, serving up Italian and Mediterranean dishes (eg roasted pulpo on chicory, or braised veal cheek with polenta) in the form of a surprise set menu – at lunchtime a two- or three-course "Business Lunch", and in the evening a four- or five-course tasting menu. The wine list, too, revolves around their homeland. Plus: friendly, proficient service and an appealingly refined, upscale decor. There is a public car park just a stone's throw away.

Name: De la Cigogne
Description: Trained in some of the world’s leading restaurants, the chef at De la Cigogne creates fine French cuisine which is full of flavour and always beautifully presented. Choose between the “old school” interior decor of mahogany panelling and padded chairs or the pleasant terrace in fine weather.

Name: Brasserie Les Trois Rois
Description: This attractive brasserie with its classic, elegant design and a fantastic view of the Rhine is located in the left wing of the hotel Les Trois Rois. The French-Swiss cuisine also has international influences: The menu includes a good selection of classic and seasonal dishes, which are presented at your table by the attentive waitstaff. Brunch is served on Sundays. Tip: You can look into the kitchen through a window in the passageway leading to reception.

Name: Seegarten
Description: For over 30 years, this elegant restaurant with a pleasant terrace has been making the most of its wonderful location on the marina. The menu is inspired by the seasons; there is also an appetising set menu, which changes on a monthly basis, but the classics are just as much in demand. Book your spot at the traditional seafood festival – Festival de Fruits de Mer – from late November to late January. Other highlights are the extensive wine list, and friendly, professional service.

Name: L'Artichaut
Description: Only the street separates this appealing restaurant from the River Arve. You will feel completely at home here, thanks to both the pleasant bistro atmosphere, including decorative paintings and posters of vintage advertisements, and the French cuisine reinterpreted with seasonal influences. Excellent wine list.

Name: La Cantine des Commerçants
Description: A neo-bistro in the old abattoir district of the city, characterised by white and bright green walls, retro decor and a large counter where you can sit and eat. The varied menu is very much in keeping with the times: risotto with prawns and wild herbs, grilled fish and pan-fried fillet of beef.

Name: Le Vallon
Description: With its pink façade and green shutters, this elegant and classically styled inn is an inviting proposition. The tastefully luxurious interior is adorned with bouquets of fresh flowers and floral wallpaper. In his open kitchen, Julien Poulain concocts classic dishes with a sprinkling of extremely subtle modern touches (roasted langoustine, celeriac risotto, bisque emulsion, tarragon, chopped hazelnuts). Friendly, attentive service and a very appealing wine list (a noteworthy selection of red wines, also available in magnums). In fine weather, make the most of the terrace and the verdant garden.

Name: Kakinuma
Description: This small restaurant in the lively Eaux-Vives district is definitely worthy of its current success. The couple that run it create fresh and elegant dishes that include the most exquisitely sliced fish, tempuras that are as light as a feather, and silky chawanmushi (an egg flan). A feast for the senses!

Name: Auberge de la Gare
Address: Rue de la Gare 1, Grandvaux, 1091, Switzerland
Description: The first thing that impresses guests here is the stunning panoramic view of Lake Geneva. The dishes are simple and fresh – house classics include tartare and fillets of perch from the lake served with fries. Family atmosphere and a lovely terrace. Comfortable guestrooms are available for guests wishing to stay the night.

Name: moment
Description: Set in the historical heart of Bern, this trendy, modern restaurant spread over two floors serves creative cuisine with a focus on regional and seasonal produce. The "Carte Blanche" menu offers a choice of two four- to five course set menus, – one completely plant based. A laid-back front-of-house team takes care of the service. There are entrances on both Postgasse and Gerechtigkeitsgasse.

Name: Casa Novo
Description: This place is now under new management, although the name has not changed. Since chef-patron Dirk Wagner took over the restaurant, the cooking has a more international flavour, but has retained a Mediterranean side – for example, beef tongue carpaccio or French guinea fowl in a wild garlic sauce. In addition, tapas are served from 5-7pm, and the "Casa Novo beef tenderloin tartare" is a house classic. At lunchtime, the menu is significantly slimmed down. The location on the River Aare is as idyllic as ever, and the terrace is wonderful! La Vinoteca also remains in operation. The Klösterlistutz car park on the other side of the river is conveniently close.

Name: Heugümper
Description: This venerable townhouse enjoys a fantastic location in the heart of Zurich – the small terrace is a lovely spot in the summer. With its elegant contemporary decor, the interior is also inviting, and the charming hostess provides attentive service. Prepared using select ingredients, the dishes draw on Mediterranean and Asian influences. Options on the menu range from veal cordon bleu with truffle Brie to tuna with sesame and a ginger and mango sauce. Shorter, simpler menu at lunchtime.

Name: Bistrot du Boeuf Rouge
Description: This restaurant is well known in the local area for its simple yet gourmet Lyonnaise specialities: rosette sausage, hot saucisson, pike quenelles, etc. The Farina family's culinary skill is demonstrated on a daily basis, to a backdrop of attractive old-fashioned decor.

Name: Sternen
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Great view,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: In this gorgeous inn, a winning father-and-daughter team conjures up modern takes on classic dishes. They propose a surprise menu – slightly cheaper at lunchtime than in the evening. Incidentally, they smoke the salmon themselves. If you would like a vegetarian menu, please indicate this when making your reservation. Well-stocked wine list.
