Try braised Zhoushan hairtail for its extra-fine flesh in a mildly sweet sauce, or the silky, flavourful braised tofu with fish roe.

Name: Les Morilles
Address: 1F, Sunflower Tower, 37 Maizidian Street, Chaoyang, Beijing, China Mainland
Description: The pared-back, uncluttered interior of this little gem tucked away on the ground-floor of an apartment block by Liangma River provides the perfect foil to modern French cuisine, characterised by top-notch ingredients, precise techniques and bold flavours. Dishes are exquisitely plated and reflect the dedication of the entire team. There are two set dinner menus to choose from with optional wine pairings. Save room for the decadent Galette des Rois dessert.

Name: Mandarin Grill
Address: 5F, Mandarin Oriental Wangfujing, 269 Wangfujing Street, Dongcheng, Beijing, China Mainland
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Brunch,Car park,Great view,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: The beautiful dining room mimics a ‘brasserie de luxe’ of yesteryear. Tufted leather banquettes, polished wood details and crisp white linen promise a marvellous meal; consistently impeccable service is yet another highlight of the space. Choose from the classic grill menu with steaks from U.S. and Australia. An apéritif or digestif on the terrace that affords unrivalled views of the Forbidden City’s skyline and eaves makes for a wonderful experience.

Name: L. Bodhi (Guanghua Road)
Address: No. 202, Building F, Sunshine 100 International Department, 2 Guanghua Road, Chaoyang, Beijing, China Mainland
Description: This branch of the chain restaurant serves three different nine-course vegan sets at various price points. Emphasising holistic well-being, both physical and emotional, the mindfully designed sets cover amuse-bouches, appetisers, hot mains, hot pot, salad, staple starch and dessert. No sign of greasy or heavily processed food here! Instead, organic produce is treated with a light touch so the natural flavours shine.

Name: Char (South Sanlitun Road)
Address: 3F, InterContinental Sanlitun Hotel, Topwin Mall, 1 South Sanlitun Road, Chaoyang, Beijing, China Mainland
Description: After passing through a red neon tunnel, diners are greeted by a copper cow sculpture that sets the scene for a beef-focused feast against panoramic views of the bustling Sanlitun area. Larger steak cuts for sharing, such as David Blackmore’s Australian Wagyu, Porterhouse and Tomahawk steaks, are portioned on individual plates tableside. The signature array of salt and mustard is equally impressive. Ask for a table on the terrace for the ultimate alfresco experience.

Name: Amico BJ
Address: Shop 109, 1F, Pacific Century Place, 2A Gongrentiyuchang North Road, Chaoyang, Beijing, China Mainland
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Counter dining,Foreign credit cards not accepted,Wheelchair access
Description: Exposed, unfinished flakeboard in an upmarket restaurant? The passionate owner-chef has used the construction material to great effects in this intimate and stylish dining room. Omakase menus offer six to eight creative courses firmly rooted in Italian traditions, but with Japanese twists. The chef’s highly original recipes fare well with precise judgment and astute handling. The eight counter seats are the most prized spots to watch the alchemy unfold.

Name: Everlasting Happiness
Address: F101-111, No.39 Capital Xindadu, 21 Chegongzhuang Street, Xicheng, Beijing, China Mainland
Description: For over 20 years, the brand has been a celebrated institution, both within and beyond Hunan. Its first outpost in Beijing greets diners with a bright red entrance, a visual clue to its hot fiery food. The must-try fried pork loin with crackling delivers fascinating textures and rich flavours. Rice paddy eel flown in from Hunan is slaughtered the same day before being stewed in shiso leaves and pickled mustard greens. The in-house preserved meat is also worth trying.

Name: Beef & Dumplings
Address: 5 Shunyuan Street, Chaoyang, Beijing, China Mainland
Description: The shop’s name is quite self-explanatory. Different cuts of beef such as shin, tripe and tendon are braised in a spiced soy marinade for over ten hours resulting in robust flavours and tenderness, but without being too mushy. Beef and pork dumplings are made on the spot with house-made wrapping. Feel free to choose your favourite toppings and vinegar dips from the self-serve condiment station. Braised beef is also available for take-out.

Name: Xiang Shang Xiang (Jinhe East Road)
Address: L301A-L302A, 3F, CP Center, 20 Jinhe East Road, Chaoyang, Beijing, China Mainland
Description: The chain now runs a few establishments in Beijing and Chengdu, but the story started in 2021 at this very first outlet. A veteran with 20-plus years of experience under his belt, Chef Peng revamps the menu every now and then to keep it fresh. He presents a good-value set menu featuring 24 different chilli peppers – heaven for spicy food lovers. The butler, tea master and sommelier go the extra mile to deliver thoughtful, meticulous service.

Name: Brasserie 1893
Address: 1F, Waldorf Astoria Hotel, 5-15 Jinyu Hutong, Dongcheng, Beijing, China Mainland
Description: Calling itself a brasserie is just being humble. The elegant space features exquisite artwork and an attractive display kitchen. The à la carte menu changes regularly to include sharing plates that are great for families; the "Deluxe Degustation" tasting menu embodies the chef's culinary vision. Tea-smoked pigeon is one of his proud creations: he marinates then smokes young birds from Shiqi, uniting Chinese flavours with French techniques.

Name: Ratatouille
Description: Ratatouille is cosy and convivial, and its spacious terrace on the historical Vischmarkt is understandably very popular. Hostess Cindy and chef Gerwin have gained a loyal following in a short period of time, and that is more than deserved. Whether you order à la carte or take a punt on the surprise menu, the value for money is second to none. The versatile chef is just as likely to serve up an oven-baked fillet of red mullet with a rich white wine sauce and a zingy antiboise as a vegetarian pie with sweet and sour nuances. His cuisine is sophisticated and very much on trend, and he puts a lot of thought into his vegetable accoutrements and his choice of suppliers.

Name: Bar Beurre
Description: Once a traditional café, this place is now a no-nonsense bistro, complete with upbeat background music. Bar Beurre certainly lives up to its name. Just like in traditional French cooking, butter (beurre) is a key ingredient here, but this cuisine is not at all lacking in sophistication. For example, the chef uses it to prepare megrim à la meunière, which he serves with anchovies, broad beans and an exquisite beurre blanc finished with a dash of sherry. The short menu features dishes that are bold and playful. Le beurre, c'est la vie!

Name: On Cru
Description: Housed in a listed building, this restaurant with its exposed brick walls is reminiscent of old England. Think Chesterfield chairs, a striking semi-circular counter and dimmed lighting. Kelvin de Pijper's classic market-fresh cuisine lets the ingredients take centre stage, for example, pairing freshly caught cod with a velvety creamed sauce made with fish fumet. Crispy sweetbreads are given a glossy finish with a veal reduction infused with cardamom, lovage and pink peppercorns. This chef honours the natural flavours of the produce while adding subtle, measured nuances. A real gem at the picturesque old port.

Name: QuiDine
Description: Drawing on experience gained at various top-flight establishments, Quirijn Bakker proposes an accessible take on fine dining. QuiDine exudes sophistication but also has a cosy, living room-like feel. Meticulously crafted dishes are served in the form of a set menu; diners simply choose the number of courses. The chef brings his culinary creations to life with ingenious flavour combinations and international influences. For instance, ajo blanco cream elevates the fillet of smoked trout, and strawberry vinegar and chilli pep up a refreshing dessert. This young chef demonstrates a maturity beyond his years.

Name: River Bar
Description: The maritime decor inside this striking oval pavilion is indeed enchanting, yet one of its main draws is the view of the Nieuwe Maas River. As you soak up the vibrant atmosphere and watch the cruise ships dock, you can choose from a fine selection of wines by the glass and the European-inspired menu. Eschewing any unnecessary frills, the chef comes up with some truly original dishes. His repertoire includes perfectly cooked Mediterranean-style turbot, foie gras as rich as anywhere in France – and even beef Wellington! The wide selection promises a delightful culinary journey along Europe's rivers.

Name: De Vijverhoeve
Address: Greveningseweg 2, Sint Anna ter Muiden, 4524 JK, Netherlands
Description: The rustic charm of this little farmhouse and the beautiful French garden demonstrate the passion with which chef Bart Grahame runs his family restaurant. This ambitious chef serves generous dishes made from top-quality ingredients and home produce, accompanied by delicious sauces that show off his classical expertise. A good place to eat after a visit to nearby Sluis.

Name: Kasteel Elsloo
Description: Dining in a castle makes for a special experience. The surrounding natural beauty and centuries-old arcades beneath which guests take their seats cannot fail to impress. This fabulous setting inspires the chef to work with respect for the region, the seasons and sustainability. French and Mediterranean flavours dominate the appealingly updated menu, which now features occasionally innovative dishes. Wine lovers will delight in the enticing selection of wines sold by the glass.

Name: Onglet
Description: To get to this restaurant, you first enter the butcher’s shop, then open the door to the cold storage room – and suddenly there you are in a fashionable, chic and cosy dining room! The attractive menu offers a choice of traditional dishes, such as cold meat platters, vegetarian options and steak, all of which are easily shared.

Name: Portfolio
Description: The expertise of chef Kasper Verlinden and maître d'/sommelier Remco van Antwerpen is palpable at Portfolio and testament to their combined wealth of experience. Meticulously prepared and ambitious, their original creations live up to high expectations. Fish, seafood and Asian flavour nuances are the name of the game here. Expressive, technically sophisticated, captivating. All that deliciousness is also enhanced by a magnificent selection of natural wines and some very appealing non-alcoholic options.

Name: Goyvaerts
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Jip, Yelle and Jesse Goyvaerts have set up shop in the heart of Eindhoven, in Domusdela, a converted church that has retained its serenity. Inside, the modern decor with Scandinavian touches works well – the wine cabinet is sure to draw the eye. The brothers conjure up creative dishes incorporating international influences, the finesse of French cuisine and Japanese seasonings. Think celeriac glazed with soy sauce in a vegetarian concoction with delicate sweet/salty/spicy nuances. Goyvaerts is a name that is synonymous with culinary excellence!

Name: Lastage
Description: Hospitality and conviviality are the bedrock of this cosy little restaurant in the heart of Amsterdam, where you can enjoy good food in a relaxed atmosphere. Rogier van Dam's dishes are full of character, and nothing on the plate is superfluous. If he serves up a fillet of venison, the whole dish revolves around that ingredient. Naturally, there is also a focus on sauces and creative garnishes. The dessert of brioche stuffed with creamy Époisses is a classic of the house, and rightly so!

Name: SAAM restaurant
Description: South Africa comes to the Netherlands in this cosy establishment, which resembles a glass conservatory from the outside. Here on the Amstelzijde strip, some big names in the hospitality industry, including chefs and sommeliers, have joined forces in an endeavour to marry the two culinary cultures. Ingredients such as granadilla, suurvygie and goat meat are incorporated into modern creations with distinct flavours. Those not familiar with South African ingredients can rest assured that the waitstaff are always on hand to offer guidance.

Name: Restaurant 273
Description: Choose a table near the open kitchen in Tommy den Hartog’s chic, modern restaurant situated on the outskirts of the city centre. Here, the chef prepares modern cuisine with ingredients from around the world, resulting in dishes with occasionally playful and surprising combinations, but above all full of such intense flavours that you’re sure to want more!

Name: Bleue Bar Bistro
Description: Rather inconspicuously located on Grote Markt, there is a distinctly Parisian feel to this bistro with a predominantly green colour scheme. The long bar with ceramic tiles and open kitchen with green panelling make for an inviting setting. As you might expect, the menu features French bistro fare with the odd fresh twist – for instance, the chef incorporates kumquat into the rich duck jus that accompanies pan-fried duck breast and orange compote, without compromising the dish's signature flavours. The house-made pâté en croûte is certainly tempting. Full flavours guaranteed!

Name: Aroma
Description: Housed in a stately villa, this restaurant feels rather like a living room. It is here that Pasquale Carfora and Elisa Leune showcase their vision of Italian fine dining. The elegant luxury of the decor perfectly complements the refined cuisine, which is a celebration of fresh seasonal ingredients, traditional Italian techniques and innovative ideas. Think fresh pasta filled with lamb ragout, accompanied by a flavoursome pea cream, cream of pecorino for some bite and a smoked lamb jus full of finesse. This chef elevates tradition to new heights. A vibrant and stylish place to dine.

Name: Restaurant 1397
Address: Grote Markt 38, Bergen op Zoom, 4611 NT, Netherlands
Description: Hotel de Draak's restaurant takes you on a journey back to 1397, taking in the Dutch Golden Age before looking to the future. The decor subtly incorporates all manner of dragons, ubiquitous touches of gold, high ceilings and large windows – this is a 21C take on historical grandeur! Treat yourself to a drink in the chic aperitif lounge before chef Torben Bouterse starts working his magic. Classic dishes are enhanced by a predilection for vegetables, nods to Zeeland cuisine and inspirations from around the globe. Take, for example, his teppanyaki scallops with a velvety Jerusalem artichoke cream, lent a hit of umami by a delicate white wine jus infused with koji. Diners delight in such a masterful and spontaneous approach to textures and flavour pairings.

Name: Orangerie De Pol
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: Talented chef Mark and his charming partner Marjolein are in their element in this restaurant in the Achterhoek region. Excellent local ingredients, produce from their own kitchen garden, and intensely flavoured sauces all feature on the trendy surprise menu which combines international variety and local quality. In this bright setting, guests will definitely feel at one with nature.

Name: Watergang
Description: This lovely little restaurant with space for just 30 guests boasts a genuine warmth and intimacy. The chefs here create a surprise five-course menu that changes each month and is particularly inspired by French and Italian cuisine. The classic comfort food on offer here, featuring the occasional original twist, is highly satisfying!

Name: Diga
Description: Diga is a trendy and intimate restaurant where colourful details brighten up the dark interior – it’s worth asking for a place at the back of the restaurant where you can see the kitchen and the impressive wine cabinet. Subtle influences from all over the world give the delicate antipasti and traditional Italian dishes a contemporary twist.

Name: Huisje James
Description: Start your meal with an aperitif by the fireplace of this former workshop, after which you will be guided to the villa. The thatched roof, the intimate ambience and beautiful art give this restaurant a cosy feel. The surprise menu features classic favourites alongside contemporary surprises, all made from regional ingredients, including home-grown produce.

Name: Héroine
FacilitiesAndServices: Counter dining,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Wheelchair access
Description: Housed in an industrial building, this restaurant has a unique feel on account of its decor incorporating retro features and modern design, as well as striking artwork on the walls. The surprise menu showcases exciting combinations, international influences and vegetables. The chef serves crispy breaded scallops, for instance, on a delicate passion fruit cream, finishing the dish with a butter sauce enhanced with coconut and dill. His bold and innovative creations will leave you craving more.

Name: de Wanne
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Terrace
Description: It is no surprise that German guests feel at home in de Wanne, with its good choice of German wines and recommendations offered by the experienced maître. Original, contemporary dishes full of flavour prepared by a classically trained chef, plus a beautiful terrace overlooking the hotel gardens.

Name: LIMES aan den Rijn
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Daan Reijngoudt is a chef who knows the importance of sauces. Think a delicate foie gras cream sauce with a hint of Calvados to add depth to fried duck liver with sweet fruit garnishes and a brioche roll. His cuisine is beautifully in step with the times, without resorting to any unnecessary frills. Inside, you can watch the chef at work in the attractive open plan kitchen. However, a spot on the terrace, nestled right next to a business complex and overlooking the river, might be your best bet.

Name: Vive La Vie
Description: This retro-style building with a warm ambience is the perfect place for a special meal. Chef Jeroen Sportel prepares complex and creative dishes, regularly taking inspiration from Asian cuisine and offering just one surprise menu which is highly influenced by the passing seasons.

Name: OH30
Description: Although its interior design is stylishly modern, OH30 fully embraces the rustic charm of the 1904 windmill in which it is housed. The surrounding terrace is an oasis of calm. Chef Emile Maessen gives you two options: you can order delicious no-nonsense classics such as entrecôte Rossini à la carte, or opt for the more elaborate and creative set menu. Think steamed cod and lobster lasagne, topped with lightly browned Gruyère cheese and encircled by a delicate bisque. This dedicated and inspired chef possesses all the necessary attributes to delight the most discerning of foodies.

Name: La Trinité
Description: The lounge-style interior of La Trinité, in its beautiful waterfront location, is particularly inviting. Here, you can settle into your seat and enjoy the unique finger food on offer, in which the chef enjoys using Asian influences to add a trendy and international touch. His many years of experience is also evident in his classic cooking styles.

Name: JanZen
Description: Cosiness reigns supreme in this beautiful Art Deco building surrounded by tranquil polders, where you will be spoilt by your hosts Jeroen and Natasja van Hensbergen. The tasting menus are a must for those keen to experience the chef’s surprising creations. Attentive service, beautifully presented dishes and flavours to match!

Name: Danyel
Description: Danyel van den Bongard is a veteran of the Maastricht food scene who knows his classics well. Experience his cuisine for yourself in this pleasant restaurant with its French bistro feel, and enjoy delicious dishes that are rich, unctuous, succulent… In short, you can eat like a king here! House specialities such as the foie gras and sweetbreads are simply exquisite.

Name: Vanille
Description: The locals (Belgian and Dutch) flock to this snug restaurant, whose vintage floor tiles immediately catch the eye. The menu is carefully crafted, subtle and deliciously in tune with the zeitgeist. The inspired chef bends over backwards to rustle up fine fare to the delight of his patrons.

Name: Restaurant Chocolat
Description: Beneath the gaze of elegant women on pictures adorning the walls to the trendy chocolate-coloured furniture, Chocolat exudes a “sexy” ambience. The overall feel is enhanced by Dorus Clement’s equally exciting creativity in the kitchen where he toys with a palette of varied flavours and is never frightened of introducing delicacies such as vadouvan and yuzu in his French-inspired recipes, showcasing his willingness to experiment.

Name: Fabuleux
Description: Fabuleux is a trendy restaurant with a classic decor in its front dining room and a more intimate ambience to the rear. On arrival, your gaze is immediately drawn to the striking wine “library”, from which host Paul van Gestel selects the best bottles. Chef Busio creates updated and beautifully presented dishes which are full of classic flavour.

Name: Landgoed Groenendaal
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: What a magnificent location! Set in the beautiful Groenendaal forest, this former coach house exudes luxury and boasts a terrace that is among the loveliest in the region. The chef likes to draw on the finest ingredients when devising his set menus (one of which is vegetarian). Diners can therefore indulge in a rich terrine of foie gras as well as a carrot dish prepared with miso, pumpkin and yellow curry. This fresh and unfussy take on authentic flavours never disappoints.

Name: De Herberg van Smallingerland
Description: Dating back to 1791, this charming inn is full of character and extremely popular. Tables in the gorgeous courtyard garden are in high demand, as are the guestrooms. With a special emphasis on vegetables, Chef Freddy and son Jurmen showcase Frisian cuisine at its best. For instance, they will draw on the distinct flavours of beetroot, cherries and capers to give a fillet of red mullet a special twist. The menu at de Herberg is full of surprises!

Name: Rantrée
Address: Het Wilhelmus 30 L, Maastricht, 6216 GK, Netherlands
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Great view,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus
Description: Rantrée welcomes you to its eclectic restaurant on the eighth floor of the Dormio Resort hotel. The interior radiates a golden glow and affords magnificent views of Maastricht and its surroundings. Diners have the choice between à la carte options showcasing first-rate ingredients and an appealing set menu (vegan version available). The chef unites French technique with complex Asian flavours; think prawn seasoned with a koji and dill oil vinaigrette. He takes pride in the beautiful presentation of his dishes and also has an interesting wine list up his sleeve.

Name: TOV
Description: TOV stands for Team Onvergetelijk Verrassend (literally, an unforgettably surprising team), giving an indication of what is in store at this trendy restaurant. The young staff are full of enthusiasm and everything is organised just as it should be. Resolutely contemporary-style cuisine created by an imaginative chef.

Name: In den Doofpot
FacilitiesAndServices: Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: Enjoy an aperitif on the restaurant’s boat or on the terrace overlooking the water before sampling cuisine which pays real tribute to the history of Leiden. In this trendy restaurant, a highly imaginative chef serves subtle and precise reinterpretations of classic dishes, while the extensive wine list is a veritable Bible!

Name: 't Pakhuus
Description: This restaurant's designer decor is delightful, with a moss-clad wall that brings a touch of nature into the dining room. However, the ultimate appeal of this historical warehouse is its view of the harbour and the shrimp boats. Fish and seafood are the speciality of the house – the centrepiece is the fish tank, which is replenished daily. Think fresh Wadden oysters or scallops, enhanced by Asian flavours such as ponzu, ginger and pimento. Of course, the menu also features other local delicacies, such as Texel lamb. To cap it all off, why not spend the night in one of the designer suites?

Name: Amused Food & Wine
Description: On one side is Next wine bar, which is a stylish and trendy spot in which to sample vinologist Corine Vink's latest finds, served with freshly prepared bar snacks. Then there is the elegant restaurant with its chic decor, where Chiel de Groot incorporates his creative ideas into a surprise menu and beautifully presented plates of food. He likes to use produce from his own vegetable garden to bring his creations to life. Intensity is his guiding principle: a grilled sandwich filled with game stew, for instance, makes for an original accompaniment to a medium-rare roe fillet, an exquisite game jus and a cream sauce with chanterelles. Prepare to be surprised with every bite!

Name: Fris
Description: Meticulously prepared sea bass terrine, perfectly fried veal sweetbreads, koji butter (fermented on site) and a penchant for exotic flavours such as coconut milk and kombu – the culinary worlds of France and Asia meet at Fris. Classic techniques, top-of-the-range ingredients and playful originality bring the dishes to life. The non-alcoholic beverage accompaniments include delicious kombuchas made using kitchen scraps, among other things.

Name: Catch by Simonis
Address: Dr. Lelykade 43, The Hague, 2583 CL, Netherlands
Description: No, you are not in New York, although this impressive restaurant in the Scheveningen marina would not look out of place there with its highly fashionable decor, prestigious bottles adorning the wine walls, and luxury terrace on which to soak up the trendy atmosphere… Talk about a hip hangout! Fish and seafood steal the show in traditional dishes, seafood specialities, sushi etc. Whether classically prepared by frying in butter or drawn into original creations, the flavours of the sea take pride of place here.

Name: Den Burgh
Description: This impressive farmhouse dating from 1859 has retained its original charm and gained in elegance since its refurbishment. Inlaid with golden coins, the main bar is sure to draw the eye, as is the terrace. This bustling establishment is popular with business people, not only due to its proximity to a business park and the airport. The extensive menu includes appetisers, salads, steak tartare and bouillabaisse. The succulent pan-fried halibut accompanied by an exquisite fish sauce shows that, although the dishes may have a modern look, they are rooted in beautiful classic flavours.

Name: Sukade
Description: Produce from all over the world, including succade (candied citrus peel), was once traded in this monumental warehouse dating back to 1860. Today, it is incorporated into contemporary cuisine served in an impressive setting that takes full advantage of its location on Stoombootkade (grab a table on the waterfront terrace if possible!). The dishes draw on influences from around the globe; succulent poussin breast, for instance, is given a twist with Asian spices. The chef finds creative ways to put vegetables and fruit in the limelight. The lunch and finger food options are slightly simpler, the evening menu more elaborate.

Name: Hofstede Meerzigt
FacilitiesAndServices: Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Zoetermeer harbours a secret oasis that is waiting to be discovered. This enchanting estate boasts a chef’s table in a wine barn, a wedding venue in a converted stable, a terrace overlooking a lush garden, not to mention a stylish restaurant in a converted 17C farmhouse. The hospitality here is genuine, as is the kitchen team's appreciation of their ingredients. Alain Adriaanse shares his passion by delivering dishes that give familiar flavours the odd twist. With an Asian touch and fresh flavours, he elevates the sea bass tartare to new heights. He also puts a unique spin on steak tartare by adding playful textures. The extensive wine list is the icing on the cake.

Name: Hoog Holten
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Your experience at Hoog Holten begins with the drive there: the charm of the surrounding Salland countryside is captivating in itself. The terrace of this romantic establishment, housed in an old hunting lodge, happens to be one of the most beautiful in the country! Brasserie Birds keeps things traditional – go to the restaurant for more varied, contemporary cuisine. The set menu changes daily, but always seeks inspiration abroad for its sometimes truly innovative dishes.

Name: Oostergoo
Description: Oostergoo is an ideal base from which to explore the picturesque town of Grou and, for that matter, the lovely province of Friesland – starting with a visit to this beautiful marina terrace. It's quite an experience! The old Dutch interior, with its Delftware and lovely parquet flooring, is no less enchanting. They serve up an authentic brand of traditional cuisine. The locally caught smoked eel is a real treat!

Name: Wilhelminapark
FacilitiesAndServices: Garden or park,Great view,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: Utrecht's city park is an ideal spot to unwind, and where better to do that than in this stylish restaurant with its authentic thatched roof and idyllic terrace overlooking the magnificent lake? Wilhelminapark has been a fixture since 1926, and you'll notice that right away. The chef wins diners over with both a rather classic fish dish accompanied by a rich beurre blanc and a steak tartare with an Asian twist. The wine pairings are equally impressive. Or just drop in to enjoy a drink and some delicious oysters.

Name: Red Chilli
Description: Asia is a world away from the peaceful polders but this intimate restaurant creates a real Eastern ambience. Its fusion Asian cuisine is authentic yet modern in style. Red Chilli will definitely spice up your evening!

Name: Dell'arte
Description: Robbert Dellaert has transformed his childhood home, dating from 1878, into a restaurant with a romantic feel. This is an intimate space with a beautiful garden. Thanks to Julie's excellent service, you can just relax and delight in the love that the chef expresses for his terroir – Zeelandic Flanders. He treats local produce with reverence, and his well-thought-out combinations create a sense of depth. For instance, he enhances ultra-fresh soused herring with avocado ice cream, yuzu gel and sweet and sour daikon. A unique culinary adventure!

Name: Kaagman & Kortekaas
Description: Giel Kaagman and Bram Kortekaas have clearly chosen to focus on quality in their lively bistro, where the chef enjoys working with vegetables, wild game and fish, transforming these ingredients into exciting dishes which are striking for their contrasting flavours. Both the menu, which changes regularly, and the wine list are full of surprises!

Name: Café Caron
Description: This cosy bistro is run by Alain Caron (a well-known TV personality and chef) and his family. The ambience here is typically French, as is the menu which features traditional, generous bistro-style dishes which are a work of art in their own right. Trying out the à la carte here is a real joy.

Name: De Kluizenaer
Description: This former savings bank has been converted into a restaurant with a touch of industrial decor, with large drawings providing a bit of fun. The internationally seasoned chef brings punchy flavours to the plate to present his own vision of gastronomy. His cuisine is resolutely contemporary, involving robust taste combinations.

Name: De Koetsier
Description: A romantic atmosphere reigns supreme at De Koetsier. Shades of blue and pink provide the colourful modernised decor at this auberge without taking anything away from its authenticity. An old wardrobe has even been converted into a cheese store! Martijn will be delighted to share his passion for wine, while Ayesta brings elegance and a subtle modernity to the kitchen.

Name: Trattoria Da Giulio
Description: Giulio keeps the traditions of his native Sardinia alive in this cheerful trattoria. He makes his own pasta and bread every day, and the orata (gilt-head bream) in a salt crust is even filleted at the table. Here the Italian art of simplicity is at its most exuberant. House-made pappardelle with a creamy duck sauce, an aromatic panna cotta topped with a subtly flavoured juniper jam... Da Giulio is undeniably the best Italian in Arnhem!

Name: THE DUCHESS
Description: This upscale brasserie in what was once a waiting room of KAS Bank exudes the captivating charm of the Belle Époque. Features such as dark marble, impressive chandeliers, antique clocks and stunning stained-glass windows create an intimate setting. The extensive menu is inspired by Mediterranean culinary tradition, with a particular emphasis on southern France and Italy. Classics such as beef Wellington and tagliolini cacio e pepe are served in generous portions, without any unnecessary frills. The weekend afternoon tea is a real treat.

Name: Nassau
Description: A centuries-old beamed ceiling, glossy parquet flooring, sleek furniture design and views of the beautiful Prinsentuin walled garden – you really dine in style at Groningen's Nassau. The chef knows the importance of an intense sauce and loves working with top-notch produce such as langoustine and Anjou pigeon, which he showcases in elaborate dishes. For instance, he elevates hamachi, along with a medley of vegetables and seasonings, with a Thai-style sauce made with miso, coconut and lemongrass. His plant-based creations are equally remarkable. A beautifully curated wine list featuring an interesting range of German wines has the perfect accompaniment in store. Sophistication is in Nassau's very DNA.

Name: Sizzles at the Park
Description: The monumental building that provides the setting for Sizzles is truly impressive – the contemporary elegance, trendy ambience and terrace almost whisk you away to Ibiza! You can eat here morning, noon and night, enjoying Leon Habers’ family-inspired and highly original dishes that include a dynamic twist, a hint of Asia and an acidic touch. Fascinating!

Name: Le Nord
Description: This authentic farmhouse dating from 1885 combines rural charm and modern design – the ideal setting in which to experience Grégory Nicole's cuisine. The finesse with which this French chef pays tribute to his homeland is a testament to his expertise. More modern inspirations add a dash of excitement without overcomplicating things. He surprises diners with, for instance, his own take on Poire Williams, or a beautiful cod fillet infused with zesty notes. Be sure to try the tuna pizza, a tribute to master chef Joop Braakhekke. Le Nod is also a sure bet at lunchtime!

Name: Tante Blanche
Description: In this contemporary restaurant Charles Ek honours the memory of his aunt’s fine cooking. Enjoy delicious, fresh dishes that are simple, copious, full of flavour and exciting without being overstated.

Name: De Goede Gooier
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Great view,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: The thatched roof and trendy yet welcoming interior are a draw in their own right. However, it's the pergola and the gorgeous terrace overlooking the heathland that steals the show. The kitchen is run by a highly skilled chef who produces French cuisine with the utmost respect. The sole meunière and pan-fried foie gras do not disappoint with their robust flavours, but the chef also has some surprises up his sleeve, such as a swordfish carpaccio finished with a spicy harissa vinaigrette. There is an appealing lunch menu, an extensive dinner menu, and they are open every day for both lunch and dinner: a firm favourite!

Name: De Hemel
Address: Moeregrebstraat 35, Bergen op Zoom, 4611 JB, Netherlands
Description: Enjoy an intimate dinner in a romantic dining room, or on the rear terrace in fine weather, and choose from a selection of tasty dishes prepared in French style, with a nod to modern cuisine. A delightful dining experience.

Name: De Steenen Tafel
Address: Weg achter het Bos 1, Arnhem, 6822 LV, Netherlands
Description: Fans of fine food put on their Sunday best to dine at this elegant conservatory restaurant on the edge of the pretty Klarenbeek park (what a view!). They come here for the traditionally prepared lobster or the wild game from the Veluwe region, although the chef also prepares more original fare such as the occasional oriental dish with foie gras. Rich, authentic cuisine is to the fore here.

Name: Dorset
Description: Dorset is intimate and trendy, with a pleasant lounge atmosphere. Chef Davy Roord will delight you with his modern fusion of local ingredients and Asian flavours. This enthusiastic cuisine is occasionally innovative and always fresh. Guest satisfaction is the priority here, both on the plate and in the wine glass!

Name: Lagrange
Description: Picture the scene: You are in the lovely town of Buren, and step into an elegantly converted barn in anticipation of an intimate dinner. The dishes served embody a modern take on French cuisine. The chef knows how to cook a fillet of wild duck to perfection, for example, but also makes his mark by seasoning leg rillettes with hoisin. At Lagrange, flavours from the local area and around the globe go hand in hand.

Name: Bij Brons
Description: At John and Yvonne Brons’ restaurant you can enjoy good food in a cosy pavilion, right in the harbour area of Almere-Haven, where fresh fish is served in season (outside the spawning period) straight from the sea onto your plate. The meat dishes are also a fine example of chef Brons’ focus on quality. Generous classic cuisine offering a delightful dining experience.

Name: Restaurant Bakboord
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Great view,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: The view you have here of Almere's marina as the boats sail away is quite something to behold. The lounge terrace is a great place to sit, but equally charming is the contemporary decor indoors. The dishes, which showcase vegetables, are brimming with creative enthusiasm. They are elaborate, even daring at times, and always display technical mastery. There are plenty of delicious vegetarian options on the à la carte menu should you wish to avoid meat and fish.

Name: Rue de la Plume
Description: Everything about this inviting restaurant makes it clear that Luella and Madelene are passionate about what they do. Luella likes nothing better than to amaze her guests with her contemporary surprise menu. Her dishes revolve around a main ingredient of the finest quality, elaborate garnishes and velvety sauces that bring it all together. The wines recommended by Madelene complement the intense flavours beautifully. This duo's enthusiasm is infectious!

Name: Bridges
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: Fish reigns supreme at this sleek restaurant, which also offers a beautiful view of the canals. Salted delicacies take centre stage in dishes that are distinctly contemporary in style. The chef combines classic sauces with the occasional Asian twist to showcase the fresh flavours of his ingredients.

Name: De Saffraan
Description: This old clipper moored in the canal has been converted into an elegant and intimate restaurant with a terrace on the deck where you can while away the hours. De Saffraan really is an exceptional restaurant with great service provided by charming waitstaff. Chef van Wechem has a penchant for punchy flavours and innovative techniques, handling top-notch ingredients with finesse. For instance, he elevates fried turbot with a wonderfully robust beach crab jus and adds coconut for depth. This place has real personality!

Name: Gaar
Description: The world is Joachim Müller's culinary playground. Generous dishes such as Limburg pork terrine or crispy tortilla with Asian-style marinated tuna and wasabi give expression to the chef's sense of fun. The extensive and varied menu never disappoints, and diners will enjoy the interesting wine pairings. Chef Joachim and front-of-house manager Myrthe make it their mission to show guests a good time. The pops of turquoise in the decor are in keeping with the convivial spirit of this place.

Name: Oan Tafel
Description: 80% homegrown produce and vegetables, the remaining meat and fish comes from further afield. Such is the concept of this natural restaurant, whose interior sports raw materials, a handsome counter and a casual vibe. Eastern exuberance meets Frisian temperance. Fermentations, sweet and sour touches, surprising flavours… Intriguing!

Name: Bar BAUT
Description: With its Banksy-style frescoes, trendy, intimate interior and delightfully relaxed ambience, Bar BAUT is a must in Amsterdam, where guests can choose from the enticing à la carte featuring international ingredients cooked in contemporary style. Enjoy intense flavours, well-prepared produce and original ideas – plus excellent value for money!

Name: NOVO New Dining
Address: Aan de Brikkenbouw 4F, Maastricht, 6211 XT, Netherlands
Description: Rodny Welters has created his own little world on the fifth floor of this factory building in Maastricht's Sphinxkwartier. Rugged surfaces meet stylish upholstery here in a tasteful symbiosis. All eyes are on the open kitchen, where chef Welters lets his cooking do the talking; his culinary creations draw inspiration from around the globe, underpinned by exquisite sauces. With dishes such as haddock à la meunière with a tandoori velouté or fried scampi with a red curry and coconut milk sauce, the "Experience" set menu certainly lives up to its name.

Name: In de Oude Stempel
Description: In this former post office, stamps and letters have made way for the on-trend cuisine of Mark van Loon. This is a chef who doesn't hesitate to play with textures or bring bold combinations to the table. His creativity is complemented by his prowess in the art of making sauces – think a rich game jus to accompany the venison fillet. For something more low key, head to Puur, the brasserie next door.

Name: Witlof
Description: With the view of the River Waal, the jovial hostess and the chef who you see cooking as you make your way to use the facilities, at the Witlof, you will immediately feel at home. Jurgen Eikholt lovingly prepares classic cuisine with his trademark sophisticated, often oriental touches. Each dish on the menu can be ordered as a large or small portion.

Name: Sukerieje
Description: Sukerieje has now relocated to Hopmanshuis, a tastefully converted warehouse brimming with character. The menu has also been revamped. Chef Yannick Roodhof likes to focus on vegetables and enjoys expressing his creative side – his creamy cashew nut 'pâté with melon and chilli causes quite a stir. Through his expertise in using exotic ingredients and his patience in imbuing his sauces with depth, he creates an exceptional intensity of flavours. This restaurant is going places!

Name: Ni Hao
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: This restaurant with an intimate Eastern feel introduces its guests to “chistro” dishes, a combination of bistro and Chinese cuisine. Chef Chen creates delicious contemporary dishes, which are made to share and which include specialities from Sichuan, Guangdong, Beijing and Wenzhou. An innovative approach to authentic Chinese cuisine.

Name: Ron Gastrobar Indonesia
Description: Top chef Ron Blaauw has a nose for a winning concept, as proven by this typical Indonesian restaurant with its bustling terrace by the River Amstel. The flavours are distinctively Asian, but he and his colleague Agus Hermawan also add their own twists for that extra fragrance and depth. The rijsttafel options "Agus" (15 dishes) and "Tim" (12 dishes) provide the perfect opportunity to share all kinds of delicious treats, such as satay kambing and udang peteh.

Name: NY Basement
Description: A jazzy vibe reigns supreme in the cellar of the New York hotel, which is reminiscent of the Big Apple of the 1920s and 1930s. After a delicious cocktail at the 11m-long bar, guests can enjoy the modern cuisine on offer here. Choose from a delicious fish or meat dish, vegetables prepared on the charcoal grill and an array of trendy suggestions.

Name: Amber Garden
Address: Van Heuven Goedhartlaan 15, Amstelveen, 1181 LE, Netherlands
Description: Amber Garden is a lavish, swanky Chinese restaurant, whose guiding line is authenticity, as the house specialty, roast duck, demonstrates. The chef enjoys adding the occasional western touch and cannot be rivalled for his ability to subtly blend texture, taste and fresh produce. A tantalising insight into Chinese cooking.

Name: YANO
Description: Scandinavian minimalist design, a Japanese Zen vibe and a convivial atmosphere are the defining features of YANO. You will be welcomed by the charming Britta before the highly experienced chef Yuri lets his cooking do the talking. His dishes are vibrant and skilfully seasoned. His culinary style has French foundations, yet he also draws on his Moluccan roots and other influences from far-flung places. Whether he is combining pigeon with pumpkin and coffee or langoustine with pipián verde and huacatay, his creativity knows no bounds and never fails to impress.

Name: De Monnikendam
Description: Originally part of Amersfoort's second city wall, Monnickendam is a watergate dating back to the early 15C. Today, this piece of history has been repurposed to create a unique culinary destination. There are intimate dining spaces within the towers and a waterside terrace affording wonderful views. Thanks to the enthusiasm of hostess Kristel and chef Richard, this establishment has made a name for itself. With each course, the tasting menu seamlessly navigates between the familiar and the exotic: Think hamachi accompanied by a tangy ponzu, or lamb saddle with a crispy crust and a lamb jus infused with rosemary, thyme and wild garlic oil. A memorable dining experience!

Name: Neder
Description: At Neder, they are committed to working with local produce. From Eastern Scheldt salt and wild-harvested herbs to Veluwe red deer and Texel mustard seeds, everything, including the drinks, comes from within a 223km radius. What they don't grow themselves is sourced from responsible suppliers. This approach presents numerous challenges, but it also inspires chefs to be more creative. They bring each season to life with a new set menu, building on a foundation of ingredients preserved using a variety of methods. Marinated hogweed flowers and a chamomile beurre blanc lend the steamed pike-perch a fresh, floral lift. Summer venison is rubbed with wheat koji for that umami flavour – this is sophisticated, aromatic and innovative cuisine. The fact that Neder is an ambassador for the Dutch terroir is also expressed in the interior design, with its landscape paintings, visible fermentation room and a combination of rusticity and soothing natural materials.

Name: Bistro Pinot
Description: Are you in Friesland and dreaming of a getaway to Paris? Then make your way through the lovely streets of Grou to this delightful bistro. The nostalgic wall tiles, the marble counter and wooden stools, the French music pouring out of the speakers… This place has real character! Bistro classics are prepared in time-honoured tradition here: succulent foie gras on brioche, zesty canard à l'orange, a crispy and wonderfully fresh macaroon tart. The dishes for sharing (choose at least four) transport you to those iconic bistros of the Parisian Left Bank.

Name: Het Sluishuys
Description: Hand-cut steak tartare with fine acidity, turbot à la meunière with a beurre blanc cooked in time-honoured tradition and ravioli stuffed with oxtail: these are the kind of classic dishes for which Erik Hendriksen is renowned. At this warm and welcoming restaurant, in an idyllic location by an old lock and close to a small harbour, familiar flavours are given the attention they deserve.

Name: Troef
Description: This bistro exudes an endlessly appealing nostalgic charm, as well as a fully à la carte menu and a chef who is able to impart his infectious enthusiasm to his team and to diners. In short, it has enough aces up its sleeve to convince any self-respecting foodie. First and foremost among them is the creative spin the chef puts on classic French dishes. Take, for instance, his perfectly cooked langoustines, topped with slivers of lardo di Colonnata and served with a delicate butter sauce infused with vin jaune and vanilla. Troef epitomises the laid-back vibe of Amsterdam!

Name: CouCou
Description: With the mixologist doing their thing behind the imposing bar, the hip CouCou is reminiscent of a London cocktail bar. Whether you prefer to watch the chefs work their magic or enjoy a more intimate meal, this chic establishment has the perfect table for you. The wide range of sharing options on the menu is equally appealing and on trend. These are inspired by French and Mediterranean cuisines and given an original twist. Take the beautifully crispy fried lobster and prawn roulade finished with a lobster bisque gel and velvety pine nut cream. Délicieux !

Name: The Church
Address: Ir J.P. Van Muijlwijkstraat 19A, Arnhem, 6828 BP, Netherlands
Description: With its stained-glass windows, sculptures, murals and old pews, this Lutheran church has been beautifully preserved. The juxtaposition of modern opulence with the venue's rich past is truly inspired. Take in the spectacle of the open kitchen while enjoying a meal prepared right before your eyes. Nestled in the church's rafters, there are a few cosy guestrooms. But first, it's time to let yourself be spoiled by Bart Leussink, a chef who embraces creativity and boldness in his cooking. For instance, he elevates lamb neck with a crispy herb crust and lamb fillet with a vibrant sweet-and-sour cucumber garnish and a rich lamb jus. The chef has a penchant for fish and seafood dishes, into which he likes weave zesty flavours. An extraordinary experience!

Name: Restaurant Renilde
Description: Renilde Hammacher-van den Brande served as a curator at the Museum Boijmans van Beuningen for many years and would no doubt have been proud of the restaurant that bears her name. Located in a creatively landscaped rooftop garden on the sixth floor of what is now Depot Boijmans, this place affords stunning views over the city. In the afternoon, the restaurant is reserved for museum visitors; in the evening, it opens its doors to everyone who wishes to discover chef De Jong's surprise menu. This creative chef has a penchant for vegetables and bold combinations. His culinary audacity shines through in his sublime combination of elderflower ice cream, the subtle bitterness of Belgian endive caramel and rhubarb root. Prepare to be blown away!

Name: De Salentein
Description: Argentina and Uruguay are the main sources of inspiration for the elegant De Salentein. Not only does the menu feature the traditional cuisines of those countries, with dishes such as chimichurri and empanadas, but the restaurant even raises its own beef cattle and has its own winery in Argentina. Led by chef Rik Jansma, the kitchen team elevates robust South American flavours with a touch of sophistication. The distinctive aromas of a sea bass ceviche, for instance, are enhanced with a leche del tigre vinaigrette. Cooked to perfection over flames, the picanha is paired with a rich brown sauce. For something a little more down-to-earth, head to Bodega Portillo, housed in the same building. A Latin American adventure awaits!

Name: Restaurant Uijttewaal
Description: Chef Sven and his brother, sommelier Lars Uijttewaal, warmly welcome you into their chic and stylish establishment. A timeless interior design and a tasteful blend of warm tones combine to create a pleasant atmosphere. Their fresh cuisine follows current trends, as demonstrated by their signature amuse-bouche – an ode to their grandfather, who owned a pickle company: a refreshing sweet-and-sour piccalilli sorbet served with sweet-and-sour pickle creams and a carrot coulis finished with dill oil. The menu intrigues from start to finish (they also serve lunch), with dishes such as steak tartare with ponzu or a delicate pairing of sole and morels. The excellent wine list, with plenty of options by the glass, is also worthy of your attention.

Name: Holsterhof
Description: With the hard work of hostess Lissa and chef Kaj, the restaurant at Holsterhof camping farm has gradually evolved into a sought-after culinary destination, set in a modern, light-filled space surrounded by lush greenery. The service is relaxed and friendly. The chef is an expert sauce maker who creates daring combinations on the plate, without making things overly complicated. His exquisite red curry with coconut milk adds depth of flavour to the tender quail leg with black lentils. Working with two set menus, he consistently surprises with subtle nuances.

Name: Heimat
Description: This restaurant has a laid-back and refreshingly natural feel; its name reflects chef Niels van Zijl's deep emotional connection to his hometown (Heimat) of Utrecht. Furthermore, it highlights his unwavering attention to the provenance of his ingredients. He makes a point of working with local suppliers and lets vegetables take centre stage, but fish and meat options are also available. His cuisine is creative and light. For instance, he ferments roasted potato skins to create a dashi, the base for an airy steamed chawanmushi. Stewed leeks, ramson oil, chive florets and tangy tobiko lend deep layers of flavour to this exuberant creation. Intriguing!

Name: Lilou
Description: This restaurant set in a row of townhouses in the centre of Goes evokes the spirit of Paris. Round marble-topped tables, high ceilings, tiled floors, French chansons – this bistro has it all. Both the tempting menu and the wines also draw on French tradition. Well-seasoned hand-cut steak tartare; pan-fried sea bream accompanied by a rich beurre blanc with fresh, zesty notes; a shellfish platter, or profiteroles with vanilla ice cream and chocolate sauce: diners are spoilt for choice! If in need of recommendations, ask the amiable hostess, who will be happy to help.

Name: Novaela
Description: Novaela encapsulates the magic of the Bagijnhof, a historical beguinage. The blend of upscale contemporary design and old architectural features is unique – as, for example, in the oval stone counter and the wooden beams. Daniel Duijster Gomero's cuisine is all about creativity, excitement and beautiful presentation. His surprise menu features some daring ideas such as the unexpectedly harmonious combination of razor clams and beetroot, but also familiar dishes like succulent quail fillet with an exquisite jus. You only have the choice of a six-course set menu and lunch, but you are definitely in safe hands with this chef.

Name: Brasserie Mijn Streek
Description: Cold or hot dishes, whether to share with your dining companions or go solo, to opt for one of the many vegetarian options or plump for fish or meat… In this convivial brasserie on the fifth floor of the Glaspaleis, there are plenty of choices to be made. Brace yourself for an international culinary adventure that takes in ceviche, ravioli, strawberry Romanoff and many other mouth-watering treats. A visit to the Schunck Museum in the same building is a must if you visit the area.

Name: Villa Coucou-La cuisine d'Alexandre
Address: Laan Van Meerdervoort 6, The Hague, 2517 AJ, Netherlands
Description: With its parquet floors, marble tables and walls adorned with works of art, the luxurious Villa Coucou, one of The Hague’s shining culinary lights, is not short on style! Enjoy a cocktail at the bar or in the wine cellar (which even has space for a game of boules!) before savouring the revisited classics of French cuisine. The chef here is passionate about top-quality ingredients and enjoys toying with intense aromas and light textures.

Name: Restaurant De Olliemölle
Description: Picture the scene: a table by the water, with water lilies floating nearby and an old-fashioned water wheel turning occasionally. Could it be more romantic? Rest assured that De Olliemölle is every bit as enchanting inside. Roel Sieverink has a soft spot for French cuisine and loves serving lobster straight from his lobster tank. The bisque here is full-bodied and spicy, the foie gras terrine is juicy and the veal jus with crispy sweetbreads is deliciously intense. The chef adds the odd modern twist to his classic dishes, introducing brighter flavours while maintaining the rich, hearty taste that his cuisine is known for.

Name: MANO Restaurant
Description: Hermanos Daniël and Kevin have been best friends since childhood. In their elegant little establishment, which has preserved the charm of this corner building, they showcase their combined experience. The food is contemporary, featuring intense sauces, an interplay of fresh and zingy flavours, and multiple international influences. Here, technically crafted creations and vigorous creativity go mano a mano.

Name: Sinck
Description: Locals and tourists alike love to meet up at this bustling place. This old building on the Prinsengracht boasts a charming waterfront terrace and a lovely bistro-style interior. The renowned wine list (there is a wine bar at basement level) and modern culinary creations complement each other perfectly. The chef has a no-nonsense approach to cooking – a few elements that are full of flavour plus sauces for a fine accompaniment. This is Amsterdam at its coolest!

Name: Le Sable
Description: This old farmhouse radiates all the charm of the peaceful hamlet of Zandoerle – diners will particularly enjoy the welcome given by the ducks. Inside, the hushed and intimate ambience combines rusticity with modern elegance. They may be young, but chef Chiel and maître d' Laura bring a wealth of talent and experience to the table, delivering cuisine that reflects their youthful enthusiasm. Although he draws primarily on French cuisine tradition, the chef likes to add his own twist, serving dishes in a series of small plates. Think candied lamb, alongside a lamb shoulder stew (with a wonderfully intense jus!) and a medium-rare rack of lamb. The palpable sense of ambition at Le Sable makes it all the more appealing.

Name: Domenica
Description: Domenica is the place to come to experience the bustling Jordaan neighbourhood. Whether you are dining outside on the terrace or inside at the bar of this modern bistro, there is always a lively atmosphere here. Authentic Italian seasonal dishes are served up with great skill and a proper sense of generosity. Think octopus with crispy skin and tender meat served alongside robust bell pepper and broccoletti. Owner Flavio pays tribute to his heritage with every vibrant plate. Be sure to check out his French and Italian wine selections too.

Name: De Dyck
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: De Dyck puts the spotlight on sustainability: a 5 000m² vegetable garden that supplies the majority of the fruit, vegetables and herbs; wines that are sourced within a 500km radius, and pigs that are reared on site and fed on kitchen leftovers. The decor of this attractive farm located amid the polders also reflects this focus on its natural surroundings. Freshly harvested produce and preserved ingredients are combined to great effect. Whether drawing on fermentations, creams or dishes prepared on the barbecue, this sophisticated cuisine puts a creative spin on what the local terroir has to offer.

Name: Morille
Description: At Morille, they strive to source all their produce from within a 15km radius of the restaurant. It feels like nature has taken root in this cosy place – and with good reason. Floris Vriens has taken over the reins and is maintaining the restaurant's commitment to sustainability: ingredients harvested from his own kitchen garden, foraged in the wild or purchased from producers in the vicinity are presented in a 14-course set menu accompanied by drinks sourced solely from the Netherlands and Belgium. This inspired, modern culinary approach – with its respect for micro-seasons – is an ode to Zeeland's (mostly vegetable-based) riches.

Name: Suzie's en Van Aken
Description: Chef Tom is no stranger to the concepts of nose-to-tail eating and zero waste. With a keen sense of the zeitgeist, this is a creative chef who draws inspiration from his extensive travels, especially to Asia. For example, a beurre blanc sauce with dashi that adds depth to a salty dish based on oyster and samphire. The jovial Suzanne plays her part, serving up excellent wine and dessert recommendations. The natural vibe of this cosy establishment will make your dinner that little bit more enjoyable.

Name: Rozewied
Description: Rozewied, "poppy" in Zeelandic, is the joint venture of Ferdy and Noëmie. The two of them do everything themselves in this centuries-old building, into which they have breathed new life, while taking care to preserve its historical character. In the kitchen, classical combinations are given a modern twist. Lamb, for example, is paired with garlic, but with the lightness and playfulness expected by today's diners. The chefs give pride of place to European produce, and have a penchant for fish dishes and delicate sauces.

Name: Het Seminar
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Het Seminar is an ode to nature that adopts "farm to fork" as its guiding principle. A former monastery, this upscale restaurant stands in its own grounds. From fruit and vegetables to livestock, everything is grown or reared on site – the focus is on sustainability. The chef invites you to create your own set menu from an array of classic-style dishes that showcase bold flavours and the freshest ingredients. For example, he expertly pan-fries duck breast to a rosy pink, elevating it with a lemongrass-infused duck jus; this is served with vegetable accompaniments such as broad beans and caramelised onion, which provides a touch of sweetness. At Het Seminar, the fertility of the Dutch soil speaks for itself.

Name: Lime
Description: The open kitchen immediately catches the eye at the contemporary Lime, which also has a charming veranda. A table by the kitchen is a must if you want to see accomplished chef Ysbrandt Wermenbol at work. He gives traditional dishes a carefully considered personal twist, often taking inspiration from Mediterranean and Asian cuisine. His surprising ideas dare to be complex, while retaining a sense of generosity and balance.

Name: Katseveer
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Great view,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: Having taken over Katseveer, chef Leon Vermaire and maître d' and sommelier Paul Labruijere are steadily finding their feet. For many years, they have been working at this restaurant that showcases the best of what Eastern Scheldt has to offer. This former ferry waiting room commands stunning views of passing ships and the surrounding countryside.Zeeland produce reigns supreme in chef Vermaire's culinary world. Whether Zeeland venison or North Sea crab, top-notch, locally sourced ingredients play the starring role. His dishes – often really creative – are beautifully crafted and frequently use acidic Asian flavours for that fresh twist.

Name: Harry's
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: This luxury brasserie is as cosmopolitan as it is vibrant. French flair characterises both the ambience and the cuisine. On the menu, international flavours and vegetarian options show that the chefs are keeping up with the times, but not at the expense of the golden rules of superior brasserie cuisine. The kitchen garden is a manifestation of their sustainable approach (more details on the website). Creative, local, seasonal: Harry's ticks all the boxes!

Name: Kruiden & Jasmijn
Description: Located just inside the historical city walls, this is an elegantly appointed restaurant featuring modern art and imposing chandeliers. The terrace exudes tranquillity, and the attentive service creates a warm and welcoming atmosphere. A passionate advocate for local produce, chef Patrick de Rade especially loves Eastern Scheldt lobster when it is in season. He also regularly harvests fruit and vegetables from his garden. Sourced from a friendly local farmer, red cabbage adds a touch of sweetness to his venison fillet, perfectly complementing the sweet-and-sour pickled red beets. His rich sauces are testament to his culinary expertise and generosity.

Name: Nolet's Vistro
Description: Zeeland oysters, grilled lobster and smoked eel from the Eastern Scheldt are just a few of the reasons why you’ll want to book a table in this charming bistro. Here, you won’t find any unnecessary fuss, just pure cuisine based around superb ingredients of the freshest quality. A generous spirit is also part of the Nolet’s Vistro DNA!

Name: La Mère Anne
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: La Mère Anne is a huge business encompassing a range of activities. You can hire the venue for parties, spend the night in modern guestrooms, but above all, enjoy good food! The chef favours regional produce, which he showcases in contemporary dishes. These steer clear of frills, focusing instead on straightforward, delicious flavours.

Name: Salon de Provence
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: An ambitious duo has taken over this cosy restaurant in which distinguished service, meticulously selected wines and creative, lovingly prepared cuisine are to the fore. Vegetables play a predominant (and playful) role here, while inspirations from around the globe, with a small focus on South Africa, are also evident on the menu and wine list.

Name: De Voetangel
Address: Rondehoep Oost 3, Ouderkerk aan de Amstel, 1191 KA, Netherlands
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Great view,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: This cosy family restaurant rises up out of the Ronde Hoep polder, from where it enjoys magnificent views across pastureland and streams. The chefs here veer more towards the traditional, although modern dishes are starting to creep into their cuisine. Organic, vegetarian and international options give the menu extra appeal.

Name: Joia
Description: To share or not to share, that's the dilemma awaiting you at this charming brasserie. Once a café, it enjoys a picturesque location beside the canal and boasts a delightful waterside terrace. The enticing menu features international cuisine – deciding will not be easy. Will it be the creamy risotto with mushrooms, a venison dish with a rich cognac-based sauce and green peppercorns, or the yellowtail kingfish with Tomasu soy sauce and passion fruit? Joia has something for everyone. N.B. Simpler lunch menu.

Name: Elea
Description: Located in a grand building in the heart of The Hague, Elea is a modern restaurant with a Greek soul. This idea finds expression in a fabulous Mediterranean-style setting that incorporates natural materials. Takis Panagakis is an inventive chef who draws on Greek tradition, using ingredients such as smoked yoghurt, caper leaf and fava beans to lend his original creations an individual touch. Vegetables play an important role here, with top-notch vegetarian options, such as a celeriac Wellington. The charming Bibi is on hand to suggest some excellent wine pairings.

Name: Oxalis
Description: Prepare yourself to be blown away as you drive past fields full of red and white cabbages en route to this cosy little establishment housed in a former post office. Geoffrey van Melick cut his teeth at top-flight restaurants such as The Fat Duck and 't Nonnetje, and it shows in his selection of quality ingredients, the depth of his sauces and his meticulous garnishes. Take, for example, the perfectly pitched and beautifully reduced veal jus that accompanies the rich fillet of veal Rossini, with fine vegetable accompaniments that add their distinctive nuances. This chef proves that creativity need not be at odds with respect for tradition!

Name: Noble
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Great view,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Noble pays tribute to the rich history of this building, which once housed Chalet Royal. Having undergone a drastic makeover, the decor features a blend of sleek design and warm materials. Wine is a serious business here, which becomes clear when you see the imposing cabinet. Thanks to the small portions, you can explore how global influences and attention to freshness create tantalising flavours. We were delighted by the chocolate mousse with peanuts, unctuous ice cream with bay leaf, crunchy caramel and a citrus cream. The bold combinations on the extensive menu never fail to impress!

Name: Landgoed de Wilmersberg
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: At Landgoed de Wilmersberg nature takes centre stage, beginning with a wonderful view of the landscape of Twente, both on the terrace and in the charming dining room. The chef makes vegetables the focus in his modern dishes. He is bold enough to present the occasional challenging combination, always applying the correct techniques.

Name: Citrus
Description: Paul Hermes and Jill van Orsouw treat their guests like friends in their intimate, convivial restaurant. The chef, who can be seen at work on his “podium” to the rear of the dining room, likes to bring his carefully prepared dishes to the table himself. He prepares dishes which are full of different textures and flavours, showcasing exciting ideas and delighting guests with his rich cuisine.

Name: Het Roode Koper
Address: Jhr. Dr. C.J. Sandbergweg 82, Leuvenum, 3852 PV, Netherlands
Description: At Het Roode Koper, diners are immersed in the fairytale setting of a romantic decor that exudes luxury and sophistication, set against fabulous English gardens and the forests of the Veluwe all around. Dennis van den Beld's cuisine is rather classical but in keeping with the times. This translates into fabulous sauces, an emphasis on the produce and creative garnishes. The excellent wine list offers both prestigious bottles and finds from small wineries.

Name: Japans restaurant Shiro
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Notable sake list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus
Description: Shiro has been famed for serving traditional Japanese cuisine since 1989. In this intimate restaurant you will discover all the delights of kaiseki-ryori cuisine – a traditional interplay of intense flavours and subtle textures. Sushi made with the finest rice and ultra-fresh fish (it's best to order sushi when you make your reservation), beautifully crispy shrimp tempura, a deeply aromatic teriyaki sauce... Accompanied by exciting sake recommendations courtesy of your hostess.

Name: Hof van Herstal
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: What used to be the guesthouse of Lilbosch Abbey is now a classic fine dining restaurant with bags of character. Martin Bruggeman takes great pride in his work, presenting his suggestions to guests and proving every day that he is a master of traditional cuisine. Try the game dishes, especially the venison – the chef slaughters the game himself and showcases the distinctive intense flavour of the meat. His generous sauces are the best evidence of his culinary skill. You can trust his judicious wine recommendations too.

Name: Aan Sjuuteeänjd
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Sustainability takes centre stage at this cosy farmhouse restaurant with its eye-catching designer lighting. Even before it was trendy, chef Thoma was working with organic produce, mostly from his own vegetable garden. He has now even planted a food forest for the future. This ambassador of local Limburg produce proposes only a surprise menu, demonstrating his close ties with small-scale suppliers. Think rosefish from the North Sea, a beautifully grainy spelt risotto and a spicy/tangy beurre blanc sauce with nettles.

Name: Allemansgeest
Description: The Vliet canal provides the stunning backdrop to this former farmhouse with an elegant decor. The waterfront terrace (with mooring facilities) will take your breath away. This is the perfect setting in which to savour a modern approach to French cuisine that is replete with subtle exotic nuances. How about tuna with foie gras, foie gras ice cream and a spicy vinaigrette? A surprising culinary delight!

Name: Stiel Oriental
Description: Stiel exudes an Oriental vibe – with bright Eastern motifs, warm tones and wicker furnishings, this is as cosy as it gets and you immediately feel at home. The front-of-house team is beautifully in sync with the enthusiastic kitchen brigade, who you can see at work in the open kitchen. Often inspired by Indonesia, their wide range of dishes to share (a regular menu is also available) pack the spicy punch you would expect. House-made dim sum with veal and five spices, a rich curry with prawns, juicy satay kambing – this is a veritable feast for the taste buds!

Name: DIELS
Description: Dietmar and Elsko's restobar is a friendly, relaxed spot where diners can come for a full dinner or a pleasant drink. The chef draws inspiration from across the borders and serves modern dishes prepared with an eye for detail.

Name: 't Golfje
Description: Housed in a quintessential Terschelling farmhouse just outside Midsland, this is a charming restaurant where diners are made to feel right at home. The gorgeous natural surroundings not only foster a mood of tranquillity, but they also determine what ends up on your plate. Many of the ingredients are picked by the staff themselves or sourced from the restaurant's own vegetable garden. These then feature in modern dishes which also draw on Mediterranean and Asian influences. This is no-nonsense cuisine. Think a perfectly fried quail fillet, a robust chicken stock and Jerusalem artichoke in cream and deep-fried. Divine!

Name: Lokaal
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Nowadays, Villa Ruimzicht is both a hotel and home to this elegant and chic yet warm and welcoming restaurant. The name Lokaal can be translated as "classroom" and is a nod to the building's past as a school. But it is also much more than that: it reflects the commitment of Bjorn Massop and his team to sustainability. They source everything from vegetables to meat and fish from local small-scale suppliers who share their values. This dining experience is a real education. For instance, you will learn that coffee grounds are used to lend earthy notes to a medlar and sherry dessert. Embracing a zero-waste philosophy fuels the chef's innovation. For example, by fermenting spruce in a vegetable broth, he creates a harmonious accompaniment to trout from De Smallert fish farm. The set menu is a celebration of the riches of the Achterhoek terroir.

Name: Villa de Duinen
Address: Oude Zeeweg 74, Noordwijk aan Zee, 2202 CE, Netherlands
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: Arriving at this Anglo-Norman-style villa (1902) feels like coming home. The cosy interior, reminiscent of a cottage, and the endearing personality of the hostess are irresistible. The youthful kitchen team favours a resolutely modern approach to cooking. They play with textures, allow the main ingredient to shine and sometimes come up with surprisingly imaginative ideas. Hand them a butternut squash, and they will turn it into something amazing, with great technical skill and subtle influences from around the globe.

Name: Plantage 87
Cuisine: Modern Cuisine, Cuisine from the Marches
Description: The first thing that strikes you at Plantage 87 is the phenomenal view of the surrounding marina. Stephan Möllers's biggest source of inspiration, however, lies a little further away, in his generously sized vegetable garden. He likes to express his creativity by working with vegetables so that they yield the right acidity or spiciness to bring out the best of the main ingredient – letting it speak for itself.

Name: Pirandello
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Great view,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: A trendy restaurant with charming views of vines and a stork’s nest, as well as one of the most attractive outdoor terraces in the Netherlands! Both the cuisine and the wine list have a strong Italian focus, the former offering authentic flavours with the occasional daring twist. The option of overnight accommodation completes the picture.

Name: Restaurant De Lage Vuursche
Description: This restaurant was opened by Willem van Oosterom in 1865 and is now run by the fifth generation of his family. Authentic details, such as a fireplace and wooden tables, add to the charm of this quintessential Dutch café and restaurant, which also boasts a delightful terrace. The kitchen team takes pride in serving up traditional French cuisine. Perfectly pan-seared scallops with blood sausage and a rich bisque, crispy sweetbreads and succulent veal tongue with a Bordelaise sauce, and a delectable Eton Mess to finish: a symphony of flavours awaits! The nearby woods are ideal for a tranquil post-prandial stroll.

Name: Marque
Description: The open kitchen and spacious bar (which you can eat at) will grab your attention as soon as you walk into this former cheese warehouse (1618). The character of this property is enhanced by the elegant decor. Marque is proud of its Mediterranean soul, and the experienced head chef wins diners over with modern textures, delicate acidic touches, and all the panache and exuberance of the South.

Name: MARIO
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: A former inn on a dyke across from a canal. Italian cuisine featured on the single menu. Elaborate Italian wine list and excellent advice from the sommelier-owner. A handful of well-kept rooms with good bedding.

Name: De Beejekurf
Description: De Beejekurf manages to blend a cosy, inviting atmosphere with sophisticated elegance. Hostess Hanneke's warm welcome and attentive service make dinners feel at ease right away.
