Chef Mathijs Jacobs allows his local suppliers to dictate what goes into his set menu. His creativity knows no bounds, yet his dishes, although made with an eye for detail, are remarkably straightforward. For example, he transforms poached veal tenderloin with its exquisite jus and sweetbreads into an interesting concoction with aubergine, a hollandaise sauce espuma, potato mousseline and truffle. This is cuisine that packs a punch!

Name: Zheng
FacilitiesAndServices: Notable sake list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus
Description: Zheng takes you back to the banquets of Imperial China. Through a parade of small dishes, often served on three plates, you will discover the traditions of the four main branches of Chinese cuisine. The succulent Peking duck, with its crispy skin, is deservedly a signature dish – it is heavenly when paired with hoisin sauce and the house-made sambal! The typical tableware and objets d'art (also for sale) add to this unique dining experience. Subtle cuisine which nonetheless offers a wealth of flavours.

Name: Soigné
Description: At Soigné, which might be described as cosy and charming, you are in the right place to discover the contemporary culinary aspirations of Dennis Jong. He makes an impression by complementing familiar flavours with exotic ingredients and rich sauces. The adjoining room can be booked for private dinners.

Name: Sequenza
Description: The intimate Sequenza has conquered a place in the hearts of its many regulars, who keep coming back for the French-influenced market menu, offering a selection from a limited number of dishes. The choice is small and the flavours are big. The high quality produced by the chef bears witness to real knowledge of his craft.

Name: 't Havenmantsje
Description: A spot in the conservatory is an absolute must when you come to this restaurant in a converted courthouse – the view of the water and the passing boats is magnificent! The restaurant is open throughout the day, so you can come for lunch, high tea or dinner. The chef skilfully navigates his way between classic and modern culinary traditions. For instance, he won't do too much to a steak tartare, but then he will conjure up a vegetarian dish based on roasted fennel and an apple jus. Be sure to check out the Asian-inspired appetisers.

Name: Wox
Address: Lange Voorhout 51, The Hague, 2514 EC, Netherlands
Description: The name gives you an inkling of the ambience here and the interior confirms it: this flashy brasserie is an ultra trendy venue. Fashionable Franco-Asian dishes feature on the menu, as well as phenomenal wines with a good selection available by the glass.

Name: 't Pestengasthuys
Description: The red-brick façade, mezzanine floor and modern dining area with a high ceiling and timber beams lend this location (1450) plenty of character. A spot under the tree is perfect for a romantic dinner of a summer's evening. The hostess wins diners over with her jovial manner, as does her husband with his generous contemporary cuisine with a preference for local, organic ingredients. He does not shy away from more down-to-earth produce such as rabbit, and he respects traditions.

Name: Pollevie
Description: Martin Berkelmans has a passion for vegetables. He sources them from a food forest and a local farm and likes to experiment with them in his fermentation lab. The versatility of vegetables makes his dishes both playful and intriguing – they dictate the culinary direction, although meat and fish are also incorporated into his cooking. The succulent partridge breast and the rich stew are elevated to new heights with parsley root, a vegetable and walnut purée and a robust sauce featuring cassis for a sweet-and-sour note. The slightly industrial feel and organic vibe lend this inviting restaurant a unique character.

Name: Tante Kee
Description: The back and forth of the ferry bringing guests to this magnificent establishment makes for a wonderful spectacle in the evenings. Inside, the decor has been given a makeover and creates a modern yet intimate atmosphere, with the surrounding water playing an integral part in the overall look. The intriguing flavour combinations in the modern, occasionally oriental dishes provide the basis for an exciting culinary experience. Think an exotic/fresh/zesty combination of mango, passion fruit, coconut and fried rice noodles. Dinner at Tante Kee is quite an adventure!

Name: Faulk
Description: Menno and Monique ensure that everything is to your liking in their cosy neighbourhood bistro. The ambitious, contemporary-style dishes are presented in a thoughtful, balanced way. The friendly enthusiastic service is also an indicator that this couple have a bright future ahead of them.

Name: Choux
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus
Description: Cabbage in winter, peas in spring, tomatoes in summer, kale in autumn: in this trendy, industrial-style restaurant, seasonal produce takes centre stage. Embracing sustainable practices, this restaurant places the emphasis on vegetables and boasts an extensive selection of organic and natural wines. Merijn van Berlo uses his creativity to bring intensity to the plate. For instance, he infuses spelt risotto with chlorophyll in a smoked eel broth and combines it with an emulsion of horseradish and pike-perch gravlax. This cuisine bursts with floral and spicy notes and just the right amount of kick to bring the seasons to life. A captivating ode to nature's rich bounty!

Name: Lyf's
Description: One of this neighbourhood restaurant's main assets is its convivial atmosphere. The commitment to quality is palpable on every plate that is brought to your table. Martijn Stroosma serves up beautifully presented dishes that showcase his creativity. This astute chef never goes over the top. For instance, he will mellow the combination of langoustine tail tempura and confit bacon with touches of mango and celeriac. He always strikes the right balance, including in the mouth-watering à la carte and lunch options.

Name: Gebr. Hartering
Description: Niek and Paul Hartering share a love of ingredients. This cheerful venue proposes a short menu, which changes regularly, as the fusion cuisine depends on the ingredients at their best on the day. Flavours don't lie.

Name: Buitenplaats Slangevegt
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Great view,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: The River Vecht is the star of the show at this warm and welcoming restaurant – the riverside terrace alone is reason enough to book a table! Another draw of this place is the extremely attentive service. The cuisine here is playful and creative. Classic combinations are elevated with original ideas and exquisite textures. The chef also enjoys adding a touch of spice to his sauces for that extra kick.

Name: Beulings
Description: Beulings is a little gem full of atmosphere. Lisja offers guests a warm welcome, and is also in charge of the excellent wines, while Bas and his team create delicious meals in the open kitchen. They put a lot of effort into the preparation of their dishes, which are full of versatile textures and carefully thought-out flavours. A delightful experience!

Name: EN
Description: Whether you opt for one of the seven seats up at the counter or for a regular table, there is no escaping EN's vibrancy. This energy is also reflected in the food. The set menus introduce you to creative Japanese dishes including an original take on tuna sashimi. The à la carte options, on the other hand, are more traditional. Whatever you choose, you can count on the characteristic finesse and richness for which this cuisine is world-renowned. The extensive sake selection is terrific.

Name: Brasserie van Baerle
Description: There is no getting around it: wine is part of the core business of this elegant, ever-inviting luxury brasserie. The impressive selection of wines by the glass and extensive drinks menu will impress even the most seasoned connoisseur. Classics from the brasserie repertoire are served up here with great attention to detail and a sense of generosity. The steak tartare is a real crowd pleaser.

Name: Ledeboer
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Until 1994 this stately building housed a bank. Today retro and industrial features complement one another beautifully at this trendy restaurant offering quick snacks as well as larger meals, with the top choices on the set menu. The chef produces modern combinations with a sophisticated twist. At Ledeboer, taste reigns supreme.

Name: De Jonge Dikkert
Description: De Jonge Dikkert has given a new lease of life to this windmill dating from 1672, with its chic decor, intimate atmosphere and attractive dining room with wooden beams. This is the epitome of Dutch charm! The chef has a penchant for Dutch produce and Asian seasonings. His dishes are meticulously prepared with a nod to classic culinary tradition, and always likes to delight diners with something unexpected. For example, he complements pink-roasted lamb saddle with a puttanesca garnish and an aromatic lamb jus, and he combines crispy lamb neck with a goat's cheese cream. This chef has a passion for bold flavours and creates dishes that pack a punch.

Name: Tollius
Description: With its sleek decor done out in burgundy and white and contemporary artwork on the walls, Tollius has an inviting feel. This is also down to chef Barry's expertise in producing hearty classics such as his wonderfully crispy pithivier filled with a rich combination of quail, foie gras and morels. But he is just as adept at whipping up a surprisingly zesty modern dessert involving wasabi and a lemon gel. If the extensive wine list is anything to go by, this place is certainly run by people with excellent taste.

Name: LIZ Restobar
Description: The wooden horse heads on the walls, the impressive chandeliers that call to mind the wheels of a horse-drawn carriage, the partitions between the tables: you can't help but notice that you're dining in the former stables of Amerongen Castle. The terrace overlooking the castle and gardens is breathtaking! The cuisine is characterised by its use of locally sourced ingredients, French cooking techniques and a global outlook. The duck gyoza in a rich game broth with marinated mushrooms and crispy scallions says it all!

Name: Bergpaviljoen
Description: Choose your fish from the counter, treat yourself to one of the classics such as steak tartare or just opt for some tasty bar food accompanied by a good glass of wine. In this light-filled pavilion, with its Art Deco design features and spacious terrace by the beehives, you are spoilt for choice. But rest assured that, thanks to the quality of the produce that the chef has to work with, you simply cannot go wrong here.

Name: Vermeer
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Brunch,Car park,Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: Sebastian Baquero Garces has taken over the reins at this intimate designer restaurant, which is every bit as upmarket as the NH Collection Amsterdam Barbizon Palace, where it is located. A champion of the farm-to-table movement, the chef is passionate about using the freshest locally sourced ingredients, and his creativity shines through in every dish. Think thinly sliced ​​hamachi and zolderspek (aged smoky bacon) with a subtly smoky bacon jus infused with dashi and soy. His cooking is intricate and sometimes complex. And if you would rather not commit to the set menu, you can simply dine à la carte.

Name: Bistro LOF
Description: The essence of nature permeates the ambience in this former farmhouse in Parc Broekhuizen, which is now a restaurant with a splendid timber framework. This is a laid-back restaurant with a modern yet rustic feel, where the experienced chef draws inspiration from Dutch produce, including from the surrounding kitchen garden. He showcases premium vegetables in a vibrant appetiser, for example, or elevates farmhouse chicken with a celeriac cream infused with curry and a rich jus. Despite their unassuming descriptions, the dishes – underpinned by modern ideas – pack a punch with their deep flavours. Cleverly devised, sophisticated and indulgent.

Name: Oud-Zuid
Description: Oud-Zuid is a restaurant that is full of character. Take a seat inside to admire the trendy brasserie-style decor or sit out on the pleasant pavement terrace where you can enjoy the vibe of this neighbourhood. The chef puts a modern spin on tradition in his tempting and no-nonsense menu that has a focus on fish, seafood and organic produce. There is something for everyone in the impressive wine selection. Less than 10 minutes' walk from the renowned Concertgebouw.

Name: Karel V
Description: Oozing with character, this 1555 historic edifice on the embankment of the port of Goes leaves no one indifferent. An open fire, harbour terrace and artwork set the inviting scene in the Karel V. The youthful chef blends the intensity of classical recipes with refreshing modernity. Flavoursome, authentic food stamped with the chef’s signature.

Name: Les Salons
Address: Joseph Corneli Allée 1, Valkenburg, 6301 KK, Netherlands
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: The Belle-Époque elegance of Les Salons is a sight to behold. The character of this historical chÂteau, the art and murals, the modern furnishings and the terrace set in the meticulously tended gardens give it that "wow" factor. The chefs put a contemporary twist on French tradition and understand the importance of precise cooking and rich sauces. Playful garnishes and fresh nuances bring their dishes to life.

Name: IJssel Restobar
Description: Part of the Pillows hotel, this stylish restaurant encapsulates the best of Deventer. Seating options include a lovely conservatory and a terrace overlooking the River IJssel – the perfect place from which to take in the city's skyline. Wouter van Leeuwen creates a menu that's simply irresistible. Timeless classics such as steak tartare are accompanied by contemporary creations that draw on international influences and feature playful textures. For instance, he serves a combination of North Sea crab, leek and carrot with an espuma and powdered tomato. Foodies are sure to be delighted by the wide range of options.

Name: Bisque
Description: Chef Niels Schievink and charming hostess Sabrina Mans's experience shines through in their inviting, intimate restaurant. Their expertise is evident in every aspect of a meal here, from the welcome to the wine pairings to the delicious dishes. The "less-is-more" approach to French cuisine relies on technical skill and a sense of balance. The chocolate and hazelnut soufflé is truly an ode to this classic dessert – not to be missed! This celebration of wonderful produce, underpinned by exquisite sauces, is captivating.

Name: Hof aan Zee
Description: Only 500m from the North Sea, this historic Scandinavian farmstead stands in the heart of the countryside. The stripped-back interior weaves a rustic spell, while the menu shines the spotlight on the rich produce of Zeeland. Seaweed, fish from the Oosterschelde, fermented vegetables, smoky flavours – superlative purity!

Name: De Keuken van Arragon
Description: Herco van Arragon’s unashamedly contemporary cuisine is based around modern techniques, a variety of menu options and home-grown vegetables. He has a good eye for quality, which he uses in his subtle garnishes to emphasise the main ingredient of a dish. The hospitality of friendly sommelier Cynthia accentuates the warmth of this rural property.

Name: De Boet
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Great view,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Occupying a beautifully renovated traditional carpentry house, De Boet blends in perfectly with the picturesque harbour of Urk. Here, chef Cees Kramer demonstrates his clear appreciation of top-quality ingredients through his beautifully prepared modern dishes with the occasional Oriental twist. Reasonably priced wines add to the appeal.

Name: Restaurant Calva
Description: This intimate restaurant is a love story in itself, where chef Tom enjoys explaining his dishes at the table and is always happy to recommend the best wine to accompany his well-constructed culinary creations. As an example, his traditional savoir-faire shines through in the way he cooks pigeon to perfection as well as his intensely flavoured sauces. His exquisite and more modern side dishes provide the perfect harmony.

Name: De Haan
Description: Three friends have come up with an original concept: they prepare a single set menu in their open kitchen, serve the dishes themselves thus dispensing with the services of any additional waitstaff. Diners are responsible for getting their own bread and beverages. The chefs enthusiastically explain in detail how they creatively combine complex flavours. They do not shy away from contrasts, but always maintain the right balance. With a vegetarian Stroganoff – intensified by a sophisticated sauce based on Madeira, port and red wine – the chefs showcase their prowess.

Name: Mei Wah
Description: Mei Wah has been a household name since 1965. The third generation now at the helm has returned to authentic Chinese cuisine with a focus on finesse and purity, not adapting to Western taste. The result is a contemporary look with flavours from overseas, accompanied by a choice of wine or sake.

Name: Blumé
Description: At Blumé, familiar ingredients are given an unexpected twist. For instance, Jerusalem artichoke is used to impart an earthy quality to a chocolate dessert; cardamom lends spicy depth to celeriac – unconventional ideas meet skilful preparation with exciting results. Head to this elegant restaurant on the edge of Groningen's city centre to discover the set menu for yourself!

Name: Locals
Description: Housed in the same building as Hotel Haarhuis, just across from Arnhem Central train station, Locals boasts a cosmopolitan atmosphere. Ingredients are sourced as locally as possible, according to the principles of Dutch Cuisine. The abundance of plants and warm colours reflects that philosophy. Upstairs, there is even a vertical farm. The chef delights in working with vegetables, eg incorporating lentils from the Netherlands into a curry with herbs from the farm, seasonal vegetables and briny seaweed, and most of the fish and meat are locally sourced. . This place really lives up to its name!

Name: Green
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Great view,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus
Description: The sustainable Valley building, which houses Green, is a visually impressive piece of architecture. To get to this sleek, luxurious restaurant, walk through the Moltenifurniture shop, to the top floor, from where the view is stunning! Plant-based creations showcase the power of nature here, with the occasional addition of fish or meat. It is fresh, original and with surprising contrasts. Using every part of the vegetables from the seed to the leaf, this cuisine is a celebration of the produce.

Name: Ambrozijn
Description: Previously a church, Irenekerk (1891) is now a restaurant where design reigns supreme. The organ has been converted into a bar, dark brick walls surround you, and the new roof truss is magnificent. You can also see the impressive Sven Nijenhuis in action in the completely open kitchen. This place is all the more exceptional because of the way the talented chef draws on French cooking styles and innovative techniques. He really makes his mark with his exquisite sauces and meticulous seasonings.

Name: Bistrotel 't Amsterdammertje
Description: Brimming with character, this building by the Vecht River is enchanting, but just wait until you're sitting on the terrace… At Bistrotel, you can truly escape the hustle and bustle for a while! Before you retire to your comfortable guestroom, be sure to pop into the spacious bistro downstairs. André Gerrits has assembled a team here who know their way around bistro classics and flavours from all over the world. With options on the menu such as steak tartare, spicy rendang or farmhouse chicken from the spit; this is the kind of place where anything goes.

Name: Reverie
Description: United by a shared passion, Stuart and Luca, who met at hotel school, have turned their dream into reality with this sleek, intimate and rather minimalist restaurant. The bonsai tree in the middle of the dining space is a nod to the Far Eastern-inspired cuisine they serve. In the evening, they propose two set menus: "Taste of Reverie" and "Indonesian Menu". Drawing on classic French foundations, they add the sweetness and piquancy of Asian seasonings. The perfectly pan-seared duck fillet is accompanied, for instance, by an intense duck jus infused with the heat and slight sweetness of finely chopped chilli. A pumpkin cream married with ginger brings out the umami flavours. A vibrant and ambitious place.

Name: De Kromme Bistro
Description: Walk through the wine cellar to discover this charming bistro, an extension of the renowned De Kromme Watergang. The lush garden and open kitchen, complete with a sturdy charcoal grill instantly catch the eye. With every bite, you will sense the chefs' deep-rooted passion for the seafood of Zeeland, which is showcased here in all its briny glory. Think cockles with finely chopped chives and a rich beurre blanc infused with the cockles' juices and a hint of lemongrass. But rest assured, they can just as easily barbecue a bavette steak or whip up a vegetarian creation. Brasserie cuisine with a unique twist.

Name: Mearkas
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: It is an 11-minute drive from the highway to Mearkas. The short journey through the stunning Frisian countryside serves as a prelude to the sense of tranquillity that awaits you in this glass-walled restaurant flooded with light. The surrounding vegetable gardens, fields, and glamping tents form the backdrop to this ode to Friesland. Chef Kees and gardener Christiaan have joined forces to showcase the finest local produce. Everything is either homegrown or sourced from nearby suppliers. In his set menu, the chef skillfully marries the hearty flavours of Friesland with a touch of sophistication, in dishes characterised by vitality and freshness. Think North Sea sole, delicately marinated in lemon, enhanced with local bacon and expressive garnishes of sour cream, fennel, lemon, puffed quinoa and paprika sorbet. A digestif by the campfire makes for the perfect ending to a uniquely serene experience.

Name: NOÏS
Description: Laura is a warm and welcoming host, and she knows the outstanding wine list like the back of her hand. Her recommendations are absolutely spot on! If you like surprises, chef Vincent is your man. There's no written menu here; your options are presented verbally only, and your trust is rewarded with imaginative, plant-forward cuisine. Whether he's imbuing various textures of celeriac with zingy flavours, or putting pork belly centre stage in an Asian-inspired dish with a bay leaf cream sauce, his elaborate culinary creations are full of flair.

Name: De Mark
Description: Leave your car outside Durgerdam and embrace the charm of this dike village as you walk to De Mark. From the terrace, you have an exceptional view over the water – simply breathtaking! The attractive interior is done out in natural tones and makes the most of the character of the building. Dinner here is a cosy affair. Each dish revolves around three main ingredients, cooked over the wood fire. Think textures of onion – from crisp and crunchy to sweet and grilled – elevated with a Zaandam mustard ice cream. The experienced chefs offer a fresh perspective on natural flavours. If you really want to explore the extensive wine list, luxurious guestrooms are available on the first floor.

Name: Il Gattopardo
Description: Il Gattopardo is a charismatic Italian restaurant that possesses a certain je-ne-sais-quoi. The chef personally comes to your table to present his signature Sicilian dishes, which he continuously revamps with exciting new takes – for instance, crème brûlée made with butter-soft octopus alongside an exquisite potato cream enhanced with seaweed. He is meticulous both when crafting intricate sauces and filling home-made ravioli with gorgonzola. Be sure to peruse the wine list, which features a tempting array of fine Italian wines.

Name: Rosie
Description: Rosie is a bustling yet cosy establishment where foodies can indulge uninterrupted from noon. A love of wine pervades the place and music fills the air – the record player spins nostalgic tunes regularly. From shrimp croquettes to Jerusalem artichoke with labneh or a no-nonsense meat or fish dish: the international menu has something for everyone. This straightforward cuisine makes the most of the versatility of vegetables. Reservations are recommended!

Name: Mont Blanc
Description: From the chalet vibe to the cowbells in the toilets, the space is an ode to French chef Thibault's native Savoie, as are the food and the selection of wines. He skilfully combines authentic flavours and creative inspirations. He likes, for instance, to work with cheese (the cheese trolley is excellent), using Bleu des Aravis to give a dish based on various mushrooms extra punch. This is Alpine cuisine with natural undertones and a focus on preparation techniques.

Name: BAK
Description: Take the stairs to the third floor of this unobtrusive warehouse (you'll need to ring the bell in the evening) to discover this rather rugged yet inviting restaurant with its splendid view over the IJ River. Benny Blisto sets great store by the origin of his ingredients, be it a carrot or ray wing. Locally sourced, seasonal produce is the inspiration behind his creativity. For instance, with slightly tart rhubarb and an exquisite beetroot sauce, he elevates a venison fillet to new heights. An exciting dining experience is guaranteed!

Name: Het Arsenaal 1309
Description: Björn de Waal has a special relationship with fruit and vegetables, which he sources as locally as possible and gives pride of place in his creative cuisine. Think mandarin orange combined with candied kumquat, a light corn foam, crispy potato chips and black truffle. The chef is also fond of cooking with game, but the vegetable accompaniments play a prominent role in those dishes, too. No visit to the picturesque Hanseatic city of Doesburg would be complete without a meal at this former monastery, a stunning blend of old and new.

Name: Arca
Description: Top Portuguese chef Henrique Sá Pessoa is the creator of the enticing sharing menu at this trendy, cosmopolitan establishment. Traditional, home-style dishes such as gambas ao alhinho are expertly given a modern twist, perhaps even a little Asian finesse. But the portions remain typically generous. The bespoke cocktails are fabulous, as is the lunch menu in the cool bar!

Name: Putaine
Description: The Rotterdam skyline and Nieuwe Maas river form the backdrop to your dining experience at Putaine. On a pontoon floating in the Rijnhaven, this on-trend restaurant has large windows and a fabulous terrace. You could happily spend the whole day here working your way through the creative à la carte menu. Chef Schook makes a point of working with Dutch produce, giving vegetables special emphasis; he has a penchant for crisp, vibrant nuances. A cosmopolitan and exciting place!

Name: Moustique
Description: This highly modern restaurant in the centre of Haarlem is open almost every day. Here, you’ll find an extensive menu on which the chef showcases his experience through cuisine with an Asian inspiration and modern presentation, including a choice of vegetarian dishes and plenty of intense and authentic flavours. An impressive new arrival on the city’s food scene!

Name: Rura by Naomi & Joey
Description: Naomi & Joey pamper their guests with a casual fine dining experience. The intimate atmosphere here is laid-back and cosy. And whether or not Joey is cooking only with vegetables (there are two set menus available), his predilection is always for elaborately prepared dishes. He sets about top-notch produce with a sense of invention; rich French sauces and ideas from around the globe pack an added punch.

Name: Robuust
Description: This warm and welcoming restaurant is run by two larger-than-life brothers: chef Raimon and maître d' Peter Ian. You can look forward to dishes brimming with distinctive flavours, as in the finely spiced beurre blanc that lends a touch of indulgence to a perfectly fried slice of cod. Such culinary excellence characterises their classic fare as well as the more creative set menu. Be sure to ask your expert host for his beer recommendations – he has some real gems up his sleeve!

Name: HFSLG Bar & Bistro
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Credit cards not accepted,Terrace
Description: The cosy atmosphere at this bistro envelopes you in its warm embrace. Views of the garden, where vegetables and vines grow, contributes to this, as do the attentive service and the pared-down cuisine. The menu features both classic dishes and more sophisticated options. Whether it's the game jus to accompany the venison fillet or the beurre blanc to go with the catch of the day, this chef knows the importance of a good sauce and takes care to present visually appealing plates.

FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: This appealing restaurant with its bright interior has an atmosphere that is welcoming and cosy, while at the same time natural and contemporary. With a wealth of experience at top-flight establishments, chef Rik and hostess/sommelier Saskia serve creative cuisine that draws inspiration from around the globe. The dishes consist of just a few ingredients that enhance each other's intensity.

Name: Concours
Description: Located on Utrecht's Biltstraat, this stylish restaurant is in keeping with its lively and inviting surroundings. Alex Zeelenberg likes to keep the courses of his set menu a secret right up until they are served, and they never fail to impress. Whether he is spicing up a pan-fried pink duck breast with a harissa-infused poultry stock, seasoning a lentil beignet with Middle Eastern spices or incorporating the sweet earthiness of beetroot into a dessert, his creativity will take your taste buds on a voyage. Their commitment to sustainability, both in the dishes and the overall dining experience, is an added bonus.

Name: VanOost
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Counter dining,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus
Description: Once upon a time, medical students used to perform dissections in the space that houses this chic restaurant today. Luxury and design go hand in hand here; a seat at the dining counter is an experience. Chef Floris van Straalen has an international outlook and a focus on local produce. His cuisine is sophisticated and creative. You can start with some modern amuse-bouches that take you on a journey from East to West, or try the Anjou pigeon with a delicate cream sauce, green pepper and anchovies.

Name: Aji
Description: Immerse yourself in the tropical world of Aji. The vintage, lounge-style decor exudes an adventurous spirit, a quality that Pelle Swinkels's cuisine also possesses. His technique is rooted in French culinary tradition, and he draws on experience gained in Asia and South America. He combines tuna tartare, for instance, with a spicy emulsion and leche del tigre vinaigrette, lime and crispy corn. With a sure touch, he uses flavour enhancers, such as sambai and aji amarillo, in original ways to add depth and complexity with umami, fruity and sweet notes. Intriguing!

Name: DOYY
Description: DOYY offers an intimate and relaxed atmosphere with a touch of Middle Eastern elegance, reflecting the Azerbaijani-Turkish heritage of owner Yavuz. Chef Daan van Lieshout knows his French classics, as evidenced in the à la carte selection, which includes dishes such as steak tartare and tournedos Rossini. However, he also likes to incorporate Asian and Middle Eastern influences into his cooking – it is his set menu that really showcases his creativity. Think salty-sweet langoustine tartare with citrus chiboust, confit tomatoes, crispy chicken skin and a frothy bisque jus. Brace yourself for bold flavours with a spicy kick!

Name: Kale & de Bril
Description: It would be a shame to pass up a visit to this discreet property where chefs Marc (the bald one or “Kale” in Dutch!) and Niek (the one with glasses – “de Bril” in Dutch!) certainly know how to please their guests. In their pleasant restaurant, savour Zeeland products (in particular from the “homarium”), generous flavours and subtle culinary creations that are always fascinating.

Name: Bistro Bord'o
Description: European wines take centre stage in this casual establishment – hence the name (a pun on Bordeaux)! Start with an aperitif before digging into fine French classical fare. Rather than prissy frills, the focus is on quality ingredients, spot-on cooking and wholesome flavours! In summertime, you can even hire a rowing boat!

Name: Het Oude Gemeentehuis
Description: Once the town hall, this is the ideal place for convivial dining. Original features provide a striking contrast with the modern design and warm colours. Indulgence is the name of the game when it comes to the food. Whether you opt for the rich lobster bisque, the sea bass with the rich beurre blanc or their contemporary take on tiramisu, you will be bowled over by the skill and charm of hosts Niels Minkman and Janneke Eerbeek.

Name: Cèpes
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: Hotel de Sterrenberg's restaurant draws on its natural surroundings. The interior is sleek yet warm, combining lots of wood with concrete, and a large wooden stag's head that draws the eye. The chef believes in sourcing his produce locally, using local suppliers such as Gert van Eldik and the Veluwe asparagus farm. Diners are served a surprise menu composed of intricate and beautifully presented dishes. Think venison from the region with carefully considered vegetable accompaniments and a game jus enhanced with vermouth. A proud ambassador for the Veluwe!

Name: Auberge des Moules
Description: Mussels, lobster and other seafood from Zeeland are the stars on the menu at this atmospheric inn. Here, these delicacies have for decades been prepared according to old family recipes. The black and white pictures on the walls demonstrate the rich history.

Name: De Mandemaaker
Description: The Mandemaker has a lot of trumps up its sleeve, such as its terrace on the inner harbour, cheerful flowers, the winning combination of hip design and a cosy atmosphere, as well as the guestrooms. Excellent seasonal produce, with a focus on fish, is beautifully showcased in contemporary creations such as pickled mackerel with crispy asparagus and lime leaf cream. Fans of classics like fried sole are also catered for with appropriate generosity.

Name: Kasteel Ter Worm
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Credit cards not accepted,Garden or park,Great view,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: This 14C castle is brimming with character, and a meal here promises an experience beyond compare. With its wooden floors, medieval paintings and old stone walls, the setting couldn't be more enchanting. The waterside terrace overlooking the verdant surroundings is an absolute delight! Dave Beckers's approach is refreshingly modern and his sophisticated creations frequently feature flavour profiles based on koji, yuzu and koshi. For instance, he adds extra depth to his lamb fillet and crispy braised lamb neck by incorporating powdered seaweed into the potato mousseline and kombu into the rich lamb jus. This is easy-to-enjoy cuisine that also pushes boundaries. An overnight stay in the castle makes for the ultimate grand finale.

Name: Restaurant 55
Description: Set in the Heggenstraat, a cosy spot in the old city centre, is this pleasant restaurant with an atmospheric, baroque-style interior. It is immediately apparent that the kitchen is run by a young team – even if they do keep the flavours classic. The prices are very reasonable too!

Name: Damianz
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: In what was once Roermond's prison, you will be served bread and water first of all. But fear not: any culinary nods to the past vocation of the premises end there. At this restaurant, which is part of Het Arresthuis hotel, historical details and contemporary design elegantly intertwine. Chef Jeroen van Gansewinkel masterfully incorporates international influences and rich sauces into his dishes. From lamb with typically Middle Eastern seasonings such as za'atar and smoked paprika to langoustine with a tangy beurre blanc infused with basil oil, the food is complex and brimming with flavour. As they say themselves – it's criminally delicious!

Name: Red Orchids
Description: If you have a hard time making decisions, we suggest you head to this intimate, trendy restaurant where the menu brings together Japanese, Chinese, Thai and Indonesian specialities. The chef always manages to add just the right dose of spices, creating dishes full of rich flavours and crisp textures. Subtle Asian cuisine at reasonable prices.

Name: De Luytervelde
Description: Karin Smits is the heart and soul of De Luytervelde. She has been welcoming guests at this converted farmhouse (1912) just outside the city centre since 1992. Diners are smitten with the stylish decor and delightful garden terrace, but the main focus remains, of course, the modern interpretation of classic flavours and the well-curated wine list. The chef will expertly fry a veal sweetbread until golden brown and knock up a robust sauce Périgueux, but he is just as adept at giving venison an exotic twist with five-spice powder. A perennial favourite!

Name: Nastrium
Description: (Temporary move to Paradijslaan 2-8 in Eindhoven) Two very different culinary traditions come together in this elegant villa, which is also home to the private Gani dining room. Here, chef Djailany’s Indian origins add spice to traditional French cuisine, with foie gras and langoustines served alongside ingredients such as soya and kombu, resulting in harmonious dishes full of subtle and exotic flavours.

Name: Auberge de Veste
Description: Dating from 1849, this restaurant right by the river is the perfect setting in which to enjoy complex and beautifully presented cuisine. The chef prepares contemporary influenced dishes with bold flavour combinations. The owner’s passion for wine is a bonus, as are the extra dishes which can be added to the interesting set menu.

Name: Zuid by Adrian Zarzo
FacilitiesAndServices: Garden or park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus
Description: Adrian Zarzo brings the world to your plate in this trendy, chic establishment. For example, you start with dim sum, then move on to an intense bouillabaisse and continue your journey with a Mediterranean take on sea bass. Zuid advocates a relaxed approach to gastronomy and is run by a chef who knows how to win over the modern diner. Be sure to drop by the bodega next door for some delicious snacks and a good glass of wine.

Name: Bistro T-bone
Description: Everything revolves around the charcoal grill in this atmospheric establishment pleasantly situated in a quintessential old Dutch building. Whether he's barbecuing T-bone steak, a rack of lamb or sole, the chef bends the flames to his will with a sure touch. The results are dishes that are generous and brimming with typically robust flavours and character. The jovial owner will be happy to guide you through the menu, which also includes classics such as snails and onion soup – there are plenty of mouth-watering options.

Name: Het Weeshuys
Description: Striking murals with a culinary theme give this orphanage chapel (1310) real individuality. The vibrant decor indoors is certainly a sight to behold, but there is also a courtyard terrace that is idyllic in fine weather. Opt for the lunch set menu or simply let the chef surprise you with inspired and delicate creations such as choucroute and prawns with an Asian twist, or a new take on wild boar terrine – a feast for the senses is guaranteed!

Name: Infini
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: The interplay of modern art and rustic features make this elegant villa a lovely setting for a fine dining experience, the terrace is the prettiest of South Limburg! The ambitious chef strongly favours modern cuisine, resulting in elaborate dishes. House specialities include the highly recommended soufflé.

Name: De Knip
Description: Tables on the sunny terrace and in the conservatory are much in demand at this long-established restaurant. The view of the shimmering Vliet canal is breathtaking! Marcel van Teijlingen's culinary creations are a testament to his attention to detail and refined palate, both in their presentation and their flavour profiles. He likes to add playful touches to his dishes, which are classic in their foundations. Think celeriac mousse finished with onion and a ponzu oil, adding vibrancy to a rich millefeuille of celeriac and oxtail. The old and the new join forces at De Knip.

Name: de Molenaar
Description: The charm of the converted Hunsingo windmill (1855) is as captivating as this picturesque village, and it houses a really special restaurant. Chef Kooijker works only with a surprise menu in which he brings to bear all his creativity, paying special attention to the presentation, creating elaborate garnishes and giving a new perspective on familiar flavours. Rest assured, you are in good hands here. And why not treat yourself to an overnight stay in the mill or granary?

Name: DYLANS
Address: Oude Zeeweg 63, Noordwijk aan Zee, 2202 CJ, Netherlands
Description: The founder of Alexander Hotel was born a butcher's son and can be proud of this restaurant for meat lovers. The trendy intimacy of the decor, the gold elements, the hip lounge and cocktail bar all make for a magnificent venue. Many of the modern dishes are prepared on the Josper charcoal oven, resulting in robust, pure flavours. A fine côte de boeuf, a salt-crusted tenderloin to share, a choice cut of Japanese Wagyu beef: a feast for carnivores!

Name: Villa la Ruche
Description: This 19C villa is alluring, chic and inviting. The classic cuisine is the real standout feature here. The chef has a good command of his techniques and cooks with wonderful subtlety. He also regularly ventures into more modern dishes to treat his guests to a whirlwind of flavours.

Name: De Zeeuw
Description: Janine and Jeroen De Zeeuw are a power couple who know exactly what they want – and their vision has been further honed by moving into this listed building. A pleasingly intimate and smart atmosphere prevails here, with art from their personal collection adding a touch of individuality. They will be happy to tell you about the sustainable concept behind their restaurant, which extends to the tableware and the close proximity of their chosen suppliers. With respect for the terroir, Chef Jeroen delivers exciting dishes rife with fresh and earthy flavours. His white asparagus, for example, is prepared with coconut and given a subtle twist in the form of a jus of clear tomato stock, vin jaune and elderflower. Meanwhile Janine wins diners over with wines she has discovered, as well as amazing mocktails and kombuchas.

Name: Bosq
Description: Bosq is a cosy establishment on the outskirts of the National Park, overlooking beautiful surroundings – the sunny terrace is particularly attractive – and offering the many delicacies that Texel has to offer. The chef here cooks with real Mediterranean finesse, serving a selection of smaller-sized portions. An appealing concept for a restaurant with real character.

Name: Breakers Beach House
Address: Koningin Astrid Boulevard 5, Noordwijk aan Zee, 2202 BK, Netherlands
Description: Welcome to the "Dutch Riviera", where dining with your toes in the sand is sure to give you that holiday feeling. The relaxed terrace affords a wonderful view of the sea, or you can enjoy the trendy brasserie ambience inside. This is the place to come for a plate of ultra-fresh oysters and seafood, followed by classically prepared dishes in which the produce (mainly fish, of course) steals the show. Simple and delicious!

Name: The Bishop
Description: The Bishop is where the bustling centre of Leiden truly comes alive. The wooden beams and supporting columns are a reminder of the building's past, yet the trendy decor and lively atmosphere give it a contemporary feel. Take a punt on the surprise menu or order from the small à la carte selection – the chef's creations include subtle nods to his Indonesian heritage. He draws inspiration from all over the world, dabbling in international flavours to create exciting dishes: serundeng and Asian spices are added to the rendang, kimchi and gochujang to the veal tartare, hot and spicy aji amarillo to the kingfish. This place is a surefire hit, especially because of the terrific wine list. Be sure to make a reservation!

Name: Old Skool
Description: Druten's old school has been converted into a restaurant with a charming retro-modern location and a menu offering a choice of modern, traditional and vegetarian dishes. Although the chef will readily produce a game dish based on pheasant, he tends towards the contemporary end of the spectrum. This manifests itself in his use of seasonings from around the globe and the presentation of the dishes. A delicious lesson for any foodie!

Name: DeliCees
Description: You could certainly call Cees Timmerman's cuisine delicate and delectable. He scours his region for the finest produce, and likes to incorporate Mediterranean influences. For instance, he has no qualms about combining beetroot with burrata and anchovies. He proposes only a surprise menu that lives up to its name, with combinations such as pluma iberico and corn. At this elegant establishment, whose decor incorporates vintage and modern design, you are in for a full evening's entertainment.

Name: Oogst
Description: With its warm and welcoming atmosphere, Oogst is right at home in the cosy Buurtschap Centrum 2005 neighbourhood. There is something of the lively Parisian bistro about this place, which makes it all the more enjoyable to dine here. The set menus are always determined by what the Laantje Voorham vegetable garden has to offer. The versatility of vegetables and herbs provides subtle nuances. By incorporating herbs into ice cream and broths, chef Van Bommel gives dishes a new twist. His modern and always generous creations are fragrant with punchy flavours.

Name: Bøg
Description: Slick Scandinavian design is beautifully executed at Bøg. You have the choice between a vegetarian menu and a meat/fish menu, both as creative as they are appealing. The pure flavours drawn from local ingredients are truly delicious.

Name: 't Arsenaal
Description: This traditional building next to the Lebuïnus church is now a modern, bright, no-frills restaurant. Attractive bar, patio garden with terrace amongst the church buttresses, tempting menus and attentive service.

Name: Woods
Description: From the magnificent sawmill next door to the wonderful waterside summer terrace to the rear, this modern restaurant enjoys a fantastic location. The chef reveals his fresh, tasty cooking style in a selection of small dishes.

Name: Bistro de Holterberg
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Great view,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: Experience the charms of each season in this cosy bistro, whether it's winter by the large open fireplace or summer on the stunning terrace, offering an awe-inspiring vista of the Salland Ridge National Park. The extensive set menu features authentic French dishes that each showcase one or two bold flavours. Crispy fried sea bass fillet, langoustine sauce and boiled fresh vegetables: unadulterated flavours at their best.

Name: Mezger
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Garden or park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Mezger is the dream of Jeroen and Sanne Tanis who found the perfect setting in this orangerie which they have redecorated with wood and trendy furniture. His cuisine highlights his own experience, which respects the seasons and products from the Zeeland region. He adds to this mix perfect cooking techniques and ingredients that work together to create a dream that is now a pleasurable reality!

Name: In Den Rustwat
Description: In den Rustwat adds an exotic touch to metropolitan Rotterdam with its thatched roof, history dating back to the 16C and an idyllic setting close to an arboretum. The food here is anything but traditional, offering contemporary-style dishes with an abundance of ingredients and cooking methods.

Name: De Gaffel
Description: De Gaffel creates a wonderful dining experience under the old Saxon farm's thatched roof and around the open hearth, which fills the rustic interior with a homely feel. Outside, the chef grows his own vegetables, working with top-quality ingredients, accentuated with contemporary techniques.

Name: Brasserie Goeie Louisa
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: This brasserie shares the medieval charm of the upscale hotel, Karel V, to which it belongs. Once a monastery, the property has been elegantly decorated but has retained its original character. The chefs here like to put their own unique spin on classic recipes. They understand the value of a decent béarnaise sauce with a succulent cut of meat, but they also enjoy playing with the tartness of orange to elevate a dish based on lobster and fennel. This cuisine presents familiar flavours with an exciting twist.

Name: Dudockx Bar & Kitchen
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: Architect Dudok is the designer behind this trendy 1930s pavilion. Each table overlooks the Hilversumse kanaal, which really is something to behold as you sit on the gorgeous terrace. The resolutely modern cuisine shows a preference for organic and local produce, yet remains down to earth. This is the place to come if you want an original take on wonton or a perfectly cooked cut of meat with an elegant sauce. The restaurant also rents out boats!

Name: Restaurant Eindeloos
Description: The biggest draws of this warm and welcoming restaurant are Willem Schaafsma's culinary prowess and the exquisite pairings dreamt up by his sommelier. Here, you can savour dishes made with top-quality ingredients that are sourced as locally and sustainably as possible – and all at excellent value for money. A firm favourite!

Name: Hanasato
Description: In this atmospheric restaurant diners will discover authentic Japanese cuisine in all its glory. The chef cooks with respect for tradition and unites subtlety of flavour with precise preparation methods. The smoked sashimi and the Shabu Shabu menu are particularly popular.

Name: Bistro Sophie
Description: Don't let the name fool you; this is an upscale restaurant with a stylish interior that features vintage decor and natural materials. Working in an open kitchen, Dejan Gavric is clearly keeping up with the times. He is a chef who likes to incorporate Mediterranean influences and techniques. This is evident in the dish comprising pan-fried sea bass fillet with mussels and sea lavender and featuring a variety of garnishes. The wine list, while not too extensive, is international, well curated and great value for money.

Name: Hendrik van Maurick
Description: A visit to this medieval castle (1257) is an experience in itself. The wooded surroundings, the drawbridge, the courtyard... What a magnificent place this is! Inside, all that historical character meets with modern comfort. The portrait of the knight Van Maurick holding a smartphone is certainly a talking point. The menu may seem classical at first glance, but it features inventive dishes in which Dutch produce is given a French twist. This cuisine is sophisticated, vibrant and ambitious!

Name: De Hinde
Description: Harmen Ligthart has converted his grandfather's café into a cosy restaurant with an endearing and authentic soul. The view over the IJsselmeer (also from the two luxury guestrooms) is truly stunning! A stroll through the village and down by the boats is a must. Whether you opt for fish or game, you can rest assured that the ingredients are locally sourced and that the classic sense of generosity is adhered to. The pâté and fine Riesling wines are firm favourites here.

Name: Oesterbeurs
Description: Lobster, oysters, sea lavender and mussels are just some of the Zeeland delicacies served in this restaurant which is decorated in warmly gilded tones. More than 80% of the dishes served here are fish based, with a richly flavoured classic bouillabaisse featuring on the menu alongside more creative fare. A true ode to Zeeland.

Name: Sillyfox
Description: Located at the top of a converted grain-processing plant, this delightful space combines a raw, industrial aesthetic with modern design elements. It also boasts a roof terrace affording panoramic views of the surrounding landscape. With years of experience, Joppe Sprinkhuizen meticulously crafts each dish, blending timeless French cooking techniques with international influences. For example, the entrecôte, cooked rare, is served with a bitterbal (Dutch meatball) filled with rendang, alongside beans cooked in red curry and lemongrass, plus a peanut cream and a red berry cream providing sweet and fruity nuances. The set menus are fantastic, although an appealing à la carte selection is also available in the evening.

Name: Scherp
Description: Mart Scherp's restaurant, which also offers accommodation, merges the historical charm of Middelburg's town centre with a trendy vibe. The talented chef likes to work with Zeeland's local produce and Asian seasonings. Enticing flavours and subtle spiciness are common features, so it's no surprise that he has gathered a loyal following.

Name: Restaurant MANNA
Description: Fashionable restaurant in a beautiful old building, which acts as a backdrop for cosmopolitan, modern cuisine with a focus on fish. Attractively priced 4-course menu.

Name: Bistro Madeleine
Description: As typical as the name sounds, this place is far from being your average bistro. Rather than a stuffy decor, you can expect a 21C take on the standard bistro setting. The chef conjures up the same impression on the plate. Upon entering, you are greeted by the delicious aroma of fresh bread. Here, simplicity is synonymous with robust flavours. The modern touches he brings to the dishes add a surprising twist. Think ray wing with a roasted pepper sauce vierge, creamed celeriac and a frothy tarragon sauce. The carefully curated wine list is second to none. An atypical bistro!

Name: Wolf Atelier
Description: Michael Wolf likes to experiment with sophisticated flavours and surprising ideas, giving diners the opportunity to test them out and then refining them to retain their best features. He is just as happy to cook up a turnip-based vegetarian take on Beef Wellington as he is to concoct surf and turf combinations that put a new spin on familiar flavours. The name Atelier is therefore particularly appropriate in this trendy, industrial-style restaurant, which is located on an old railway bridge with a beautiful view of the IJ.

Name: De Ertepeller
Description: The steady stream of boats passing by provides a captivating backdrop for this bright and airy restaurant located at a point where three rivers meet. Large windows afford uninterrupted views. During the week, Arjan Kuipers serves up an appealing selection of simple dishes, including crispy battered fish and freshly cut chips. Alternatively, you can opt for a more ambitious and adventurous set menu. A variety of textures and international flavours are expertly combined, and the dishes are beautifully presented. With an accomplished chef at the helm, De Ertepeller offers the best of both worlds, and the quality is second to none.

Name: De Silveren Spiegel
FacilitiesAndServices: Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: These two step-gabled houses from 1614 take you back in time . From the open fireplace with matching tiles to the romantic candlelit setting, silver cutlery and beautiful porcelain plates, everything here exudes Dutch charm at its best. The menu features exquisite, intricate dishes that showcase Dutch produce. The young chef has a keen eye for freshness, as demonstrated by the foamy mussel sauce he uses to elevate the salty symphony of mussels and seaweed. With its good selection of natural wines and a penchant for French labels, the wine list is definitely worth a look.

Name: Le Moulin
Description: At the warm and cosy Le Moulin, they have been paying their respects to classic French-Flemish cuisine for more than 35 years. Frans Glas knows the importance of a sauce, like the amazing beurre blanc that he serves with the flawless sole meunière. They steer clear of unnecessary frills and everything revolves around flavour. Salmon is still smoked according to an old family recipe. His sister Yvonne provides charming service and astute wine recommendations.

Name: La nouvelle Auberge
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: Ask for a table in the elegant glass conservatory at this intimate restaurant with its modern auberge feel and enjoy the view of the greenery outdoors. The chef here delights fans of rich cuisine with dishes which are influenced by French and international culinary traditions and made from locally sourced ingredients.

Name: Etablissement 1880
Description: Etablissement 1880 is much more nuanced than the black and white that dominate its colour scheme. The charm of the decor and the location on Groede's historic market square make for a cosy setting. For her surprise menu, chef Mariëlla draws on flavours from around the globe and Zeeland produce. With an eye for detail, the creative chef focuses on subtle touches such as zesty garnishes and rich sauces that bind her dishes together. If you wish to extend your stay, book one of the two guestrooms upstairs.

Name: Het Binnenhof
Address: Bocht van Guinea 6, Goes, 4461 BC, Netherlands
Description: Het Binnenhof exudes all the charm of Goes's historic centre. A narrow alleyway leads you to this stylishly refurbished restaurant, which is tucked away in a courtyard and boasts an inviting terrace. The seafood comes directly from the Vismijn Colijnsplaat fish auction; the vegetables and meat are also locally sourced. Chef Arjen spoils you for choice with his à la carte and set menus, and it doesn't stop there! Generous and highly accomplished, he whips up the most fabulous sauces.

Name: Carelshaven
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: Carelshaven has been providing comfortable overnight accommodation since 1772, in a stunning location near Twickel Castle. Here, the chef prepares fine French cuisine using produce from his own vegetable garden, giving classic flavours a fresh twist without the need for excessive flourish.

Name: Restaurant Kasteel Engelenburg
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: In this restaurant, occupying a 19C conservatory, the cooking style is modern and the wines South African. Lounge featuring an impressive whisky collection to round off the evening.

Name: Arles
Description: Arles brings Provence to Amsterdam. The prints on the walls of this bustling little bistro hark back to the hometown of the chef, who also shares his love of jazz music here (get a table in the dining room at the front if you prefer a quieter space). His culinary style is neo-bistro – a fresh take on the familiar flavours of French cuisine. Think the earthy flavour of beef cheeks cooked in red wine with buttery carrots or a new take on rice pudding. The set menu changes monthly and offers unbeatable value for money!

Name: Porta Sud
Description: This pleasant restaurant with its charming Art Nouveau style is located along the Passage Zuidpoort. Don’t expect a traditional Italian dining experience, however; instead, you’ll be treated to contemporary Southern European flavours with a local and Nordic influence and a different take on time-honoured combinations that will definitely tempt your tastebuds.

Name: Hemel & Aarde
Description: Rene van der Weijden and his team move heaven and earth (Hemel & Aarde) to showcase the seasons in their cuisine. It's hard to miss the majestic building on a corner plot that houses both this restaurant and the Nox Hotel. Done out in blue, gold and white, the stylish interior makes for an opulent setting. Rich flavours derived from garums and time-honoured techniques, such as fermentation, are incorporated into modern, sophisticated creations. This dynamic chef takes a bold and creative approach to highlighting the wealth of delicious produce the earth has to offer.

Name: Oesterput 14
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Credit cards not accepted,Great view,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: The oyster tanks and the Eastern Scheldt reveal all their secrets in this sparkling establishment, which is the height of contemporary cuisine. Fish-lovers are well placed here for mouthwatering sea delicacies delivered fresh and unadulterated to the plate. Those who opt for a delicious piece of meat will also find tailored dishes on offer.

Name: Puur Sanh
Address: Zevenheuvelenweg 87, Berg en Dal, 6571 CJ, Netherlands
Description: Puur Sanh's cuisine is captivating with its creative, daring, and exciting flavours. Chef Witte focuses on plant-based dishes and likes to think outside the box. For instance, he combines textures of pineapple with a sweet potato beignet, coconut and curry cream, spicy fennel and sesame seeds, and a potato crème brûlée. Daring, but it absolutely works! Treat yourself to a seat on the terrace and sample the wonderful selection of whiskies and wines. A feast for the senses!

Name: Het Bosch
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Great view,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: From this contemporary restaurant diners enjoy a breathtaking view of the Nieuwe Meer marina. In this dream location the chef entertains diners with lavish, up-to-date dishes prepared with real know-how.

Name: Senses
Description: Indulge your palate at Senses, where the cuisine brims with vibrant Asian flavours, invigorating acidity, and showcases a mastery of both classic and new techniques. Prepare to be captivated by the imaginative and daring flavours. The enthusiastic team behind this graceful restaurant leaves nothing to chance. The sophisticated atmosphere and fine wines are the icing on the cake.

Name: Visaandeschelde
Description: Visaandeschelde has been a haven for seafood enthusiasts since 1999. The maritime theme of this brasserie is emphasised by details such as anchors and fish drawings on the tiles, scale patterns on the windows and the blue and white colour scheme. In this lively establishment, you can savour briny oysters, sumptuous seafood platters and the freshest fish. The dishes are rather traditional in style – it is the quality of the produce that counts. When you order lobster, expect it to be perfectly cooked and served with a subtly sweet olive oil vinaigrette with parsley and a crisp salad. The lunchtime menu comes highly recommended!

Name: Kook Atelier op Oost
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Wheelchair access
Description: Nature takes centre stage at this tastefully converted farmhouse, which also has splendid guestrooms. The restaurant's Nordic-inspired design and large windows that make you feel connected to the outdoors reflect the house's commitment to sustainability. The menu is centred on ingredients from the Wadden Sea and Texel, which they have either grown themselves or sourced from friendly local purveyors. Produce such as peas, algae and lamb are showcased in vibrant creations, in which techniques such as fermentation and koji add intensity and depth. This exploration of Texel's ecosystems is truly fascinating.

Name: Maris Piper
Description: Done out in green and gold, this handsome luxury brasserie has a chic, London-style atmosphere. For the ultimate experience, be sure to secure a seat at the Chef's Table (only available on Fridays and Saturdays). In keeping with the location, the menu presents an original take on brasserie dishes. For example, you could start with a crispy brioche bun with smoked eel and foie royale; then you might move on to the barbecued turbot served with a beurre blanc that possesses a delicate acidity. The chefs here work with the finest – often Dutch – produce, and it pays dividends.

Name: Reblochon
Description: Elise and Jurgen have transformed a charming cottage into a cosy living room-style restaurant, welcoming diners with genuine hospitality. The chef only serves a surprise menu, which he executes masterfully. Expect no gimmicks, but rather carefully crafted dishes with occasional influences from far-flung places. For instance, he combines pickled salmon with the earthy sweetness of beetroot and the umami of miso. Be sure to try the cheese board – a delicious way to discover the inspiration behind the restaurant's name.

Name: Valuas
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: The stunning view of the Maas River from the terrace here is something you won't soon forget. The same goes for the warm welcome you will receive and the genuine hospitality that is so characteristic of the Limburg region. At this restaurant, they aim to please, as you will see from Eric Swaghoven's extensive menu. The range of delectable options includes a rich North Sea crab remoulade with textures of potato and an exquisite shrimp bisque, a guinea fowl and rabbit paté en croûte, mackerel sashimi, as well as a Mediterranean-style risotto. The experienced chef's versatility shines through, and the value for money is exceptional. Oenophiles will delight in the extraordinarily extensive wine list.

Name: De Rozario
Description: With its street art-inspired decor and laid-back atmosphere, this restaurant couldn't be more hip. The quirky and creative self-taught chef fuses French culinary tradition with Indonesian influences. His wonderfully hot and spicy hot-and-cold rendang is a signature dish. But he just as deftly elevates sea bass fillet with grated Belper Knolle cheese and a rich jus seasoned with tom kha kai herbs. Jermain de Rozario is always on the hunt for unconventional flavours and is accompanied on his quest by an expert sommelier with a rock 'n' roll edge.

Name: Prix de Rome
Description: As far as Maastricht foodies are concerned, all roads lead to Prix de Rome. Inside this impressive building just outside the city centre a cosy interior awaits, in which exposed beams work well as part of the otherwise modern design of the place. The open kitchen at the back is a nice added touch. Here, chef Wouter alternates sophisticated, original creations with dishes that focus mainly on the produce. Among the favourites on the menu are the salmon ceviche and house special crispy fried veal sweetbreads. A winning combination!

Name: Broederenklooster
Description: The authenticity of this former monastery (1293) has been preserved in every detail. Where once the friars used to take their meals, you can now enjoy a luxurious dining experience in a historical setting. The ultra-modern open kitchen immediately catches the eye. Niels van Dooijeweert prepares French dishes using contemporary techniques. Turbot fried À la minute, a robust jus enriched with butter and juicy veal cheeks. For fans of such delicacies, this is the place to be. Top-notch produce takes pride of place at Broederenklooster. The beautiful guestrooms are perfect for a good night's rest.

Name: MEI
Description: Marco Blok is an enthusiastic champion of sustainable development. His menu and restaurant have been treated to a makeover, in particular the splendid counter. This seasoned chef crafts subtle dishes in which the wide diversity offered by vegetables is exploited to its full. He plays with fermentation, acidity, fruity flavours and slow cooking… Subtly balanced guest star appearances of local meat and fish.

Name: Céline
Description: The austere appearance of Fort Jutphaas is in marked contrast to the restaurant it houses, which boasts an intimate atmosphere with subdued lighting and cosy terrace. Chef Rick works principally with Dutch produce, such as Dutch yellowtail, which he likes to season with subtle Asian flavours. This is original and modern cuisine, in which vegetables take pride of place. In fact, why not opt for the appealing vegetarian set menu?

Name: Graphite by Peter Gast
Description: A scanner next to an unassuming façade on Paardenstraat marks the beginning of your adventure. Scan the QR code you received when you reserved and enter this speakeasy restaurant, an intimate, nightclub-like space with trendy music playing in the background. Peter Gast's cuisine is detailed and inventive, at times even complex. This chef likes to play with tangy and sweet-and-sour nuances. For example, he combines melon and red/yellow beetroot with a zesty herb vinaigrette and various edible flowers. The mysterious Graphite is a world unto itself.

Name: Barres
Description: Edwin Dingemanse and Sjoerd Dooge's bar/restaurant exudes youthful elegance – everything here is impeccable without being stiff. Their sincere commitment to guests manifests itself in the cuisine. Diners are bowled over by the complex interplay of local delicacies – Zeeland shellfish, for instance – with influences from all around the globe. The sauces are rich and the garnishes playful, yet it is always the core ingredient that steals the show.

Name: Nazka
Description: You might, for a moment, feel as if you have stumbled across a wine cellar, but you will soon see that this hip South American eatery is very much at home in this cosmopolitan city. Nazka unleashes a whirlwind of bold flavours on your palate, from pisco cocktails to ceviche and other Peruvian specialities. This is exhilarating cuisine featuring a captivating interplay of spicy and sweet chilli peppers, Asian umami and the zing of leche del tigre. The well-curated selection of wines from around the globe adds extra character to this unique dining experience.

Name: Bistrobar Beaune
Description: The magnificent Rosendael Castle houses this fashionable upscale bistro that affords views over the delightful surrounding grounds. This is a seriously cool bistro bar! The wide-ranging menu proposes a range of appealing entrées served in modest portions that diners will find hard to resist. Vegetarian options, a classic cod dish, meat specialities, the house version of an eclair for dessert… You'll be spoilt for choice!

Name: Tres
Description: Walking down the steps to Michael and Emy's intriguing basement restaurant is akin to embarking on an extraordinary adventure. At Tres, the vintage-style decor is pared down and somewhat rugged yet inviting. The best of what local producers have to offer is showcased here. At the expansive dining counter, you will discover the fascinating work of the inventive self-taught chef: his tangy fermentations, rich garums, complex ageing processes, state-of-the-art preparation techniques. Every season brings with it a new set menu, and it is always full of surprises.

Name: Foer
Description: Foer certainly has character both in terms of the stylish decor – nab a place at the dining counter if you can – and the food. The focus here is on vegetables and herbs, perhaps complemented by a fish or meat dish. Using inventive preparation techniques, Steven Broere succeeds in elevating vegetables in original combinations. For instance, he marries intense beetroot cooked in a salt crust and an emulsion of egg yolk with subtle acidity to create a remarkable flavour sensation. The select wines add to this unique sense of harmony.

Name: Bij Hammingh
Description: It is impossible to resist the authentic charm of this former ferry house, from the terrace of which you can fully appreciate the lovely views across the canal and drawbridge. Inside, you can sense the building’s rich heritage, where the chef focuses on regional delicacies that showcase modern techniques and natural finesse.

Name: The Green Rose
Description: Vegetables, fish or meat – the wonderful produce that the Netherlands has to offer is the biggest source of inspiration for Jin Hu and his team of artisans. He takes his cue from the micro seasons and lets nature dictate what goes into his French-Asian fusion dishes. Sustainability is at the heart of this cuisine, which is characterised by the intense authentic flavours of ultra fresh ingredients, as well as an element of surprise. Be sure to sample the extraordinary range of natural wines and special beers.

Name: Puur Zee
Address: Van Ogtropweg 2, Wijk aan Zee, 1949 BA, Netherlands
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: Master chef Imko Binnerts knows how to bring out pure seafood flavours, and how to combine them into a delicious meal. His interesting cuisine is cleverly presented, while the modern combination of flavours is as elegant as the decor.

Name: De Harmonie 23
Description: Whether you opt for the 23-course tasting menu or something from the enticing à la carte selection, creativity is the hallmark of this restaurant. Marco Sommer uses his own house-made ingredients as much as possible in his ambitious cuisine. His dishes are finely balanced and unpretentious. For example, he brings together juicy chicken with a crispy crust, fried morels, Cévennes onion with a surprising pine nut stuffing, as well as a rich poulette sauce, creating a glorious ensemble. This stylish establishment, with its tranquil terrace at the back, pushes boundaries while maintaining a sense of harmony.

Name: 't Nieuwe Diekhuus
Description: This old thatch-roofed farm on the banks of the Yssel provides a charming setting (including a terrace with a stunning view of the river) in which you’ll feel immediately at ease. To this splendid backdrop, enjoy international delicacies (often with an Asian influence) prepared with top-quality ingredients and well-crafted garnishes that provide the perfect accompaniment. Generous cuisine that is well thought out yet gentle on the pocket!

Name: Flores
Description: Owner and sommelier Elroy Slijkhuis has transformed this family-run business into a cosy gastro bistro – the tables on the patio by the wine store are much in demand! He has a clear vision for this enterprise: The emphasis is on plant-forward cuisine, with a commitment to using home-grown/local produce and ensuring the welfare of all parties. Natural wines dominate the wine list. Chef Luuk Freriks's dishes tend to be daring – even unsettling at times. He painstakingly transforms vegetables such as carrots and beetroot into a remarkable "charcuterie" platter. Koji is a tool he frequently uses to create depth, for example drying beef heart in it and then shaving it over a cut of meat to imbue it with profound intensity. At Flores, nature's bounty is showcased in the most innovative of ways.

Name: Bistro Refter
Description: Roelfien Steen and Cor Klevering's cosy bistro is a firm favourite. Don't expect creative excesses here, just authentic classic fare cooked up by an experienced chef; he draws much of his inspiration from French cuisine but also likes to express his love for Mediterranean flavours. This is the kind of place where you can feast on an intense bouillabaisse and a choice cut of meat with a bearnaise sauce prepared in time-honoured tradition.

Name: Restaurant Vannu
Description: Today's culinary landscape is characterised by a shift towards plant-based, zero-waste dishes underpinned by long-established techniques such as fermentation and pickling. At Restaurant Vannu, Gijs Kemmeren gives his creativity free rein, incorporating all those sustainable elements into a multi-course set menu. With seaweed, for example, he adds nuance to the earthiness of beetroot and fresh celery. He also whisks up an intensely flavoursome chanterelle sauce to tie together al dente vegetables and a millet polenta cake. His cuisine is sophisticated, playful and certainly intriguing. The accompanying natural wines and juices underscore the ethos of this establishment. A memorable dining experience is guaranteed.

Name: R21
Description: Start off with an aperitif at the marble counter, before being greeted by the chefs in the kitchen on your way to one of the dining areas, all of which exude a certain Scandinavian elegance. Having long worked with Sergio Herman, Orlando David has developed a vibrant style of cooking. Take, for example, his asparagus, briefly seared to lend it extra flavour, pepped up with wild garlic flowers, and served with a beurre blanc made from fermented asparagus and wild garlic oil to round off the dish with refinement. Sommelier Mattia has a keen understanding of the cuisine and complements it with judicious wine pairings. R21 delivers an exciting and creative culinary experience!

Name: Le Jardin
Description: Behind the dark blue façade on the Mariaplaats, plants and cacti dominate the floral decor at Le Jardin. The front of the restaurant is more intimate; the back is brighter and airier, but it is cosy and inviting throughout. This is a lively place, both in terms of the atmosphere and the cuisine. "Groentenomie" is the name of Tamara de Borst's culinary concept, which builds on vegetables and herbs; meat or fish can be added, if you wish. Rooted in French tradition, her cuisine incorporates innovative twists and occasional Asian seasonings. Think fleshy pumpkin with a herby crunch, a fruity jus with mandarin and a succulent pollock fillet. Garden produce at its best!

Name: De Etalage
Description: What was once a menswear shop is now a cosy bistro with a touch of Parisian charm. The fact that the young chefs have experience at top-flight establishments under their belts is evident in the dishes they create. They put an original spin on the classic combination of veal sweetbreads and onion – the beurre blanc with a hint of caramelised onion is the perfect finishing touch. These chefs have mastered the art of using flavours from around the globe to add nuance to their dishes. So, if you happen to be in Geleen one afternoon, be sure to stop by for a drink and a bite to eat.

Name: SEAson - Arsenaal
Description: Originally erected in 1688 as a military barracks, this building was converted many years later by renowned interior designer Jan des Bouverie.
