Description: There is a well-executed fusion of the old and the new at this city centre restaurant. Stylish, contemporary décor is brought into the vaulted cellar of a 19C riverside merchant's house,  whilst the cooking combines traditional techniques with modern presentation. The finest Nordic ingredients run through the creative dishes, with the combinations offering memorable contrasts of flavours and textures.

Name: Brasserie Blanche
Description: A cosy French restaurant housed in an 18C building which was originally a stable and later spent time as a garage and an interior furnishings store. It has a small front terrace, a bar decorated with wine boxes and a wall made of corks. The chef is a Francophile and creates flavoursome classic French dishes.

Name: Lux Dag för Dag
Description: A stylish, red-brick former factory dating back to 1916 is the home for this brasserie-style waterside restaurant that has a welcome brightness to both its décor and its atmosphere. Local produce is key to their ethos, including the likes of Östergötland lamb and Ängsö pike-perch; expect to see plenty of seasonal ingredients like asparagus and rhubarb appearing on the menu too. Straightforward dishes allow the produce to shine, and demonstrate a solid classical base.

Name: Nokka
Description: A huge anchor and propeller mark out this harbourside warehouse and, inside, three high-ceilinged rooms juxtapose brick with varnished wood. An on-view kitchen allows you to watch wonderful, sustainably sourced ingredients being prepared in a rustic style. There is a strongly Finnish heart to the cooking, which includes classic dishes like freshly made blini topped with crème fraîche, pickled red onions and vendace roe. Friendly, professional service adds to the experience.

Name: Kiin Kiin VeVe
Description: A former bread factory houses this chic restaurant, which serves creative and sophisticated vegetarian cuisine; start with an array of snacks in the lounge. The 6 course tasting menu revolves around the seasons and offers some imaginative combinations. Wine and juice pairings accompany.

Name: Ulla Winbladh
Description: Ulla Winbladh was originally built as a steam bakery for the 1897 Stockholm World Fair and is set in charming parkland beside the Skansen open-air museum. Sit on the terrace or in the older, more characterful part of the building. Typical Swedish dishes include the likes of fish roe and sweet and sour herring.

Name: Vaaghals
Description: In-house aged and cured hams – sliced at your table for an extra dash of theatre – are a feature at this restaurant in one of the city’s modern ‘barcode’ buildings. The place as a whole is bright and relaxed in feel, with an open kitchen affording views of the chefs and a terrace on-hand for the warmer weather. The cooking is underpinned by Norwegian, and largely seasonal, produce; order a few plates to share or go for the set menu to experience the full range of dishes.

Name: Bravo
Description: Bravo was opened at the end of 2022 by a young couple on their first venture – and their enthusiasm and friendliness infuse this sweet little restaurant in a converted house. The menu is refreshingly concise and chef-owner Daniel, from his open kitchen, concentrates on clean, seasonal flavours using local ingredients.

Name: Voisine
Description: Homely and cosy, there is a wonderful lack of pretension to this French-inspired bistro. Flavourful dishes from the small open kitchen include classical French desserts like blueberry clafoutis and Paris-Brest. The restaurant has a lived-in feel, with stripped wooden flooring and leather banquettes. The owners have a wine bar next door and it shows in the excellent wine list and shelves stacked full of bottles.

Name: aster
Description: The faux industrial décor feels like an appropriate fit for this restaurant housed in a former warehouse, in an area once home to the city's shipyards. The kitchen forms part of the room, bringing a certain energy to proceedings, and the friendly team also help to create an enjoyable atmosphere. The short menu offers dishes with a rustic edge, where distinct flavours are nicely balanced – such as minty salsa verde with grilled lamb loin, or sharp apple cutting through a rich chocolate dessert.

Name: Farang
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Wheelchair access
Description: The flavours of Southeast Asia are the inspiration behind this stylish restaurant and bar that occupies the building once home to the Stockholm Electric Company. The unusual front door harks back to its former occupation, but once inside it's a chic space with soft lighting and a large open kitchen. The colorful, zingy cooking includes Thai dishes like laab and crying tiger beef, along with Vietnamese-style sashimi and other influences from the wider region. Strong service, sensible prices and a fun atmosphere complete the picture.

Name: Cru
Description: This friendly neighbourhood restaurant offers guests a choice of dining experiences. Upstairs, in the rustic dining room, they serve a 5 course set menu with inventive British touches and 2 optional extra courses. Downstairs, in the wine bar, you can enjoy everything from snacks to a full meal from an à la carte that includes dishes like bone marrow with beef tartare, chimichurri and toast.

Name: Arakataka
Description: A smart glass-fronted restaurant with a central food bar, an open kitchen and a buzzy atmosphere. Choose from a concise menu of seasonal Norwegian small plates – they recommend 3 savoury dishes plus a dessert per person.

Name: Plah
Description: Norwegian ingredients blended with Thai flavours is the core concept behind this well-run restaurant centred around an open kitchen. The cooking comes in the form of a seafood-focused tasting menu that takes you on a real journey through Thai cuisine and features eye-catching, imaginative dishes that are full of flavour. Adding to the experience are the lively atmosphere and attentive service. Sister restaurant Ahaan offers a simpler take on Bangkok street food, with both eateries housed inside the Sommerro Hotel but independently run.

Name: B.A.R.
Description: This bright, buzzy restaurant is just a cast away from the waterfront and has a semi-industrial fish-market look. Choose your seafood from the fridge or the tank, along with a cooking style, a sauce and one of their interesting sides.

Name: Kolonialen Bislett
Description: Close to the stadium you’ll find this popular neighbourhood bistro, which was previously a grocer’s shop for nearly 80 years. The concise, keenly priced menu includes oysters, cured meats and wholesome Norwegian classics that have been brought up-to-date. There’s a diverse selection of wines by the glass.

Name: Trattoria La Strega
Description: Run by passionate, charming owners, this lively little trattoria is nestled within a quiet residential area, and serves the kind of authentic Northern Italian food that you would find in a good trattoria in Piemonte or Triveneto. Boldly flavoured dishes are best enjoyed from the 'Menu Degustazione', accompanied by a candlelit table and a glass of wine from the extensive Italian selection.

Name: Sjömagasinet
Address: Klippans Kulturreservat, Adolf Edelsvärds gata 5, Gothenburg, 414 51, Sweden
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: A charming split-level restaurant in an old 1775 East India Company warehouse; sit on the upper floor to take in the lovely harbour view. Cooking offers a pleasing mix of classic and modern dishes, with seafood kept to the fore. The wine list offers a good selection of top burgundies.

Name: Bryghuset Vendia - Gourmet
Description: A microbrewery plays host to a stylish brasserie and this tiny gourmet restaurant, which consists of just three tables. It serves an 11 course themed surprise menu of creative, elaborately presented dishes designed to stimulate the taste buds.

Name: Moment
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: A welcoming glow draws you towards this restaurant, as you navigate the dark streets of the small hamlet of Rønde. It’s clear that sustainability runs through Moment’s veins: its permaculture garden guides the menus, the chefs explain the philosophy behind every dish and there’s a remarkable selection of natural wines. Depending on the day, you can choose between a short and a long version of the tasting menu, where well-presented plant-led recipes give prominence to vegetables with dishes such as ‘greens’ or ‘corn, tomatillo and tomato’. Fully vegan and vegetarian menus are available too.

Name: Ghrelin
Description: An elegant, modern restaurant with an open kitchen at its centre, set in the up-and-coming dockland area. Set menus showcase good quality produce and the skilful cooking has a classic French base and some complex, creative touches. Attentive, professional service completes the picture.

Name: Møf
Description: Ask for a seat at the counter to watch the young chef-owners cook in the open kitchen at this cosy, relaxed restaurant. The cooking is Danish at heart and based on local produce, providing great value in dishes that accentuate the central ingredient, like pumpkin gnocchi with smoked and pickled pumpkin. An impressive selection of organic and natural wines are available, as well as a wide range of orange wines.

Name: Shelter
Description: A fun night out is guaranteed at this converted warehouse in a corner of Katajanokka Harbour, close to Uspenskin Cathedral. The serving team are enthusiastic, the atmosphere is contagious, and from the open kitchen come meticulously prepared and appealingly presented dishes that deliver on flavour.

Name: Boon Nam
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Wheelchair access
Description: A fun, intimate restaurant in the basement of the Hotel St George; the perfect place for a night out with friends. The fragrant dishes cover all the regions of Thailand and are good for sharing. Unsure what to order? Then go for one of the set menus, which also include good vegetarian options. A range of cocktails will help to keep you in the party mood, including some specially made to go with dessert.

Name: Hotell Borgholm
Description: The beautiful island of Öland is famous for its wild herbs, and that’s reflected in the cooking at this historic hotel’s restaurant, where the chefs enhance their elaborate dishes with thyme, basil and a host of other flavours from their garden. The cooking comes in a tasting menu format, either short or long, and marries classical techniques with subtle modern ones – all while delivering bold flavours and original combinations The wine list is a real treasure trove for oenophiles.

Name: Carbon
Description: There is an elegant quality to this smart, modern bistro de luxe with rich décor and crushed velvet banquettes. The seasonal menu mixes contemporary techniques with a more traditional base and all dishes come with suggested wine pairings; choose between 5 or 8 courses – alternatively, come on a Wednesday or Thursday for a lighter 3 course option. This is a deservedly busy spot where the attentive, personable service adds to the experience. Be sure to look out for the dishes from the Josper oven.

Name: Geita
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Credit cards not accepted,Wheelchair access
Description: Chef-Owner Axel Nordahl grew up in this area of Oslo and always hoped to open a restaurant in the neighbourhood; years later his dream has come true and he's running this rustically styled spot, dominated by its kitchen counter and embellished by some eye-catching artwork. The cooking comes in the form of a set 4 or 7 course menu, where seafood from cod to hamachi plays a big role. The latter hints at the subtle Japanese influence, which enhances the produce.

Name: Restaurant Saga
Description: There is some eclectic, striking art adorning the walls of this relaxed and trendy restaurant with an adjoining wine bar. The array of bottles to choose from is as impressive as you’d expect, with real depth to the list and numerous vintages from heavy hitting producers. The 8 course tasting menu offers modern, restrained cooking and original touches – like a deconstructed XO sauce – that enhance the dishes.

Name: Boen Gård
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list
Description: Lovingly restored buildings in a beautiful bucolic setting make dining here a memorable experience. The surrounding gardens, meadows and river provide the vegetables, fruits, herbs and fish that are used so respectfully and expertly by the classically trained kitchen; all complemented by an impressive wine cellar. The chef's philosophy of using local ingredients will be explained to you by the excellent service team.

Name: Kappo Andō
Description: Contemporary Japanese cooking and an extensive sake selection are on offer at this chic restaurant just outside the city centre. The décor suits the Japanese theme, with dark wood furnishings and a pure, minimalist feel. Flavourful dishes are underpinned by quality ingredients, with the sashimi proving a highlight and a 'yakitori of the day' option allowing you to enjoy the smoky flavours of meat cooked over binchotan charcoal. Choose between an à la carte or a 7 course tasting menu.

Name: Kiin Kiin
Description: A charming restaurant, whose name means ‘come and eat’. Start with refined versions of street food in the moody lounge, then head for the tasteful dining room decorated with golden Buddhas and fresh flowers. Menus offer modern, personal interpretations of Thai dishes, which have vibrant flavour combinations.

Name: JORD
Description: ‘Forest to plate’ is the message here, with wild and hyper-seasonal ingredients at the fore. Some of the produce is foraged, whilst meat is often hunted by the owner in the surrounding area. The surprise tasting menu delivers a large array of creative dishes with intriguing blends of flavours and textures. Preserving, pickling, smoking and curing are all done in-house, giving new life to the local ingredients.

Name: Fasangården
Description: In an 18th Century house packed with period charm in the famous Frederiksberg Gardens, there's a bucolic feel to this restaurant that's split over three rooms and comes with bold wallpaper, fine plasterwork and crystal chandeliers. Dishes are generous and well-judged, and accompanied by service from an eager-to-please young team. At lunch, the focus is on classic Danish smørrebrød, plus a couple of more substantial offerings; in the evening, there's a short à la carte and a good-value seasonal menu.

Name: TIDES
Description: Surrounded by the sea, mountains and the old harbour, this stylish restaurant benefits from an enviable location nestled inside The Reykjavík EDITION hotel. Quality Icelandic produce forms the core of the menu, which includes carefully cooked dishes like baked arctic char with celeriac, apples and smoked almonds. The warm colours and tasteful décor help make a visit here all the more enjoyable.

Name: Restaurant Palægade
Description: It’s easy to see why this cosy, classic eatery is so popular: from the professional, friendly service to the good value, well-crafted cooking, the team here get everything spot on. Lunch sees smørrebrød brought up-to-date, with seasonal European dishes on offer in the evening.

Name: Lieffroy
Description: A beautiful, yellow-painted house in a lovely location overlooking the sea; inside it’s traditionally furnished, with rustic-chic vibes, a romantic atmosphere and formal service. Classic French cooking features local seafood and is accompanied by a well-chosen wine list.

Name: Det Røde Pakhus
Description: Two experienced owners bring their knowledge together at this modern, wood-furnished restaurant set in the centre of Bornholm’s capital. The chef is passionate about good produce and skilfully prepares local ingredients to create refined, imaginative dishes. Desserts are a highlight.

Name: The Pescatarian
Description: Dine in one of three rooms at this buzzing, minimalist restaurant that, unsurprisingly, features plenty of freshly caught seafood. Choose from the fish-based tasting menu or a vegetarian version, both offered in either 4 or 6 courses. The chef prepares modern dishes with all the typical Danish hallmarks, including preservation techniques and a lightness of touch.

Name: Lyran
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: A small, simply styled restaurant run by a friendly team; sit at the ground floor counter for the best atmosphere. Set tasting menus are created daily from the best available seasonal and local produce and dishes are carefully prepared and well-balanced, with a classic Swedish heart and a modern style.

Name: NISCH
Description: This pleasantly relaxed little neighbourhood restaurant is sleekly and stylishly decorated with a monochrome colour scheme. For its part, the kitchen produces accomplished dishes and boasts some good eco-credentials. The modern, understated Nordic set menu is inspired by global flavours and changes every few weeks. The interesting wine list is mainly organic and biodynamic in nature.

Name: Atelier 33
Description: Bouillabaisse, Paris-Brest and a great selection of burgundies… with a menu like this, it’s hard to believe you’re not in France. Classic bistros and brasseries are the inspiration behind this charming place with a warm, friendly atmosphere. Danish produce is nevertheless at the heart of the cooking, which provides well-executed and satisfying versions of these traditional dishes. The lunch menu includes lighter bites like a croque madame, while at dinner you can pick between the à la carte and a surprise 4 course seasonal menu.

Name: Washoku TOMO
Description: In the western half of Södermalm, Chef-Owner Tomoko Hayashi is bolstering Stockholm’s Japanese dining scene by offering an omakase experience that doesn’t break the bank. While this is Japanese cooking that’s not entirely focussed on sushi, seafood nevertheless plays a central role in the menu. The produce comes from all over the world, be it Spanish sea bass, Argentinian prawns or Canadian black cod. Tomoko leads the smooth service herself with personality and professionalism.

Name: Madonna
Description: Named in part after the painting by Edvard Munch, it is appropriate that this restaurant sits just a few long strides away from Oslo’s Munch Museum. The dining room is small here and so are the plates, which work well for sharing and provide an appealing range of flavours. The influences are global, so don’t be surprised to see tacos sitting next to chawanmushi on the menu, along with some more typically Norwegian fare. There’s a fun, relaxed vibe in the air, and a pleasing eclecticism to the wine list.

Name: Moon
Description: Twin brothers have brought a little piece of France to Bergen in the form of this proudly run, intimate bistro, where Jules cooks and Nicolas runs the service. Honest, classically based French cooking makes use of local produce; desserts are a highlight and wine pairings, well chosen.

Name: Brút
Address: Radisson Blu 1919 Hotel, Pósthússtræti 2, Reykjavík, 101, Iceland
Description: Seafood lovers will feel right at home at this celebration of wonderful fish and shellfish. The likes of marinated scallops and Icelandic whelks join a roll call of prime quality fish, cooked well by an able kitchen in pleasingly uncomplicated dishes that let the central ingredient shine. Stone floors, upholstered benches and open pipework give the dining room a simple, casual feel – and this is accompanied by a lively atmosphere.

Name: xef
Description: A little slice of Spain has landed in the Oslo restaurant scene thanks to this lively spot that sits overlooking the harbour in a modern waterside development. Elaborate and visually striking, dishes are creative but grounded in the influence of northern Spain in particular, including the Chef’s native Galicia. The appearance of components like romesco sauce typify cooking that is as bold in colour as it is in flavour. An excellent Basque cheesecake will ensure your visit ends on a high.

Name: Brasserie Sture 1912
Description: Sture has been an icon of Malmö since 1912, and it’s now been reborn as a classic brasserie with décor to match; think mosaic flooring, closely set tables, a long bar and black-and-white photos of celebrities adorning the walls. A pavement terrace and bustling atmosphere only add to its appeal, as does an extensive menu mixing Swedish dishes with traditional Western European fare like confit rabbit or salad Niçoise. The lengthy wine list has a similar ‘Old World’ focus.

Name: Forma
Description: Chic and sultry, this Södermalm spot delivers the look and vibe of a bar, with the added bonus of flavoursome small plates. The cooking is bang on-trend, blending Nordic and French influences with pan-Asian elements including Korean kimchi, Chinese wontons and a daily selection of Japanese mochi for dessert. If you’re an indecisive diner, go for the keenly priced tasting menu to appreciate the full breadth of the kitchen's talents. Well-versed, professional service is the icing on the cake.

Name: Restaurang Atmosfär
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: A formal yet relaxed eatery on the main road; dine at the bar, in the restaurant or on the pavement terrace. The menu consists of small plates, of which three or four should suffice. Fresh Skåne cooking is delivered with a light touch.

Name: Brutalisten
Description: Owned and created by German artist Carsten Höller, this intriguing concept restaurant abides by the ‘Brutalist Kitchen Manifesto’. Dishes are labelled as either 'Orthodox Brutalist', 'Brutalist' or 'Semi Brutalist', depending on how far they take the ethos of unadulterated prime ingredients presented with minimal accompaniments, freed from the shackles of unnecessary frippery. The first-rate produce is skilfully cooked with a refreshing emphasis on purity of flavour.

Name: Mark
Description: The produce of the Danish countryside is the inspiration behind this stylish city centre bistro that also features some classical French methods in the kitchen. There is a wonderful feeling of spaciousness to the dining room, with its central counter, high ceilings and modern décor. Top quality Danish ingredients are seasoned and cooked with real skill, resulting in a roster of refined and well-balanced dishes.

Name: Natura
Description: Well-chosen Finnish ingredients are used to good effect at this intimate restaurant and techniques like fermenting, pickling, salting, chargrilling and smoking all play their part. Choose from a range of colourful modern small plates or opt for the 'All Out' menu – the full range of dishes in miniature!

Name: Muru
Description: You’d be hard pushed to find a restaurant with a greater focus on wine than Muru. This cosy little bistro is home to quirky touches such as a wine bottle chandelier, a bar made from old wine boxes and a raised ‘cellar’ – and that’s not to mention the nearby wine bar they run. Simple, tasty dishes are on-hand to accompany the excellent wine list, and the sommelier’s pairing suggestions are spot-on.

Name: Festningen
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Great view,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: THIS RESTAURANT IS TEMPORARILY CLOSED DUE TO A FIREA smart, friendly restaurant with a terrace and lovely views over the water to Aker Brygge; it was once a prison and its name means ‘fortress’. The experienced kitchen creates unfussy, attractively presented modern Nordic dishes using fresh local produce. The impressive wine list is strong on burgundy.

Name: Rolfs Kök
Description: A buzzing neighbourhood restaurant in a lively commercial district, run by a passionate chef-owner. The contemporary interior was designed by famous Swedish artists; sit at the counter to watch the chefs in action. Dishes have big flavours, a classic heart, and a wine match each from the impressive list.

Name: Vinkkeli
Description: This charming, deservedly popular restaurant is smartly laid out and run by a delightful team, whose attentive and personable service will make you want to become a regular. The honest, well-judged cooking is a pleasing mix of the modern and the traditional.

Name: Matur og Drykkur
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Wheelchair access
Description: This simple little eatery is named after an Icelandic cookbook and shares its premises with the Saga Museum. Old recipes are given modern twists, resulting in delicious dishes with a creative edge. The finest seasonal produce is used throughout the tasting menu, and transformed into refined, well-balanced dishes by the kitchen team. Friendly, professional service completes the picture.

Name: Pasfall
Description: Watch the eponymous chef at work in the open kitchen of this bright, contemporary restaurant. Top seasonal ingredients are used to create robustly flavoured dishes which are classic in their foundation but modern in delivery.

Name: Restaurant vRÅ
Address: Clarion Hotel Post, Drottningtorget 10, Gothenburg, 411 03, Sweden
Description: The imposing 1920s city post office is now a hotel, and this glamorous restaurant sits within what was the central hall – the listed cashier booths still on display. A Nordic-Japanese approach sees fine Scandinavian produce meet Asian techniques, and there’s an impressive range of sake by the glass.

Name: Amalie
Description: A charming 18C townhouse by Amalienborg Palace - its two tiny, cosy rooms are decorated with antique prints. The menu offers a large choice of traditional Danish dishes, including herring prepared in various ways; pickled, fried and marinated in curry or port are some of the options available for lovers of the fish. Salmon, salads and smørrebrød are also available, in satisfyingly tasty versions of tried-and-tested classics.

Name: Falsled Kro
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list
Description: This charming whitewashed, thatched inn will draw you in with its enticing fireplace and lovely conservatory dining room overlooking the garden. The kitchen takes its cue from the French gastronomy of old, producing rich and indulgent dishes based on quality produce, be it rabbit or langoustine. Many of the ingredients are local, with fruit and vegetables often coming from the estate itself. Watch the chefs in the open kitchen to feel closer to the action.

Name: FYR Bistronomi & Bar
Description: A vibrant restaurant in the barrel-ceilinged cellar of a striking 19C building; its terrace overlooks the adjacent park. Refined, modern bistro cooking includes smørrebrød and snacks at lunch and creative, generously sized dishes at dinner. Sustainability is important to the chef, particularly on issues like their carbon footprint and animal welfare.

Name: Savoy
Description: This local institution’s refurbishment has restored much of its original charm and its 8th floor setting boasts superb views over Esplanade Park. Sophisticated classic dishes have a Finnish-French slant and a modern edge, with the occasional Russian touch. The wine matches are first class.

Name: Vækst
Address: Sankt Peders Stræde 34, Copenhagen, 1453 K, Denmark
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Dining outside ‘inside’ is the theme here, and you’ll find plants, garden furniture and a full-sized greenhouse at the centre of the room. Interesting Danish cooking follows the seasons and is light, stimulating and full of flavour.

Name: Admiralgade 26
Description: This historic house dates from 1796 and sits in one of the oldest parts of the city. It’s a relaxed place: a mix of wine bar, café and bistro, with minimalist décor. From oyster mushrooms to actual oysters, the à la carte comprises a selection of vegetable and fish-led dishes. Wednesday nights are reserved for communal dining and movie nights, while Saturday lunch sees a set, Japanese-style 'choushoku' served. Owner Christian is always eager to let you taste some of the 4,000 wines from the cellar.

Name: tabu
Description: Hidden within a handsome townhouse near the harbour, this contemporary restaurant serves a 5 or 10 course tasting menu, with an à la carte option also available. High quality local and international produce, be it seasonal vegetables or Jutland seafood, is one of the restaurant's greatest strengths – along with the satisfying desserts. Dishes are brought to the table by the chefs themselves and, with notice, can be adapted for vegetarian or vegan diets.

Name: Kanalen
Description: This quaint building was once the Harbour Police Office, and there's a delightful canal-side terrace from which you can watch the boats bobbing up and down as you eat. Inside it has a bistro-like feel, with long wooden benches and old plank flooring. Dishes are seasonal, unpretentious and full of flavour; some honouring Danish traditions and others bringing Mediterranean ingredients into play.

Name: Mielcke & Hurtigkarl
Description: Set in a delightful spot in Frederiksberg Gardens, its walls painted with garden scenes, is this charming 1744 orangery with a fire-lit terrace. Dishes come from around the globe, with Asian influences to the fore – and an amazing array of herbs from the gardens.

Name: Restaurant ET
Description: When this smoothly run brasserie moved location to an elegant 19C house near Aarhus Harbour, the team took the original spirit with them. Familiar Gallic dishes like fish soup are generous in size and robust in flavour, whilst the seasonal dishes have some more modern Danish touches. All the food can be accompanied by wine from their exclusively French and highly impressive cellar.

Name: L' Enoteca di Mr. Brunello
FacilitiesAndServices: Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus
Description: Tucked away near the Tivoli Gardens is this restaurant and wine shop run by passionate, experienced owners. Refined, classic Italian cooking uses good quality produce imported from Italy. As you'd hope, the good value Italian wine list offers over 150 different Brunello di Montalcinos.

Name: Young Hearts
Description: There is a comfortable and contemporary feel to this restaurant in the neighbourhood of Töölö. The cooking is inspired by the seasons and the well-constructed dishes deliver layers of intense flavours, with texture and acidity also playing a key role. There is generosity in the tasting menu offer, including some servings split across multiple complementary dishes – as with scallop presented both raw and as a dried powder to add flavour to a cabbage salad. Wine pairings are available to enhance the experience.

Name: à terre
Description: Tucked behind the Royal Danish Theatre, there is a proud French heart to this cosy bistro created in homage to Jean-Louis le Lay, the Chef-Owner's father, who passed on his love of gastronomy to his son. The tasting menu incorporates global influences including – Caribbean and North African – alongside the classical French base, with good quality ingredients underpinning pared-back and boldly flavoured dishes. A shorter version of the menu is available on Wednesday and Thursday evenings, as well as Saturday lunch.

Name: Söl
Description: Overlooking the 12th Century Stavanger Cathedral, this cosy restaurant has a friendly touch and offers guests a seasonal set menu. Expect an abundance of vegetables in summer and more meat and fish in winter, but with maximum flavour all year round. The Røros butter and freshly baked sourdough bread are a reason to come alone. They are equally passionate about wine, with one of the biggest natural wine lists in Norway.

Name: Tavolo
Description: Step through the heavy brown doors into this buzzing, airy brasserie in a breathtaking conversion of the original stables; a massive horse’s head provides a talking point, as does the American-style bar. Italy provides the inspiration for the food and dishes are simple, tasty and ideal for sharing.

Name: Woodstockholm
Description: A compact bistro owned by a group of friends, who set up a furniture making business and now use the bistro to showcase their products. Cooking follows a theme which changes every two months – perhaps a country, a style of food or a famous chef – and the rustic small plates are simple yet full of flavour.

Name: Koefoed
Description: An intimate collection of rooms in an old coal cellar, where everything from the produce to the glassware celebrates Bornholm island. Modern cooking is accompanied by an impressive range of bordeaux wines. Lunch sees reinvented smørrebrød.

Name: Tollbua
Description: In the Brattøra waterside development, this large eatery provides the crackling atmosphere you want from a brasserie like this. Banquettes and a central bar fit the bill décor-wise, while visible ducting and terrazzo flooring lend an industrial edge. Choose from a 4 or 6 course set menu, with a signature dish of scallops, sea buckthorn, XO and celeriac available as an extra. It’s beautiful Norwegian seafood like this, and skrei cod of course, that will be among the highlights of the meal.

Name: Bon Lio
Description: Kitty and Cato will warmly welcome you into their bright neighbourhood restaurant, which offers a friendly experience that’s more relaxed than most. The ground floor Gastrobar is for drinks and bistro-style small plates, while upstairs it’s all about a multi-course tasting menu. Local, seasonal produce is the bedrock of Cato's cooking, which brings together elements from both his Majorcan and Norwegian heritage in a sophisticated manner. You’ll find the likes of perfectly seared turbot with almond, soya and carrot purée, accompanied by some excellent Spanish wine recommendations.

Name: Lola
Description: This laid-back restaurant is set within a 17C former windmill on the old city ramparts and comes complete with gardens, a terrace and even a pétanque pitch! The original, globally inspired dishes make use of quality local ingredients and are bursting with freshness and packed with flavour. At lunch, choose from a simpler smørrebrød menu.

Name: Levi
Description: Japanese and Italian cuisine join forces at this stylish restaurant near Rosenborg Castle Gardens. Expect to find Italian ingredients mixed into recognisable Japanese dishes and vice versa, such as salsiccia gyozas or spaghettoni with yuzu miso. The ambitious, high quality dishes are served by the friendly, attentive team in a strikingly designed room with high ceilings, bare tables and a large glass front.

Name: STUD!O
Address: Paulas Passage 5, Carlsberg Byen, Copenhagen, 1799, Denmark
Description: Part of the redevelopment around the former Carlsberg Brewery, this is a spacious, stylish restaurant with an open kitchen that lets you observe the chefs as they work. Vegetables from local farms, game in season and top quality seafood – like squid, langoustine and Pacific oysters – underpin original, creative dishes that showcase the ambition of the young team. In a demonstration of their zero-waste ethos, the leftovers from their freshly baked bread are sometimes used as the basis for the dessert.

Name: Café Savoy
Description: Located in the same building as the iconic Restaurant Savoy, on the city’s central esplanade, this well-run brasserie is spacious, airy and deservedly busy. The cooking is classical with a southern French influence, so expect to find the likes of salade Niçoise and ratatouille on the menu. The chefs prepare their good quality ingredients with care, resulting in authentic and flavoursome dishes.

Name: Eero
Description: Perched on the top floor of the former American Embassy and named after its architect Eero Saarinen, this restaurant and cocktail bar features a wrap-around terrace with views of the Oslofjord on one side and The Royal Palace gardens on the other. A wood-fired oven is at the heart of the cooking, which is fish-centric and takes a ‘fin to gill’ approach. So you might get cod tongue as a snack, then later its belly on the bone, enhanced by the richness of its liver and roe. Everyone is served at once from a tasting menu, and some of the dishes are presented ‘family style’.

Name: Black Milk Gastro Bar
Description: A younger sibling of Aloë, this intimate restaurant offers more great cooking with a fun and lively night out thrown into the bargain. Influenced by South America, Asia and Europe, the creative dishes deliver vibrant flavours and well-judged spicing, whilst using plenty of modern techniques. Expect to see some luxury ingredients, like Oscietra caviar and Périgord truffles, alongside an enjoyable dose of theatricality.

Name: Ego
Description: Simplicity runs through the team’s ethos at this relaxed neighbourhood spot, from the minimalist Nordic décor to the straightforward cooking that eschews overcomplication. On the ground floor you’ll find the brighter of the two dining rooms, which also has plants dotted around, whilst the cellar offers moodier lighting and exposed brickwork. There are Finnish elements to the menu, along with some seasonal French ingredients and classic dishes like steak tartare.

Name: Västergatan
Description: An unpretentious modern bistro on a city centre street; owned and run by a young couple (he cooks, while she looks after the service). The regularly changing set menu offers fresh seasonal dishes with a classic Swedish heart. Vegetarians are well looked after and juice and wine flights are available.

Name: Symbios
Description: There’s a wonderfully unpretentious feel to this relaxed, friendly restaurant perfectly suited to the trendy suburb of Södermalm. Watch the world go by as you relax with an aperitif on the pavement terrace, before enjoying classic Swedish and southern European dishes that are simple, fresh and full of flavour. The midweek lunch menu represents great value for money, and the place is informally yet professionally run by a friendly team.

Name: Frank
Description: The open kitchen takes centre stage at this relaxed, contemporary restaurant, with its soft lighting, flickering candles, comfy sofas and designer wooden furnishings. Choose between an à la carte and a tasting menu – both of which offer flavour-packed, original and understated modern dishes.

Name: Sushi Anaba
Description: A Japanese staple through a Nordic lens is what you can expect at this compact quayside sushi restaurant that seats just eight diners round its counter. The Danish Chef-Owner trained in Tokyo and brings a passionate approach to the cooking, which is underpinned by superb produce from Nordic waters, be it Norwegian scallop or lobster from Jutland. An excellent sake selection highlights some lesser-known choices.

Name: Brasserie Hansken
Description: A delightfully traditional brasserie, centrally located by the City Hall, with various charming dining areas and a fantastic terrace. Classical cooking follows the seasons and mixes French and Scandic influences; seafood is a speciality.

Name: Theo
Description: Located in the heart of Copenhagen, this is the sort of restaurant we’d all love to have in our neighbourhood. The team here have dedicated themselves to serving uncomplicated, appealing dishes that offer good value for money. Charming service and an unpretentious approach to both the décor and food strengthens their mission, as does the simple yet consistently high quality cooking.

Name: BORD
Description: You’re guaranteed a warm welcome at this sweetly run bohemian bistro. A communal table is at the heart of things, with a few smaller tables and counter seats available too. Starters merge into mains on the Mediterranean-inspired daily menu of unfussy, pared-back dishes. Skilful cooking keeps the focus on the top quality ingredients; don't miss the turbot from the wood-fired oven if you get the chance.

Name: BELLIES
Description: Vegetable lovers will find paradise at this plant-powered restaurant that celebrates fabulous, yet often overlooked, ingredients. Whether it's beetroot, pumpkin or Jerusalem artichoke, quality vegetables are given a starring role that they are rarely afforded. A range of Asian elements, from Sichuan pepper to ssamjang, are used to embellish the natural flavours of the produce, as are fermented and preserved components made in-house. There’s a lovely atmosphere and all dishes are served with a smile.

Name: Boulevard
Description: The welcome is warm, the room elegant, and the food heartening and eminently satisfying. The passion and experience of the two chef-owners is evident in all areas of this likeable restaurant. The quality of the fish and shellfish really comes through, thanks to the classic techniques used by the kitchen.

Name: Bulot
Description: There’s a real buzz about this neighbourhood wine-bar-cum-bistro, which makes it so appealing as soon as you set foot through the door. The personable team keep things relaxed as they serve a seasonal tasting menu which comes with a subtle French slant and plenty of seafood – the restaurant’s name is French for whelk, so expect to find one somewhere on the menu. The simple, well-cooked dishes are also available from the à la carte as small plates.

Name: freyja.
Description: Head straight for the roof terrace to kick off your visit with a cocktail and 360° views of Stockholm and, once inside, opt for a seat by the curved window to capitalise on the 13th floor location. The menu includes modernised yet comforting Swedish classics like Kroppkaka, executed with care and confidence, yielding well-balanced flavours. This is a place where you'll feel equally at home dining in a couple or as a group, as it delivers something for everyone.

Name: Oxenstiernan
Description: You can’t miss this stylish, orange-painted bistro which stands out against the greenery of a city park; in summer, dine on the terrace, under the trees. A sustainable ethos runs throughout, from the interior design to the ethically sourced produce used in the unfussy, boldly flavoured Swedish dishes.

Name: Pull
Description: Within the rejuvenated, pre-war industrial area of the ‘Rotermann Factories’ sits an impressive 19C grain elevator and, inside that, this fittingly rustic restaurant with exposed stone walls and concrete pillars. Generously proportioned Estonian dishes focus on meats and charcoal-grilled steaks.

Name: Wicca
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Angelica Udeküll is not only a TV chef but a torchbearer for Estonian food. Her elegant restaurant at the LaSpa hotel sits in a beautifully tranquil spot overlooking the pine trees and the sea – and is the perfect location to showcase her ethical cooking. Dishes are creative, with some Nordic touches.

Name: Hõlm
Description: The restaurant is named ‘Hõlm’ and the hotel within which it sits, ‘Lydia’ – after Lydia Grünmann Hõlm, on whose recipes the dishes here are based. Full-length windows flood the elegant dining room with light and the attractively presented dishes exhibit appealing combinations of both texture and flavour.

Name: Art Priori
Description: Set in the heart of the Old Town, this is a wonderfully elegant, romantic spot, where two striking rooms ooze period charm and an eclectic mix of artwork fills the walls. In contrast, the food is modern and understated. Well-formed dishes give each core ingredient the space to shine, with unadulterated flavours fitting together seamlessly. You might find earthy yellow beetroot paired with soft goat’s cheese or wonderfully mature venison with a silky celeriac purée. Friendly service and a great choice of cocktails and wines by the glass finishes things off perfectly.

Name: Olevimägi 9, Tallinn, 10123, Estonia
FacilitiesAndServices: This pop-up turned permanent is sister to Mere 38 in Võsu. It exudes a cool, fashionable vibe, courtesy of a modern interior with striking murals which contrast with its historic exterior and quaint Old Town setting. Well-judged, creative dishes have subtle Asian influences and are attractively presented.

Name: Tchaikovsky
Description: Set within the well-known Hotel Telegraaf, in the heart of the Old Town, this glass-roofed, restaurant has something of a celebratory feel, courtesy of a beautiful chandelier and battleship-grey walls hung with gilt-framed pictures. Cooking has a classical French base with Russian influences and modern overtones.

Name: Lee
FacilitiesAndServices: Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: A ‘Lee’ is the ancient communal fireplace around which families would sit together to prepare a meal – and this powder blue restaurant with ornate columns and a charming courtyard setting certainly has a historic feel. The cooking ranges in style from the traditional to the modern, with the chef’s background showing through in dishes with distinct Asian influences, like Liivimaa dry-aged beef short rib with cauliflower cream and wasabi or cherry mille-feuille with green tea and tofu cream.

Name: Rado
Description: It might be located in the delightfully historic Old Town but Rado is contrastingly smart and modern. It has a buzzy vibe on the ground floor and a more intimate feel in the basement. The chatty team will guide you through the menu of seasonal modern dishes; don’t miss the venison carpaccio.

Name: Fotografiska
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Brunch,Counter dining,Great view,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Above the Fotografiska photo gallery sits an equally striking restaurant offering picture-perfect views out across the Old Town; be sure to start or end your night with cocktails in the rooftop bar. A concept of ‘Sustainable Pleasure’ leads the way here, with a ‘leaf to root, nose to tail’ ethos and a zero-waste approach. Organic, sustainably farmed ingredients are showcased in a highly original selection of assured, understated dishes which reflect the chef’s French and Swedish training; go for the daily changing 360° surprise menu and the interesting wine pairings.

Name: Joyce
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: A modern shopping centre in the heart of the city plays host to this large, split-level brasserie with bold décor, a popular cocktail bar and a buzzy vibe. Attractively presented dishes mix local and Baltic influences: the kitchen adds creative twists and flavours pack a punch.

Name: ÂME
Description: Housed within a small boutique hotel on the edge of the Old Town is this elegant restaurant where the old and the new combine: part of the Medieval city wall runs down one side of the room, yet it also has a contemporary, design-led style. Âme is French for ‘soul’ and, while the appealingly understated dishes certainly have a French heart, flavours are also drawn from around the globe and, as such, are described as ‘dishes that feed the soul’. Opt for one of the two tasting menus to sample a range of these dishes, such as goose breast à l'orange or roasted cauliflower à la Marrakech.

Name: Gianni
Description: Pop into the café for coffee and cake, or dine in a more cossetted environment in the modern restaurant. The charming team are eager to please and will even skilfully fillet your fish at the table for you. The comprehensive menu offers all the Italian dishes you know and love; the saltimbocca is a highlight.

Name: RADIO
Description: Part wine shop, part café-cum-bistro, this neighbourhood establishment is all things to all people. You enter via a shop packed full of interesting wines, before heading through the restaurant where a glass wine cave takes centre stage. The room has a bistro feel – there are even a few sofas available for those who like it super laid-back – and dishes come in the form of medium-sized plates that are designed for sharing. From sausage soup to cured trout or onion pie, each dish comes with the perfect wine recommendation.

Name: Kolm Sõsarat
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Credit cards not accepted,Garden or park
Description: Three Sisters run this small, remotely set restaurant and each has their role to play: Kerti does the cooking, Triin looks after the service and Kadri tends to the kitchen garden. The playful set menu is a showcase of the area, featuring top quality produce from their garden and farm – such as in the country-style mushroom, potato and sauerkraut – while superb honey from their father’s long-established hives is celebrated in desserts such as honey, apple and milk with sea buckthorn. This is a truly special place where the passion of the team is palpable, as they go above and beyond to care for every guest.

Name: Lahepere Villa
Description: Built by the owner himself, this homely restaurant sits in a wooded spot behind the beach. Inside are chunky wood tables and cushion-strewn sofas; outside, a blazing firepit, fleece-covered chairs and a ‘Big Green Egg’. The fortnightly set menu is inspired by the area and warm service is from a family team.

Name: Alexander
Address: Pädaste Manor, Muhu Island, Pädaste, 94716, Estonia
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Valet parking
Description: A visit to Alexander starts with a ferry ride from the mainland to Muhu Island. Named after the last noble owner of the beautiful Pädaste Manor – within which it sits – this elegant restaurant welcomes you in with its tranquil atmosphere and sweeping parkland views. Foraged and seasonal island produce guides the ambitious new Nordic cooking. Choose between the 4 course daily menu or the 7 course Degustation menu; the latter must be booked 24hrs in advance.

Name: SOO
Description: Visionary owner Ragnar Sass purchased the Maidla Estate and manor house back in 2019, then added some rather smart eco-lodges in the woods and wetlands – as well as this intimate 5-table restaurant. Sustainability and ecological considerations are key, and the set dinner menu looks to the seasons and the region for its inspiration. Dishes are rich in flavour but come with a welcome lightness, and foraging, pickling and preserving all play their part. Wines are organic and natural.

Name: Horisont
Description: Arrive early for an aperitif in the bar, which affords stunning panoramic views towards the harbour from the 30th floor of the smart Swissotel Tallinn hotel. There’s a formal feel to the room, with modern European menus to match; to see the full talents of the kitchen, go for the tasting menu.

Name: Mon Repos
Description: This former imperial summer residence comes with a charming interior which blends original stained glass windows and panelled ceilings with sleek, modern furnishings. The modern menu reflects the locale and extends across to the Mediterranean, with colourfully presented dishes exhibiting flavours and textures which have been well thought through. The gravlax with beets, horseradish and blinis is a must to start, and to finish the tiramisu is a winner. The lovely terrace looking out over Kadriorg Park is a popular spot.

Name: Nok Nok
Description: Nok means ‘bird’ in Thai, which makes sense when you spot the two stone owls set into the stonework. With its central location and two spacious, colourfully decorated dining rooms, this is a popular place to eat both amongst locals and visitors. Authentic Thai flavours are sure to warm you up on colder days and you’ll find all your Thai favourites, from a wonderful chicken satay with sweet and sour pickles to rich curries, such as a Massaman made using braised short ribs. Be sure to save room for dessert though, as the sticky rice with mango is superb.

Name: Moon
Description: The word ‘Moon’ refers to the poppy seed, which is an apt name, as it’s hard not to eat too much of the delicious poppy seed bread here! Split into three rooms, this intimate bistro comes with bright décor, a lovely teacup chandelier and a seasonally changing menu comprising flavoursome Slavic dishes. The sweet team greet both locals and visitors as if they are regulars.

Name: R14
Description: The impressive 19C stone-built powerplant of the Rotermann factories is now a wine-shop-cum-wine-bar with a rustic, laid-back vibe, where a glass-walled wine cellar takes centre stage. Good value, unfussy Mediterranean dishes have a leaning towards Italy; come on a Sunday if you’re a fan of brunch.

Name: Barbarea
Description: A former rubber boot factory in an up-and-coming area plays host to this city hotspot, which starts the day as a bakery and then morphs into a stylish, laid-back bistro in the evening. Family-style dining is at the heart of their ethos and the vibrant, flavour-packed sharing plates follow the seasons, with 50-75% of the ingredients (depending on the month) having been produced organically. The wine list comprises a good selection of natural, organic and biodynamic wines, and they have a wine bar next door where you can continue your night.

Name: Puri
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Credit cards not accepted,Great view,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Part of the marina development northwest of the city centre is this striking modernist building with an equally impressive split-level interior boasting floor-to-ceiling windows and contemporary blonde wood furnishings. Creative modern cooking sees seafood dishes taking the starring role; maybe start with a wine ‘baba’ topped with succulent langoustines before moving on to gratinated crab with creamy risotto. To accompany are a great selection of wines by the glass, with everything brought to the table by a cheery team.

Name: Rado
Description: Sister to the restaurant of the same name in Tallinn – and also with their signature bicycle parked outside – is this bright, modern bistro run by a sweet, friendly team. The small menu is chalked up on the blackboard and the fresh, unfussy cooking represents great value. In summer, head for the terrace at the back.

Name: Mere 38
Description: Set in a quiet village, this green-painted wooden house boasts both a fashionable New England style restaurant and smart apartments. It has a cosy dining room with fleece-covered chairs, as well as a lovely summer terrace. Dishes are largely Mediterranean influenced and are vibrant and full of flavour.

Name: Paju Villa
Description: The suburb of Nõmme is home to this elegant art nouveau villa named after Karoline Paju, who built the house in 1931. Dining takes place over two floors, with several small, interconnecting rooms creating a stylish, intimate space. Instead of being listed as Starters, Mains and Desserts, the appealing dishes are listed under the tempting-sounding headings of 'Can’t Resist', 'For a Real Gourmand' and 'Cherry on Top'; modern twists bring an extra element to classically based recipes.

Name: Casa Rios
Description: Chef Rodrigo Aguiar, originally from Rio de Janeiro, combined his skills with owner Giovanna Perrone to realise her dream here. This charming restaurant features an open kitchen where guests can view the wood oven and churrasco grill, both of which exude the smoky flavours for which Casa Rios is famous. If you sit at the bar counter, you can watch the preparation process in full flow as well as appreciate the aromas emanating from the kitchen. The cuisine here is based around typical Brazilian cooking with a focus on the south-east of the country, using ingredients from small-scale producers and a constant nod to seasonality. Whether you opt for the tasting menu or à la carte, make sure you try the wood oven-baked pizzeta of merguez sausage made with cornbread – an absolute must!

Name: Borgo Mooca
Address: Rua Barão De Tatuí, 302, São Paulo, 01226-030, Brazil
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Bring your own bottle,Counter dining,Valet parking
Description: Fried gnocchi, egg pasta, langoustine, octopus and black rice with squid ink are just some of the dishes and ingredients you’ll find here, a list enhanced by the slow-fermented and Maraschino cherry babá with a smooth crème anglaise. This gastronomic refuge is located in the Santa Cecília district and features a modern-retro style and uncluttered atmosphere. It includes a bar counter overlooking the kitchen, decoration that is teeming with details on the walls and ceiling, plus a basement bar called Bargo offering an array of superb cocktails. Chef Matheus Zanchini conjures up creative cuisine with Italian nuances, including homemade pasta, all of which is prepared with top-quality ingredients. The menu is updated weekly in line with the availability of ingredients sourced by the chef.

Name: Bicol Korean Cuisine
Address: Rua José Getúlio 422, São Paulo, 01509-000, Brazil
Description: Bicol is a must if you’re keen to try Korean barbecue-style cuisine. This classic address in the Liberdade district of the city has been run by a South Korean family for three generations. In this spacious restaurant, the tables have their own grills so that guests can cook meat (usually cut super-fine) to their individual taste. Dishes for sharing are the mainstay here, including the Burgogui, Garbi and Samguiopsar combos, always accompanied by Banchan (small side dishes of the day). The Bibimbap (a typical rice dish) and the soups are other interesting options on the menu, not forgetting the delicious kimchi, of course. Why not pair your food with the traditional soju, a typical Korean beverage with differing strengths of alcohol?

Name: Corrientes 348 - Marina da Glória
Address: Avenida Infante Dom Henrique, Rio de Janeiro, 20021-140, Brazil
Description: The name of this restaurant is a reference to the famous Argentinian tango “A Media Luz”, while the number 348 corresponds to the number of the street where the first of the brand’s ventures opened in Greater São Paulo. It overlooks the Marina da Glória, hence the spectacular views from tables on the terrace, and features several spacious dining rooms and an extensive glass-fronted wine cellar. The culinary focus is of course on Argentina and choice cuts of meats cooked on the grill, including specialities such as ribeye, centre cut ribeye, filet mignon with garlic, chorizo sausage and top sirloin, all accompanied by sides designed for sharing. To finish, the “dulce de leche” pancake served with sorbet is an authentic Argentinian dessert that is truly irresistible.

Name: Mäska
Address: Rua Joana Angélica, 159, Rio de Janeiro, 22420-030, Brazil
Description: It's worth braving the frenetic traffic along Ipanema’s narrow streets to eat at this modern but relaxed restaurant with a contemporary bistro feel and a kitchen that opens on to the dining room in which you can savour chef Danilo Parah’s “innovative and emotional” cuisine. Here, the chef showcases Asian ingredients in contemporary dishes that are generous, colourful and pleasing on the palate. The impressively varied menu is complemented by dishes inspired by ingredients available in the market, such as the highly popular spaghetti with beurre blanc and braised prawns. The dining experience and atmosphere are enhanced by Mäska’s array of refreshing cocktails.

Name: NOTIÊ
Description: Although only recently opened, this restaurant is already being talked about by the city’s foodie community. Located on the rooftop of the Shopping Light building, its design comes as a pleasant surprise as soon as you walk through the door thanks to its decor of yellow tones, glass-fronted kitchen enabling guests to watch the chefs hard at work and, first and foremost, the 18m panel on the ceiling depicting images of nature. At the helm in the kitchen is Paraíba-born chef Onildo Rocha who impresses with his use of typical Brazilian ingredients and combinations that result in intense and striking dishes. His recipes are based around his journeys to different Brazilian regions every season, and are showcased on 5-, 7- and 11-course tasting menus. The name of the restaurant is a fusion between one of the country’s most colourful birds, the tanager (tiê in Portuguese) and the Portuguese word for night (noite).

Name: Tiara
Address: Rua Ataulfo De Paiva, 270 loja 111, Rio de Janeiro, 22440-900, Brazil
Description: The name Tiara refers to the district (Itacoatiara) in which chef Rafa Gomes was born. Nowadays, he owns two restaurants called Itacoa and, to complete the full name, Tiara. This famous chef is known for his appearance on reality cooking shows and his impressive career thus far, including stints in leading restaurants in New York. Housed in the Rio Design Leblon complex, the restaurant boasts an elegant backdrop of soothing tones for innovative cuisine that relies on modern techniques and the use of seasonal ingredients where possible. Here, the chef elevates duck meat (a key ingredient in his story) to another level. An example of this is the aged duck lacquered with honey and spices served with pumpkin, miso and a “gastrique” sauce – a quite surreal combination!

Name: Chez Claude São Paulo
Address: Rua Professor Tamandaré Toledo 25, São Paulo, 04532-020, Brazil
Description: Part of the Le Quartier food complex, this space is divided between the Chez Claude restaurant, the Bar du Quartier and the refined Bistrot du Quartier. At the helm, famous chef Claude Troisgros follow the same concept as in Rio de Janeiro. The kitchen, which is completely open in the middle of the room, enables guests to really feel and be part of the lively and vibrant ambience here. The menu is based around French techniques and influences from Brazil and elsewhere in Latin America, resulting in colourful recipes full of flavour and texture. Standout dishes include the superb combination of scallops served with caviar, chuchu and Jataí honey; the duck magret accompanied by pear in wine and blueberry; and for dessert the light and creamy “doce de leite” cheesecake with a Canastra cheese sauce.

Name: Naga
Address: Rua Bandeira Paulista 385, São Paulo, 04532-011, Brazil
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining,Notable sake list,Valet parking
Description: A legendary Japanese restaurant in the city that has for a long time been a favourite address for aficionados of the country’s cuisine. It’s no surprise that the Nagayama group does not just have a single restaurant – in fact, in this area they own almost an entire block that includes the Bar do Naga, the Café do Naga etc. It is split between two floors, with access to the floor above via an attractive steep staircase. In the latter you’ll find two rooms: a waiting area with just a few tables, and a second more spacious room with a direct view of the pleasantly and subtly illuminated sushi bar. The extensive menu features a wide array of carpaccios, sushi, sashimi, uramaki, temaki, tartares and teppanyaki, and if there are several of you, you may want to try combination options such as the popular Naga Case 2 or the enticing Omakase-style tasting menu.

Name: Kosushi
Description: The name of the restaurant has a direct link with Japanese philosophy as the word “ko” (which translates as “turtle”) is associated with long life and the symbolism of the number 1. Opened in 1988 by chef George Yuji Koshoji, it is now located at a different address (in the Itaim Bibi district), where it has become a popular meeting place for locals. It boasts a welcoming, contemporary ambience, soft lighting and a decor of bright colours, plus an impressive large balcony from where guests can watch their dishes being prepared. The extensive menu offers a variety of options such as gyosas, tartares, ussuzukuri, uramaki, sushi and sashimi, as well as hot dishes that include yakisoba, octopus yaki and Wagyu medallions. It also features a superb selection of sakis and innovative cocktails.

Name: Loup
Address: Dr. Mário Ferraz 528, São Paulo, 01453-011, Brazil
Description: Loup’s unique decor and atmosphere, featuring several dining spaces, designer details, lofty glass ceilings and an impressive vertical garden, have been very carefully curated, and provide the backdrop for an enticing fusion of cuisine from different parts of the world, prepared with top-quality ingredients and enhanced by a Raw Bar section serving an array of tartares, carpaccios, ceviches etc. If you prefer to be seated at a more traditional table, the menu includes delicious mini palm heart pastries with prawns, appetising dishes such as arroz de pato (rice with duck) that take you back to Portugal, and for dessert, the irresistible cannoli with a light yet crunchy dulce de leche and red berries, which transports you to the shores of Italy. It’s also worth taking time out to enjoy a cocktail in the lounge.

Name: Charco
Address: Rua Peixoto Gomide 1492, São Paulo, 01409-002, Brazil
Description: In this restaurant inspired by the typical cuisine of the Rio Grande do Sul region, chef Tuca Mezzomo leads his team alongside Nathalia Gonçalves – masters in the art of preparing grilled and flame-cooked dishes with a continual focus on the best and freshest ingredients. Dishes that you won’t want to miss include the toasted mushrooms with smoked pumpkin and parmesan, and the succulent grilled Wagyu short rib, served with a wild tomato salad and a Bordelaise sauce. In addition, the restaurant also produces its own delicious sausages, butter and fresh goat’s cheese. The backdrop to the dining experience is a rustic, welcoming mix of exposed brickwork, wooden tables and subdued lighting that adds to the pleasant ambience.

Name: Pobre Juan
Address: Rua Comendador Miguel Calfat 525, São Paulo, 04537-082, Brazil
Description: The first Pobre Juan outlet opened in the Vila Olímpia in 2004 and nowadays you’ll find the brand all across the country. Inspired by traditional Argentinian steakhouses, Pobre Juan serves top-quality grilled meats in an informal and rustic setting. Each of its restaurants features a wide array of carefully selected meats, a process that extends from their provenance to the maturing process. Whether you order classic options such as short ribs, ribeye or flank, or the more exclusive centre cut ribeye, porterhouse or Wagyu, every dish here is perfectly cooked. If you’re eating out with friends, you may want to order the Gran Tabla, which serves three people and comes with delicious sides. Fish, seafood and chicken, all cooked on the open grill, are also available, as well as sublime desserts such as the exquisite churros with dulce de leche.

Name: Cepa
Address: Praça Dos Omaguás, 110, São Paulo, 05419-020, Brazil
Description: Cepa is one of those restaurants that always features in food-related conversations in the city, and now it has a new home in the Pinheiros neighborhood! Here, chef Lucas Dante presents creative, seasonal cuisine that prioritises the freshness of ingredients and champions small-scale producers. By his side is sommelier and front-of-house manager Gabrielli Fleming, who is in charge of sourcing biodynamic and organic wines for the cellar that are always the perfect pairing for your choice of dish. We can highly recommend the simply incredible starter of Wagyu tongue with chicken broth, okra and mint.

Name: Lilia
Address: Rua do Senado 45, Rio de Janeiro, 20231-005, Brazil
Description: This unique restaurant, with an unremarkable façade that could easily pass unnoticed among the historic colonial-style houses in the Lapa district, is located just a few metres from the conical São Sebastião cathedral. As you walk up a long, narrow staircase, you come to this two-storey restaurant featuring brick walls and corrugated iron panelling which endow it with a spacious, uncluttered and industrial feel. Here, chef Rafael Scatolin heads up a kitchen characterised by its creativity, where the cuisine is updated daily in line with the availability of ingredients. A three-course set menu is available at lunchtime, while at dinner you can choose between options on the à la carte or an eleven-course tasting menu. And make sure you save space for the Chocolate ganache, cupuaçu caramel and cocoa crunch, which it is an absolute must!

Name: Mesa do Lado
Address: Rua Conde Bernadotte 26, Rio de Janeiro, 22430-200, Brazil
Description: A recent innovation from the Troisgros Group and one with a completely different concept that ensures a unique dining experience. Here, inside the renowned Chez Claude restaurant in Leblon, chef Claude Troisgros offers a sensory gastronomic experience that aims to awaken all five senses. The small dining room, with seating for just 12 guests per sitting, provides the setting for a tasting menu that evolves in line with lighting effects and the projection of images that varies according to the background music. The contemporary cuisine has a strong French influence and somewhat nostalgic feel thanks to family recipes handed down through the generations. Timings are strict here so you’ll need to arrive and depart at your appointed times!

Name: L'Etoile
Address: Avenida Niemeyer 121, Rio de Janeiro, 22450-220, Brazil
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Great view,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus
Description: L'Etoile is the perfect option if you’re planning a romantic dinner with breathtaking views. Located on the 26th floor of the imposing Sheraton Grand Rio Hotel & Resort on Leblon Beach, the restaurant boasts a sophisticated and romantic atmosphere and a menu that bears the signature of renowned chef Jean-Paul Bondoux, who reinterprets classic French techniques and combines these with Brazilian ingredients. The kitchen is under the daily charge of chef Juan Garcia Molina, who brings his own personality touch to dishes, which are available on an à la carte and a seven-course tasting menu. The creative desserts are the domain of pastry chef Mariana Ribeirinha, who conjures up delicate dishes with sublime flavours!

Name: Térèze
Address: Rua Felicio dos Santos 15, Rio de Janeiro, 20241-260, Brazil
Description: Térèze is the perfect choice if you’re on the lookout for a quiet setting for a romantic supper. It is part of the Santa Teresa Mgalley hotel, a delightful historic property built in 1850 with a sophisticated atmosphere and breathtaking views. The menu is based around a contemporary theme that uses seasonal ingredients, plus a mix of Brazilian and international recipes. Chefs Jérôme Dardillac and Luanna Malheiros conjure up surprising combinations such as the perfectly grilled octopus with a chickpea purée, ratatouille and a delicious rougail sauce. After lunch or dinner, why not prolong the enjoyment with a drink in the delightful surroundings of the charming bar?

Name: Mr. Lam
Address: Rua Maria Angélica 21, Rio de Janeiro, 22470-201, Brazil
Description: Mr. Lam gained renowned for his culinary prowess in restaurants in New York and London, however he has run this modern, sophisticated eatery on the edge of the Rodrigo de Freitas lagoon for almost two decades. In contrast with other gastronomic restaurants these days, the majority of dishes on the menu have been mainstays since it first opened, in so doing keeping with the tradition of offering the best Chinese cuisine. Featuring a hint of cutting-edge innovation as well as a focus on top-quality ingredients, the menu boasts memorable dishes such as the lightly battered and crispy Senhor Batista prawns, with a delicious sweet and sour sauce. The restaurant is laid out on three floors, with an attractive dining room and welcoming bar on the top floor that includes picture windows and a glass roof that provide lots of natural light and stunning views.

Name: Sud, O Pássaro Verde
Address: Rua Visconde de Carandaí 35, Rio de Janeiro, 22460-020, Brazil
Description: Walking into this restaurant is like entering the home of a friend, as you’ll need to knock on the door or announce your presence in order to be let in. Occupying a house in the quiet Jardim Botânico district, this is the domain of chef Roberta Sudbrack who describes it as a space in which to “tell and eat stories”. Inside, the decor is modest yet welcoming, with an impressive wood-fired oven next to the main dining room, plus a charming open kitchen, from which comforting home-style dishes emerge prepared with ingredients from small-scale local producers. As a result, the menu changes daily in line with market availability and freshness. However, one mainstay that is always on the menu is the superbly textured and irresistibly flavoured chocolate cake (“bolo de chocolate molhadinho”).

Name: Giuseppe Grill Leblon
Address: Avenida Bartolomeu Mitre 370, Rio de Janeiro, 22431-001, Brazil
Description: As the name clearly states, all the dishes (fish and meat) at this restaurant are cooked on the charcoal grill. The menu here includes dry-aged meat options (T-bone, prime rib, bone-in tenderloin etc). Other standout dishes include the Maminha (sirloin trip-tip), the Picanha supra sumo (supra sumo rump cap), the brand’s registered trademark, as well as the slow-cooked Uruguayan lamb shoulder served with its own jus. A number of fish and seafood options are also on display, which vary according to availability on the day. The decor here features exposed stone walls, wooden chairs and leather sofas, all of which combine to add a rustic-elegant touch. Not forgetting the extensive wine cellar in the basement, featuring over 400 labels from different countries.

Name: Fasano
Address: Rua Vitório Fasano 88, São Paulo, 01414-020, Brazil
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: The grand piano at the entrance and the lounge with its high ceiling and skylight take us right back to the New York of the 1940s. A symbol of quality, glamour and fine dining, the Fasano is renowned across Brazil for its classic Italian cuisine, albeit with a modern touch. The menu, designed by chef Luca Gozzani, showcases an extensive array of copious and surprising dishes on which pasta plays a starring role. We can recommend starting with the creamy burrata with Parma ham, followed by a succulent lamb fillet with gnocchi, with a delicious panna cotta as a final flourish – a combination of dishes that will take you on a gastronomic adventure back to Italy. The exceptional service from the front-of-house team makes the experience even more special!

Name: Casa Santo Antônio
Address: Avenida João Carlos da Silva Borges 764, São Paulo, 04726-001, Brazil
Description: This extraordinary partnership is the result of a bond of friendship, the fruits of which are clearly visible in this superb gastronomic restaurant. Located somewhat off the beaten track in the southern section of São Paulo, it occupies a property built in the 1960s. It features a charming and elegant space with various dining rooms, a stunning bar and an outdoor terrace when the weather allows (a section of the glass-fronted kitchen is also visible to guests). The menu showcases an Italian influence with fresh homemade pastas, generous portions and moderate prices. An “executive” menu is also available during the week. Standout dishes here include the authentic and extremely delicious spaghetti alla carbonara, and the classic tiramisu, with its perfect creamy texture.

Name: Território Aprazível
Address: Rua Aprazível 62, Rio de Janeiro, 20241-270, Brazil
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Great view,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Valet parking
Description: Aprazível is a must for those who love delicious food inspired by nature. This family-run restaurant, located inside an exuberant tropical garden and furnished in rustic style, boasts a superb view of the city. Here, chef Ana Castilho conjures up typical Brazilian dishes teeming with flavour and created using organic and biodynamic ingredients, yet without neglecting either elegance or delicacy. One of her signature dishes is the free-range “galinhada caipira”, served with a delicious free-range chicken-flavoured rice, plantains, sausage from Minas Gerais, braised cabbage, and a tasty pepper jelly and beans. Enjoy Aprazível’s pleasant atmosphere and charming setting in the company of a relaxing drink!

Name: Aconchego Carioca
Address: Rua Barão de Iguatemi 245, Rio de Janeiro, 20270-060, Brazil
Description: A whole host of traditional dishes such as the rice-based “arroz de rabada”, “baião de dois” (black-eyed peas with rice) and the unmissable Bolinho de feijoada (fried feijoada dumplings) are just some of the dishes served in this restaurant, which has become a popular culinary focal point in the northern part of Rio de Janeiro. Here, well-known chef Kátia Barbosa creates cooking with a focus on typical Brazilian dishes with influences from the north-east of the country, all of which are prepared with meticulous detail and lots of flavour. In this completely relaxed and informal setting, decorated with hammocks hanging from the ceilings, the pleasant garden and friendly staff make you feel very much at home. Make sure you also try the innovative and amazing cocktails!

Name: Aiô
Description: If you’re keen to enjoy a different type of dining experience, make sure you book a table at Aiô, where the menu is based around Taiwanese cooking with an international touch that will take you on a journey to some surprising flavours. Located in the same street as its sister restaurant Mapu, Aiô features a distinctive glass façade, behind which you’ll find a bar by the entrance offering an array of delightful and inventive cocktails. The menu is uncomplicated and does not differentiate between starters and mains, enabling guests to share and order individual tasting menus. Standout options include the pork char siu, consisting of mini pancakes served as tacos, accompanied by a delicious dish of meat, red rice and honey, and featuring an explosion of mouthwatering and stunning flavours.

Name: Chez Claude
Address: Rua Conde de Bernadotte 26, Rio de Janeiro, 22430-200, Brazil
Description: Run by the famous French chef Claude Troisgros, this dining space has plenty of detail to pique your interest. Firstly, the completely open kitchen in the centre of the room, enabling diners to watch dishes being prepared at close quarters, which are based around French cuisine with the addition of some Brazilian elements. And secondly, the fact that food is served in bowls for sharing, to add to the sense of home-style cooking. The staff here recommend four dishes for two people including delicacies such as the fillet steak au poivre with a sauce that will make your mouth water, accompanied by cassava puff pastry and broccoli with Grana Padano cheese. To finish your meal, don’t miss the impressively textured melted chocolate Carola cake.

Name: Bottega Bernacca
Description: A small restaurant with a bistro-style ambience where the cuisine and decor are as meticulous as each other, the latter featuring a plethora of wood, impressive wine display cabinets and unusual details such as chairs hanging from the ceiling, a detail that is also found in its sister restaurants. The cooking here is authentic and delicious, and includes pasta cooked al dente in traditional Italian style and served straight from the pan to the table as if you were eating at home. Musts on the menu include the legendary Cipriani carpaccio, prepared with wafer-thin strips of filet mignon, served with a special house sauce and crunchy toast; and the pesto lasagne that is suitable for sharing. For dessert, the classic tiramisù, made with mascarpone, is balanced by the flavour of bitter chocolate.

Name: Maza
Address: Rua Manuel Guedes, 243, São Paulo, 04536-070, Brazil
