The wine list is extremely well curated and the vast majority of the wines are available by the glass.

Name: MatCha
Description: Everything is fresh and made from scratch: the veg comes from small, local growers and the meat and poultry is free range. An enticing menu tailored to modern appetites. Smiling service.

Name: Pilgrim
Description: Hideki Nishi (owner of Neige d'Été in Paris) has entrusted Yurika Kitano with the cuisine of this restaurant near Montparnasse. In a central and slightly raised kitchen, the chef crafts her elegant, delicate dishes, like tiny masterpieces influenced by France and Japan. This paradise for our tastebuds looks all set to become a place of pilgrimage for foodies.

Name: Le Landemer
Description: This fine stone house with a shale roof has an undeniable charm. Inside, a pleasant young Dutch chef cooks up modern cuisine with a dose of creativity, out of which he devises several courses according to his whims. The ingredients are exclusively from Normandy – not least fish, vegetables, wild herbs and flowers. The dishes are precise and on point, as are the food and drink pairings (the drinks, too, are local). The restaurant has a breathtaking view of the sea and coastline, as do the delightful guestrooms – it would be a shame not to book an overnight stay!

Name: Le Terroir des Vignobles
Address: CC Le Valaisan 2, Montvalezan, La Rosière, 73700, France
Description: Terroir and vineyard: the name says it all, summing up this young couple's passion for good food, good ingredients (local, but not exclusively – you'll see tuna and sea bream on the menu) and fine wines; the wine list features an organic selection from Savoie and elsewhere. Whether after or before skiing, mountain biking or hiking, the chef's recipes will whet your appetite: saddle of rabbit, red cabbage compote; cod loin, parsnip purée and mixed vegetables; vanilla sablé, blueberry cream and sorbet, pistachio cream. This pleasant rustic-style mountain bistro is perched on the top floor of a building in the resort.

Name: Auberge aux 4 Saisons
Description: Beyond the threshold of this large regional-style 1920s building with oriel and stained-glass windows is a lovely, inviting restaurant. Venison pâté en croûte; roasted pike-perch fillet, Brussels sprouts and chestnuts; clementine jelly, melt-in-the-mouth sponge and chestnut ice cream: the young chef delights diners with his seasonal ingredients from start to finish. A short wine list with a focus on organic and biodynamic wines; possibility of gin and tonic pairings (with local gins of course!).

Name: La Fine Bouche
Description: The chef's interest in regional traditions and his creative spirit are reflected in his use of the capuchin, an ancient utensil with a cast iron cone attached to a long rod, in which pieces of bacon are melted and used to flambée his scallops, lending them a slight grilled and smoked taste. With its hardwood floors, mouldings and exposed stonework, the tastefully refurbished dining room makes for an intimate dinner setting.

Name: Sushi Shunei
Description: Located on Montmartre’s hill, this joint sports an elegant, minimalist interior that celebrates the aesthetic codes of Japanese restaurants: light wooden furnishings, a long counter and an amazing origami-inspired ceiling by an interior design firm. Chizuko Kimura and the Sushi master Takeshi Morooka pursue the legacy of Shunei Kimura, who made this eatery such a success. The omakase menu comes in two versions, which must be chosen when you book. Both embark the diner on a genuine sensorial experience courtesy of razor-sharp nigiris, a truly exceptional selection of fish, expert handiwork and a range of subtle seasonings, without forgetting Japan’s unique vision of hospitality that is both unobtrusive and highly attentive.

Name: Les Têtes d'Ail
Address: 6 rue de la Fonderie, Toulouse, 31000, France
Description: This is the place for wholesome bistronomic fare from southwest France! Market-fresh, flavoursome dishes that keep pace with the seasons, well-selected local produce, excellent value for money (particularly at lunchtime), all of which in a busy shopping high street near Place des Carmes. Invariably packed, which is always a good sign!

Name: Kaito
Address: Four Seasons Megève, 373 chemin des Follières, Megève, 74120, France
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Counter dining,Garden or park,Great view,Terrace,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: At the Four Seasons Hotel, flawlessly fresh sashimi, tataki and sushi rub shoulders with delicately crafted alpine specialties. Fusion cuisine to be enjoyed on the terrace commanding a splendid view of the slopes or in the softly lit interior.

Name: Le Lion et l’Agneau
Description: A lion and a lamb adorn the coat of arms of Auch, which is the birthplace of chef Thierry Lebé. His bistronomic score is founded on top-drawer produce: Janzé chicken, cuttlefish, Pénestin mussels… The lunchtime menu is a steal.

Name: Lume
Description: A 14-seater restaurant with an intimate atmosphere that is due in part to the candlelight (lume in Italian). Venetian chef Riccardo Suppa regales guests with an appetising single set menu that gives pride of place to seafood and organic vegetables. Everything is made in-house, from the pasta to the bread prepared using heirloom wheat flour. Alice, the chef's partner, is an accomplished hostess who knows her way around a wine list featuring carefully selected Italian labels. On the menu: cicchetti (Venetian canapés), scallop crudo, paccheri with chanterelles, vanilla panna cotta etc.

Name: Le 1825 - La Table
Address: Domaine de la Brûlaire - 404 La Brûlaire - Gesté, Gesté, 49600, France
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Wheelchair access
Description: Hidden deep in the countryside, this small 19C château is home to an elegant restaurant and a number of guestrooms. Housed in the converted orangery, the vast space boasts high ceilings, exposed stonework, trendy furnishings and picture windows overlooking the courtyard. The chef's refreshing creativity makes itself felt in dishes that contain aromatic herbs from the garden – for instance, the pollack with shiso leaves and a sauce evoking the flavours of Thailand.

Name: Halle aux Grains
Address: Bourse de Commerce, 2 rue de Viarmes, Paris, 75001, France
Description: Not only is the old corn exchange home to part of the Pinault Collection, it also houses a highly creative restaurant. In homage to the history of the building, Michel and Sébastien Bras take seeds, cereals and legumes as their starting point and cook up healthy and contemporary cuisine. Be sure to sample a tasty dessert, such as their take on the Paris-Brest: choux pastry meets pumpkin seed cream in a crunchy praline affair. Unbeatable view of the rooftops of Paris.

Name: La Table du Marquis au Château de Maubreuil
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Brunch,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: The illustrious history and pageantry of this romantic castle dating from the 19C can be felt both in the grounds, dotted with works of art, and in the plush, stylish interior (huge mirrors, carved fireplaces, parquet floors and Napoleon III-style furnishings). All that remains is to enjoy the well-crafted food, fully in tune with today’s tastes and palates.

Name: Kaiseki
Address: Château de la Gaude, 3959 route des Pinchinats, Aix-en-Provence, 13100, France
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Wheelchair access
Description: In the magical setting of an 18C bastide, the Kaiseki upholds Japanese gourmet dining traditions with its “Omakase – The Great Journey” tasting menu that gives the chefs carte blanche. Chefs Matthieu Dupuis Baumal and Kazunari Noda have pooled their skill and talent to create a genuine culinary voyage poised between France and Japan. The next-door brasserie, Le K, offers a varied, more affordable score.

Name: La Canourgue
Address: Place de la Canourgue, Montpellier, 34000, France
Description: Established in the lavish inner courtyard of Hotel Richer de Belleval under a glass roof, this bistro of the Pourcel brothers is the quintessence of stylish: cornices, mouldings, crystal chandeliers… The food is equally first rate: beautifully crafted, rich in flavour and just the right dose of creativity. A genuine pleasure.

Name: Auberge du Rohan
Description: This traditional old Brittany farmhouse is located by the entrance to the Gulf of Morbihan Nature Park. Here, a self-taught chef welcomes his loyal patrons with traditional, carefully executed, hearty food: tuna gravlax, cairn and caper seasoning, nasturtium oil and caper croutons; chicken supreme stuffed with spring vegetables, smoked at the last minute, and a punchy rosemary gravy. Lunchtime bistro menu on weekdays.

Name: L'Azimut
Address: 1 rue du Men-Du, La Trinité-sur-Mer, 56470, France
Description: A resolutely maritime ambience pervades this cosy restaurant, an institution in La Trinité-sur-Mer since 1965. On the menu: seafood and fish as well as meat cooked in the open fire… The dishes are packed with textures and flavours: pollack gravlax served ceviche-style, citrus cream, parsley oil, Calamansi vinegar pearls and lace tuile. Fine selection of wines; large terrace with a view of the harbour. A delightful dining option!

Name: Roscanvec
Description: This restaurant is set in the historical surroundings of a 17C mansion built by the Lord of Roscanvec, royal council. The pared-back dining area is furnished in a contemporary style. The chef cooks up dishes that cater to modern tastes, while the two Kaczorowski sisters provide professional, smiling and attentive service. Pleasant guestrooms are available, should you wish to prolong the experience.

Name: Biscotte
Description: Pauline and Maximilien, two alumni of the most prestigious establishments (Le Bristol, Lasserre, Arpège), have set up their own place near Porte de Versailles. Convivial bistro interior, large atelier windows separating the kitchen, tasty and studied dishes: all the ingredients are in place for an enjoyable experience.

Name: Le Boeuf Noisette
Description: Take a seat in this vintage - style bistro, dotted with benches, marble tables and mirrors to sample a brief, well - designed menu focused on regional produce (particularly “Rouge des prés” beef). Ideally located behind the theatre, parallel with the Loir embankment and close to a large carpark. First - class, short food supply chain produce.

Name: Source
Description: Fillet of beef with tiger’s tears sauce, pak-choi cabbage; calf’s sweetbread seared in savory (the chef’s signature recipe) are some of the dishes of this bistro that focuses on hearty, simple fare. Two veterans from Annecy, keen to pay tribute to local ingredients, are behind this culinary treasure trove in the heart of the resort.

Name: Château du Bost
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: A few minutes from Vichy, in peaceful grounds, this château with towers and a water-filled moat (15C-19C) offers a contemporary and cosy decor, complemented by a beautiful terrace and some comfortable guestrooms. The restaurant has a refined setting and serves tasty seasonal cuisine.

Name: Pickles
Description: This bright, industrial-style restaurant run by British chef Dominic Quirke is all about indulgence and bold flavours. He likes to come out of his kitchen and chat with diners (in English!) as the pop/rock soundtrack plays. Based in Nantes for the last 10 years, his delicious modern cuisine is inspired by his travels in Asia and his excursions into the surrounding countryside to visit organic market gardeners. His dishes include tourte de volaille au vin jaune (puff pastry chicken pie); Vendée pork with beetroot, kale and chard; and cauliflower, seaweed and kasha coulibiac with shiitake mushrooms. There's no shortage of vegetarian options either.

Name: La Ferme Auberge - Domaine de La Font des Pères
Address: 1306 chemin de Pontillaou, Le Beausset, 83330, France
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: In the heart of Provence’s hilly terraces, the terrace of this Farm Inn commands a staggering view over the valley and the Sainte-Baume range. Produce from the estate takes pride of place on the menu (the chickens have the run of the pinewood, orchard, olive grove, herb and vegetable garden), which is healthily and creatively crafted by the chef and paired with estate wines. Pretty rooms and cottages also available.

Name: Hostellerie du Château des Monthairons
Address: 26 route de Verdun, Les Monthairons, 55320, France
Description: A thick slab of pan-fried duck foie gras with Granny Smith apple chutney; fillet of beef, new potatoes; game in season: this family-run château restaurant serves heart-warming food that adds the occasional contemporary spin to a patriotic line-up of French recipes. The historic château, set in the Meuse Valley and originally a Benedictine monastery, is magnificent with mouldings, old parquet floors, and plush drapes.

Name: Maison Chabran - Le 45ème
Description: As you motor south down the iconic N7 highway, why not stop off in this verdant spot that boasts a shaded terrace overlooking the garden, which is blissful in fine weather? This bistronomic eatery is a pleasant alternative to the parent establishment, a renowned temple of regional gastronomy. In its younger sibling, you will sample light, unstuffy dishes presented in a series of set menus. A few guestrooms are available should you wish to relax for longer.

Name: Côté Sud
Description: You are bound to enjoy your visit to this stone house with a garden and pleasant terrace. The chef whips up intelligent recipes packed with regional tributes. Examples include a 64°C poached egg, mushrooms and foie gras, or a breast of guinea fowl marinated in garden thyme and garnished with sweet potatoes and an olive oil sauce. The wine list focuses on organic and biodynamic wines. Charming service.

Name: La Tête au Loup
Address: Lieu-dit la Tête-au-Loup, Le Pin-au-Haras, 61310, France
Description: Stéphane and Agnès Mabille greet guests warmly in their spruce, traditional inn, appointed in a rustic vein. The seasoned chef concocts homemade terrines and assorted Normandy delicacies. In fine weather, make a beeline for the garden and terrace, which overlook the horses grazing in the next-door world-famous Haras du Pin stud farm. Unstarched, friendly vibe.

Name: La Bodega
Description: Diners come here for the atmosphere and tastes of Spain, especially Asturias, where the family who own the place hail from. On the menu, you'll find top-notch ingredients, succulent Iberian recipes – Iberian pork pluma, paella bodega (chicken, chorizo, cuttlefish, mussels and prawns), salt cod with aïoli, delicious turrón for dessert – as well as some daily specials. You won't be disappointed!

Name: Domitia - Maison de Cuisinier
Description: Slices of Mediterranean dentex served raw, caraway, cauliflower and elderberry vinegar; Camargue bull, oyster tartare from the Étang de Thau and salicornia-pistachio pesto: there's no doubt that chef Jérôme Faure has a masterful understanding of gourmet cuisine. His subtly innovative take on fine dining is based on a rigorous selection of local ingredients. The same goes for the wines.

Name: Tandem Saveurs Nomades
Description: The title says it all – a duo of chefs who trained under Thierry Marx and innovative fusion cuisine in which South American and Asian influences rub shoulders with pedigree French ingredients. The aubergines are underscored by miso sauce; pollock is flanked by creamy green peas, risotto of quinoa and Thai herbs sprinkled with grilled buckwheat for a roasted flavour; beef dumpling and a teriyaki sauce: everything is intelligently and patiently combined and assembled by our gourmet duo. This warm, colourful bistro, fully in tune with its era, is good news for the town centre of Saint-Maurice!

Name: La Table de Villeneuve
Address: 28 rue du Pré-Étienne, Les Sables-d'Olonne, 85180, France
Description: In a residential area blissfully free of the seaside town’s throngs of tourists, this enjoyable eatery has a well-designed menu whose dishes star carefully selected ingredients: haddock and beetroot carpaccio; black pudding and Savora-flavoured hollandaise sauce; ballotine of free-range poultry, fried polenta and tomato caviar…

Name: Le Soufflot
Description: Jérémy Pèze rustles up delicate, appetising, gourmet fare in a former winegrower’s house, which, unsurprisingly, also boasts a stunning wine list.

Name: Cécile
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: In the lively, bustling Carmes neighbourhood, a close-knit young team welcomes you to this modern bistro with a wood-decked veranda, large open kitchen and contemporary decor. The short menu is inspired by a real mix of cultures: exotic touches are incorporated into dishes such as Thai duck tartare and farm-reared pork loin with mango and pomegranate.

Name: La Mère Hamard
Description: This stone-built inn, which opened in 1903, is a genuine institution. The delightful dining room is flanked by a welcoming terrace shaded by wisteria, ideal to sample delicate, generous dishes, tinged with the occasional exotic influence. Attentive welcome and a few guestrooms for overnight stays.

Name: La Terrasse
Description: Do not worry, the Beast of Gévaudan is no more! However, if you are as hungry as the wolf, this place is for you. The chef, Cyril Tardy, cooks a contemporary interpretation of cuisine du terroir using good, very fresh, locally sourced ingredients.

Name: Maison Chabran - La Grande Table
Description: By the side of the legendary N7 holiday road of France, this family business has come a long way after its debut as a small bistro in the 1930s to what is now a culinary landmark. It continues to champion its own distinctive brand of tradition and modernity.

Name: Auberge de Clochemerle
Description: You will feel right at home in the understated Auberge de Clochemerle in the heart of a picturesque winegrowing village. The "surprise menu" (only the ingredients are listed) stars seasonal ingredients. The cooking is spot on and tasty, apparently classical at first glance, but often scattered with unorthodox notes (spicy Japanese seasoning), Maury-chocolate sauce, etc.). Rather than restrict itself to a single region, the menu pays tribute to French cuisine in all its glory and diversity, illustrated by a Brittany starter of scallops and Guémené andouille sausage. A long-standing favourite with the locals, the establishment is equally popular with passing tourists and visitors. A few comfortable guestrooms available for overnight stays.

Name: Le Mermoz
FacilitiesAndServices: Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus
Description: It is easy to see why this convivial neo-bistro located close to the Champs Elysées is always busy! Diners are won over by bistronomy-style cuisine that strikes a balance between tradition and modernity: impeccable produce, punchy, indulgent dishes and distinctive flavours. The reasonably priced wine list features an interesting selection of organic and natural wines.

Name: La Côte Vermeille
Description: This local institution boasts a breathtaking view of the port, especially from the stunning, first-floor terrace. The chef crafts light, colourful seafood cuisine with Mediterranean influences, cleverly underscored by spices and citrus fruits in a bid to showcase the catch of local fishing boats.

Name: Le Gentiane
Description: Gentian root is lauded for various properties, one of which stimulates the appetite – true to its name, this place does just that! Nicolas Bachon and his father work in tandem in the kitchen, cooking up traditional dishes with a modern twist (such as the sautéed beef mignon). Service with a smile from their respective wives. During the week, the lunch menu is a real bargain!

Name: La Table de mon Père - Castel Beau Site
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Great view,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Wheelchair access
Description: Comfortably ensconced in this sleek, elegant interior, soak up the glow of the magnificent sunsets over Plage St Guirec. As you feast your eyes on the view, tuck into carefully presented, contemporary cuisine featuring ingredients of indisputably high quality, such as pigeon from Le Ménez Bré, monkfish, spider crab and white asparagus.

Name: Plume
Description: Born in Tunis, the chef brings a touch of diversity and plenty of talent to this small street near Le Bon Marché. Diners squeeze into this tiny bistro to tuck in to seamless cuisine that is perfectly in tune with the seasons, such as a silky cream of celeriac soup with an intense and slightly spicy taste! Reasonably priced lunch menu and ambitious tasting menu in the evening.

Name: Le Cheval d'Or
Address: 21 rue de la Villette, Paris, 75019, France
Description: In the sleepy Jourdain neighbourhood in Upper Belleville, a brand-new team has taken over the reins of this golden horse, without changing the scenery (oriental red façade, polished concrete, whitewashed walls and open-plan kitchen). The eclectic Asian-inspired menu is jazzed up with nods to Gallic traditions, or is it the other way round? Examples: tofu and caviar consommé à la royale, barbajuan raviolis in sweet pepper sauce, tofu and shitake tortellini, stuffed duck à l’orange, vegetable cassoulet (100% vegetarian).

Name: Omija
Description: At the helm of his own restaurant since 2019 and with a splendid starred experience under his belt, Romain Bonnet crafts a creative surprise menu of Asian inspiration: the ‘omija’ is a Korean berry known to feature the five ‘flavours’ in perfect harmony. Romain is unswerving in his dedication to taste: radish and seaweed gnocchi brilliantly play on acidic notes as shrimp adds a well-judged spicy edge. Flawlessly cooked, gutsy stocks and irresistible big-boned sauces. The produce, mostly organic, is painstakingly sourced (common shrimp from la Cotinière, Oléron Island, line-caught pollack, Vendée squab). An infectiously cosy eatery with unstarched, yet seamless service.

Name: Petrossian
Address: 13 boulevard de la Tour-Maubourg, Paris, 75007, France
Description: A legendary name in the hearts of caviar lovers since 1920, when the Petrossian brothers, of Armenian origin, began importing it. The restaurant honours the history of the house with "classic" caviar tasting, but also with well - thought - out dishes in which this delicacy appears in other forms (pressed, dried, matured, liquid).

Name: Le Bistrot du Paradou
Address: 57 avenue de la Vallée-des-Baux, Paradou, 13520, France
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: This inviting restaurant with blue shutters is a genuine local landmark. Telephone (only) bookings compulsory. The dish of the day changes daily, but comes back every week – e.g. cassoulet on Wednesdays, in the single set menu. On top of that, Provence's culinary repertory is celebrated with generous wholesome dishes, of the likes of aioli, spit-roast Bresse chicken and calf's head with ravigote sauce, to be devoured in a lively and laid-back vibe cultivated by the bubbly, unstarched front-of-house team. Wine and a generous cheeseboard are included in the price of the single set menu.

Name: Rhizome
Description: The rhizome is an underground shoot full of energy resources that is the equivalent to a root for some plants. A name that cleverly references the return of this young Soissons couple to their Picardy roots, after stints in top establishments (Mère Brazier, Parisian Saturne, Auberge du Vert Mont). The name also depicts their lively and instinctive, market-fresh cuisine and regularly changing menu, together with the couple’s clear preference for local produce and organic and natural wines. A firm fixture on the local culinary scene and not only because of its (single) lunch set menu. We recommend booking.

Name: L'Intimiste - Auberge de Buellas
Description: In the heart of Buellas village, take a seat in the snug, plush dining room to sample polished, thoughtfully curated dishes presented in a single set menu that shines the spotlight on a seasonal ingredient: lobster, Bresse poultry, celery, etc. The Auberge Bressane de Buellas is more traditional in style.

Name: La Petite Ferme
Description: This chic contemporary brasserie run by Ronan Kernen, the chef-owner of Côté Cour, showcases dishes from all over the world as well as serving a wide choice of meat cooked over embers, spit-roasted or in a wood-fired oven.

Name: L'ArtYsan
Address: 35 plan de la Gare, Quissac, 30260, France
Description: Yohann Boucard has turned the old station of Quissac into a fine establishment, sporting minimalist lines and iron work by local artisans… The food is equally enthralling, thanks to painstakingly selected ingredients and unusual, flavoursome combinations. Professional service.

Name: Vista
Address: Lily of the Valley, colline Saint-Michel, quartier de Gigaro, La Croix-Valmer, 83420, France
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Great view,Terrace,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: The hotel, perched on an unspoilt hillside overlooking the sea, is divine, and the swish, yet funky restaurant is equally fantastic! Take a seat by the pool and bask in the exclusive vibe as you sample recipes by chef Vincent Maillard (shoulder of Sisteron lamb braised in savory or a chocolate and Piedmont hazelnut eclair). Valet parking.

Name: Le Garde Champêtre
Description: This former railway warehouse has been turned into a sustainable farm restaurant with greenhouses and an organic vegetable garden by a group of four partners judiciously teamed up with two local winegrowers. They serve fresh and fortifying cuisine, based on ingredients sourced locally or from the garden. A very pleasant locavore and ecological approach. A pleasant place.

Name: Les Chants d'Avril
Description: The enthusiasm of chef Christophe François is infectious. Every day brings his own appealing and confident bistronomy-style take on market-fresh cuisine. Fine ingredients from the region are showcased in surprise set menus (without options), served in a pleasant bistro setting. As for the wine, try some of the surprising picks in their selection, to be tasted blind. A sociable experience!

Name: Le Bouchon
Description: Appetising, up - to - the - minute food, reinvented daily, a prettily appointed interior (terracotta tile floors, old beams and mirrors) and the wonderful terrace, which is a haven of greenery in the town centre. It isn’t difficult to understand why this establishment is so popular with Nantes’ inhabitants!

Name: L'Art de Vivre
Address: Château de L'Hospitalet, route de Narbonne-Plage, Narbonne, 11100, France
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: At this vineyard nestled in the La Clape mountains, chef Laurent Chabert sources some of his ingredients (including aromatic herbs) from his own kitchen garden, and also uses fine local produce (organic for the most part). He creates colourful, fragrant dishes, such as grouper cooked over the embers of a barbecue, braised aubergine glazed with tomato juices… The food and wine pairings draw on a selection of bottles from the estate.

Name: Culina Hortus
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Wheelchair access
Description: This vegetarian restaurant offers beautifully crafted dishes that are unabashedly creative in a tasting set menu made with seasonal ingredients. The food is paired with a concise organic and biodynamic wine list, to enjoy in a snug, modern decor of wood, concrete, adobe.

Name: L'Essentiel
Description: Off the beaten tourist track, chef Morgan Ortéga goes straight to the essentials: industrial loft interior, open kitchen, huge bay window, glazed wine cellar and leather bench seats. His talent and skill metamorphose market-fresh produce, enabling each ingredient to shout its name, to the delight of diners.

Name: Le Parvis
Description: This picturesque house on the banks of the Charente in downtown Saintes is where Pascal Yenk rustles up mouth - watering regional dishes using ingredients fresh from the market. Everything is homemade, including the sauces, to the delight of diners’ taste buds. Sheltered terrace in fine weather.

Name: L'Auberge de la Poule d'Or
Description: Part and parcel of its flagship, Michel Trama’s iconic gourmet restaurant, this Golden Hen (Poule d’Or) is a smart inn sporting old stone walls, a long central wooden table, the legs of which are adorned with lion’s heads, chandeliers and still-lifes... Michel’s son is in charge of the impeccable service. The menu reads like a culinary textbook of bistro classics: ox tail pie, calf’s head in poulette sauce, giant cream puffs with a dribble of caramel. Spot-on, confident cooking, flavoursome ingredients and heart-warming dishes in an authentic setting. A foodies’ gold mine!

Name: LAZU
Description: The chef was second in command to Bruno Doucet for three years at La Régalade St-Honoré – so he knows the ropes! Here, he serves up well-crafted bistronomy fare with inspired associations of high-quality seasonal ingredients. The menu changes weekly, but specialities such as caramelised veal sweetbreads and pâté with a potato crust have been permanent fixtures since the restaurant opened. Inviting atmosphere.

Name: Chez Monsieur
Description: The Parisian bistro in all its splendour (zinc countertop, velvet-upholstered wall seats, patterned tiles), with the immutable – and delicious! – cuisine that goes with it: Burgundy snails with white butter sauce, veal blanquette served in a casserole dish, not to mention a wide selection of wines from all over France.

Name: Au Fil du Temps
Description: In a pedestrian area, just opposite the old church, which has been turned into a cultural centre, this former grocery store is now a charming little restaurant. Sustainable agriculture is favoured, with well - packed dishes: for example, the beef carpaccio, slipper lobster jus, marinated seaweed and oyster fritters.

Name: Mahé
Address: 581 avenue de la Pompignane, Montpellier, 34000, France
Description: Sabrina Delcros and Richard Juste, who previously ran the restaurant Idée Saveurs, are now at the helm of the inviting and spacious Mahé, which has a peaceful terrace sheltered from onlookers. The chef creates dishes that he describes as "straightforward and no nonsense", cooking and putting them together with notable precision, eg grilled leeks, soft-boiled egg, potato gnocchi, parmesan and truffle; monkfish tail, kohlrabi risotto-style, carrots in olive oil sauce vierge with fennel. Small selection of local wines.

Name: Les Inséparables
Address: 4 avenue de la Reine-Astrid, Aix-en-Provence, 13090, France
Description: Les Inséparables is the brainchild of Christophe Bonanno (the chef, whose CV includes Crillon, Astrance and Laurent) and Mathieu Jégo, a born manager with a passion for food. In a contemporary interior, they serve a limited menu: tomato, burrata and pata negra tarte fine; pollack, langoustine mousseline and broccoli; strawberry-pistachio dessert. On sunny days, plump for a table on the large terrace beneath the boughs of two old plane trees.

Name: Lauracée
Description: There is no doubt that the chef of this joint tucked away behind the old port only serves fresh produce, because, as he himself says “I don’t know how to cook anything else!” Take a seat in the fashionable interior and treat yourself to good food sprinkled with Mediterranean twists. A few examples: stuffed courgette flowers, ewe’s milk cheese, aubergines; Marseille-style melt-in-the-mouth lamb’s tongues; warm chocolate mousse, cocoa-flavoured crème brûlée, chou pastry stuffed in hazelnuts. Slick service and warm welcome.

Name: La Deuvalière
Address: 18 rue de la Monnaie, Tours, 37000, France
Description: Julien and Alexandra have poured every ounce of their enthusiasm into successfully wooing local and visiting gourmets. Their seasonal cuisine is a treasure trove of culinary gems. The charm of their old country house, appointed with bare beams, terracotta tiled floors and a fireplace, together with the odd contemporary detail, further adds to the experience!

Name: L'Arche de Meslay
Description: The surroundings are quickly forgotten (a business estate), as you concentrate on the fine and fresh food, truly bursting with flavours. One case in point is the speciality of the Breton chef: Tours - style bouillabaisse – packed with red mullet, scorpion fish, pork rillons and andouillette.

Name: La Réserve à la Plage
Description: The Pampelonne beach version of the Réserve Ramatuelle casts its magical seaside spell in a smart, casual interior signed by Philippe Starck. Normandy-born chef Nicolas Cantrel has bewitched the clientele with his Riviera-inspired cuisine, which features carefully sourced meat, the local catch of the day and an array of top-notch produce.

Name: Soulenq
Address: 469 rue de la Thériaque, Montpellier, 34090, France
Description: A restaurant and a wine cellar, fitted out in a former nursery by four young associates who show lots of promise. The dishes are simple and delicious, with some dazzling highlights (winter salad with Galician octopus, calamansi vinaigrette; cabbage stuffed with vegetables, rice, Thai curry emulsion), plus cuts of meat for sharing. The seasonal ingredients are sourced at the market: a real treat.

Name: Villa Morelia
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: Villa Morelia exudes a certain discreet charm. The setting offsets the refined, tasty and inventive market - based cuisine. You can really taste the freshness and savour the flavours.

Name: Petit Boutary
Description: Petit Boutary is certainly living up to the standard set for it by Boutary, its Left Bank counterpart. In this refined bistro, with its chequered floor, zinc-topped bar, leather-clad banquette seating and hanging light bulbs, modern, creative cuisine is served in the form of a single menu with several courses.

Name: Bistrot 1954
Description: Overlooking the grandiose scenery of Pointe Saint-Mathieu, this bistro makes your mouth water: a terrace in the fresh sea air, contemporary decor combining untreated wood and rattan furniture, and dishes from the chef, who lovingly showcases Brittany's fresh produce in his dishes: from shellfish and fish to buckwheat and seaweed.

Name: Le Quai de Champagne
Address: 1 bis quai des Comtes-de-Champagne, Troyes, 10000, France
Description: On the banks of the Cordé, this 19C mansion, tastefully refurbished in a modern vibe with two large dining rooms whose windows overlook the leafy, tree-lined garden, provides the perfect foil to chef Jean-Paul Braga’s spot-on, seasonal cuisine. Recipes which also feature the occasional nostalgic tribute (braised calf sweetbreads with morels, Rossini tournedos) or even a sprinkling of mouth-watering Portuguese delicacies from the chef’s homeland.

Name: Bo-tannique
Description: These attractive premises (with a contemporary interior and exposed Bordeaux stonework) are located on a charming cobbled pedestrian square. The fresh cuisine is full of contrasts and draws on influences from far and wide: grilled sardines with burnt miso and Lebanese-style tomato tabbouleh. The fine wine list features mostly organic and natural wines. Friendly service... A recipe for success!

Name: Licandro - Le Bistro
Address: 18 rue de la Couronne, Aix-en-Provence, 13100, France
Description: This small family business is run by chef Felipe Licandro, who honed his skills in some of France’s top establishments, and his wife Julie. The lunchtime chalkboard menu offers well-crafted, market-fresh fare; more extensive evening menu, but always in a traditional bistronomy spirit.

Name: Le Paris-Brest by Christian Le Squer
Description: Christian Le Squer has reinvented the railway station buffet concept whilst teasingly jazzing up traditional Breton fare. A trendy interior, a bistronomic menu and a wine list by Eric Beaumard: you’re in for a treat in Rennes.

Name: La Rissole
Description: The name of this bistro pays tribute to a great chef of the last century and celebrates the joys of cooking. The concise menu highlights the changing seasons and regional produce (asparagus, snails, freshwater fish). A flair for seasoning makes for simple and tasty food, such as white asparagus mimosa, broccoli and vadouvan. There are only a few tables, so be sure to book!

Name: L'Expression
Description: This city-centre establishment serves top-drawer ingredients, many of which are to share (whole fish from the market, rib of Galice beef, butterflied, plump fattened Bresse Miéral chicken), in two trendily appointed dining rooms (open kitchen, glazed wine cellar and high tables). The food is cooked in a wood-fired oven. Extroverted, friendly atmosphere. Beautifully curated wine list.

Name: Brasserie du Louvre - Bocuse
Description: Take a seat in the sleek, spacious dining hall framed by bay windows and marvel at the quintessential view over Paris: Comédie-Française, Conseil d’Etat, Louvre… The enticing menu cleverly navigates between iconic Lyons classics (hot pistachio sausage in a soft bread roll, pike quenelle and nantua sauce) and timeless brasserie staples (foie gras salad, sole meunière, etc. ). Splendid terrace beneath the arcades of this emblematic Haussmannian edifice.

Name: L'Hostellerie d'Acquigny
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: This small village inn with a lively contemporary vibe has been run by the same couple for many years. As keen as ever, chef Éric Georget rustles up generous and indulgent modern cuisine to make your mouth water, organising it into a set menu and an à la carte menu. Carefully selected produce goes into dishes that are packed with flavour: fillet of John Dory and poached oyster with seaweed butter and, for dessert, Calvados and apple hot soufflé. Pleasant guestrooms available.

Name: Ébullition
Description: In this lovely restaurant steeped in character in the heart of historic Montpellier, Boris Caillol (formerly Le Petit Nice and La Maison Troisgros) signs a bold creative modern score and the inventive, no-holds barred chef continues to set our tastebuds tingling! He scours Montpellier’s organic market himself, hunting out the best seasonal ingredients. The resulting subtle dishes are admirably paired with an enticing wine list that demonstrates a weakness for biodynamic wines from the region. The old stone walls are offset by soft lighting and contemporary fixtures, all of which is further enhanced by the graceful greeting of Coralie Semery, who elegantly supervises the front of house.

Name: Du Bruit en Cuisine
Description: A chef who trained in several Ducasse establishments is at work in this genuine gourmet bolthole. Mathieu Lévèque creates up-to-the-minute, deceptively spontaneous cuisine in the shape of small, tapas-inspired dishes. This veteran chef has a knack with jus, sauces and spot-on cooking, illustrated by his confit of ox cheeks garnished with mushroom and celeriac gnocchis. The venue sometimes hosts musical evenings, adding a festive dimension to the venue. As it goes from strength to strength, we are likely to hear more from this boisterous kitchen.

Name: Le Petit Comptoir
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus
Description: This gastronomic eatery with a 1930s character serves bistro cuisine with fine ingredients. If you fancy buying a bottle of one of the wines served here – there are 350 on the list, most of them local – pay a visit to the cellar!

Name: Nomade
Description: This restaurant, opened in the middle of the Médoc region by a local young couple, is a pleasant surprise. The chef serves up French cuisine with exotic touches, using local produce as much as possible: the results are tasty. Pleasant decor and a friendly welcome.

Name: Pinson
Description: This enticing city-centre establishment overflows with the infectious enthusiasm of its youthful owners, who, like its namesake chaffinch, adore travelling… After stints in London and Paris, the chef rustles up a melting-pot menu, while his partner brings her experience in the luxury trade to bear in the dining room. Gracious, warm welcome and vibe.

Name: La Table de l'Hôtel Sainte-Victoire
Description: Brazilian chef Mateus Marangoni concocts unusual menus rich in exotic notes, in tribute to his South American upbringing and time spent in Spain. The food is balanced and fresh; in fine weather, meals are served on the patio, opposite Sainte-Victoire and Vauvenargues Castle.

Name: Casa Fuego
Address: 80 bis boulevard de Garavan, Menton, 06500, France
Description: Just opposite Mauro Colgreco's flagship restaurant, this is the Italian-Argentine chef's hacienda-style Argentinian grill, which has a large covered terrace overlooking the sea, the town and the harbour. Here, they have mastered the style of cooking over a wood fire that is so typical of Argentina. Expect tasty dishes infused with a pleasing smokiness: aguachile San Remo white shrimps; grilled octopus; dulce de leche flan. A masterclass in gourmet conviviality.

Name: Le 26-28
Description: Contemporary design, open kitchens, a chef – Arthur Friess (with a fine Michelin-starred career) – and, managing the restaurant floor, Charlotte Le Gall: these are the ingredients that make this place a success. Lovely contemporary cuisine made from impeccable ingredients – such as pigeon, spelt au gratin and roots. Menu renewed every month.

Name: L'Arlatan
Description: The flamboyant, Instagram-worthy interior designed by Cuban artist Jorge Pardo makes an immediate impression. Your attention is then drawn to the seasonal, Mediterranean-inspired menu. Delicious, well-crafted dishes that make the most of local produce to conjure up bold and appealing flavours: think Camargue oysters, beef marinated à la provençale, Camargue red rice, pistachio millefeuille to share.

Name: Au Cheval Blanc
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: "The soul of a winstub... and all the flavours of the region lovingly presented: blue trout, venison steak with sauce grand veneur, kirsch mousse etc. The same spirit is mirrored in the decor: lots of wood panelling and two ""stuben"": rustic rooms that are typical of the region. Finally, a special mention for the absolutely exemplary service. "

Name: Les Bouteilles
Description: Next to the Marché de Talensac, an impressive wine bar/bistro: appealing wine - inspired decoration, excellent food based on quality products (Italian cold cuts, rough - and - readycanaille dishes, fresh fish) not forgetting – the clue is in the name – a memorable wine list (1,500 types), with a particular penchant for Burgundy.

Name: Jean-Michel Couron
Description: Over more than 30 years, this chef has built up a loyal clientele of happy diners courtesy of his contemporary cuisine featuring nods to the Mediterranean, in dishes such as bouillabaisse jus and carpaccio of large wild prawns. The yakitori sauce on the duck fillet is one of his more exotic marriages. You can choose to dine in either the contemporary space or the former 14C cloister.

Name: L'Adress...
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: A glazed parallelepiped extended by decking and framed by greenery: such is the modern, stylish setting! David Seguin’s inventive menu is devised around high-calibre produce. The cooking is flawless, the plating exquisite and the flavours ideally balanced, such as crab and avocado ravioles with buckwheat and a tangy shellfish stock. Splendid cheese platter.

Name: L'Instinct Gourmand
Description: Two young men, who met in Oxford, have teamed up in this ‘no label’ bistro, determined to forge a name for themselves without the usual traditional trappings. Simple, fresh food is their goal, illustrated by the enticing slate menu that changes daily depending on market produce. Trust your own instincts and book a table!

Name: Ô Dissay
Description: The Château de Dissay, a 15C stately home with an elegant and refined interior, serves modern, visually exciting cuisine, created by two young chefs, Henri Dupont and Stanislas Simonet. A trained pastry chef, Simonet has not lost his touch, as his work with blackberries in season amply illustrates. In autumn, the duo harness their talents to revealing the big-boned flavours of game. Pleasant terrace in the castle courtyard.

Name: Ververt
Description: In a former residential house, now converted into this restaurant, the charm of the local architecture blends perfectly with more contemporary elements. In the kitchen, Romain Butet crafts cuisine that embraces tradition and incorporates just the right dose of modernity: semi-cooked trout, courgette, sauce vierge with piment d'Espelette, fresh goat's cheese; meagre, lemon-ginger sauce, local vegetables. A good choice of wines at reasonable prices, and al fresco dining in the pleasant courtyard to the rear.

Name: Âma Terra
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Terrace,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: Diners are faced with a dilemma in the restaurant of this magnificent hotel. You can opt to dine in the inside space, with its Second Empire glass roof, crystal chandeliers and imposing china cabinet, or on the gorgeous terrace, with the gentle sound of water tinkling in the pools and fountains and the scent of typical Mediterranean fragrances hanging in the air. The Chef cooks up gourmet cuisine with Provençal overtones and a backdrop of original and striking associations.

Name: Yam
Description: You can rely on chef Chatchai Klanklong (chef/patron of L'Orchidée, 1 star at Altkirch) and his brother Kriankai to concoct flavoursome Thai cuisine, such as Tom Yam (prawn and coconut milk soup), or 30-day aged Iberico pork chop with cauliflower and spiced tamarind jus... Premium ingredients, distinctive, well-balanced flavours, precise culinary technique and careful presentation.

Name: La Golmotte
Description: Not far from Le Mont-Dore, authenticity is guaranteed in this inn, where the dining area was originally a cowshed! Fresh ingredients and copious portions of tasty traditional cuisine, such as tender pork cheeks, home-made potato purÉe and Saint-PourÇain white wine sauce… even if the chef allows himself a few incursions into more contemporary territory, with dishes such as salmon gravlax.

Name: Le Pré Fillet
Address: Route du Pré Fillet aux Molunes, Les Molunes, 39310, France
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus
Description: This former farmstead, turned into a restaurant three generations ago, stands in a landscape of meadows and woodland at an altitude of 1200 metres. Simplicity and generosity are the bywords of this establishment which shines the spotlight on the region’s knockout produce. The chef crafts wholesome, hearty fare: calf sweetbread flambéed in Jura marc and asparagus in flaky pastry or melt-in-the-mouth knuckle of lamb braised in assorted veggies. To be sampled and enjoyed in a dining area overlooking the unspoiled countryside. Diners are pampered by attentive staff.

Name: Auberge du Moulinel
Address: 116 chaussée de l'Avant-Pays, Le Moulinel, St-Josse, 62170, France
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus
Description: This peaceful inn between Le Touquet and Montreuil-sur-Mer sports a smart rural vibe. The chef painstakingly selects his ingredients to carefully craft flavoursome traditional fare. House specialties include lobster salad, pigeon cooked two ways and a decadent millefeuille smothered in a light frothy cream. Everything is prepared in house, including the bread and ice creams!

Name: Le Saint-Martin
Description: Olivier Prevot - Carme's flavoursome cuisine is all about the ingredients. He uses each one in a straightforward way but the apparent simplicity is misleading, as the recipes, cooking and seasoning bring out all of the flavour within. Nothing pretentious, nothing complicated, nothing but pleasure!

Name: Auberge du Cellier
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Typical of the region, this charming house is the setting for a chef – with roots in the district who has returned home – to create delicate fare. It is from locally sourced ingredients, authentic and bursting with flavour. A feast for the eyes and the taste buds! The accommodation is simple yet agreeable.

Name: Le Carré d'Ange
Description: This updated, airy Provençal inn outside town provides the perfect foil for generous, throbbingly good Mediterranean food. Examples include a mouthwatering breast of guinea fowl and truffles with girolles and a millefeuille of potatoes. Served on a pretty patio in fine weather.

Name: Yushin
Description: Between Île de la Jatte and the American Hospital of Neuilly, this traditional Japanese restaurant offers a variety of menus: sushis, bento, omakase and a tasting menu. The fish is of the freshest quality and meticulously prepared as one would expect. The traditional Japanese desserts are exquisitely presented. The interior is unsurprisingly pared down with light wooden fixtures and white walls and the 100% Japanese staff is dutifully attentive. The tea service is carried out with full ceremony and each diner is walked out to the street and thanked on leaving.

Name: L'Altiplano
Address: Le K2 Chogori, 143 avenue du Prariond, Val-d'Isère, 73150, France
Description: We may be in the Alps, but this place fêtes an entirely different mountain range – the Andes! The culinary offering here is inspired by Peruvian history and cuisine: think barbecued specialities, condiments, dishes for sharing etc. Be transported to Peru, without even leaving this chic, intimate and friendly setting.

Name: Au Cœur d'Artichaut
Description: This contemporary restaurant, run by an enthusiastic young couple from the village, is depicted by dishes that keep pace with current tastes, while remaining true to the ingredients and seasons. The lovely dining room is in a conservatory. Attentive service.

Name: La Pinède
Address: Chemin du Langoustier, Ile de Porquerolles, 83400, France
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Garden or park,Great view,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Patrons of this out-of-the-way hotel are collected from the village in a shuttle bus; the laidback restaurant of Le Mas du Langoustier is only open at lunchtime. The menu showcases the Mediterranean and Provençal dishes: pistou soup, "panier du pêcheur façon bourride", grilled fish and crayfish etc – to savour against a backdrop of Mediterranean plants and the sea: simply sit back, tuck in and enjoy the moment.

Name: Le 7 Restaurant Panoramique
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Great view,Interesting wine list,Wheelchair access
Description: As the name implies, this restaurant is located on the seventh floor of the Cité du Vin, commanding a matchless view over the Garonne River and historic Bordeaux. The food is pleasantly up - to - date and well - prepared, accompanied by a fine choice of wines by the glass.

Name: La Cantinetta
Description: Since childhood, Pierre-Antoine Denis has been passionate about Italian food and regularly pops over the border to scour the country for premium produce. Chalked up on a slate, the menu spans antipasti, fresh house-made pasta and the chef’s signature dish: scaloppine di vitello. Tightly-packed tables, a buzzy vibe and a patio to the rear set the scene.

Name: Jean des Sables
Address: 121 boulevard de la Dune, à Soorts, Hossegor, 40150, France
Description: This beach front restaurant sports a fashionably stark interior: polished concrete, a light colour scheme, a live lobster tank and an ocean view… The modern cuisine is presented in a brief, well-crafted menu. Special lobster menu. Attentive welcome and service.

Name: L'Étier
Description: Between the road and the étier (a seawater channel) onto which the conservatory backs, this characteristic island house showcases splendid local seafood: grilled lobster, wild turbot cooked on the bone, sole meunière, marsh eels in garden herbs, without forgetting the desserts, soufflé au Grand Marnier or Paris-Brest pastry – to die for! The food of a genuine craftsman – fresh and oozing with flavour.

Name: Le Gentil
Description: This restaurant on the rue Surcouf, a street strewn with eateries, is the work of a Japanese pair, chef Fumitoshi Kumagai in the kitchen and his wife front of house. They propose contemporary French cuisine with the occasional Asian influence, such as pig's trotters stuffed with pak choi and beef faux-filet with a Japanese sauce.

Name: Avarum
Description: This restaurant is housed in a converted 19C coaching inn opposite the medieval castle. A tight-knit chef and sommelier duo are at the helm, pooling their gourmet skills. The chef carefully prepares local ingredients and freshly caught fish to create mouth-watering dishes, such as Roi Rose de Touraine pork, perfectly confit, packed with sweet and savoury flavours and served with delicious pak choi steamed then flash-seared over a flame. As you will see, there's a lot of work involved; apart from the wonderful bread from the local baker, everything from the amuse-bouche to the dessert is beautifully crafted and made in-house. A lovely dining experience, not to mention friendly service and savvy wine recommendations from the sommelier.

Name: Lacaille
Description: This neighbourhood bistro offers no-fuss market cuisine that keeps pace with the seasons. Service with a smile.

Name: La Côte Bleue
Description: The Étang de Thau, a major shellfish farming site and lake in Languedoc, famous for its mussels and the legendary oysters of Bouzigues, is also well-known for its biodiversity on land, in the sea and in the airs. So, taking a seat on the terrace overlooking the lagoon is an opportunity not to be missed. Expect to tuck into delicious, ultra-fresh seafood, including oysters, mini squid in garlic and parsley or mussels broiled in garlic butter.

Name: Le 80
Description: Adorned in colourful hot-air balloons, Le 80 presents a patriotic culinary line-up of French traditions in well-crafted dishes: Richelieu pâté en croûte (porkpie), free-range pork chop smoked in hay or rose-scented praline meringues in a vanilla custard cream. More festive in the evenings. Follow in the footsteps of Jules Verne!

Name: La Table de la Réserve
Description: Supervised by chef Julien Roucheteau, this restaurant is a welcome gourmet addition to the dining options at this superb establishment. The contemporary Mediterranean-inspired menu takes inspiration from the local terroir – note the textures of pissaladière with house-marinated anchovy and a sweet onion espuma, or the tartlet showcasing figs from the Var, with its melting brambleberry centre. You might also like to sample their bouillabaisse (Fri and Sat), traditional octopus dishes from the South of France, or rockfish soup. Diners take their seats in a bistro-style setting that is suitably cordial and laid back.

Name: Le Grand Chaume
Description: Architects Patrick Bouchain and Loïc Julienne designed this unique venue with a traditional thatched roof and an exposed timber frame that calls to mind a star-studded night sky. The pared-back, minimalist interior seems to be open to the elements, courtesy of floor-to-ceiling windows, some of which command a view of the small terrace and its water feature. The entire project is truly jaw dropping! The seasonal menu stars produce from the Val de Loire region.

Name: La Table d'Edgar
Description: Chef Sébastien David, who has an impressive career to his name, conjures up appealing cuisine using top-notch ingredients: quality poultry from the Ferme de la Paumerais, brightly coloured farmhouse butter, fresh fish from Guilvinec, and plump, fleshy oysters from Paimpol. The balanced flavours in both the savoury dishes and the desserts come down to meticulous craftsmanship and expert cooking: chicken supreme with lardo di Colonnata, the leg roasted in a lovage broth; pear with white chocolate and pistachio fondant. A bright and harmoniously decorated interior with tables laid out around a lovely glass-roofed seating area.

Name: Madame FAN
Description: This restaurant celebrates the delights of Chinese cuisine courtesy of a short menu devised by Chinese-born executive chef. He produces masterful dishes using quality ingredients – raw bluefin tuna, marinated cucumber; Padrón peppers, beef and chicken stuffing; Kung Pao prawns with cashew nuts; chocolate bao, black sesame ice cream... to savour in a contemporary-style interior with a glass-paned roof.

Name: 83 Restaurant
Description: A ten - minute walk from the Centre Pompidou - Metz, this pleasant restaurant showcases Italian food, through carefully selected ingredients (charcuterie, burrata, pasta, wild fish, purebred meats). And to accompany it all, a fine selection of Italin wines!

Name: Le Bénaton
Description: In the heart of Burgundy, Beaune is known the world over for its annual charity wine auction held in the iconic Hospices edifice, famous for its glazed tile roof. A steadfast champion of fine French food and wine, Japanese chef Keishi Sugimura, couldn’t have found a town that suits him better. Trained in Japan, the chef excels in the art of the porkpie, which earned him the title of vice world champion in 2013. Flavoursome seasonal dishes sprinkled with creative touches.

Name: Le Sirocco
Address: 8 bis rue des Gobelins, Paris, 75013, France
Description: The warm air of the Sirocco has reached Les Gobelins, bringing its fragrances of tajines, couscous and hariras into the old stables of the Château de la Reine Blanche, where this Moroccan restaurant with typical decor is located. The owner himself imports the argan oil that flavours his traditional dishes. Of course the couscous itself is home-made, and very fine, just as it should be.

Name: Bistro de l'Hôtel
Description: The elegant, chic bistro - style interior is the setting for cuisine that honours tradition and first - rate ingredients. The house speciality is roasted Bresse chicken. As for the wine list, it is quite simply impressive.

Name: Le Petit Restaurant
Description: In the heart of historic Ajaccio, this restaurant may be small by name, but it thinks big! Seasoned chef Vincent Boucher crafts a repertory that extends far beyond the Mediterranean with the overriding goal of creating modern dishes with a dash of creativity and the odd exotic tribute. On the menu you may find a 65° boiled egg, gently sautéed onions and local charcuterie; low temperature poultry breast, seasonal veggies, velvety mash and a gutsy gravy; fleur de sel crumble, sorbet flavoured with verbena from the garden, foamy mascarpone and a light dusting of fig leaves and Corsican strawberries. Kristel Paries bends over backwards to pamper guests in the dining room, making sure they enjoy every moment of their meal.

Name: Piero TT
Description: Welcome to Pierre Gagnaire's Italian restaurant, where the great chef proposes his personal and creative take on cucina italiana, beautifully made with rigorously selected produce. The dishes are punctuated with subtle contrasts created, for example, by bitter salad leaves, spices and condiments. You can look forward to a chic and opulent but nonetheless relaxed atmosphere, a warm welcome and expert recommendations on the best Italian wines from the sommelier. Booking strongly advised.

Name: Wistub Brenner
Description: In this authentic winstub in the heart of Little Venice, the cuisine is – of course – regional: salad with Comté cheese and cervelas, "Papi Lucien's onion tart", sauerkraut and braised pork knuckle, Pinot Noir sauce. Local produce, a friendly atmosphere and a pleasant terrace.

Name: Genty Magre
Description: In the street of the same name, this bistro adds a joyful, even delicate spin to French country cooking, with special mention for the house speciality: cassoulet with duck confit and sausages, served on ceramic plates. Flawless preparations and high-flying seasoning; good value for money.

Name: La Ruche
Description: In the wine country where Marsanne and Roussanne grapes are grown (the two varieties used to make white Saint-Péray), a modern bistro done right! On the menu: tasty, carefully prepared neo-bistro cuisine in tune with the seasons, and an excellent list of wines from the northern Côtes du Rhône region. Reservation required.

Name: Tabi - Ippei Uemura
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining,Notable sake list,Wheelchair access
Description: Tabi, which means journey in Japanese, says it all! Born in Kyoto, the chef has adopted the city of Marseilles as his own. He incorporates locally caught fish into traditional Japanese recipes, prepared in front of customers. Food-saké pairings for aficionados. One of a kind!

Name: Parapluie
Description: This lilliputian restaurant serves globetrotting food in the zeitgeist, with a sprinkling of spices and based on seasonal, mostly local, ingredients. The culinary offer is rolled out in a single set "mystery" menu comprised of several courses at dinner, and a reasonably priced lunchtime menu with options. Fine selection of wine, beer and spirits (whiskies, eaux de vie etc).

Name: Le Bélouga
Address: L'Agapa, 12 rue des Bons-Enfants, Perros-Guirec, 22700, France
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Wheelchair access
Description: This granite, glass and steel structure commands a breath-taking panoramic view over the coast and the bay of the Sept-Îles archipelago from its chic black-and-white interior. The subtle, meticulous cuisine oscillates between classicism and creativity, with the occasional more exotic note, such as raviole of duck foie gras and tonka bean cream or Breton lobster rubbed in saté and served with a red lentil houmous. From Tuesday to Saturday, the evening menu errs towards ambitious, with a more bistronomic streak the rest of the time.

Name: Mantesino
Description: The Naples-born chef, who used to be an engineer, has enthusiastically donned an apron (mantesino in Italian) and opened this small bistro in a street near the Église Saint-Aubin. He gives pride of place to his roots by tapping into the culinary traditions of Southern Italy, from Campania to Puglia. A far cry from stereotypical Italian fare, his no-nonsense bistro cuisine wins diners over by drawing solely on flavoursome, meticulously selected ingredients: mortadella from Bologna, hazelnuts from Piedmont, Ibaïama pork, as well as meat from Aveyron and vegetables from local growers. Uplifting!

Name: Auberge de la Roche
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: In the heart of the Mercantour National Park, between the valleys of the Tinée River and Vésubie River, a duo with a longing for nature set their sights on this traditional stone-built inn. The calm beauty of the surrounding countryside won them over, as it will you, too. Our hosts serve a single set menu of natural, creative cuisine with a strong vegetable component, as well as local produce (including from their kitchen garden). There is a good selection of natural beers and wines.

Name: Bohème
Address: 47 avenue du Moulin de la Croix, Mougins, 06250, France
Description: In this smart, trendy establishment with a decor of premium and untreated materials, the food is an ode to the very best breeds of beef cattle, aged and prepared by the famous butcher Alexandre Polmard in his unique way. Peruvian chef Manuel Rondan is in a class of his own when it comes to cooking over hot coals and wild-fish ceviche, as well as some lovely Mediterranean dishes. There is a drop-dead view from the terrace.

Name: La Bulle d'Air
Description: From his open kitchen, the chef consummately crafts dishes such as low-temperature arctic char, flanked with a velvety gribiche sauce and a crunchy salad of fennel. The single set lunchtime menu is a steal – all the better when leisurely sampled on the delightful, cobbled patio in summertime.

Name: Au G'Retz des Saisons
Description: Well-travelled young chef Samuel Duchêne aligns his cooking with the seasons. His short menu, which changes every month, showcases first and foremost local Pays de Retz farmers and artisans – fish, free-range eggs, sea salt. Beetroot marinated in cider, confit egg yolk, watercress coulis or fillet of sea bass, carrot, coconut emulsion, turmeric: hard work, audacity and flavour. The house-made bread is very good, too. Limited capacity, so it's best to book in advance.

Name: Le Clos de la Prairie
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Set in the countryside, this charming restaurant is peaceful and bucolic. Behind his stove, the chef masterfully prepares dishes in tune with the zeitgeist and the seasons. In summer, enjoy the quiet terrace overlooking the meadow. Accessible only by reservation.

Name: Peron
Description: On the coast road, this building clinging to the rocks offers a breathtaking view of the bay of Marseille and its islands and the château d’If. A brisk sea breeze has shaken up the menu which features dishes such as local and wild fish of the day, stuffed vegetables, duck breast and beef fillet, without forgetting the ubiquitous bouillabaisse, all of which served on the splendid terrace. A genuine institution since 1855!

Name: Chez Fonfon
Description: This family restaurant (1952) is pleasing in terms both of its contemporary interior and its seafood, freshly fished in the wooden pointu boats that can be seen bobbing about in the little port.

Name: Epiro
Description: After a stint in Rome, where they ran a highly sought-after bistro, Alessandra and Marco are giving it another go near the port in Nice. Appetising Roman delicacies, heart-warming home-made pasta, lashings of generosity and tingling tastebuds, without forgetting the splendid Italian wine list – bang on every time!

Name: Auberge de l'Abbaye
Address: 2 rue de la Libération, Beaumont-en-Auge, 14950, France
Description: Local produce, meticulous plating, generous helpings and a taste for fresh herbs, all in tune with the seasons: the scene is set. And let’s not forget the rustic interior of this inn in the heart of a Normandy village that is the epitome of French rural charm.

Name: Emotions
Description: In the heart of the village, this former winegrower's house has been turned into a restaurant (previously La Vigne d'Adam) with a pared-back interior design that blends wood, fabrics and natural materials. The cuisine follows the seasons to create marriages of premium ingredients: hare à la royale in autumn, truffle menu in winter, asparagus in spring and lobster in summer! Over 400 wines.

Name: Lazare
Address: Parvis de la gare Saint-Lazare, rue Intérieure, Paris, 75008, France
Description: In the heart of the famous Gare St - Lazare is this elegant railway brasserie, version 2013. It is the brainchild of Éric Frechon, who respects the canons of the genre: French - style devilled eggs, pike quenelles or mackerel in a white wine sauce. Fine French tradition is right on track! Pleasant and very lively.

Name: Le Relais de Saulx
Description: This characterful establishment (1673) in the town centre, not far from the Hospices de Beaune, is in the capable hands of Charles Danet (previously of Le Timbre in Paris) and it would be an understatement to say that he has settled in quickly! His unmistakable signature style errs towards wholesome market-fresh cuisine, which he describes as "artisanal seasonal" cooking.

Name: L'Agastache
Address: 1 rue de la Cave, Volnay, 21190, France
Description: This restaurant, whose reputation has grown by word of mouth, is fully deserving of its success. The chef is very attentive to the quality of his ingredients and his creative cuisine, in which vegetables and plants play a pivotal role, is as tasty as it is balanced. Examples include houmous of winter veggies with curcuma and egg parfait or a purée of celery with finely diced Granny Smith apples. Bargain priced menu at lunchtime.

Name: Autrement
Description: At a slight remove from the town centre, this quiet little restaurant lays out its own fresh vision. The chef perfectly masters cooking times and seasonings, and works with quality ingredients. His original and colourful cuisine is meticulous and tasty; for instance, his half-cooked veal carpaccio, beetroot, carrots and citrus fruit is a showstopper. Not forgetting his signature dessert: the Paris-Brest. What are you waiting for?

Name: Eclipses
Description: This restaurant, by a chef who has carved out a career in Michelin-starred kitchens (Ledoyen, Apicius, Le Grand Véfour), serves contemporary cuisine that is heedful of ingredients and the seasons. Enjoy your meal in the tastefully decorated neo-Classical setting. Lovely vaulted cellar.

Name: Le Pré de la Cure
Address: 1 place de la Mairie, Yvoire, 74140, France
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Fancy diving into Lake Geneva! The view is as stunning as the food is mouth - watering. Fish and produce from the lake take pride of place in the menu, as do succulent local specialties. Depending on availability, you will taste pike, perch or trout. A treat for the taste buds!

Name: Le Bout du Quai
Address: Route de la Corniche, Cancale, 35260, France
Description: Aptly located at the end of the quayside (hence the name), the fashionable slate grey glazed front of this restaurant overlooks the Atlantic and Mont St Michel. Chef Romain Roland, after a stint at a star restaurant in Corsica, crafts ambitious, creative cuisine, dotted with subtle Mediterranean notes.

Name: Les Ronins
Description: In Japanese culture, ronins are samurai without a master, which is Anthony and Émilie’s metaphor for their unfettered approach to cooking and, of course, their exquisitely presented Franco-Asian cuisine, such as Angus beef hanger steak served with crying tiger sauce and a hearty gratin dauphinois. Trendy Alpine-inspired decor, friendly service and good vibes!

Name: Le Goût du Large
Description: Sheltered from the bustling port, take a seat in this cosy, modern eatery and dig into the contemporary, generous nosh of youthful Jonathan Selliez (assisted by his mum for pastries) who plays on textures and flavours. The fish is from sustainable fishing boats, such as the superb fillet of mackerel, flanked with a maki of leeks rolled in nori seaweed leaves and a medley of carrots, jelly and pickled. All the more reason not to set sail straight away…

Name: L'Atelier
Description: Chef Fabrice Rodot is a food lover, and he proves it with his dishes, which feature local and seasonal ingredients. He has a perfect grasp of the classics, and this cosy restaurant with rustic touches is a lovely setting in which to eat: cauliflower in a brioche crust, mousseline cream; organic veal, peas and carrots, sauce Périgueux-style jus; crêpes Suzette flambéed on a pedestal table. Not forgetting the excellent house-made bread! In fine weather, head for a table by the fountain on the terrace.

Name: Côté Toqués
Description: Chef Julien Chabozy's aromatic, tasty food showcases the best of local produce, with lashings of personality to boot. Friendly and endearing depict the front of house vibe, supervised by his wife Marie. The establishment also boasts a delicatessen and a wine shop, La Cave des Toqués, next door… It was love at first bite.

Name: La Table du Chef
Description: Only open in the evenings, this small bistro just two minutes from Rue d’Antibes never disappoints. In an open kitchen, a youthful chef works with local, seasonal produce, crafting subtle, tasty dishes, such as his knockout velvety carrot soup with star anise and lightly seared shrimp. Market availability dictates the contents of the “Surprise” menu which is great value for money… Booking recommended.

Name: La Table de Marie-Ange
Description: The terrace overlooking the Aravis range is so mesmerising, it is difficult to tear oneself away. Marie-Ange aims to serve fine regional dishes oozing with authentic flavour: pan-seared cèpes, fillets of wild perch from Lake Geneva, fillet of beef simmered in mushrooms and grandma’s potato gratin, without forgetting the wickedly lavish dessert trolley. The interior sports old wood and farming tools – charming welcome.

Name: LiLi
Description: Opened by the Hong Kong luxury hotel group of the same name, the already famous Peninsula Hotel is a fitting home for this Asian restaurant. In a strikingly theatrical decor, the long menu, prepared by the Chinese chef, unveils a wide range of the country's specialities (some adapted to European tastes). A culinary ambassador for China.

Name: Capitaine
Description: After working in the kitchens of some restaurants with a great pedigree (L'Ambroisie, L'Arpège, L'Astrance), Baptiste Day decided to open this pleasant bistro. Diners are treated to lovely market-fresh dishes that are inspired by his Breton origins and enhanced by exotic flavours. The popular starter of pork croquettes (ginger, garlic and chilli mayonnaise) will certainly whet your appetite! Selection of organic and natural wines.

Name: Restaurant des Grands Boulevards
Description: A hip, trendy vibe and a warm welcome set the scene beneath the hotel's central winter garden structure. The concise Italian-themed menu, devised by chef Giovanni Passerini, is both simple and succulent, illustrated by grilled cuttlefish, risotto of spelt and grilled aubergine; Giovanni’s ravioli of spinach, ricotta and sage butter; monkfish in spices, wax beans and chard, emulsion of Savagnin (variety of grape). The beverage list features an intriguing lineup of wines and cocktails. Just the ticket for a party night out on the town!

Name: Auberge Nicolas Flamel
Description: The oldest house in Paris (1407) is named after a learned bourgeois who dabbled in alchemy, one Nicolas Flamel. In a pared-back tasteful interior set off by old stones and timber rafters, the high-flying kitchen brigade of Alan Geaam is hard at work crafting premium ingredients into appetising dishes in the zeitgeist: Plouguerneau crab, Baeri caviar; Racan pigeon, chard, buckwheat; confit of citrus fruits in a lime jelly.

Name: Rooster
Description: After training in prestigious houses (from Passedat to Darroze), Frédéric Duca has set up shop in the more working-class part of the 17th arrondissement. In a former street corner cafe, the Marseille-born chef signs dishes which pay numerous tributes to his Mediterranean and Provençal roots. The lunchtime menu is at delicious eater-friendly prices. More ambitious in the evenings.

Name: Tadam
Description: This delightful little eatery proposes a brief, seasonal and mouth-watering menu, underscored by a commitment to sustainable development. The food hits the spot every time thanks to tip-top ingredients stripped of unnecessary frills, illustrated by the scrumptious hot mushroom pie. A casual vibe and brunch on Sundays. A welcome addition to the Gobelins culinary scene.

Name: Auberge du Cheval Blanc
Description: This 18C coaching inn has been run by the same family since 1959. Chef Jean-Claude Tellechea adds a new spin to the traditional regional line-up: crispy hake, black pudding, Ibaïama ham, Bayonne chocolate. The interior is patriotically decked in red and white Basque Country colours. The range of menus is such that there is something for every budget.

Name: Marso & Co
Description: Tomy Gousset (Tomy & Co, near Les Invalides) runs this restaurant that sets out to take diners on a culinary journey: the food tours the entire Mediterranean basin from Greece to Portugal via Italy and Lebanon (but also Latin America). Examples of the Colombian born chef’s handiwork include an aguachile of seabream and shrimp, pink grapefruit, cucumber and coriander. The octopus-themed artwork on the walls is by street artist Kraken. Soul-warming recipes, spot-on flavours, fantastically fresh ingredients – a felicitous feast awaits you!

Name: Poulpette
Description: Now, this is a place that has it in the bag. The deliberately short menu offers tasty market-based cooking, with flights of fancy far and wide; it is made with fine ingredients prepared with care and originality. Amandine, once a dance teacher, now head of service and partner, and Antoine, alumnus of the elite Paris Institute of Political Studies but passionate about food (stints at Lucas Carton and Jadis) have joined forces to offer a delightful culinary experience.

Name: Kodawari Ramen - Yokochō
Description: The bustling vibe and cramped dimensions of this eatery instantly conjure up pictures of historic Tokyo. The ramen, made on site and served in delicious broths of Loiret poultry, attract gourmets from every horizon. The house speciality is kurugoma ramen made with a secret black sesame seed sauce and pata negra pork. Avoid peak times, as the place is very popular. Fully deserving of its success.

Name: Rhapsody
Description: This spruce eatery in the Parisian suburbs works with first-class produce to rustle up appetising, well-curated bistronomic recipes. Examples include puréed chicory in flaky pastry and seasoned with cancoillotte (sort of cream cheese) and pomegranate; fillet of hake with squash spaghetti, seawater and bergamot stock and for dessert, a wickedly decadent creamy chestnut and Corsican clementine delight. Ask for a table on the lovely rear patio with a view of the kitchen.

Name: Les Trois Forts
Description: From the seventh floor, the panoramic view over the port is simply sublime! The contemporary dishes with a delicious Southern flavour make for a wonderful gourmet interlude.

Name: L'inaTTendu
Description: The inaTTendu, which first opened in Lyon, has opted for a radical change of venue in this attractive sand-coloured stone house idyllically set on the banks of the Saône. The chef continues to craft modern, generous fare, inspired by regional traditions with the odd Asian twist. Smart interior and a knockout view of the river from the lush green terrace.

Name: Le Comptoir de la Mère Germaine
Description: This offshoot of the star establishment doesn’t do things by halves: wood prevails in the contemporary interior and an imposing counter-cum-kitchen with a gleaming spit-roast oven and a shaded terrace. A bistronomic lineup strewn with South American notes.

Name: L'Escargot
Description: A pleasant contemporary setting for traditional cuisine and emblematic dishes, such as snails in butter, garlic and parsley. Chef-owner Dominique Dubert jazzes up a traditional repertory with the odd dash of modernity (combava, ginger, curry, etc). It is a pleasure to linger over a meal on the terrace of this Snail in summer.

Name: L'Ouillette
Description: An enthusiastic young couple is at the helm of this family - run inn on the village square.
