Description: For winter, a modern dining area with wood panelling; for summer, a pretty, flower-decked patio… and all year round, simple and nicely crafted cuisine made with market ingredients – cream of cauliflower soup with pigeon, toast with offal; red mullet fillets, squash stuffed with smoked bacon and cooking juices; Suzette-style crepes with Grand Marnier. With a bit of luck, your visit will coincide with a day when the chef is making a surprise dish on the block in the middle of the dining area, before diners' eyes… a show worth seeing!

Name: Song, Saveurs & Sens
Description: Self-taught chef Nhung Phung was born in Vietnam, but grew up in Laos, Cambodia and Thailand. The aromas and perfumes of her childhood have forged her culinary identity: sensitive, intelligent, balanced cuisine, poised between Southeast Asia and France, delicately spicy and crafted with premium produce. The interior sports a striking blend of turquoise, black and wrought iron – a fine setting for a sensibly priced meal.

Name: Brioude
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Great view,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: This endearing family inn has been serving well-crafted food, in which local producers take pride of place, since 1887! The elegant dining room which overlooks the countryside of southern Ardèche provides the perfect foil to sample Claude Brioude’s “Discovery” menu: a new spin on the omelette with Ardèche watercress, gravlax of trout and leeks, trilogy of lamb with a veggie pie…

Name: Mathieu Kergourlay - Château de Boisgelin
Description: Chef Mathieu Kergourlay welcomes diners to this 450-hectare property and small castle, tastefully restored and decorated by his companion and himself. The tasty, generous and consummately crafted food is full of surprises, such as the mini pissaladière reworked by the chef, which is served with a marinated fillet of mackerel, perfectly grilled over the BBQ.

Name: Gram's
Address: 64 rue de la Colombette, Toulouse, 31000, France
Description: Bang in the centre of Saint Aubin, chef Laura Pelou adds a new twist to country recipes from Aveyron and her grandmothers’ cooking – hence the name! The spruce dining room, depicted by elegant oak parquet floors and lots of room between tables, believes in serving wholesome, simple fare such as leeks in vinaigrette, sprinkled with hard-boiled egg and croutons or a hummus of lentils, risotto of spelt and mushrooms – there is often a vegetarian starter and main course. Regularly renewed menu.

Name: L'Auberge du Château
FacilitiesAndServices: Garden or park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: This restaurant opposite the town hall in an Aveyron village is well known to food lovers, who come here to enjoy contemporary cuisine which places the onus on herbs and vegetables. The dishes are colourful and flavoursome. Lovely flower - filled terrace.

Name: La Signoria
Address: Route de la Forêt de Bonifato, Calvi, 20260, France
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: Just a few minutes from Calvi, this restaurant surrounded by pine forest and vineyards is housed in what used to be a Genoese aristocratic estate, with the mountains of the Bonifatu Cirque on the distant horizon. The terrace overlooking a garden that exudes the scents of the Mediterranean is the idyllic setting in which to savour a menu designed by MICHELIN-starred chef Stéphane Pitré and cooked by Romain Foubard; Valentin Mifort takes care of the desserts. The menu stars local ingredients such as red mullet from the village, Corsican porcu nustrale pork and local strawberries. Pretty villas and suites await you, as well as the spa and Le Bistrot dans l'Herbe.

Name: Clovis
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus
Description: In this bistro in the heart of a medieval village, kick off your meal with a drink and nibbles, before sampling the chef’s unusual concept which involves several variations (starter & main course), all of which are based on one main ingredient (vegetable, meat or fish). Warm welcome and small private room.

Name: Le Relais d'Ozenay
Address: 1244 route de Brancion (Le Bourg), Ozenay, 71700, France
Description: In the picturesque medieval village of Ozenay, you cannot miss this colourful fronted inn. The contemporary interior provides the perfect foil to well-crafted cuisine by a chef who boasts a fine CV. His plating is particularly precise and flowery. Examples include velvety green peas, poached egg and an emulsion of smoked bacon. Fine view of the castle from one of the venue’s two terraces.

Name: Lamaccotte
Description: Generosity, flavour and good ingredients are the elements underpinning Maxime Fillaut's cuisine, which reaps the rewards of his time at La Mare aux Oiseaux and Le Clarence in Paris. The restaurant occupies a modern, light and airy ground-floor space in a stone building in the historical city centre. The menu changes daily, reflecting the produce available at the market, and the dishes are beautifully presented. This is simple and delicious food: fondant home-made gnocchi, vegetable tops and roasted almond pistou; vegetable carbonara, parmesan emulsion, paprika-glazed celery and helianthis; meadowsweet parfait glacé, blossom honey and lemon marmalade, buckwheat sablé and caramelised dried fruit. Fast, well-paced service.

Name: Transparence - La Table de Patrick Fréchin
Description: A short walk from Place Stanislas in a busy pedestrian street, transparency is more than just a name and you can actually see chef Patrick Fréchin working his magic in the theatrically visible kitchen. His enticing dishes showcase premium seasonal ingredients, such as loin of skrei cod, roasted in bay leaf oil with mead-flavoured yoghurt.

Name: La Table du Relais du Bois Saint-Georges
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Fall under the spell of this restaurant housed in an old farmhouse, where the chef has a penchant for beautiful seasonal ingredients (sourced from local producers or the aromatic plant garden located in the grounds). Drink in the view of the terrace, fountain and small lake through the bay windows, as you savour calf sweetbread, spatchcock, elderberry – the soft juicy meat makes for a taste sensation!

Name: Les Jardins de Kerstéphanie
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: This old stone farmstead smothered in Virginia creeper and set in wooded grounds is home to the new headquarters of Emmanuel Kouri, previously encountered at Les Climats (Paris). Mindful of the provenance of his produce (line-caught fish, organic market gardeners, local dairy produce), he conjures up seafood dishes, like little tunny in kari-gosse, marinated cucumber and iced coriander soup or ikejime pollock, violin courgette in basil and a pistachio and lime sabayon. To be enjoyed on the shaded terrace in fine weather.

Name: La Cigale Égarée
Address: 8 rue d'Athenry - ZA Villeneuve-Braouic, Quimperlé, 29300, France
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: This cricket has taken up abode in Brittany, in a quirky antique shop-style décor, flanked by a lush green patio. The menu is depicted by seasonal market produce, fish of the day and garden veggies, grown by the inspired chef. Flavoursome, no-frills recipes (roast hake, spring vegetables and gravy), cooked to perfection.

Name: Côté Mas
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: This inviting restaurant in the heart of a winery is appealingly appointed with contemporary objets d'art and exotic wood furnishings and overlooks the Cévennes. The perfect foil to sample contemporary bistronomic cuisine: duck magret, spicy jus, roast melon in elderflower; panacotta flavoured with lavender honey, apricots and a dairy mousse. Most of the produce is local and seasonal, like the lovely fruity olive oil which is produced on the estate. A fine list of wines from the estate and nearby vineyards, and an impressive selection of wines by the glass.

Name: Le Vieux Castillon
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Terrace,Valet parking
Description: All around, nothing but narrow medieval streets and fields of lavender. In this corner of Provence, bathed in light, this elegant restaurant – done out in the colours of the South of France – adheres to the seasons as it sources sun-kissed ingredients. At lunchtime, a simple menu; in the evening, fine dining.

Name: L'Esberit
Description: This handsome 19C listed stone house, located by a road and just a few minutes from downtown Pau, deploys all its charms to the rear of the property thanks to the peaceful garden patio, shaded by a hundred-year-old oak tree. Inside, the stylish dining room sports herringbone parquet flooring and high ceilings. Chef Nicolas Lormeau has been thriving in this plush setting for some years now. His inventive recipes are a treasure trove of plays on texture and harmonious or surprising flavours (such as the multiple textures of marinated scallops with passion fruit and sweetcorn or the semolina milk with truffles from Lot, kiwi and yuzu-flavoured white chocolate ice cream). Béarn produce takes the limelight in creative, skilfully plated dishes, served professionally and seamlessly. Book (well) in advance!

Name: L'Entre Pots
Description: This former warehouse is now dedicated to the pleasures of the palate. The cuisine combines regional flavours with creative touches, and the wine list features a good selection of local wines. Small delicatessen.

Name: La Passerelle
Description: The chef now at the helm of this maritime-inspired restaurant, where she once trained with her father, is giving us her own modern take on family tradition. She likes to add good concentrated jus to her dishes (octopus with pork jus) as well as sweet-and-sour flavours (langoustine, turnip, almonds). She is also a sommelier, and puts her heart and soul into coming up with optimal food and wine pairings.

Name: La Coursive des Alpes
Description: Welcome to the ski resort’s former cinema, with a lounge bar on the ground-floor for snacks and a drink, and the restaurant proper up on the mezzanine. The chef cooks modern, tasty, well-crafted cuisine, such as toasted ham with truffles and Beaufort cheese; sweetbread and buckwheat, harissa of carrots; to finish, rum baba with orange preserve and vanilla cream. Charming welcome.

Name: Le Pré du Moulin
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Originally a mill, then a primary school, this stone-built village house draws you in with its lovely bucolic atmosphere... and traditional Provençal-inspired cuisine. The terrace, shaded by old plane trees, exudes the essence of Provence.

Name: Nancy Bourguignon
Address: Lieu-dit de Bourgeac, 1 chemin de l'Ancienne-Voie-Ferrée, Paradou, 13520, France
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: What a pleasure it is to take a seat in this establishment where you are welcomed naturally and simply by a Burgundian family. In this charming restaurant, the chef concocts subtle and delicate dishes, sprinkled with Provençal innuendo. The patio, next to the swimming pool and surrounded by Mediterranean vegetation, invites you to slow down and take things easy. An oasis of peace and charm.

Name: Aux Ateliers
Address: 115 avenue de la Vallée-des-Baux, Maussane-les-Alpilles, 13520, France
Description: This warm buzzy bistro with a vintage vibe is always packed to the rafters. The chef, a Normandy lad who fell in love with the Alpilles, titillates our tastebuds with generous, down-to-earth cooking: Provençal-style stuffed veggies; terrine de campagne; rabbit leg confit in olive oil; shoulder of Maussane lamb baked all night long; two-lemon pie with orange blossom. A regular clientele and a pétanque ground outside.

Name: Flocon
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus
Description: In a lively neighbourhood, this is the first business venture of the Flocon brothers, Alexis and Josselin: one is dedicated to the running of the establishment and the other to the cooking. In a bright interior, tuck into surprising, well-thought-out dishes made from carefully sourced products. On top of that, they keep the prices low, wine included.

Name: Ô Gayot
Address: 2 avenue de la Ferté-Macé, Bagnoles-de-l'Orne, 61140, France
Description: This chic bistro in a pretty stone house certainly has its finger on the pulse. On the menu find good bistro recipes that change on a weekly basis. These include, soft - boiled egg with cream of mushroom soup and Calvados baba. A taste sensation!

Name: La Ferme du Chozal
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Terrace
Description: The restaurant may sport a characteristic rustic Alpine vibe, but the appetising cuisine is no less modern. It is made with fine local ingredients illustrated by Leman fera in grilled leeks and a herby butter or a haunch of tender veal, poivrade artichokes and gnocchis. And let's not forget the remarkable list of Alpine wines.

Name: Empreinte
Description: Make a stop at this establishment on a small square in the city centre. The interior is inviting, with its warm decor of untreated wooden floorboards, fabrics and vintage porcelain. Marine and Baptiste Fournier put their hearts into serving particularly polished cuisine, showcasing fish sourced from the market and vegetables from farmers. Menu-carte at lunch, "surprise" menus at dinner. Natural wines.

Name: SouKa
Description: In this tiny village in the heart of the Terrasses du Larzac vineyards, SouKa (root in Occitan) focuses on market ingredients and local producers. The playful chef enjoys conjuring up surprises, such as the mystery lunch and evening menu, whose ingredients you’re asked to guess! The fine local tipples can be purchased from the wine shop on the premises.

Name: Chapeau de Paille - Bistrot Provençal
Description: Bourvil and Piaf play in the background, while straw hats adorn the walls in this cheerful flea market vibe! This rustic, Provençal bistro, located on the town’s ring road, concocts a seasonal menu with an emphasis on market-fresh ingredients: pork terrine, anchovy purée, aïoli, Alpilles lamb, quail flambéed in pastis at your table, baba à la provençal…

Name: Le Bastion
Address: 50 boulevard de la Promenade, Lagrasse, 11220, France
Description: Take a seat in one of two pretty rustic dining spaces to sample "avant-garde country fare", inspired by Auguste Escoffier but with a modern twist. Great produce from the region is used – tomatoes from the Estarac Gardens, vinegar by Cyril Codigna, fish fresh from the market at Port la Nouvelle… Concise tapas menu and spacious terrace.

Name: Le 428
Description: The term ouvrée refers to the area of vineyard - 428m² - that could be dug by a winegrower in one day. Chef Christophe Ledru welcomes diners in a sleek, contemporary interior and serves up modern, well-prepared cuisine ("surprise" menus only), accompanied by a good selection of wines from the village (and beyond).

Name: Restaurant Bohrer
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: This handsome regional abode is steeped in bourgeois, countrified elegance. It is ideal to sample gourmet cuisine accompanied by fine, mainly local, vintages. The chef takes pleasure in surprising us with goose fillet tataki and pistachio-teriyaki sauce, or a lobster bao with passion fruit and parmesan. Alternatively, the lively, friendly Brasserie Chez Julien is housed in a former cinema.

Name: Restaurant de l'Écluse 16
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Wheelchair access
Description: This restaurant standing beside the Canal de la Sarre towpath was once a coaching inn, along which horses used to tow coal from the mines. The chef, from Morbihan in Brittany, cooks up delicious and meticulous cuisine, such as saffron risotto with chorizo served alongside premium quality poultry with wild prawns, or his truly unforgettable take on tarte Tatin. He occasionally uses ingredients from the local terroir, enhanced with condiments or home-made aromatic oils.

Name: L'Écrin
Description: This endearing restaurant, slightly off the historic town’s crowded tourist track, offers fresh, seasonal, expertly crafted Mediterranean cuisine, such as brandade of forkbeard fish, bottarga and a peppery piquillo cream. The dinky terrace is invariably taken by storm in summertime. Infectiously cosy welcome. A genuine bijou of an eatery.

Name: Le Grand Réfectoire
Address: 3 cour Saint-Henri, Grand Hôtel-Dieu, Lyon, 69002, France
Description: In the heart of the grandiose Hôtel Dieu, beneath the hundred-year-old vaults of the nuns’ former refectory, the menu of this huge brasserie is signed by Marcel Ravin (2*-chef of Monaco’s Blue Bay). The modern food is sprinkled with exotic West Indian influences. The swish rooftop bar (L’Officine) draws city slickers like bees to honey, as does the exquisite patio in the inner courtyard.

Name: L'Abélia
Description: Chef Vincent Berthomeau and his spouse Pascale have set up shop in an edifice dating from 1900 that is slightly outside the city centre of Nantes. Their handsome mansion is further enhanced by a conservatory, a terrace and a garden. The regulars return for the chef’s generous seasonal score and his menus vary depending on what he finds on his frequent forays to Talensac market. Enticing dishes such as a cassolette of langoustines and pleurote mushrooms in a flavoursome seafood stock or an exquisite chocolate, butterscotch and caramelised peanut tartlet, further jazzed up by a carrot sorbet and carrot coulis.

Name: Comptoir du Marché
Description: In the heart of bustling historic Nice, casual and friendly are the watchwords of this vintage-inspired market counter, whose name is equal to the chef’s colourful, flavoursome dishes. Concise menu, unfailingly fresh and reasonable rates: it is always a pleasure to spend time here.

Name: L'A Cheda
Description: Take a seat on the terrace overlooking the pool in a setting, steeped in romanticism. The chef has a preference for local ingredients and rigorously selects his suppliers. You will enjoy wild fish, organic Corsican meat and vegetables fresh from the permaculture garden. Attentive service and a wine list rich in pleasant surprises.

Name: Relais du Teulet
Description: This former coaching inn, run by the same family for five generations, is a pleasant surprise! The chef devises simple and accessible contemporary cuisine, based on a short menu that highlights the region's great produce – Corrèze meats, Aurillac fruit and vegetables.

Name: Villa Mon Rêve
Address: 2 levée de la Divatte, Basse-Goulaine, 44115, France
Description: On the banks of the Loire, this restaurant is set in a pretty townhouse dating back to the late 19C. It has been proudly serving its guests delicious food in an elegant, cosy decor for 75 years – so you could say it's an institution. The current chef uses the finest local produce in traditional regional cuisine: frogs' legs with parsley butter or a herb sauce; local fish (pike, pike-perch and sea bass) with beurre blanc; golden-brown calf sweetbreads with a morel cream. A smiling welcome awaits you, as does a large shady terrace surrounded by a bucolic garden planted with colourful flowerbeds. Mon Rêve really is a dream!

Name: Auberge du Vieux Gachet
Address: Le Vieux Gachet, au bord de l'Erdre, Carquefou, 44470, France
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: The sprawling terrace, which commands a superlative view of the fairytale Gacherie château, seems to float above the River Erdre. A peaceful, refreshing venue set in the heart of unspoiled countryside. Even better, the floor-to-ceiling windows of the dining room offer the same fantastic view when the weather is less suited to alfresco dining. The owner-chef, Walter Lescot, works only with ingredients he himself loves: Scandinavian gravlax of salmon, lemon cream; loin of cod, celery and chorizo risotto and a piquillos sauce. The tart of citrus fruit and lime sorbet is delicate, flavoursome and fruity – an ideal conclusion to your meal. With over 350 references, the wine cellar adds the final cherry to this appetising portrait.

Name: Le François II
Description: For the last ten years, Breton chef Jérôme Evain has been paying tribute to his region as he crafts primarily local produce of flawless quality. An endearing venue, a tempting score and a bargain-priced lunchtime menu, illustrated by 65°C free-range egg, green lentils, emulsion of Ossau Iraty cheese, melt-in-the-mouth cod cooked at a low temperature and an iconic gâteau nantais with banana confit and butterscotch to finish. The professional, friendly front-of-house service is courtesy of Solenn.

Name: Le Cercle
Description: Deftly crafted dishes, high-quality ingredients and cheerful service: it is a delight to eat at Le Cercle. Some of our favourites include snails in garlic and an emulsion of potatoes; turbot with sand carrots and langoustine bisque. Elegant contemporary artwork graces the interior that is both chic and cosy.

Name: Bonnotte
Description: A 10-minute walk from the Albert Kahn Museum, the restaurant of Antoine Guichard (David Bizet's former sous-chef) and Manon Negretti pays homage to the Île de Noirmoutier, the island where the bonnotte potato is cultivated. In a low-key contemporary bistro setting, the dishes, concocted with fresh produce, are in step with the latest in bistronomy cuisine. Set menu at lunchtime and à la carte menu in the evening.

Name: Ar Maen Hir
Address: 15 bis rue du Prieuré, Locronan, 29180, France
Description: For his first restaurant, youthful Thibaud Érard chose the picturesque, medieval village of Locronan, near Quimper, where he is clearly flourishing. His traditional, wholesome cuisine quietly feeds you well. Pleasant, casual service.

Name: La Toq'
Description: The professional, highly experienced, virtuoso chef crafts high-flying dishes using top-notch ingredients: smoked to order slab of salmon with cauliflower and French caviar; Alsace poultry, Agria potatoes, roasted leeks and a velvety Albufera sauce… These flavoursome delicacies are served in a plush, fancy interior enhanced by century-old stone walls. Fine wine list.

Name: Le Capu
Description: In an ideal location 300m from Place Stanislas, this restaurant boasts an elegant decor in a bold, contemporary vein, enhanced by baroque notes (rich hues and crushed velvet). The cuisine is suitably generous – for example, filet mignon of veal, with aubergine caviar, grilled courgettes and a tarragon sauce.

Name: Ourea
Address: 72 rue de la Paix-Marcel-Paul, Marseille, 13006, France
Description: Matthieu Roche moved from Paris (where he worked at Semilla) to open this tiny bistro with his partner Camille. The space, located between the port and the courthouse, reflects the colours and flavours of Provence. The chef is attentive to the seasons, buying locally (Mediterranean fish directly from the port, vegetables from Mallemort's market gardens, citrus fruits from the Domaine du Jasson).

Name: Chabrol
Description: “Faire Chabrol” is an ancient custom in rural southern France, which consists in adding a little wine to the dregs of soup to further dilute the stock, before gulping it down. In the restaurant of the same name, two childhood buddies seek to enhance simple (but high-quality) ingredients, thanks to modern recipes, strewn with a sprinkling of intelligent inventiveness – to the delight of diners.

Name: Terminal #1
Address: 1408 avenue de la Mer, Montpellier, 34000, France
Description: The Pourcel brothers have upcycled this former wine storehouse into a vast space where stone, steel and wood are blended in a smart neo-industrial vein. The dishes, which draw on locally sourced ingredients at their height of their maturity, are infused with inspirations from far and wide. As you peruse the menu ranging from super-fresh seabream, red mullet and seabass to fried potato cakes, rockfish soup or roast squid with tempura of squid head, houmous cream and lemon confit dressing, you will get an excellent foretaste of the “gastronomic bistro” spirit of this terminal.

Name: Domaine de la Tortinière
Address: 10 route de Ballan, à Veigné, Montbazon, 37250, France
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: In the former orangery of this picturesque château, with a terrace overlooking the Indre valley and wooded grounds planted with hundred-year-old trees, you will be treated to meticulous contemporary cuisine that is in tune with the seasons: artichoke velouté and smoked trout with brebis du lochois ewe's milk cheese; Arctic char with hazelnuts, confit potatoes, lemon sauce with Avruga "caviar"; pistachio and orange blossom cheesecake. Precise dishes and an enchanting setting: why not extend your time here with an overnight stay at the hotel?

Name: La Gloire
Description: A venerable Montargis institution, located alongside the N7. For several generations, culinary tradition has been revisited with flair and generosity; do not miss out on the rather imposing dessert trolley.

Name: Le Montaigu - Domaine de la Bretesche
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Wheelchair access
Description: The outhouses of Bretesche castle, an imposing medieval behemoth, are home to a plush dining room which overlooks the grounds and lake. Delightful bar in the former stables. The chef signs a score that caters to modern palates: Brittany scallops, parsnips, coffee; locally grown carrots, Brière honey and cardamon orange.

Name: La Table du Château
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Terrace
Description: In the hushed, elegant decor of this Montreuil-sur-Mer institution, a young chef from Lille serves creative, eco-responsible cuisine (fermentation, decoction). He puts the emphasis firmly on plants and vegetables and showcases small-scale local producers. The yellow pollack, courgette from the market gardener, fish roe and elderflowers is a surprising, hearty dish with wonderful marriages of flavours.

Name: Jérôme Brochot
Description: Jérôme Brochot concocts a set menu made with market-fresh produce that changes on a weekly basis and comprises several courses. He works with excellent produce: green asparagus, lobster, turbot etc. They offer a cookery class on Sunday mornings.

Name: Émile Job
Description: This restaurant extends a cordial invitation to sample the popular classics that showcase the terroir: Bresse poultry, frogs' legs in parsley sauce, lake fish, cherries jubilee and vanilla ice cream. The chef sticks to tradition, much to the delight of his guests. Dine on the lovely terrace, in the shade of the hundred-year-old lime trees and overlooking the river.

Name: Anecdote
Description: In the words of Anecdote's owner Alexandre Gauthier, who is also chef at La Grenouillère, Samuel Pesquet creates a "cuisine of memory" – in it, he pays homage to the dishes his father used to make in the 1980s. This is generous and mouth-watering cuisine made from fine ingredients – goujonnettes with gribiche sauce, braised rib steak, crêpes Suzette or tarte Tatin – that you won't be forgetting any time soon.

Name: Le Petit Jardin
FacilitiesAndServices: Garden or park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: As its name ("The Little Garden") suggests, this traditional fine dining restaurant has one of the prettiest terraces in the city, nestled in a lush, quiet garden. There is a subdued and bucolic atmosphere in the dining area with its large glass-paned façade, where the beautifully presented seasonal dishes are served. Those with a sweet tooth won't be disappointed by the delicious desserts, such as the remarkable trompe l'œil lemon, fleur de sel sablé biscuit and lemon sorbet. There is also a bistro serving international cuisine.

Name: Le Lucullus
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: In a modern interior, this restaurant puts local ingredients centre stage. On sunny days, on the peaceful patio, you will make the connection between the name of this place and its namesake, the Roman general Lucullus, renowned for his lavish dining table. The flavoursome dishes, such as Anjou quail roasted whole, with confit legs, burnt corn purée and royal sauce, are beautifully presented.

Name: La Quincaillerie
Description: A talented pair: Guillaume Weil, a young chef from Moselle (with an impressive international background) and Jérôme Douay, who shuttles between the restaurant floor and the kitchen. They propose rather traditional French cuisine (from pâté en croûte to veal filet mignon with truffles; floating island) with a handful of influences from around the world. They stick scrupulously to the seasons, in dishes that are full of flavour. This former ironmonger's with a large wooden staircase that leads to a dining area on the first floor has kept its slightly retro style. There is an open kitchen and a wine boutique on the ground floor.

Name: La Baratte
Description: A small brick house in a residential neighbourhood has been home to this family-run eatery for four generations. The stylish, contemporary dining room opens onto a pretty garden and teak decked terrace. The chef impressively crafts enticing dishes, such as sautéed snails in a light frothy garlic and parsley emulsion and a bacon-flavoured cake. The after-dinner marshmallow treats are almost too pretty to eat!

Name: Annette
Description: This pair – she is from Ile de Ré, he hails from Bristol – met in a restaurant in Amsterdam and went on to open this modern bistro in La Rochelle. The space comprises pale wood tables and furniture, a glassed-in kitchen at the back, a zellige-tiled wall and a small terrace overlooking a pedestrian street. They propose French cuisine that is packed with freshness and flavour! The chef shows he has technique and talent, eg with his wild sea bass, white wine sauce, cockles, broccoli purée and lightly grilled green cabbage. As for dessert, Audrey delights diners with her "gâteau au chocolat d'Annette" (her grandmother's recipe), served with chestnut cream ice cream – potent and delicious.

Name: Le Relais Plaza
Description: Ensconced within the Hotel Plaza Athénée, it is impossible to resist the charm of the lovely 1930s decor inspired by the liner SS Normandie. A unique atmosphere in which to sample cuisine with a pronounced sense of tradition, ranging from the "granny's cooking" dear to Jean Imbert (sea bream gratin, stuffed tomato and pilaf rice) to the classics that have sealed the reputation of this famous Art Deco spot.

Name: Aux Trois Rois
Description: The bistro classics reign supreme (meat pie, calf's head) but there is still room for seafood dishes. The slate board features constantly changing dishes and the wines are real finds. A restaurant where taste, quality and conviviality are the order of the day!

Name: Le Jarrousset
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Terrace
Description: In a lush green setting, this recently restored inn is a champion of local produce, illustrated by the chef’s painstakingly selected network of nearby farms and producers. Meals are served in a pared-down, modern interior, whose furniture and tableware is the work of local artisans. Let yourself be guided by the expert tips of the knowledgeable sommelière.

Name: Le Petit Banc
Description: Originally from the Lyon area, Véronique and Gilles have been at the helm of this pretty regional building at the foot of the Château de Noirmoutier for some 10 years. The quaintly quirky interior sports red Skai banquettes, bistro furniture, mirrors and old wooden floorboards. The menu stars charcuterie from Lyon and Vendée delicacies in a reasonably priced set menu that changes frequently. The vibe is suitably buzzy and casual and reminiscent of a “bouchon lyonnais” that has been uprooted to the island of Noirmoutier, much to our delight!

Name: Maison Castet
Address: 44 avenue de la Gare, Martres-Tolosane, 31220, France
Description: This contemporary eatery at a remove from the town centre used to be the station café. The chef here employs premium ingredients and his considerable technical skill to conjure up his creative cuisine, transporting diners to Brazil, for example, with a wild pollack moqueca, herb salad and farofa. His impressive desserts, such as beef heart tomato in puffed sugar and sage cream, deserve a special mention. Terrific wine list.

Name: La Colombe
Description: Salmon gravlax with citrus fruit, cream of chives and Timut pepper; slow-cooked lamb, a gutsy jus, cream of sweetcorn and roast winter squash… The generous, seriously Provençal score of Pascal and Nadège Bonamy has made their restaurant, at the foot of the Maurettes range, one of the region’s gourmet beacons.

Name: Au Fil des Saisons
Address: 55 route de la Roche-sur-Yon, Luçon, 85400, France
Description: This engaging roadside inn provides an opportunity to sample stripped-back, seasonal fare that relies on fresh ingredients of traditional and regional inspiration (duck foie gras with juniper berries, breast of roast guinea fowl in herbs, etc.). A small cottage garden supplies the kitchen with some veggies and herbs. Take a seat in the conservatory or in the garden, depending on the season.

Name: L'Endroit
Description: Not the kind of place you would expect to find here! Innovative loft - style interior and kitchens that open right onto the dining area. Hamburger with foie gras, rognons revisités (kidneys), superb desserts. This is the place to be.

Name: Le Vallon de Chérisy
Description: The name is a passing nod to an ode composed by Victor Hugo in this very inn back in 1821. The food has remained voluntarily rustic and hearty and faithfully keeps pace with the seasons, in particular the veggies and aromatic herbs. Save room for the wickedly decadent house dessert: a hot vanilla and butterscotch soufflé – to die for!

Name: Le Petit Mézériat
Description: In a small village near Vonnas, the owner chef serves a bargain priced lunchtime menu and a surprise menu (in several stages) which varies according to the season and market availability, with a distinct fondness for locally sourced ingredients. All of which is served by cheerful Amandine, the chef’s spouse, in their spruce, tastefully appointed venue.

Name: Le Clos Perché
Description: Once upon a time, there was an inn on the high plateaux of the Monts du Forez, set at an altitude of 1 150m. It is here, on the edge of this tiny village, that Julien Magne has set up shop. In the kitchen, this chef creates colourful, inventive cuisine with a playful approach that brings a smile to your face!

Name: Le Jardin de Bellevue
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Wheelchair access
Description: The comfortable and elegant setting of this century-old building has been rejuvenated by the recent arrival of Élise and Paul Fabuel. He is the young chef who appeared on French TV's Objectif Top Chef, as well as completing stints at À Table in Metz and À l'Échevin in Colmar. Here, he serves up an attractive seasonal menu, eg a medley of pumpkin, roast chestnuts, Iberian ham and porcini, or turbot a la plancha, radishes, courgettes with mint and sauce vierge.

Name: La Place de Mougins
Description: On the village square as the name suggests! Chic and pleasing are adjectives equally applicable to this charming restaurant and its cuisine, thanks to a passionate and creative chef. Month by month he gives pride of place to a succession of seasonal ingredients... celebrating the truffle, the asparagus and so on.

Name: Amour Blanc
Address: Hôtel Fleur de Loire, 24 quai Villebois-Mareuil, Blois, 41000, France
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Terrace,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: Christophe Hay's second restaurant is named after a species of carp. It is located on the first floor of a modern extension slightly set back from the original building. This inviting wood-panelled and light-filled interior, with its large bay windows looking out over the Loire, immediately works its magic. The chef of Fleur de Loire gives free rein to his passion for Loire ingredients (local cheeses, géline de Touraine heirloom poultry, fried small fish and mullet from the River Loire, lamb and caviar from the Sologne), but also Wagyu beef from his own farm. In short, fine ingredients treated with care to create dishes that tend towards the classical.

Name: Au Cheval Blanc
Description: In this small village on the doorstep of the Sundgau, you can taste carefully-prepared, flavoursome dishes, devised by a chef who draws his inspiration from market produce – green asparagus with poached egg and Gascon bacon, gently-cooked veal fillet, etc. An appetising establishment.

Name: Le Cammissar
Description: This youthful chef isn’t lacking in ambition. In this half-timbered red-painted 15C edifice, restored at great cost, he produces modern dishes using painstakingly selected produce – pearlescent wild turbot with baby artichokes à la barigoule, or Breton lobster tail, with white asparagus and morels.

Name: La Colline du Colombier
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Deep in the countryside, overlooking the Loire, this restored farmhouse has a style that is rustic but also chic and minimalist! It allies nature and design and serves refined dishes made from local ingredients, combined with modern touches.

Name: Boat aux Saveurs
Description: This contemporary villa set away from the bustle of the town centre is run by a mother and daughter team. Foodies adore the lovingly prepared dishes fully in tune with the times. The chef makes a point of honour of sourcing ingredients from local producers and most of the veggies come from their own vegetable garden.

Name: Huître Brûlée
Description: Don’t worry, the oysters aren’t burnt - despite the establishment’s name! Updated recipes, quality ingredients, locally sourced whenever possible (organic veggies, fish from small boats), concise, seasonal menu. This friendly bolthole is run by an enthusiastic couple: local lad Paul Lacheray, in the kitchen and his partner, Chloé Woestelandt, who runs the dining room with considerable brio…

Name: Le Palace de Menthon
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view
Description: A vibrant colour scheme and an unrivalled view of the lake depict this smart, trendy restaurant which serves finely crafted bistronomic fare: foie gras and duck breast; fillet of roast John Dory with seaweed butter; Brittany shortcrust with exotic marmalade.

Name: Maison Cluny
Description: Much to our delight, the gourmet duet, formerly of the Cornichon in the Daguerre district, has teamed up again in this stylish bistro opposite the Cluny Museum garden in the heart of the Latin Quarter. The slate menu reads like an old-school cookbook: chicken liver pâté, veal kidneys, game in season, rice pudding… Warm interior and casual, upbeat vibe.

Name: Racine
Description: She is Canadian and he’s Belgian and they have set up shop in Lectoure in a narrow street near the cathedral. They regale diners with healthy, unpretentious food in the zeitgeist that shines the spotlight on regional producers and on aromatic herbs, fermented seasonings and citrus fruits, all of which washed down with a fine lineup of natural wines. Meals are served in a workshop-inspired interior, whose high ceiling, timber rafters and old stone walls are cleverly paired with stylish modern furnishings. Now add eater friendly prices and you will understand that a meal in this establishment often requires forward planning.

Name: Le Binôme
Address: 32A avenue des Carrés - à Annecy-le-Vieux, Annecy, 74940, France
Description: Mathilde and Remi work together like clockwork. He is in charge of savoury dishes, she crafts the desserts and together they cheerfully wait at table. Market-fresh, throbbingly simple, deftly executed cuisine, illustrated by melt-in-the-mouth chuck beef stew with fluffy mashed potatoes. A few seats at the bar offer an insight into the chefs’ handiwork.

Name: Symbiose
Description: Run by four young partners, Symbiose makes it all look easy: the bold and efficiently prepared dishes, the friendly, relaxed service, the mostly young, if not trendy, clientele. Then there is the little bistro - style dining area – and unbeatable value for money at lunchtime. Highly recommended.

Name: Sébastopol
Description: This engaging small eatery, something of a landmark in Lille, is the haunt of a chef who concocts a regularly renewed, concise menu strewn with personal touches and a fondness for surf and turf combinations (scallops from Boulogne, roast artichokes, puree of Camus artichokes and Noir de Bigorre pork belly). Fine wine list and attentive yet unstarched service.

Name: Hercule Poireau
Address: 2 rue de la Nation, Périgueux, 24000, France
Description: At the foot of Cathédrale St Front, this restaurant that pays homage to the fictional detective occupies a 16C room with a pale stone vaulted ceiling. Thanks to his little grey cells, Poirot would no doubt have detected the sincerity behind the deliciously revamped recipes based on produce from the exceptional terroir of the Dordogne: terrine of semi-cooked foie gras and rhubarb pickles with Monbazillac; pan-fried magret de canard; tarte Tatin with salted butter caramel ice cream. A warm welcome and dynamic service.

Name: Le Saint-Martial
Description: Valérie and Jean-Marc Réal have been at the helm of this delightful restaurant in a peaceful Black Périgord village for over twenty years. The chef enhances seasonal produce, cleverly blending tradition and modernity, in particular courtesy of punchy gravies and carefully balanced combinations of ingredients. Examples include sautéed snails and calf’s head wrapped in green leaves, garnished with a watercress-flavoured crème of cep mushrooms. A warm welcome and an extensive wine cellar add the final flourish to a slap-up meal.

Name: Maison Soubeiran
Description: We fell in love with this family-run establishment whose chef whips up spontaneous regional fare made with fresh, seasonal ingredients from local organic market gardeners. Scents and flavours from the garrigue, Camargue and Mediterranean, jazzed up with spicy notes and flanked by homemade sourdough bread made with heritage wheat. Authentic warm welcome and an exquisite patio shaded by a natural trellis.

Name: À Table ! Chez Éric Léautey
Description: Being at Chez Eric Léautey is a pleasure. The small porch prepares you for the tasting to come, and your taste buds stand to attention as you read the menu. The suggestions are deliberately down - to - earth, drawing on the seasons and local terroir, such as the veal chop, as tender and juicy as can be. So, what are you waiting for?

Name: Le Cénacle
Address: La Cour des Consuls, 46 rue des Couteliers, Toulouse, 31000, France
Description: Le Cénacle has a plush, elegant atmosphere (superb 16C sculpted fireplace, a Caravaggio print, exposed beams). The chef takes pride in forging long-lasting partnerships with good regional producers: organic vegetables from Gers, lamb from Béarn, line-caught fish. Inventive cuisine with a Mediterranean flavour, and good value for money at lunchtime.

Name: Le Séran - Château d'Audrieu
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: A listed 18C stately house, the epitome of special occasion indulgence, provides the perfect foil to polished French cuisine. Forthright recipes inspired by the classics which star local and seasonal produce that hit the spot every time, illustrated by saddle of lamb in marjoram garnished with potatoes and seaweed. First-class sauces and craftsmanship courtesy of a virtuoso chef.

Name: Aux Poulbots Gourmets
Description: The rascally, iconic poulbots (street urchins) of Montmartre have now been joined by those of Thionville! Large bay windows, Lloyd Loom chairs and modern light fixtures add to the timeless elegance. The menu features recipes such as lobster salad and seasonal vegetables or pan-fried frogs’ legs…

Name: Mas de Dardagna
Address: 1 chemin de Dardagna, Rangueil, Toulouse, 31400, France
Description: Now, this is simple, well-made fare that does justice to its ingredients (the chef uses short supply chains as much as possible): guinea fowl and black Gascon pork charlotte, artichoke cream, full-bodied gravy and fresh mushrooms. No doubt about it, this typical Toulouse farmhouse is a haven for foodies! On sunny days, make the most of the terrace beneath the wisteria.

Name: L'Instant...
Description: Take an instant to savour a gourmet interlude not far from Toulouse! Diners eat cheek to jowl at immaculate white tables. In the kitchen the chef creates contemporary cuisine with a few Southern French and Asian touches. Don't miss the "L'instant gourmet" set menu!

Name: La Table d'Auzeville
Description: In this white house in the heart of a village in the suburbs of Toulouse, the chef serves up generous traditional cuisine, including dishes such as fillet of duck with a spicy reduction or tournedos of beef with morel mushrooms. For dessert, a crunchy strawberry tartlet with home-made pistachio ice cream. In fine weather, enjoy your meal on the shady terrace.

Name: La Table de Monrecour
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: This gourmet restaurant is housed in a contemporary extension at the heart of this estate overlooking the Périgord countryside. It is furnished in a resolutely classical style and reflects modern culinary tendencies with the skilfully prepared and flavoursome dishes. Perfect for hotel residents, and anyone else.

Name: Auberge de Groisy
Description: This engaging 19C farmstead has been renovated in keeping with today’s tastes: stylish bare beams and stonework and contemporary comforts adorned in beige and linen. Perfect to sample up - to - the - minute cuisine, which focuses on local produce. All the bread and ice cream is homemade.

Name: La Brucelière
Address: 54 place de la Capelle, Issigeac, 24560, France
Description: This authentic country inn restored by the owner couple is the epitome of charm. Star-studded chef Anthony Hardy has built up a network he can rely on, starting with his wife Marie for the front of house, and including a handful of local producers for the ingredients. The resulting cuisine combines consummately crafted seasonal produce, spot-on seasonings and flawless cooking. Start with mackerel cooked over a direct flame and organic marinated celery, followed by exquisitely plated French duckling roasted whole and served with glazed carrots, finishing with a chou pastry stuffed with hazelnut cream, both minimalist and comforting at the same time. Pretty terrace overlooking the garden to the rear is heaven when the weather permits.

Name: La Table des Merville
Description: This glass extension on a pretty square with a terrace has kitchens that open onto the dining area, giving the impression that the chef is working among the guests. Claudie and Thierry Merville have succeeded in creating an original space in which to serve their nicely contemporary and lovingly prepared dishes!

Name: Au Pois Gourmand
Description: Extended and refurbished, the terrace of the Pois Gourmand, which commands a matchless view of the Garonne, offers a rural setting in the heart of town. The food is equally uplifting from semi-cooked duck foie gras in apricots to grilled Mediterranean croaker with fennel and orange confit. Simply delicious.

Name: Mimosa
Description: "This establishment, close to the marina, offers modern cuisine with Provençal influences. Tomato gazpacho, niçoise vegetables; seared prawns and risotto: the dressings are meticulous, the flavours robust, and the cooking skilful. In short, culinary delights every step of the way! Truffle menus when in season, and a pleasant terrace for summer days. "

Name: La Coquerie
Description: Close to the famous naval cemetery, this chic, contemporary little place boasts the Mediterranean as its backdrop and a panoramic terrace for fine weather. The restaurant serves exceedingly fresh cuisine focused on market produce and local producers, with a single six-course set menu served at both lunch and dinner. Chef Guilhem Blanc-Brude juggles Mediterranean inspirations and more inventive dishes, such as sea bass cooked scales on, potatoes confit with saffron, hollandaise sauce with wild fennel and dill, and chanterelle pickles. They also have a terrific list of natural wines.

Name: Le Quai
Description: You could stay on this quayside for hours admiring the Rhône and the vineyards. On the terrace or in the bright dining area, you could almost be on an ocean liner! A modern-day bistro in which to enjoy generous dishes.

Name: La Bourse et la Vie
Description: This bistro owned by an American chef is a big hit. So what is the secret of his success? Distinctly French dishes, slightly tweaked, quality ingredients and flavours that are on point. Leeks with vinaigrette; onglet de bœuf (a skirt steak) with peppercorn sauce; chocolate mousse: all manner of bistro classics that you'll be delighted to come across (again).

Name: Shu
Description: You have to stoop to get through the doorway that leads to this 17C cellar. In a minimalist decor, discover authentic and finely executed Japanese cuisine, in which the freshness of the ingredients works its magic in kushiage, sushi and sashimi.

Name: Les Tamaris - Chez Raymond
Address: Boulevard de la Baleine, Le Lavandou, 83980, France
Description: Bourride, stuffed capon, grilled Mediterranean langouste, and, above all, the iconic bouillabaisse cooked over a wood fire. Under the watchful eye of its colourful boss, Raymond, the local catch of the day takes pride of place in this iconic institution on Saint-Clair beach. The terrace overlooking the sea is exquisite – so remember to ask for a seat here when you book (compulsory).

Name: Aux Prés
Description: An openly vintage bistro (red banquette seating, smoked - glass mirrors, floral wallpaper) in St Germain and international cuisine by Cyril Lignac, whose creativity never strays entirely from its French country roots.

Name: Le 39V
Description: International customers flock to the sixth floor of 39 Avenue George V... and for good reason! Overlooking the rooftops of Paris, you will enjoy consummately crafted, polished French food. After a major makeover, every detail, from the wooden parquet floor to the made-to-measure seating and the haute couture crockery, has been preened and pondered over. The epitome of understated luxury!

Name: SOlange
Description: Slightly out of the lively city centre, you can expect creative, heart-warming dishes made with local ingredients (most sourced from small local producers) and a menu that changes weekly. Daring combinations and inventive, tasty recipes such as cuttlefish, peppers and black pudding or Iberic pluma ham, chickpeas and chorizo…

Name: Philippe Redon
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: If you like a certain vibrancy in your food, this is the place for you: recipes oscillate between gastro - bistro, contemporary and old - school gourmet, with a predilection for made - to - measure ingredients (poultry, oysters etc); on - point wine advice thrown in for good measure.

Name: Nodaïwa
Description: This little restaurant, an off - shoot of a Tokyo - based eatery, boasts an unusual speciality: eel! The unagi is meticulously crafted and seasoned with soy sauce, or sanshô, an Asian pepper. The vast majority of diners who come here are Japanese, which gives an idea of the quality of the cuisine.

Name: Mori Venice Bar
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Take a seat here, in front of the former stock exchange, to savour the great specialities of Venice and northeast Italy in an interior by Philippe Starck that evokes the refinement of Venice. Painstakingly chosen ingredients: the veggies come straight from a “respectful cottage garden” and the fish from sustainable sources, like the turbot cooked in butter and prosecco with spinach leaf and cream of celery. Let’s not forget the cicchetti (small snacks) or the delicious ice cream topped with hazelnuts from Piedmont.

Name: Roche Belle
Address: 455 corniche du Liouquet, La Ciotat, 13600, France
Description: This small house, smothered in Virginia creeper and complete with a patio planted with olive trees, paints an archetypal portrait of Provence. The aromatic, sun-soaked cuisine, steeped in the fragrant aroma of the Mediterranean, illustrates a culinary quest whose goal is “simply good food” (to quote chef Arnaud). The bargain lunchtime set menu is as devilishly tempting as the à la carte lineup. We sampled snails in parsley and garlic and hazelnut-flavoured squash; veal blanquette stew with girolle mushrooms and red rice from Camargue; roast figs in muscat grapes and fennel, honey mousse and raspberry sorbet. The house speciality is whole fish and poultry (seabream, capon, etc.). Cheerful welcome and service.

Name: Émile
Description: An appealing wine list, 100% house-made traditional cuisine that focuses on fresh produce and local producers and – the icing on the cake – a pretty terrace overlooking a lovely square. The star of the show is obviously the cassoulet, but the menu proposes plenty of delicious alternatives, all at reasonable prices.

Name: Auberge de Grilly
Description: In a charming village between Gex and Divonne, Auberge de Grilly stands close to the church. While the interior decor tends toward the rustic, the cuisine is modern, with dishes based on fine ingredients cleverly curated into just one generous tasting menu. Service with a smile, plus a pleasant terrace.

Name: Aromatic
Description: In La Croix-Rousse, Frédéric Taghavi conjure up inventive, modern recipes which add a new twist to culinary traditions, as well as featuring a scattering of international influences: Limousin sweetbread, leeks and morels in a kalamansi reduction; quickly seared squid in coconut milk and yellow curry shrimp sauce; slow-cooked beef cheeks in red wine with farm-reared bacon risotto…

Name: Le Terminus
Description: The menu of this former 1900s station buffet features modern cuisine that places freshness above all other virtues! You can have lunch or dinner in the brasserie, in an intimate and cosy room, to enjoy the regional classics that have made the house so successful (pâté en croûte, quenelle de brochet, frogs' legs). There are a few guestrooms on the first floor.

Name: Dessance
Description: Housed in a private mansion in the Marais, this restaurant is run by an Argentinian chef who creates inspired seasonal cuisine. He devises two "carte blanche" menus, one focusing on meat and fish ("Terre & Mer"), the other vegetarian. To give a few examples: "revisited croque-crevette"; foie gras, smoked eel and mushrooms; pollack, celeriac and wasabi. The wine list includes a number of biodynamic and natural choices. The elegant setting, with its high ceilings and greenery, is reminiscent of a winter garden – the location is full of charm and style.

Name: Lavandin - Château Les Oliviers de Salettes
Description: This peaceful 16C château, restored to the highest standards, is the quintessence of Drôme provençale. From the terrace overlooking the grounds and lavender fields or in the cosy dining room with its vaulted ceiling and a fire crackling in the hearth, get ready to embark on a poetic culinary voyage inspired by regional delicacies. Thanks to chefs Kévin Vaubourg and Lucille Routin, the castle boasts a knockout fine dining option. Each dish is carefully thought out and crafted to allow the ingredients to shout their name, depicted by an incredibly delicate tomato or locally reared lamb prepared in two ways and underscored by a chervil jus and olive seasoning. Delightful welcome. Book one of the lovely rooms and stay longer.

Name: Le Panoramic
Address: Glacier de la Grande Motte, Tignes, 73320, France
Description: Accessed by a funicular railway, this high-altitude restaurant (elevation: 3 032m!) promises a breath of fresh air as well as fine dining. In an inviting interior that is done out in wood, staff in traditional costume serve up authentic and delicious wood-fired dishes, including choice cuts of meat and fish to share (eg rib steak, pork shoulder and whole turbot). A delightful change of scene.

Name: Les Enfants Rouges
Description: Once upon a time, a Japanese chef, fresh from his apprenticeship with Yves Camdeborde and Stéphane Jégo, opened a characteristic Parisian bistro, serving heart-warming market-fresh Gallic fare. Duck terrine in aspic paired with plum and cucumber pickles; tempura of line-caught croaker with a seaweed dashi stock, cabbage and broad beans; baba with vintage Martinique rum and chantilly cream… And the icing on the cake, it's open at weekends.

Name: Amarante
Description: This bistro wedged between Bastille and Lyon railway station serves a bighearted, no-nonsense score rich in nostalgic flavours. The ingredients, such as ‘triple zero’ jumbo shrimps from Nantes, Kintoa pork or monkfish caught by small fishing boats, are allowed to shout their name. The interior is equally simple and authentic: tiled floor, red imitation leather benches and wooden tables. Bags of substance and atmosphere!

Name: Towa
Description: Japanese chef Shin Okusa is at the helm of the Towa, close to the bustling Aligre market. A champion of old-school French culinary traditions and a true disciple of Escoffier, he not only whisks up the great classics (French lamb stew, breast of duck in flaky pastry), but also sauces, hot terrines and pies, with superlative skill and flair.

Name: Montée
Description: This is what you get when a talented Japanese chef decides to share his love of French cuisine: graphic presentation of the food and solid technical skill. The stripped-back designer decor adds to the experience.

Name: Le Bistro du Clos
Description: Whether outdoors, in the shade of hackberry trees or indoors, in the bistro dotted with old knickknacks, you will inevitably find yourself surrounded by an enthusiastic crowd of faithful regulars. The chef ticks all the boxes in his open kitchen. A talented craftsman, he curates generous, seasonal dishes from fresh, premium ingredients in a Provençal register that hits the spot every time: chuck beef stew, braised vegetables, fresh tomato vinaigrette or red fruit pannacotta. The establishment is located in the left wing of the Maison des Terroirs, aptly devoted to promoting regional produce.

Name: Bistrotters
Description: A lovely place in the southern reaches of the 14th arrondissement near Métro Plaisance. The Spanish chef carefully selects his ingredients, with a preference for small-scale producers in the Paris region, and instils them with various influences (Asian, Mediterranean etc). Laid-back service.

Name: Au Fil des Saisons
Address: 3 rue de la Libération, Étupes, 25460, France
Description: Stéphane and Fabienne Robinne’s establishment is home to a cleverly refurbished interior, depicted by untreated wooden tables and velvet upholstered chairs… A refreshing modern vibe that provides the backdrop to the chef’s signature recipes oozing in traditional accents.

Name: Auberge des Ruines
Address: 17 place de la Mairie, Jumièges, 76480, France
Description: In this pretty half-timbered house just opposite the ruins of the abbey, a friendly green-fingered chef showcases his passion for the riches of Normandy's terroir. Following the seasons, he fêtes ingredients such as trout, beef and lamb, ciders and Calvados, goat's and cow's cheeses. Everything comes from Normandy, not least the fruit and vegetables picked in the restaurant's kitchen garden – the chef does his own planting. With the greens and pastures of Normandy on his doorstep, he composes the magnificent cheese trolley using produce from neighbouring farms. Savour in an inviting and chic contemporary interior, or in the glass-paned extension giving onto the terrace.

Name: L'Arpège
Description: This pair of Japanese chefs cook lovely creative, Japanese - inflected cuisine, in which broths, seaweed and seasonings show off good - quality ingredients. The interior, in keeping with the presentation on the plates, is elegant and contemporary.

Name: L'Agrume
Description: In the open kitchen of this bistro, the chef delicately crafts refreshingly wholesome dishes, such as poultry in vin jaune paired with asparagus or a piece of roast turbot with mashed potatoes and poultry jus. Flawlessly fresh produce is the name of the game (the fish comes from Brittany and the fruit and vegetables from the very best suppliers). Tasting menu in the evening.

Name: Liza
Address: 14 rue de la Banque, Paris, 75002, France
Description: Originally from Beirut, Liza Asseily gives pride of place to the food of her homeland. In a bright interior strewn with Middle Eastern touches, you can expect mezze to share, grilled meats or fattet batinjan (aubergine, minced lamb and yoghurt). Numerous vegetarian dishes and a fine selection of Lebanese wines.

Name: Auberge du Paradis
Address: 70 route des Crus-du-Beaujolais (Le Plâtre-Durand), Saint-Amour-Bellevue, 71570, France
Description: Two restaurants in one! Chez Lucienne showcases a concise array of creative often spicy dishes to share: free-range chicken kebab marinated in ras-el-hanout; lamb gyoza in herbs and curry, leeks and soy mayonnaise; deep-fried scallops and tikka masala girolles pickles. On the other hand, Joséphine à Table features a wine bar with traditional starters and a dish of the day (marbled ham, pork pie, chicken kebabs, rice pudding). Both establishments boast a pleasant patio and a friendly, buzzy vibe – all of which washed down with tipples from Mâcon and Beaujolais and a range of wines by the glass from a magnum. Fans of Sunday brunch should make a beeline for chez Lucienne.

Name: L'Initial
Description: This Japanese chef with a brilliant track record proposes French cuisine that demonstrates remarkable precision and is made with fine produce (sea bass, scallops, langoustine, morel mushrooms) and represents good value for money. The roast rack of Lozère lamb, celeriac purée, lemon condiment and reduced lamb jus was a stand-out dish. Highly attentive service and a refined and light-filled setting.

Name: Le Mazenay
Description: The emphasis here is on good cooking technique, the right jus and fine produce. There is no unnecessary fuss when you feast on wild snails with herbs or a poached farm-reared chicken. But the chef hankers after just one thing – the start of game season! Roasted Scottish grouse, hare à la royale. A place for bon viveurs.

Name: ERH
Description: The initials E, R and H stand for water, rice and men in French (eau, riz, hommes): a mysterious and poetic name for this unusual place that shares its premises with a sake shop and a whisky bar. The Japanese chef delivers lovely French cuisine that is full of flavour and has a distinctly Japanese feel to it; he also takes some rather original detours in his creations. You might like to opt for food and sake pairings. The remarkable contemporary space has a large glass roof and a long counter that stretches out in front of the open kitchen, where, as in Japan, the chef officiates.

Name: Anicia, table nature
Description: Hailing from the Haute-Loire area, François Gagnaire carefully selects small-scale farmers from the vicinity, kitting himself out with excellent raw material for his cooking. Puy lentils, Limousine des Monts-du-Velay beef, Mézenc fin gras beef, Artisous farmhouse cheese, Vellavia beer… His dishes are both delicious and beautifully presented, making a meal here a real treat; the lunch menu is a real bargain in this neighbourhood. Afternoon tea is served, plus a more fine dining menu in the evening.

Name: Étude
Description: Inspired by his encounters with small-scale producers, chef Keisuke Yamagishi, who hails from the rural province of Nagano, Japan, serves surprise menus based on seasonal ingredients. In a minimalist setting (the overhead lighting is by Serge Mouille), the chef treats us to his creative outlook, his refined vision of plating and his passion for Burgundy wines, in particular.

Name: La Laiterie
Address: 138 avenue de l'Hippodrome, à Lambersart, Lille, 59000, France
Description: Grandson of dairy farmers and son of restaurant owners, chef Édouard Chouteau, who trained with the likes of Pierre Gagnaire, Alain Passard and Christophe Pelé, has settled in this historic cottage, a former dairy farm (yes, really!), next-door to Citadelle Park and a stone’s throw from the banks of the Deûle. The tastefully appointed dining rooms open onto a huge garden and a patio. The perfect foil for the chef’s creative score, which delves freely into produce from Northern France with a fondness for surf and turf recipes.

Name: GrandCœur
Description: Take a seat in the warm, welcoming interior (with exposed beams and stonework, marble table tops and velvet upholstery), or on the pleasant terrace in the picturesque, cobbled courtyard of the Marais Dance Centre. The brainchild of Mauro Colagreco, the pedigree Gallic recipes come with an international, often Italian twist… Examples include stuffed confit of lamb in a provençal sauce, Taggiasche olives and a gutsy gravy – high-flying culinary art!

Name: 24 - Le Restaurant
Description: In a quiet street just a stone's throw from the Champs-Elysées, this establishment offers well-crafted, pedigree Gallic cuisine with an occasional personal spin, such as breast of Dombes duckling, chutney of yellow peaches, pine nuts and duckling jus underscored by mulled wine. Cheerful and professional welcome in a stylish setting.

Name: Méson Chalut
Address: 8 rue de la Corne-de-Cerf, Saint-Malo, 35400, France
Description: In his "méson" (which means "house" in Gallo, the language of Upper Brittany), the chef-owner goes all out Breton, showcasing seafood and other regional ingredients (buckwheat, lait ribot (Breton buttermilk), Coco de Paimpol beans, salted butter) that he sources locally. Freshness, flavour and a respect for nature.

Name: Atelier Maître Albert
Description: An attractive medieval fireplace and roasting spits take pride of place in this handsome interior designed by J.-M. Wilmotte. Guy Savoy signs the menu which boasts a knockout cast of first-class ingredients. T-bone steak, free-range poultry, spit-roasted suckling lamb chops and leg – all that remains is to choose your side dish, for example, gratin dauphinois or purée, both crafted with text-book precision.

Name: Kitchen Ter(re)
Description: In his third establishment devoted to pasta, William Ledeuil crafts a kaleidoscope of pared-back tastes and flavours, starring high-flying creations from spelt, durum wheat, einkorn or tender Roussillon wheat by artisan Roland Feuillas. Chef Julien Jéquier (with stints at Le V and L’Écrin) orchestrates a balanced score in which Asian notes and fresh herbs play major supporting roles. From the exquisitely laid tables to the plating, balance is the key word, as is illustrated by his dish of coquillettes (small pasta shells) made out of fresh milled khorasan wheat flour with chicken wings, Taggiasche olives, spinach and Thai broth! Vibrant, lively and the epitome of charming!

Name: Elmer
Description: Close to République, this terribly chic bistro is officiated by a chef with an impressive career (including L'Oustau de Baumanière, Pierre Gagnaire, travels in Asia and Latin America). He composes a flavoursome menu that packs a punch, with fine meats cooked on embers or on the rotisserie.

Name: À La Biche au Bois
Description: In an atmospheric interior reminiscent of historic Parisian bistros and two minutes from Lyon railway station, regulars and travellers rub shoulders as they dig into traditional no-nonsense nosh. Country terrines, Burgundy snails and Royan ravioles star alongside duck breast in honey, fillet of beef served with cèpes and foie gras or coq au vin (the house specialty), without forgetting game in season (venison and even Scottish grouse!). The crème caramel to finish is wickedly addictive…

Name: Mamagoto
Description: Mamagoto is Japanese for tea party. Seasoned chef Koji Tsuchiya serves an appealing selection of dishes you can share (or not!), combining Japanese and Basque influences – for example, sea urchin with parsley sayon or grilled squid with pesto. The wine list includes some unusual natural wines. A simpler set menu at lunchtime.

Name: Semilla
Description: In a street teeming with restaurants and art galleries, Semilla ("seed" in Spanish) is a bistro with an exceptionally friendly atmosphere and trendy, industrial-style decor. In the kitchen, which opens directly onto the restaurant floor, a young and enthusiastic team work exclusively with fresh, selected produce: sea bream ceviche, leche de tigre, quince confit with hibiscus and kohlrabi; roasted cod, Granville cockles, Roscoff onion, Poiré sauce. Delicious and brilliantly done!

Name: Caffè Stern
Description: On Passage des Panoramas, the historical Graveur Stern engraving workshop has been turned into this smart trattoria, while retaining its period cachet (carvings, photos and original wood panelling). The menu features well-crafted and decidedly original Italian cuisine, served in generous portions: seasonal risotto; dill tagliolini with spider crab, clams and black olive sauce; "Stern" pistachio ice cream. Service with a smile.

Name: L'Atelier Bistrot
Description: This adorable stone house, home to an inviting bistro inn, is five minutes from the peaceful Brittany village of Guéméné-sur-Scorff. This rural idyll is in the capable hands of an enthusiastic young couple who expertly rustles up market-fresh menus that shine the spotlight on small local producers and artisans. Simple, down-to-earth lunchtime menu; more elaborate offering in the evening.

Name: Winstub Arnold
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Dive headlong into Alsace traditions at this winstub featuring numerous elsässische Spezialitäten, including kougelhopf, sauerkraut, black pudding, apple purée, baeckeoffe hotpot or specials such as "Marie Leczinsca vol-au-vent"… Choose a wine from the family estate to accompany your food, then sit back and enjoy in a setting that couldn't be more characteristic of the region.

Name: Les Flots
Address: 52 boulevard de la Mer, Châtelaillon-Plage, 17340, France
Description: This picturesque 19C blue and white house stands on the boulevard that skirts the immense beach. Take a seat in a contemporary dining room overlooking the sea and dig into beautifully presented super-fresh fish and shellfish platters, the establishment’s pride and joy. Guaranteed to find favour with seafood lovers!

Name: Les Terrasses de Clairefontaine
Description: In the heart of the Chevreuse Valley and Rambouillet forest, this restaurant on the edge of Clairefontaine pond serves heart - warming, up - to - date food, with a weakness for truffles and game (in season). Fine view of the pond (all year long).

Name: Le Pierre Scize
Address: Place de la République, Châtillon-sur-Chalaronne, 01400, France
Description: Behind a handsome half-timbered façade in the centre of this picturesque medieval town, this restaurant has a charming interior. Like any self-respecting disciple of Escoffier, the chef prepares delicious regional-style dishes, such as pike quenelles with "Geoffroy sauce", Bresse chicken pot-au-feu, sabodet (pig's head sausage) à la beaujolaise, Dombes carp. Pleasant guestrooms available.

Name: Zorn - La Petite Auberge
Description: Low-temperature poached egg, cream of parsnip, mushrooms and shallots; guinea fowl, cabbage, rosemary jus; jellied strawberries, meringue, strawberry sorbet… The “carte blanche” menu of seasoned chef, Willy-Marc Zorn, at the helm of this eatery near Laon station, highlights market-fresh ingredients. Fine wine list. On the spot every time!

Name: Les Gourmands Disent
Description: In Île St-Laurent's "restaurant street", an enthusiastic double act (Laurent is in charge of savoury dishes, while Nadine handles the desserts) has breathed new life into this engaging eatery. Bare stone walls and high coffered French ceilings set the scene for well-crafted dishes, before perusing the knockout selection of trompe-l’œil desserts, such as the chocolate Montecristo. Do as the regulars do: book well in advance.

Name: Hostellerie de l'Abbaye de la Celle
Address: 10 place du Général-de-Gaulle, La Celle, 83170, France
Description: Near Celle Abbey, this remote fine dining inn occupies a stunning 18C edifice. Part of the Ducasse Group, the restaurant boasts all the facilities one would expect of a luxury establishment, including a finely crafted Mediterranean score with a soft spot for veg, illustrated by stuffed Provençal vegetables overflowing with herbs and garlic. Unostentatious tradition.

Name: Auberge du Prunelli
Description: A cosy, inviting atmosphere reigns in this restaurant that first welcomed guests in 1860 in its former life as a coaching inn. It's been a family affair since 1997, when father André Orlandazzi bought the place – today his sons have taken over the reins. Charcuterie, cheeses and honey from the valley, vegetables from the garden, simple dishes simmered for hours on the stove, tarts made with fruit from the orchard, over 200 Corsican wines... Timeless! In fine weather, you might like to take advantage of the large terrace surrounded by greenery overlooking the Prunelli.

Name: La Garenne
Address: Le Dracy, 4 rue du Pressoir, Dracy-le-Fort, 71640, France
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: An appealing place where you can enjoy, for example, melt-in-the-mouth salmon gravelax with a creamy carrot purée and potato espuma, and, for dessert, chou au craquelin, lemon yuzu mousse and citrus fruit flavours. The low-key decor incorporates some pretty prints of artwork by Alain Thomas, and the veranda overlooks the terrace and grounds. The hotel, meanwhile, boasts pleasant guestrooms, a swimming pool and a spa.

Name: Le Quai 21
Address: 15 quai de la Poissonnerie, Colmar, 68000, France
Description: Head down to the docks of Little Venice for a fine dining experience, courtesy of Le Quai 21 and its expertly prepared contemporary cuisine, eg fillet of German sashi beef accompanied by chanterelles, onions, cherry tomatoes and parmesan. The inviting dining area on the first floor is complemented by a pleasant patio terrace. Chic bistro vibe on the ground floor.

Name: Auberge du Pont de Rethondes
FacilitiesAndServices: Garden or park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: The pretty traditional façade epitomises the charm of this village on the banks of the Aisne. Inside is a modern and refined dining room, perfect for enjoying a meal put together by an imaginative chef with good seasonal ingredients at his disposal. Garden terrace.

Name: La Corniche
Address: 1 chemin di u Fornu (Hameau de Castagneto), San-Martino-di-Lota, 20200, France
Description: A family business clinging to the mountain with a splendid terrace shaded by plane trees overlooking the sea... Exquisite plating, delicious flavours with notes of Corsican saffron and confit of citron, twice-cooked mouth-watering veal or the decadent vacherin dessert perfumed with the one and only Madagascan vanilla, all of which washed down with locally grown vintages.

Name: Les Oliviers
Address: Hôtel Île Rousse, 25 boulevard Louis-Lumière, Bandol, 83150, France
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Great view,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: In Renécros Bay, this posh, stylish, fashionable restaurant commands a breathtaking view of the Mediterranean. Open for dinner (only!), Martin and Fleur craft colourful, flavoursome Mediterranean and Provençal cuisine, presented in several tasting menus, starring ingredients such as green asparagus from Mallemort, line-caught fish direct from local boats, strawberries from Hyères… As you might expect, the vision of the sun gently setting over the glittering horizon is truly spectacular!

Name: Le Carré des Saveurs
Description: In the charming, peaceful setting of this former silkworm farm, surrounded by vineyards and olive groves, dine in the resolutely contemporary interior or on the pleasant terrace in a pretty courtyard. The cuisine draws inspiration from the terroir and tradition to showcase local ingredients: aubergine caviar with extra virgin olive oil; delicious daube provençale (beef stew); pistachio financier and vanilla mousseline. As an added bonus, you can taste the wines and olive oil produced right here on the estate. Spacious contemporary guestrooms and a sense of serenity.

Name: Kapara
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Wheelchair access
Description: In their new venue, Kapara, whose interior is almost identical to that of the former Balagan, Assaf Granit and his partner Tomer Lanzman have called upon chef Zohar Sasson. In a setting depicted by groovy background music and hoots of laughter from the ebullient kitchen brigade, Ms Sasson cheerfully conjures up dishes loosely inspired by Sephardic culinary traditions. The menu rolls out a colourful culinary anthology, boosted by spices, seasonings and chickpeas. Some of the emblematic dishes of the former Balagan remain on the menu, such as “deconstructed” kebab. Festive, friendly and (very) buzzy vibe.

Name: Les Alisiers
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: This lovely panoramic restaurant has a minimalist decor. The food showcases local ingredients but stands out from local dishes by mixing influences and flavours.

Name: Côté Vigne
Description: In this charming village, an imposing 16C half-timbered house. The chef crafts modern dishes, scattered with exotic flavours, such as beef terrine with grated egg and wasabi cream, or grilled squid with leeks, pumpkin gnocchi, mussels and red curry. On the wine side, you will be treated to the organic vintages from the family estate. The terrace is very popular in summertime. Simpler lunch menu.

Name: La Vieille Fontaine - Le Club de Cavalière & Spa
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
