Description: In the Part-Dieu neighbourhood, near Paul Bocuse Market, Olivier and Maryline Delbergues’ establishment rolls out market-fresh recipes with the odd creative twist: tataki of sea trout, sweet-sour red meat radishes, mashed squash, green apple and pecan nuts… Intelligent wine list.

Name: La Maison Carrier
Description: Part of the luxurious Hameau Albert I hotel, this typical farmhouse is home to a friendly restaurant. They serve a beautifully devised seasonal menu – sample the charcuterie that they smoke and dry on site, and take your pick from the legendary and lavish buffet of desserts ("vré de toutes les tartes de la Grand-Mère"), including biscuit de Savoie and blueberry tart. Pleasant terrace.

Name: Le Mas - Alexis Osmont
Address: Chemin de Saint-Blaise (Les Imberts), Gordes, 84220, France
Description: Alexis Osmont’s market-inspired cuisine is as spontaneous as the old farmhouse seems timeless. Let yourself be transported into Alexis’ creative and culinary universe – he cannot be rivalled for his knack for enhancing the treasures of the Vaucluse: asparagus, girolle mushrooms, artichoke…

Name: Auberge de Vigny
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Up - to - the - minute cuisine served in a former classroom that is a treat for the eyes. The lady of the house is also an accomplished pastry chef. Lovely south - facing garden - terrace.

Name: Daniel et Denise Croix-Rousse
Description: Daniel and Denise Croix - Rousse – the third in the series, after locations on rue de Créqui and in the St Jean quarter – is enjoying the same success as its older siblings. Fill up on hearty Lyon cuisine in a traditional bouchon (tavern) setting.

Name: Philip
Address: Chemin de la Fontaine, Fontaine-de-Vaucluse, 84800, France
Description: This restaurant has an incredible location at the foot of the famous fountain from which the Sorgue river springs, and it certainly knows how to play on its bucolic charms. Father and daughter (the house has been in the family since 1926) offer a cuisine that plays the traditional card. Smiling and efficient service. Booking is obligatory in season.

Name: Les Trois Dômes
Address: Sofitel Lyon Bellecour, 20 quai du Docteur-Gailleton, Lyon, 69002, France
Description: In addition to knockout views over the city, the rooftop restaurant of the Sofitel Lyon Bellecour offers pared-down cuisine in a contemporary brasserie vibe (tartare of seabream and langoustine, semi-smoked confit of centre-cut salmon) and the odd new twist to perennial favourites: green lentils, Lyon saucisson, port; pike in brioche, spelt, crayfish.

Name: Anga - Beaulieu
Description: A narrow street of historic Montpellier is home to the characteristic old traditional stone-built edifice that houses chef Cyril Garcia's new restaurant. His aim is clear: to showcase top-notch Mediterranean produce in a pared-back, fuss-free style. Diners have a choice between two set menus, one vegetable-based, the other featuring fish and seafood, and each with three courses at lunchtime and six courses in the evening – and the components change every month. For example, try wild Mediterranean prawn with kale, satay condiment and a gutsy prawn jus.

Name: Les Boulistes
Description: On La Croix-Rousse plateau of Lyon, this restaurant, overlooking a square popular with boules’ players (hence the name), proposes authentic cuisine with a twist and, more recently, jazzed up with a few inspired Mediterranean tributes: Moroccan harira, portokalopita (a Greek, orange-flavoured pastry), etc. Meals are served in the bistro interior or on the al fresco patio, which is taken by storm as soon as the temperatures begin to rise.

Name: La Cour d'Eymet
Description: In a style typical of the region, this house on the town’s main street is flanked by a little courtyard where tables are laid on fine days. Impressive cuisine based on excellent produce. Local wines. A few spacious, smart guestrooms.

Name: Comptoir à Huîtres
Description: Far from the bustle of the seafront, along the quays, this Comptoir is a popular new spot in Dieppe. After you have been presented the catch of the day, with no frills, it is time to make your choice. Which fish? Whole, cut? À la plancha? Unless, that is, you prefer the oyster menu... All as fresh as can be!

Name: La Cuisine du Marché
Description: The old town is a lovely setting for this pleasant restaurant, the name of which sets the tone. Indeed, quality market produce goes into cooking simple and tasty food, peppered with a few Spanish touches. After all, that is where the chef’s origins lie.

Name: La Tour
Address: 7 ter route du Fraisse, Dunières, 43220, France
Description: Local ingredients (Puy green lentils, Grazac snails, free - range guinea fowl etc) are transformed into appetising meals by the chef. The food is good and hearty, as well as carefully prepared. The cheese trolley, which includes lots of cheeses from Auvergne, is an added bonus. It is all very appealing, not least the very well - appointed rooms.

Name: L'Insolite
Description: This establishment is run by a seasoned chef, Gaël Ruscart, whose inventive cuisine gives pride of place to fish and seafood. Grilled prawns in a Béarnaise emulsion, Chinese cabbage salad with peanuts and crunchy vegetables; blue lobster from Brittany's coasts in a creamy emulsion of coral and sweet spices… An institution in this town.

Name: Les Arômes
Description: In this 1930s house basking in the aromas of Provence, unflappable hostess Françoise Besset and her husband Yannick officiate. His innkeeper's soul has not changed and he continues to regale guests with fresh and inventive regional cuisine. Enjoy in one of the charming little dining spaces or, in fine weather, on the terrace on the veranda overlooking the garden planted with olive trees. An exemplary place.

Name: La Table de Jérôme
Address: 26 rue de la République, Luzy, 58170, France
FacilitiesAndServices: Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Wheelchair access
Description: In the walls of the Hôtel du Morvan, chef Jérôme Raymond plays a modern, culinary score based on regional produce. A single set menu, with more upmarket ingredients at the weekend (Charolais beef is a firm favourite). Whopping 400-bin wine list of mainly Burgundy origins. Comfortable rooms should you wish to stay longer.

Name: L'Edulis - Jonathan Datin
Description: The restaurant's tasteful interior nicely offsets the food, which is devised by an enthusiastic and talented chef, the grandson of a baker. Meticulous cuisine, fine regional produce and culinary delights: quite simply, the best restaurant in Granville.

Name: Cazenove
Description: Bronze sculptures and Chesterfield leather seating sets the turn-of-the-19C vibe. In this snug, yet plush ambiance, Best Craftsman of France Pierre Orsi masterfully rustles up smart bistro dishes of classical inspiration. Regularly packed to the seams, so bookings are advisable.

Name: La Maison Haute
Description: Veteran chef Thomas Chegaray (in Basque, the “maison haute” (upper house) is called an “etchegaray”), rustles up modern dishes based on seasonal produce presented in a concise menu. The food is fresh and colourful, with a focus on taste and texture: thick, juicy, tender, farm - reared pork chops, cooked on the bone. Terrace in fine weather and service with a smile.

Name: La Pointe du Cap Coz
Address: 153 avenue de la Pointe, au Cap Coz, Fouesnant, 29170, France
Description: This white cottage seems to sit right on the ocean. The chef has chosen this isolated location to craft delicious cuisine in line with his commitment to local surf and turf produce. The result is beautifully presented dishes, such as slow-cooked pork cheeks in cider vinegar served with cabbage and apples baked in salted butter.

Name: Le Bistro Chapouton
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: The second offshoot of Le Clair de la Plume, the nearby parent establishment, occupies a stunning 18C edifice set in fragrant, flower-decked gardens. Fresh, seasonal produce are the stars of the bistro lineup: homemade terrine of foie gras and Ardèche pork; poultry from the Blaches farm and, to finish, a selection of wickedly appetising home-made pastries. The spacious, covered terrace commands a matchless view of Grignan Castle in the distance and the treelined, walled garden in the foreground.

Name: Les Avisés
Description: You would be well advised to stop off at the Selosse family estate. Both having worked for Anne - Sophie Pic, Stéphane Rossillon (in the kitchen) and his wife (front of house) create a single set menu based on choice ingredients. Served in a charming guesthouse atmosphere; when the sun is out you can enjoy the large terrace. Superb wine list.

Name: Les Vignes et son Jardin
Address: Hôtel Coquillade Provence, Hameau Le Perrotet, Gargas, 84400, France
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: This bistro serves tasty food that is infused with local flair and made with seasonal ingredients. Dine in the wine - tasting cellar in winter and in the garden, among the vines, in summer. All in a hotel that is in itself worth a look!

Name: Le P'tit Bouchon
Description: This small restaurant located between the town centre and the Faïencerie de Gien ceramics museum is a real hub of bistronomy. Tradition is somewhat revisited in a short set menu dictated by the seasons, but the crispy duck confit with its coteaux-du-layon sauce and the chocolate fondant are among the must-tries. Tuck in!

Name: Le Périgord
Description: If you pay a visit to this restaurant covered in Virginia creeper, be sure to try the calf's brains in gribiche sauce. This is one of the house specialities and highly renowned! This place is rustic in the best sense of the word.

Name: Cook'in
Description: This restaurant is where France (the chef) meets Thailand (front of house). The result is fusion cuisine (pan-fried scallops, lentil salad with ginger, red curry shellfish bisque) with a few “unmissables” (“tom yum talay” soup, or wok-fried Dublin Bay prawns with panang curry…). Reasonable prices.

Name: La Sassa
Address: à la tour de Nonza, Nonza, 20217, France
Description: This unusual restaurant, without an inside dining room, nestles at the foot of the watchtower built by Paoli (18C), a veritable crow's nest, perched 160m up, offering an exceptional view over the coast of Cap Corse and Saint Florent bay. The terraces with their many nooks and crannies mean you can enjoy the good, Corsican - accented Mediterranean cuisine with a certain amount of intimacy.

Name: Terra Cotta
Description: This enchanting little restaurant boasts an amazing terrace that unfolds along the quayside of the port. Chef Thomas Duval works with the catch supplied by his fisherman brother, which he brilliantly combines with other ingredients to create dishes throbbing with contrasting flavours. Examples include crunchy wild prawns, panko breadcrumbs, fregola of veggies, herbs, sweet-sour sauce or low-temperature fillet of umbrine in a lemony sauce of capers and parsley with courgette fritters. Consider us smitten!

Name: Au Chamois d'Or
Description: This elegant restaurant is one of the many highlights of the Hotel Chamois d'Or, thanks to its classy, cocooned dining area decked out in wood, and its well-crafted up-to-the-minute cuisine. Inviting lunchtime terrace and a romantic vibe in the evenings.

Name: Le Bistrot à la Mer
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Terrace
Description: In a hotel overlooking the coastal road to Collioure, you will taste tip-top regional produce, assembled in recipes drenched in Mediterranean aromas. The lovely terrace overlooking the sea provides the perfect foil to the splendid menu.

Name: Auberge Le Cabaliros
Description: This pleasant village "inn" halfway between two famous passes – Col d'Aubisque and Col du Tourmalet – stands surrounded by the peaks of the Pyrenees. The menu features wonderful traditional dishes that are big on flavour and nicely presented: noir de Bigorre black pork loin, braised sweetbreads, Pyrenean trout. Pretty little guestrooms available!

Name: Le Viscos
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Welcome to the village of Saint-Savin, which is a vantage point overlooking the Argelès valley and home to this family-run restaurant with a classic, elegant feel. In the kitchen, Alexis (representing the seventh generation of chefs in the family!) treats diners to dishes that are an ode to the terroir, courtesy of local produce enhanced with more modern touches. The desserts, in particular, are fantastic, eg the macaron and nougatine ice cream. Charming guestrooms.

Name: Le Moulin de Poustagnacq
Description: If you like eating by the water, this old mill is the stuff of dreams! The chef prepares fresh ingredients and cooks up traditional cuisine with plenty of appealing regional flair: sole meunière, braised calf sweetbreads with morel sauce, fillet of beef, and chips cooked in goose fat. In fine weather, sit on the terrace overlooking the lake. Bucolic atmosphere guaranteed.

Name: Le Bistrot Gourmand
Description: "Pleasure and tradition" is the motto of this former butchery, where Camille Maître has taken over the family business and is now alone at the helm. The menu is rich in Bresse and Jura ingredients, with distinctive flavours such as quenelle of pike in a creamy lobster bisque. Concise, attractive wine list. Fully deserving of its name!

Name: Didier Méril
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Great view,Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: In a cosy, contemporary interior, enjoying lunch with a magnificent view over the bay of Le Prieuré promises to be a memorable experience. As they drink in the open sea, gourmets will appreciate the creative cuisine of chef-owner Didier Méril. His top-notch seasonal produce comes mainly from the market and local fisheries (Jerusalem artichokes showcased in a variety of textures and shellfish marinière; mackerel, spaghetti squash and a fish head jus finished with butter; pear tartlet with almond crisp, Tonka bean vanilla cream and pear sorbet). Good value for money at lunchtime.

Name: Le Bistrot du Praz
Address: Rue de la Chapelle, Le Praz, Courchevel, 73120, France
Description: This pleasant establishment stands slightly back from the road in the up-market ski resort of Courchevel. In a friendly alpine bistro vibe, you will sample hearty, painstakingly crafted dishes, in tune with today’s palates: carpaccio of scallops, lovage oil and citrus fruit; open raviole of veal and poached egg. Insightful wine-food pairings and a terrace overlooking the lake in fine weather.

Name: Le Dauphin
Description: This place is just the ticket for fans of Normandy's specialities: oysters from the bay of Isigny - sur - Mer, Swiss Normandy pigeon, and Vire andouille sausage. The onus is on ingredients from the region but the chef also knows how to compose more original recipes. Elegant and bright decor.

Name: Argi Eder
Address: 64 argiedereko bidea -  quartier Boxate, Ainhoa, 64250, France
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Piperade egg "revisited"; Axuria cooperative veal with gnocchi and chanterelles; "Argi Eder tart" with caramel, vanilla and yellow lemon – the menu at this spruce rustic-style restaurant comprises fine cuisine with a Basque flavour, devised by a chef with a passion for local produce. Run by the same family for generations and surrounded by greenery, the hotel it is part of is an oasis of calm.

Name: La Table d'Alaïs
Description: Within the medieval walled city, this is your best bet if you want to avoid the tourist traps. Up the stairs, you'll find the pared-back dining area leading onto a courtyard terrace for dining in fine weather. On the menu, traditional and modern go hand in hand: 64-degree egg, truffle and button mushrooms; cassoulet with Castelnaudary beans and duck confit; pavlova with seasonal fruit and vanilla mascarpone cream.

Name: Chocho
Description: After forging his style for 15 years, Franco-American chef Thomas Chisholm has set up home at Chocho. The high-ceilinged, rectangular dining room is bright and buzzy – ideal to sample food devoted to sharing and sustainable gastronomy. Ikejime fish, rows of jars and fermentations and agroforestry ingredients add punch to his creative, even playful approach in a conscious bid to mix influences: roast carrots, garlic emulsion, egg yolk powder or red tuna, Corsican lemon and dashi of smoked beetroot…

Name: La Chaumière
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: This family-run place, a 19C coaching inn, has been in the hands of chef-patron Philippe Arnault since 1992. He is ably assisted by his wife, daughter and, in the kitchen, his son-in-law, Sébastien Provendier (who has previously worked for the Meilleur family and Passedat). Tuck into delights such as trout gravlax with beetroot, buckwheat pancake and horseradish cream, in a pleasant dining room with large bay windows giving onto the inner courtyard. There is a shaded terrace to be enjoyed in fine weather and six guestrooms done out in a modern style inspired by the Sologne region.

Name: Des Petits Pois Sont Rouges
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: No need to be a guest at the Miramont Hotel to enjoy the chef's cuisine. He of course pays homage to Pyrenean culinary heritage but doesn't hesitate to make a few welcome innovations.

Name: La Pinède
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Garden or park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Whether for a relaxed lunch by the beach or dinner beneath the arbour, the intimate and romantic setting is utterly magnificent. The simple and delicious Mediterranean cuisine, courtesy of chefs Pascal Cayeux (for the savoury dishes) and Francis Péan (for desserts), is a celebration of local ingredients. Herbs and vegetables from the 3 000m2 organic kitchen garden are often incorporated. And let's not forget the maturing cellar for cheeses and the enticing wine list.

Name: U Santa Marina
FacilitiesAndServices: Garden or park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: The view of the Gulf of Santa Giulia is superb, and, come evening, the sunset is jaw-dropping. The tasty, personal, inspired culinary score is the handiwork of chef Nikolaz Le Cheviller who oscillates between two proud, untamed lands: Brittany and Corsica, courtesy of handpicked, locally sourced (whenever possible), organic produce: kari gosse, kig-ha-farz, Roscoff onions and fermented milk are intelligently and masterfully blended with brocciu, Corsican olives or oysters from Diana’s lagoon. A flavoursome and delightfully romantic moment.

Name: La Saulire
Address: 16 place du Rocher, Courchevel 1850, Courchevel, 73120, France
Description: An interior decked out in pale wood and decorated with old mountain objects is the authentic and inviting setting in which chef Benoît Redondo cooks up meticulous food: the famous Savoyard fondue rubs shoulders with the Périgord truffle. Please note that the restaurant is closed at lunchtime in good weather, to let skiers enjoy the snowy slopes of the resort.

Name: Le Vieux Four
Description: This warm, rustic restaurant housed in an old farmhouse (1852) delights its guests with its authentic ambience. Admire the figurines nestling in the stable manger, while enjoying delicious cuisine from the Savoie region.

Name: Auberge de la Marine
Description: In a small regional-style building near the docks, this young couple beautifully showcases local ingredients. Example dishes include pressed sea bass with sand carrots, chervil sorbet; fillet of hake, beurre blanc with sea aster, mashed sandy potatoes; baba with a citrus syrup, cream with lemon balm… Tasty and expertly executed cuisine!

Name: La Vallée
FacilitiesAndServices: Great view,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: With its large bay windows, the interior is pleasant, but it is outdone by the irresistible south-facing terrace just beyond the picturesque Bec de la Vallée dock. It's the perfect place to sample fine seafood (charred leeks, cockles from the bay with fresh herbs), as well as classics from Brittany's terroir, eg tranche de lard paysan du pays malouin (salted smoked bacon), far breton (traditional flan-style dessert).

Name: Alchimy
Description: In the heart of the old town, this handsome Art Deco building is home to a contemporary-style brasserie with an attractive glazed roof and an imposing Murano chandelier – a pleasant setting in which to peruse a menu packed with enticing options. Using local produce, the chef puts his own spin on the classics: seared salmon gravlax served with a mushroom salad; a fine cut of Tarn pork; a new version of tarte Tatin with Granny Smith opaline. Pure alchemy!

Name: Autour d'un Cep
Description: This little place, the origins of which date back to some time between the 15C and 16C, stands halfway between the cathedral and the Maine River. Chef Thony Pohu turns out generous and flavoursome cuisine that is in tune with the times and the seasons and has a strong emphasis on plants. The high-quality ingredients are sourced locally, and the suppliers are featured prominently on the menu. The wine list boasts over 300 labels, mostly organic and natural.

Name: L'Essentiel
Description: This handsome redbrick edifice at a crossroads in the hamlet of Petit Attiches is run by an enthusiastic young couple. A stylish, modern interior, a terrace and a pretty garden to the rear set the inviting scene. Carefully crafted, up-to-the-minute dishes are paired with fine wines.

Name: L'Ambrosia
Address: Carrefour la Madeleine, sur D 6113, Pezens, 11170, France
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: On the road to Toulouse, take a break in this modern house: the chef’s preparations are meticulous, coherent and crafted to suit modern tastes, all the more so as he uses premium ingredients: seabass, sweetbread, langoustine… Reasonably priced too.

Name: Le Moulin de Trèbes
Description: This old mill is steeped in charm, illustrated by the terrace directly overlooking the Canal du Midi. The food is simple and modern, with a speciality of caramelised calf sweetbreads with sesame and stewed endives. A real pleasure to be sampled with one of the carefully selected local vintages.

Name: La Récréation
Description: School’s out! In its place, this gently nostalgic establishment has a classroom - style dining room, courtyard terrace and kitchen garden in the old playground. Contemporary cuisine.

Name: Le Lucé
Address: Château du Grand-Lucé, 7 place du Château, Le Grand-Lucé, 72150, France
Description: An 18C palace provides the enchanting location for this restaurant set in a Classical decor of mirrors and chandeliers. When it comes to the food, a savvy approach has been adopted of serving fine dining cuisine based on ingredients sourced from the region and grown in the kitchen garden: white asparagus with wild garlic, a full-bodied vegetable jus, roast asparagus and wild garlic pesto; trout and chard, hazelnut butter sabayon, crispy and wilted chard. And what better way to round off your meal than a post-prandial stroll through the magnificent formal gardens?

Name: Ruche
Address: Domaine les Bruyères, 251 avenue de Neuville, Gambais, 78950, France
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus
Description: On the outskirts of Rambouillet Forest, chef Cybèle, who also runs the Table de Cybèle in Boulogne Billancourt, fell in love with this estate dating from 1850, where she now grows practically everything she cooks according to permaculture methods… Fresh greens thus play a pivotal role, flanked by fermentation techniques and produce from local growers. The bread, butter and yoghurt are all homemade and the wine list is rich in biodynamic and natural vintages. The interior displays a Scandinavian slant and offers five pretty guestrooms for peaceful wellness retreats.

Name: Drum Café
Description: Designed as a landmark and tribute to the Arles region, architect Frank Gehry's Tower for the Luma campus not only draws art lovers but is also a beacon for foodies. The undeniably trendy venue boasts impressively high ceilings and a huge stainless-steel bar in the centre. All the furniture and materials were designed using recycled materials and natural resources, such as merino wool from Arles. As for the food, contemporary art connoisseurs can sample dishes starring good, fresh local produce (lamb from the Alpilles, rice and oysters from the Camargue etc), crafted generously by resident chefs who don’t hesitate to push culinary boundaries: aubergine glazed with soy and mirin, sesame caviar and chimichurri condiment; tartare of quasi of veal, black garlic aioli, preserved lemon and Romaine salad; riz au lait, salted butter caramel and caramelised hazelnuts... The predominantly organic wine list shines a spotlight on small wine estates.

Name: Oma
Description: The minimalist decor (waxed concrete floors, Scandinavian furniture and designer pendant lights) suggests the food is the main focus here. The menu varies according to season and inspiration: smashed avocado, gravlax salmon and orange vinaigrette; roast veal fillet, potato and artichoke fricassee; raspberry compote, crumble, mint and lemon sorbet. Very reasonably priced menu-carte.

Name: Le Channel
Address: 3 boulevard de la Résistance, Calais, 62100, France
Description: This is a pleasant spot to eat before crossing the Channel. It has an elegant decor, classic cuisine, seafood, and a fine wine list (cellar opens onto restaurant).

Name: Les Caudalies
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: At the helm of this stylish bourgeois establishment is an inspired sommelier, Best Craftsman of France, Philippe Troussard. His immense talent and the sheer scope of his wine list (over 1,000 references) raise the concept of food-wine pairing to an art form. The well-crafted recipes are the work of a skilful chef. The terrace enjoys a sweeping view of the grounds, the River Cuisance and the legendary Arbois vineyards.

Name: La Table de la Caillère
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Idyllically located for anyone touring the châteaux of the Loire, this inn, firmly in the zeitgeist, is run by an enterprising couple who work together in a bucolic setting of forests and meadows. The original 18C farmhouse has been replaced by a modern building, which reflects the chef's culinary ethos that favours local produce (girolle mushrooms, regional veggies, honey, Racan pigeon, Touraine pork, etc.), but also his homeland, Brittany, illustrated by a wafer-thin tart of spider crab covered in a warm mayonnaise flavoured with sea urchin roe. Each legible dish is a masterclass of exquisite plating and crisp forthright flavours.

Name: Domaine du Châtelard
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: In this lovely "country house" the chef chooses his ingredients well. He cooks fresh and fine cuisine for the modern palate, and some dishes having interesting Italian influences. Lunch on the terrace with a view over the lake is not to be missed.

Name: Le Mas de Peint
Address: Le Mas de Peint, route de Salin de Giraud (D36), Le Sambuc, 13200, France
Description: Using good ingredients and vegetables from the kitchen garden, the chef creates lovely dishes that put a new spin on the old classics (bull beef gravlax, gazpacho made with old tomato varieties, etc). The ravishing terrace beneath the wisteria and the charm of the setting make this a great choice.

Name: L'Aubinière
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Wheelchair access
Description: This attractive, contemporary dining space basks in the light of the windows that open out onto the wooded parkland. The seasonal cuisine never compromises on the quality of the ingredients (Richelieu asparagus, Mouliherne escargots, line-cut meagre etc) and the cellar is packed with regional wines: L'Aubinière restaurant has it all. There are also a number of elegant guestrooms, plus a wellness area.

Name: La Table du Sommelier
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: A father-and-son team of trained sommeliers work in tandem in this pleasant contemporary bistro. The result is flavoursome, indulgent wine-based dishes that put a skilful new spin on the offerings of the local terroir, such as the fillet of blue ling with parsley, wild rice and sesame oil, or the raspberry and vanilla in sablé and mousse forms. The cellar boasts almost 500 wines, and in summer there are two terraces to choose from: beneath the pergola or in the open air. Highly recommended and excellent value for money.

Name: L'Atelier de Nicolas
Description: This restaurant, bang in the historic heart with a wrought iron and glass front door, is where chef Nicolas rolls out a modern line-up, with the odd Asian twist picked up during his forays to Thailand. Examples include Tom Kha Kung (spicy soup) of shrimp and coconut milk or a Wellington-style Kushikatsu of Camargue bull. Each Asian-sounding, fresh, aromatic dish comes with lashings of reassuring explanations! The chef works with local organic producers and breeders whenever possible and the concise wine list demonstrates a distinct fondness for natural tipples.

Name: Le Bouchon du Vaugueux
Description: Behind a simple exterior is this bistro with the soul of a true bouchon lyonnais (counter, cheek - to - jowl dining). That said, the chef does not limit himself to tradition and adorns his dishes with more modern ideas. Nice selection of wines from producers.

Name: Brasserie à 4 Temps
Description: A modern brasserie complete with a shady terrace, where you can enjoy classics that have been given a new spin by Franck Putelat's former sous-chef. Devilled eggs and leek vinaigrette, beef tartare, cassoulet… absolutely delicious. Book ahead to secure your table.

Name: Le Pêché Gourmand
Description: A restaurant on the banks of the Guisane, run by a young French-Australian couple who are smitten with gastronomy. Sharon creates the lovely seasonal food including pastries, and Jimmy takes care of diners and the wine. Friendly, professional service.

Name: Bvañ
Description: Chef Romain Le Cordroch has travelled extensively, across continents (China, Australia, Brazil) and from one fine restaurant to another (Atelier de Rabanel, Atelier Robuchon, Violon d'Ingres). Now returning to his roots, he has established a natural style of plant- and fish-based cuisine. He lets nothing go to waste – everything is transformed. For instance, his gomasio is made from fish scales warmed in the oven! His dishes always demonstrate his know-how, eg mussels marinière, Armenian cucumber with verbena and a gwell (Breton fermented milk) foam.

Name: Chez Francis
Description: Chez Francis has the perfect family - run bistro atmosphere with its old - fashioned poster adverts, all manner of bric - a - brac and messages left by clients. You come here as a friend and are made to feel at ease as you sample the quality ingredients woven into lovely recipes: crab remoulade, Jerusalem artichoke and green apple, wok sautéed squid served with Languedoc wines!

Name: Le Cairn
Description: On the road to the mountain resorts of the Aravis range, between La Clusaz and Le Grand Bornand, this small mountain chalet needs to be marked with a pile of stones, like a cairn! In the small, inviting space done out in mountain style, there is no doubt about it: chef Adrien and maître d' Charline (all smiles) know how to delight their faithful guests. Adrien creates astonishing dishes that are full of flavour and beautifully fresh: the cold lettuce soup with cream of country bacon is a tasty sensation; tender medallions of farm-reared lamb served rare...

Name: Aquar'aile
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Great view,Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Wheelchair access
Description: This pleasant top-floor restaurant boasts a peerless panoramic view over the Strait of Dover and the English coast… it is like something you would expect to see in a painting! The food showcases locally caught fish: lobster casserole, sea bass in a salt crust, sole meunière. To be washed down with a good wine chosen from a list carefully curated by the proprietor.

Name: Breizh Café Cancale
Description: On the port of Cancale, Breizh Café has one motto: "A new take on crêpes." After all, the concept was originally born in Japan! The owner, Bertrand Larcher, was the first to export Brittany's galettes (buckwheat pancakes) to Tokyo, and several Japanese restaurants later, he has founded one back home. The produce is organic (eggs, cheese, meat) and first rate. The crispy flavoursome galettes and wafer-thin, soft pancakes are made entirely traditionally. The filling depends on your mood, ranging from classical to unusual: artichoke rolls, scrambled egg, Comté cheese or Saint Malo wakame seaweed. The upstairs window commands a splendid view of Cancale port. Something of a local landmark, it is often fully booked.

Name: Auberge de l'Île Enchantée
Description: This former fishermen’s bar enjoys a verdant setting practically on the banks of the Orne. In keeping with the house traditions, the chef revamps hearty, wholesome recipes that keep pace with the seasons. Searingly good food!

Name: Les Deux Canailles
Description: Les Deux Canailles are two energetic business partners who have brought together a young, disciplined and passionate Franco - Japanese team. Fresh modern French cuisine prepared with finesse and with a few Japanese touches.

Name: Le Grand Bleu
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: The chef, Matthieu Colin, puts the experience he gained in Michelin-starred establishments to good use. In a lovely contemporary interior, he continues to pay tribute to local fishing, but also brings local produce into creative dishes that thrive on originality: cod with seafood condiments, grapefruit, crozets, spiced fennel. Friendly and efficient service.

Name: Les Passantes
Description: When strolling down the main street of Houlgate, you will pass this spruce, slate-roofed villa. In a contemporary, cheerful interior depicted by wood and stone, local lad Maxime Lehoucq has grown into a talented chef. He works with seasonal Normandy ingredients (veal, free-range eggs and cream) together with fish supplied by his fisherman brother from Trouville. Maxime’s bistronomic signature and the occasional exotic note do the rest: flame grilled mackerel, beetroot and seaweed mayonnaise; Prieuré leg of poultry, gnocchi, creamy mushrooms, Comté cheese and hazelnuts. The menu, which changes monthly, is served by a cheerful young team eager to please. Consider us smitten!

Name: Blue Flamingo
Description: All hands on deck! Made entirely out of glass, steel wood and aluminium, this floating restaurant, akin to a 21C barge, is anchored on the banks of André Malraux Presqu’île. Flooded in light, the waterside dining room commands a view of the kitchen to the rear. The rooftop terrace sports a delightful riverside café vibe. Chef Benoit Migeon, former sous-chef of the Crocodile, rustles up recipes rich in international flavours and steeped in fresh, vibrant ingredients, such as semi-cooked tuna, watermelon, chimichurri and feta.

Name: Vivant
Description: In a dining room as fresh as a spring morning, the former owners of the Moulin du Ponceau (Chartres), for whom sourcing locally is deep in their DNA, wanted to get closer to nature and to their producers. The chef crafts dishes in the zeitgeist with a weakness for seafood and veggies, depicted by hake from the coast and multiple versions of cabbage. Fermentation is a prominent feature of his cooking.

Name: Vent Debout - Hôtel Les Hautes Mers
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Just imagine: the Île d'Yeu, a pretty little hotel overlooking the sea, a chic, laid-back restaurant, a terrace and a dining area decorated with models of old sailing ships... All in all, a truly charming spot for food lovers who can expect a deliciously fishy regional menu.

Name: Le Constance - Abbaye de Villeneuve
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Wheelchair access
Description: The brasserie of this hotel that has been tastefully refurbished from top to bottom, is set up in a space that is flooded with light through a beautiful glass roof and bay windows overlooking the swimming pool and grounds. The chef presents a menu that combines traditional dishes (e.g. pâté en croûte, egg mayonnaise, fish with beurre blanc sauce, Loire fish quenelle with crayfish bisque) with more modern recipes. We also like the attractive wine list with (very) reasonable prices, especially for the wines from the region.

Name: Auberge du Château
Description: Christèle and Xavier Vanheule are passionate about food and wine, and put their all into making this Auberge a wonderful establishment. The produce they source from surrounding farms is bursting with freshness. While contemplating the peaks of the Monts du Lyonnais, you can enjoy dishes with robust flavours, including filet of Dombes duckling, split pea purée, grilled pork belly etc.

Name: L'Espérance - Stéphane Carbone
Description: Treat yourself to a bucolic gourmet getaway a stone's throw from Caen, in Stéphane Carbone's terracotta-coloured establishment. The chef, well known to locals, serves traditional dishes with a modern twist, for example knuckle end of lamb, bulgur risotto with turmeric and turnip roasted with sweet tonka pepper. Each table commands a lovely view of the canal.

Name: Auberge de Bel Air
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: This granite-built farmhouse on the banks of the Aber Ildut cuts a picturesque figure with its large garden and lake. On the menu: the fish and seafood cuisine for which Brittany is so famed, eg fillet of pollack with lobster cream. A rustic setting in which to really unwind.

Name: Le Baligan
Description: Fishing rods, lithographs, and frescoes set the maritime scene in this bistro. Flawlessly fresh fish from the local fish auction and knockout seafood platters (oysters and scallops) take the limelight on the table. The fish of the day, in our case sole and turbot, is sold by the kilogramme – to the delight of our appetites and wallets!

Name: Stéphane Carbone
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Wheelchair access
Description: Just a stone's throw from the marina, in the bustling hub of Caen life, chef Stéphane Carbone explores France's terroirs, from Normandy and the Lyonnais to Bresse (where he grew up and learned to cook) to his parents' and grandparents' native Calabria. Using the freshest ingredients, he serves modern cuisine with a dash of creativity, proceeding according to the mood on any given day. Signature dishes are available à la carte, including the heart sweetbread cooked in a sauté pan or the Caribbean chocolate shell with a hot chocolate velouté… To be enjoyed in the contemporary dining area, from which you can watch the activity in the kitchen from behind a large picture window. A lobster set menu and cookery class every Saturday morning.

Name: Hostellerie Les Gorges de Pennafort
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: The restaurant has an elegant, contemporary decor and a terrace beneath the plane trees. The setting is enticing, and the food even more so. Flowers, spices, herbs and the chef's personal touches bring together tradition and generosity.

Name: La Maison des Blés - Le Bouche à Oreille
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: A contemporary place with a modern interior, with two ears of wheat emblazoned on the walls in homage to the surrounding countryside, and two eateries where you can indulge yourself: Brasserie Louis (knuckle joint of lamb, seasonal vegetables etc) and the gourmet restaurant, Bouche à Oreille. Professionalism and dishes that showcase top-notch ingredients every time.

Name: Les Flots
Address: 1 rue de la Chaîne, La Rochelle, 17000, France
Description: This restaurant in a converted 18C estaminet boasts an ideal location on the port of La Rochelle, and has a delightful terrace at the foot of the Tour de la Chaîne. They serve refined cuisine in which the flavours of the ocean enjoy the limelight, for example, "lobster stew with glazed seasonal vegetables, mushroom ravioli with lobster roe, a jus made from lobster juices and an inkling of ginger", chef Grégory Coutanceau's signature dish.

Name: La Vieille Auberge
Description: Splendid high vaulted timber ceilings and huge floor-to-ceiling windows reminiscent of a conservatory overlooking the garden: the scene is set in this well-known culinary landmark. Matthijs Bartman rolls out modern, enticing dishes illustrated by pastrami of bazadais beef, smoked beetroot and blueberries or a more classical choux pastry stuffed with tonka bean diplomat crème, yuzu caramel and mango sorbet… A traditional lineup with a modern twist, presented in two eater-friendly priced menus. Enthusiastic and delightful front of house team.

Name: Kashiwa
Description: Don't be fooled by the sign: this small Japanese restaurant (kashiwa means "oak leaf") housed in a former tapestry - maker's workship, offers a lovely array of Japanese dishes (sushi, sashimi, soba etc). Small terrace, and prime location close to the Musée Pierre Bonnard. A pleasant place.

Name: Bonhomme
Description: The trio who founded this lively bistro in the Faubourg Poissonnière are certainly not short on bonhomie! In this trendy, distressed decor (hand-scraped walls, marble-topped pedestal tables, glass-paned cellar), the chef has savvily set about creating tasty bistronomy fare without falling for faddish effects: breaded pork croquettes, red onion and chilli chutney; seared mackerel, braised pencil leek, sorrel; dark chocolate mousse, caramel, chocolate crumble... Great atmosphere guaranteed.

Name: Maison Nipa
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Wheelchair access
Description: This restaurant, opened by an experienced Franco-Philippine couple (Jason is in charge of savoury dishes, while Sharon rustles up desserts), specialises in Gallic cuisine influenced by the flavours and aromas of the Philippine archipelago. The food takes you on a culinary tour from Sarthe to the Philippines, depicted by Croisic squid à la “Adobong Pusit”, stuffed with a sisig of bellota chorizo and coated in a subtle cuttlefish ink sauce or wild duck with coffee-flavoured ceps and an “Adobo” sauce, together with other delicately perfumed dishes that might feature sweet-savoury or surf-turf notes. The roof may not be covered in palm leaves (meaning of nipa), but the modern dining room which cleverly mixes materials, is delightful, as is the seamless service.

Name: Le Clos du Château
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Adjacent to the Château de Proméry, this imposing contemporary building has been run for 17 years by Pascal Avertis, who hails from the village. The chef is equally at ease with traditional recipes (braised chuck with an excellent Mondeuse sauce, potato croquettes to dip in a delicious home-made ketchup) as he is with more modern and creative creations, such as leek and nori maki with Thai vinaigrette and smoked caviar – absolutely delicious! To be savoured on the pleasant terrace, in the shade of the plane trees.

Name: Cavalieri
Description: Between Place du Trocadéro and la Muette, this smart, contemporary venue offers another spin on timeless Italian classics: aubergine parmigiana, fritto misto, a smoked version of vitello tonnato, linguine alle vongole... The interior sports Sicilian walnut furnishings, two-tone Italian marble and hand-painted tableware reminiscent of the Amalfi coast.

Name: Relief
Description: Slap-bang in the middle of the Saint Esprit neighbourhood, Thibault Deverre is at the helm of this bistro that cultivates a nostalgic vibe with rustic furnishings and rush straw-upholstered seats. The chef prepares fresh, spontaneous, multi-dimensional dishes with finesse and originality, eg crabmeat, asparagus ice-cream and grapefruit tempura; red tuna, creamy polenta, smoked aubergine caviar, crisp red cabbage salad; white chocolate cream, gariguette strawberry and sorbet. A resounding success, especially with Bayonne's young foodies!

Name: La Grande Salle
Address: Hôtel de France, place de la Libération, Auch, 32000, France
Description: Revamped from top to toe, this city-centre institution is still going strong under the aegis of a family team, namely three brothers – one in the dining room (an MOF), one in the kitchen and one is a pastry chef! The culinary lineup aims to highlight the gastronomic heritage of the Gers region: raw and cooked scallops; Bigorre black pork and leeks; duck and foie gras pie, sliced at the table; baked Alaska, flambéed in front of you! Foodies with an appetite will be delighted to learn that the sauce boats are left on the table – irresistible with the house made bread! Simpler fare at Le 9ème brasserie.

Name: La Table de Mentone
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Chef Sébastien Sanjou pops in from down the road (the Relais des Moines at Arcs-sur-Argens) to supervise the cooking of this luxuriously appointed restaurant in the cellar of one of the finest winegrowing estates of the Var. As guests savour the superlative setting (a panoramic landscape of vineyards and olive groves outdoors and a designer-inspired interior), they dig into fine seasonal provençal cuisine which makes the most of the estate’s wide range of produce (chicken coop, orchard, cottage garden, olive groves), illustrated by a tartare of cucumber and fennel with fresh herbs; Mediterranean skipjack, crunchy salad of quinoa and courgette spaghetti. The food is naturally washed down with one of the estate’s fine organic vintages. A few guestrooms and holiday cottages are available to prolong your stay in style.

Name: Jeanne-Aimée
Description: Bingo for this semi-industrial, semi-cosy bistro alongside Notre Dame de Lorette Church, where two mates tick all the boxes to regale us. On one side, Dan Humphris (who also runs a nearby bakery-grocery store where he sells organic produce from his father’s farm in the Yvelines) and on the other, youthful Sylvain Parisot, with stints in star-studded establishments (l’Astrance and La Marine with Alexandre Couillon) under his belt. Conclusion? First class ingredients (Gascony pork chops, Landes poultry), daring ideas (oysters and camembert ice cream), generosity, sensible prices and spot-on, friendly service.

Name: Comète
Address: 35 rue de la Grève, Saint-Lunaire, 35800, France
Description: Comète is in the centre of the seaside resort, near the beach. Each dish by chef Victor Nicolas is a reminder of his Michelin-starred career in Paris and, more particularly, his time working for Christophe Pelé: the dishes are on the creative side, the ingredients top-notch, the no-frills preparations don't mess around, the sauces are elegant and the condiments punchy. For example, spider crab, fennel and strawberries; roast brill, potatoes, chard and meunière sauce. The decoration of this small old-school bistro (old pine floorboards, salvaged and mismatched furniture, vintage-style light fittings) does the rest.

Name: Le Comptoir du Relais
Description: Yves Camdeborde has entrusted the keys of his famous diminutive bistro to chef Bruno Doucet, whom he had already put in charge of La Régalade. Suffice to say, on his watch the place's bistronomy philosophy is scrupulously adhered to. In the tiny restaurant with tightly packed tables or on the heated terrace looking onto the Carrefour de l'Odéon, you can enjoy a menu (served right through from noon to 11pm, which is rare) that embraces local and market cuisine, and absolutely respects quality produce. They do not take reservations.

Name: Tekés
Description: One of the establishments owned by chef Assaf Granit, Tekés is summed up by its name, which is Hebrew for "ceremony". More than a restaurant, it's also a veritable musical extravaganza. The kitchen team puts on a thrilling show, cooking vegetables over an open fire, while the well-drilled waitstaff stand by, ready to spring into action. Flame-grilled leeks with potato and feta purée, fattoush salad with labneh and za'atar, fried gnocchi with yellow curry and yoghurt – just some of the delicious dishes on offer! This culinary journey taking in Levantine tradition and influences from the Middle East embraces intense flavours and carefully selected spices. The options on the mainly vegetarian (although not vegan) menu take the form of dishes to share – which is very much in keeping with the convivial atmosphere!

Name: Couvert de Vignes
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: The village of Chigny-les-Roses in the heart of the Montagne de Reims is the site of this restaurant in a former classroom, which is, indeed, entirely hemmed in by vineyards. Chef Benjamin Gilles can be seen in the kitchen through a window in the dining room. Now his own boss, he signs modern dishes overflowing in fresh flavours and enhanced by a zest of creativity. Vegetables and fruit feature prominently in his culinary score through a variety of preparations (raw, cooked, pickled).

Name: Sépia
Description: Lucie Berthier Gembara, riding high from her appearance on France's Top Chef TV competition, often has a full house at her trendy designer bistro on the ground floor of this fine 18C building. After stints working with Gérald Passedat and Alexandre Mazzia, she has retained a clear sense of creativity and an appetite for the Eastern influences of the Mediterranean basin. Her dishes, such as aubergines with charred baba ganoush, eggnog and feta crumble, are full of pleasant surprises. They are distinctly playful, going against the grain when it comes to the codes of gastronomy but no less tasty for it. The lighter lunchtime menu is expanded in the evening.

Name: Alebrije
Description: After training at the Paul Bocuse Institute and a number of noteworthy spells in top establishments, such as Troisgros, youthful Carla Kirsch, who hails from Veracruz in Mexico, has settled in the Croix-Rousse district. The signature here is clearly Mexican from the décor, which features old rafters with splashes of colour, to the food, which Carla joyfully crafts using top-notch seasonal ingredients (sweet corn in the starter and chili peppers in the dessert). The menu changes monthly and the beverages include a few Mexican wines as well as tequilas and mezcals.

Name: Osma
Description: "Osmazôme is a term popularised by the gastronome Brillat-Savarin to define the principle of the sapidity of game in broths," explains Valentin Barbera. Having worked at Le Lièvre Gourmand in Orléans and Christian Têtedoie in Lyon, this young chef nevertheless elected to set up his trendy "table de copains" – a place for friends to eat together – in an out-of-the-way village in the bocage landscape of the Perche region. The tables, lit by a cascade of pretty designer wall lights, are made from salvaged railway carriage floors. The on-point dishes are made using only local ingredients, or as good as: lentils, pumpkin, wood sorrel; egg, potatoes, pike eggs; turnip, eel. All of the wines are natural.

Name: Finestra by Italo Bassi
Description: Among the traditional shopfronts, this elegant façade stands out from the crowd on Bonifacio harbour. On the first floor, this superb designer space mimicking the shape of the inverted hull of a ship, with a subtle maritime-inspired decor, features a large window (finestra in Italian) overlooking the port. Chef Italo Bassi, who presides also over the kitchens of his restaurant in Sardinia, has devised a menu that allies the cuisines of Italy and Corsica. The mainly local ingredients are handpicked in these masterfully prepared dishes – the double ravioli with two fillings, burrata, guinea fowl casserole and its reduction, light cream of parmesan and fresh thyme is a particularly appetising signature dish!

Name: Acte 2
Address: 3 rue de la Petite-Calade, Avignon, 84000, France
Description: In the city of the famous arts festival, theatre is even part of the restaurant experience. Act I: a young couple of industry professionals set up shop in the historical centre. Act II: dishes that are packed with delicious, fresh local and seasonal ingredients. Act III: excellent value for money, whether you opt for the five-course dinner or the three-course lunch. The scene is set! Tuck into scallop carpaccio and turnip with lemon and juniper, or the veal fillet with truffle and Albufera sauce.

Name: Petit Jacques
Description: As you make your way up through the pretty paved streets of Grimaud to this enchanting leafy patio, you are already bewitched. Spread over two floors, the charm of this house is undeniable (light wooden floors, raftered ceilings, lime plastered walls, well-worn bench seating and soft lighting). The Quebec-born chef and his partner in charge of the front of house regale diners with spot-on market-fresh cuisine and a traditional culinary line-up, featuring family favourites like onion soup or French toast (of brioche) with a scoop of Madagascan vanilla ice cream to die for! Everything is made in house, including the bread!

Name: L'Argousier
FacilitiesAndServices: Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: In this pleasant contemporary restaurant, the young chef’s cuisine varies with the seasons. The food is cooked and seasoned to perfection, the presentation flawless, as in this duck fillet with confit vegetables and red wine jus. Friendly and attentive service and a fine selection of vintage rums.

Name: Frédéric Carrion Cuisine Hôtel
Description: The elegant dining room combines the character of this former coaching inn (parquet, fireplace) with more plush and cosy touches. The chef uses fine regional produce to concoct wonderfully creative dishes. Your meal is accompanied by a delightful selection of wines, including a range of Viré - Clessé wines. The pleasant rooms and spa round off your stay in wine - growing country.

Name: L'Orangerie
Address: La Bastide de Gordes, 61 rue de la Combe, Gordes, 84220, France
Description: This famous village is one of the most prized in the Luberon Regional Nature Park. This stately home, which dominates the valley, now houses a luxury hotel – as well as this restaurant and its stunning terrace shaded by chestnut trees. In the style of a luxury brasserie, the menu gives some of the classics a Provençal twist: think gambero rosso with grapefruit, sole meunière and dauphinoise potatoes with lemon, or fillet of lamb with white asparagus.

Name: La Grange
Description: In this city centre restaurant, old stones blend seamlessly with contemporary decoration. On the menu: market - fresh ingredients and a handful of bistro specialities with Basque overtones. In summer, make the most of the terrace beneath the arcades, on the banks of the Nive.

Name: Le Seize
Description: This small Provençal bistro nestling in the old town of Arles ticks all the boxes, with its decor of burnt sienna and cream tones and wrought-iron tables. Sarah and Julien Richard have hit upon a winning formula right off the bat, serving dishes such as tomato confit with vanilla oil and lime, and courgette and basil velouté; thinly sliced monkfish with seaweed butter, Camargue rice with fennel, and a fish soup jus. The chef uses aromatic herbs and flowers from his kitchen garden to enhance his dishes. The lunch menu is excellent value for money; more extravagant tasting menu on Thursday and Friday evenings; brunch on Sundays. A small selection of regional wines.

Name: Le Bistrot de la Caillère
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Ideally located for anyone visiting the châteaux of the Loire, this inn is firmly rooted in its era. It is run by an enterprising couple, who work and live in harmony with the bucolic landscape of forests and meadows. The original 18C farmhouse has been replaced by a modern building – modern like chef Éric Rialland's cuisine. His well-thought-out bistronomy dishes follow the seasons and oscillate between creativity and tradition. Pleasant terrace for fine weather.

Name: Utopie
Description: In the heart of a small wine-growing village, this Utopia is being nurtured by a couple we first met in Strasbourg. Now installed in this handsome old edifice enhanced by contemporary fixtures and fittings, the experienced chef (George V, Pierre Gagnaire, Jean Imbert…) crafts a set menu in several courses in which vegetables take the limelight: green peas, sorrel, hemp oil; romaine lettuce, tarragon, black garlic and meat jus. Insightful wine-food pairings.

Name: L'Escudella
Description: L'Escudella is, aptly enough, "plate" in Occitan! Paul-Arthur Berlan, the young chef, has worked in some prestigious establishments (Michel Sarran, Yannick Alléno). Here, he marries produce from the terroir of the Greater Paris area with the flavours of Languedoc. With fresh, high-quality ingredients and well-crafted dishes, he hits the mark.

Name: Le Lien
Description: The bond here (‘lien’ in French) is that which ties this young couple (he’s in the kitchen, she in the front of house) to the winegrowers and producers whose work is showcased in the plates and glasses of this friendly bistro. Modern food with a creative twist founded on first-class seasonal ingredients that are allowed to shout their name. Two lunchtime menus and a more elaborate offering in the evening. Highly recommended.

Name: Séquence
Description: Chef Antoine Triquet may have an unusual career path (which led him from insurance to cooking), but the culinary fundamentals are present and correct! Ingredients are carefully selected to put the spotlight on local producers, nature and the seasons, and the cooking is always on point... This is modern, clear and uncluttered cuisine with a sincere, even generous approach! At dinnertime, the set menu is divided into three sequences, each featuring a given ingredient prepared in three different ways, which allows them to use the ingredient in its entirety. For example, veal: veal croquette, vitello sardinia, or standing rump served medium rare, accompanied by an onion purée and a delicious gravy. To be enjoyed in a contemporary decor with an open kitchen.

Name: Regain
Description: Near the Saône embankment, a youthful team crafts appetising market-fresh fare (tempura of white tuna, aubergines, blackberries; veal cutlet and sweetbread from Clavisy farm, samphire, potatoes and white butter; figs and goat’s milk). The lunchtime menu offers a concise choice of dishes, while more extensive tasting menus are available in the evening. The interior sports an artfully distressed industrial vibe.

Name: Cascade
Address: 26 cour de la Filature, Salles-la-Source, 12330, France
Description: What a pretty village clinging to a cliff and famous for its cooling waterfall! What a pleasant, convivial place, with its warm, colourful bistro decor, lovely old wooden floorboards, counter and arty posters on the walls (and let's not forget the terrace overlooking the courtyard in front of the town hall). In the kitchen, chef Marine Guichou cooks up a feast, using carefully selected local produce, which she skilfully prepares in a fresh, authentic bistro style. And with her almond pannacotta and chocolate mousse on a cocoa crumble, she has created the quintessential dessert for anyone with a sweet tooth!

Name: Ro'cha
Description: The philosophy of seasoned chef Jean-Luc Rocha (who has captained many Michelin-starred restaurants) is that one experienced chef is worth two – especially one who has been a Meilleur Ouvrier de France since 2007. On every plate, you can sense the work of a wise and accomplished chef who masters all the tricks of his trade without ostentation; this certainly applies to his crispy "croque juste croustillant" with a poultry stuffing and herbs – a masterclass in finesse. From start to finish, the cooking and seasoning are deftly executed, a case in point being the lovely rare-cooked saddle of veal accompanied by seasonal vegetables glazed with butter and a meat jus. Professional service in the refined setting of a townhouse.

Name: Goxoki
Description: Goxoki means an "inviting place" in Basque, which is perfectly suited to this restaurant run by the Hourcastagnou family in the Petit Bayonne neighbourhood. In a timelessly elegant setting, the food shines a spotlight on local seasonal produce, with a mouth-watering game menu including fillet of wood pigeon and pithiviers of the legs, hare à la royale and wild turbot with beurre blanc. Regulars come back often to tuck into the indulgent, generous dishes.

Name: Choral
Description: In the Romains district, 10 minutes from the centre, take a seat in this long, Scandinavian-inspired dining room opened by a chef who did a stint at Le Clos des Sens with Laurent Petit, before globe-trotting around the planet. The memory of his line-caught cod, tetragon, lemon and capers à la grenobloise lingers with us still. Alban’s instinctive, fine dining score (free of butter, cream and milk, except for desserts) is, for the most part, dictated by the availability of fresh market produce (such as baked apricots, honey and rhubarb sorbet), which are then given a deft professional spin. Mystery menu in several courses in the evening.

Name: Les Gueules Noires
Address: 66 rue de la Vallée-Coquette, Vouvray, 37210, France
Description: The troglodyte dining room, wood burning fire in winter and the terrace shaded by a wisteria in fine weather are just a few of the discreet appeals of this charming establishment. The cuisine is tasty and wholesome, based on local produce and served with Loire wines. Booking advisable.

Name: Nous Restaurant
Description: With its discreet façade and small glass-paned front door, this restaurant is located in a pedestrianised cobbled street in the city centre. The light-filled interior has bay windows overlooking the street on one side and a pretty courtyard decorated with large window boxes on the other. The chef puts a lot of work into his dishes, which are made using local ingredients. The courgette flower, soufflé with fine pollack stuffing, shellfish sauce vierge, rocket cream and two-lemon fritter is a good illustration of his masterful dishes that are packed with flavour.

Name: Les Toits - Hôtel de Paris Saint-Tropez
Address: 1 traverse de la Gendarmerie, Saint-Tropez, 83990, France
Description: Timeless Saint Tropez remains as legendary as ever – this outdoor restaurant perched on the roof terrace of the fabled hotel is further proof of that. Gazing out over the bay and the tiled roofs of the village, you can savour cuisine inspired by the Mediterranean and Provence, with a few Italian touches thrown in for good measure (Sicilian gambas, tiramisu etc) – after all, the new chef, whose CV includes Il Carpaccio, Le Grand Véfour and Pierro TT in Paris, is Italian. A simpler set menu is proposed at lunchtime.

Name: L'EssenCiel
Description: Chef Jean-Marie Baudic (formerly of the Youpala bistro in St Brieuc) chose this modern eatery to craft a bistronomic repertory with his second chef Julien Rouault. Premium seasonal ingredients and intelligently crafted recipes are the focus: seabream and crunchy veggies; melt-in-the-mouth wing of skate with crunchy diced vegetables and a gutsy jus; shoulder of lamb paired with arancini… Different set menus at lunchtime, in the evening and at weekends.

Name: L'ExtrA
Address: 23 ter rue du Temple, Reims, 51100, France
Description: Opposite Boulingrin covered market (a listed monument), this restaurant is housed in an elegant 1920s Art Deco edifice. The majority of the staff from the kitchen to the front house is mentally impaired, in line with the establishment’s founding ethos to operate as an inclusive business. The kitchen team is managed by a seasoned duo made up of chef Philippe Joly (former second of the Foch) and pastry chef Francois-Xavier Cormarie. In a minimalist, contemporary setting, you can dip into a well-crafted modern menu: espuma of asparagus on a tartlet of Reims ham; skate wing, spelt risotto and nettle jus with a beurre noisette; strawberry pavlova and tartare with a red fruit sorbet. Fine selection of champagne wines.

Name: Gric
Description: Marie Gricourt's career has already taken her to the heights of Christophe Hay's La Table d'à Côté, where she was head chef. She has since opened her own restaurant, a convivial place in keeping with her personality. In this restaurant not far from the banks of the River Loire, the chef and her mainly female team (who provide service with a smile) put a new twist on bistro-style cuisine, simply and precisely: a surf and turf starter with scallops cradled in a sweet potato, bacon and prune purée; conchiglioni stuffed with beef chuck and porcini; and for dessert a delicious floating island with citrus fruit, honey and pollen.

Name: Cadet
Description: Between the Villa Majorelle and the Musée de l'École de Nancy, this restaurant is housed in a hundred-year-old former hairdressing salon. In a Scandinavian-style interior, brightened up by crates of vegetables, a few trendy cookery books and a vintage Faema coffee machine behind the counter, chef Theo Mareschal (previously encountered at La Maison dans le Parc in Nancy and Kontrast in Oslo) sticks to the brief and cooks up appealing contemporary cuisine that's simple and accessible, a case in point being the veal, mushrooms and baby potatoes or the surprising dessert of vanilla ice cream with squid ink, as black as a painting by Pierre Soulages!

Name: Agapes
Description: This is a small neighbourhood bistro that hasn't been revamped for the purposes of Instagram. A young couple with impressive interstellar careers give free rein to their (delicious) inspiration: vitello tonnato, rocket, capers and meticulously seasoned parmesan; excellent duck breast, koshihikari rice, Japanese ume plums, and raw and cooked quetsches, with their bittersweet flavours; and for dessert, a deconstructed Bourdaloue tart that leaves no doubt about pastry chef Arnaud Darbas's credentials. Front of house, cordial, competent Virginie Béziaud has up her sleeve well-chosen wines from small winegrowers served by the glass.

Name: Le Bouillon
Address: 9 rue de la Gare, Annecy, 74000, France
Description: In addition to meaning stock, a bouillon also refers to the first restaurants opened in Paris in the 18C. In a recently refurbished modern interior, the chef crafts tasty market-fresh recipes, with the odd Asian twist, such as a splendid loin of croaker in a chorizo crust underscored by a red curry and curcuma stock.

Name: La Table du Château
Description: The lord of the manor, who now owns this beautiful 17C inn, has entrusted the kitchens to chef Élisabeth Passédat. She may have worked abroad for many years, but she hasn't forgotten her French classics – pan-fried foie gras, pâté en croûte with Houdan poultry, veal sweetbreads, tournedos Rossini-style Charolais beef. She puts a modern spin on these dishes, blending them with seasonal ingredients and drawing inspiration from France's terroirs. In this way, she comes up with creations such as monkfish and spaetzle, Normandy cider velouté, or ravioli with mushrooms, Morbier cheese and a vin jaune emulsion.

Name: Ekume
Description: After clocking up some remarkable experiences, Panamanian chef Edgar Bosquez has dropped anchor in Marseille, not far from the abbey of St Victor. In a spruce, pared-back interior, he showcases fish, seafood and Provençal flavours in a lineup of deftly crafted, suave-tasting menus, including one devoted to bouillabaisse.

Name: L'effet Papilles
Description: In the heart of the town, almost within shouting distance of the castle, this small modern bistro, which sports a workshop vibe of wood and metal, is the brainchild of chef Adrien Barrier, who was born in Le Mans and knows Mayenne inside out. After stints with Yannick Alléno and Philippe Mille, this gifted craftsman curates feel-good, flavoursome food that hits the spot every time, be it his white asparagus with haddock, houmous and hazelnut crumble or the confit of pork belly, pressed aubergine and pork jus.

Name: Lil'Home
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: This attractive restaurant on the Quai des Chartrons has a dining area with parquet flooring made up of repurposed wine crates, velvet-upholstered seats, wicker lampshades and hanging plants – think "chic bistro" style. The modern and creative cooking takes the form of multi-course surprise menus. Good selection of organic and biodynamic wines.

Name: Rouge
Description: Behind the port, in the antique dealer neighbourhood, a disciple of Yves Camdeborde is at the helm of this friendly wine bar. The chef prepares lovely Mediterranean sharing plates, concocted with ultra-fresh produce. It is delicious and hearty, and the wallet doesn't take too heavy a hit. A hundred or so lively wines feature on the list, also at reasonable prices. Open all day from noon (no reservations taken).

Name: Le Roc
Address: 13 vieille route des Pensières, Veyrier-du-Lac, 74290, France
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Garden or park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Tasting menus, an appetising à la carte lineup (perch from Lake Geneva with sorrel and pike roe, poached scallops in helianthus, pithiviers of duck and foie gras), a splendid wine list, a contemporary stylish interior in a chic alpine vein and a youthful team that is always spot on: chef Yoann Conte has covered all the bases in this, his second restaurant, also housed in the famous Maison Bleue. And, as always, the view of Lake Annecy is jaw dropping.

Name: Braise
Description: The former second of Substance, Sylvain Courivaud, is determined to kindle our appetites in this contemporary venue entirely devoted to wood-fired cooking. Whatever the method from Japanese barbecue or Big Green Egg to a smoker, Sylvain combines consummate technique with a love of high-quality produce. The vibe of this trendy eatery is warm and welcoming.

Name: Auberge des Gorges
Description: With its cosy mountain-style decor, this converted 18C coaching inn on the road to the Gorges de la Diosaz is home to a creative restaurant that piqued our curiosity. Over the course of a single multi-course set menu, the young chef cooks up dishes that draw ingredients both from the lakes and the mountains, such as Arctic char with beurre blanc, cooked to perfection, or crayfish ravioli enhanced by a beautifully emulsified bisque. On top of that, the welcome and service are the epitome of charm. Six guestrooms for an extended stay, and view of the summit of Mont Blanc.

Name: Restaurant du Pont
Description: Next to the small Canal de Goulaine, this white building, once a bar and inn, has a refined contemporary interior and pleasant terrace-garden for fine weather. Having plied his trade abroad, chef Mathieu Corbineau now navigates between rather traditional recipes and more contemporary influences: crispy chicken with tandoori spices, carrot, cumin and kumquat sabayon; herb-crusted catch of the day, cereal risotto, citrus butter; gariguette strawberry, yuzu cream, frosted marshmallow gariguette, Montélimar nougat ice cream. An affordable set menu at lunchtime, and a wine list that gives Muscadet top billing.

Name: Auberge du Cheval Blanc
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Wheelchair access
Description: An upscale restaurant, run by the same family since 1785. In the attractive contemporary dining area, meals are paired with fine wines from Alsace, including an interesting selection by the glass. The culinary style is refined, the products of high quality, often locally-sourced, and the presentations elegant. The ambition to treat diners well is clear: you're sure to come out with a spring in your step. Guestrooms.

Name: Maison Renard
Address: 15 place de la République, Béthune, 62400, France
Description: Chef Sébastien Renard (Top Chef semi-finalist in 2022) has taken over the former premises of his mentor, the great chef Marc Meurin. This red-brick mansion oozes style, and its bar and elegant glass roof lend it undeniable flair. The chef, who hails from the region and made his solo debut here, turns out a carte blanche menu inspired by conversations with the growers who supply his kitchen with their produce. Dishes such as green asparagus, sheep's milk fromage frais and tarragon cream, or poached eggs in a red wine sauce with mushroom cream and walnut emulsion showcase all the savoir-faire of this chef with an impressive CV to his name.

Name: Le Bistrot du Brau
Description: A gorgeous bastide tucked away in the refreshing shade of a Provençal oak grove, chirping cicadas, the gentle lapping of water in the pool, a menu of traditional cuisine supervised by chef Christopher Hache (whose MICHLIN-starred Maison Hache is next door) and fresh local ingredients: Mollégès escargots with parsley butter; Mt Ventoux pork belly confit and medley of carrots; "tartelette" with lemon sorbet. The scene is set for an irresistible culinary interlude on the patio dotted with wrought-iron tables or in the all-white dining area furnished in black.

Name: Delicatessens
Address: Domaine du Berthiol, 725 route de Saint-Chamarand, Gourdon, 46300, France
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: On the terrace or through the restaurant's large bay windows, the landscape seems to insinuate itself between the tables, as you can drink in a wonderful panoramic view over the grounds and the rooftops of Gourdon's old town in the distance. The menu showcases produce from the region through its own spin on traditional cuisine, which is enhanced by moments of creativity: potato gnocchi with sweet garlic, mushroom consommé and salsify espuma; trout fillet, creamy risotto with wild nettles and green asparagus.

Name: Le 49R
Description: Behind the somewhat terse name (referring to its address at 49 rue Royale), there lies a charming private mansion whose original decor is enhanced by well-placed modern touches. The delightful terrace overlooking the courtyard to the rear of the building is a particular highlight. The dishes are creative and rigorously executed: sea bass ceviche, hazelnuts and seaweed; duck breast, chanterelle mushrooms, red curry sauce. Excellent wine list and selection of spirits.

Name: Isolé
Description: Close to the town hall, this pretty single-storey building stands out from the urban landscape with its terrace and small vegetable garden. Victor Gaillard and Alice di Cagno (previously at Chatomat in Ménilmontant) are at the helm, enthusiastically sharing their love of good food and their commitment to sustainability. The duo propose a superb lunchtime set menu that is reasonably priced and lets the ingredients speak for themselves: watercress, hazelnut and Pecorino Pepato arancini; pulled veal in sauce blanquette, creamy polenta and button mushrooms; rum semolina cake, poached pear with smoked tea. On the last three days of the week, more sophisticated and creative fare can be sampled in the evening. A small selection of natural and organic wines.

Name: Ginko
Description: Near the Grand’Place, this unobtrusive eatery with a glazed facade is the brainchild of two pals, both of whom boast virtuoso CVs: Valentina Giacobbe was born in Italy and grew up in Asia, graduated in political science before she turned to cooking, training at Gaya with Pierre Gagnaire before working at Rozo and then at SOlange; and Julien Ingaud-Jaubert, who trained as a pastry chef and who has also worked in top establishments (Pierre Gagnaire, Meurin, La Laiterie). Their trendy venue is the picture of a sleek contemporary bistro complete with a red-brick wall, a tribute to Lille. Valentina’s creative, delicate recipes are both distinctive and exquisitely balanced. Her seasonal menu features dishes dominated by vegetables (like green peas paired with nettles or the wild garlic-flavoured hollandaise sauce that accompanies the cod), all of which might feature Italian or Asian accents. A fully vegetarian menu is also available.

Name: Maison Zugno
Address: Les Monts de Vaux, Barretaine, 39800, France
Description: Dating back to the late 18C, this former coaching inn has been turned into a charming hotel (nine guestrooms, a swimming pool and spa) and a restaurant with three small dining areas (wooden floors, walnut tables, exposed brick walls, floral wallpaper or a green wall). Chef Quentin Defert makes modern, entirely gluten-free cuisine from seasonal, often local produce (but that's not all). Starters include a pear brunoise paired with blue cheese from the nearby dairy in La Marre, creamed corn combined with hazelnuts, and melt-in-the-mouth Iberian pork belly served with romanesco and elevated by a flavoursome Thai emulsion.

Name: Mr Guss
Description: Augustin Guibert aka Guss, a chef with an impeccable track record, is going solo with this contemporary restaurant set at the foot of a beautiful 19C stone building. This inventive cook impresses with his substantial technical prowess, which allows him to play with flavours and textures, as he does with his violetta aubergine, roasted then glazed with honey and satay, potato fritters, hollandaise sauce with caramelised onions. Without fail, the arrival of the delicious dishes bursting with colour puts a smile on your face. Congratulations, too, for showcasing the finest local produce, most notably the vegetables.

Name: Le Bois Blanc
Address: 11 rue de la Sirène, Romorantin-Lanthenay, 41200, France
Description: Chambord asparagus and Sologne strawberries, freshwater fish like pike, catfish and carp, game in season: chef Maxime Valleye, with stints at Georges Blanc and in his parents’ establishment, sings an ode to his region.
