The chef, who has an impressive track record (L'Espérance with Marc Meneau, Le Grand Coeur in Méribel, La Villa in Calvi), follows the seasons closely with his mouth-watering dishes: fish mousse, mussels and pig's trotter; pork filet mignon, polenta and corn. A warm welcome and smiling service.

Name: TLALI
Description: This Franco-Mexican establishment run by a native of Guadalajara, chef Kristian de Anda who was at the helm of the kitchen of the Parisian Biondi, is a delightful surprise. Only open in the evenings, his establishment masterfully proves that there is more to Mexican cuisine than tacos and enchiladas! In fact, the score is more fusion as pedigree Gallic recipes are dotted with intelligent Mexican notes – you won’t find a single tastebud-burning pepper in sight! We do however recommend ordering his array of tacos, in tribute to different regions of Mexico, as the ideal appetiser to kick off your meal in style.

Name: Comptoir du Lac
Address: 410 allée de la Plage, Duingt, 74410, France
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: This restaurant looks like a modern industrial greenhouse and is surrounded by greenery, the mountains and a lake. A really lovely place that serves up dishes that are equally appealing!

Name: Auberge Bienvenue
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: This place may have celebrated its 30th birthday but it shows no sign of tiring. Comfortably ensconced beneath the beams and arcades of the large dining area, you have to admit that at times nothing beats tradition, especially when it comes to cooking.

Name: Au Vieux Porche
Description: This typical residence (1707) stands in the winegrowing estate of the manager's family. His partner cooks classic regional dishes, but he is also a winemaker. So it goes without saying that you can enjoy some fine vintages here too.

Name: La Verdoyante
Description: Standing among the vines, this former rustic farmhouse enjoys a fine panoramic view... But La Verdoyante would be nothing without the enthusiasm of the couple who hold the reins. In the stylish interior or on the charming terrace, diners savour delicious Provençal cuisine that smacks of the garigue.

Name: Le Chalet
Description: A fortified house during the Middle Ages, and a monastery until 1905, this "chalet" is now a hotel and restaurant run by the Prayer family. The tasty dishes, such as house - smoked salmon or seven - hour leg of lamb with gratin du Vercors, attest to the two primordial values of the establishment: tradition and generosity.

Name: Le Cigalon
Description: This warm friendly eatery outside the village of Flayosc is run by a couple: she works front of house, while he crafts fine food: barigoule of fennel, olives, focaccia and squid; Mediterranean seabream, cranberry beans, courgettes and mussels; roast pear, star aniseed and hazelnut ice cream. The quintessence of the South of France.

Name: Le Carillon
Address: 10 avenue du Luberon (place de la Libération), Goult, 84220, France
Description: Facing the church on Goult's main square, this restaurant offers excellent Provençal-inspired cuisine with the odd contemporary twist. Tables are set up in a small dining area with modern decor and out on the terrace, where you can soak up the village atmosphere. A charming welcome and a well-devised wine list that pays particular attention to organic options. A lovely spot.

Name: Les Jardins Sauvages - La Grée des Landes
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: In the restaurant of the Yves Rocher hotel, you can expect modern, healthy, niftily crafted, flavoursome food, made primarily out of organic produce from the garden and local growers in keeping with the eatery’s sustainable ethos. Bathed in light, the glazed dining room stretches out between the rows of veg in the cottage garden on one side and a conservatory that leads into the garden on the other, maintaining an organic link with nature as befits the establishment’s mindset.

Name: L'Un des Sens
Description: Near the antique dealers’ district, this restaurant serves scrumptious food, presented beautifully and rich in distinctive flavours, illustrated by a rack of Ségala veal, ravioles of green peas and pecorino cheese and spring onions. The vegetables and fruit come from the chef’s garden. Several-course surprise menu in the evening and simpler fare at lunchtime. Courtyard patio for alfresco dining.

Name: Les Santons
Description: This lovely Provençal inn is full of character, with its exposed beams, flower arrangements and, of course, its collection of figurines (santons in French). The menu never gets boring, alternating between classic cuisine and contemporary dishes, such as rack of lamb with crispy new garlic, garnished with a millefeuille of candied peppers and chard. The traditional aged-rum baba with vanilla whipped cream deserves a special mention.

Name: Le Pavillon Gourmand
Description: This village house (1683) offers a setting bathed in light, tastefully combining the historical character of the building with more contemporary touches. Tuck into cuisine that includes Alsace recipes (onion tart, sauerkraut, wild boar stew) and more modern dishes. Wines from the Eguisheim vineyard are well represented, and the small terrace is popular in summer.

Name: Les Gentianettes
Address: 73 route de Chevenne, La Chapelle-d'Abondance, 74360, France
Description: A mountain chalet decor with exposed beams, a traditional dining room with a fireplace in the middle and decorated with a collection of bells – it doesn't get much more inviting than this! The kitchen serves both traditional dishes, including beef tenderloin with a morel mushroom sauce, and slightly more modern and creative recipes such as carpaccio of sea bass with passion fruit. For Savoyard specialties, guests can head to La Baratte, the restaurant's ground-floor eatery, to tuck into authentic cuisine in a friendly atmosphere.

Name: L'Arbousier
Address: D55 - Boulevard Marie-Jeanne Bozzi, Porticcio, 20166, France
Description: A throwback to another time in this establishment with a slightly old-fashioned atmosphere, where Mediterranean cuisine with Corsican influences is served on the very pleasant terrace facing the sea. Lobster, fish from small-scale local fishermen… and fricassee of lobster with buttered capellini, the house speciality. The wine is served by the glass from magnums, which is a nice touch! More limited menu at lunchtime.

Name: La Taula Gallici
Address: Villa Gallici, 18 avenue de la Violette, Aix-en-Provence, 13100, France
Description: Luxury and tradition, with not a hint of ostentation... and far from the crowds, in the upper reaches of town. On the menu: good sun-drenched French cuisine to relish around the low tables of the superb lounges, or by the plane trees on the peaceful terrace. The chef's specialities include chilled lobster and gambero rosso bisque; vitello tonnato-style tortellini, ricotta, sun-dried tomatoes and taggiasche olives; "Gallici" tiramisu. The spirit of the South of France!

Name: La Bartavelle
Address: 24 rue de la République, Argelès-sur-Mer, 66700, France
Description: This place is an open secret among food lovers – and with good reason! Chef Thibaut Lesage and Stéphanie, his pastry chef wife, put an inspired spin on the classics to produce dishes that diners delight in. You will need to book ahead if you want to try it for yourself!

Name: La Poya
Description: In a mountain-inspired decor, the chef serves up good-quality traditional cuisine that often takes meat as its starting point… but does not exclude the odd Asian note (eg gravelax salmon tataki marinated in beetroot, served with mustard sorbet). The dishes are beautifully presented and service comes with a smile. A good place to recharge your batteries after hitting the slopes on your skis!

Name: À la 12
Address: 6 place de la République, Delme, 57590, France
Description: This has been the fiefdom of the François family since it was founded in 1954. After a worthwhile experience at the Bras family's Laguiole restaurant, Thomas (in the kitchen) and Laura, his charming partner (on the restaurant floor), have both returned to the fold in Delme. So it's now the third generation at the helm of this contemporary restaurant, which is popular with locals and visiting guests alike. The menu is both indulgent and delicate, oscillating between tradition and modernity, showcasing an appreciation for herbs and spices. Uplifting!

Name: La Gaffe
Description: Chef Yann Le Scavarec, who hails from Morbihan, is at the helm of this restaurant, which boasts an ideal location on the Saint-Florent harbour front. His well-crafted contemporary cooking showcases local produce, eg lamb and veal from Oletta, fish sourced directly from a local fisherman and barbecued crayfish. The grouper, courgette flower with spider crab and Vadouvan spices made an impression! The modern interior is in keeping with the menu.

Name: MaThy'S
Description: Picture a red façade preceded by a delightful patio shaded by a mulberry tree. On a street corner of Saint Florent, this eatery aims for a friendly village restaurant vibe and serves Mediterranean and Corsican cuisine (carpaccio of langoustines, olive oil and dried caviar, tartare of red tuna or grilled squid with chorizo), without forgetting a few more exotic Asian notes (yuzu-flavoured gyoza or crunchy king prawns, nori and wasabi). Simpler lunchtime menu and a highly tempting wine list add the final touch to this inviting portrait.

Name: La Table de Courcelles - Château de Courcelles
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: With the arrival of Italian chef Massimiliano Sena (originally from Sorrento), armed with his impressive CV, this noble and elegant Grand Siècle-style residence has entered a modern culinary era that bodes well. Local and seasonal ingredients take pride of place, and the chef's Italian roots make themselves felt in a delicate and subtle manner. There's no showboating or recourse to culinary techniques just for the sake of it; the confident expertise and harmoniously preserved marriages of flavours allow diners to fully appreciate the slow-cooked egg with its airy chanterelle mousse, or the cod with courgette, raspberry and black garlic. Terrific wine list with over 700 wines. There is a pleasant view of the formal garden and canal from the glass-roofed dining area.

Name: La Table de la Grotte
Address: Domaine de Murtoli, Vallée de l'Ortolo, Sartène, 20100, France
Description: Above the Domaine de Murtoli golf course, set deep in the maquis, this restaurant charms diners with its absolutely unique location and its delicious and flavoursome cuisine, which features quality ingredients either from the estate itself or sourced from neighbouring producers. On wooden benches nestled among the rock formations, or on one of the superb little terraces with a splendid view, you dine by romantic candlelight, tucking into typical Corsican dishes that take the form of a single set menu: courgette à la Sartenaise, confit shoulder of lamb... and a tomato sauce with herbs from the maquis that in itself is worth the trip. Booking essential.

Name: Les Orfèvres
Description: Bang in the middle of town, this restaurant sports a modern, pared-down, workshop interior and a friendly vibe. The menu is no stranger to the classics, albeit with the odd more modern touch. The chef avows a weakness for fish, illustrated by his superlative low-temperature loin of cod, honey-flavoured fermented milk, leeks and celery.

Name: Le 59 Restaurant
Description: This restaurant is a family affair for the Campanellas, with Cédric having taken over from his brother Boris at the reins of this converted grocer's shop. The cuisine demonstrates a sense of precision, and comprises modern, ever-inventive dishes. One of the best spots in town.

Name: La Cigogne
Address: 5 impasse de la Cabane-Bambou, Soyaux, 16800, France
Description: Not far from Angoulême, La Cigogne is located at the foot of old stone quarries – a rather unusual location, to be sure. Elegant contemporary setting, verdant terrace, and fresh cuisine prepared with good local ingredients.

Name: L'Aubergade
Description: Chef Éric Boutté, a fine connoisseur of local Picardy produce and sometime globetrotter, makes classically inspired cuisine that is in tune with the seasons and made with the best the market has to offer. The elegant dining area has an appealingly restrained decor. Don't leave without tasting the house special of stuffed cabbage: over 20 000 have already been served!

Name: Grand Largue
Description: From the upper floor of this villa, diners enjoy fine views over the gulf of Morbihan and gastronomic seafood cuisine (lobster, sea bass, shellfish). On the ground floor, the P'tit Zeph is a bistro with a distinctly seafaring air.

Name: Tempi Fà
Description: Welcome to "bygone days" (tempi fà), in this grocer's-cum-bistro run by a passionate man who selects the island's finest ingredients! You enter via the shop, reminiscent of an actual village market (cold cuts, cheeses, myrtle liqueur etc). You'll enjoy tucking into the tender, flavoursome Abbatucci veal chop with a jus flavoured with herbs from the maquis... and a fine wine from the island!

Name: Les Cornettes
Address: 43 route des Frasses, La Chapelle-d'Abondance, 74360, France
Description: This restaurant, listed in the Michelin Guide since 1933, is a real institution, renowned throughout the Chablais region. On the menu: game pie, lake trout fillet with wild garlic and morels, guinea fowl roasted on the bone. The cold cuts are matured and smoked on site in a typical mountain atmosphere. It's simple, tasty and rustic as can be.

Name: Cuq en Terrasses
FacilitiesAndServices: Garden or park,Great view,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: High up in the village, this charming 18C house is a haven of calm, boasting an unusual terraced garden that showcases the produce of the kitchen garden. It's a new departure for this restaurant run by two young professionals who have worked in MICHELIN-starred establishments in Toulouse, and who serve up cuisine that is essentially plant-based and finely executed: artichoke au gratin with aromatic herbs, chorizo emulsion; river trout from Condax fish farm, almond stuffing. Take in the breathtaking view of the Lauragais plain and the Pyrenees from the veranda and terrace. There are charming guestrooms, should you wish to extend the experience in this tranquil setting.

Name: L'Attilio - Château de Noirieux
Address: Château de Noirieux, 26 route du Moulin, Briollay, 49125, France
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Terrace
Description: This handsome little 17C château and charming 15C manor house are set in grounds on the banks of the River Loir. The restaurant has an elegant interior refurbished in a contemporary style, in a palette of light tones, and a pleasant terrace overlooking the valley. Italian chef Attilio Marrazzo chooses quality ingredients – including produce grown in his own vegetable garden – for his modern cuisine. His dishes (free-range poultry, fricassee of chanterelles with parsley, Caesar-style salad) show a good command of culinary techniques, and can be washed down with a wine from a list that focuses on regional tipples.

Name: Comte Roger
Description: This restaurant within the medieval city walls has a sleek contemporary design and tables set up on a lovely airy patio – Comte Roger knows how to welcome guests! Cassoulet (the house speciality) is of course given pride of place, along with seasonal and regional ingredients (asparagus and local lamb, Lauragais lentils, Belpech poultry etc), which are prepared with a keen sense of precision.

Name: Auberge Larochette
Description: This pleasant village inn serves hearty traditional cuisine, such as a fine Charolais entrecôte with gratin dauphinois, or crispy calf sweetbreads. In winter the fire crackles in the hearth; in summer the shady terrace is the place to be. Attentive front-of-house staff.

Name: Le 1131 - Abbaye de la Bussière
Description: Pouvait-on rêver lieu plus inspirant qu'une abbaye cistercienne du 12e s. ? Sous ces impressionnantes voûtes en croisées d’ogives, le terroir bourguignon est mis à l'honneur de belle manière : escargots, grenouilles, poissons de lac et de rivière, cassis et miel des fleurs du parc... Prolongez votre méditation dans le parc de 7 hectares ou dans l'une des luxueuses chambres. Au déjeuner, cuisine plus simple au Bistrot des Moines.

Name: Le Shardana
Address: 16 rue de la République, Bandol, 83150, France
Description: Bang in the middle of the seaside resort, this spruce, modern edifice is reminiscent of Sardinia, both in terms of the décor and the succulent seasonal food. The menu, which changes monthly, is liberally strewn with local and Sardinian ingredients. Examples include gently steamed local croaker in a tomato and cognac sauce with crunchy vegetables and black garlic or panettone French toast with roast apples, salted butterscotch and a scoop of stracciatella ice cream. The chef’s radiant wife cheerfully and professionally manages the front of house. Concise wine list of mainly Italian and local vintages.

Name: La Brasserie du Corton
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: The brasserie offshoot of Villa Madie continues to foster simplicity with its market-fresh ingredients and enticing surf and turf combinations. The set menus are different at lunch and dinner, as well as being changed on a weekly basis. Less expensive than at the original restaurant, the dishes here are just as tasty (beef tartare with Tamaris oysters, real Marseille sôcisse with fennel, lemon tart. When the weather is fine, head for the terrace, which commands a knockout view of the pretty bay.

Name: Le Bellevue
Description: The interior is light, and the menu is short. Two reasons to linger in this tastefully decorated restaurant. Traditional cuisine is revisited with enthusiasm and a keen sense of the pleasure of food. Try off - the - bone pig's trotter terrine or, for dessert, the hot soufflé with pear brandy.

Name: Maison Demarcq
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: This grand town house close to where the famous Treaty of Cambrai is said to have been signed (1529) has gone down in history for hosting Napoleon. The decor fosters classical elegance, and the food is contemporary and meticulous – a good option in the town renowned for its "Bêtises de Cambrai" sweets. The simpler traditional cuisine served at the brasserie L'Éphémère is an alternative option.

Name: La Sittelle
Description: This inviting late-1940’s villa is enjoying a new lease of life thanks to two associates, formerly of Locguénolé chateau. The chef enhances regional produce in recipes with a creative twist, displaying a preference for surf and turf dishes. Welcoming and attentive service.

Name: Auberge de la Forêt
Address: 276 rue des Verriers, à Lettenbach, Abreschviller, 57560, France
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: This turreted inn is nestled in the Abreschviller valley. Gone are any airs of a country bistro; the style is now up to the minute, elegant and refined, in line with the food, which is very contemporary.

Name: Les 3 Lieux - La Table
Description: In this restaurant on the banks of the River Loire, diners enjoy chef Sylvain Justice’s creative, high-spirited cuisine with lashings of generosity to boot: soup of bouchot mussels in kari-gosse spices, green peas, confit of lemon and crunchy croutons; carpaccio of squid, peppers and lemon; roast monkfish, lobster bisque risotto with parmesan and basil; roast John Dory, spring veggies and hollandaise sauce; nectarines in verbena and almonds or Mirabelle plums and mead in shortbread. Pop next-door to the Bistrot for a more casual dining experience.

Name: Notes de Saveurs
Description: Sitting in the vaulted room with exposed stones, looking onto the ruins of the former Benedictine convent, you can enjoy food that places the onus on quality ingredients. The dishes are generous, delicious, flavoursome and original. A friendly and pleasant place, opened by a young couple in 2011.

Name: Mâche
Description: Butternut, carrot and haddock in shades of orange; a gutsy duet of squab and asparagus, both crunchy and tender. The inventive cuisine of Michaël Gamet (with a stint at l’Astrance) is a culinary festival of taste, colour and flavour that packs a punch (of which fermented and confit ingredients and powerful seasonings are the stars) and is dotted with souvenirs of the chef’s travels and culinary encounters. The handsome interior mingles vintage details with contemporary geometric design features, while an upbeat vibe and a friendly team set the scene for the front-of-house service.

Name: Chez Jules Le Don Juan
Description: The major appeal of this particular Don Juan is its enthusiastic, hardworking owner-chef, who tirelessly sources produce (vegetables from his family, veal from an Aveyron farm etc). His food is steeped in the flavours of Provence and Nice cuisine: house specialties are pissaladière, petits farcis niçois, gnocchi à la daube and aioli. The restaurant is part of a convivial little hub for gourmets, complete with café, grocery shop and bistro. Atmosphere guaranteed.

Name: L'Assierois
Description: In the village centre, opposite the church, this former inn with a pleasant shady terrace now presents a sleek contemporary interior. The chef proposes fairly simple seasonal cooking on weekday lunchtimes, and much more ambitious dishes in the evening and at weekends, but he always takes care to maximise local ingredients.

Name: La Cuisine
Description: In the centre of this town, “la cuisine” is well and truly honoured in this excellent eatery. Chef Johann Dubernet, assisted in the dining room by cheerful Isabelle, his partner, signs colourful, fragrant and beautifully presented dishes whose influences are manifold: tempura of frog’s legs in curry and saté sauce; John Dory in a green tomato and shiso leaf chutney; brownie with pineapple poached in combava and a spicy sorbet. Subtle, suave, spot-on cooking!

Name: Château de Salettes
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: This restaurant enjoys a prime location: a 13C château in the heart of a Gaillac wine estate. The food, very much in tune with the zeitgeist, is based on fine ingredients and the attractive wine list proposes Château de Salettes wines. On fine days, the terrace oozes with charm, as do the contemporary-furnished guestrooms and suites established in the edifice’s historic towers and the surrounding wall.

Name: Ryoko - Comptoir à ramen
Address: 14 rue de la Fontaine, Vannes, 56000, France
Description: The flavoursome codes of Japanese cuisine are now part and parcel of French dining habits. This pocket handkerchief bistro embodies this trend, depicted by a red, white and black façade. You will taste one of the best ramens in town, based on pork (tonkotsu) or chicken (Tori chintan) broth – it’s your choice! Made with first-class local ingredients (pigs fed on flax seed), each dish is a masterpiece of Japanese tradition. A word of warning: they don’t accept bookings and the place is often packed to the seams!

Name: Hyacinthe
Description: Previously active in the humanitarian sector, this chef found a new calling while being trained by mentors such as Cyril Lignac and Hélène Darroze. Remaining true to his ethos here in his vintage restaurant, he is mindful of the relationship between his cooking, nature and people, sourcing vegetables from the Hortillonnages (cultivated islets in Amiens), saltmarsh lamb from the Baie de Somme estuary, line-caught fish from the Côte d'Opale etc. Filet mignon pie, vegetable pickles or monkfish, tomato, aubergine and sea herbs: his – at times creative – dishes draw on various preparation techniques, good ingredients and flavours.

Name: Jeu de Quilles
Description: Iced courgette velouté with mint and burrata, or grilled Aubrac beef with smoked pepper: the chef of this tiny bistro proposes simple and appetising market-based cuisine. The very reasonably priced dishes are listed on the blackboard. Don't miss the pleasant terrace under the arbour.

Name: Prélude
Description: Far more than a prelude, this is a full-blown symphony! Now established in a spruce traditional building, Élodie Ouchelli and Thibault Étienne practiced their scales in top star restaurants, among which that of Romuald Fassenet. The virtuoso chef, whose talent is a masterclass in culinary subtlety, composes harmonious dishes in which first-class local produce plays the leading role. Several tables of the contemporary dining room provide a view of the chef at work in the kitchen.

Name: Le Petit Jardin - La Chenevière
Description: The Château de la Chenevière bistro is housed in the old orangery and has retained its large glass roof. Nestled between the garden and the swimming pool, it is decorated in a charming "English cottage" style. Tuck into good seasonal bistronomy fare: low temperature egg, cream of celery, cockles, samphire and wholegrain mustard; goat cheese risotto, snow peas, mushrooms and garlic cream.

Name: Onaka
Description: Tucked away in a cul-de-sac, this sushi bar is invariably packed to the seams (booking highly recommended). The chef at the helm, sushi champion of France, trained in several of chef Nobu Matsuhisa’s establishments, no less. Impeccably cooked rice, moist tender chicken, melt-in-the-mouth salmon, juicy red tuna, firm seabass, spicy miso sauce dusted with fresh garden herbs, last-minute grated wasabi and a knockout selection of sakés (the sommelier and partner knows his business). The omakase menu features a festival of flavours for a fine dining experience that can be adapted to suit the appetites and wallets of everyone.

Name: L'Estran
Description: Ceviche of seabass, coconut milk, ginger and sweet potato guacamole; lightly seared wild prawns in Espelette pepper, artichokes glazed in tarragon with a langoustine emulsion… In this dinky quayside restaurant, whose terrace overlooks the port, chef Xavier Audren pursues a bistronomic quest that takes its cue from the seasons and the fish market just down the street. A concise menu, flawless craftsmanship together with lashings of flavour and colour.

Name: La Plancha
Description: This place may be discreet, but its original menu makes it well worth coming for a meal here. The dishes are simple, effective and occasionally creative; the flavours are striking, eg Iberico pork belly with peas, bacon and horseradish. Special mentions have to go to the punchy bulli dog sauce and the profiteroles, which are made in time-honoured tradition.

Name: Le M
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Plenty of originality in the design of the dishes and the marriages of flavours in this typically Breton granite house done out with a contemporary decor. Tuck into modern cuisine that sources its ingredients (fish, poultry, vegetables etc) from local producers. In summer, dine alfresco on the pleasant terrace.

Name: 16âme
Address: 32 rue des Glaciers, Le Monêtier-les-Bains, 05220, France
Description: Behind a discreet façade is this inviting restaurant with decor that calls to mind a trapper's hut – we are in the mountains, after all! Julien Momon, originally from Corsica, worked in the kitchens of Christophe Bacquié and Gérard Boyer (formerly chef at Les Crayères in Reims) before becoming head chef at a hotel here in Monêtier-les-Bains. His dishes contain nothing but seasonal and local ingredients from this rural and Alpine territory, such as lamb from the Hautes-Alpes, coriander, mint, a pearly jus with olive oil or his lovage-infused cream.

Name: Taokan
Description: Come inside this pretty restaurant in the heart of St-Germain-des-Prés to enjoy light and fragrant Cantonese cuisine, with a few detours to the territory of Southeast Asia: the obligatory dim sum, steamed fish, spicy beef or lok lak. Lovely presentation and good ingredients: a real ambassador for Chinese food.

Name: Prosper
Description: When a winemaker from the Côte de Beaune meets a starred chef, you get Prosper! This lovely contemporary bistro in the Château St Aubin is the result of a collaboration between the Prosper Maufoux wine estate and the restaurateur Édouard Mignot (restaurant Ed.Em in Chassagne-Montrachet). The chef proposes a menu inspired by the Burgundy terroir. Pleasant terrace with a view of the vineyards.

Name: Les Parisiens
Description: Inside a new luxury hotel located in Faubourg-Saint-Germain, this restaurant adopts all the codes of the luxury brasserie genre. Wood panelling, large mirrors, mosaic floors, velvet banquettes, gilding, black marble tables: it is elegant, slightly retro and very cosy – a winning formula. Curated by Thibault Sombardier, the menu represents a refreshed and updated take on tradition. A fine and eclectic wine list, complete with some great bottles.

Name: Milagro
Description: An American chef who was born in New Mexico, Justin Kent honed his skills with the likes of Alain Passard and David Toutain. His dinky neo-vintage bistro couldn’t be more bang on: white marble and oak counter, parquet floor, light wooden tables, vintage green velvet wooden armchairs. International and Parisian bistronomic influences happily rub shoulders in the kitchen: fritters of chorizo and sweet potatoes, Greek yoghurt; lamb chops, emulsion of sweetcorn, risotto of spelt; creamy delight of celeriac with white chocolate, ice cream and meringues.

Name: Magma
Description: Like magma, Japanese chef Ryuya Ono fusions French haute cuisine with his own constantly renewed inspiration and gourmet instincts in a tasting menu that shows the greatest respect for the seasons. Spot-on associations are the chef’s hallmark, illustrated by trout garnished with chanterelle mushrooms. The desserts, like the squash-flavoured creamy mont-blanc delight, are equally inventive. Crisp, elegant interior and slick service.

Name: So'Mets
Description: After honing her skills in top restaurants (including La Vague d’Or), chef Anne-Sophie Sabini has struck out on her own in this modern, colourful gastropub, flanked by a lovely terrace. She has devised a concise menu that changes monthly, in which she adds a feminine, modern touch to Gallic standards: cream of green peas with a 64° poached egg, coppa, crunchy croutons and organic olive oil from Provence; roast squid and black pudding, purée of carrots, citrus-flavoured dressing; sorbet of Beaulieu mandarin, anis-flavoured biscuit, praline and drizzled citrus fruit and bergamot … Slick service, charming welcome. Heaven for foodies!

Name: Patachée
Description: This small traditional restaurant in the town centre sports a bistro vibe, while rustic touches bear witness to the establishment’s age. The seasoned chef concocts tasty dishes with what his suppliers bring in fresh daily in a modern, hearty vein in which spices are often cast in the leading role: raviole of squab in Thai stock; lobster and cockles in curry-flavoured court-bouillon or line-caught pollock with an emulsion of Hanoi spices. Lunchtime menu at prices that make sense.

Name: Garenne
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Wheelchair access
Description: In a landscape of hills and vineyards in Drôme Provençale, the farmhouse on this small organic winegrowing estate has been restored and is now home to a hotel and a fine dining restaurant. The lovely, bright contemporary space (almost a veranda with its open sides) allows you to feast on the surrounding nature, too. Artichoke and creamed artichoke accompanied by a surprising oyster ice cream; sole garnished with dulse seaweed, white asparagus caramelised and in an emulsion, shredded bottarga and confit shallot purée: local and organic produce, the plating, jus and sauces all appeal to the taste buds! A charming welcome and professional service.

Name: Black Bass
Address: Black Bass Hotel, 921 route d'Albertville, à Sevrier, Annecy, 74000, France
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: A smart vibe, a hip interior and a sweeping view of the lake set the scene for bistronomic recipes scattered with creative, exotic accents: ceviche of croaker with coriander and jalapenos; barbecued organic seabass with a harissa of raspberries and salad of green beans; spaghetti with toasted breadcrumbs, lemon and basil…

Name: POF
Description: The lunchtime menu is chalked up on a slate, while in the evening, the dishes of the concise menu carry playful, tongue-in-cheek names, which do however require a certain command of the French language to be appreciated! The globetrotting partners aim for a friendly vibe, a wide range of culinary influences (cream of cauliflower with Brittany curry spices, wakame crumble; crunchy quinoa and a Mexican-inspired jus; pear, myrtle, star anis, mascarpone and matcha tea) and market-fresh ingredients in line with the zeitgeist.

Name: Ezkia
Address: 6 avenue de la Grande-Plage, Bidart, 64210, France
Description: Whether beneath the lime trees (ezkia in Basque) on the terrace, or inside the small, inviting and intimate restaurant room with exposed stonework, floorboards, saffron-coloured velvet seats and banquettes, it is the same traditional Basque house. Standing in the heart of the delightful village of Bidart, it exudes a quiet, refined atmosphere. The couple who run the place, defectors from Michel Guérard's restaurant, serve nice seasonal precisely cooked dishes, full of good local Basque produce e.g. farm-reared pig, line-caught tuna, black cherry, mature farm cheeses.

Name: Patern
Description: This superlatively located eatery is only a 5-minute walk from Stanislas Square! In a smart, modern interior, Martin Debuiche, former deputy of Jean-Pierre Vigato of the Apicius in Paris, crafts surprise menus based on flawlessly sourced premium ingredients: fish from Brittany, Vosges pigeon, dairy produce from Meurthe-et-Moselle, saffron from Lorraine, etc. Examples include frothy potatoes, Oscietra caviar from Aquitaine and a bay leaf emulsion, or blowtorch-seared Brittany mackerel garnished with fish bone powder and sautéed girolles.

Name: Eunoé
Description: Japanese chef Ryuji Sato and Félix Perotte (front of house) are two friends who are passionate about food and wine. They offer hospitality at this location near Square Maurice Gardette. In a modern, stylishly "unfinished" setting in sand and ochre tones, the chef delivers his fine, no-holds-barred take on the culinary zeitgeist, with an emphasis on flavour in every dish: pork loin soaked in its full-bodied jus with aged sherry vinegar and a hint of thyme, smoked potato mash and a small salad of fresh herbs, seasoned to perfection. At dinner, the elegance goes up a notch.

Name: Benjamin Schmitt Restaurant
Description: In the heart of Pigalle, this eatery pays tribute to the land and those who work it. The youthful chef cultivates culinary eclecticism, seamlessly segueing from one style of cuisine to another and from traditional to modern. The enticing names of the dishes live up to their promise: duck, foie gras and pork pâté en croûte; veal breast confit with olives, aubergine and anchovies; strawberry and rhubarb pavlova... Sensibly priced lunch menu, tasting and à la carte menus in the evening.

Name: Le France
FacilitiesAndServices: Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Between Morteau and La Chaux-de-Fonds, not far from the French-Swiss border, this restaurant welcomes guests to the heart of the Haut-Doubs mountains. In this family-run place, chef Hugues Droz offers guests typical Franche-Comté hospitality, just as his father and grandfather did before him. With a keen eye on seasonal produce, he loves to ally terroir and innovation. He also enjoys creating themed meals, such as his morel-based menu, in which this mushroom features in every course.

Name: Alluma
Description: Former Balagan chef Liran Tal has tastefully revamped this establishment with immaculate white walls. He crafts delicious Mediterranean cuisine with Israeli influences, served in the form of tasting menus that are very good value for money: delicious msabbaha hummus, yellowtail crudo with figs and spices, lamb sirloin and an apricot-miso condiment. Choice of organic and biodynamic wines, most notably from Italy, Spain and Armenia.

Name: La Dariole
Description: In the heart of the old town and not far from the cathedral, this 15C half-timbered house showcases an easy alliance of old stonework and cosy touches. The chef, who even trained here when he was learning his trade, hits the mark with delicious cuisine that is in tune with the times. The seasonal menu changes regularly and features appealingly tasty dishes such as pork chop with potatoes and a caper jus.

Name: Kazumi
Description: Behind the discreet façade of this Japanese restaurant, chef Kazumi Hatakenaka is at the helm. Having first come to France to work in a traditional inn in the Beaujolais region, he is now serving cuisine that speaks to his dual culinary culture (French and Japanese). His tasting menu alternates classic French dishes with ingredients prepared on the teppanyaki – expertly infused with subtle Japanese flavours. Fresh produce (fish, meat and vegetables), mouth-watering dishes such as pan-fried foie gras, melt-in-the-mouth kohlrabi and veal jus, and on-point cooking and seasoning make this a delightful culinary escapade. For dinner, allow three hours at your table.

Name: Castel Ac'h
Description: Brittany is full of magical places and the Abers region is one such! Just a stone’s throw from the lighthouses of Ile Vierge and Ile de Wrac’h, this handsome neo-Brittany house enjoys a superb location opposite the picturesque Lilia Beach. The food is of regional inspiration with a range of tasty surf and turf ingredients and the lunchtime menu is a steal. In the evening, two set menus and one à la carte play a bistronomic Brittany score: oysters, abalone, fish of the day, veggies from the cottage garden, seaweed and sarrazin wheat...

Name: Les Roseaux Pensants
Description: This quaint historic village is the lair of a self-taught couple, who sources their organic ingredients entirely locally thus enabling them to develop close ties with producers. The gutsy result demonstrates a weakness for veggies and fermentation illustrated by vegetarian black pudding paired with apple and black garlic pickles, although the menu also features a sprinkling of meat and fish dishes. A delightful patio shaded by linden trees in fine weather and swish, slick service complete the portrait.

Name: À l'Échevin
Description: In the heart of “Little Venice”, the half-timbered Le Maréchal hotel is home to a comfortable and classically-decorated restaurant. The food is rather more adventurous and the chef deftly crafts modern recipes, putting a new spin on regional and gastronomic favourites, thanks to a sprinkling of creative touches. Delicious desserts, like this duo of figs and creamed rice in a crisp cinnamon-scented tuile. We recommend booking a seat in the blue dining room which overlooks the Lauch River.

Name: La Cotriade
Description: On the quayside facing the fishing port, the seafood counter piled high with fish and shellfish sits proudly in front of the restaurant. This seafaring theme is naturally pursued indoors, where the chef is busy in his open-plan kitchen. The menu features seafood platters, fresh fish chalked up on the daily specials board, a few family favourites and a scattering of signature dishes like seabream cooked in a banana leaf, lime and coconut milk, whole sea bass roasted in fennel and flambéed with aniseed, or their famous cotriade – Brittany's answer to bouillabaisse. A few meat dishes are also available.

Name: Saba
Description: There is no shortage of Japanese chefs mad about French food, but here is a French chef who is crazy about Japanese cuisine, which he showcases beautifully in his tiny restaurant in historic Annecy. His freshly-sourced, vibrant dishes hit the spot every time: gyozas of smoked eel and saba (mackerel in Japanese); koshihikari rice, giant prawns and curry… All of which in line with a sustainable agriculture and fishing ethos. Cheerful service.

Name: L'Altiplano au K2 Palace
Address: Le K2 Palace, 238 rue des Clarines, Courchevel 1850, Courchevel, 73120, France
Description: At this high altitude restaurant with a cosy and intimate interior, ceviche classico of white fish marinated in tiger's milk; grilled prawns, spring onion, red pepper and lime; and postre estilo pisco are just some of the (delicious) examples of the modernised Peruvian food you can tuck into – think tasty, colourful and spicy with a delicate touch.

Name: Oktobre
Description: In one of the most bookish streets of the scholarly St André des Arts neighbourhood, Oktobre is warm and welcoming, like an Indian summer. The chef's pantry is stocked with only the finest, painstakingly sourced produce (he buys some animals whole). He takes a fresh, delicate, natural approach to cooking, deftly seasoning his dishes with varied spices and Asian accents. “Dentelles de Cucugnan” cuttlefish pasta with a shellfish bisque; Dombes quail, buckwheat risotto with mushrooms, fig and gochujang pickles; figs topped with a shiso-scented diplomat cream…

Name: L'Ancienne Auberge
Description: This establishment is in a former lemonade factory. The nostalgic 1940s bistro decor pays tribute to the inn opened by the Blanc family in the late 19C (old photos and posters). Regional cuisine.

Name: ROS[O]
Description: The name is a play on words referring to the reeds (roseaux) on the banks of the Louet, overlooked by this restaurant's delightful terrace. Quail eggs, Comté cheese and courgettes make for a fresh, well-seasoned dish; tender Duroc pork chop cooked rare, served with Noirmoutier new potatoes and vegetables – chef Tony Pasquier (formerly of Casa Corneille in the centre of Angers) knows the ingredients and the seasons inside out. He has a knack for coming up with mouth-watering dishes for you to enjoy in this bright, modern space.

Name: Le P'tit Bateau
Description: In the heart of the medieval city, Le P'tit Bateau sets out to tantalise our taste buds with fresh produce, including fish sourced directly from Brittany's fish markets, as well as game from Sologne in season. The dishes are generous, precise, carefully presented and tasty. It is worth noting there is a pleasant patio for a meal al fresco. An eatery committed to doing a good job.

Name: Le Restaurant 1451
Description: In the heart of this market town near Roanne, imagine an old stone house lit up in blue at nighttime, whose tasteful elegant interior is flanked by a lovely alfresco courtyard terrace that is perfect for special occasions. The scene is set for a fine dining experience. Chef Jérémie Louis crafts fresh, modern recipes in which artistically displayed vegetables are often cast in the lead roles. The cheese trolley is truly in a class of its own. Océane, the chef’s partner, supervises the front-of house cheerfully and seamlessly. A family-run establishment depicted by a genuine “home from home” vibe!

Name: Lacertus
Description: Good-humoured staff, friendly service, a convivial atmosphere, modern cuisine with a touch of inventiveness (eg fish sausage or a seaweed/mustard sorbet as part of the mackerel starter; a lime/pea sorbet alongside a chocolate dessert), quality local produce and a few ingredients gathered wild (mustard seeds): this is the winning formula behind this small restaurant a stone's throw from Le Remblai promenade. In case you were wondering, the name Lacertus means "mackerel" in Latin.

Name: La Conciergerie
Address: 4405 rue de la Lys, Sailly-sur-la-Lys, 62840, France
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: The former concierge lodge in the grounds of the Château de Bac-Saint-Maur is now home to this modern restaurant. Bathed in light thanks to its large bay windows, the space features a few design details that reflect the season. Langoustine and beetroot for starters; veal, mussels and samphire for the main course; tomato, vanilla zephyr and oregano ice cream for dessert: the chef aims to surprise with cuisine that is creative (in moderation), and made with good ingredients, mainly local and seasonal.

Name: Les Allées
Description: Antoine and Coralie met in Jean Cousseau's two-Michelin-starred restaurant (Relais de la Poste in Magescq) after gaining solid experience in France and Spain. This former café-restaurant has been given a facelift that subtly blends vintage and modern features (waxed concrete floors paired with exposed beams). As for the food, this pair of pros focuses on flavour, often drawing on the Iberian pantry to put a spin on traditional dishes: calf's head croquette; leeks in vinaigrette; sautéed sweetbreads; grilled octopus etc. Two terraces: one out front and one in the courtyard, away from the street.

Name: Sharma Ji
Description: At the helm of several establishments, Manoj Sharma has boldly set about freeing Indian food from its hackneyed clichés (like the predictable tandoori or korma chicken). In a spruce, modern, colourful venue, his authentic bistronomic cooking delves into an Indian score that has shaken off its traditional visual and technical fetters. Examples include masala fried chicken, with coconut and curry leaves; long sweet peppers stuffed with masala cheese and yoghurt sauce; caramelised ginger cake. Simmered and crafted with lashings of spices and aromatic herbs, Manoj’s delicious dishes nonetheless find favour with delicate western palates. The lunch menu is a bargain. The à la carte menu changes regularly.

Name: La fleur de Sel
Description: The initiative by this pair, chef Willy Lardry and maître d' Edwin Smietanski, to open their restaurant here is most welcome. Both hail from Le Creusot but met while working for Yohann Chapuis in Tournus. The interior is inspired in part by nature (with, in particular, wallpaper depicting a forest in the mist). The chef, working alone in the kitchen, shows undeniable maturity. Delicacy and finesse are the order of the day, for example, the lovely courgette flower with cod stuffing and the olive oil sabayon accompanying the cod tournedos, or the mackerel and its marinated cucumber ravioli.

Name: Le Bistrot de Cancale
Address: à Port-Mer, 5 rue Eugène-et-Auguste-Feyen, Cancale, 35260, France
Description: Run by Hugo Roellinger, this restaurant is located opposite the beach at Port-Mer with its small boats bobbing at anchor and Mont-Saint-Michel visible in the distance. The menu features dishes such as oysters, shellfish, langoustines, sole with a caramelised jus, turbot cooked on the bone, lobster cooked over hot coals – excellent fish, distinguished by its remarkable freshness and often seasoned with Olivier Roellinger's famous spice mixes. There is a beautiful terrace with a sea view and, inside, knick-knacks related to Brittany and fishing create a chic and modernised seaside bistro vibe that is enhanced by a 1930s fresco depicting a scene from life in the port of Saint-Malo.

Name: L'Ouzeri
Description: Saganaki cheese, gyro merida, myzithropita (cheesecake), spanakopita – the menu gives it away: this is French-Greek chef Mikaela Liaroutsos's Greek taverna, and it's just a stone's throw from the original restaurant Etsi that made her name. The food is served as a series of mezes, to savour as you dream of Greek holidays, past or future. The traditional songs playing in the background might tempt you to pull out a sirtaki step after a glass of ouzo.

Name: La Cage aux Fleurs
Description: Flowers and colours abound in this spruce-looking bistro, both in the decor (floral wallpaper, varnished porcelain knick-knacks) and on the plate: tuna tartare, pumpkin seeds, grilled butternut condiment, anchovies with green pepper; roast fillet of sea bass, panisse (chickpea fries), saffron, fennel. This cuisine in tune with the zeitgeist is delivered by a professional couple – themselves the offspring of restaurant owners – who work in tandem. French classics that are the winegrowers' favourites and cuts of meat to share are also present and correct.

Name: La Colombe
Description: At the foot of Mont Ventoux surrounded by vineyards, this gourmet dove coos a delicious melody. Chef Christophe Schuffenecker (formerly of the star-rated Château de Mazan) serves modern, spot-on dishes, blessedly free of superfluous extras, such as Sarrians pigeon with geranium-perfumed mashed carrots. When the weather is fine, make a beeline for the terrace shaded by awnings overlooking the vineyards. The stylish interior sports bare beams and a large Provençal fireplace, as well as a permanent art exhibition.

Name: L'Embarcadère
Address: 15 avenue de la Plage, Jassans-Riottier, 01480, France
Description: Georges Blanc's new restaurant, on the banks of the Saône, is a cross between a chic guinguette and a contemporary brasserie. The food is traditional but trendy with dishes like frogs' legs, poached free - range egg with whiting, and Bresse chicken.

Name: La Mère Germaine
Description: Jean Cocteau used to eat at this local institution, which has been serving fresh fish and seafood since 1938. It is lovely just to sit on the terrace and gaze out over the harbour!

Name: Boccafine
Description: A small, listed village on the Cap Corse road is home to this demure restaurant, hidden by a curtain of Virginia Creeper and tall plane trees. The chef unveils his know-how as he crafts painstakingly sourced, local and seasonal ingredients, illustrated by ultra-fresh croaker, pancetta and pork jus in a surf and turf recipe of wondrous harmony. Love at first bite.

Name: L'Affable
Description: In the centre of Cannes, this contemporary bistro is always busy and, indeed, it has much to recommend it. First and foremost its menu: courgette flower fritters, cod aioli, rack of lamb roasted with thyme… and the classic Grand Marnier soufflé, the house speciality.

Name: L'Espace PH3
Description: This is the Henriroux family’s second venture, created directly inside La Pyramide. The tasteful interior displays a strong plant focus in line with the menu’s healthy, wellness leaning, without forgetting pedigree classics, like calf’s head and pink praline. Everything is in the energetic hands of a charismatic team. Bags of vitality and flavour!

Name: Asterales
Address: Hôtel du Golf, Les Ritons, 784 route du Clos-de-la-Balme, Corrençon-en-Vercors, 38250, France
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Wheelchair access
Description: Poetically named after an order of flowering plants, this tasteful restaurant sports a low-key alpine style. Chef Ludovic Nardozza’s painstakingly crafted cooking showcases his favourite, first-class ingredients: roasted langoustines in marjoram butter, girolles and vin jaune bisque; John Dory lacquered in wild fennel, courgette flowers and grilled cuttlefish; apple like an upside-down pie with local honey and black cardamon… Service with a smile. Pleasant guestrooms make it an ideal basecamp to explore Vercors.

Name: Premnord
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: The restaurant of the Prieuré-Roch estate rises up to greet visitors with its distinctive wood and steel U-shaped architecture, whose centre is graced with a vast patio overlooking the vineyards. Indoors are a parquet-floored lounge, a bar decked in light wood and a spacious contemporary dining room with immense floor-to-ceiling windows. Chef Céline Dedinger (who boasts stints with Thomas Collomb at the Rôtisserie du Chambertin and the Maison des Cariatides) crafts a modern score based on mainly local ingredients (whose exact source is indicated on the menu) in line with the seasons.

Name: Campelli
Description: This diminutive restaurant with a midnight-blue and gold façade boasts a chic yet understated decor (velvet banquettes, wooden chairs upholstered in matching velvet, exposed stone walls) – all the better to showcase the creative cuisine and multicultural culinary experience of chef Vartivar Jarkezian. Firmly rooted in French tradition, his cooking also draws discreetly on the influences and pantry of the Middle East (cumin, pistachio, turmeric, yoghurt sauce).

Name: Godaille
Description: Godaille in French slang means feasting and making merry among good friends. So let's get to it and tuck into this invigorating, flavoursome cuisine! This eatery run by a group of pals gives pride of place to spices and fresh herbs, in dishes such as fried chicken with super-soft meat in a crispy golden crumb, alongside a ginger-lemon sauce; bouchot mussels are served with a coconut-green curry sauce and Thai herbs. The pleasant, slightly retro interior is complemented by a lovely bunch of fresh flowers on each table. A fine selection of natural and organic wines (including some orange wines).

Name: jjii
Description: Exposed stone walls, visible electric cables and streamed music in the long, narrow dining space, and, at work in the open kitchen, Korean chef Jaywook Hur. Going solo in the kitchen, he can be seen cooking up modern, creative French cuisine with a few Asian touches (on this particular evening, they include tempura, sesame, kimchi), as his mystery menu unfolds: a surprising and beautifully fresh starter such as sea bass, kimchi and avocado, accompanied by raspberries and a quenelle of smoked herring roe; or the oh-so-tender matured Simmental sirloin, fennel, beetroot and its bold jus.

Name: Le Point d'Origine
Description: Situated opposite the Abreuvoir – the ‘Watering Place’, framed by its famous sculpted horses, this old bourgeois abode is now home to a delicatessen, a wine shop and a restaurant, enthusiastically run by a dynamic team. The restaurant occupies a lovely conservatory with herringbone parquet flooring and an unrivalled view of the Abreuvoir. The chef crafts modern, well-polished dishes: organic œuf parfait, green lentils from Le Puy, smoked herring, parsley sauce and pickled shallots; confit of turbot in Mat-Khen pepper, braised fennel and citrus notes. A stroll in the park after your meal is just the ticket!

Name: L'Atelier de Damien
Description: Just 10min from the historic town centre, this restaurant is to be found where you would least expect it: on the first floor of an unremarkable building that, so we're told, was once a fire station. The contemporary setting is definitely appealing, as is the cuisine of the chef, who has an impressive track record (Alain Ducasse in Paris and Py-R in Toulouse). The three set menus, which echo today's culinary standards, certainly whet the appetite: roast onions and grilled mackerel; glazed pork belly, a meat jus, potatoes, leeks and peppers. Cordial service.

Name: Des Terres
Description: A buzzy casual vibe depicts this neighbourhood bistro in the 20th arrondissement of Paris. In the company of natural wines displayed on a bookshelf, you will joyfully do justice to the chef’s competently crafted fare: cauliflower in a herring, hazelnut and green oil sauce; roast beetroot, Colonnata pork and creamy goat’s cheese. Seasonal nosh and a bargain-priced lunch menu.

Name: Omma
Address: 38 rue de la Poste, Roussillon, 84220, France
Description: Taking in the Luberon and the famous ochre cliffs of Roussillon, the view from this restaurant is nothing short of spectacular! As for the food, the short, seasonal menu proposes bistronomy-style dishes with Provençal influences: crispy aubergine, baba ganoush with coriander and fromage blanc with lime; grilled Ventoux pork, peppers stuffed with Coco de Paimpol beans, piperade and apricot condiment; Musquée de Provence pumpkin confit with vanilla, sponge cake with pistachios. A moment of culinary bliss far from the crowds of tourists.

Name: Nananère
Description: Sometimes it is fun to revisit your childhood! Run by the former owners of Le P'tit Cageot, this restaurant has a playful decor that draws on comic strips and action figures of characters such as Spiderman and Buzz Lightyear. Things get serious, however, when it comes to the delicious food. The menu abounds with French classics (leeks in vinaigrette, saucisson brioché, poire belle Hélène), as well as dishes catering to teenage diners (mac & cheese and burgers) and fresh house-made pasta – everything is professionally prepared using quality ingredients. Large terrace. No reservations for parties of fewer than six people.

Name: Kitchen by Madame Rêve
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: Restored from head to toe, the iconic Haussmannian Louvre Post Office building is also home to a luxury hotel and a classy neo-brasserie, nestled under an impressive ceiling. The menu is divided into culinary themes in a tongue-in-cheek poke at your usual restaurant codes: healthy trendy, veg out, flashback, etc. The onus is definitely on unstuffy pleasure!

Name: Dame Augustine
Description: This is the other restaurant of chef Lilian Douchet, who hails from Bordeaux: you can expect a laid-back atmosphere and a veranda-style space with the feel of a small brasserie. He serves several set menus, including a good-value lunch deal. Diners savour dishes such as a selection of heirloom tomatoes, fresh herb pesto, parmesan buttercrumb biscuits and mizuna sorbet, or a fillet of whiting simmered with coco de Paimpol beans and a lemon thyme emulsion. A welcome address in this residential area.

Name: Guefen
Description: At Ohad Amzallag's restaurant a stone's throw from Place de la République, diners sample his cooking in convivial fashion, all seated at a large marble table d'hôte. The Israeli chef serves Middle Eastern-influenced cuisine that gives pride of place to seafood ingredients and fermented vegetables, such as oyster cream with mint granita, chilli and koshu; lobster and agnolotti with ricotta, spinach and sage cream; and a delicious cheesecake with caramelised garum.

Name: Pamparigouste - Le Couvent des Minimes
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: In addition to his fine dining restaurant, chef Louis Gachet lovingly oversees this upscale bistro. The space is soothing and relaxing, plus there is a dining room-cum-terrace, whose picture windows are opened fully in fine weather. The menu is a skilful blend of traditional favourites and contemporary dishes with a smattering of Provençal touches.

Name: Gaua
Description: Chef Benoit Sarthou (who held a Michelin star at Moulin d'Alotz) has chosen to make his restaurant a celebration of conviviality and the "night" (gaua in Basque). This former garage has been turned into a trendy industrial-style lounge with a central bar-counter and large open kitchen. Share an array of tapas in an ambience fostered by skilfully curated playlists. Think comfort and fusion food, with various ingredients matured or cooked over an open flame.

Name: Colvert
Description: Revealed by the French Top Chef TV show, Arnaud Baptiste and his flamboyant moustache and numerous tattoos, is something of a media darling. He has set up shop in a vintage street corner bistro (banquettes, bistro chairs, tightly packed tables, bare stone walls, cement tiled floor and a counter which now serves standing customers) in the somewhat touristy, but nonetheless picturesque 6th district of Paris. Arnaud happily crafts market-fresh, bistronomic fare. The seasonal menu is suitably concise and hits the spot every time: confit of cod, hollandaise sauce, courgettes and absinthe gel or figs, served roasted, raw and in pickles with a fig sorbet and ice cream.

Name: Le Cercle Guiraud
Description: In the heart of the village, this traditional eatery offers a choice between a dining room whose countrified décor is dotted with the odd contemporary touch, or, in fine weather, a terrace shaded by mulberry plane trees that commands an exquisite view as far as Château Guiraud, which owns the restaurant. Yoann Amado, former chef of Maison Darroze in Langon, and his pastry chef partner, Juliette Bonnard, craft a scrumptious gourmet score that hits the spot every time: truly flavoursome oxheart tomatoes, burrata of goat’s cheese, infusion of tomato water and verbena; trout marinated in miso and confit, baby spinach shoots, beurre blanc of pike roe; vanilla-flavoured crème brûlée, apricots and an exquisite last-minute lemon thyme-flavoured sorbet.

Name: La Table du 5
Address: Hôtel 5 Terres, 11 place de l'Hôtel-de-Ville, Barr, 67140, France
Description: This contemporary restaurant located within the 5 Terres Hotel looks out over the magnificent Renaissance town hall (1640). In a light-filled space done out in premium materials, you can enjoy contemporary cuisine that brings the best out of carefully sourced local ingredients. The wine list is particularly impressive, featuring hundreds of organic and biodynamic labels.

Name: 19.20 by Norbert Tarayre
Address: Prince de Galles, 33 avenue George-V, Paris, 75008, France
Description: Built in 1928, the Prince de Galles is a legendary jewel of the Parisian Art Deco movement. It has chosen to democratise luxury hotel cuisine by entrusting its kitchens to Norbert Tarayre, the firebrand chef discovered on French TV show Top Chef in 2012. In a cosy setting that pays tribute to artistic life in Paris, the chef serves up traditional cuisine that channels the tasty regional cooking of yesteryear: grated carrot salad, leeks in vinaigrette, celeriac in remoulade dressing, pork shoulder and pommes Anna, salmon tournedos – not to mention the dessert trolley. It's all lovingly prepared and delivered. Incredibly reasonable price of the menu.

Name: Achillée
Description: Pieter Riedijk, previously chef at Le Montgomerie (K2 Altitude in Courchevel), has come down into the valley to open this bistro serving "food for sharing". In an inviting and convivial rustic-style decor, he focuses on quality ingredients from the terroir, which he cooks simply: cep and aubergine marmalade, to be spread on toast; roast pork, straw potatoes and a good béarnaise sauce with plenty of vinegar; rhubarb meringue. His goal is to make the most of the treasure trove of seasonal produce the region has to offer in spring and summer. He selects local farm ingredients as well as picking some himself.

Name: Château Fage - La Maison des Vignes
Description: Built in the white stone typical of the region, this 19C château standing proud amid the vineyards is now a hotel-restaurant. The contemporary cuisine, at once straightforward and bold, wins diners over. Every ingredient is carefully selected and expertly prepared, for dishes such as fillet of pink sea bream, shellfish sauce vierge and mussels with samphire, or the appetising dessert trolley. Accompanied by wines from the estate.

Name: Mansouria
Description: Just a stone's throw from the Bastille, this restaurant has proved popular with fans of Moroccan cuisine for over 40 years. You are instantly transported by the aromas of this venerable institution, which is now run by the daughter of the founder. In a discreetly North African decor, traditional tagines and couscous are served alongside a host of lesser-known dishes, such as pigeon pastilla and traditional spicy lamb mourouzia "Al-Andalus" with sweet notes supplied by honey and sultanas – the house speciality. Top-quality ingredients and attentive service make for a delicious culinary voyage.

Name: Baillotte
Description: Perhaps chef Satoshi Amitsu (previously at Georges Blanc) is just being modest when he uses the term "semi-gourmet" cuisine on his website, because this bistro with an alluring red frontage easily holds its own against other restaurants. Deploying the precision for which the Japanese are renowned, the chef delights diners with French cuisine replete with colours and contrasts, backed up by meticulous jus and sauces: flame-charred mackerel, fregola sarda, beetroot, raspberry, walnut and shiso vinaigrette; veal, mushrooms, chervil root, quince condiment, full-bodied gravy. There's a good selection of wines by the glass, not just the usual favourites, with expert advice from the service team.

Name: Abîme - L'Auberge du Pont
Description: This long-established inn stands by a bridge spanning the gorge – the Chéran River flows a few hundred metres below! A native of the area, the chef likes to work with regional ingredients he sources from local producers. Even amateur mushroom foragers are welcome to offer up their pick of the day. His squash risotto, fricassee of shiitake, polypore and oyster mushrooms is a prime example of his culinary style, which is geared toward plants and vegetables and the interplay of textures. A "discovery menu" made up of several courses is available in the evening and at weekends. Appealing lunchtime set menu.

Name: Le Petit Basson
Address: 4 rue de la Madeleine, Troyes, 10000, France
Description: This is the first restaurant of chef Yann Caputo, who is a big fan of vegetables; not only does he grow them in his kitchen garden, but he also has them tattooed on his arm. No wonder, then, that he refers to his new venture as a "garden bistro", even though he also cooks meat (and wild-caught fish). The reasonably priced lunch menu is a steal: lentils from Champagne, smoked bacon chantilly, watercress from the garden; wild sea bream, turnips from the garden, coconut milk, ginger, lemongrass. The evening menu features more high-end ingredients (eg langoustines, wild sea bass) – these, too, served with vegetables from the chef's garden. Charming natural decor (strings of garlic, wheat and dried flowers adorn the walls) with wooden furnishings.

Name: Twist & Buckle
Address: 29-31 Chatham Road South, Tsim Sha Tsui, Hong Kong
Description: Two young South Americans opened this shop specialising in churros. Besides the traditional version with cinnamon sugar, also try them glazed, in dips like dulce de leche and salted caramel, or even in sundaes with ice cream.

Name: Celestial Court
Address: 2F, Sheraton Hotel, 20 Nathan Road, Tsim Sha Tsui, Hong Kong
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: The astute chef has over 25 years of experience and was brought up in a family who owned a dried seafood business. His shrewd insights on sourcing and preparing those gourmet ingredients are reflected in the menu. The speciality roast whole suckling pig with pearl barley and black truffles needs pre-ordering. Scrambled egg with lobster and caviar is another highlight. The windowless dining room is nicely furnished with rich wood accents.

Name: Ippoh
Description: Now run by the fifth generation, this family business rooted in Osaka still strictly follows the traditional rules of making tempura. The owner-chef insists on battering and frying every morsel himself without delegating his duty. Seafood is flown in daily from Osaka and Toyosu fish market and they use flavourless safflower oil, so as not to overpower the ingredients’ natural tastes. The sauce is made to a secret recipe. Omakase is the best way to go. Bookings are essential.

Name: Fong Kei
Description: A longstanding shop offering Chinese cakes and biscuits. The almond cakes and egg rolls stand out.

Name: Fat Boy
Address: 3 Hau Fook Street, Tsim Sha Tsui, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR China
Description: Hong Kong-style snacks including octopus, pork liver & turkey gizzard marinated in soy sauce. Sweet sauce and mustard add to the flavour. The combo set offers great value with three signature items.

Name: Golden Bauhinia Sang Kee
Address: GF, Expo Galleria, Hong Kong Convention and Exhibition Centre, 1 Expo Drive, Wan Chai, Hong Kong
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Great view,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: This space was taken over in 2021 by Sang Kee, a famous Cantonese restaurant with over 40 years of history. In addition to the same specialities from their Wan Chai flagship, the menu here boasts old-time artisan dishes exclusive to this branch. Barbecue chicken liver with pork is hard to find elsewhere; pan-fried deboned fourfinger threadfin with scallion and sea salt entices with its deep umami. The panoramic harbour views are also delightful.

Name: Tsui Hang Village (Tsim Sha Tsui)
Address: Shop 507, 5F, FoodLoft, Mira Place One, 132 Nathan Road, Tsim Sha Tsui, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR China
Description: A staple of the Tsim Sha Tsui restaurant scene since 1970s, this place is famous for its authentic Cantonese and Shun Tak fare, namely its bestselling honey-glazed char siu pork, braised beef ribs and shredded chicken, alongside some original creations by the head chef, such as fried king prawns in mango sauce topped with caviar. The dim sum is also good. Watching the chefs work their magic through the large window is all part of the experience.

Name: Keung Kee
Address: 406 Lockhart Road, Wan Chai, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR China
Description: After moving to this new spot, this simple shop boasts better comfort and a bigger menu. But signatures like glutinous rice with preserved meat, wok-fried rice rolls, and pork bone congee remain as tasty as ever.

Name: Ngao Kei Ka Lei Chon (Macau)
Address: GF, 1 Rua de Cinco de Outubro, Macau, Macau
Description: Don’t judge a book by its cover because the simple neon signs outside do not reflect the quality of food and service at this friendly, well-run noodle shop. The key draw is the swimmer crab congee – crabs are dressed à la minute and burst with seafood flavours, while the creamy congee imparts a rich aroma of rice. Other recommendations include braised E-fu noodles with crab roe, beef brisket in clear broth, and curry chicken with coconut milk.

Name: Mak Kee (May Ka Mansion)
Address: Shop 1, May Ka Mansion, 21 Fort Street, North Point, Hong Kong
Description: This shop serves Shanghainese delicacies made fresh daily, such as pot-stickers, pan-fried pork buns and sour and hot noodle soup. Scallion pancakes are available from 3pm until they run out.

Name: Lord Stow's Bakery (Rua do Tassara)
Address: 1 Rua do Tassara, Coloane Town Square, Coloane, Macau
Description: For over 30 years, the store has prided itself on its Portuguese egg tarts that have a crisp shell and silky, smooth filling. Tarts are made from scratch, baked throughout the day and sold fresh from the oven. Takeout only.

Name: China Tang
Address: Shop 411-413, 4F, Landmark Atrium, 15 Queen's Road Central, Central, Hong Kong
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: This handsome restaurant was conceived and designed by the late Sir David Tang as a sister to the London branch, and mixes traditional Chinese art with contemporary Western design. Tables are set closely together and there are several private rooms. Dishes from Beijing, Sichuan and Canton feature and dim sum is popular. The chef has introduced a more modern element to the menu.

Name: Beanmountain
Address: GF, 1 Canal Road East, Causeway Bay, Hong Kong
Description: For over 20 years, sugar fiends have been getting their fix of Chinese-style sweets here – from traditional crowd-pleasers such as put chai ko and Hakka tea cake made with stinkvine to novelty treats like mango sticky rice ball.

Name: Plaisance by Mauro Colagreco
Address: 1F, 1 Duddell Street, Central, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR China
Description: Mother of pearl finishes, turquoise accents and a whirlpool of metal fish sculptures introduce the ocean theme. Begin the meal with Chef Mauro's grandma's recipe – house-made bread with his favourite olive oil. The seafood-led menu delivers spellbinding dishes that incorporate the best ingredients from around the world alongside local vegetables, all finessed by solid French skills. Ask the sommelier to pick a wine for you.

Name: Sabah
Address: Shop 1, GF, Pao Woo Mansion, 177-179 Wan Chai Road, Wan Chai, Hong Kong
Description: Sabah, a staple of Wan Chai’s restaurant scene for 18 years, shuttered its doors in 2019 before reopening here with the same kitchen team. Both the room and the menu are downsized, but signatures like bak kut teh, beef rendang, and seafood laksa remain, tasting just like before. Boneless Hainan chicken rice boasts bouncy skin and velvety juicy flesh. Even the trio of dips and pearl rice are also hard to find fault with.

Name: The Steak House
Address: GF, Regent, 18 Salisbury Road, Tsim Sha Tsui, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR China
Description: The iconic Regent Hong Kong has reopened with several new F&B outlets. One of them is The Steak House commanding sweeping harbour views through its tall windows. As its name suggests, the menu revolves around steak – from Italy, Spain, Korea, Japan, Australia, and the U.S. The Moroccan chef ages his own beef - ask the servers. Season your favourite cuts with rock salt, charcoal salt, yuzu salt or the array of sauces and mustards on offer.

Name: Cafe Bau
Address: Shop 8, Podium 1F, J Residence, 60 Johnston Road, Wan Chai, Hong Kong
Description: Cafe Bau, a new dining concept by the self-proclaimed “Demon Chef” Alvin Leung, is styled like a vintage brasserie dripping in retro glam. Sit at the bar and watch the bartender concoct exquisite beverages. On to the food, order the 3-course menu for traditional European fare, or opt for  the 8-course tasting extravaganza for more innovative, adventurous dishes. Local produce like oysters and fish is used to good effect. Service is off-the-cuff and to-the-point.

Name: Ho Lee Fook
Description: Walls covered in gilded maneki-neko, mahjong tiles, pop art and red Chinese floral motifs make this a bold, unorthodox spot for a fun night out. The 80s Canto-pop soundtrack is also a proud expression of its local DNA. The open kitchen on ground level is a spectacle to behold and its creative Cantonese cooking harnesses bold distinctive flavours and wok hei. Try the crispy three-yellow chicken with sand ginger dip, and other wok-fries. Check ahead for dishes that need pre-ordering.

Name: She Wong Hei
Address: 59 Percival Street, Causeway Bay, Hong Kong
Description: The manager that ran the famous snake soup shop She Wong Yee opened this restaurant on the same street. The classic snake soup is reworked with a slightly altered consistency, alongside fish maw, chicken, hand-sliced pork, dried tangerine peel, wood ear fungus and shiitake mushroom. Of course, you can still order barbecue meats, and glutinous rice to go with the soup. Duck liver sausage with snappy casing is certainly worth trying.

Name: Yuè (Gold Coast)
Address: LG, Gold Coast Hotel, 1 Castle Peak Road, Gold Coast, Tuen Mun, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR China
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Garden or park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: It’s not often one can enjoy Cantonese food surrounded by verdant scenery but here on the ground floor of the Gold Coast hotel that’s exactly what you get as this comfortable restaurant looks out onto a delightful garden. The menu includes both traditional and more contemporary dishes and it’s worth seeking out the chef’s specialities such as barbecued pork and double boiled pork lung soup with almond milk and fish maw, and deep-fried chicken with shrimp paste.

Name: The Swiss Chalet
Address: GF, 8 Hart Avenue, Tsim Sha Tsui, Hong Kong
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus
Description: Despite moving next door, the room still retains the same quaint Alpine chalet ambiance with wood furniture and beams set nicely against whitewashed walls. The classic Swiss menu covers a variety of cured meats and sausages, over 20 cheeses, and of course the unmissable fondue made with five cheeses and kirsch, to be paired with their extensive selection of Swiss wines. Thinly sliced veal with white mushrooms in a cream sauce is also worth trying.

Name: Ki Tsui
Address: 135 Fa Yuen Street, Mong Kok, Hong Kong
Description: Despite the small size, this shop offers a wide array of Cantonese traditional puddings and pastries like Xiaofeng cake and walnut cookies.

Name: Kika
Address: GF, 11A Travessa da Sé, Macau, Macau
Description: Pop in for an artisan Japanese gelato. Customers are spoiled for exotic choices here – crown melon from Shizuoka, Hokkaido 3.6 milk, Hojicha, and, of course, their famous ultra-strong matcha green tea for die-hard tea lovers.

Name: Terrazza
Address: Shop 201, 2F, Galaxy Hotel, Galaxy, Estrada da Baía de Nossa Senhora da Esperança, Cotai, Macau
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: The menu covers the culinary traditions of every region in Italy and is updated every three months to keep it fresh. Guests get to see how the food is prepared through the glass wall. Pizza dough, tagliatelle, ravioli and tagliolini are made from scratch in-house and the extensive wine list is well worth exploring. Add in exceedingly comfy chairs and warm, welcoming service and you have a great place for a relaxing meal.

Name: Joyful Dessert House
Address: Shop 2-3, GF, Ngai Hing Mansion, 74 Hak Po Street, Mong Kok, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR China
Description: Come for beautifully plated Western desserts, such as waffles, chocolate fondant and velvety shaved ice. Recommendations include mango Napoleon, caramelised pineapple sorbet, and green tea fondant à la mode.

Name: Carbone
Address: 9F, 33 Wyndham Street, Central, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR China
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus
Description: A nod to Manhattan’s American-Italian diners circa 1950s, this colourful spot celebrates the era in everything from the floor tiles and chandeliers, to the cutlery and servers’ uniforms. In the same way, the menu embraces classics like pastas and steaks, such as the signature Tasmanian lamb tomahawk. Portion sizes are more American than Italian, enough for a few to share. House-made limoncello makes great apéritifs and digestifs.

Name: Fishball Man (To Kwa Wan)
Address: GF, 50 Tin Kwong Road, To Kwa Wan, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR China
Description: Though local snacks like shaomai and cheong fun are offered, its eponymous speciality remains the most popular. Besides the spicy variety, the springy and flavourful white fish balls drizzled in chilli oil are unmissable.

Name: Cornerstone
Address: 49 Hollywood Road, Central, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR China
Description: Owner-chef Shane Osborn of Arcane fame calls it an ‘Australian café’ – in fact, it feels more like a hip bistro with its faux-industrial décor.
