The small menu is a tapestry of global culinary cultures, including Aussie, European and Asian favourites. Though it changes a few times each month to keep things fresh, dishes are always competitively priced and loaded with big flavours and pleasing textures. Online reservations only.

Name: Hung Hom Pancake
Address: Shop 2, Polly Court, Taku Street, Hung Hom, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR China
Description: For over 40 years, this neighbourhood shop has provided the childhood memories of many. Pancakes, waffles and egg waffles are all made to order. Tricolour egg waffles in plain, chocolate and matcha flavours particularly stand out.

Name: Giando
Address: Shop 1, GF, Tower 1, Starcrest, 9 Star Street, Wan Chai, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR China
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Brunch,Car park,Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Italian chef Gianni Caprioli owns several restaurants in Hong Kong but this one, tucked away in a quiet corner between Wan Chai and Admiralty, is his jewel. Besides the booths along one side of the smart dining room, outdoor seating is also prized for an al-fresco Italian feast or just a glass of Italian wine pre- or post-dinner. Expect to see dishes from all over Italy, such as hand-rolled strozzapreti pasta, or Milanese-style veal chop.

Name: Owl's
Address: GF, 32 Mody Road, Tsim Sha Tsui, Hong Kong
Location: Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR China
Description: You’ll need to wait as the homemade choux pastries are filled on order with cream and custard of different flavours but, rest assured, the wait is worth it. Check out the occasional limited time offers. Take-out only.

Name: Ving Kei (Macau)
Address: GF, 47 Rua da Tercena, Macau, Macau
Description: Apart from the signature cold or hot tofu pudding and soy milk, it also provides tofu products, squid and noodles.

Name: Hop Yik Tai
Address: 121 Kweilin Street, Sham Shui Po, Hong Kong
Location: Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR China
Description: The menu at this always busy shop features Hong Kong-style snacks like fish balls, pork skin and braised radish. The hugely popular rice rolls are silky-smooth, with a hint of richness from the lard.

Name: Cuisine Cuisine at The Mira
Address: 3F, The Mira Hotel, 118 Nathan Road, Tsim Sha Tsui, Hong Kong
Location: Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR China
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: The striking chandelier with hundreds of glowing glass globes is set nicely against the calming green colour scheme and verdant views. Cantonese classics underpinned by solid, traditional techniques are revitalised by creative use of ingredients and modern twists. On top of special dim sum such as crispy frog legs with peppered salt, try also Mrs. Song’s fish soup made with fresh grouper fillet. Wine pairings are thoughtfully matched.

Name: Heimat
Address: 8F, 33 Wyndham Street, Central, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR China
Location: Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR China
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Wheelchair access
Description: Heimat translates as “homeland”. After working in some prestigious kitchens, the German owner-chef Peter Find reinterprets classics from his home country with quality ingredients, dexterous care and much sophistication. The 6-course tasting menu takes diners on a journey across Germany with flavours from his childhood memories. A shorter 3-course menu is available at lunch. And who can resist the gummy bear trolley at the end?

Name: La Brasserie
Address: GF, Lyndhurst Building, 23-29 Lyndhurst Terrace, Central, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR China
Location: Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR China
Description: As its name suggests, this restaurant serves authentic French fare in a convivial atmosphere. Seafood choices abound – from smoked salmon and bouillabaisse to the seafood platter. Meat lovers should check out the pâtés in the charcuterie section. A visit to the pastry counter is a must for classics such as éclairs and opera cake as much as novel creations like genmaicha St Honoré. The wine list boasts a good range of by-the-glass options.

Name: Chiado
Address: Shop 2206, 2F, The Londoner, Estrada do lstmo, Cotai, Macau
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: As well as a neighbourhood of Lisbon, Chiado is celebrity chef Henrique Sá Pessoa’s first dining concept outside Portugal. The room is modern and cosy, setting the mood for a feast of Portuguese classics oozing with understated elegance and robust flavours. Choose the 6-course degustation menu to sample all the chef’s signature dishes. Don’t miss the boneless suckling pig that is slow-cooked then grilled, boasting crispy skin and silky meat.

Name: Ho Kee Dessert (To Kwa Wan)
Address: Shop 111 & 122, GF, I-Feng Mansions, 237A To Kwa Wan Road, To Kwa Wan, Hong Kong
Location: Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR China
Description: The staple in Mong Kok for over 30 years moved to this location in 2020. Rest assured their traditional sweet soups like black sesame paste, and glutinous rice balls in ginger syrup taste as good as ever.

Name: Clarence
Address: 25F, H Code, 45 Pottinger Street, Central, Hong Kong
Location: Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR China
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: After working and living in Asia for over a decade, chef Olivier Elzer founded this restaurant that aims to allow new ways of enjoying French cuisine. He minted an original concept known as “Yakifrenchy” – a menu that serves French classics like duck confit, frogs’ legs and escargots on skewers, like Japanese yakitori. Local family table culture is taken to another level with meat and fish cooked whole on the bone, perfect for sharing.

Name: Testina
Location: Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR China
Description: Aptly named after its signature pig’s head dish, Testina is the collaboration between the Milanese trattoria Trippa Milano and a local hospitality group. Championing a nose-to-tail philosophy, the kitchen team serves every part of an animal to great effect. Besides pig’s head, expect to see tripe, bone marrow and veal tongue on the menu. For an authentic taste of Trippa Milano’s cooking, try homemade tagliatelle with duck ragù.

Name: Jing Alley
Address: GF, Dawning House, 145 Connaught Road Central, Sheung Wan, Hong Kong
Location: Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR China
Description: The chef’s modern Sichuanese fare is made with ingredients from around the world: duck blood curd from Chengdu, chillies from Yunnan, pork from Japan, chitterlings from Spain… The signature water-boiled black pearl fish uses a green chilli and pork bone stock that doesn’t look red or oily like traditional ones; the freshwater fish with springy flesh also adds to the texture and flavour. The chitterlings with mixed chillies are addictively tasty.

Name: One Harbour Road
Address: 7-8F, Grand Hyatt Hotel, 1 Harbour Road, Wan Chai, Hong Kong
Location: Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR China
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Great view,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: The split-level room affords sweeping harbour views, while the high ceiling and sound of the fountain exude serenity. Exquisite Cantonese cooking is the name of the game here. Start with the crispy and appetising deep-fried shiitake in osmanthus honey glaze; for mains, opt for Wuxi-style Boston lobster that is spicy, tangy and sustainably sourced. Some dishes are available in smaller portions. Detailed and thoughtful service adds to the experience.

Name: Toritama
Address: GF, Greenville, 2 Glenealy, Central, Hong Kong
Location: Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR China
Description: Tokyo restaurants keep opening branches in Hong Kong and this time it’s all about yakitori. Seats are limited so it’s worth booking ahead and asking for the counter to watch the expert preparation in the kitchen. 40-day-old chickens are used, and 28 different parts of the birds are offered – rare cuts such as sweetbread may need pre-ordering. Pickles made with different produce according to the season make the perfect side dish for the skewers.

Name: Wing
Address: 29F, The Wellington, 198 Wellington Street, Central, Hong Kong
Location: Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR China
Description: The second venture from owner-chef Vicky Cheng who runs the well-acclaimed Vea upstairs, Wing is named after his Chinese name, meaning eternity. The tasting menu features contemporary Chinese courses made with mostly local ingredients but underpinned by European techniques. He reinterprets classic recipes and familiar flavours with creative twists and playful food combinations. Online reservations open at midnight for up to 28 days ahead.

Name: The Ritz-Carlton Café
Address: GF, The Ritz-Carlton, Galaxy, Estrada da Baía de Nossa Senhora da Esperança, Cotai, Macau
Description: Tiles, mirrors and marble are used to great effect in this bright, lively French brasserie with an all-day dining concept. It prides itself not only on its friendly service, but also the array of classic French food on offer. Besides the daily special, steak is big on the menu with many prime cuts to choose from. Seafood lovers should try freshly shucked oysters. Round out your dinner with the spectacular tableside Grand Marnier flambéed crepes.

Name: Ami
Address: Shop 302, 3F, Alexandra House, 18 Chater Road, Central, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR China
Location: Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR China
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Brunch,Car park,Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Ami, decorated on a forest theme, offers a fine dining experience in a casual setting. On top of tasting menus, all-day à la carte choices abound – Gallic classics, plates to share and bar snacks are all up for grabs. The enthusiastic, young chef from Southern France imbues the menu with novel ideas, such as yellow chicken cooked two ways: poached breast and grilled leg with morels and a vin jaune sauce. Made-to-order orange blossom soufflé is fluffy and custardy.

Name: The Kitchen
Address: 3F, Grand Lisboa Hotel, Avenida de Lisboa, Macau, Macau
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Counter dining,Interesting wine list,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: Beef is the star of the show at this handsome, masculine dining room which also houses a sushi bar, a salad bar and a live fish tank. Choose from prime cuts from the U. S. and Wagyu from Kagoshima and Australia; then have it seared on an open flame to your desired 'doneness' and pair it with one of the 17,000-plus wine labels from around the world. Bread is baked daily and appetisers are made in the open kitchen à la minute.

Name: Imperial Court
Address: GF, MGM Macau, Avenida Dr. Sun Yat Sen, NAPE, Macau, Macau
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: On the same floor as the hotel’s VIP lobby, this sleek, contemporary dining room wows guests with a vividly carved Chinese dragon entwined around a marble pillar. The head chef has over 20 years of experience and updates the menu regularly to star seasonal dishes. Try his crispy-skin fried baby pigeon, and dim sum with a creative twist – order as few or as many pieces as you like. The impressive wine list boasts over 2,000 labels.

Name: Mok Yee Kei
Description: Offering Serradura pudding and ice cream. The signature durian ice cream comes with Musang King, D24 and Mon Tong choices.

Name: A Lorcha
Address: 289 Rua do Almirante Sergio, Macau, Macau
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Wheelchair access
Description: Business is booming at this friendly restaurant near Barra Temple as regulars just can’t get enough of the hearty food from a kitchen helmed by the owner’s mother. Start with the obligatory salted cod fritter. Besides barbecue dishes cooked over a charcoal grill, the extensive menu includes specialities like sautéed pork and clams Alentejo style, mixed seafood rice, and Macanese coconut and turmeric chicken; all great choices to share.

Name: Palace Garden
Address: Shop 306, 3F, Grand Lisboa Palace, Grand Lisboa Palace Resort, Rua do Tiro, Cotai, Macau
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: The room is the epitome of lavish maximalism – one wall is covered in a 35-metre-long Suzhou silk embroidery with a chrysanthemum theme. On the menu, ingredients from around the world are used to make refined Cantonese dishes, including labour-intensive items from ancient recipes. Crispy skin squab with lemongrass uses 18-day birds from Shiqi, boasting juicy flesh and mild smokiness. The menu can appear overwhelming, so ask servers for recommendations.

Name: Shum Shum Desserts
Address: Shop C, GF, 46 Kweilin Street, Sham Shui Po, Hong Kong
Description: Classic Hongkongese and Taiwanese sweet soups on offer here include creamy coconut soup – a silky delight on its own but even better with chewy taro or sweet potato balls. Try also purple glutinous rice soup with elastic jelly cubes.

Name: Hyde Park Garden
Address: 44 Hoi Pong Road Central, Lei Yue Mun, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR China
Description: The owner also sells seafood from the opposite stall so diners can pick from a dazzling selection flown in daily. Ask servers for the best way to cook your meal; for instance, razor clams are typically stir-fried in chilli black bean sauce, and abalone with ginger and scallion in a claypot. The signature fish soup is simmered for hours with freshwater fish and tofu. Try also the deep-fried eggplant, and tofu skin sweet soup with pearl barley.

Name: Hing Kee
Address: 1F, Bowa House, 180 Nathan Road, Tsim Sha Tsui, Hong Kong
Description: It started two generations ago in Causeway Bay but the family’s reputation for Boat People style cuisine was made in Tsim Sha Tsui. Elder sister heads the serving team; younger brother runs the kitchen. They are famous for their stir-fried crabs with black beans and chilli, roast duck and rice noodles in soup and congee. You can decide level of spiciness for some dishes. Guests aren’t seated until everyone in the party has arrived.

Name: So Kee
Address: Shop 15, GF, Block A, Ho Shun Yee Building, 9 Fung Yau Street East, Yuen Long, Hong Kong
Description: There’s just one item on the menu – double-steamed egg white custard with milk, boasting a silky runny centre under a firmer crust. Order the chilled ones if you’re in a rush, or wait patiently as the hot ones are made to order.

Name: Man Kee Cart Noodle
Address: 121 Fuk Wing Street, Sham Shui Po, Hong Kong
Description: The number of topping choices can be overwhelming, but Chinese chive dumplings and Swiss chicken wings are especially good. Fancy a spicy kick? Try the house-made chilli sauce over your noodles.

Name: Yi Shun (Macau)
Address: 381 Avenida de Almeida Ribeiro, Macau, Macau
Description: A longstanding shop offering traditional desserts, such as pineapple with crushed ice and sweet lotus seed soup with egg. Milk custard and ginger milk pudding are house specialties, to which you can add lotus seeds or red beans for extra flavour.

Name: Lei Garden (Wan Chai)
Address: 1F, CNT Tower, 338 Hennessy Road, Wan Chai, Hong Kong
Description: An inventory of restaurants in Wan Chai wouldn’t be complete without a Lei Garden. This branch is bigger than most and boasts a busy, bustling atmosphere, particularly at lunchtime. It follows the group’s tried-and-tested formula of offering an extensive menu with luxurious dishes alongside less elaborate but classic Cantonese specialities. Seafood enthusiasts should consider pre-ordering the Alaskan king crab or Brittany blue lobster.

Name: Chuen Kee Seafood (Hoi Pong Street)
Address: 53 Hoi Pong Street, Sai Kung, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR China
Description: Two family-run restaurants just a few minutes’ walk from each other have been in business since the 80s; choose the one by the quay for the rooftop terrace and harbour views. A wide array of seafood is available from adjacent fishmongers: cuttlefish, crab, lobster, molluscs, shrimps…Select your meal from the tank and ask the servers the best ways to cook it. Abalone and mantis shrimp in peppered salt are the smash hits not to be missed.

Name: Farm House
Address: 1F, Phase 1, China Taiping Tower, 8 Sunning Road, Causeway Bay, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR China
Description: The aquarium running the entire length of one wall certainly catches the eye. But it’s the traditional dishes painstakingly crafted with quality ingredients and gourmet dried seafood that win the hearts of the regulars. You must try their famous fried chicken wing stuffed with sticky rice. Baked sea whelks stuffed with foie gras, steamed rice with chicken, abalone and dried scallops are also deftly prepared. Friendly, thoughtful service.

Name: Tai Tsai (Tsuen Wan)
Address: GF, 99 Hoi Pa Street, Tsuen Wan, Hong Kong
Description: "Tai Tsai" is a homophone of "Taiwanese cuisine" in Chinese. The owner missed his home island's classic braised pork rice so much that he opened his own shop. He cooks the signature rice dish in Taipei style, adding sugar in moderation, and with hand-diced pork belly slow-cooked in aromatics and soy for up to four hours. Top it with onsen tamago or soft-boiled egg. The pepper salt popcorn chicken and boba tea are also well made. Arrive early to beat the crowd.

Name: Lucale
Address: Shop A, GF, 100 Third Street, Sai Ying Pun, Hong Kong
Description: Named after a portmanteau of the two chefs’ first names, this neighbourhood joint uses fine artisanal ingredients from Italy to craft Italian favourites, ranging from homemade pasta to seafood and meat dishes, best enjoyed with their selection of Italian wines. Black truffle chitarrino with Pienza pecorino is guaranteed to melt your heart with its al dente texture and tantalising aroma. The eater-friendly prices also explain its popularity despite its hidden location down an alley.

Name: Saffron
Address: 31F, Banyan Tree, Galaxy, Estrada da Baía de Nossa Senhora da Esperança, Cotai, Macau
Description: The hotel’s restaurant has been completely revamped and moved to the 31st floor, commanding breathtaking views. Now helmed by a native Thai chef with extensive experience, the kitchen specialises in refined Thai cuisine, such as chargrilled organic pork jowl from the royal farm in Thailand with a tamarind fish sauce that is out of this world. The signature curry king crab is also unmissable with a three-chilli blend adding heat and aroma.

Name: Portugália
Description: After a hiatus, Portugália has reopened in the historic town with the same kitchen and service teams. The blue-and-white interior, dotted in matching azulejo tiles from their previous address, is relaxed and cosy. The menu features authentic Portuguese family favourites in sharing portions, such as gambas a la guillo, and the signature steak ‘a Portugália’ in a secret gravy. Round off the meal with a fluffy, whipped serradura.

Name: The Mews
Address: 1F, The Londoner, Estrada do lstmo, Cotai, Macau
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Wheelchair access
Description: Diners are bowled over by the high-ceilinged room adorned in colourful lanterns and wood carving, all of which on a mews (stabling for horses in historic London) theme. The native Thai kitchen team reinvents specialities from their homeland with a contemporary spin. Try the mouthwateringly juicy grilled Wagyu beef with red curry and chakram leaves, or the tangy sunflower chicken tom kha soup. Thai-inspired nibbles and cocktails are also highly recommended.

Name: Pin Yue Xuan
Address: Shop 1016, 1F, The Venetian, Estrada da Baía de Nossa Senhora da Esperança, Cotai, Macau
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Valet parking
Description: The high-ceilinged room, which sports a smart modern Chinese vibe, is the quintessence of stylish flair. The Hong Kong head chef, who has been honing his skills in Macau for many a year, imbues the mostly Cantonese menu with creative touches and luxe delights, such as crispy quinoa on smoked tofu skin rolls, and steamed savoury custard made with Breton blue lobster and Japanese Ranou eggs. The exquisitely crafted petit fours are not to be missed.

Name: Sếp
Address: 19F, High Block, H Code, 45 Pottinger Street, Central, Hong Kong
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining,Interesting wine list,Wheelchair access
Description: The executive chef spent seven years working in Vietnam where he fell in love with wood-fired cooking. He was keen to introduce the concept to Hong Kong audience when he returned home. His project Sếp specialises in modern Indochine Vietnamese fare using a wood-fired grill in the open kitchen. Menus with 8 or 10 courses feature must-tries like Hoi An poulet made with dry-aged local three-yellow chicken, and bún bò Huế with premium black angus beef.

Name: Mosu
Address: 3F, M+ Tower, West Kowloon Cultural District, 38 Museum Drive, Tsim Sha Tsui, Hong Kong
Description: Nestled in an art museum with commanding panoramic harbour views, the spacious room imparts serenity with its concrete walls and scattered lights that resemble a starry sky. The head chef has years of experience in French cooking, working in some prestigious kitchens in Japan. A single tasting menu is served and it changes from time to time. The courses reflect the chef’s multicultural exposure with its creative combinations of globally sourced ingredients.

Name: Temple Street Beef Offal
Address: 18 Arthur Street, Yau Ma Tei, Hong Kong
Description: This long-standing shop is popular with locals. Tripe, intestine, pancreas or lung can be ordered individually or as an assortment, on a skewer or in a bowl. The offal soaks up the broth nicely, with three sauces on the side.

Name: Jardin de Jade (Wan Chai)
Address: G3-4, GF, Sun Hung Kai Centre, 30 Harbour Road, Wan Chai, Hong Kong
Description: The first Hong Kong venture of the renowned Shanghai restaurant group is certainly not lacking in grandeur, with its double-height ceiling and striking chandelier. Shanghainese classics and dim sum are made the traditional way but with updated presentation. The xiao long bao with beautifully pleated paper-thin skin, soupy filling and spot-on seasoning is the jewel in the crown. The seasonal menu covers regional specialities from beyond Shanghai.

Name: SW Steakhouse
Address: GF, North Esplanade, Wynn Palace, Avenida da Nave Desportiva, Cotai, Macau
Description: The room is designed like an auditorium, with all tables providing a decent view of the stage. Multimedia shows are put on every half hour for a total experience of art, sound, technology and gastronomy. On top of classics like oysters on the half shell, crab cake, and beef tartare; beef steak cooked in the 1200°F grill is certainly a highlight. Choose among USDA prime, Aussie Black Angus, pureblood and crossbred Wagyu from Japan, NZ and the U.S.

Name: Yi
Address: 21F, Morpheus, City of Dreams, Estrada do Istmo, Cotai, Macau
Description: Established on the 21st floor of a sky bridge, Yi’s knockout location is matched by stunning views, impressive architecture and an exotic interior. The 9-course seasonal-driven tasting menu refers to the 24 solar terms of the Chinese calendar, incorporating quality produce from around the world. Rare, premium ingredients, such as nodoguro and A4 Wagyu from Miyazaki, Japan, are deftly and creatively crafted with artful plating.

Name: Luk Yu Tea House
Description: Large numbers of both regulars and tourists come to Luk Yu Tea House for the traditionally prepared and flavoursome dim sum, and its three floors fill up quickly. The animated atmosphere and subtle colonial decoration are appealing but no one really stays too long; the serving team in white jackets have seen it all before and go about their work with alacrity. Popular dishes are crispy deep fried chicken and fried noodles with sliced beef.

Name: Leela
Address: Shop 301-310, Lee Garden Three, 1 Sunning Road, Causeway Bay, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR China
Description: The room, furnished in a neoteric Indian style, sports a balcony for pre- or post-prandial drinks. The Indian head chef champions a menu starring specialities from all over India, with contemporary, creative twists. Every course tells a story and diners can truly experience India’s food culture from different perspectives. Try the tandoori dishes from the custom-made oven. With firm yet tender flesh, monkfish imported from France works a treat in the curry.

Name: Mrs. Fong Chinese Desserts
Address: 198 Temple Street, Jordan, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR China
Description: This busy family-run shop moved here in 2022. Over 10 Chinese sweets are made from scratch daily, such as red bean cake or put-chai cake. Black sesame roll is especially prized for its soft-springy texture and deep flavour.

Name: Above & Beyond
Address: 28F, Hotel Icon, 17 Science Museum Road, Tsim Sha Tsui, Hong Kong
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: The stylish décor, sweeping harbour views and extensive menu make this restaurant a popular choice for Cantonese dining. The chef puts a new spin on the dim sum tradition by melding imported ingredients with authentic local flavours. Signatures such as steamed Alaskan king crab dumplings, and scallop rice flour rolls with cordyceps flowers are nothing short of ingenious. The set lunch can be ordered individually with a vegan option.

Name: Chesa
Address: 1F, The Peninsula Hotel, 22 Salisbury Road, Tsim Sha Tsui, Hong Kong
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: Even since opening as a ‘pop-up’ restaurant created by the Swiss-born manager back in 1965, Chesa has been the go-to place in town for those wanting authentic Swiss cuisine. The Alpine chalet-style décor more than compensates for the room’s lack of windows, while the menu covers all bases, offering fondue, raclette and the famous Chemin de Fer wines. You can even specify how strong you want the brandy taste to be in your fondue.

Name: Involtini
Address: 11F, The L. Square, 459-461 Lockhart Road, Causeway Bay, Hong Kong
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Wheelchair access
Description: The young chef, an alumnus of Otto e Mezzo, attracts a loyal following with his fresh pasta, handmade in-house daily. Italian eggs and flour are used in the dough which is rested overnight to give it a lovely al dente texture. The signature tagliolini with springy carabineros red prawns boasts a rich sauce loaded with seafood flavours. The pasta menu is updated from time to time to keep it fresh and reflect what’s in season.

Name: Yuè (Causeway Bay)
Address: Shop 1301, Food Forum, Time Square, 1 Matheson Street, Causeway Bay, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR China
Description: Having worked in some prestigious kitchens in Japan and Macau for over 40 years, the chef designed a menu of refined Cantonese dishes using top-notch ingredients from around the world, such as Alaskan king crab, Japanese chillies and Taiwanese bird’s-nest fern. The classic sweet and sour pork is given a new spin with aged vinegar and dried plums, plus an option of plant-based ‘meat’. Private rooms in various sizes are perfect for parties.

Name: Manuel Cozinha Portuguesa
Address: 90 Rua de Femão Mendes Pinto, Taipa, Macau
Description: After a spot of renovation for cosier feel, authenticity and hospitality remain the establishment’s hallmark. The friendly owner-chef has revamped the traditional Portuguese menu, now arranged by key ingredient. Using only top-notch seasonal produce, most dishes are barbecued traditionally. Grilled codfish and fried rice with squid ink are the must-tries. Check out the daily specials on the blackboard before ordering.

Name: The Merchants
Address: 43-45F, Forty-Five, Gloucester Tower, Landmark, 15 Queen's Road Central, Central, Hong Kong
Description: The top three floors of a prestigious office tower in Central have been remodelled into a swanky restaurant with drop-dead harbour views. Green velvet is a prominent feature, with contrasting splashes of orange on the semi-circular banquettes. Well-crafted traditional Shanghainese and Jiangzhe classics like braised wheat gluten, sautéed “dragon beard” shredded mandarin fish, pan-fried eight-treasure rice, and braised Chinese ham in osmanthus honey.

Name: Tuber Umberto Bombana
Address: Shop 113A, 1F, K11 Musea, 18 Salisbury Road, Tsim Sha Tsui, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR China
Description: This dining concept by the eponymous chef is dedicated to his favourite ingredient – the white and black gold of gastronomy; its name also refers to the genus to which truffles belong. Only one degustation menu is served, combining the best seasonal ingredients from around the world with the prized fungus. Artisanal linguine with jumbo carabinero prawns from Spain stands out in particular, with the tomalley loaded with sweetness and umami.

Name: Hong Kong Cuisine
Address: 1F, Elegance Court, 2-4 Tsoi Tak Street, Happy Valley, Hong Kong
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Bring your own bottle,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus
Description: This upstairs restaurant was rebranded and remodelled in 2022. Chef Li started cooking professionally in the UK at the age of 16 and his dishes are rooted in Chinese traditions, but underpinned by modern French techniques and novel food combinations. He has an affinity for perfumed oils and the use of fried tofu and pork rind in caramelised sweet and sour Iberico pork is ingenious. His aromatic smoked soy sauce chicken is also unmissable.

Name: Mâm Amis
Address: Shop A & B, GF, Fu Fai Commercial Centre, 27 Hillier Street, Sheung Wan, Hong Kong
Description: The smart wood panelled front contrasts sharply with the distressed walls, vintage lamps and hanging greenery inside. Vietnamese chefs are keen on bringing authentic Vietnamese food to Hong Kong, with chargrilled items and phở among the highlights. Try the chargrilled river prawns that boast bouncy, briny-sweet flesh and exceptional smokiness. Phở comes in generous portions with a flavour-packed soup base.

Name: Don Alfonso 1890
Address: Shop 307, 3F, Palazzo Versace, Grand Lisboa Palace Resort, Rua do Tiro, Cotai, Macau
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: This family-owned haute cuisine brand from Italy opened this high-end outpost in Macau. Versace may have taken care of the design, but the fashion house's signature glamour doesn't outshine the food. The kitchen excels at delivering vibrant flavours from the Amalfi Coast, using fresh produce from the family's own organic farm – try the handmade tagliolini with scampi and white truffle. Ask the sommelier for help navigating the long wine list.

Name: Blind
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: This is one of those places where you don’t just come to eat, but where you’ll find quality ingredients, impressive flavours and solid technique as part of a gastronomic experience that touches the emotions. This is showcased in its homage to José Saramago’s novel “Blindness” and a philosophy built around three concepts (to feel, to touch and to provoke) that play with the senses. Part of the Torel Palace Hotel but with its own separate entrance, this restaurant is overseen by chef Vítor Matos and impressively run day to day by young chef Rita Magro. Here, the cuisine is based around a serious, common sense yet fun approach (some of the dishes are served “blind” to guests), with a desire to demonstrate a high level of cooking and to create an element of surprise in terms of technique, with presentation and flavour always to the fore. This is showcased on a single surprise tasting menu entitled Blind Emotions, with a choice of two different options (10 or 12 “moments”).

Name: Drogaria
Description: This restaurant, with its small entrance, is located on the exact spot of the erstwhile Drogaria do Sr. Albino (hence the name) in the busy Lapa district. Its retro ambience, featuring marble tables, various mirrors dotted around the two dining rooms and a checkered floor (all of which provide added personality) is in perfect harmony with a modern and sophisticated decor. The menu here is based around classic Portuguese dishes, albeit with a contemporary flair. Iconic dishes such as cod croquettes, “bacalhau à bras”, roast suckling pig, and rice pudding are all attractively presented and full of surprising textures. The delightful atmosphere on the charming outdoor terrace comes into its own on a summer evening!

Name: Quinta do Tedo Familia Geadas
Address: Quinta do Tedo N222 M512, Folgosa, 5110 204, Portugal
Description: If you’re looking for somewhere with good food and stunning views, this is the perfect place. Part of the quinta of the same name, at the confluence of the Douro and Tagus rivers, the restaurant boasts a welcoming ambience and extensive windows to maximise views of the spectacular landscapes here. It is run by the Geadas brothers (chef Óscar Geadas and sommelier António Geadas), who are known for the success of their restaurant in the north of the country. The focus is on the culinary traditions of the Trás-os-Montes region, which is reflected in deliciously fresh fish dishes and perfectly prepared meats. Make sure you save space for the sublime desserts!

Name: Casa do Gadanha
Address: Rua da Vasco da Gama 4, Estremoz, 7100-559, Portugal
Description: A restaurant with a cosy, intimate feel featuring warm, bright colours. It is located in the historic centre of Estremoz, better known as the “white town” as a result of its famous marble. The kitchen is visible from the dining room, enabling guests to watch the preparation process in full flow. The cuisine here is centred around dishes for sharing and two tasting menus (6 or 8 “moments”). An added bonus is the artisanal home-made dough used for the bread and pizzas.

Name: Romando
Description: Located in a district on the outskirts of Areia, Romando has a single modern - style dining room. The emphasis is firmly on traditional Portuguese cuisine, including a good selection of savoury rice dishes and a few seafood options.

Name: Bomfim 1896 with Pedro Lemos
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Great view,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: At the Quinta do Bomfim, an estate run by the Symington family since 1896 (hence the name of the restaurant), this project is a partnership with renowned chef Pedro Lemos. Situated on the banks of the River Douro, it boasts a classic and sophisticated ambience, plus a completely open dining room with a view of the kitchen, and superb vistas through the large picture windows. The fireplace and wood-fired oven take centre stage here, alongside cuisine that revisits the flavours of the Douro Valley’s time-honoured kitchens, albeit with a more contemporary vision.

Name: Cisco - Cozinha Tradicional
Description: This restaurant is located in Almeirim, in a region renowned for its famous “sopa da Pedra”, a soup which understandably makes an appearance on the menu. However, you’ll also find lots of other options here, such as the “cozido à portuguesa” stew, the mouthwatering rice with veal cheek, the traditional “bacalhau à brás” and, for dessert, the classic “leite-creme”, and grandma Mariazinha’s almond pudding, both of which provide a fitting end to your meal. If you enjoy high-quality traditional and home-style cooking this is definitely the place, thanks to chef Alexandre Albergaria Diniz use of fresh ingredients to create authentic dishes without unnecessary frills, as well as daily specials, in a welcoming, traditional space run by an excellent team.

Name: Raiva
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Great view,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: (Temporarily closed for refurbishment) This restaurant takes its name from the parish in which it is located along the banks of the Douro, from where it enjoys superb views. Following his return to Portugal having worked in leading restaurants abroad, chef Dárcio Henriques embarked on this project, which sees him working with ingredients sourced from the length and breadth of the Douro. The cuisine here is showcased on à la carte and two tastings menus (one of which is vegetarian), and includes dishes such as Wild mushrooms and DOP terrincho tortellini or Arouquesa Vazia with smoked celery and soufflé potatoes. The perfect place to unwind, given its setting in a delightful hotel.

Name: Essencial
Description: This small restaurant, located on a narrow street in the bustling Bairro Alto district, features a completely open-view kitchen in the centre of the dining room, plus a minimalist decor of neutral tones. Influenced by his experiences in international restaurants, chef André Lança Cordeiro combines French techniques with seasonal Portuguese ingredients. Dishes such as the famous pâté en croûte with different fillings, the vol-au-vent of lobster and sweetbreads, and the pistachio and yuzu Paris-Brest take guests on a gastronomic flight of fancy to France without having to leave Lisbon! Options here include the Bistrot menu, with one starter, a main course, and a dessert, and the Amuse-Bouches tasting menu, accompanied by an interesting wine pairing.

Name: Salão Nobre
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Valet parking
Description: A spacious, elegant restaurant occupying the large ballroom of a former palace. Contemporary cuisine that features a few vegetarian dishes as well as tasting menus.

Name: Fogo
Description: Those who are familiar with chef Alexandre Silva’s cuisine will know all about the excellence and quality that you’ll always find at Fogo. As soon as you walk through the door you’ll sense the true essence of its cooking aided, of course, by a name (“fogo” is the Portuguese word for “fire”) that speaks for itself, as well as the delicious aromas and intense energy from the open grill. Every dish is meticulously prepared on it, from the starters (such as the enticing grilled oysters) and the freshest of fish sourced directly from the auction to the mouthwatering beef sirloin – not forgetting the undoubted house speciality, the traditional baked rice. Make sure you also cast your eye over the truly spectacular cocktail list.

Name: Oficina
Address: Rua de Miguel Bombarda 282, Porto, 4050-377, Portugal
Description: Oficina combines an industrial atmosphere with the world of the avant-garde, given its location in an area full of art galleries. Traditional cuisine with a modern twist.

Name: Pequeno Mundo
Description: The perfect venue for an intimate supper. Its setting is in a typical Algarve - style house with romantic patios and warm and welcoming dining rooms. International menu showing clear French influence.

Name: Terroir
Address: Avenida Duque De Loulé 86A, Lisbon, 1050-090, Portugal
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus
Description: A restaurant with a contemporary and somewhat relaxed feel where the focus is on strong technique and seasonal Portuguese ingredients. Surprise tasting menus are also available.

Name: Sem Porta
Description: Sem Porta is located inside the main building of the superb Hotel Sublime Comporta, in a glass-fronted space boasting a decor of wood and neutral colours. The focus here is on Portuguese cooking that features fresh ingredients sourced daily from its own garden or from local producers. This is showcased on a single 5-“moment” tasting menu or the à la carte, which includes fish starters such as smoked eel on a delicate potato foam, and main courses such as sea turbot with creamy rice, and Iberian pork “presa” with a smooth smoked celery purée.

Name: Alambique
Address: Estrada de Vale do Lobo a Quinta do Lago, Almancil, 8135-160, Portugal
Description: A fine exponent of traditional Portuguese cuisine, featuring delicious grilled fish and specialities such as fish cataplana. Idyllic terraces surrounded by vegetation add to its appeal.

Name: Tasca do Zé Tuga
Description: A superb location within the walls of the old town, with a terrace boasting superb views of the castle. Traditionally inspired cuisine with plenty of personal touches.

Name: Turismo
Address: Rua Duques de Bragança, Barcelos, 4750-272, Portugal
Description: This restaurant, with its impressive statue of a Barcelos cockerel by the entrance, stands out for its modern architecture in the heart of this historic town, a location close to all of Barcelos’ main tourist sights, and its impressive views of the river. It is divided into three elegantly decorated dining rooms with a glass-fronted wine cellar at the heart of everything, but it is the energy of the team here that is particularly impressive. The menu follows traditional lines with a few contemporary touches in dishes such as the sautéed alheira with apple purée, the grilled octopus with potato crumble, and the “priscos” pudding with tangerine and a citrus sorbet, none of which will disappoint.

Name: Taberna d'Adélia
Description: A pleasantly colourful taberna with a rustic feel just a few steps from the beach. The high-quality fish and seafood on the traditionally inspired menu is particularly impressive.

Name: Grenache
Address: Pátio de Dom Fradique 12, Lisbon, 1100-624, Portugal
Description: If you’re keen to take your tastebuds on a gastronomic odyssey across France, this delightful, intimate restaurant with a charming outdoor terrace in the heart of the Alfama could be the place for you. It is run by chef Philippe Gelfi who, ever loyal to his origins, offers cuisine rooted in French tradition but with a contemporary touch and a focus on seasonal Portuguese ingredients on a choice of two tasting menus: Grenache and Experience. Unusual details include petits-fours served on a bed of coffee beans, with their enticing aromas from countries as diverse as Angola, Ethiopia, Brazil and Costa Rica.

Name: Terra
Description: Behind the somewhat surprising façade is a sushi bar, plus a neo-rustic-style dining room with a designer feel upstairs. Extensive à la carte menu with a nod to Asian cuisine.

Name: Herdade dos Grous
Description: A good option for discovering the essence of the Alentejo, given its location on a charming quinta surrounded by trees and vineyards (it also has two dozen guestrooms), with access via a private road that is well signposted from the village. Here, the focus is on traditional cooking with plenty of personality thanks to the use of organic ingredients grown on the estate or from meat from its own livestock (Alentejo veal, merino lamb, Iberian pork etc). A choice of wine-tasting options is also available, ranging from three wines on the Basic package to six, including tapas, for those booking the Flight pairing.

Name: Cavalariça
Description: This space, formerly a stable for horses, has been converted into a modern, elegant restaurant that has managed to maintain vestiges of its past. Following time spent working in England, chef Bruno Caseiro teamed up with Filipa Gonçalves (he is executive chef; she is the pastry chef) to create this unique restaurant, where the focus is on contemporary cooking with an international influence and the use of regional ingredients, with dishes designed for sharing. Cavalariça’s signature dishes include cured meat croquettes with clam mayonnaise and mustard, and grilled brioche with a chicken liver parfait and orange chutney.

Name: Mercearia Gadanha
Address: Largo dos Dragões de Olivença 84, Estremoz, 7100-457, Portugal
Description: This centrally located restaurant with a welcoming feel comes as something of a surprise, as it is accessed via a bar- gourmet shop that has the feel of an authentic grocery store. In the rustic-contemporary dining room, featuring exposed wood beams and even a table for two in the fireplace, choose from an extensive menu combining regionally inspired dishes (crispy prawns, scrambled eggs, different black pork recipes) with those with a more international feel, all of which are prepared with a subtle, modern touch. Cheese, sausages and wine from the Estremoz area are available for purchase in the boutique.

Name: Casa da Dízima
Address: Rua Costa Pinto 17, Paço de Arcos, 2770-046, Portugal
Description: This restaurant owes its name to the history of the building, which was once used to collect taxes. There are several dining rooms, most of which are rustic yet contemporary in appearance. The modern cooking is based around traditional Portuguese and international fare.

Name: Aladin Grill
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus
Description: Part of the Vila Vita hotel, where the Moroccan-inspired decor is reminiscent of the Arabian Nights! Oriental flavours, aged Galician meats and Portuguese fish all feature on the menu, with many dishes cooked on the grill.

Name: Prado
Address: Travessa Das Pedras Negras 2, Lisbon, 1100-404, Portugal
Description: When a restaurant adopts the “farm-to-table” principle, it’s easy to imagine what this entails, namely fresh, seasonal dishes prepared with local ingredients. What is even better is that every time you visit you’ll find new suggestions on the menu that are always skilfully prepared and full of flavour. At the helm in this setting full of natural light and decorated with lots of plants that add a touch of freshness is chef Antonio Galapito, who emphasises the important of small-scale producers and allows the seasons to guide him in the creation of his dishes. In the evening, the attractive tasting menu (as well as the à la carte available at all sittings) showcases all of the chef’s culinary skill. We can also recommend the organic wines that are part of the wine-pairing option.

Name: BAHR
Address: Praça Luís De Camões 2, Lisbon, 1200-243, Portugal
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Brunch,Great view,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: Located on the top floor of the Bairro Alto Hotel (hence the origin of its name) and featuring a kitchen that opens onto the dining room, BAHR describes itself as a “bohemian and irreverent space”. At lunchtime it offers a much more informal market-inspired “executive menu”, with more elaborate, exclusively à la carte dishes in the evening, but all featuring the very best ingredients.

Name: O Talho
Description: Entering a restaurant through a butcher’s shop (“talho” in Portuguese) provides a clue as to the focus here and is a guarantee that the meat quality will be high and that it comes directly from the source! And it is in this modern yet at the same time informal space that chef Kiko offers his unique cuisine to guests through superb dishes prepared in an exceptional way. Meat-lovers can savour irresistible choices such as picanha from Uruguay, Galician 60-day dry aged T-bone, and A5 Kobe flank, considered one of the world’s best cuts of meat. Meat can also be purchased to be cooked at home.

Name: Solar dos Nunes
Description: A renowned family-run restaurant which opened its doors in 1988 and has retained the essence of an old-style eatery serving traditional Portuguese cooking. To a backdrop of typical decor, including photos of famous faces who have eaten here, you’ll find an extensive menu that showcases the flavours of the Alentejo region, including an impressive selection of sausages and cured meats (such as the Jamón Ibérico Joselito Gran Reserva), daily specials, and game dishes in season. Don’t miss the fish soup, the Alentejo-style garlic “açorda” with cod, or “grandma’s dogfish soup”.

Name: Tia Alice
Address: Avenida Irmã Lúcia de Jesus 152, Fátima, 2495-557, Portugal
Description: A family-run restaurant that has been tastefully brought up to date. The dining rooms are complemented by an attractive shop selling household items, as well as a delightful garden. Delicious traditional cuisine!

Name: Lamelas
Address: Rua Cândido da Silva 55 A, Porto Covo, 7520-437, Portugal
Description: The name of this restaurant is a reference to chef Ana Moura’s grandfather, who was from Porto Covo, a small coastal village south of Lisbon where she spent her summers as a child. Having worked in renowned restaurants such as Eleven and Arzak, she made the decision to return to her family roots. In this informal restaurant, she showcases the “Flavour of the Alentejo”, combining contemporary ingredients with impressive technique and traditional flavours. We particularly recommend the “migas de chouriço” with spare ribs; the forkbeard fish with clams in green sauce; and the cheesecake with caramel and pistachio. The superb views from the tables on the terrace are an added bonus!

Name: NUMA
Description: NUMA is a combination of the names of the two owners: Nuno Martins (chef) and Manuela João (front of house manager), who followed a "family dream" in opening their own dining space. Situated along a busy avenue in a residential district, it boasts a refined ambience, with plenty of wood decor and warm tones that combine to create a welcoming feel. The cuisine is centred around local and Portuguese ingredients and a contemporary vision which is showcased on two tasting menus (NUMA and Estação) and an à la carte. Make sure you order NUMA’s two signature dishes: the Carabineiro red prawns and the sirloin steak.

Name: Marlene,
Address: Avenida Infante D. Henrique. Doca do Jardim do Tabaco, Lisbon, 1100-651, Portugal
Description: A contemporary gastronomic restaurant adjoining the Zunzum Gastrobar, both of which occupy a completely glass-fronted building. A standout feature here is the large central kitchen, surrounded by a counter from where guests can watch the chefs at work. Innovative cuisine from Portugal and further afield, which is only available on two unique tasting menus.

Name: O Palco
Address: Avenida Dom Afonso Henriques, Coimbra, 3000-011, Portugal
Description: The aim here is to bring to the stage (“palco” in Portuguese) all those involved in this culinary project, from producers and their ingredients to the owners themselves, namely chef Marco Almeida and front-of-house manager Ana Almeida. Everything here revolves around the freshness and local provenance of its ingredients. Thanks to the restaurant’s zero-miles philosophy, the majority of these are sourced from local suppliers within a radius of 100km of Coimbra, as is highlighted (the producer’s name and the distance) alongside each dish. Menus are divided into Acts I, II and III, on which you can choose five, seven or ten “scenes”, alongside a vegetarian menu.

Name: fago
Description: This restaurant is situated in Marvão, a village at the highest point of the Serra de São Mamede, just a few kilometres from the Spanish border. It occupies a small house that has been completely remodelled by Diogo Branco, a chef from Porto, and Daniel Boto, a native of this region. The concise à la carte here changes constantly according to the seasons and availability from local producers. Three main dishes are always available: one vegetarian, one meat, and one fish or seafood.

Name: SEM
Address: Rua Das Escolas Gerais 120, Lisbon, 1100-220, Portugal
Description: In this completely relaxed and informal setting, the decor is enhanced by the shelves of jars full of the preserves and fermented products that feature on the menu. Here, chefs George Mcleod and Lara Prado (George is from New Zealand; Lara is from Brazil) take their responsibility towards a sustainable approach seriously, using ingredients from regenerative agriculture, reducing their use of plastic much as possible, and doing their utmost to eliminate food waste, all of which they manage to achieve without detracting from the flavour and freshness of their ingredients. Their cooking is centred around a single tasting menu that varies in line with what is available from their local producers.

Name: SEIVA
Address: Rua Sarmento Pimentel 63, Leça da Palmeira, 4450 790, Portugal
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Wheelchair access
Description: Chef David Jesus is a strong advocate of the idea that it is possible to create great food by using what nature provides for us, and his restaurant is clear proof of this. The menu here changes with the seasons and according to the creativity of a chef who is always looking to innovate and create new combinations. Dishes include kimchi nigiri, a croquette with a creamy centre and superb texture; the “cuttlefish from my roots”, with rice tagliatelle, passion fruit curry and crispy cabbage; and to round things off, the mouthwatering vegetable brioche with almond milk and condensed tamarind milk.

Name: Elemento
Description: Chef Ricardo Dias Ferreira has unashamedly gone back to basics here, cooking exclusively over wood, to such an extent that he rarely uses the grill or oven. With his combination of traditional Portuguese cuisine, smoky flavours and modern touches, he offers à la carte options alongside an “8-moment” tasting menu, and his cuisine varies from day to day depending on the availability of ingredients from small-scale local producers. Allow yourself to be guided by recommendations from the interesting selection of Portuguese wines, and if you’re keen to enjoy the experience to the full, take a seat at the counter in front of the kitchen so you can watch the chefs in action at close quarters.

Name: Sabores d'Itália
Address: Praça 5 de Outubro 40, Caldas da Rainha, 2500-111, Portugal
Description: A sober façade conceals this attractive restaurant with two modern dining rooms. The predominantly Italian menu is enhanced by a few Portuguese dishes.

Name: Dona Júlia
Description: A restaurant striking for its modern interior design, traditional cuisine with a strong Minho flavour and a pleasant ambience in which to enjoy its abundant dishes. These are centred on a vast selection of fully certified meats, many from the restaurant’s own estate, as well as fish and seafood direct from the auction.

Name: Boubou's
Address: Rua do Monte Olivete 32 A, Lisbon, 1200-280, Portugal
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: A welcoming restaurant next to the Museu Nacional de História Natural e da Ciência which became famous when its chef, Louise Bourrat, won the French version of Top Chef in 2022! The young international team (between them they speak seven languages) creates modern, globally inspired cuisine featuring delicate textures that exude femininity, and which is available (for dinner only) on two tasting menus: Omnivorus and the vegetarian Terra. One dish that we particularly enjoyed was the sweet potato ceviche with pomegranate, coconut and kaffir lime.

Name: Ferrugem
Description: A particularly attractive restaurant occupying an old barn. In the dining room, with its high ceilings and rustic - modern ambience, discover contemporary cooking with a creative flair.

Name: CHECKin by Leonel Pereira
Description: This charming restaurant occupies a former cereal and wine storehouse which has been completely remodelled in Faro’s historic centre. The cooking of chef Leonel Pereira, a native of the Algarve, is based around seasonal ingredients with a strong focus on creativity and flavour. The menu is divided into different sections: Check-in, Cozinhados no Tacho, Momentos Especiais and Check-out. Make sure you try the cheesecake with strawberries, lime, meringue and tangerine peel ice-cream.

Name: Avenida
Description: The old adage that talent runs in the family is particularly appropriate here! Dutch chef Roeland Klein’s passion for cooking came from his father, a chef in a one-Michelin-star restaurant in his native country. Located within the walls of the Hotel Avenida, opposite Lagos marina, the restaurant features an open kitchen where guests can sit at the counter to watch and interact with the chef as he prepares his dishes. Choose between the tasting menu and à la carte, both offering a variety of fish and seafood, although the aged meats sourced from the renowned El Capricho by José Gordón are worthy of special mention.

Name: Dos Artistas
Address: Rua Cândido dos Reis 68, Lagos, 8600-681, Portugal
Description: A restaurant with a pleasant terrace and a dining room with a classic-colonial-style decor. Internationally inspired cooking including à la carte and set menu options, with a more extensive choice on offer in the evening.

Name: 2 Passos
Description: A modern construction with lots of charm located on Ancão beach, a beautiful setting with protected status. Traditional Portuguese cuisine specialising in fish and seafood.

Name: Alameda
Address: Rua da Polícia da Segurança Pública 10, Faro, 8000-151, Portugal
Description: This restaurant pays a genuine homage to the Algarve region through its name (from the town’s famous park) and the dishes featuring on the menu. Chef Rui Sequeira, who has returned to his native area having worked in prestigious restaurants elsewhere, creates innovative cuisine that combine modern technique and traditional roots. The tasting menu, entitled “Love beyond time: A journey through the tales of the Algarve”, tells a story from the region in every dish, and is complemented by dishes from the à la carte. The sophisticated and contemporary ambience also includes a charming glass-enclosed terrace on the street.

Name: Salpoente
Address: Cais de São Roque 83, Aveiro, 3800-256, Portugal
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Wheelchair access
Description: This restaurant is located along the São Roque canal in a building once used as a salt warehouse. Contemporary cuisine with an innovative touch, to a backdrop that features designer details.

Name: Näperõn
Description: A surprisingly modern restaurant in this rustic and typically Portuguese village. Updated traditional cuisine based around two tasting menus (one short; one long).

Name: Rei dos Leitões
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Wheelchair access
Description: In a region renowned for its roast suckling pig (as well as the production of sparkling wine), this is one of many restaurants in the area specialising in this popular dish. Occupying a charming house along an avenue in town, this longstanding eatery definitely lives up to its name (The King of Suckling Pig)! The recipe and preparation of the pork follow tradition to the letter and we recommend that you accompany the dish with a glass of excellent local sparkling wine. Fish, matured meats and rice dishes also feature on the menu – all prepared with top-quality ingredients and lots of flavour. A superb wine selection completes the picture.

Name: S. Gião
Address: Rua Comendador Joaquim Almeida Freitas 56, Moreira de Cónegos, 4815-270, Portugal
Description: A space that symbolises authentic Portuguese cuisine, enhanced by well-conceived dishes and excellent service. Occupying a house with plenty of charm on the outskirts of Guimarães, and more specifically in Moreira de Cónegos, it features surprising aspects such as the central fireplace and superb views towards the Moreirense stadium and the surrounding vineyards. The cuisine, which is influenced by the north of Portugal but with an added touch of international flair, features generous portions and dishes prepared with top-quality ingredients on a menu that is constantly updated.

Name: dop
Address: Largo de São Domingos 16, Porto, 4050-545, Portugal
Description: Occupying an historic building, this restaurant boasts contemporary dining rooms on two floors where guests can enjoy high - quality traditional cooking. Superb cellar of Portuguese and international wines.

Name: Cantinho do Avillez
Address: Rua Mouzinho da Silveira 166, Porto, 4050-416, Portugal
Description: This is media - friendly chef José Avillez’s first venture outside of Lisbon. The urban bistro look and reasonably priced contemporary menu ensure that it is always full.

Name: Cais da Villa
Address: Rua Monsenhor Jerónimo do Amaral, Vila Real, 5000-570, Portugal
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: Cais da Vila has added fresh impetus to the local restaurant scene. Traditional cooking is to the fore here, showcased by classic recipes such as the cataplana of grouper, squid and shrimp. Excellent meat from the Trás-os-Montes region also features heavily on the menu.

Name: Dom Joaquim
Description: Dom Joaquim is located next to the Porta de Serpa Pinto, one of the access gates to the historic centre of Évora. The stylish, classic-contemporary ambience here features bare stone walls and a series of hanging sculptures that add a welcoming feel. Chef Joaquim Almeida bases his cuisine on traditional Alentejo cooking with a modern touch. On the menu you’ll find daily specials, traditional and local dishes, plus a selection of “convent”-style pastries and desserts. Make sure you try the “auga de prata” pudding, the recipe for which originates from the Convento de Santa Clara, just a few metres away.

Name: Go Juu
Address: Rua Marquês Sá da Bandeira 46A, Lisbon, 1050-149, Portugal
Description: Enjoy authentic Japanese cooking in this unique, almost minimalist space featuring a profusion of wood and a sushi bar in the dining room. There’s also an exclusive area for Go Juu’s club members.

Name: O Leão de Porches
Address: Rua Padre António Gregório A Cabrita 8, Porches, 8400-473, Portugal
Description: A romantic, rural restaurant with plenty of charisma! Choose between the tasting menu and an internationally inspired à la carte with different influences (Portuguese, French, Italian, Asian etc).

Name: Horta
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: This restaurant is more than just the gastronomic showcase of the renowned PortoBay group. Here, the stars of the show are the vegetables and plants used to create its healthy and well-balanced dishes. Ingredients are sourced from its own kitchen-garden (“horta” in Portuguese) or from growers around the island. On the menus, standout vegetable-based dishes include the delicious home-grown roast pepper and carrot hummus. Fish and meat options also feature, such as the tasty scabbard fillet with a mussel nage, plus a new, head-turning version of Crema Catalana served with fruit grown in Horta’s kitchen-garden.

Name: Gastro by Elemento
Address: Rua Maria Adelaide Freitas Gonçalves 13, Porto, 4350-109, Portugal
Description: Chef Ricardo Dias Ferreira focuses on time-honoured cuisine in which the wood fire takes on a starring role. Here, everything is cooked on a wood grill or in a wood-fired oven, hence the distinctive and special flavour evident in each dish. The restaurant has an industrial feel that includes an elegantly decorated and welcoming dining room, but why not sit at the bar-counter in front of the kitchen, where you’ll experience the full preparation process and the aromas emanating from the grill and oven. The offer is based around a single tasting menu, made up of ten moments and changes with the products available each season.

Name: Origens
Description: Somewhat hidden down a narrow street, Origens is a worthwhile choice given its location in the heart of Évora’s historic centre, where you can savour contemporary Alentejo cuisine prepared with sophisticated modern techniques. The menu is updated several times a year to ensure that the ingredients used are as fresh and seasonal as possible. One dish has been a mainstay since the restaurant first opened: “brás à farinheira”, made with smoked sausage. There’s also a surprise wine pairing option.

Name: À Mesa
Address: R. Álvaro de Campos 14, Tavira, 8800-320, Portugal
Description: À Mesa is situated next to the charming 17C São Paulo church, on the ground floor of a small boutique hotel but with its own private entrance. The tasteful dining room features stone walls and a section of glass floor through which the wine cellar is visible as a reminder of the property’s history. The menu was created by chef João Dias, whose partner is chef Luís Brito (A Ver Tavira). Choose between the à la carte and three tasting menus (Viagem pelo Atlântico, Iguarias que rimam and Terra e mar). The charming terrace comes into its own in summer!

Name: Âmago
Description: A unique and intimate restaurant with an informal ambience where the single surprise menu is only served to a maximum of ten guests all seated at the same table. The highly technical cuisine here changes according to the seasons produce and ingredients available in the market. Booking ahead is essential.

Name: Downunder by Justin Jennings
Description: If you’ve never eaten crocodile or kangaroo, now is your chance in this unpretentious restaurant run by a young Australian chef who fell in love with Lisbon and set up his own business here. His somewhat unusual cuisine, available on an à la carte and two set menus, shines a light on Australian cuisine and its exotic meats.

Name: Noélia
Address: Rua da Fortaleza - Edifício Cabanas Mar Loja 6A, Cabanas, 8800-595, Portugal
Description: Nicknamed the Queen of Ria Formosa, chef Noélia, whose restaurant bears her name, is a well-known celebrity across Portugal. This passionate, self-taught cook is always seeking to create new recipes and experiment with new combinations. Her recipes are based around locally caught fish and seafood that feature on a fixed menu, although there are always a variety of choices that focus on the day’s freshest ingredients. We recommended booking ahead as it is always full.

Name: MA
Description: You’ll find delicacies such as tuna with caviar, Azores squid, sea urchin, crab gunkan and John Dory, as well as mochis and macaroons to round off your meal in this intimate space just a few steps from the old cathedral (Sé Velha) in this city located along the banks of the Mondego. The wooden bar counter is where MA serves its Omakase menu, while the à la carte dining room boasts more subdued lighting and a romantic feel. The culinary experience here is overseen by chef Ricardo Casqueiro, who combines Japanese tradition with Western techniques and Portuguese ingredients. Open for dinner only.

Name: Vinha
Address: Rua Quinta Fonte da Vinha 383, Vila Nova de Gaia, 4430-487, Portugal
Description: This restaurant is part of the Vinha Boutique Hotel, a 16C manor house on the banks of the River Douro, where sophistication and elegance are key elements. Decorated with exquisite taste, it offers a menu that bears the signature of highly respected chef Henrique Sá Pessoa. The cuisine here is centred around seasonal Portuguese ingredients with an international influence which is showcased on an à la carte and a single tasting menu entitled “Identity”, on which dishes such as the “shore sea bass” and the “Alentejo pork presa” will linger long in the memory. An extraordinary experience and the perfect setting in which to relax and enjoy the hotel.

Name: Apego
Address: Rua de Santa Catarina 1198, Porto, 4000-457, Portugal
Description: A modest yet unique restaurant serving Franco-Portuguese cuisine which pays homage to the family roots of the female chef at the helm (her father was French and also worked as a cook). The somewhat concise à la carte is complemented by a tasting menu that is based around Apego’s signature dishes.

Name: Plano
Address: Rua da Bela Vista à Graça 126, Lisbon, 1170-075, Portugal
Description: Trás-os-Montes-born chef Vítor Adão’s roots are strongly anchored in tradition and the provenance of his ingredients. Having worked in several leading restaurants, he decided to open his own eatery where he showcases the heritage of his native region. His cooking is based around two surprise tasting menus (6 and 9 courses) that vary according to what is available from producers. Despite its simple decoration, enhanced by numerous jars of pickles to highlight the connection with the land, the overall feel here is elegant. The pleasant terrace is perfect for outdoor dining in warmer weather.

Name: A Carvalheira
Address: Rua do Eido Velho 73, Ponte de Lima, 4990-620, Portugal
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Wheelchair access
Description: Located at the Quinta do Eido Velho, where guests will fall in love with its beautiful rustic ambience and gardens. Traditional Portuguese cuisine including two standout dishes: cod with a cornbread crust and roasted kid.

Name: Arkhe
Description: Situated in the centre of the city, Arkhe features a discreet façade and an interior where the dominant decorative themes are open stonework and tasteful minimalism. The cuisine here is the realm of chef João Ricardo Alves who, having worked in various kitchens around the world, decided to open this new space with a focus on vegan/vegetarian cooking, accompanied by Alejandro Chávarro (sommelier and front-of-house manager), who also boasts extensive international experience. Alves’ cooking is showcased on three menus at lunchtime (but just one midweek) and two dinner menus, all of which are created using a combination of seasonal ingredients, plentiful flavour and impressive technical skill.

Name: Taberna do Lopes
Address: Rua De São Filipe Néri 23, Lisbon, 1250-225, Portugal
Description: If you enjoy eating well-matured meat, this steakhouse occupying a two-storey building will definitely impress thanks to its superb-quality Portuguese meats and regionally inspired dishes.

Name: Al Quimia
Description: A restaurant in a large resort with an impeccable contemporary design and a focus on luxurious decorative detail. Painstakingly prepared cuisine showcasing high levels of technical ability.

Name: Malhadinha Nova
Address: Herdade da Malhadinha Nova, Albernoa, 7800-601, Portugal
Description: Despite its access via a long lane, this restaurant surrounded by stunning vineyards is clearly signposted. It occupies the ground floor of a small house which is glass-fronted throughout and boasts breathtaking views. The cuisine here bears the signature of chef Joachim Koerper and is based on Alentejo cooking with hints of international influence. We can highly recommend the local eggs, DOP-certified Malhadinha-reared merino lamb and the honey produced on the estate.

Name: Almeja
Description: This centrally located, bistro-style eatery, impressively run by married couple João and Sofia, offers a different culinary experience in the city, showcased on a contemporary à la carte and extensive tasting menu. A relaxing terrace-garden adds to its appeal.

Name: Hool
Address: Rua de Santa Maria, Largo da Oliveira, Guimaraes, 4800-443, Portugal
Description: A visit to Guimarães offers a deep-dive into Portuguese history – a result of its historic relevance to the country and its title as “the cradle of the Portuguese nation”. Part of the Hotel da Oliveira, in the heart of the city, this dining space boasts a classic decor of stone walls and wood-beamed ceilings. The gourmet cuisine created here by head chef Vítor Matos and overseen daily by chef Liliana Moura is both innovative and focused on the country’s traditional culinary roots. This is presented on three tasting menus (À Descoberta, Raízes and Terra Mãe), alongside a choice of à la carte options.

Name: Don Sebastião
Description: A pleasant and interesting option, where the cuisine is traditionally Portuguese, well presented and copious, with fresh fish presented at your table before being prepared. The impressive wine cellar features no fewer than 75 different ports.

Name: Grand Salon
Address: Avenida da República 171, Vila Real de Santo António, 8900-203, Portugal
Location: Vila Real de Santo António, Portugal
Description: A restaurant occupying one of the most emblematic buildings in town within the walls of the Grand House hotel, where you can enjoy a delightful view of the port of Vila Real de Santo António and the banks of the Guadiana river that acts as a border between Portugal and Spain. Here, a meal is akin to delving deeply into the sophisticated ambience of another era. The decor has been thoughtfully designed, with wicker tables and decorative detail in which wood is the primary resource. The cuisine here is based around ingredients from the Algarve and is showcased on a concise menu that values freshness, seasonality and minimum waste. As a fitting end to this unique experience, enjoy a classic cocktail in the elegant Grand Salon Bar, with its old-style service.

Name: Porto de Santa Maria
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Terrace
Description: This attractively renovated classic restaurant right by the beach has returned to its origins serving wild-caught fish and seafood that is as popular as ever!

Name: A Velha
Address: Alameda De Santo António 18, Abrantes, 2200-297, Portugal
Description: A small yet highly authentic property with lots of mementoes of those who lived in this area in the past, a time when this restaurant was no more than a simple “tasca”. Entry is through a door reminiscent of days gone by, which gives an indication of what you’ll find inside –a space that showcases the simplicity of another era. The menu comes courtesy of award-winning chef Rodrigo Castelo, who is renowned for keeping the traditions of Portuguese cuisine alive, while always adding his own personal touch to proceedings. Dishes such as the oxtail croquettes, the “arroz de tomate” served with a fillet of sea bass, and the traditional fritter-like “velhoses” (here, they are served with salted caramel and ham), will live long in the memory.

Name: Kappo
Description: Named after the Japanese term “to cut and to cook”, Kappo is a restaurant with an elegance and intimate ambience that come as a pleasant surprise. At the helm here is chef Tiago Penão, who has extensive experience working in leading restaurants. His skill and his respect for his ingredients are clearly evident, as he expertly combines the traditional and contemporary in his cuisine, resulting in precise and extraordinary dishes. Alongside his team, he brings great passion to his Omakase menu, which is complemented by an array of à la carte options (nigiri, sashimi, temaki etc). The highlight of the space is the dining counter, where guests can appreciate the synchronised preparation of dishes to the full, although other dining tables are laid out around it. A unique dining experience!

Name: Villa Cipriani
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Terrace
Description: Occupying a villa at the Belmond Reid's Palace, the Villa Cipriani provides an elegant setting for Italian cuisine with superb views of the cliffs, particularly from the terrace. The professional team here is very much old school!

Name: Cafeína
Description: The unique azulejo covered façade leads to two elegantly contemporary dining rooms, one in the style of a library. Good menu of traditional Portuguese and international cuisine.

Name: Largo do Toural 23, Guimaraes, 4810 427, Portugal
FacilitiesAndServices: There are few places where you can enjoy a meal accompanied by a view teeming with history but this is definitely the case at 34. So, if you’re exploring the charming town of Guimarães, make sure you book a table on the third floor of this restaurant boasting a delightful view of Toural square and the historic São Pedro basilica. The ambience here is modern and relaxed, accompanied by a tasteful decor of different woods that are in harmony with the verdant backdrop. The menu features an array of international dishes from the fresh burrata to Japanese-inspired options such as the salmon belly, rounding off your meal, perhaps, with the refined “borrego” with chestnut purée – reasons galore to book a table here!

Name: Castas e Pratos
Address: Rua José Vasques Osório, Peso da Régua, 5050-280, Portugal
Description: A delightful restaurant occupying a former train station warehouse with a terrace overlooking the tracks, a wine bar and a dining room with high ceilings. Superb wine cellar!

Name: Armazém do Sal
Description: A rustic - style property with lots of character and charm thanks to the combination of traditional wood and stone and modern art on display. A contemporary take on traditional cuisine.

Name: Suba
Address: Rua de Santa Catarina 1, Lisbon, 1200-401, Portugal
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Great view,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: The name (Suba translates as “climb up” in Portuguese) offers an invitation to dine at this restaurant on the top floor of the Verride Palácio Santa Catarina hotel, a palatial 18C property that has provided the aristocratic inspiration for the uniforms worn by the attentive team. Once you’ve savoured its modern and extensive Portuguese-style cuisine (á la carte, including vegetarian options, and as many as five menus), head up to the panoramic rooftop with its stunning 360° views of Lisbon. Children under 12 are not permitted in the restaurant.

Name: Willie's
Description: Located in a popular tourist area where the focus is very much on golf! In the welcoming dining room, enjoy classic, attractively presented cuisine aimed at an international clientele.

Name: Marinheiro
Address: Rua Gomes de Amorim 1842, Póvoa de Varzim, 4490-091, Portugal
Description: A ship run aground is the setting of this imaginative restaurant on two levels. Charming nautical décor and a varied menu.

Name: Petiscas
Address: Largo da Alegria, Ponte de Lima, 4990-240, Portugal
Description: An attractive and intimate restaurant with a good location next to the Ponte Velho. Impressive à la carte menu of traditional and regional Portuguese cooking, including the must - try cod with corn bread (bacalhau com broa).

Name: Casinha Velha
Description: Casinha Velha occupies a charming two-storey house with a rustic decor and homely ambience where tradition and high-quality ingredients are key tenets. Starters include a platter of cheeses and Iberian black pork sausages, accompanied by a basket of different types of home-baked bread. These are followed by signature mains that include cod with cream and shrimp and “duck rice” with dried fruits, followed by an assortment of “convent”-style desserts and pastries – all prepared with great dedication and panache!

Name: DOC
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: (Temporarily closed for refurbishment) This restaurant in a contemporary - style is beside the Douro river and has an attractive terrace over the river. Enjoy the good views and taste its traditional cuisine with a creative flair.

Name: Fauno
Address: Rua Estreita de Lóios 5, Porto, 4050-244, Portugal
Description: Behind the green retro-style glass doors of this restaurant in one of the city’s narrow streets you’ll find a unique dining space run by brothers Pedro Amorim (sommelier) and Tiago Amorim (chef) who have embarked on their first project together here.
