The cuisine comes courtesy of a single tasting menu (including a vegetarian option) that constantly evolves with the seasons and the availability of ingredients from local producers, all characterised by faultless execution and good taste. For an even more impressive dining experience, pair each dish with different wines or a cocktail or mocktail. We can also highly recommend the chef’s daily specials!

Name: Nast
Description: Dean Masschelein has added his inimitable stamp to a former chicory factory, retaining the original rough brick walls, but cleverly dotted with modern fixtures and fittings. The chef is a genuine West Flemish lad, as his exuberant personality and passion for regional produce quickly reveal. The food is succulent, straightforward and international and he might mix presa iberico with a sweet-sour baba ghanoush and Mediterranean fregola, all of which comes together thanks to an emulsion of bacon. Creative seasonal cooking, rendered even more flavoursome when paired with gueuze beers or organic wines.

Name: Dah Makan
Description: Cod marinated in miso and grilled on a robata, served with crunchy veg and lashings of frothy beurre blanc spiked with yuzu… Dishes to share such as these explain the success of this snug eatery. The culinary score, depicted by Asian flavours and western influences, demonstrates a clear preference for superior produce such as wagyu beef or crab from the North Sea, which are often finished on a robata grill or teppanyaki griddle. The menu is almost impossibly varied!

Name: Dante
Description: “Falling and getting back up” is how Sven Fonteyn describes his journey. He designed this charming friendly restaurant as his very own paradise, a feeling he endeavours to communicate through his cooking. Each dish is depicted by his open-minded outlook and commitment to quality. Exotic, often Asian twists add a refreshing dimension to his playful recipes, illustrated by his new take on the traditional rabbit with prunes recipe. The spot-on menu changes regularly, to the delight of the loyal crowd of patrons.

Name: Delphine Ronsyn
Description: Delphine Ronsyn opened this cheerful spacious restaurant, whose floor-to-ceiling windows command fantastic views of the surrounding fields and meadows, less than a kilometre from the family farm. Naturally enough, Delphine is a champion of local produce and her region. Her bistronomic menu is deceptively simple and straightforward, as the delicate chervil sauce that flanks gilt-head bream consummately illustrates.

Name: la petite Madeleine
Address: rue de la Madeleine 19, Tournai, 7500, Belgium
Description: Behind the authentic historic façade lies a contemporary interior, adorned with arty photos and boasting a fine terrace to the rear. Chef Dufranne enjoys surprising diners with his original recipes and generous helpings. Each dish is a treasure trove of meticulously prepared ingredients and fascinating combinations.

Name: Guzzi
Description: This characteristic town house with a small garden is a stalwart champion of Italian simplicity. The chefs add a new, yet respectful spin to authentic flavours. The menu is devised according to the availability of fresh, preferably organic ingredients, occasionally jazzed up with a Mediterranean twist. We recommend their sourdough pizzas cooked in a clay oven – your tastebuds won’t know what has hit them!

Name: Brimer
Description: Looking for a delicious but inexpensive meal? The Brimers do it with flair. Their magic formula? Fine ingredients cooked with originality, generosity and flavour. And Mrs Brimer knows where to find the tastiest mushrooms.

Name: Escabèche
Description: The trendy welcoming interior of Escabèche is a hit with the inhabitants of Knokke. They pop in to chat with the friendly hostess, Lisbeth, and to sample the delicacies rustled up by chef Verhasselt, a virtuoso in the art of enhancing first-class ingredients. Blessedly free of fancy frills, you can expect a wholesome lineup of pedigree Gallic nosh, flanked by subtle side dishes and occasionally jazzed up with Mediterranean or Oriental twists. The extensive appetising menu ranges from a hamachi-based festival of Asian flavours to a juicy fillet of turbot in a Dijon mustard sauce or the gamey earthiness of pheasant à la brabançonne during game season. The vast menu is heaven for foodies!

Name: De Steenen Haene
Description: An irresistible friendly vibe echoes throughout this pretty modernised cottage, whose terrace-garden is set amidst fields and pastures. The family-run restaurant serves classical delicacies such as grilled lobster and the spring chicken and croquettes exhibit the chef’s talent. Flavour and generosity epitomise this establishment.

Name: Roosenberg
Description: Waasmunster’s discerning foodies make up the faithful clientele of this smart eatery. They come for the elegant interior, friendly vibe and top-quality produce, without forgetting the lure of the wine cellar, well stocked in Burgundy and Tuscan tipples. The à la carte lineup embodies the establishment’s devotion to quality. Chef-owner Bruno De Wilde errs towards flame-licked techniques and seasonal ingredients, together with signature dishes like vol-au-vent, tartare steak, asparagus à la flamande or local game in season. What’s not to like?

Name: Lys d'Or
Description: Black marble, a blue and gold colour scheme and a grand piano set the scene in this stylish, modern venue, providing the perfect foil to the elegant, classical cuisine by chef Wattenberge. The purity of the produce is enhanced by consummate technique. Star ingredients include turbot, sole from the North Sea and pigeon from Anjou.

Name: Resto 136
Description: Make a beeline for this peacock blue townhouse at number 136 where you will be pampered by Niels and Laura. Their elegant contemporary establishment upholds tradition and while the chef clearly enjoys mixing spicy Asian flavours with Mediterranean extravagance, he is equally capable of winning you over with a flawless piece of cod flanked by knockout beurre blanc and creamy mashed potato.

Name: Klost’r
Description: As soon as you venture over the threshold into this stylishly restored farmstead, you are warmly greeted by sommelier Lennert Holstens. His pals in the kitchen, Marco Veraldi and Chiem Boijen, take your tastebuds hostage with their creative talent. Gourmet cuisine meets family favourites is the hallmark of their modern elegant score. Surprises abound, such as a dessert of Hesbaye cherries and white chocolate. Expertly chosen Limburg wines add the final flourish, without forgetting the B&B, wellbeing facilities and beauty parlour!

Name: L'inizio
Description: Old family photos adorn the walls of Fabian Dichiara's sleek establishment, near the centre of Herve. The open kitchen is the focal point in the cosy dining space. The chef here combines familiar Italian flavours in his own special way, ensuring you leave satisfied. Whether you opt for the al dente calamarata pasta with wild mushrooms and bacon, or the stuffed tomato with its juicy meat and bold tomato sauce, this cuisine is sure to warm the cockles of your heart. Only a set menu is served at lunchtime; in the evening you can order à la carte.

Name: Talloor d'Or
Description: You will immediately feel at home in the tasteful interior of the Talloor d’Or. Seated at the counter, you can admire the chef at work, rustling up contemporary dishes in keeping with the establishment’s vibe. Subtle vegetable dishes, fine sauces and a few citrus notes enhance and underscore the main ingredient. Seasoned Matthias and Nikki give free rein to their creative bent.

Name: Racines
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Bring your own bottle,Car park,Interesting wine list
Description: Enter this wine bar boutique, choose a bottle (€15 corkage fee if you drink it here) and take a seat in the conservatory overlooking a stream. Welcome to Racines, where Louise and Maxime are on hand to guide and advise you. They enjoy waxing lyrical about their sustainable development beliefs and their love of all things local, which the chefs transform into enticing dishes rich in youthful appeal. A “slow wine and food” concept oozing with genuine authenticity.

Name: Yijiangnan
Description: The patterned wallpaper and understated class of this posh establishment are obvious right from the first minute, but it is the alfresco patio that will win your heart. Every detail counts from the first hello to the last farewell. Yijiangnan specialises in straightforward, generous Chinese cuisine. Rather than a never-ending menu, you will find family favourites such as Peking duck, together with a few more modern creations. All the better when you know that the prices won’t break the bank.

Name: Pur Boeuf
Description: The remarkable maturing room and attractive open wine cellar set the scene for chef Hanselaer’s two overriding passions. Son of a cattle breeder, Blanc Bleu Belge beef takes pride of place on the menu, which also showcases the strength and flavour of other fine ingredients. The resourceful chef is never short of creativity, demonstrated by his modern take on Belgian endive baked in ham and cheese and while his carne cuisine occasionally reaches the realm of high-flying, it is never OTT. The cheese and dessert trolley in particular is spectacular! A must if you plan on touring the Lake Donk area.

Name: Julienne
Description: This upmarket establishment dripping in marble, which is bright and airy by day and cosy by night, extends a warm welcome typical of the Kempen region, before presenting an enticing menu and list of daily specials. Seasoned chef, Tim Moeskops, knows his classics and skilfully turns out dishes ranging from crispy, generously filled shrimp fritters and fresh, juicy sole to flavoursome eel in sorrel or a Poire belle Hélène, straight from his own pear orchard. Julienne celebrates heroic classics and does so with flair and know-how.

Name: DOOR73
Description: OAK’s younger sibling is hip and friendly. The handsome mosaic tiled floor and open kitchen first draw the eye, before you sit down to sample the Greek-born chef’s Mediterranean fare. You can choose between three types of menu: Comfort, Trust and Discover, featuring a range of international, unusual and deftly crafted dishes to share, such as his fascinating Holstein tonnato 2.0! Expect to be surprised!

Name: Le Jardin de la Gaichel
Description: Le cosy Jardin de la Gaichel est en parfaite harmonie avec son environnement boisé (un cadre idéal pour passer une nuitée !). La cuisine d’inspiration bretonne va droit au but. Fruits de mer (sur réservation), foie gras, canard découpé en salle… Une vraie cuisine de produits classique.

Name: Lafarques
Description: This heritage country mansion, gleaming with classy elegance, will take your breath away. Both the surrounding countryside and the stylish guestrooms are exquisite. The cordon bleu chef allows the (preferably local) ingredients to shout their name, whilst seeking to generously and delicately enhance their traditional flavours. Don’t miss the game in season.

Name: Brasserie Latem
Description: There is more to this stylish brasserie on the busy Kortrijksesteenweg than you might expect. Chef Van den Bossche's love of Asia is evident throughout the restaurant, from the decor of the izakaya to the lounge-like terrace and the cigar lounge. Although you will find sashimi options and a bento box on the menu, it is dominated by classic fare. Think sumptuous vol-au-vent, onglet à l'échalote and pan-fried ray wing – prepared the way it should be: generously and using the finest ingredients. The extensive wine list is definitely worth exploring!

Name: De Huifkar
Description: Fish and lobster are the specialties of this vintage-modern restaurant. Admire the quality and freshness of the produce in the lobster tank at the entrance. The chef is keen on classical recipes and generous flavours, depicted by timeless dishes such as monkfish with shrimp, local-style poached cod, without forgetting Belgium’s family favourite, veal kidneys in mustard sauce. Affordable gastronomy!

Name: Vinke
Description: The understated modernity of Vinke, which verges on the mysterious, is enhanced by a huge brass counter. Each dish showcases chef Gilles Demeere’s talents, demonstrating a modern culinary repertory of undiluted purity. Classics like sole meunière rub shoulders with more creative inventions, such as pink Steenvoorde pigeon served with a jus of the bones and a mousse made out of the liver and heart for extra depth and flavour. The chef’s generosity is further underscored by velvety mashed potato and thyme-flavoured green peas.

Name: Graspoort
Description: Graffiti on the walls and a homemade tropical tree hung with brightly coloured leaves set the scene in this fun, offbeat eatery. Thibault Van Stratum cooks instinctively and frequently finds his inspiration in Asia. Highly creative fusion cuisine brimming in influences, illustrated by croaker and marinated mussels jazzed up by smoked oil-perfumed dashi.

Name: Chez Flo
Description: Imagine crispy, yet tender pigeon breast, flanked by legs cooked in a foie gras preparation, all of which in a full-bodied jus overflowing in gutsy flavour. Such dishes are emblematic of Florence Porignon’s culinary flair. After honing her skills in top establishments, Ms Porignon’s distinctive signature shines through in a modern repertory, which hits the spot every time and is depicted by a delicate touch that enhances knockout flavours.

Name: Vier
Description: Concrete, black and turquoise set the unusual scene in this imposing, yet nonetheless cosy venue. Fine produce such as cottage garden veggies and black chicken from Burgundy takes pride of place in the cooking of chef Bas. Natural, simple and seasonal sum up his ethos, all of which flanked by knockout sauces and at prices that make sense in the heart of Kortrijk!

Name: Amélys
Description: This light, airy brasserie pleases everyone. It serves tasty, scrumptious food all day long. The varied menu features classical and more modern dishes, always with the chef’s surprising and distinctive hallmark. Delicious Sunday brunch.

Name: Les Abris
Description: Ring the bell and enter this friendly eatery, taking a seat in the lovely sitting room for a drink as you admire the lush green garden. Chef Kristof Timmermans and sommelier Tijs Coessens have pooled their joint talents to create a customised experience. After the host’s insightful explanations, we immediately noticed that everything is cooked to order. The chef’s skill can be tasted in the spot-on cooking and fascinating side dishes, for example, as oxalis and a sweet-sour cream of chickpeas add whoomph to langoustine. Les Abris offers gourmet shelter to foodies in search of sustenance!

Name: De Koolputten
Description: These former coal shafts overlooking the Mirabrug bridge have been carefully restored and are now home to a comfortable B&B, an exhibition area, an events venue and this restaurant. A trendy, pleasant setting in which to sample contemporary fare with classical roots, with a very open feel. Up-to-date cuisine with gastronomic flair.

Name: Equilibrium
Address: 107 Rue de la Tour Jacob, 1831, Luxembourg
Description: Baptiste Heugens boldly steps outside the box to create unexpected, yet balanced dishes, pairing his consummate knowhow with unconventional associations. The chef likes to cook fish (from Brittany) simply and purely, adding a new dimension thanks to side dishes jazzed up with fresh, spicy or tangy notes for added depth and intensity. A fascinating quest for culinary balance. We advise choosing a table downstairs for a bird’s eye view of the zinc counter where the cold dishes are prepared.

Name: Béus
Description: Maria and Michel welcome guests to their gourmet establishment as if they were old friends of the family. Maria tends to your every need in the dining room, while Michel crafts what appears to be classical fare, yet with a subtle modern spin. Examples range from old-school grilled white pudding and traditional sole meunière with fresh fries to scallops served with curry-flavoured beurre blanc. Soul-warming food that has kept up with the times. At Béus, which loosely translates as “our home” in the local lingo, flavour is the overriding goal every time.

Name: Maurice
Description: The friendly eatery of delightful Kaatje De Blick and chef Karl Ave is in fact named after their cat! They aim for a home-from-home vibe and welcome guests like old friends: “Maurice is like coming home” in their own words. The sommelier can be relied on to ply you with insightful tips, whilst the veteran chef masterfully deploys his classical training to craft knockout dishes and sauces, albeit with the occasional more modern twist. For example, he often slips in Asian notes, illustrated by a ballotine of langoustine underscored by a sublime yuzu and dashi sauce.

Name: Refter
Description: Top notch ingredients, complex-free combinations and gutsy flavours. Don’t expect fancy frills in this casual bistro, adorned with a colourful eye-catching mosaic. The food is always first rate and flawlessly executed – skin-on cod and yummy dame blanche (vanilla ice cream and hot chocolate sauce) dessert.

Name: L'Espérance
Description: The experience starts with the lovely 1930 façade. Inside, historic details such as period windows set the stylish scene. In his open-plan kitchen, the chef crafts fresh bistronomic fare with the odd Mediterranean tang. He might pair fresh, briny turbot with a champagne-flavoured beurre blanc liberally garnished in garden herbs. The (mainly Gallic) wine list impresses both by the range and by its affordable prices.

Name: Lounge Roannay
Description: The contemporary brasserie of the luxury Le Roannay Hotel is more than a match for our expectations: pedigree French cuisine served in a relaxed ambience. How about the rich velvety flavour of a foie gras terrine is paired with apples to add a subtle acidic kick or a thick slice of cod flanked by a smoothly unctuous beurre blanc? Familiar flavours and stellar execution are the hallmarks of the Roannay Lounge.

Name: Côté Préféré
Description: A delicious slab of turbot cooked on the bone with a beurre noisette, al dente asparagus and a creamy morel sauce. Such are some of Tim Versyck’s emblematic recipes. The ingredient rules in his mainly classical repertory, albeit with the occasional international spin. The chef sources his produce locally, particularly fish from the North Sea and veggies, meat and poultry from the polders of West Flanders. The bright contemporary interior aims to pay tribute to the earthy, wholesome terroir of Flanders.

Name: OX'E
Description: Take a seat by the open fire for a drink before your meal and admire the refurbished Art deco interior as you get ready to sample an ode to classicism in a cosmopolitan vibe. Chef Xavier Leys, who avows a weakness for matured meat, cannot be faulted for his textbook craftsmanship when it comes to recipes such as Rossini tournedos or seabass in a salt crust. The focus is on familiar, even regressive comfort food, which is perfectly paired with South-African, French or Italian wines.

Name: Otoro
Description: Pajtim Bajrami makes no bones about his love of produce, as the top-drawer scallops, wagyu beef and other delicacies quickly demonstrate. His Anjou pigeon is a perfect example: he first cooks the breasts rare before adding a high-flying felicitous blend of foie gras and truffles. Polished French classics are right up his street, enhanced by gutsy sauces and the odd Asian tang. A cosy interior depicts this eatery sodden with rippling ambition. A knock-out wine list and Ardita’s friendly, professional service add the final flourish.

Name: Decan
Description: Jan Decan is a pianist and a chef down to his very core, as his restaurant, an elegant harmony of ebony and ivory, musically reflects. You may even see him play if you’re lucky! Jan enjoys jazzing up classical recipes, adding contemporary notes with the greatest respect for the ingredient. He excels in orchestrating dishes such as sole meunière or saddle of lamb with morels and green asparagus. His subtle sauces, flavoursome acidic melodies and familiar tunes demonstrate his talent as an accomplished (culinary) conductor. Ah! Music to our ears!

Name: L'Entretien
Description: On the first floor of a modern BMW dealership, this open-plan restaurant sports a huge, glazed facade. Chef Robin is a dab hand at looking after our inner well-being. Adding a modern spin to French recipes, he shines the spotlight on ingredients, among which foie gras and pork. He may have a playful approach to textures, but the attention he lavishes on the vegetables and rich flavours is second to none. Even better, the restaurant is open for breakfast.

Name: Bottega Vannini
Description: This lively bottega doubles as a delicatessen, so you tuck into your meal surrounded by shelves of Italian delicacies (be sure to stop by the counter afterwards). Expect no frills here, just unadulterated Mediterranean flavours. Their take on beloved classics like vitello tonnato and saltimbocca alla romana showcases the full potential of these dishes. Or how about perfectly al dente cavatelli pasta with succulent sausage meat and crunchy niebé beans? Accompanied by interesting wines (corkage fee €15). Irresistibly authentic!

Name: Hors-Champs
Description: Stefan Jacobs has metamorphosed the Ernage farmstead. This gifted chef has opened a B&B, a bakery and a tasteful restaurant that sports a rough, brutalist look. His sustainable ethos can be tasted in subtle dishes, rich in unexpected and playful combinations. He pays a sincere homage to his region as he showcases the produce of local market gardeners and from his own garden. Examples include lamb from the Censier farm (an earthy stew of lamb shoulder, a fritter of chopped lamb tripe and a succulent lamb fillet) flanked with different textures of sweet corn.

Name: Bar Bulot at Botanic
Description: This hip, cosmopolitan brasserie, Antwerp’s outpost of Bruge’s Bar Bulot, has found refuge in the lavish Botanic Sanctuary Hotel. Timeless classics such as asparagus à la flamande, vol-au-vent of Bresse chicken, sweetbread and shrimp are revamped to tempt and tickle today’s tastebuds. Top-notch ingredients and contemporary flavours, by way of exotic spices, add character to each dish. Heaven for discerning foodies!

Name: Lin’eau
Description: This former flax factory (1907) is steeped in history, as is illustrated by the bare stone walls, authentic details and photos. This heritage is cleverly set off by trendy influences and personal works of art. A young couple is behind the helm, rustling up modern, painstakingly devised, international recipes, flanked by infused sauces and varied textures. The epitome of culinary delicacy.

Name: Rôtisserie Ardennaise
Description: Glittering light fixtures and colourful chairs set the scene in this buzzy brasserie, whose watchwords are tradition and emotion. The ingredient is the star of the chef’s distinctive cuisine. He modernises traditional classics, creating contrasts and playing on textures. Spit roasted chicken (also take-away) is one of the house specialties.

Name: Mout
Description: Walk past the Damse Brouwers microbrewery to the cosy dining space and treat yourself to a brew straight from the tank. What a lovely prelude to a fine meal in a convivial setting! Chef Monteyne's passion shines through in the restaurant's exciting, modern dishes. In the afternoon, you can tuck into light snacks and lunch options; the evening menu offers a wider selection. He has a penchant for bold accoutrements, such as salt-crusted celeriac and the tangy beurre blanc emulsion that he uses to elevate plaice.

Name: Casello
Description: This former toll station on the Turnhout-Antwerp road has morphed into a sophisticated restaurant. The sleek annexe drips with designer luxury and gilt details, and the open kitchen is sure to draw the eye as soon as you arrive. The chef works with top-notch ingredients, elevating them with subtle Asian touches and the bold flavours of Italy. Whether in the form of langoustine with wawasai and enoki, or tagliatelle with truffle and horn of plenty, this modern approach to the principle of "less is more" is captivating.

Name: Linéa
Description: Frederic Scavone made a name for himself at Le Pontecino in Liège, before setting up shop in this impressive edifice, flanked by a modern wing. His contemporary spin on Italian cooking does feature the occasional Gallic twang, but Mediterranean exuberance is probably its overriding characteristic. Rigatoni alla norma, homemade ravioli with fresh sausages and a personal interpretation of tiramisu… Flavour is the watchword of Linéa. Book a room and treat yourself to a truly relaxing weekend in style.

Name: Les Frères Louise
Description: This beautifully renovated miller's house (1737) has retained its classic soul and rustic charm – open fireplaces, rotating art collection, selection of cigars and pipe tobacco, and a lovely courtyard terrace. The Mertens family invite you to their restaurant, where you will be treated like an old friend as you tuck into timeless classics made with the finest ingredients, such as partridge shot by a local hunter and soufflé generously infused with Grand Marnier. This restaurant is known for its freshly cooked fries, delicious sauces, masterful cooking on the charcoal grill and large à la carte menu. The sommelier has a penchant for German wines, and his passion is infectious!

Name: Brasserie David
Description: The menu of David Dewaele’s friendly brasserie showcases all the traditional delicacies of this coastline. The entirely open-plan kitchen allows you to admire his work as he prepares sole, seabass and shrimp. The side dishes are creatively crafted and add an extra whoomph to each dish. Ideal to sample Belgian favourites with a sprinkling of originality.

Name: Le Grand Pré
Address: Rue du Grand Pré 13A, Hantes-Wihéries, 6560, Belgium
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Sprawling meadows encircle this old riverside stone farmstead, so it isn’t surprising that the country vibe has wound its tendrils into the interior. This friendly eatery takes pride in sourcing local Walloon produce that is crafted into a lineup of pedigree seasonal Gallic fare, like saddle of lamb, cooked rare in a herby crust, garnished with a subtle rosemary gravy and potato salad. The splendid wine list boasts over 400 references and is definitely worth a gander. A meal at the Grand Pré makes the perfect ending to a tour of this beautiful rural region. Country life at its best!

Name: L.E.S.S. Eatery
Description: Love Eat Share Smile is the baseline of this hip urban eatery, which is equally suited to a hunger-obliterating snack at the bar as to a full-course feast with all the trimmings with all the family. You can expect an international culinary repertory with a definite Asian slant. From steak tartare with a Korean kick and ceviche scattered with distinctive fresh, spicy, tangy Peruvian notes to Hong-Kong-style young turbot, the extensive menu is a treasure trove of premium produce and creativity. A trendy, suitably casual vibe depicts one of Bruges’ most popular foodie hotspots!

Name: Cosma
Description: The bright, hip, relaxed vibe of this restaurant immediately sets everyone at ease. This enthusiasm is further enhanced when you take a glance at the menu which sports a wide range of dishes to be shared, countless vegetarian suggestions and excellent side dishes – bravo! An unusual formula and heart-warming international influences.

Name: Les Tilleuls
Description: The former village hall of Céroux-Mousty has been turned into a welcoming bistro. Marc Volkaerts has thrown all his experience and enthusiasm into his own individual version of classical cuisine, such as tartare steak or duck shepherd’s pie, adding a personal and distinctive spin to consummately bistronomic dishes. Masterful!

Name: Locàle by Kok au Vin
Description: Locally sourced ingredients and a deep respect for nature's rhythms are the cornerstones of this cosy establishment. Influences from around the globe and the occasional use of the Mibrasa charcoal oven take things up a notch. The menu features dishes for sharing, such as zingy ceviche made with earthy beetroot or Zeeland mussels cooked in Bruges wheat beer. Nothing overly complicated, just playful, on-trend delicious food.

Name: Bistrôt Le Ciel
Description: The sky is visible through the glazed roof and tropical plants and contemporary artwork set the singular scene indoors, while the terrace is taken by storm in fine weather. The food features a pageant of polished French fare with the occasional Italian twist, illustrated by terrine of foie gras or venison in a Grand Veneur sauce. Consummate craftsmanship and a reverent respect for culinary tradition.

Name: Adagio & Gusto
Description: Philippo Santangelo and his right-arm man John Oremans take their time to ensure that your culinary experience will be truly memorable. They invite you to step inside their tastefully appointed townhouse and lovely adjoining garden. Their modern version of Italian cuisine from the authentic flavours of minestrone soup, which are treated to a creative new twist, to the cannelloni of sole in a noisette butter sauce, has already acquired numerous fans.

Name: Clash
Description: Clash is a hip and vibrant restaurant with posters of celebrities providing an extra touch of cool. The lighting even gives the place a bit of a disco feel (be sure to check out the regular DJ nights). Classic dishes reign supreme on the menu, with aged meat being a big feature. No unnecessary frills, just straightforward, bold flavours. You might start with some crispy shrimp croquettes, then, during the game season, move on to pheasant roasted on the bone à la brabançonne. Be sure to leave room for the Brussels waffle, prepared to a time-honoured recipe. The extensive menu will leave you spoilt for choice.

Name: Le Délice du Jour
Address: Rue du Chemin de Fer 57, Chapelle-lez-Herlaimont, 7160, Belgium
Description: Fabrizzio Chirico, who needs no introduction in Wallonia, is back on the gastro scene. He has set up shop in this elegant villa adorned with tasteful decor in warm tones. The chef's passion for working with top-quality, local ingredients is evident in every dish, and the sauces are particularly impressive. Classically trained, he is nonetheless keen to embrace new techniques and likes to play with zingy and smoky flavours, as well as juxtaposing textures. Think raw scallop taken to the next level with a lacto-fermented sauce or black tea enriched with the scallop's coral. One thing is for sure: you won't leave hungry!

Name: RectoVerso
Description: Loïc Thirion and Robin Van Habost are fanatical about pedigree Gallic cuisine. They invariably wave a cheerful greeting to diners from the open-plan kitchen of their contemporary establishment. First class produce, such as local game and mushrooms, is crafted into comfortingly familiar dishes rich in enticing aromas, to which the youthful chefs add a distinctive, personal and sometimes surprising touch. Feelgood French fare by fervent foodies.

Name: 't Pachthuis
Description: Behind the walls of this characterful villa hides a romantic restaurant and a lovely garden patio – ideal for lunch or dinner in summertime! Chef De Keyser shares his fondness for classicism as you will quickly remark when you taste his sauces. However, he is not averse to a dash of originality thanks to subtle combinations of flavours and modern influences. Excellent value for pleasure!

Name: Akko
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Akko’s lounge vibe never fails to appeal as you savour the panoramic view over the gardens from the bay windows. Ingredients take centre stage in the cuisine of a youthful chef who creates up-to-the-minute associations. Unexpected details, varied textures and distinctive sauces set the delicious culinary scene.

Name: Toit
Description: The Boulemberg firm has opened this unusual restaurant on the roof of its manufacturing showroom. Floor to ceiling windows (their stock in trade!) and a terrace command splendid views of the lush green countryside, while a Mediterranean-inspired interior provides the perfect foil to extravagant, full-bodied Sardinian recipes underscored by French technique. Hence the contrast between steamed seabass and cooked sweetbread, paired with a lemon confit beurre blanc. The menu (renewed every six weeks) is rich in big-boned Mediterranean flavours and aromas.

Name: Nyde
Description: The decision to call their restaurant Nyde, which means “to enjoy” in Danish, was far from ingenuous. Chef Céline, flanked by Martijn, your host, bend over backwards to make sure their guests enjoy their meal. The restaurant, whose vibe is serene and boasts a gorgeous patio to the rear, offers a set menu and a selection of cocktails and mocktails and insightful food-wine pairings. Céline underscores each ingredient’s purity as she seeks to sensitively enhance their flavours. She may garnish a lemon-flavoured mackerel tartare with a delicate concoction of diced cucumber and briny oysters, all of which is further offset by a lemon and cucumber dressing. Feelgood food that is guaranteed to lift your spirits.

Name: Tafeltje Rond
Description: Tafeltje Rond enjoys something of a reputation as a romantic venue. Parisian chic defines this brasserie which sports parquet floors, elegantly laid tables, a black and white colour scheme and tableware that is as classy as the wine list and chef Slangen’s polished Gallic score. Old school classics like seabass in a salt crust, tournedos Rossini and hop shoots in a divine hollandaise sauce are rich in the distinctive flavours of yesteryear and the ethereal profiteroles filled with rich vanilla ice cream and smothered in intense dark chocolate are to die for! Don’t hesitate to give the chef your feedback directly as he loves popping out of the kitchen to add a final touch to dishes and say hi to his guests. Set menu at lunchtime only; à la carte in the evening.

Name: Schéiss
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: The colourful "lounge" vibe of the Schéiss provides a perfect backdrop to its owners’ very personal vision of classicism. The meat is carved before diners at the table and the menu is essentially composed of traditional dishes, to which the chef adds his own modern flourish.

Name: Atelier Noun
Description: Bert and Sandra’s workshop sports a cosy, lounge vibe, underscored by Scandinavian accents and a splendid leafy al fresco area. The couple’s passion can be felt throughout the restaurant and Bert adores rustling up fascinating modern recipes, scattered with Asian nuances and incisive, acidic notes. Paradise for foodies!

Name: Roma
Description: Opened in 1950, Roma was the first Italian restaurant of Luxembourg, and it remains true to its founding authentic values. Seventy years on, little has changed and the venue, adorned with Venetian chandeliers, is still as vibrant and colourful as the food is wholesome. The pasta is homemade and oozes with crisp Mediterranean accents. Examples include pasta stuffed with seafood and a velvety vongole-type sauce or why not order a melt-in-the-mouth medallion of lamb, flanked by a gutsy gravy, mashed potatoes and scamorza? Themed festivals and a varied menu with something for everyone transform each meal into a feast.

Name: Tomo Ya
Description: Sushis are the speciality of this minimalist establishment. The extensive menu also offers a wide range of noodle dishes, but we particularly recommend you try the mind-blowing lineup of fresh fish dishes. Salmon maki, beef gyoza or wafer-thin sashimi: forthright, authentic flavours blessedly free of fancy frills.

Name: De Jangeli
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: The focus in this airy, elegant restaurant is on fresh and varied bistronomic recipes. The menu (changed monthly) is deliciously appetising, as is the theme menu (also regularly renewed). Don’t hesitate to ask the experienced wine waiter for advice.

Name: Heritage
Description: Behind a characteristic brick façade in the historic Patershol district lies a charming restaurant whose soul is clearly devoted to nature. Fish and vegetables top the bill in recipes oozing with Latin-American accents. Gutsy enchiladas and tortillas acquire gourmet status in this characterful establishment, which bills itself as a “Match made in heaven” – fascinating!

Name: De Pefferkär
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Wheelchair access
Description: An elegant restaurant adorned with vibrant modern artwork. The boundless energy of the lady of the house and her son can be felt in their cuisine. Building on a classical repertory, they don’t hesitate to introduce modern textures and techniques and the owner-wine waiter will suggest fine local wines.

Name: Hostellerie Stafelter
Description: Tom Brosius is the culinary guardian of this modern, elegant hotel. He sources excellent market-fresh produce and locally grown ingredients which are assembled using modern techniques. Varied and delicious, with an appetising vegetarian menu. Comfortable guestrooms.

Name: Les Jardins d'Anaïs
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Valet parking
Description: These gardens are the epitome of posh elegance from the conservatory overlooking the lush greenery to the guestrooms, without forgetting the champagne trolley. All of which doesn’t prevent chef Parjouet from occasionally erring from the path of classicism and giving a free rein to his creative streak. Fillet of smoked sturgeon is paired with a striking gin and caviar sorbet and subtly offset by asparagus, foie gras and grapefruit. Bold, daring, spot-on cuisine!

Name: Bistronome
Description: At this chic bistro, chef Hospital imparts a lesson in bistronomy every day, giving popular dishes and flavours a gourmet spin. The food is as exquisite to behold as it is to taste. Throw in the occasional creative twist and a fine dose of generosity and the scene is set. Along with dishes that have been revamped with seasonings from around the globe, the menu also features classics such as braised beef cheeks in a bold red wine sauce and al dente pappardelle.

Name: La Paulée Marie-Pierre
Description: This friendly establishment is named after an ancient Burgundy wine festival, which is far from a coincidence. It is even possible to buy a bottle to take home from the sensibly priced wine bin. The culinary score errs towards the traditional, albeit with a more contemporary lineup of suggestions. Examples include tender juicy veal garnished with a poultry sauce enriched in Comté cheese and a gratin of sliced potatoes and onions. The lunchtime menu embodies the big-hearted mindset of this culinary landmark of Tournai.

Name: L'Auberge
Description: The mix of leather, wood panelling, copper and glass gives L'Auberge the look and feel of an authentic brasserie. Located in Spa's bustling town centre, this restaurant has plenty of regulars, who come to savour traditional Belgian cuisine. The menu features hearty classics such as mussels in white wine (also available in half portions), veal kidneys à la liégeoise, crêpes mikado – the generous flavours will leave you feeling warm and satisfied. The guestrooms are worth a look if you're considering a longer stay.

Name: Manoir de Lébioles
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus
Description: The chef working at this manor house creates his own personal style of up - to - the - minute cuisine using the highest quality ingredients. Chic, modern decor and lovely panoramic terrace.

Name: La Cour de la Reine
Description: The ‘Queen’s Courtyard’ aims to serve creative bistronomic dishes with strong classical overtones. The chef, a seasoned stalwart, has no qualms about letting creativity guide his inspiration and you will taste the chef’s personal version of a Belgian classic, shrimp fritters, together with a cutlet of venison with a heroically wondrous pepper sauce. A distinctive metal structure forms the centrepiece of the elegant establishment, which also offers swish guestrooms.

Name: Al Piccolo Mondo
Description: Chef Jonathan and wine waiter Rino have added a classy touch to their dad’s pizzeria and the result is both upbeat and appealing. Immaculately selected Italian wines are perfectly paired with flavoursome food, revealing a fine balance between intense and subtle flavours. The à la carte menu reveals the chef’s knack with traditional dishes such as vitello tonnato, while the set menu is more modern in inspiration.

Name: Nage
Description: The character of this medieval mansion has been intelligently enhanced by the cosy, trendy revamp. Niki shares his know-how in terms of choice of excellent natural wines to pair with the modern French recipes crafted by Koen. The chef sprinkles his cooking with the occasional unexpected note in a bid to further highlight the ingredients’ authentic flavours. Examples include saddle of lamb cooked in butter with suave, flavoursome side dishes based on wild garlic. A word of warning: à la carte only at lunchtime and set menu only in the evening.

Name: Eddy Vraie
Description: Chef Eddy’s last name (True) is emblematic of his powerful, authentic cooking. No pointless frills or fuss. Generous helpings of good wholesome food await the hungry diner.

Name: La Barrière de Transinne
Address: rue de la Barrière 4, Transinne, 6890, Belgium
Description: There is no question as to the rich heritage of the Barrière de Transinne, but rather than the ubiquitous olde worlde clichés, this former hunting lodge is a picture of modernity and Ardennes hospitality. Enticing gastronomic nosh is served à la carte and in set menus (named after the owners’ sons). A fervent upholder of Gallic culinary traditions, the Barrière respects its region and the seasons.

Name: De Kruidenmolen
Description: Ostend-style shrimp fritters, rabbit stew in stout beer, a German jam doughnut filled with rosemary flavoured crème patissière: such are a few of the culinary gems that explain the success of this tastefully restored former miller’s house in the heart of the unspoiled polder countryside. Ask for a table on the terrace sheltered by panes of glass and admire the landscape. A fan of humble, often overlooked ingredients, the chef has no lack of creativity and his enticing menu appeals to all foodies. The establishment’s continuing popularity is borne out by the lively, bustling vibe that inevitably sets the scene at mealtimes.

Name: Bistro Mathilda
Description: This modern bistro is much more than a pleasant trendy interior. The chef’s influences are wide ranging with a focus on first class ingredients. Bistro Mathilda brings the promise of a fine meal!

Name: Table Rase
Description: Ludovic and Clarisse tick all the boxes when it comes to good food, starting with the eater-friendly prices of their welcoming eatery. Chef Ludovic enjoys shining the spotlight on his region, as he jazzes up immaculately crafted dishes with acidic, savoury or other subtle touches. He cleverly mixes smoked eel, foie gras and red beetroot in a punchy celery and wasabi jus. A “clean slate” for a fresh beginning with the distinctive signature of a veteran chef.

Name: La Manufacture
Description: This sprawling, industrial-inspired restaurant with a central, open-plan kitchen and a disco mirror ball amusingly hanging over the stoves lies behind the grocery store. Trendy and fashionable is the name of the game as the chefs’ open-minded, no-holds barred approach to Mediterranean fusion cuisine illustrates: creativity, top quality ingredients and consummate technique.

Name: Magnà
Description: “Magnà!” is what Steven Mirelli’s grandmother used to shout to summon the family at mealtimes. No need to shout now, as the eatery is packed with fans of its authentic Italian cucina. From the subtle hint of lemon peel in the osso bucco to the big-boned aromas of pasta alla carbonara, the ingredients are first-rate, the flavours authentic and familiar and the generosity second to none at Magnà!

Name: Il Trionfo
Description: Il Trionfo is both an elegant restaurant and a family story. The father and daughter-in-law preside front-of-house, and their enthusiasm is infectious. He also has some fantastic wine recommendations up his sleeve. Upon entering the restaurant, you will catch a glimpse of the mother and son at work in the kitchen. You can opt for the more creative set menu or order à la carte from a selection of traditional robust Mediterranean classics like vitello tonnato and spaghetti vongole. Don't miss the osso buco – the meat is unbelievably tender, and that typically rich tomato sauce is simply divine. The quintessence of Italian generosity!

Name: Le D'Arville
Description: This inviting redbrick, 19C farmhouse features a clever mixture of rustic and modern, while its terrace, furnished with wooden tables, commands a fine view of the countryside. The creative cuisine is depicted by regional recipes and a large proportion of house - made preparations. The Barabas guest rooms offer modern comforts.

Name: La Ligne Rouge
Description: This stylish contemporary eatery depicted by crisp clean lines is the epitome of tranquil. On the edge of Soignes Forest, get ready to be pampered by a friendly waiting team. Guillaume Desart himself describes his style as “nouvelle classical cuisine”. Indeed, his passion for top-drawer ingredients and his flair for sauces are indicative of a desire to uphold tradition, albeit scattered with playful notes, such as crispy calf sweetbread flanked by a velvety béarnaise with nasturtium-flavoured vinegar.

Name: Château du Mylord
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Terrace
Description: Martin and Nuria Simonart have breathed a new lease of life into this English-looking manor house (1861), a landmark for foodies for many years. Rich in period charm, you can expect a log-burning fire to greet you in winter. The food is high-flying, with a quest for perfection that occasionally borders on daring. Cream of Jerusalem artichoke with coffee-flavoured mushrooms and scallops, all of which jazzed up by a tangy mandarin jelly. Delicacy is what best defines this establishment.

Name: Agnes
Description: The restoration of this former presbytery in the picturesque lanes around Sint-Martens-Bodegem Church has preserved the edifice’s authentic character, oozing in subtle charm. Diners are invited to choose from a range of amusing and unusual dishes to share, such as open sushi of river eel, Szechuan pepper and wasabi and sesame seed mayonnaise or traditional sweetbread and mushroom vol-au-vent. The intelligently curated wine list and insightful tips from the sommelier add the final flourish.

Name: Robuust
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Credit cards not accepted,Terrace
Description: The contemporary elegance of this delightful villa is more than worthy of a home decoration magazine. Even better, it is flanked by a lovely patio and boasts a small conservatory to the rear. The chef focuses on flavours which he crafts into his own versions of traditional recipes such as classic eels in green herbs and vol-au-vent. High-flying, inspired craftsmanship and lashings of flavour illustrate that Robuust is far from averse to showcasing its delicate facet.

Name: La Baita
Description: Authentic aromas and flavours of linguine alla Genovese, thickly cut wagyu picanha, grilled rare or a modern take on cannoli: this enchanting restaurant celebrates all the facets of Italian cuisine. Chef Sandro gets a kick out of mixing techniques and textures, adding his own distinctive hallmark to each dish, whilst remaining true to his homeland’s culinary roots – the chef hails from Marche.

Name: RAS
Description: The view of the Scheldt River and the docks makes this restaurant's terrace one of the finest in Antwerp! Thanks to all the windows, the water feels omnipresent, even if you are seated inside. Charcoal sketches by Rinus Van de Velde lend an arty feel to the sleek interior. The extensive menu is dominated by traditional favourites. The fried sole is an obvious classic, but for something truly special, try the crispy veal sweetbreads in a brown stock and port sauce. The generous portions certainly go down well. And for those in a hurry, a quick lunch is always available, too.

Name: Ember
Description: A smoky live fire focus is at the core of the DNA of Ember, as the wood-burning BBQ in the open-plan kitchen illustrates. In fact, as soon as you cross the threshold of this splendid 17C castle, your tastebuds are taken by storm by the enticing aromas. The interior is as minimalist as the menu. Zino Jacobs is a fan of local produce and his cooking embodies a zero waste ethos. Jacobs wholeheartedly conveys his culinary vision via unusual dishes presented in a set menu. The food is carefully crafted and steeped in fresh, acidic notes. Examples include charred whole pumpkin, which is then mashed and enhanced by a shiitake-based XO sauce; melt-in-the-mouth Brasvar pork undergoes the same treatment with a punchy gravy that is offset by crushed hazelnuts, smoked bacon and grilled almonds. Truly fascinating!

Name: Esmeralda
Description: Stefan Verhasselt has been at the helm of this elegant edifice, next-door to Knokke casino, since 1975. His vast experience can be felt and tasted in every detail and particularly in the choice produce, which is mainly from the sea. He has a flair for transforming Zeebrugge shrimp into crispy fritters and his sole meunière garnished with fresh tartare sauce and piping hot fresh fries is second to none. Rather than complex or fussy preparations, you will be treated to a banquet of classical know-how, illustrated by the house specialty, seabass in a salt crust.

Name: La table du Royal Snail
Address: avenue de la Plante 23, Namur, 5000, Belgium
Description: This laid-back restaurant is appointed in the same trendy, glamorous vein as the Royal Snail Hotel in which it is housed. The welcoming, casual vibe provides the perfect foil to sample Carl Gillain’s bistronomic vision. The slate menu features a pageant of unconventional bistro dishes and sensibly priced wines. He might add depth to ravioli of turnip with a stock of roast onion and veal, imparting subtle umami, but then again, he may simply pair a juicy entrecote with a fresh, wonderfully light, silky bearnaise sauce. Most of the dishes are designed to be shared, although you may not always wish to do so…

Name: Les Potes au Feu
Address: avenue de la Plante 4, Namur, 5000, Belgium
Description: A couple of pals, Damien Gorjanec and François Schepens, have added a new spin to the bistronomic concept with creativity as their baseline, depicted by locally grown veggies, unorthodox combinations and throbbing sauces. For example, they might mix black and Morello cherries with a cocoa crumble and vanilla ice cream made with unpasteurised milk. A casual, fun vibe bordering on rock ‘n roll with masses of taste in the plate.

Name: Barisdam
Description: As chef Puype casts his culinary spell with top-drawer produce such as asparagus or loin of veal, you know you’re in for a magical bistronomic treat. Examples include a ceviche of rockfish with creamy goat’s cheese to offset the acidity and a crunchy medley of finely diced celery and carrots. Recognisable food crafted with flair thanks to gutsy sauces and intelligently balanced generous flavours. A word of advice: Pieter and Virginie’s friendly eatery is ideal for family get togethers.

Name: Yirmi
Description: A meal in this elegant villa starts with the solicitous welcome of Adrien, who will later be your host in the bespoke glazed wine cellar where you are invited to select your own bottle at fixed prices depending on your menu (watch out for bargains!). Jeremy Vandernoot has harnessed his creativity to devising a formula in which you are free to choose the number of courses. Our inspectors were particularly impressed by the chef’s apple brioche and croissant ice cream, served with butterscotch caramel and cider sabayon. The team’s enthusiasm can be tasted in each bite.

Name: Aster
Description: Veg, locally caught fish and fire are the raison d’être of this urban eatery at the end of Rue Dansaert. The menu sports a cornucopia of creative combinations and amusing textures that frequently astound. Examples include monkfish underscored by a fascinating butter and sake sauce, while fish liver, steamed in spinach leaf, further highlights the savoury notes and finely chopped lovage adds a powerful final flourish. Aster is well and truly in the zeitgeist thanks to wholehearted, big-boned flavours and perfectly judged nuances.

Name: Pazzo
Description: Ingrid Neven’s jovial, casual eatery with a separate patio is well-known among foodies for its international score and superb wine list (wine bar above the restaurant). Ingrid avows a weakness for Italian recipes and truffles, without forgetting Asian and Middle Eastern notes. The extensive menu features dishes such as risotto al dente with black truffle, Korean-style gnocchi and seabass in mandarin and cardamon. A seasoned chef, Ingrid lures us back with her playful, unconventional approach to cooking.

Name: Cuisine & Nous
Description: Cuisine & Nous is a no-nonsense eatery, known for its warm, welcoming vibe. Modern materials adorn the characterful walls of this Ardennes edifice. The enthusiastic chef enjoys reworking Gallic recipes, adding his own hallmark signature. Fancy a duck breast in a popcorn crust? His no-holds barred approach to cooking is underscored by his superlative culinary expertise. Exemplary value for money!

Name: The Chick
Description: Ancient murals and untreated or designer materials paint the picture in this authentic 16C edifice, idyllically located at the foot of Saint Rumbold’s Tower. A glamorous vibe provides the perfect foil for the creative, international set menu. You can expect unusual dishes such as a barbecued slice of watermelon with crumbly feta, pieces of herring, pistachios and crunchy rice noodles. An apparently classical façade hides a treasure trove of surprises. While you’re there, take the time to explore The (wine) Cellar boutique and The Chapel, ideal for events and special occasions.

Name: Savage
Address: Rue de la Paix 22, Ixelles, 1050, Belgium
Description: The trendy natural interior of Savage is perfectly at home in the fashionable Saint-Boniface neighbourhood. The plant-based cuisine is depicted by fascinating combinations of herbs and vegetables, whose varied impressions and textures never fail to surprise. You can choose meat (from the refrigerated meat counter) or fish to accompany your meal, also selected according to sustainable development criteria.

Name: An der Villa
Description: Enthusiastic Thomas Murer has taken brasserie cuisine to dizzying new heights. His authentic soul-warming fare, sprinkled in subtle modern details has earned him a devoted crowd of regulars. Orange sorbet and vinaigrette spiked with passion fruit and saffron add a refreshing kick to smoked salmon. The reasonably priced lunchtime menu offers the perfect opportunity to pay a visit to this opulent, upmarket historic villa which tastefully marries old and new!

Name: Osteria Cellini
Description: Dining at this cosy osteria is an immersive experience. As soon as you enter this converted school, you are greeted by the sound of Italian songs playing in the background; you will notice the Mediterranean colour scheme, the terracotta and the decorative plants. And then there's the friendly welcome extended by the charismatic owner and maître d. The Italian specialities served here are mainly based on recipes from the Marche region and Sicily. Think al dente tagliolini, a slightly sweet tomato sauce with white wine, chopped lobster and flat-leaf parsley. And if you order the zabaglione, they bring the whole pot to your table. Mediterranean generosity at its best!

Name: Controverse
Description: Crisp clean lines set the scene of the modern brasserie of De Kluizen Golf Club (overlooking the greens), which is as well suited to a date night as to a business lunch. It rightly defines its cuisine as authentically characterful, with a classical repertory starring vitello tonnato, asparagus à la flamande and sabayon. The ingredients are outstanding, the cooking bang on and the sauces subtly suave. In season, you will also find game dishes like saddle of hare. The lunchtime menu never disappoints!

Name: Au Moriane
Description: This 1693 edifice adds a contemporary touch to the historic character of En Neuvice lane by way of bare stone walls and modern comforts. The exquisitely presented food is the handiwork of a gifted chef who demonstrates his international eclecticism, delving freely into the establishment’s cottage garden for his fruit and veggies. The accent is on tradition first and foremost.

Name: Gastrobar Hop
Description: Hop is a gastrobar that celebrates wine and craft beer. The head-spinning choice is fortunately accompanied by the owner’s knowledgeable insights. Whether you choose an unusual natural wine or a craft beer, the chefs will always find a playful combination to enhance your dish. Eschewing luxury ingredients, they have honed in on the flavours of yesteryear and subtly textured variations. Gourmet dining in a delightfully casual setting that hits the spot every time!

Name: Antoine
Description: Lisa’s old family home has lost none of its welcoming allure. Today it is a magnificent restaurant, where Lisa offers excellent, mainly German, wine-food pairings. Chef Mirko concocts elegant dishes whose distinctive flavours are jazzed up with a bold individual touch, all of which founded on modern techniques. Examples include a subtly sweet carpaccio of strawberries paired with a bergamot sherbet and a yoghurt ice cream. Whether you plump for a meat, fish or vegetarian score, you can be certain to taste a festival of flavours.

Name: L'Atelier Windsor
Description: Escoffier, Bocuse; the sources of inspiration immediately set the scene in this restaurant, which honours classical cuisine. The chef seduces the senses with excellent produce, precise preparations and pleasing accompaniments. The décor is equally attractive courtesy of large windows, antique tiling and contemporary furniture... superb!

Name: Lily's
Address: Avenue Emile de Mot 1, Brussels, 1000, Belgium
Description: Lily’s, which recreates the vibe of a Saint Tropez or Los Angeles club in Brussels with elegant, premium materials, a pretty green pergola in summer and dancing at the weekends, has become a hotspot of the Belgian capital. Indulge in a glass of wine or a signature cocktail as you cast your eye over the awesome menu. Familiar Belgian favourites, such as immaculately cooked veal chop with fresh béarnaise sauce, are prepared with the same flair and talent as a ceviche of seabass or truffle taglioni. Attracts A-listers like bees to honey for an unforgettable evening!

Name: Upton
Description: Upton is a hip eatery in a buzzy neighbourhood. Experienced chef, Gianfranco Van de Maele, invites you to sample his globe-trotting approach to food. Start with a cold glass of draught lager, before digging into his succulent fresh pasta, the recipes of which come from his “nonna”. Bisque-flavoured homemade spaghetti and super fresh seafood and shellfish – magnifico! A fascinating modern culinary melting pot that blends Italian authenticity with Asian influences gleaned from his travels.

Name: Un Max de Goût
Description: The charm of the Ourthe running by the side of the restaurant enhances the contemporary elegance inside. The creative, subtle cuisine of talented Maxime Zimmer underscores flavoursome local specialties. His youthful take on text-book classics stimulates our tastebuds. A restaurant with ambitions!

Name: Le Bouton d'Or
Description: The soul of this friendly restaurant bears the hallmark of a love of nature. The veggies come from a neighbouring farmer and the chef hunts the game himself. Generous, unfussy cooking at its best. Partridge is one of the chef’s iconic specialties. The lady of the house can be trusted to suggest flawless wine-food pairings.

Name: Deboeveries
Description: The regulars to this characterful farmstead (awesome terrace!) know that on Fridays, sole, the house specialty, takes pride of place on chef Bert Deboeverie’s menu. The food is steeped in with flavour and rich in clever contemporary combinations. Choice of menus - the all-inclusive formula is highly recommended. Fine selection of mainly French tipples.

Name: Zicht
Description: You can enjoy the knockout view over the Flemish Ardennes as much as you like thanks to Zicht’s immense window walls. The experience is even better on the terrace. A veteran couple pampers you from the start to finish of your meal. Efficient and gracious, Hélène supervises the dining room, while Kwinten concocts subtle Franco-Belgian dishes that reveal his talent and craftsmanship.

Name: September.
Description: As you step over the threshold of September, you will immediately find yourself immersed in its zenitude. A stripped-back, minimalist vibe depicts the spacious interior, which is dotted with plants and has soft music playing in the background. It’s as if nature has merged with inner city Antwerp. Every detail of this establishment has been puzzled over and preened from its respect for the produce and attention to the seasons down to the ‘farm to fork’ concept. Veggies are the stars of the show, sometimes served with meat or fish. Ann Van der Auwera’s inventive, expressive cuisine is bold and distinctive and occasionally sprinkled with the odd Italian or Japanese accent. Intense umami flavours are frequently paired with fresh Mediterranean ingredients. It is summertime at September all year round!

Name: CRKL
Description: Squares and circles set the scene both for the tableware and CRKL’s romantic interior, decked in white and pink, as in the food. The menu’s goal is clear – add a modern twist to seasonal produce. Subtle interactions between the ingredients, international expertise and sauces that create finely balanced flavours.

Name: Klei
Description: Inconspicuously located on the historic Grand Place, this cosy restaurant has a somewhat mysterious feel to it. At the helm, an experienced duo showcase their talents. Sommelier Carl Couvreur bowls diners over with his astute recommendations, while chef Jonathan Devogel delivers haute cuisine in which intricate sauces and influences from around the globe bring the flavours to life. Though his creations can be elaborate, they are ultimately defined by their boldness. Think marinated weever as the main ingredient in an aromatic dish with fig and celery in various guises. The short menu never fails to intrigue!

Name: Pino
Description: As soon as you take a seat, you will be served with a few slices of parmesan to whet your appetite. Pino Rigante is the perfect host and an authentic character. With the help of his sons and family, the team bends over backwards to ensure that their flavoursome, generous Italian dishes are irresistible!

Name: Aal Schoul
Description: The school bench at the entrance and the blackboard pay tribute to Aal Schoul’s former vocation as a village school; it is now a warm eatery adorned in huge works of art. Red meat is omnipresent on the menu, but the chef’s bold, unconventional recipes are what most intrigue. For example, his recipe for poultry breasts rolls out a whole series of cooking techniques, while his highly individual take on a Caesar Salad features a sweet-sour vinaigrette with pili that adds a distinctive kick to the entire dish. An intriguing meal awaits you at Aal Schoul!

Name: De Victorie
Description: This imposing historic farmstead, opposite the vineyards of Chateau Vandeurzen winery, is depicted by a stylish interior, whose centre piece is a sculpted flock of birds in flight that is most eye catching. The estate’s excellent wines are paired with a Gallic lineup of contemporary leaning. The chef enjoys pairing sweetbread with truffles or pheasant with Fine champagne cognac, adding a personal twist along the way by playing with the tangy freshness of ingredients such as kalamansi, yuzu and wine vinegar. It has proved a hit with fans of familiar flavours who appreciate an added twist.

Name: Clairefontaine
Description: Whether it be Bresse chicken or sole, Arnaud Magnier can be relied upon to pamper the ingredients. His classical training shines through in spot-on cooking and intense sauces, although he doesn’t shy away from bolder, more inventive touches. Striking, designer-inspired interior.

Name: Umā
Address: Rue de la Reinette 8, Brussels, 1000, Belgium
Description: Umā stands on a quiet side street near the bustling Porte de Namur. Its white-washed brick outer facade and modern artwork inside are both inviting and attractive. Admire Aurélie Kluyskens at work in the open-plan kitchen, rustling up her own spin on Nikkei cuisine, which she rolls out in a spot-on blend of gutsy Japanese and powerful Peruvian flavours. She adds her signature with subtle spicy notes, imparting a spicy/sweet edge to scallops, courtesy of an espuma of smoked pork. Both the varied à la carte menu and the enticing set menu provide an insight into Ms Kluyskens’ distinctive culinary flair and talent.

Name: Bistrot Blaise
Description: A palette of ochre and pastels make for an inviting atmosphere in this cosy bistro. Dining here is fun. Hanna, who knows the wine list like the back of her hand, immediately makes you feel at home. Chef F-X confidently asserts his distinctive culinary style, which is characterised by Gallic indulgence, phenomenal technique and a wide range of contemporary notes. The chalkboard lists exquisitely seasoned dishes that feature combinations such as langoustine, pig's foot croquette and cauliflower. Occasionally playful, this is satisfying cuisine that celebrates the natural flavours of the produce. The team's enthusiasm is infectious!

Name: L'O à la Bouche
Address: rue Armand de Wasseige 1, Wépion, 5100, Belgium
Description: Tightly packed tables, the characteristic hum of a busy brasserie and the smiling faces of satisfied diners bear witness to the flair and talent of this chef who customises characteristic brasserie dishes. Risotto is a staple of the menu, without forgetting the knockout marriage of a 64° egg, asparagus, eel, bacon and emulsion of haddock. The pain perdu is simply out of this world!

Name: Vintage
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Wheelchair access
Description: Cyril Moulin and Florian Vanderhoeven craft intelligent cuisine that is both bold and polished. Big-boned sauces and playful fresh nuances set the culinary scene. For example, they may pair textbook perfect cod with seaweed, pistachios and a zest of lemon, while velvety green asparagus, a light frothy espuma of seaweed and a pistachio crumble conclude the dish. The chefs conjure up recipes in which outstanding ingredients are delicately and harmoniously assembled. Steven Wullaert suggests insightful food-wine pairings. The scene takes place in a tastefully revamped farmstead surrounded by meadows: huge windows, exposed beams and works of art. A gourmet getaway destination par excellence!

Name: La Cuisine du Côté Vert
Description: The restaurant of Le Côté Vert Hotel unsurprisingly bears the hallmark of nature. Natural materials adorn the interior, whose floor to ceiling windows command a splendid view of the garden. Vegetables are the stars of the show in the chefs’ updated recipes, without forgetting meat and fish. The focus is on allowing each natural ingredient to shout its name.

Name: Le Val d'Amblève
Description: Le Val d’Amblève has had a very successful facelift! The terrace in the garden is exquisite. The chef illustrates his firm grasp of new trends whilst enhancing classical flavours.

Name: Brasserie Côté Cour
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Great view,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: This nostalgic brasserie enjoys an idyllic location in the courtyard of Bourglinster Castle. The terrace on the rampart affords stunning views! The food is mostly plant based, but there is also a separate menu including fish and meat. The cauliflower "risotto" combined with marinated tomatoes and crushed hazelnuts is a shining example of this cuisine, which is inspired by the local nature and is all about bold flavours.

Name: Le Petit Axhe
Description: A journey through the lovely Liège countryside, the owner’s delightful welcome and chef Claes’ scrumptious dishes: get ready to treat yourself from start to finish, safe in the knowledge you are in the hands of an experienced and accomplished chef. You may taste a flawlessly fresh fillet of whiting flanked by an elegant beurre blanc. No compromise on quality is ever tolerated, all the better because the prices make sense.

Name: La Cuisine d'un Gourmand
Description: Ambitious John Maes is a genuine good food lover. His mission in life is to source the best regional ingredients, to unfetter his creativity and to please or surprise his patrons with subtle fare. Outstanding quality at affordable prices. The tasteful, modern interior commands a fine view of the river Meuse.

Name: Découverte
Description: Take a seat in this modern, elegant restaurant by the ramparts and you may hear the moving ‘Last Post’ ceremony that takes place at the nearby Menin Gate every evening at 8pm… Local Westhoek delicacies, cooked creatively and playfully, are rich in the distinctive, crisp flavours that depict the spontaneous, market-fresh cuisine of chef Jeroen. Gracious Séverine can be relied upon for her insightful wine-food pairing tips. Book a room at the B&B, ideal to explore the fascinating heritage of Ypres.

Name: L'Air de Rien
Address: Place du Vieux Tilleul 14, Esneux, 4130, Belgium
Description: A log-burning fire is the centrepiece of this stylishly converted 18C farmstead. In his splendid glass-fronted kitchen, chef Diffels can be seen barbecuing most of the main ingredients, which are largely locally sourced. These take centre stage in particularly creative dishes featuring rich sauces and complex flavours. Fermentation adds a vibrant twist. The chef has a gift for coaxing the best out of every ingredient. He celebrates the earthiness of celeriac, for instance, cooking it in a salt crust and combining it with Comté cheese and sherry. This chef has an artistic bent, and his dishes are truly original.

Name: L'O de Source
Description: The old railway line is visible from the well-tended garden, but this former station is now the venue of a pleasant restaurant. You will be pampered by an enthusiastic couple. Chef Fisset, a keen believer in sustainable farming, concocts food that features subtle technique with rich flavours. A fitting tribute to the outstanding produce of Liege.

Name: Stad 10
Description: Bert Brouwers has set up shop in Stad 10 in Hamont, rolling out his considerable know-how to great effect. He trained with the top chefs of Limburg and this experience can be tasted in his personal takes on pure-bred French fare, jazzed up with the odd creative touch. Japanese and fresh acidic flavours frequently find their way onto the menu. For example, he might slip in a hint of grapefruit and daikon winter radishes to exalt a dish of Anjou pigeon. The natural zen vibe of Stad 10 is emblematic of both the interior decoration and the food.

Name: Nesta
Description: As you enter the lifestyle boutique, you will notice the snug restaurant at the rear leading into a pretty garden, where, as you sit on the patio, you may even be forgiven for thinking you’re in Italy! Chef Kayes Ghourabi soaks his recipes in Italian sunshine as recognisable Mediterranean aromas and flavours unfold and captivate our tastebuds. Examples include a pedigree vitello tonnato or a breast of duck with a hazelnut crumble and a drizzling of subtle cooking juices. Bang on every time and always open to new twists.

Name: De drie ridders
Description: As you cross the threshold and see the red and green colour scheme of the decor, the huge fireplace and period flooring, you will fancy yourself back in 18C West Flanders. So take a seat and soak up the splendour. Emily and Bart are passionate about their work. This manifests itself in their choice of mostly local ingredients, their reinterpretations of time-honoured recipes and the finesse of their creativity. They are committed to using traditional cooking techniques as evidenced in the medium-rare duck fillet with a fine crust, accompanied by glazed vegetables and a jus de canard that incorporates the subtle bitterness of Picon. The carefully curated wine list gives exposure to smaller producers. This is cuisine with soul, bundled into a single set menu.

Name: Couleur Rouge
Description: Wonton, mashed potato with wasabi illustrate the happy marriage between Asian sophistication and French gastronomy. Save room for the splendid platter of Belgian cheeses. The delightful terrace will almost make you forget you are in the heart of Eupen!

Name: Wagyu
Address: Rue du Comte Théodule d'Ursel 14, Durbuy, 6940, Belgium
Description: (Temporarily closed due to a fire) Wout Bru is at the helm of this chic BBQ restaurant. Vintage lighting sets the scene in the tasteful interior, creating an intimate vibe. The open grill, striking bar counter and the dry-ageing fridge all catch the eye. You can expect prime beef from breeds like Wagyu and Holstein, gutsy sauces and a host of meat-based recipes, concocted with consummate culinary know-how.

Name: Octopus
Description: Claude and Sylvie bend over backwards to pamper guests in their seafood eatery near the seawall. Sylvie’s warm welcome and service are framed by distinctive artwork (of octopi), while Claude sensitively adds a new spin to a classical repertory, all of which in a playful vein. Grilled pork fritters, pedigree vol-au-vent, fish from the North Sea (his passion) or rice pudding with strawberries: it is always a pleasure to return to the Octopus.

Name: La Cravache
Description: The culinary classics have no secrets for Koen Devos, whose team can be relied on to add the odd contemporary touch to pedigree dishes. You can expect a repertory of premium produce such as lobster and partridge and recipes that show a reverence for authentic flavours, albeit with modern side dishes. Chef Devos is a horse lover, as you will quickly discover when you admire the elegant interior of this lavish villa. The B&B offers a view of the horses grazing from the windows.

Name: 't Notenhof
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Everything works like clockwork in the lovely ‘t Notenhof establishment. The seasoned owner welcomes guests, sharing his insightful wine tips along the way, while the rich flavours of classical cuisine, albeit with a modern twist, have no secrets for his wife. Eels, Anjou pigeon and seabass are frequent guest stars on her deftly cooked and generously served menu. The lunchtime menu is a steal.

Name: Chez Louis
Description: Chez Louis is a friendly eatery with something for everyone. The menu features Belgian family favourites such as sole meunière and veal kidneys in mustard, as well as chef Lekeu’s more sophisticated culinary score, all of which is depicted by classical generosity. From November to February, a seafood bar is available at weekends. The extensive range of choice is undeniably one of the trump cards of this establishment, as are mussels, in season.

Name: Hof Ter Doest
Description: A 17C monastic farmstead and its 13C barn depicts the picturesque setting of this country restaurant, run by the Dendooven family. You will taste delicious local turf (beef and poultry in particular) and surf (oysters and lobsters from the tank) produce. Hearty, wholesome cooking such as crispy shrimp fritters or Belgian Blanc Bleu beef roasted in a wood-fired oven. Luxurious guestrooms for overnight stays.

Name: Ma Passion
Description: Chef Kris and elegant Sandra share a passion for fine food and fine wine! This handsome townhouse with a lovely patio tastefully blends old and new with an inimitable Belgian knack for colours and materials. The chef voluntarily tries his hand at different styles, mixing the classical flavours of foie gras and sweetbread with subtle sauces and fresh, acidic side dishes, demonstrating his playful side and virtuoso talent.

Name: Bulthaup
Description: Chef Philippe Stevens knows how to pamper his diners. All year long he can be found in this stylish kitchen shop, conjuring up market-fresh fare with a focus on taste and presentation. This modern chef, whose technique is matchless, delicately coaxes the flavour out of choice ingredients. Ask for a table near the kitchen range!

Name: La Brasserie Xavier
Description: This vast brasserie (thankfully, with highly efficient service! ) is divided into several areas, including a fine terrace. The good brasserie food makes ample use of top quality produce.

Name: L'artiste
Address: rue de la Gare 85, Falaën, 5522, Belgium
Description: In the heart of the Ardennes forest, make a beeline for this old railway station decorated in modern style. Chef Depuydt’s creative and contrasted menu combines originality with subtlety and the dishes overflow with details that pay tribute to local produce and Asian influences. Culinary art at its best!

Name: d'Afspanning
Description: Dark floor tiles and bare brick walls set the scene in this historic edifice of Beernem, albeit elegantly paired with modern fixtures and fittings. Diners can choose between cosy nooks or the spacious glazed extension. The varied menu appeals both to fans of classical fare and to those keen to try out world cuisine. The veteran chef is equally at home with the ubiquitous shrimp fritter as with an Asian take on steak tartare. Honest, wholesome fare.

Name: D'Oude Pastorie
Description: Jan Audenaert believes in simplicity before all else, mixing vegetables and exotic herbs to compose stunningly presented dishes. His creativity shines through in the detail he lavishes on the side dishes, illustrated by his upside-down pumpkin pie which is served with a gutsy breast of pheasant. Nothing leaves his kitchen that hasn’t been endlessly pondered and puzzled over. We recommend his lunchtime menus. The minimalist interior of this restored presbytery suits this culinary offering down to a T!

Name: a food affair
Description: As soon as you set foot in this eatery of oriental inspiration, you will feel the serene vibe, further enhanced by the exquisite terrace to the rear. Chef Locquet shares his passion for Thailand and Vietnam. Traditional recipes made with first-class ingredients and dishes that shout the talent and deft touch of their chef. An Asian excursion steeped in subtlety and enthusiasm.

Name: Vos
Description: This trendy joint is unusually located in a tennis club. The Audenaert brothers have successfully taken up the challenge. The youthful chefs’ hallmark can be tasted in mouth - watering dishes. Tasty, creative and flawlessly crafted.
