The modern British dishes come with a creative touch and are prepared with care, letting the natural flavours and textures of the ingredients shine through. Smooth, attentive service adds to the experience.

Name: Chef's Table
Address: 1a Avon Crescent, City of Bristol, BS1 6XQ, United Kingdom
Description: In the old part of the city close to the famous docks you’ll find this intimate, personally run, 2-room restaurant, with a small front terrace, a warm service team and a buzzing atmosphere. The two menus – most diners plump for the tasting menu – offer original, modern and sometimes intricate dishes, which are aesthetically striking and full of flavour.

Name: The Lanesborough Grill
Address: Hyde Park Corner, London, SW1X 7TA, United Kingdom
Description: This ornately decorated restaurant sits at the heart of the Lanesborough Hotel. Its menu moves with the seasons, offering modern British dishes brimming with prime ingredients, and includes lighter options as well as plenty for carnivores. Old school desserts are delivered with a degree of refinement, as befits the surroundings. Weekend dinners come with musical accompaniment.

Name: Bay Horse
Address: 45 The Green, Hurworth on Tees, DL2 2AA, United Kingdom
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: The jewel in the crown of this 15th-century coaching inn is its lovely garden and terrace, closely followed by its crackling fire for a warm winter's welcome. It's a smart, efficiently run but still relaxed and friendly pub, with serious modern cooking made up of many elements. The kitchen team show an ambitious edge, as well as strong classical technique underpinning the dishes – such as a finely made red wine sauce with grouse. If you want to extend your trip, settle in for the night at their cottage next door.

Name: Quaglino's
Address: 16 Bury Street, St James’s, London, SW1Y 6AJ, United Kingdom
Description: This colourful, glamorous restaurant manages to be cavernous and cosy at the same time, with live music and a late night bar adding a certain sultriness to proceedings. The kitchen specialises in contemporary brasserie-style food.

Name: Hakkasan Hanway Place
Address: 8 Hanway Place, Fitzrovia, London, W1T 1HD, United Kingdom
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Notable sake list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus
Description: The very first Hakkasan continues to offer a great night out, thanks to its moody, sensual looks and glamorous, energetic atmosphere. It's well-suited to both a romantic date or a group celebration, and it's certainly worth arriving early for a cocktail or two in the bar. Luxury Cantonese specialities are plentiful across the choice of menus, with the set 'Signature' options representing the best value for money.

Name: Quality Chop House
Address: 91-94 Farringdon Road, Clerkenwell, London, EC1R 3EA, United Kingdom
Description: A landmark London restaurant with a history dating back to 1869, this ‘progressive working class caterer’ champions quality British produce, with the focus on steaks and chops, like Belted Galloway rib-eye, Mangalitsa loin and Barnsley chops; just be sure to also order their deliciously crunchy confit potatoes. The booths are the prized seats and the wine list contains lots of gems, more of which are available at their wine bar just next door.

Name: Café Deco
Address: 43 Store Street, Fitzrovia, London, WC1E 7DB, United Kingdom
Description: The chefs also get involved in the service here at this simply furnished, intimate restaurant. Their dishes are fresh, seasonal, appealingly straightforward and packed with flavour, whether that’s cured ham hock, a lovely smoked eel pie or their delicious chicken. It's one of those relaxed restaurants where you know you’re in the hands of a clued-up and experienced team.

Name: Ochre
Address: The National Gallery, Trafalgar Square, St James’s, London, WC2N 5DN, United Kingdom
Description: Situated on the ground floor of the iconic William Wilkins building, this smart, comfortable bistro deluxe is revolutionising museum dining. All-day menus offer something for everyone, from brunch to dinner, via afternoon tea. Small and large plates have sharing in mind; flavours are vivid and international influences abound.

Name: Chapter One
Address: Farnborough Common, Locksbottom, Bromley, London, BR6 8NF, United Kingdom
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: They’ve got a loyal following at this long-standing restaurant that offers an extensive and appealing menu of modern European dishes. The cooking has some light, delicate touches and prime British produce cooked on the Mibrasa grill is a feature, like Cornish monkfish or Angus rib-eye. It’s all delivered inside a property that dates back to the 1930s and there are subtle references to this period in the elegant décor. The service team bring an enthusiastic smile and real care to their work.

Name: The Three Fishes
Address: Mitton Road, Mitton, BB7 9PQ, United Kingdom
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Chef Nigel Haworth has always been a strong ambassador for Lancashire produce – particularly from the Ribble Valley – and now has his own vegetable garden and polytunnel at this contemporary dining pub. The à la carte might include such unpretentious options as tempura scallops or flavoursome corn fed chicken; there's also a seasonal set menu available in 5 or 8 courses, bookended by cheese rolls and mini Eccles cakes – which have rightly become restaurant staples.

Name: Planque
Address: 322-324 Acton Mews, Dalston, London, E8 4EA, United Kingdom
Description: Set under two railway arches, this boldly styled restaurant is centred around a huge communal table. Listed in size order, the modern British dishes are far more complex than they first appear and show tremendous skill from the kitchen. They are often comprised of three main ingredients, all working in perfect harmony to achieve a great balance of flavours: succulent guinea fowl, for example, might be complemented by earthy Jerusalem artichoke and a hint of bitterness from radicchio. The interesting wine list has an emphasis on small-scale and low-intervention producers.

Name: Salt Yard
Address: 54 Goodge Street, Fitzrovia, London, W1T 4NA, United Kingdom
Description: Having opened it 2005, this buzzy basement restaurant was one of the first in the city to offer small plates and promote the sharing philosophy. Spanish and Italian flavours lead the way, with top-notch ingredients showcased in a mix of traditional and more imaginative dishes. Plenty of Spanish wines and sherries are there to accompany, and the serving team are enthusiastic and sincere. The booths at the back are a great spot.

Name: Chatora
Address: 100 Kew Road, Richmond, London, TW9 2PQ, United Kingdom
Description: With dining on 3 levels and bifold doors leading onto a small terrace, you can sit somewhere different every time you come. The experienced owner and 3 chefs represent the North, East, South and West of India. Generously proportioned, original dishes are authentically spiced and burst with flavour.

Name: Jolene
Address: 21  Newington Green, Islington, London, N16 9PU, United Kingdom
Description: Jolene is the sort of place that we'd all love to have at the end of our street. It's a bakery first and foremost, selling wonderful pastries, biscuits and cakes – as well as delicious bread from flour they mill themselves. There's also a daily written blackboard menu of confidently executed sharing plates, with their house-made pasta something of a feature. The vibe is relaxed and the friendly service team will ensure you're well looked after. You can find more of the same at their Hornsey Road branch.

Name: Bocca di Lupo
Address: 12 Archer Street, Soho, London, WID 7BB, United Kingdom
Description: Longevity in this part of town is a mighty achievement, but it's easy to see why Bocca di Lupo has remained popular for so long. Besides the switched-on service and buzzing atmosphere, the cooking itself provides the classic Italian techniques that everyone loves. The extensive menu takes you on a journey around Italy, with the region of origin listed beside each dish; share some fritti Romani while you make your decision. The marble counter is the place to sit and, for the sweet-toothed, the team also run an ice cream shop, Gelupo, across the road.

Name: Art Sushi
Address: 42E Poole Road, Bournemouth, BH4 9DW, United Kingdom
Description: You can sit at individual oak-topped tables, but it’s at the counter where you can best appreciate the humble and determined approach of chef-owner Kamil. His dream of opening a bright, busy sushi restaurant became a reality here in the suburbs of Bournemouth. The seafood and vegetarian preparations are undertaken with care, understanding and respect; remove the stress of decision making by going for the omakase menu.

Name: Etto
Address: 18 Merrion Row, Dublin City, D02 A316, Ireland
Description: Etto means ‘little’ and this cosy, rustic restaurant close to the National Gallery certainly fits the bill. Start with a snack and a sherry before enjoying eye-catching, modern dishes which are generously sized and full of flavour. The comprehensive wine list has a focus on the Med.

Name: Pickle
Address: 43 Lower Camden Street, Dublin City, D02 N998, Ireland
Description: The modest exterior of this restaurant belies the buzzing atmosphere within. It’s a busy spot and deservedly so, with fresh, vibrant dishes and a service team that do a great job of handling their huge popularity. With spices lined up on the kitchen counter, the chefs aim to marry Irish produce with Northern Indian techniques and flavours in what they sweetly call ‘pickle country’. There’s a good value midweek lunch menu on offer and a tasting menu at dinner alongside the à la carte.

Name: Apricity
Address: 68 Duke Street, Mayfair, London, W1K 6JU, United Kingdom
Description: Just yards from the bustle of Oxford Street is a veritable sanctuary of calm. Chef-owner Chantelle Nicholson’s bright and welcoming restaurant comes with delightful service and a menu that showcases seasonal British ingredients from small producers with whom she’s built strong relationships. Her green credentials are omnipresent and inform her every decision.

Name: Goldsborough Hall
Address: Church Street, Goldsborough, HG5 8NR, United Kingdom
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Wheelchair access
Description: A pretty village plays host to this grand, 16C country house which is surrounded by delightful grounds. There might be a classically formal feel to the place but not when it comes to the food. Modern, French-based dishes are eye-catching, well-balanced and full of bold flavours, with a good mix of classic and contemporary techniques showcasing the skill of the team. Go for the tasting menu with accompanying wine pairings.

Name: River Restaurant by Gordon Ramsay
Address: Savoy Hotel, Strand, London, WC2R 0EU, United Kingdom
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining,Great view,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Wheelchair access
Description: Gordon Ramsay’s second restaurant within the iconic Savoy Hotel offers a great Thames view and an extensive menu specialising in top quality fish and shellfish from UK waters; sit at the seafood counter if you’re after caviar, oysters or ceviche. The ‘River Trio’ perform as the weekend approaches.

Name: Belzan
Address: 371 Smithdown Road, Liverpool, L15 3JJ, United Kingdom
Description: Its somewhat unassuming location makes this smart, modern bistro stand out even more. The cooking offers well-judged, interesting combinations, with portions that are as generous as they flavoursome, but while sharing is encouraged, dishes work better on their own; the Guinness rarebit potato is a must. They also offer a good value early dinner menu. The narrow room has a cosy feel, and service is confident and clued-up.

Name: The Morrison Room
Address: Carton House, Carton Demesne, Maynooth, W23 TD98, Ireland
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Wheelchair access
Description: We all need a little luxury in our lives and this beautiful restaurant in the heart of the impressive Carton House mansion ticks all the boxes. The breathtaking room features a high curved ceiling, Greek Corinthian columns, ornate plaster cornicing and sweeping banquettes, while the menu matches it for opulence with an abundance of first-rate produce, be it Union Hall crab or Achill lamb. The cooking is rooted in the chefs’ strong classical technique, but some wildcard flavour combinations work wonders thanks to their fine judgement.

Name: Library Street
Address: 101 Setanta Place, Dublin City, DO2 W3Y7, Ireland
Description: As you open the door to this trendy restaurant, you’re greeted by a lively buzz and smiling faces. Sit at the counter or one of the lovingly restored 100-year-old ash tables, while surrounded by laughter and contented chatter. The cooking comes in the form of a regularly changing menu of sharing plates, including options like roast lamb with kalamata olives and Jerusalem artichoke. Local ingredients are key to the bold, original dishes.

Name: Birchwood
Address: 13 Flimwell Park, Hawkhurst Road, Flimwell, TN5 7FJ, United Kingdom
Description: Set in a sustainable business park in 46 acres of woodland, this bistro features communal tables and a lovely terrace overlooking the trees. The daily changing breakfast and lunch menu is informed by the owners’ sustainable ethos, the seasons and the surroundings, and dishes are fresh and full of flavour.

Name: Homestead Kitchen
Address: Prudom House, Goathland, YO22 5AN, United Kingdom
Description: The North York Moors and their produce are the inspiration behind this charming little restaurant housed inside a rural, stone-built former farmhouse. Chef-Owner Peter Neville and his partner Cecily Fearnley show great pride as they enthuse about their sustainable philosophy. Local produce – be it Moorland roe deer, Whitby crab or any number of ingredients from the kitchen garden – is used in hearty dishes that pack a punch when it comes to flavour. Sauces and accompaniments are a particular strength of the kitchen.

Name: Maison
Address: Wrecclesham House, Wrecclesham Road, Wrecclesham, GU10 4PS, United Kingdom
Description: In this lovely 15C red-brick house, chef Ben Piette and his wife Lornette found the ideal setting for their dream project. They live upstairs and have converted the downstairs to serve their guests, but view the whole thing as part of their home. The constantly changing surprise tasting menu features plenty of local ingredients in assured dishes which have a French base. Sit at one of just a handful of tables or book “Ben’s Table” in front of the open kitchen; here you can bring in your own ingredient which he will use to create an extra course. Lornette treats guests as if they were old friends, which helps add to the ‘dinner party’ feel.

Name: Cyprus Avenue
Address: 228-230 Upper Newtownards Road, Belfast, BT4 3ET, United Kingdom
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: You’ll find something for everyone at this appealing, all-day bistro. It’s an expansive place, with the booths and the lovely covered terrace among the most prized seats. There’s an extensive choice at breakfast, while at lunch and dinner, freshly baked breads come with delicious hop butter and are followed by a wide selection of hearty, robustly flavoured dishes – sweet-toothed diners shouldn't miss the opportunity to try the sticky toffee madeleines. There's a substantial plant-based offering too.

Name: Craig Millar @ 16 West End
Address: 16 West End, St Monans, KY10 2BX, United Kingdom
Description: A former pub with an attractive interior and a small terrace; most of the tables afford superb harbour views and, as one might expect, there’s a seafood bias to the menus. Good quality ingredients underpin refined, attractively presented dishes which are full of flavour. There’s a good value set price lunch menu, and the evening tasting menus come with a choice of main course.

Name: 'Seasgair' by Michel Roux Jr
Address: Inverlochy Castle, Torlundy, Fort William, PH33 6SN, United Kingdom
Description: ‘Seasgair’ means ‘warm and cosy’ in Gaelic, and diners will certainly feel cosseted in the impressive Inverlochy Castle. The whole experience is like stepping back in time to the country houses of old. Begin with an aperitif in the Grand Hall, accompanied by live music, before taking your seat in one of the elegant dining rooms. A 5 course set menu is served to everyone at the same time with canapés on arrival. Michel Roux Jr’s influence on the menu sees classic French dishes combined with the Scottish ingredients.

Name: Killiecrankie House
Description: A young couple swapped their city lifestyle for this period country house in the Cairngorms National Park, which they lovingly restored to fuse original and modern features. Arrive at 7pm for drinks before dining on a tasting menu of Scottish classics brought playfully up to date. Bedrooms are sumptuous.

Name: Cafe Cecilia
Address: Canal Place, 32 Andrews Road, Dalston, London, E8 4FX, United Kingdom
Description: Don’t be fooled by the name, for this popular local spot is less a café, more a pared-back, industrial-style restaurant with a modern bistro feel. The chef previously worked at St John and the River Café, and now mixes these influences with his Irish heritage. The Guinness Bread ice cream is sublime.

Name: Edie's
Address: 10 Beach Road, Carlyon Bay, St Austell, PL25 3PH, United Kingdom
Description: It's a family affair at this relaxed, friendly restaurant, with Nigel at the stoves, and his wife Kelly out front, aided by their daughter, the eponymous Edie. Inside, brightly coloured chairs stand out against whitewashed brick walls; the shelves are crammed with cookbooks, and there’s a buzz from the open kitchen. Nigel’s experience shows in the unfussy modern British dishes, which deliver appealing and effective flavour combinations with notable clarity.

Name: Lunar
Address: World of Wedgwood, Barlaston, Stoke-on-Trent, ST12 9ER, United Kingdom
Description: Housed in the former staff canteen of the ‘World of Wedgwood’, this vast restaurant is named after The Lunar Society of which Josiah Wedgwood himself was a founding member. Naturally, fine Wedgwood china and tableware is a feature – as are prime British ingredients. The hidden bar is a great place for a drink and the chef’s table looks through a large window into the kitchen so you can get a good view of the team in action. Do take the time to immerse yourself in the amazing visitor experience as a whole.

Name: Smoke
Address: Shadowbrook Lane, Hampton in Arden, B92 0EN, United Kingdom
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Counter dining,Garden or park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus
Description: There’s an air of relaxed conviviality at this charmingly rustic restaurant, which sits in the former smokehouse – beside the kitchen garden – in the grounds of Hampton Manor. A seat at the counter means you can join in the buzz of the kitchen, but in summer it's hard to look past the charms of the greenhouse. The food celebrates seasonal produce and, while dishes may appear simple, they have a hidden creativity and harbour some punchy flavours. The small wine list offers interesting natural, biodynamic and orange wines.

Name: Mulcahys
Address: Main Street, Kenmare, V93 W35F, Ireland
Description: Having been a presence in Kenmare since 1995, this smart, warm restaurant has become a part of the town’s fabric, with plenty of the locals contributing to its lively atmosphere. Come for cocktails and snacks in the bar or settle in for the evening to enjoy a menu underpinned by local beef and seafood. There is a classic edge to the cooking, with options like beef Wellington and fish pie featuring among the flavoursome, carefully cooked dishes.

Name: Mr Fox
Address: 38 Parnell Square West, Dublin City, DO1 X9TO, Ireland
Description: A welcoming restaurant with a charming team and a lovely tiled floor, set in the basement of a striking red-brick Georgian house. The well-priced set menu showcases wonderful Irish produce and the tasty, modern dishes are skilfully enhanced by global flavours.

Name: Volpe Nera
Address: 22 Newtown Park, Blackrock, A94 D780, Ireland
Description: Nestled away in a small parade, the ‘Black Fox’ takes its name from its position midway between the suburbs of Blackrock and Foxrock. Split over two floors, the upstairs has a slightly plusher feel, while the atmosphere is livelier downstairs, in part thanks to the open kitchen. The menu evolves with the seasons, mixing Mediterranean influences like rabbit cavatelli with Asian elements like cep dumplings, across modern, flavoursome dishes. Service comes from a friendly and knowledgeable team, while a carefully curated wine list completes the experience.

Name: Mamó
Address: Harbour House, Harbour Road, Howth, D13 E9H9, Ireland
Description: An experienced couple run this friendly bistro located in a pleasant spot on Howth seafront. Irish ingredients are the bedrock of the menu, including Winetavern Farm pork loin from Wicklow and plenty of seafood from the harbour just over the road. This produce is fashioned into fresh, flavoursome dishes that are carefully cooked and neatly presented. Stick around for dessert, as it’s likely to be a highlight.

Name: Rocket Store
Address: The Harbour, Boscastle, PL35 0HD, United Kingdom
Description: This compact restaurant sits within a 19C store which once housed the coastguard’s horse-drawn rocket firing equipment. The blackboard lists small plates and whole fish dishes; most of the produce is supplied by the owner’s father who, as well as being the harbourmaster, owns a boat and runs a small farm.

Name: 104 Chepstow Road, Bayswater, London, W2 5QS, United Kingdom
FacilitiesAndServices: It might only have six tables but the cosy 104 certainly proves that great things can come in small packages. The Chef-Owner works alone preparing a surprise tasting menu of sophisticated dishes with smart flavour combinations and stand-out sauces. Underlining the modernity in the cooking, there is a pleasing simplicity to each dish, allowing superb luxury ingredients like Cornish turbot or Scottish XL langoustine to shine. For dessert, look out for the deliciously rich signature '104 chocolate bar'.

Name: Stove Bistro
Address: 455 Ormeau Road, Belfast, BT7 3GQ, United Kingdom
Description: As you approach the top of the staircase leading to this first floor restaurant, you are hit by the buzz of happy locals, so book well in advance to secure yourself a table. The concise à la carte menu offers flavoursome, modish bistro dishes created using locally sourced produce.

Name: Stage
Address: 31 Magdalen Road, Exeter, EX2 4TA, United Kingdom
Description: A fun, trendy spot set up on a budget by an enthusiastic group of young men known as the ‘Taco Boys’. Foraged ingredients and produce from the kitchen garden inform the daily changing, surprise tasting menus, and the original, modern dishes have bold flavours and contrasting textures.

Name: Tallow
Address: 15a Church Road, Southborough, TN4 0RX, United Kingdom
Description: You'll get a warm and friendly welcome at this cosy neighbourhood restaurant run by experienced couple Rob and Donna. Situated overlooking the green at Southborough, it's a rustic, homely place with an intimate chef's table counter upstairs if you're looking for a special occasion. Time and care is poured into every well-constructed dish, with each one showcasing the kitchen's strong knowledge of culinary techniques while delivering bold, hearty flavours.

Name: Haar
Address: 1 Golf Place, St Andrews, KY16 9JA, United Kingdom
Description: An appealing restaurant with a modern, Nordic edge; ask for a table on the more characterful first floor, with a view of the open kitchen. The tasting menu reflects the owner’s travels, and offers some bold and powerful flavour combinations. Try the signature smoked lobster – and don’t miss Nana's banoffee.

Name: da Mirco
Address: 4 Bridge Street, Cork, T23 H10E, Ireland
Description: Transport yourself to Italy at this authentic osteria in the heart of the city, where light pours over the tightly packed tables and plants line the walls. Both Irish and imported ingredients feature in the rustic, no-frills dishes, with homemade pastas like spinach and ricotta cannelloni a particular highlight. The service is led by eponymous owner Mirco, who brings a chatty approach to this lively little spot.

Name: Kai Restaurant
Address: 22 Sea Road, Galway, H91 DX47, Ireland
Description: The long-standing, sustainably minded Kai is really two places in one. At lunch, they take walk-ins only and serve one course followed by homemade cakes and pastries (they also have their own bakery). Things ramp up a gear at dinner, with a 3 course à la carte heavily guided by the seasons and the local area. Dishes are often understated in appearance, but just a handful of ingredients are needed for plentiful flavour; keep an eye out for the specials, like a super 'conference pear tarte Tatin'. Excellent wine pairing suggestions will enhance your visit.

Name: Peploe's
Address: 16 St Stephen's Green, Dublin City, D02 KF34, Ireland
Description: An atmospheric cellar restaurant – formerly a bank vault – named after the artist. The comfy room has a warm, clubby feel and a large mural depicts the owner. The well-drilled team present classic Mediterranean dishes and an Old World wine list.

Name: Awabi
Address: 63 Halkett Place, Saint Helier, JE2 4WG, United Kingdom
Description: Owner and self-taught chef, Stephen, takes inspiration from his travels and discoveries across Asia when compiling the immensely appealing menu at this cute neighbourhood spot, which resembles something between a little bistro and an izakaya. There are lots of local ingredients, the bao buns are delicious, and be sure to end with the Japanese French toast.

Name: Neighbourhood
Address: 1 North Main Street, Naas, W91 RH96, Ireland
Description: A pool of young but experienced talent came together to create this contemporary restaurant out of a former pub on the town's main street. The menu is so appealing you’ll have trouble choosing; all the dishes, which rely on superb produce, are comforting and satisfying, with some of the larger options designed for sharing. The bar upstairs offers a small plates menu as an alternative dining option. The service team are full of energy and really help to bring the room alive.

Name: Gwen
Address: 21 Heol Maengwyn, Machynlleth, SY20 8EB, United Kingdom
Description: This warm and welcoming restaurant from the team behind Ynyshir is more of a cousin than a little sister – thanks to the personality Chef Corrin Harrison brings to both his cooking and the service. After a drink in the wine bar, all eight guests are served together in the intimate dining room. The surprise tasting menu offers bold flavours, a good dose of creativity and no small amount of skill. The chefs chat away with diners as the thoroughly enjoyable evening just flies by.

Name: Olivomare
Address: 10 Lower Belgrave Street, Belgravia, London, SW1W 0LJ, United Kingdom
Description: Sardinian cuisine is the order of the day at this bright, well-run Belgravia restaurant. It’s been around for some time, which is a testament to the quality of the seafood-centric cooking. Whether it’s steamed mussels with garlic and parsley or monkfish with courgettes and lemon, the fruits of the sea are celebrated heartily – and the simplest dishes are often the best. Much of the high quality produce in the kitchen is also available to buy at their deli, Olivino, next door.

Name: Oarsman
Address: Bridge Street, Carrick-on-Shannon, N41 AK19, Ireland
Description: This traditional family-run pub sits close to the river and is filled with pottery, bygone artefacts, fishing tackle and, of course, plenty of locals. Service is chatty, there’s a lovely deli, and they even have a lager brewed specifically for them. Flavoursome cooking uses local produce, with the fish dishes being a sure-fire hit, and all of the bread is home baked. The upstairs restaurant opens later in the week.

Name: Delahunt
Address: 39 Camden Street Lower, Dublin City, D02 K277, Ireland
Description: Delahunt must surely be one of the most charming and characterful restaurants in Dublin. Exuding a sense of history throughout its quirky interiors, this old Victorian grocer's shop is mentioned in James Joyce’s ‘Ulysses’, and what was once the clerk’s snug is now a glass-enclosed private dining room. The cooking itself is a showcase for Irish produce, such as fine lamb from The Comeragh Mountains served with a punchy black olive ketchup. As the evening draws to a close, retire to the 'Sitting Room' for a digestif.

Name: Tannery
Address: 10 Quay Street, Dungarvan, X35 XN99, Ireland
Description: Close to the harbour sits this characterful 19C stone tannery that also houses a cookery school. Sit downstairs for small plates at the counter or head upstairs to the bright restaurant. The classically based dishes are generously sized and use good seasonal ingredients – don't overlook the specials either. Stylish bedrooms are spread across two nearby townhouses.

Name: Bay Tree
Address: Newry Street, Carlingford, A91 V054, Ireland
Description: This honest little neighbourhood restaurant sits on the bustling high street of a small town, just a stone’s throw from Carlingford Lough. The carefully prepared dishes are hearty and well-balanced, often featuring vegetables from the garden and seafood from the lough – including its renowned oysters. A range of Asian influences are also on display, be it rogan josh curry or char siu pork belly. Simple, cosy bedrooms are on hand for those staying the night.

Name: Imperial Treasure
Address: 9 Waterloo Place, St James’s, London, SW1Y 4BE, United Kingdom
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Wheelchair access
Description: The first London outpost of this globally renowned group is housed in an imposing former bank, which provides a luxurious backdrop for the traditional, mostly Cantonese cooking. White leather, onyx walls and wood partitions provide some intimacy amongst the opulence, and the extensive selection of dishes offer ample flavour. If you’re after money-is-no-object luxury, look no further than their signature Peking duck with caviar, but you'll still have a great time with the crispy pork belly and honey-glazed char siu pork.

Name: Land to Sea
Address: John Street, Dingle, V92 ET22, Ireland
Description: Proving to be one of the most aptly named restaurants in Ireland, the menu here showcases fine produce from the surrounding fields and nearby waters. The kitchen team take advantage of Kerry meats and wonderfully fresh fish and shellfish with dishes that have a strong classical base and demonstrate a good understanding of flavour. Charming service enhances the overall experience.

Name: Wild Flor
Address: 42 Church Road, Brighton and Hove, BN3 2FN, United Kingdom
Description: A group of lifelong friends own this relaxed neighbourhood restaurant, and they lead the service with obvious pride. The room takes on a modern bistro style and there’s a pleasingly unpretentious feel to the place. Well-prepared, seasonally changing dishes – try the goose rillettes with redcurrants in the winter – have a similarly unfussy style and good depth of flavour.

Name: Kildrummy Inn
Description: There is a luxurious feel to this smartly renovated pub, where the cooking mixes the modern with the traditional. Among the well-executed dishes on the menu are some contemporary choices alongside recognisable classics like rib-eye steak, fish & chips and chicken liver parfait. Come at lunchtime to enjoy their classically served haggis, neaps and tatties, which is a real treat. Four bedrooms, cosy sitting rooms and an immaculate terrace complete the very pretty picture.

Name: 1826 Adare
Address: Church View, Main Street, Adare, V94 R672, Ireland
Description: This pretty little cottage feels right at home in Adare, a picture-postcard village with brightly painted shops and rows of thatched roofs. Inside, there's a cosy, characterful feel to the place, which is run with warmth and confidence by an experienced couple. The interesting, attractively presented dishes proudly spotlight fine Irish produce like Dooncastle oysters and the famous Skeaghanore duck from West Cork; the black sole served on the bone is a real crowd-pleaser. On Sundays, a 'late lunch' menu offers good value for money.

Name: Dean Banks at the Pompadour
Address: 4 Lothian Road, Edinburgh, EH1 2AB, United Kingdom
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Wheelchair access
Description: The Pompadour is one of the city’s most famous restaurant names and it sits within one of its best-known hotels, The Caledonian – if you’re lucky, you may get one of the tables that look up to the castle. The tasting menu makes creative use of prime Scottish produce but with a noticeable Asian influence; contrasts in flavours, textures and temperatures all feature.

Name: Marle
Address: Heckfield Place, Heckfield, RG27 0LD, United Kingdom
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace
Description: Within Heckfield Place – a Georgian country house hotel decorated with the owner’s extensive post-war British art collection – you’ll find this charming, orangery-style dining room looking out over a lake and parkland. Sustainability drives everything they do here, with a great number of ingredients coming from the estate’s own farm; these are fashioned into light, clean dishes that rely on honest, natural flavours. Why not start by ordering the plate of farm vegetables to share, giving you an opportunity to really taste the garden?

Name: The Old Bank
Address: 8 Market Square, Westerham, TN16 1AW, United Kingdom
Description: The contemporary interior of this former high street bank is a perfect match for the beautifully presented modern dishes. Cooking is technically accomplished and flavour combinations display depth and sophistication. You can visit the old vaults to sample wines suggested by the sommelier.

Name: Caractère
Address: 209 Westbourne Park Road, Notting Hill, London, W11 1EA, United Kingdom
Description: 'Never judge a book by its cover' certainly rings true here, as within this former pub sits a convivial and really quite stylish restaurant, where sophisticated cooking combines with efficient, unstuffy service. Alongside an à la carte, you have the option to ‘build your own’ 5 course tasting menu by selecting one dish from each of their ‘character’ profiles; these range from 'Subtle' (such as Acquerello risotto) to 'Robust' (roast lamb, perhaps) and finish with 'Greedy' for dessert. Top-notch ingredients and strong classical technique run throughout.

Name: Lucky Cat by Gordon Ramsay
Address: 10 Grosvenor Square, Mayfair, London, W1K 6JP, United Kingdom
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Notable sake list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Wheelchair access
Description: Gordon Ramsay’s foray into Asian culture is a moody, masculine space in the former Maze, with a chef's table, a striking bar, a banging soundtrack and a fun feel. Accomplished Japanese and Chinese dishes blend British ingredients and are designed for sharing; the bonito fried duck leg bao is a must-try.

Name: Rhosyn
Address: Penally Abbey, Penally, SA70 7PY, United Kingdom
Description: Rhosyn means ‘rose’ in Welsh and there are plenty on display in the gardens of this lovingly restored country house. The gorgeous setting provides a calming atmosphere in which to dine, with a tasting menu or an à la carte to choose from. The seasonally guided cooking is modern in execution but rooted in tried-and-tested flavours we all know and love. Pembrokeshire is well-represented on the menu, so look out for delicious local lamb and some superb new potatoes.

Name: Ugly Butterfly by Adam Handling
Address: Carbis Bay Estate, Carbis Bay, St Ives, TR26 2NP, United Kingdom
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Wheelchair access
Description: From dry ice in the snacks to the original use of beetroot in the desserts, expect creative cooking that is designed to impress at this wonderfully contemporary restaurant. The dishes are often tersely or intriguingly titled – such as ‘All About the Crab’ – and zero waste is also a feature; offcuts are used in bar snacks and also as the basis for drinks, pickles and ferments. The setting, providing uninterrupted coastal views over to Godrevy thanks to floor-to-ceiling windows, is equally impressive.

Name: Pizarro
Address: 194 Bermondsey Street, Southwark, London, SE1 3TQ, United Kingdom
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: José Pizarro has a refreshingly simple way of naming his establishments: after José, his tapas bar, came Pizarro, a larger restaurant a few doors down. A selection of small plates – like croquetas, boquerones and padrón peppers – are joined by larger main courses including presa Ibérica, with dishes proving to be satisfying and cleanly executed. The surroundings are stylish and an all-Spanish wine list boasts some big names.

Name: La Potinière
Address: Main Street, Gullane, EH31 2AA, United Kingdom
Description: An icon in the Scottish hospitality industry, this sweet little restaurant is run in a very personal way by owners Mary and Keith, who share the cooking and have showed great professionalism and dedication over the years. They offer a choice of two dishes per course, each prepared with care and pride. The cooking is traditional at heart with the odd ambitious edge, but with technique this accurate and ingredients this delicious, there's really no need for unnecessary frippery.

Name: Arros QD
Address: 64 Eastcastle Street, Fitzrovia, London, W1W 8NQ, United Kingdom
Description: Rice, and lots of it, is what you can expect to find at this huge, strikingly decorated restaurant from the mind of Spanish Chef Quique Dacosta. Specifically, the menu offers an array of takes on the classic Valencian paella, from pork knuckle to tofu & sea lettuce, but plenty of other dishes are available too, including several cuts of meat and fish cooked over fire. There’s a real theatrical element to the place, so ask for a table on the ground floor where you can watch the action in the open kitchen and see the flames from the wood-fired stoves.

Name: Naïfs
Address: 56 Goldsmith Road, Peckham, London, SE15 5TN, United Kingdom
Description: Owned and run by an alumnus of Vanilla Black, this friendly neighbourhood spot serves solely vegan dishes. The restaurant is simply decorated, with an on-view kitchen, and from here come hearty, original plates full of bold flavours. The set menu makes good use of what's in season and is served all at once, served 'family style' to be shared by the whole table. A few small plates and snacks are available too if you want to enhance the experience.

Name: Little Social
Address: 5 Pollen Street, Mayfair, London, W1S 1NE, United Kingdom
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Little Social has a clubby, comforting feel and a smart, stylish look, with on-trend copper, dark wood, and duck egg blue upholstery ensuring it fits in perfectly with its Mayfair surroundings. The seasonal British menu offers something for everyone, and its creative modern dishes are full of flavour.

Name: Water House Project
Address: 1 Corbridge Crescent, Cambridge Heath, Hackney, London, E2 9DT, United Kingdom
Description: As soon as you walk into this calm, Nordic-style restaurant with an open kitchen and smiling team, you just know you’re going to have a good time. Sit back and enjoy the house aperitif and some fabulous snacks before beginning a tasting menu founded on the finest British ingredients. The produce is treated with a deft touch in elegant dishes that offer refined, balanced flavours – such as West Country mussels with native seaweed and koji. The cooking can be accompanied by either a bespoke wine pairing or a homemade non-alcoholic option.

Name: littlefrench
Address: 2b North View, Westbury Park, City of Bristol, BS6 7QB, United Kingdom
Description: This neighbourhood bistro’s authentic Gallic feel will warm your soul. It’s family owned and run and is certainly a busy place, with visitors being warmly welcomed as if they were regulars. Well-executed dishes are fresh and hearty with a rustic style and bags of flavour; in the evening go for one of their sharing dishes. Service is friendly; ask for a booth beside the semi-open kitchen.

Name: yeni
Address: 55 Beak Street, Soho, London, W1F 9SH, United Kingdom
Description: Anatolian-inspired cooking from experienced chef-owner Civan Er, who made his name at acclaimed sister restaurant Yeni Lokanta in his home city of Istanbul. Daily changing menu of vibrant, gutsy, flavoursome sharing plates; techniques are rooted in tradition, with dishes cooked over oak in the Josper oven.

Name: Exmoor Forest Inn
Description: There’s a rustic charm to this beautifully restored Victorian inn, where they make excellent use of the surrounding estate. The dishes are powered by organic produce from their own farms, which is then turned into a mixture of traditional and modern pub food. Generous and flavourful dishes do these local ingredients proud. A fire-lit lounge and 11 pleasant, relaxing bedrooms complete the package.

Name: Straker's
Address: 91 Golborne Road, Notting Hill, London, W10 5NL, United Kingdom
Description: This is a tale of our times: a chef creates a large fanbase by giving cooking demos on TikTok during lockdown and then opens a small restaurant in Notting Hill so that they can come and experience his cooking first-hand. It’s a very likeable place, with no frills, easy-to-eat cooking that’s modern British by way of Italy; always start by ordering one of the flatbreads – and the sweetbreads are always a good bet too. Low intervention wines are a feature.

Name: Penmaenuchaf
Address: Penmaenuchaf Hotel, Penmaenpool, Dolgellau, LL40 1YB, United Kingdom
Description: Set into the hillside, this attractive country house was built for a Lancashire industrialist around 1860 and is surrounded by beautiful terraced gardens and woodland. Its original features include a wood-panelled former billiards room, which now acts as the drawing room; follow this through into the restaurant, where you'll find the best seats are in the conservatory. The cooking's strength is drawn from the prime quality produce, be that Cornish monkfish or naturally delicious fruits for dessert. Stay overnight to make a proper occasion of your visit.

Name: Furna
Address: 6 New Road, Brighton and Hove, BN1 1UF, United Kingdom
Description: This stylish city centre restaurant is the first solo venture for Chef-Owner Dave Mothersill, who has been a fixture of the Brighton food scene for some time and brings an array of techniques to his precisely crafted dishes. The food is largely served by the proud chefs and focuses on seasonal British produce, with a few international influences and a creative edge. A chic mix of vintage and contemporary décor helps to enhance the experience, with counter seating available to make the most of the fully open kitchen.

Name: Bouchon Racine
Address: 66 Cowcross Street, Clerkenwell, London, EC1M 6BP, United Kingdom
Description: Those with fond memories of the original Racine in Knightsbridge rejoiced when chef Henry Harris opened a new version in 2022. Racine Mark II is just a few steps from Farringdon Station, located above the Three Compasses pub. The blackboard menu is a veritable rollcall of classic French bistro dishes, from escargots to rabbit, duck confit to steak tartare. There are so many tempting dishes; just be sure to end with the terrific crème caramel.

Name: Norma
Address: 8 Charlotte Street, Fitzrovia, London, W1T 2LS, United Kingdom
Description: This Fitzrovian townhouse has been transformed into a handsome, intimate restaurant spread over three floors, with Moroccan tiles and cosy booths. The food of Sicily and its Moorish influences inform the menu, with the 'primi' options including the dish that gave the restaurant its name: pasta alla norma. Generous portions add to the appeal, particularly the immensely satisfying fritto misto and the super-sized cannoli for dessert.

Name: The Small Holding
Address: Ranters Lane, Kilndown, TN17 2SG, United Kingdom
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus
Description: There's a rustic, farmhouse-like feel to this former village pub run by two brothers. The team's focus is firmly on self-sufficiency, growing an array of fruit and vegetables on their own land, using no-dig and low-intervention methods. This seasonal produce heavily informs the monthly changing tasting menu, which blends British and Nordic culinary influences in dishes that have bold, well-balanced flavours and lots of personality. In summer, grab a seat on the terrace for an aperitif overlooking the garden.

Name: Aven
Address: 10 Camden Place, Preston, PR1 3JL, United Kingdom
Description: On the ground floor of the Winckley Stays Hotel, you’ll find this sweet restaurant where an open fire greets you on arrival in the colder months. There’s a cosy feel to the room, which is minimally decorated but enlivened by some bright artwork on the walls. The cooking takes the form of a seasonal tasting menu, with dishes like duck leg suet pudding delivering intense flavours. Friendly, efficient service enhances the experience, as does the choice between two wine flights and even a beer pairing.

Name: Orwell Road
Address: 8 Orwell Road, Dublin City, D06 H2Y5, Ireland
Description: Located in the city's smart suburbs, this buzzy little restaurant is a proper neighbourhood spot. Enjoy snacks and cocktails to start, before moving onto the menu of dishes founded on quality Irish ingredients. Each one is skilfully cooked and provides ample flavour, with the blackberry vacherin dessert a must-order if it's on the menu. It's a small place with a quick turnover of tables, but the chatty and efficient service team handle it with aplomb, making their fast-paced jobs look rather easy. The wine list includes some unusual but intriguing choices.

Name: Cora
Address: 3-7 Duke Street Arcade, Cardiff, CF10 1AZ, United Kingdom
Description: Tucked away in the Castle Quarter Arcades, this small and personally run operation has just five tables and offers a surprise tasting menu full of fresh, seasonal flavours. Chef Lee Skeet is on his own in the kitchen, with his wife Helen delivering charming service out front. Skilful, pared-back dishes showcase quality ingredients and Lee’s eye for detail; he serves many of them himself, turning down the hip-hop soundtrack to explain his cooking with great pride. Their wine and oyster bar, Jackson’s, is situated on the floor below.

Name: Aquitania
Address: High Street, Seaview, PO34 5EX, United Kingdom
Description: Named after an ocean liner known as 'The Ship Beautiful', The Aquitania is a delightfully intimate restaurant which upholds The Seaview Hotel’s proud culinary tradition. The team are warm and welcoming, and the wide-ranging menu bursts with the island’s artisan ingredients. As can be expected from a coastal restaurant, seafood plays an integral role, whether it's crispy crab beignets or a Friday fish & chips special.

Name: The Red Lion
Address: Church Place, Freshwater, PO40 9BP, United Kingdom
Description: It’s not just the open fires and friendly service that make this such a warm and welcoming pub – the delicious beef fat crumpet and the sticky toffee pudding also help! The traditional building has origins dating back to the 11th century, so it's a place full of character, with the garden also supplying super-fresh produce for the clean, well-executed dishes. While there are more informal 'light' and 'large bites' on offer at lunch, the à la carte is available at all times to show off the kitchen's skills.

Name: Da Noi
Address: 63 Bridge Street, Chester, CH1 1NG, United Kingdom
Description: To say that your hosts at this little Italian restaurant are passionate would be an understatement. Chef-Owner Valentina Aviotti and her husband Fabrizio bring pride and personality to all that they do, with Valentina's Italian heritage coming across in a tasting menu of freshly made, authentic Italian cooking; the lasagne made using a recipe from Valentina's nonna is a delight. Wine flights are available and, pleasingly, the list is Italian-dominated.

Name: The Farmers Arms
Description: Open fires and exposed timbers set against touches of contemporary design help make this restored Grade II listed pub, set in a delightful hamlet, a charming place for replenishment and recuperation. The frequently changing menu has an eye on sustainability and utilises quality ingredients from their farm, be it their own hogget or lemon verbena cleverly used to mimic the taste of lemon in a 'zero-mile' lemon geranium cake. Wonderful homemade syrups help create some refreshing aperitifs.

Name: Levan
Address: 12-16 Blenheim Grove, Peckham, London, SE15 4QL, United Kingdom
Description: You can expect a good soundtrack playing over the speakers at this lively, friendly local restaurant named after DJ Larry Levan. The menu is a sharing plates affair – with dishes of mostly European influence – but there's also a tasting menu option, which allows you to sample more of the carefully prepared, original dishes. Be sure to start with the comté fries, and look out for the range of natural wines from smaller producers – more of which are available in Bar Levan next door. The friendly, attentive service team ensure there's a laid-back vibe to proceedings.

Name: Tytherleigh Arms
Address: Chard Road, Tytherleigh, EX13 7BE, United Kingdom
Description: This sympathetically refurbished 16C coaching inn is an endearing place, with a characterful timbered interior that features a large inglenook fireplace. The cooking is best described as wholesome and boldly flavoured, with a menu that blends more modern dishes with pubby favourites like sirloin steak or haddock & chips. Stylish bedrooms await in the old stables if you fancy staying the night.

Name: Kutir
Address: 10 Lincoln Street, Chelsea, London, SW3 2TS, United Kingdom
Description: A pretty end-of-terrace townhouse in an elegant Chelsea street is the setting for this relaxed, stylish Indian restaurant. There’s a lively buzz throughout the various smart yet cosy rooms, with the more intimate upstairs the best choice if you’re on a date. The interesting style of cooking draws from multiple regions of India and offers a wide choice of dishes, from tandoori broccoli to duck madras. The extensive choice of menus cater for a range of diners, with proper vegan and gluten-free options among them.

Name: Canton Blue
Address: 1 Grosvenor Place, Belgravia, London, SW1X 7HJ, United Kingdom
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: Housed inside the spectacular Peninsula Hotel, this Cantonese restaurant is part of a brand housed inside their hotels around the world. The London version boasts its own entrance at the side of the hotel and a sumptuous cocktail bar, Little Blue, which is the perfect way to kick off a rather glamorous evening. The restaurant itself is equally stylish, and the extensive menu offers a wide selection of authentic, flavoursome dishes, from finely executed dim sum to Peking duck for two. The interesting wine list includes a selection of Chinese rice wines by the glass.

Name: Fairmont Windsor Park, Bishopsgate Road, Englefield Green, Egham, TW20 0YL, United Kingdom
GreenStar: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Wheelchair access
FacilitiesAndServices: Named after the date of the signing of the Magna Carta 'down the road' in Runnymede, this elegant restaurant can be found in the slightly labyrinthine Fairmont Windsor Park Hotel. Choose from two lengths of tasting menu or the à la carte, all of which feature prime British ingredients like Suffolk lamb, Torbay crab and vegetables from their own estate. The chefs treat this produce with an unfussy approach, resulting in enjoyably pared-back dishes. Service is smooth and, if you’re dining as a couple, ask for one of the semi-circular booths.

Name: Pêtchi
Address: Unit 13C, Liberty Wharf, La route de Liberation, St Helier, JE2 3NY, United Kingdom
Description: Overlooking Liberation Square, this buzzing restaurant takes inspiration from the chef’s time working in Spain. Ingredients from Jersey and the surrounding area meet techniques often associated with the Basque region; glowing hot coals and a wood-fired oven are both visible in the open kitchen, with a few counter seats available if you can stand the heat. From chops of turbot and ex-dairy cow to Ibérico ham collar, plenty of quality produce gets the fire-based treatment, in dishes that push natural flavours to the fore.

Name: Giulia
Address: 77 Askew Road, Shepherd's Bush, London, W12 9AH, United Kingdom
Description: There’s an authentic, honest feel to this small Italian neighbourhood restaurant. The eponymous owner Giulia can be seen chatting away to guests in her native language and offering great hospitality alongside the cooking. Her partner Endris is in the kitchen following the ethos of pure, ingredient-led cooking with a seasonal focus. Pasta is offered as a separate course, including classic dishes like spaghetti alle vongole. The wine list is sensibly priced and, unsurprisingly, all Italian.

Name: Seasonality
Address: 26 Queen Street, Maidenhead, SL6 1HZ, United Kingdom
Description: What started out as a produce shop has morphed into a bright and airy restaurant, which is run with a lovely personal touch by Chef-Owner Wesley as he cooks at an on-view island kitchen. As its name and history suggests, seasonal ingredients are the foundation of the cooking, put front and centre in assured, colourful dishes that carry an appealing clarity of flavour. Regular supper evenings offer tasting menus inspired by the produce of the moment, while they still offer the 'dine at home' boxes they've done since day one.

Name: Mazi
Address: 12-14 Hillgate Street, Kensington, London, W8 7SR, United Kingdom
Description: A real neighbourhood restaurant with a pure Greek heart, there is a wonderful buzz to the intimate Mazi. It’s one of those places where you can leave the decision making to the passionate, engaging team, who are ready to recommend their favourite Greek wines and dishes. The menu is designed for sharing and mixes classic choices with more modern creations; for dessert however, it’s hard to look past the loukoumades. A small front terrace and larger rear one add to the appeal – if the weather’s good enough, you can pretend you’re in Athens.

Name: The Dory Bistro & Gallery
Address: 15 East Shore, Pittenweem, KY10 2NH, United Kingdom
Description: Opposite the harbour in this little fishing village, you'll find a thoroughly charming restaurant where East Neuk produce is cooked with the care it deserves. Seafood dominates both the menu and the décor, with the restaurant walls doubling up as gallery space for plenty of aqua-based art. The blackboard is the place to look for fresh daily specials, like plump and juicy langoustines or hake with seaweed butter sauce. If you’re local to the area, this could quickly become a favourite haunt – you may even go home with some new artwork.

Name: The Wolseley
Address: 160 Piccadilly, St James’s, London, W1J 9EB, United Kingdom
Description: Like the other restaurants in this group, The Wolseley serves classic European dishes in an elegant setting with a buzzing atmosphere – well-organised service ensures that everything runs like clockwork even in a packed dining room. The extensive menu features top quality seafood dishes, from clams and oysters to crevettes and caviar. The sweet-toothed among you will not be disappointed by a large dessert menu that includes apple strudel and a choice of coupes.

Name: Fallowfields
Address: Housel Bay Road, Lizard, TR12 7PG, United Kingdom
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Wheelchair access
Description: Perched on a cliffside and boasting gorgeous bay views, this restaurant really does provide a setting to die for. It’s backed up by generous dishes that emerge from an open kitchen, served as either a short or long tasting menu. The cooking is detailed and creative, as evidenced by dishes like vodka-cured brill with ginger beer granita. Wine pairings are fairly priced and if there’s a chocolate dessert on the menu, you’re in for a treat.

Name: Fish Shop
Address: 3 Netherley Place, Ballater, AB35 5QE, United Kingdom
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining,Credit cards not accepted
Description: From the genuine, professional service to the array of quality seafood, there is a lot to love about this smart restaurant decorated with a wicker shoal hanging from the ceiling and photos of fishermen on the walls. Fabulous produce, much of it Scottish, powers dishes that accentuate the flavours of their core ingredient with a few well-judged, finely made accompaniments – such as Shetland halibut accompanied by slow roasted tomatoes and salsa verde. As always with the best seafood restaurants, keep an eye on the specials board for more fresh delights.

Name: enotèca
Address: Charing Cross, St Aubin, JE3 8AA, United Kingdom
Description: Jersey meets Italy at this wine bar serving hearty, full-flavoured dishes in what was once a delicatessen. The owners run a business called Wild Wine, which imports natural wines from small producers – and a fabulous choice of these bottles is available to enjoy while dining. The pasta and gelato are both made in-house, and all the cooking is executed with such care. Keep an eye out for the blackboard specials.

Name: Kicky's
Address: 9 Castle House, South Great George's Street, Dublin City, D02 WK13, Ireland
Description: A striking, pop art-style mural frames the kitchen pass at this casual, trendy and thoroughly lively restaurant. The airy interior features whitewashed brick walls, some counter seating and loud hip-hop. Start with ‘bites’ and small plates to share, before moving onto the concise selection of main courses cooked over charcoal. Fabulous produce like Wicklow venison and wild brill on the bone yields bold, satisfying flavours. Make sure you finish with the ‘Irish coffee’, their take on a tiramisu.

Name: Hearth
Address: 10.5 King Street, City of Kingston-upon-Hull, HU1 2JJ, United Kingdom
Description: Run by a trio of friends and located among some fine buildings in the old part of town, this buzzy spot operates over two levels. The ground floor houses a bar and bakery, while the upstairs is home to the rustic two-room restaurant. The menu fuses small plates with larger dishes, often coming from the grill – or ‘hearth’ – that takes centre stage in the open kitchen. Start with sourdough from the bakery, then make sure you check the boards for daily specials, as you might get to enjoy delicious seasonal produce like Yorkshire grouse.

Name: Mara
Address: 11 O'Connell Street, Waterford, X91 F304, Ireland
Description: What was formerly known as The Old Couch Café has been reborn as Mara, retaining its predecessor's quirky vibe and bijou space. Chef-Owner Luis Martin has both passion and ambition in abundance, largely working alone in the kitchen and serving his dishes in the cosy, well-lit room to just six tables. His well-balanced cooking incorporates locally foraged produce alongside a few influences from his native Spain, such as ajo blanco or cod buñuelo; the cep tiramisu, meanwhile, has become something of a signature.

Name: ÖRME
Address: 218 Church Road, Urmston, M41 9DX, United Kingdom
Description: You will find a pleasantly welcoming quality at this small restaurant run by three young owners. There’s a distinct Nordic touch to proceedings, yet British produce is at the heart of the appealing tasting menus, available in 5 or 7 courses. Attractively presented dishes offer bold, vibrant flavours with a mix of the classic and the modern in their influences. Wine flights are also available, including a particularly interesting British themed option.

Name: Argile
Address: 21 Argyle Place, Edinburgh, EH9 1JJ, United Kingdom
Description: Inspired by the sticky clay used for making pottery, the naming of this hidden-away neighbourhood restaurant feels rather apt given the wonderful array of china, pottery and earthenware they use. It’s an intimate operation with modern, sometimes technically complex dishes that draw on global influences. Chef-owner Jack Montgomery serves many dishes himself, pouring passion and a personal touch into the experience.

Name: New Coast Kitchen
Address: 1 St Mary's Road, Croyde, EX33 1LF, United Kingdom
Description: With its relaxed vibe and cheerful service, this is just the kind of restaurant you want to know about when on holiday around the North Devon coast. Head for the terrace out front in good weather – a perfect spot for people watching – or sit inside surrounded by the sleek, modern décor. The adventurous cooking is executed with flair and delivers well-judged combinations of bold flavours, as with the contrast between rich butter sauce and citrus marinated fennel in a wild bass dish. Save room for dessert too, as the confit apple terrine is a highlight.

Name: Tamil Prince
Address: 115 Hemingford Road, Barnsbury, London, N1 1BZ, United Kingdom
Description: It’s such an obvious pairing – a revived old neighbourhood pub with sharing plates of Indian food – that you wonder why there aren’t many more. The appealing menu is nominally inspired by Tamil Nadu but is not bound by its borders and does occasionally venture north. Highlights include Chettinad lamb curry and channa bhatura, while nothing goes with a pint quite like onion bhajis.

Name: Dilsk
Address: 44 Marine Parade, Brighton and Hove, BN2 1PE, United Kingdom
Description: Visit this intimate and slightly moody spot inside the Drakes Hotel and you will likely be treated to some of the delicious, red-brown seaweed – more commonly known as dulse – after which the restaurant is named. Both the Short and Full tasting menus on offer include colourful dishes that are the epitome of modern British cuisine, like hogget with wild garlic and purple sprouting broccoli. The roster of well-chosen wines offers less-common choices that complement the food well.

Name: Lilac
Address: Cellar, 57-58 Broad Street, Lyme Regis, DY7 3QF, United Kingdom
Description: There’s a lovely, relaxed feel to this wine bar and restaurant; it’s a place where you can pop in for a couple of small plates, enjoy a glass of wine or two and, if you’re still hungry, order some more. The cellar location has a rustic, cosy yet surprisingly spacious feel and the seasonal dishes make local ingredients a feature. In line with this sustainable outlook, the wine list spotlights natural, bio-dynamic and low-intervention options. Local botanicals and house-made ferments make their way into the creative cocktail selection.

Name: Atrium
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Wheelchair access
Description: Lords of the Manor is an appropriate name for a 17th-century Cotswolds hotel, and Atrium is an equally apt name for this restaurant located within the hotel's inner sanctum. A large skylight allows natural light to flood into the compact dining room, where diners are served a tasting menu all at the same time. The dishes come with attractive modern presentation and their greatest strength is in the natural flavours of the central ingredients, which are ably cooked by kitchen team. A wine pairing and overnight stay will make an event of your visit.

Name: Rathfinny Tasting Room
Address: Rathfinny Wine Estate, Alfriston, BN26 5TU, United Kingdom
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Wheelchair access
Description: The upper floor of the Rathfinny Winery houses this smart, well-run restaurant that boasts lovely vineyard views. Modern British cooking is guided by seasonal Sussex produce and the colourful dishes prove fresh and flavoursome. Lunch sees a concise fixed price menu, with a tasting selection at dinner; to drink, look no further than their must-try sparkling wine. They also operate bedrooms in The Flint Barns, a nearby farmhouse.

Name: Temple
Address: 10 Granville Terrace, Bude, EX23 8JZ, United Kingdom
Description: This chic, casually run eatery offers ethically sourced, modern rustic cooking in a lively setting. It’s a place of two halves, with the Temple Up Top bar and roof terrace the ideal spot to get the cocktails flowing. Downstairs is the restaurant, which operates more as a café in the day with a few small plates and cakes from the counter. At dinner, a fixed-price menu is served with a selection of snacks to start, followed by a choice of main and dessert. The provenance of the ingredients is paramount, and dishes are fresh, vibrant and full of flavour.

Name: Margot
Address: 45 Great Queen Street, Holborn, London, WC2B 5AA, United Kingdom
Description: The service and the surroundings are equally slick at this plush Italian restaurant on the edge of Covent Garden. The menu offers an appealing choice of dishes, from simply prepared fish of the day to veal-based classics like ossobuco and vitello alla Milanese – and top quality ingredients and bold flavours run throughout. Take time to study the well-chosen wine list, which has a strong focus on the regional wines of Italy.

Name: Vanderlyle
Address: 38 - 40 Mill Road, Cambridge, CB1 2AD, United Kingdom
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Wheelchair access
Description: A large, open-plan kitchen takes centre stage at Vanderlyle, which blends shabby chic styling with designer comfort. The well-balanced vegetarian tasting menu shows imagination and creativity, along with a passion for seasonal produce – all evident in dishes like roasted wild mushrooms with Roscoff onion and Bordelaise sauce. The friendly service team run the restaurant well and the wine or juice pairings enhance the experience. It’s a popular spot, so book in plenty of time.

Name: Twenty Seven
Address: 9 Mill Street, Kingsbridge, TQ7 1ED, United Kingdom
Description: Hidden away in a side street is this small and intimate restaurant which is run with infectious enthusiasm by its chef-owner – making it obvious why it’s such a hit with the locals. The split-level space includes characterful exposed beams in the upstairs dining room, while the cooking itself has an ambitious edge with roots in the county's seasonal larder. There are several menus available, from a tasting option to an à la carte, as well as fixed-price options offering good value for money.

Name: Hannah
Address: County Hall Building, Southbank Riverside, Belvedere Road, Lambeth, London, SE1 7PB, United Kingdom
Description: Never judge a book by its cover – or a restaurant by its entrance! It may be quite quirky in its looks, but this sweetly run Japanese eatery provides an enjoyable and well-rounded omakase experience. It's led by Chef-Owner Daisuke Shimoyama, who shows off his impressive knife skills when preparing a procession of high quality ingredients, be it Wagyu beef, sea bream or lobster. The sake list provides the ideal accompaniment to the cooking.

Name: Decimo
Address: 10 Argyle Street, King’s Cross, London, WC1H 8EG, United Kingdom
Description: Cacti and succulents fill the room and a DJ adds to the buzz at this deliciously different 10th floor restaurant with commanding city views. Peter Sanchez-Iglesias blends the flavours of Spain and Mexico in appealing small plates, by drawing from his father’s Spanish heritage as well as time spent in Mexico.

Name: Bubala
Address: 65 Commercial Street, Spitalfields, London, E1 6BD, United Kingdom
Description: Start with a freshly cooked laffa flatbread and one of their delicious dips before feasting on Middle Eastern-inspired vegan and vegetarian sharing plates, which are elevated by their delicate spicing. Wines are mostly unfiltered, natural and orange – and service is charming and attentive.

Name: Number 16
Address: 16 Byres Road, Glasgow City, G11 5JY, United Kingdom
Description: The passionately run Number 16 occupies a narrow former shop and its tables are split between the ground floor and a mezzanine level. Dishes showcase prime Scottish ingredients and many exhibit subtle modern touches. The wine list provides interest and, like the cooking, represents good value.

Name: Adrift
Address: Dunmore House, Dunmore, P85 HC03, Ireland
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Wheelchair access
Description: Run by the fourth generation of the owners’ family, this restaurant is set in an enviable position on the ground floor of the Dunmore House Hotel with views out over Clonakilty Bay. Tasty, modern dishes showcase locally sourced produce, including some from their own organic kitchen garden.

Name: Upstairs at Landrace
Address: 59 Walcot Street, Bath, BA1 5BN, United Kingdom
Description: Landrace itself is an artisan bakery, which specialises in sourdough bread from stoneground British grains; if you can tear yourself away from the delicious aroma of the baking, head upstairs and you'll find this simply decorated restaurant with a pleasantly bright feel. There are some delicious cakes and pastries served with coffee in the morning, while the daily blackboard menu lists seasonal British dishes which are carefully cooked and full of rustic flavours – the bread and butter to start is, of course, a highlight.

Name: OSMA
Address: 132 Bury New Road, Prestwich, Manchester, M25 0AA, United Kingdom
Description: Located in the city’s northern suburbs, this restaurant’s name is a nod to the owners’ birthplaces – OSlo and MAnchester. They offer chatty, genuine service and are keen to recommend dishes from their mightily appealing seasonal menu. Sauces are a highlight, be it their take on ponzu with sashimi, or a simply delicious creamy romesco. The set lunch menu offers terrific value, while at dinner small plates take over. The stylish room comes with an open kitchen, a communal island table and smart curved banquettes.

Name: Clockspire
Address: Gainsborough, Milborne Port, DT9 5BA, United Kingdom
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Wheelchair access
Description: There's a lot of beautiful restaurants around, but Clockspire might be one of the most strikingly attractive spots you'll find. Housed within a converted 19th-century school, its high ceiling and exposed rafters provide plenty of ecclesiastical 'wow factor', while the lavishness of the refurbishment is mightily impressive. As you may expect, the dishes are impeccably presented and the polished cooking makes good use of its British ingredients. The slick service comes with a personal touch that feels as though the team really care about your experience.

Name: il trillo
Address: 4 Hollywood Road, Chelsea, London, SW10 9HY, United Kingdom
Description: The Bertuccelli family have been making wine and running a restaurant in the Tuscan Hills for over 30 years. Two of the brothers run this smart local which showcases the produce and wine from their region. Cooking is gutsy, with pasta the speciality. Relax in the delightful courtyard.

Name: THOMPSON St Albans
Address: 2 Hatfield Road, St Albans, AL1 3RP, United Kingdom
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Eponymous Chef-Owner Phil Thompson’s restaurant is split over three contemporary dining rooms, each featuring bold artwork from the local gallery. The dishes are equally good-looking and can be enjoyed from either an à la carte, or a 7 or 9 course tasting menu. The kitchen’s skills are evident across the accomplished cooking, while the friendly and efficient service team run the place well.

Name: Drapers Arms
Address: 44 Barnsbury Street, Islington, London, N1 1ER, United Kingdom
Description: A stalwart of London's pub dining scene, Islington continues to be well-served by this imposing neighbourhood local. Not much has changed over the years and it's all the better for it; rustic décor, eager-to-please staff and a relaxed, unpretentious approach ensure the perfect pub atmosphere. The cooking is as hearty and satisfying as ever, but these days the traditionally British (steak & ale pie) sits alongside French influences (braised rabbit leg), courtesy of a Breton-born Chef. The courtyard garden is a great place to enjoy a glass from the superb wine list.

Name: The Art School
Address: 1 Sugnall Street, Liverpool, L7 7EB, United Kingdom
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Wheelchair access
Description: Having celebrated 10 years in business, Paul Askew's restaurant continues to nourish the good diners of Liverpool. The spacious, elegant dining room has a stylish streak with its bright red chairs and crisp white tablecloths, while the formality of the décor is matched by the service team. The cooking is ambitious and full of colour, while a serious wine list adds to the appeal, with a particularly strong selection of reds. Do check out the array of special events they run, including guest chef dinners and live music nights.

Name: Michael Nadra Primrose Hill
Address: 42 Gloucester Avenue, Primrose Hill, London, NW1 8JD, United Kingdom
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Brunch,Restaurant offering vegetarian menus,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: You'll be spoilt for choice at this neighbourhood restaurant with its extensive, brasserie-style menu. Influences over the cooking come from around the world, so you'll find dishes inspired by everywhere from the Mediterranean (such as a Greek and niçoise salad cross) to Japan (miso black cod). A set lunch menu offers bang for your buck and a roast dinner is available on Sundays – not to mention a wide array of cocktails. The unusual vaulted room adds intimacy, while service is warm and friendly.

Name: Bellanger
Address: 9 Islington Green, Islington, London, N1 2XH, United Kingdom
Description: With awnings stretching over the pavement and walls festooned with classic posters, Bellanger has the feel of a Parisian grand café. The cooking, however, looks more broadly to the Mediterranean for inspiration; the Italian influences are clear, with dishes such as chicken Milanese sitting alongside the ubiquitous French classics like steak frites. The vibe is very much that of a neighbourhood restaurant, despite a well-organised formality to the service, and the large cocktail bar is perfect for an aperitif.

Name: Santo Remedio
Address: 152 Tooley Street, Southwark, London, SE1 2TU, United Kingdom
Description: The cooking inspiration comes from the owner’s time spent in Mexico City, the Yucatan and Oaxaca. Ingredients are a mix of imported – like grasshoppers to liven up the guacamole – and home-grown like Hertfordshire pork. Spread over two floors, the rooms are as colourful as the food.

Name: Noble Rot
Address: 51 Lamb’s Conduit Street, Bloomsbury, London, WC1N 3NB, United Kingdom
Description: With its dark, rough-lacquered wood and tiny candles, there is something pleasingly intimate about this wine bar and restaurant, where the walls are adorned with covers of the owners' Noble Rot magazine. This really is an oenophile's paradise, with the enthusiastic, clued-up team happy to suggest a smart, sometimes surprising, pairing to go with your meal. The cooking itself is decidedly classical, unfussy and more than a little French. The braised turbot with vin jaune sauce epitomises this spirit, which comes in tandem with gutsy, satisfying flavours.

Name: 36 on the Quay
Address: 47 South Street, The Quay, Emsworth, PO10 7EG, United Kingdom
Description: A quayside cottage plays host to this intimate restaurant, which affords lovely harbour views – and the sheltered terrace is a hit come summer. Modern dishes display a wealth of different flavours and textures, with the desserts being particularly playful. Bedrooms are cosy and stylish.

Name: Ginger Pig
Address: 3 Hove Street, Hove, Brighton and Hove, BN3 2TR, United Kingdom
Description: The whole package is here at The Ginger Pig: an early 20C inn near the seafront; a restaurant offering an extensive choice of British favourites and Mediterranean classics; bespoke cocktails; charming staff who are attentive and on the ball; and, finally, comfy bedrooms upstairs for those wishing to make a night of it.

Name: Mount St.
Address: First Floor, 41-43 Mount Street, Mayfair, London, W1K 2RX, United Kingdom
Description: There’s nothing anodyne about the art in this particular restaurant, which is hardly a surprise when you discover that art gallery group Hauser & Wirth are behind it. It’s a striking room with a stunning collection of pieces, from Matisse to Man Ray. The menu offers satisfying, classic British dishes like omelette Arnold Bennett and others inspired by the capital, such as ‘Pigeons in Pimlico’. If you’re early, you can always nip into The Audley pub downstairs.

Name: Elis
Address: Patriot Square, Bethnal Green, London, E2 9NF, United Kingdom
Description: Rafael Cagali, chef-owner of Da Terra, named his second restaurant, located in the Town Hall Hotel, after Brazilian jazz singer Elis Regina. The bright and lively 12-tabled room on the first floor reflects Rafael’s Italian and Brazilian heritage, so expect to see sharing dishes like 'bolinhos de bacalhau' vie with panzanella salad, and picanha skewer with crab linguini.

Name: Piazza
Address: 5th Floor, Royal Opera House, Bow Street, Covent Garden, London, WC2E 9DD, United Kingdom
Description: If you’re coming to see an opera or a ballet at the Royal Opera House, plan ahead and eat here on the 5th floor – either before or after the performance – to really take in its full splendour and magnificence. The room has the feel of a brasserie and its terrific terrace has great views over Covent Garden. The dishes are modern and exactingly prepared; the fish dishes are especially good, as are their sauces.

Name: The Spence
Address: 39 St Andrew Square, Edinburgh, EH2 2AD, United Kingdom
Description: Until 2017 this was the Royal Bank of Scotland, and the restaurant now occupies what was formerly the banking hall. All the grandeur is here, from the granite columns and the exquisite plasterwork to the magnificent cupola which allows natural light to flood in. The Scottish larder is the focus of the accessible menu, with the kitchen showing a keen eye for presentation.

Name: CULTURE
Address: Custom House Quay, 38b Arwenack Street, Falmouth, TR11 3JF, United Kingdom
Description: The open kitchen takes centre stage at this old quayside warehouse.
